- New `testcase.yaml` (`build_only: true`) covering all four board targets --
  this app needs Alif's proprietary `ensemble_vela.ini` to match the bench
  runtime and boots via MRAM slot0/Flow D, so it is a bench build, not a
  twister run.

Verified: `west build` for `alp_e1m_aen803_m55_hp/ae822fa0e5597ls0/rtss_hp`
links (FLASH 419,360 B of 2688 KiB slot0). The Flow C ITCM bench fragments
do NOT fit this model on HP ITCM either (overflows by ~154 KiB, same as the
existing HE build) -- both cores still boot this app via MRAM slot0/Flow D,
not a J-Link ITCM RAM-run.

Bench, E1M-AEN803 serial 2026W36-0009: the HP build written to the HP's
MRAM slot0 at `0x802B0000` with an `M55_HP` MRAM-XIP ATOC entry boots on
the M55-HP (banner `alp_e1m_aen803_m55_hp | CPU 400 MHz`) and runs the
network on the HP-local U55: `RESULT PASS: NPU inference via
alp_inference_open -- model=person_detect_u55 out_bytes=2 argmax=0`, again
after a cold power cycle. The image (419,360 B) does not fit the HP's
256 KiB ITCM, so it has no Flow C RAM-run path.

### Added — INA236 energy-sampler API + `aen-inference-energy`, millijoules per Ethos-U inference measured on silicon (#933)

Extends the `chips/ina236` driver with the averaging / conversion-time /
mode configuration (`ina236_configure()`), the conversion-timing helpers
(`ina236_avg_count()`, `ina236_conversion_time_us()`,
`ina236_sample_period_us()`), and the raw high-rate energy-sampling path
(`ina236_read_power_raw()`, `ina236_power_lsb_w()`) an energy-integration
sampler needs on top of the existing rail-monitoring API.

Adds `examples/aen/aen-inference-energy`, an on-target firmware that runs a
Vela-compiled model on the Ethos-U85 while sampling one of the E1M-EVK's six
INA236 rail monitors, and reports the incremental energy per inference as a
carrier-rail delta — see `docs/measuring-inference-energy.md` for the full
method, the whole-board cross-check, and the error budget, including what
the number is explicitly NOT (not NPU energy, not silicon energy, not
vendor-comparable, and not module-isolated: the default rail this app
selects, the EVK's +5V rail (INA236B U30 @ 0x4A), measures the WHOLE +5V
rail — SoM + LCD + carrier together). This ships only the on-device firmware
and its machine-readable console protocol; the host-side runner that will
parse and validate that protocol lives in `tan-cli` (see alp-sdk#1470 /
ADR-0028) and is not part of alp-sdk.

Split out of the stale `integration/model-edge-ai` branch (originally PR
#933): the model-tooling scripts that PR also carried
(`scripts/alp_model/{analyze,zoo,prep,measure,ondevice}.py`) belong to
`tan-cli` per ADR-0028 and are not part of this change.

### Fixed — INA236 POWER register under-reported by 625x, plus two more calibration defects (#933)

Three scaling defects in the shipped `chips/ina236` driver, all confirmed on
silicon by an independent bus-voltage x current cross-check: POWER reported
625x too low (the bus-voltage LSB was applied a second time on top of
SBOSA81D eq. 4's 32, which already carries it), SHUNT_CAL was never divided
by 4 for ADCRANGE=1 (SBOSA81D §8.1.2), and a saturating calibration clamp
left CURRENT_LSB describing a register value that was never written.

**This is a BEHAVIOUR CHANGE for every existing consumer of `ina236_read_power_uw()`
and `ina236_read_all()`**: a value read before this fix is ~625x too low (or,
on the fine ADCRANGE, additionally off by the missing /4). The calibration
arithmetic (`ina236_calibration_for()`) and the full-scale helper
(`ina236_full_scale_a()`) are now pure functions, publicly callable, and
unit-tested directly, so the tests drive the same code that ships.

Cross-checked on silicon (E1M-AEN803, 2026W36-0009): the POWER register mean
(2.2060 W) against shunt-voltage x bus-voltage (2.195 W) agree to a ratio of
1.005, and `CAL` read back `0x0800` (2048) at `ADCRANGE=1` (`CONFIG` `0x5407`),
exactly as the fixed calibration derivation predicts.

### Documented — ADR 0032: vendor data under its own terms gets a segregated subtree, not a `library-v1` allowlist entry (#948)

#948's acceptance list made "add `LicenseRef-Alif` to `metadata/schemas/library-v1.schema.json`
`license.enum`" its first item and the hardest prerequisite for shipping the Alif Ensemble SVDs.
Checked against the tree, that enum is the wrong gate: it governs `metadata/libraries/*.yaml` — the
35 library manifests a project pulls through a `libraries:` selection — and its own description says
why it exists, "so a copyleft surprise cannot ride in through a `libraries:` selection (ADR 0018
non-goal)". An SVD is not west-pulled, is not selectable, and `soc-spec-v1.schema.json` carries no
`license` field at all. Admitting `LicenseRef-Alif` there would widen 0018's guard to authorise
something that never travels that path.

The second finding is that the carve-out is bigger than a new directory. The root `NOTICE` already
states, as a published claim, that "Silicon-vendor BSPs and SDK binaries (Alif Ensemble, Renesas
RZ/V2N, NXP i.MX93, DEEPX DX-M1) are NOT redistributed in this repository" — so vendoring an Alif
file amends a representation this repo has already made, rather than filling a blank.

`docs/adr/0032-vendor-data-under-its-own-terms.md` records the mechanism: the curated-library
allowlist stays permissive-only; vendor data the vendor permits us to redistribute lands in its own
subtree — `metadata/svd/<vendor>/` for vendor register descriptions and
`vendors/<name>/` for vendored source — with the vendor's
unmodified licence file beside it, a README naming the upstream repository and commit and the
field-of-use restriction, and a matching root `NOTICE` entry; and the `NOTICE` amendment lands in
the same change as the first file it describes, never ahead of it. It records the mechanism, not an
authorisation — whether Alp Lab redistributes any given vendor's files stays a per-vendor maintainer
decision, and nothing in it is legal advice.

Consequence for the two coupled issues: #948's stated blocker is **proposed** to be
withdrawn — the ADR is `Status: Proposed`, and acceptance items 1 and 2 remain a
maintainer/legal decision, the remaining one being the per-vendor redistribution
call. #383 would be decoupled if the ADR is accepted — memfault-firmware-sdk genuinely is a
curated library, so its `LicenseRef-Memfault` question stands on its own and still needs the legal
review ADR 0018 requires.

Docs only; no schema, metadata or code change. `docs/README.md`'s ADR count moves 30 -> 31.

### Added — `variants[].debug.svd`: declare where a Cortex Peripherals SVD comes from, gated, with no file shipped (#948)

`cortex-debug`'s Cortex Peripherals view is driven entirely by `svdFile`, and the SDK gave a
consumer nothing to resolve — alp-sdk-vscode's field is still the literal `"<resolved-svd>"`
placeholder. This ships the resolution *mechanism* and deliberately not the files.

`metadata/schemas/soc-spec-v1.schema.json`'s `$defs/variant/properties/debug` gains an optional
`svd` **map keyed by `cores[].id`** beside `pyocd_target`, `jlink_device`, `jlink_flash_device`,
`expect_dpidr` and `openocd_config`. Keyed, not one string per variant, because an SVD is one
*core's* register view of the SoC: the Alif DFP ships `<order_code>_CM55_HE_View.svd` and
`<order_code>_CM55_HP_View.svd` as separate files (cited at
`metadata/socs/alif/ensemble/e3.json:225` and `metadata/socs/alif/ensemble/e5.json:173`), and
`scripts/gen_rzv2n_cm33_svd.py` emits a CM33-only view for a SoC that also has A55s. The
sibling `jlink_device` in the same object is already a `cores[].id` map for exactly this reason,
while `expect_dpidr` and `jlink_flash_device` are per-variant and each argues why in its own
description. A first draft of this key made no such argument and picked the single-string shape,
which cannot carry the data — the first vendoring PR would have had to change the schema and the
gate again, and in the meantime the only way to use the key was to declare one core's view and
let a launch config attach the HE register map to an HP session, which this key's own
description calls worse than shipping none (#1890 review). Each value is a **bare relative
path** — never absolute, never containing `..`, never a URL — resolved **repository directory
first, then `ALP_SVD_DIR`**, the same shape `SETOOLS_DIR` already has for genuinely
licence-gated vendor tooling. Absence semantics match
the rest of that block: an unresolvable path is not an error, the consumer omits `svdFile` and
the session runs without a register pane. Substituting another variant's SVD is called out as
worse than omitting one, because a register map from the wrong part reads plausibly.

`_check_soc_debug_svd_shape` in `scripts/validate_metadata.py` enforces it, and it cannot be a
single rule: **shape** is checked always, because an absolute path bakes one machine's layout
into published metadata, a `..` escapes whichever root resolved it, and a URL is not a path a
debugger can open. **Existence** is checked only for a value under `metadata/svd/` — the
subtree ADR 0032 designates — because anything else names a file on the customer's machine
that no build host can see, and failing it would break a correctly-configured project on a
host with no vendor SDK installed. The discriminator is that declared prefix, not the
filesystem: a first draft keyed it on "does the parent directory exist", which inverted the
check, letting a value that names a subtree nobody has created yet — the first mistake a
vendoring PR would make — pass silently. That case is now a test.

Two further defects in that gate, both found on review and both proven by executing the shipped
code rather than reading it. **Shape was judged with `PurePosixPath`, which does not treat `\` as
a separator**, so every rule the schema publishes was unenforced for a backslash spelling:
`..\outside\x.svd`, `\alif\x.svd` and `\\server\share\x.svd` all PASSED while their
forward-slash twins were refused, and `metadata\svd\alif\x.svd` slipped the existence half too
because its `parts[:2]` never equalled `('metadata', 'svd')`. That is the likeliest real mistake
on this repo's own Windows maintainer host. Shape is now judged with `PureWindowsPath`, which
treats both separators, and the vendored prefix is matched on a POSIX-normalised copy. **And the
gate printed nothing.** It built its messages, returned them, and `main()` only summed the
count — so tripping it produced a red build naming no file, no core and no rule, with the six
carefully-worded diagnostics unreachable in the only invocation CI runs. It now prints
`FAIL <path>` and a bulleted reason like every sibling checker in that file, and appends the
`str` relative path they all append rather than a `Path`. A test captures stdout, because
asserting on the returned list is exactly what let the omission through.

**No SoC declares the key**, and a test pins that absence so it fails loudly the day it
changes. Whether Alp Lab redistributes Alif's SVDs under Alif's terms is still a per-vendor
maintainer decision: ADR 0032 records the mechanism, not an authorisation, and the root
`NOTICE` currently publishes the opposite claim, which the first vendored file would have to
amend in the same change. Until then the supported source is a customer-supplied file reached
through `ALP_SVD_DIR` — which is enough for alp-sdk-vscode to stop shipping a placeholder.

Schema, gate, tests and docs only; no vendor file, no `NOTICE` change, no `metadata/socs/**`
data change. Every committed SoC document still validates, and the shape change costs no
metadata churn precisely because nothing declares the key yet — which is the reason to fix the
shape now rather than after the first value lands.

### Added — Alif Ensemble E8 SVD files, so debuggers get a peripheral/register view (#948)

`metadata/svd/alif/` now carries Alif's CMSIS-SVD register descriptions for
the Ensemble E8 M55-HE and M55-HP cores, copied unmodified from
`alifsemi/alif_ensemble-cmsis-dfp` at `b83f2944`. The files are vendor data
under Alif's own licence, not Apache-2.0. Following ADR 0032, Alif's
unmodified `License.txt` sits beside them, with a README recording
provenance, SHA-256 digests and the field-of-use restriction (Alif silicon
only), and the root `NOTICE` names the exception.

`alif/ensemble/e8.json` declares `variants[].debug.svd` for `m55_hp` and
`m55_he`, which tooling passes as cortex-debug's `svdFile`. The files are
named `AE822FA0E5597BS0_*`: the DFP's own pack description maps the
modules' `AE822FA0E5597LS0` part to exactly these files, so this is the
vendor's mapping, not a substitution of another variant's register map.
`validate_metadata.py` now checks that both files exist.

### Added — `cores.<core>.toolchain` lets a project declare a non-default toolchain variant (#964)

`board.yaml` had no input for the toolchain a slice builds with, even though the
system manifest and build-plan already carry a `slices[].toolchain` field —
until now it was always the SoM preset's derived default (`arm-zephyr-eabi` for
Zephyr, `poky-glibc` for Yocto), never customer-declared. This blocked
alp-sdk-vscode#314's toolchain picker: there was no input to write to.

`metadata/schemas/board.schema.json`'s `core_entry` now accepts an optional
`toolchain:` string per core, e.g.:

```yaml
cores:
  m55_hp:
    os: zephyr
    app: ./src
    toolchain: llvm
```

Omitting it keeps today's default unchanged — additive, and no existing
`board.yaml` changes behaviour. The value flows through the already-existing
`Slice.toolchain` plumbing (`scripts/alp_orchestrate/loader.py`'s per-core
merge already let a project override any SoM `topology.<core>` field; only
the schema was missing the key) into `--emit build-plan`'s
`slices[].toolchain.id`/`targetTriple`/`compiler` and
`system-manifest.yaml`'s `slices[].toolchain`, unchanged surfaces the same
`_slice_toolchain` derivation already populates from the SoM-preset default.

Deliberately out of scope (open questions the issue itself raises, not
resolved here): a validated enum vs. free-form value set, and a
host-local path for a vendor toolchain (`GNUARMEMB_TOOLCHAIN_PATH`-style) —
a maintainer call, not a schema addition.

### Fixed — MCUboot's scratch-swap trailer could survive a completed swap forever on a no-explicit-erase device, plus a separate ambiguous-swap_size crash (#1066)

The self-perpetuating re-swap this issue reported — a completed swap that
never clears its scratch magic and so keeps resuming forever — was
**confirmed on real silicon** (E1M-AEN801, 2026-07-31). Two independent
bootutil defects were found while root-causing it, and both are fixed
here; only one of them is the actual re-swap mechanism.

**The real re-swap mechanism, now fixed:** `swap_scratch.c`'s
`boot_swap_sectors()` writes a full temporary trailer — magic included —
to the scratch area while the primary slot's own trailer is rebuilt. The
comment right after it, *"Erase the temporary trailer from the scratch
area"*, is meant to remove that magic once it is no longer needed, but on
a flash device that does not require an explicit erase before rewrite
(Alif Ensemble on-die MRAM), that call is a **documented no-op**:
`boot_erase_region()` (`bootutil_area.c`) takes its
`device_requires_erase(fa) == false` branch, logs `"device without
erase"`, and returns success without touching flash. The GOOD magic
survives, and on the next boot `boot_status_tables[]`'s scratch-source
entry matches on that magic alone — regardless of the primary slot's own
`image_ok` — resuming the same completed swap forever. A second,
independent bug compounds this class of fix: `boot_scramble_region()`'s
backwards branch never wrote the block at its own range boundary (an
off-by-one in the loop guard), which for a trailer-scoped scramble is the
trailer's first status entry. Both are fixed in
`zephyr/patches/mcuboot/0004-scramble-scratch-trailer-and-backward-scramble-off-by-one.patch`:
the no-op erase is replaced with a trailer-scoped scramble (not a
whole-area one, to avoid an unnecessary MRAM endurance cost), and the
backwards loop is split so it writes its boundary block.

**`0002`'s own contribution is a separate, real, reproduced defect on
the `find_swap_count()` path — not the re-swap mechanism above.**
`swap_status_init()` (`swap_misc.c`) writes `swap_size` before magic
within the same call, so a GOOD scratch magic implies a
genuinely-written, nonzero `swap_size`; the re-swap mechanism above
never involves an erased `swap_size` field. `0002` closes a different,
narrower crash: `swap_size == 0`
also feeds `find_swap_count()` (`swap_scratch.c`), which
`boot_read_image_header()` uses to decide whether to substitute a
different slot's header — an ambiguous `0` there makes it substitute the
**wrong slot's** header, and the unpatched read segfaults inside that
substitution on the mcuboot host simulator. Fixed at the shared choke
point: `boot_read_swap_size()` now treats an erased-value `swap_size` as
a read failure (`BOOT_EBADSTATUS`, via the same `bootutil_buffer_is_erased()`
helper `boot_read_flag()` already uses for `image_ok`/`copy_done`) instead
of handing out a meaningless `0`. Both callers already fail safely on
that with no further change — `loader.c`'s existing `assert(rc == 0)`
propagates up to `boot_read_image_headers()` failing, which declines the
swap outright (primary slot left untouched) rather than proceeding on a
`0`; `swap_scratch.c` already turns any nonzero return here into
`BOOT_EFLASH` before it can substitute the wrong slot. **An earlier
version of this fix guarded `copy_size == 0` at the `loader.c` call site
alone and force-cleared the scratch trailer there directly — this was
caught on review and replaced**: that guard could destroy an in-flight
swap's only surviving copy of a sector and then report success,
converting a harmless reboot loop into a bootloader that signs off on a
corrupted image, and it left the `find_swap_count()` call site unguarded.
Carried as
`zephyr/patches/mcuboot/0002-bootutil_misc-reject-erased-swap_size-trailer.patch`,
touching no flash on the failure path.

**Regression-verified on the mcuboot host simulator** (`sim/`, cargo + a
C compiler, no embedded toolchain needed), against the pinned upstream
revision `6d3b3d2c38ab20c242e5b9abb04d050086383eb2`:

- `0003-sim-swap-size-erased-collision-regression-test.patch` (companion
  to `0002`) force-writes an interrupted, genuinely in-progress swap's
  `swap_size` field to the device's erase value and asserts the primary
  slot is never left stamped complete over a corrupted image. Pre-`0002`,
  this **segfaults** inside `boot_read_image_header()`'s wrong-slot
  substitution.
- `0005-sim-scratch-trailer-no-erase-device-regression-test.patch`
  (companion to `0004`, covering BOTH of its fixes) adds two tests.
  `scratch_trailer_cleared_after_swap` runs a real, uninterrupted,
  permanent upgrade to completion on a device that does not require an
  explicit erase, and asserts the scratch area's temporary trailer never
  reads back a GOOD magic afterwards — this covers fix (i). Pre-`0004`,
  it **fails on the very first device/align/erased_val combination it
  tries**. Getting there needed a small maker of its own
  (`ImagesBuilder::make_image_undersized()`): every existing maker fills
  its slot to capacity by design, which keeps the swap on the
  `bs->use_scratch == true` path `0004`'s fix (i) does not touch, so the
  no-op-erase mechanism was unreachable by ANY existing sim test — not
  just an untested one. `scramble_region_backwards_boundary` calls
  `boot_scramble_region()`'s backwards branch directly instead, over an
  arbitrary sub-range of the scratch area, and asserts the write-block
  boundary at the low end of that range was written and nothing below it
  was touched — this covers fix (ii), which the first test's own
  end-to-end shape (every real caller's off/size sums to the flash
  area's own size) cannot distinguish from a no-op: with fix (i) applied
  but fix (ii)'s `bootutil_area.c` hunk alone reverted, **27 passed and
  only the new direct test failed**.

Post-`0004`+`0005`: `cargo test --release --test core` — **28 passed, 0
failed** (26 pre-existing cases plus these two), across every
device/alignment/`erased_val` (`0x00` and `0xff`) combination the harness
sweeps. All five patches verified to apply cleanly, in order, on the
pinned upstream revision.

**Not bench-verified on AEN silicon, and cannot be from this tree
today**: #1100 and #1445 removed the AEN family's scratch/slot1
partitions to fit the disjoint dual-core slot0 budget, so no AEN board
target currently builds the scratch-swap path either fix touches. This
closes the mechanism ahead of a secondary slot being reintroduced, so the
swap-path work does not have to be redone from scratch before OTA can be
re-enabled. It does **not** close #1066's second finding (a clean, valid
PERM upgrade request that produced no swap at all), which was never
root-caused and still gates the revert-on-bad-image security claim. That
finding's own trace runs through a stale non-`0x00` primary status byte
surviving into the next boot, not the scratch-magic mechanism `0004`
fixes; `0004`'s off-by-one fix (ii) plausibly removes that stale byte's
source, but that link is a **hypothesis, not proven here**.

### Fixed — the V2N-family SoC RTC has no crystal fitted; Linux now uses the on-module RV-3028-C7 instead (#1139)

Bench-proven 2026-09-24 on an E1M-V2N-family SoM (E1M-X-EVK, image
som-0.2.0, kernel 6.1.141-cip43): `rtc-rtca3 11c00800.rtc: error
-ETIMEDOUT: Failed to setup the RTC!`, then `probe of 11c00800.rtc failed
with error -110` on every boot. Root cause: RTXIN/RTXOUT has no 32.768 kHz
crystal fitted on the E1M V2N-family SoM (schematic crystal DNP) — the
SoC RTC was never going to probe. `docs/soms/v2n.md`'s catalogue always
carried the real RTC (a Micro Crystal RV-3028-C7 at I2C `0x52` on
BRD_I2C), but nothing on the Linux side used it: `# CONFIG_RTC_DRV_RV3028
is not set` in the kernel config left `/sys/class/rtc` empty, and the
carrier dtsi separately re-enabled the crystal-less SoC RTC anyway
(`meta-alp-sdk/recipes-kernel/linux/linux-renesas/e1m-x-evk.dtsi`
previously carried `&rtxin_clk { clock-frequency = <32768>; };` and
`` &rtc { status = "okay"; }; `` — ported from the Renesas EVK reference
dts, which does populate the crystal). Also stale:
alp-sdk#1139's own current-state line, "RTC (internal) — `&rtc` okay on
A55".

Fixed at the SoM layer, not the carrier: `` &rtc { status = "disabled";
}; `` now lives in
`meta-alp-sdk/recipes-kernel/linux/linux-renesas/e1m-v2n-som.dtsi` (that
line's own state is superseded a few hours later, see the note below --
no line-number citation here since it no longer says "disabled"), with
the carrier's conflicting override removed (SoM dtsi composes before the
carrier dtsi, so leaving the carrier's `"okay"` in place would have
silently won). A new `rtc@52` node under the existing `&i2c8` block,
`meta-alp-sdk/recipes-kernel/linux/linux-renesas/e1m-v2n-som.dtsi:458`
("rv3028: rtc@52 {"), binds `compatible = "microcrystal,rv3028"`, and a
new `aliases { rtc0 = &rv3028; };` makes it `/dev/rtc0`.
`CONFIG_RTC_DRV_RV3028=y` is now built in,
`meta-alp-sdk/recipes-kernel/linux/linux-renesas/rv3028-rtc.cfg:7`
("CONFIG_RTC_DRV_RV3028=y"), so `hwclock` has a working RTC at early
boot, not racing module load order. No `trickle-resistor-ohms` is set — whether
the RV-3028-C7's VBACKUP net carries a backup cap/coin cell on this SoM
is not confirmed on the schematic. RTC_ALARM (INT) is not wired to an
`interrupts` property either; the SoC-side pin/mux isn't confirmed yet —
both are follow-ups, not guessed here.

**Maintainer decision:** CA55/Linux is the sole master of the *whole*
RIIC8/BRD_I2C bus — every device on it (the RTC, DA9292, the GD32 I2C
slave, TMP112, the clock generator), not just the RTC this fix touches —
the CM33 must not master RIIC8 at all.
`metadata/e1m_modules/v2n/core-ownership.yaml` (`core: "a55"` on
`RIIC8_SCL8`/`RIIC8_SDA8`) records that. The rest of the reconciliation —
`supervisor-links.yaml`'s `brd_i2c` link, the generated CM33 Zephyr
board's `i2c8`/`alp-i2c0` pinctrl, `src/zephyr/v2n_power_mgmt.c`'s DA9292
bring-up, `examples/v2n/v2n-rtc-multi-alarm`, and the clock-ownership
kernel patch's `riic_8_ckm` hunk — lands in #2045.

**Superseded same day:** the `&rtc { status = "disabled"; };` cited
above was itself corrected to `"okay"` a few hours later, once #2045
bench work found RTXIN's actual reference (fed by the on-module clock
generator, not a discrete crystal) and a runtime fix for it — see the
later `#2045` fragment (clock-generator fixup). The RV-3028-C7 stays
the RTC of record (`rtc0` alias, unchanged); the SoC RTC is a second,
now-also-enabled timebase.

### Added — a Linux devicetree claim on a CM33-owned RZ/V2N pad is now a CI failure (#1142)

V2N is an AMP part, and its two cores declared pads in two trees that never met:
the A55's claims live in the Linux devicetree under `meta-alp-sdk/`, the CM33's
in `metadata/pinmux/v2n.yaml`'s `core` field (#1157). Neither side could see the
other at build time. That is how the USB over-current `gpio-hog` on `P9.6`
silently clobbered the CM33's live `SCK7` mux at every Linux boot once the GD32
supervisor SPI took the pad — a `PMC9`/`PM9` byte-RMW landing at ~1.9 s, inside
the CM33's pin-setup window, recorded at `docs/errata-e1m-x-v2n.md:127`
("half of the hog REGRESSED"). A bench session found that; nothing in CI could.

`scripts/check_amp_pad_claims.py` closes the loop. Every `RZV2N_GPIO(...)` and
`RZV2N_PORT_PINMUX(...)` under `meta-alp-sdk/recipes-kernel/linux/` resolves to a
pad, and a pad the pinmux table attributes to the CM33 is now a hard error naming
the file, the line and the fix. The gate is validated by execution against the
known-bad tree, not by reading: the pre-2026-06-12 `P9.6` hog is replayed
verbatim in `tests/scripts/test_check_amp_pad_claims.py` and must go red.

The devicetree side of this issue was already correct in the tree and is
unchanged. The hog is `PB.1`-only, and the port-9 AMP rule is already written
above `usb-ovc-disable-hog` in
`meta-alp-sdk/recipes-kernel/linux/linux-renesas/e1m-x-evk.dtsi` — "P9.6 (usb20
OVC) is DELIBERATELY absent". What was missing was anything that enforced it.

**One documented exemption, and it is a finding, not a formality.** `BRD_I2C` /
`RIIC8` (`P06`/`P07`) is dual-master by design. The CM33 muxes it at
`zephyr/boards/alp/e1m_v2n101_m33_sm/alp_e1m_v2n101_m33_sm-pinctrl.dtsi:47-48`
("RZV_PINMUX(PORT_00, 6, 1)"), and so does Linux, whose `i2c8_pins` group claims the same two pads
to drive the GD32 bridge expander through a purpose-built kernel driver
(`0005-gpio-add-gd32-bridge-expander-driver.patch`). The `core` field cannot say
"both": `m33` is the value it carries today, and an absent `core` is documented
as "not attributed", never "shared". So the metadata cannot state the truth about
these two pads either way, and the pair is exempt in one place with both claims
cited. Widening that vocabulary is a schema decision (#1157) left to the
maintainer. An exemption matching no `core: "m33"` row is itself a hard error, so
it cannot rot into decoration.

### Changed

- `metadata/e1m_modules/v2n/core-ownership.yaml` records PA0 (`eMMC_V_SEL`) as A55-owned (maintainer decision, #1142): U-Boot sets it before the first MMC access and the Linux `emmc_v_sel_1v8` gpio-hog keeps the eMMC at 1.8 V I/O for HS200, so no CM33 board file may claim it. `metadata/pinmux/v2n.yaml` now carries the core attribution.

### Fixed — the DRP-AI bring-up doc still offered a rejected boot mechanism as a live option, and the doc-drift gate carried two allowlist entries to let it pass (#1145)

`docs/bring-up-drpai-v2n.md`'s deploy section pointed readers at a second,
unmerged `CONFIG_ALP_FDT_FILE` / `CONFIG_ALP_SD_ROOT` implementation on
`feat/1145-drpai-v2n-bringup` and told them to "see #1175 before relying on
either". Three things about that were no longer true:

- **#1175 is closed.** `dev` carries the fix (#1182, eMMC half completed in
  #1186); the branch's version was deliberately not landed, because two
  mechanisms both setting the boot dtb is worse than either. Reasons are
  recorded on #1175 and #1238 — it is history, not a pending alternative.
- **Its one stated advantage is gone.** The V2M gap `dev`'s hardcoded
  filename left open is closed in-tree by `CONFIG_ALP_E1M_FDTFILE`
  (`meta-alp-sdk/recipes-bsp/u-boot/u-boot/fdtfile-v2m.cfg`, wired per
  MACHINE in `meta-alp-sdk/recipes-bsp/u-boot/u-boot_%.bbappend`; #1252).
- **Nothing has still booted a board**, so that caveat stays — but it is now
  attached to the mechanism that actually ships.

`scripts/check_doc_drift.py`'s `_ALLOWLIST` existed only to excuse that
paragraph: `ALP_FDT_FILE` and `ALP_SD_ROOT` are symbols this repo will never
define. Both are dropped. `ALP_E1M_FDTFILE` is added in their place — a real
identifier, but defined in
`meta-alp-sdk/recipes-bsp/u-boot/u-boot/0002-rzv2n-dev-ALP-E1M-production-boot.patch`
and set in a `*.cfg`, neither of which the meta-alp-sdk harvest scans
(`*.conf` / `*.bb` / `*.bbappend` / `*.inc` only), and the one `.bbappend`
that names it spells it `CONFIG_`-prefixed, which the harvest regex
deliberately does not strip. Same shape as the existing `ALP_CA55_1P8GHZ`
entry. Net: the allowlist shrinks by one and no longer vouches for a symbol
that does not exist.

**No change to the DRP-AI enablement itself.** `ALP_SDK_USE_DRPAI_V2N` still
defaults OFF and `ALP_ENABLE_DRPAI` still defaults `"0"`; #1145's two gates
are untouched. The backend has not been baked with `PACKAGECONFIG[drpai]`
enabled and has not run on DRP-AI silicon (#1268).

### Changed — DRP-AI3 is reachable by default on V2N/V2M images (#1145)

Every shipped V2N/V2M image already carried the DRP-AI3 kernel driver
(`CONFIG_DRPAI=y`), its 512 MiB `drp-ai@d0000000` arena and the vendor
runtime (`lib-tvm`, `mmngr`), but not `/dev/drpai0`: `&drpai0` stayed
`status = "disabled"`, because `ALP_ENABLE_DRPAI` defaulted to `"0"`. Board #1
(E1M-V2M103, Alp SDK 0.7.0 image) showed exactly that on 2026-09-28.

Changes:
- `ALP_ENABLE_DRPAI` now defaults to `"1"` whenever meta-rz-drpai is in
  bblayers.conf, in all six V2N/V2M machine confs and the kernel bbappend
  fallback. `ALP_ENABLE_DRPAI = "0"` opts out.
- `PACKAGECONFIG[drpai]` (the SDK backend) turns on by itself on an
  `rzv2n-family` MACHINE when the node is on and `RUHMI_DRPAI_TVM_DIR` points
  at a RUHMI checkout. Without one, it stays off instead of failing the bake.
- `alp-image-edge` installs the `alp-drpai-inference` demo only when that
  backend is built.
- `docs/bring-up-drpai-v2n.md`, `meta-alp-sdk/README.md` and the example
  docs describe the new defaults.

### Added — `v2n-drpai-inference` example + the `ALP_ENABLE_DRPAI` opt-in that wires DRP-AI3 into `alp-image-edge` (#1145, #1268)

Salvaged from `feat/1145-drpai-v2n-bringup` (`1cadada9bb12b3039db35642c29bbef592b832e0`)
as a fresh PR after #1693 was found to overclaim what had actually run;
`docs/bring-up-drpai-v2n.md` (already on `dev`) carries the honest
BENCH-UNVERIFIED status this entry keeps.

**🟡 Code-complete, bench-unverified. No `drpai`-enabled `alp-image-edge`
bake has ever completed, on any host, and nothing has run on DRP-AI
silicon.** Bench sign-off is tracked as #1268.

- **`examples/v2n/v2n-drpai-inference/`** — the exhibition-booth demo: reads
  one or more raw pre-processed 640x640x3 float32 NCHW (planar) frames given on the
  command line, runs each through `<alp/inference.h>` with
  `backend = ALP_INFERENCE_BACKEND_DRPAI`, and prints per-image top-5 raw
  scores + timing. `[UNTESTED on silicon]`. `src/top_scores.c` (the top-N
  selection helper) is unit-tested by `tests/unit/top_scores/`.
- **`ALP_ENABLE_DRPAI`** (default `"0"`; the flag itself predates this change
  — added by `cbea0e29`) is declared on all six RZ/V2N-family machine confs
  (`e1m-v2n101-a55.conf`, `e1m-v2n102-a55.conf`, `e1m-v2n103-a55.conf`,
  `e1m-v2m101-a55.conf`, `e1m-v2m102-a55.conf`, `e1m-v2m103-a55.conf`) and
  does two things: it gates the `&drpai0` devicetree node, and -- on
  `alp-image-edge` only -- gates installing the demo binary below. It
  installs no userspace runtime package itself. The four v2n101/102 + v2m101/102 confs do not gate a machine-conf
  `IMAGE_INSTALL:append` (`lib-tvm kernel-module-mmngr`): that would duplicate `alp-image-common.inc`'s existing `ALP_RZ_DRPAI_INSTALL`
  (#1176) pair-for-pair for every `alp-image-*` image, so it would always be a
  no-op there, never a drift guard -- `alp-image-common.inc` is the userspace pair's single
  packaging authority for `alp-image-*` builds. The demo binary, **`alp-drpai-inference`**,
  rides the same `ALP_ENABLE_DRPAI` opt-in but from a separate, IMAGE-level
  append in `alp-image-edge.bb` (not the machine confs), gated on the same
  `rzv2n-family` `MACHINEOVERRIDES` check as the `bb.fatal()` guard below,
  so this booth demo (#1268) reaches `alp-image-edge` only -- and only on
  an `rzv2n-family` MACHINE -- never `alp-image-prod`. The
  alp-sdk backend's own `PACKAGECONFIG[drpai]` stays the released,
  independently-set second
  switch ("Two independent switches, both default OFF, deliberately not
  merged into one" — `CHANGELOG.md`'s v0.15.0 entry). The two are not coupled via
  `PACKAGECONFIG:append:pn-alp-sdk`. `alp-image-edge.bb` gates a
  `bb.fatal()` guard on the `rzv2n-family` `MACHINEOVERRIDES` override so
  opting in without `meta-rz-drpai` in `bblayers.conf` fails loudly at
  parse time instead of an obscure missing-recipe error.
- **`meta-alp-sdk/recipes-examples/alp-drpai-inference/alp-drpai-inference_0.6.bb`**
  packages the example the same way `alp-edgeai_0.6.bb` /
  `alp-lvgl-dashboard_0.6.bb` do.
- **`alp-sdk_0.6.bb`'s `PACKAGECONFIG[drpai]`** (added on `dev` separately by
  `cbea0e29`) gains the genuine delta this branch needed: the OFF branch now
  also sets `-DALP_SDK_DRPAI_REQUIRED=OFF`, and the DEPENDS/RDEPENDS field
  adds `mera2-drpai-tvm` as a runtime dependency — plus a `do_configure`
  prefunc (`do_generate_toolchain_file`) that keeps `${WORKDIR}/toolchain.cmake`
  from going stale under `externalsrc` bakes.
- **`src/yocto/inference_drpai.cpp`**'s header comment is corrected, not
  copied verbatim from the source branch: the branch claimed a
  `drpai`-enabled bake resolved all 9 `MeraDrpRuntimeWrapper` symbols with
  "0 unresolved" — that never happened. What is actually established (see
  `meta-alp-sdk/recipes-renesas/mera2-drpai-tvm/mera2-drpai-tvm_2.7.0.bb`):
  the wrapper source cross-compiles to a valid `.o` with every symbol
  defined, confirmed by hand with `nm` on an x86_64 dev host, NOT by a bake;
  the final link against the real aarch64 `obj/build_runtime/v2h`
  libraries has never been exercised (that same host stops at "skipping
  incompatible ... when searching for -lmera2_runtime", an architecture
  mismatch, not proof of symbol resolution).

**Redundant per-machine DRP-AI appends removed:** the four RZ/V2N-family
machine confs' own `ALP_ENABLE_DRPAI`-gated `IMAGE_INSTALL:append`
(`lib-tvm kernel-module-mmngr`) overlapped `dev`'s existing
`ALP_RZ_DRPAI_INSTALL` in `alp-image-common.inc` (#1176) — both installed
the same `lib-tvm kernel-module-mmngr` pair on every `alp-image-*` image
(the three recipes that `require alp-image-common.inc`), one
unconditionally there and one opt-in. `bitbake` dedupes the repeated
package names, so it was never a build break, but it was also never a
drift guard for `alp-image-*` builds: `ALP_ENABLE_DRPAI = "0"` still left
the pair installed via `alp-image-common.inc` whenever the layer +
MACHINE_FEATURES matched, so the two mechanisms couldn't drift relative to
each other there and the four appends bought nothing. Removed; the
corresponding comments in each machine conf and in `alp-image-edge.bb` are
corrected to name `alp-image-common.inc` as the single packaging authority
for `alp-image-*` builds.

**Behavioural change, stated honestly, not glossed over:**
`alp-image-common.inc` is required only by `alp-image-base`/`-edge`/`-prod`
(the three `alp-image-*` recipes), whereas the removed machine-conf
`IMAGE_INSTALL:append` reached EVERY image built for those four MACHINEs --
including a bare `core-image-*` or any other non-`alp-image-*` recipe. A
non-`alp-image-*` build that relied on `ALP_ENABLE_DRPAI = "1"` alone to
pull in `lib-tvm` + `kernel-module-mmngr` must now add that pair itself
(its own `IMAGE_INSTALL`), or rely on the vendor layer's own `core-image`
bbappend for it -- no such bbappend exists anywhere in this tree today, so
there is currently no fallback install path for a non-alp image here.

**Dead `alp_model build` command dropped:** the example's README and
`main.c` taught `python3 -m alp_model build --target drpai --product V2N
<model.onnx>` as the way to produce the `drpai_dir` bundle `argv[1]` loads,
but `scripts/alp_model` has no `__main__`, so the command fails outright —
and even a working invocation could not compile this model, since the
adapter's calibration path rejects a `1,3,640,640` detector shape. The dead
command is dropped everywhere (README.md, `main.c`'s teaching comment and
`usage()` string) and replaced with an honest statement: there is no
supported path in this SDK today to produce this bundle; producing one is
tracked in [alplabai/alp-sdk#2236](https://github.com/alplabai/alp-sdk/issues/2236);
until then the bundle has to be compiled outside the SDK, directly with the
Renesas DRP-AI TVM (RUHMI) toolchain, and tarred the same way
`adapters/drpai.py` would.

`docs/board-config-schema.md`'s example preset count is corrected to match:
after merging `dev` (which added its own new examples in parallel), 101
examples target a preset today (76 on `e1m-evk`, 25 on `e1m-x-evk`), counted
directly off `examples/**/board.yaml` post-merge, not carried over from
either side's pre-merge count.

### Fixed — `alp-mcp`'s `peripheral_support` tool read a silicon fact as a support claim (#1146)

`metadata/catalog.json`'s `soms[N].soc_peripherals` map is documented (`scripts/gen_catalog.py`,
#1243) as a literal silicon projection, not "does `<alp/CLASS.h>` work on this SKU" — and
correctly so. `scripts/alp_mcp/server.py`'s `peripheral_support()` MCP tool read that same map
one hop downstream and returned it under keys literally named `supported` / `supported_by`, with
no caveat, in all three of its response modes. An agent asking "does E1M-V2N101 support CAN"
got `can: true` uncaveated, while `alp_can_open()` returns `ALP_ERR_NOT_READY` on every channel:
no CANFD devicetree node exists for V2N/V2M on either core (#1146's own body; see also #914 for
the AEN-side equivalent).

The V2N/V2M SoC (`renesas:rzv2n:n44`, `metadata/socs/renesas/rzv2n/n44.json:67`) integrates 6
CAN-FD controllers in silicon, but the E1M-X V2N module bonds out only **2** of them —
CANFD2 (`CRX2`→`P85`, `CTX2`→`P84`) and CANFD3 (`CRX3`→`P87`, `CTX3`→`P86`), per
`metadata/e1m_modules/v2n/renesas-peripheral-map.tsv:16-19` and `metadata/pinmux/v2n.yaml:28-31`
— and the tool reports at module level, so the module figure is the one that must be quoted, not
the SoC figure.

`peripheral_support()` now returns a `note` field on every successful response (the `sku`-only
map, the `sku`+`peripheral` boolean, and the `peripheral`-only list) stating plainly that
`soc_peripherals` reflects silicon integration only, not portable-API availability or backend
implementation status, and to check `src/backends/<peripheral>/` and the board's devicetree
before assuming a `true` means the peripheral works.

### Documented — CAN-FD on V2N/V2M is blocked upstream, not merely unwritten; both trees now say exactly how (#1146)

The enablement half of this issue was investigated and **deliberately not built**. It cannot be
built honestly at the pinned toolchain, and the reason belongs where the next person will look,
because in both trees a plausible wrong value is sitting one file away from the right one.

The first framing to retire is "there is no driver". Zephyr v4.4.1 *does* ship an RZ CAN-FD
driver and both bindings (`can_renesas_rz_canfd.c`, `renesas,rz-canfd.yaml`,
`renesas,rz-canfd-global.yaml`), and `src/backends/can/zephyr_drv.c` already binds any
`DT_ALIAS(alp_canN)`. Four separate things stop that driver binding on the RZ/V2N CM33, and each
one is vendor data this repo does not carry:

- **No FSP CAN-FD module for RZ/V.** `CONFIG_CAN_RENESAS_RZ_CANFD` selects `USE_RZ_FSP_CANFD`,
  which compiles `fsp/src/${SOC_SERIES_PREFIX}/r_canfd/r_canfd.c`. hal_renesas at Zephyr v4.4.1's
  pin (`06282060fa20cbd21d4ebbc7d46a1fc9533fd24e`) carries that module for RZ/G only —
  `fsp/src/rzg/r_canfd/` and `fsp/inc/instances/rzg/r_canfd.h` exist, the `rzv` counterparts do
  not. Turning the symbol on under `SOC_SERIES_RZV2N` is a CMake configure error on a missing
  source file, and the driver's `#include "r_canfd.h"` does not resolve on the `rzv` include path.
- **No CAN-FD node in the SoC devicetree.** `arm/renesas/rz/rzv/r9a09g056.dtsi` declares none, so
  there is no label to reference and no `reg`/`interrupts` to inherit. The only RZ SoC dtsi that
  carries them is RZ/G3S's `r9a08g045.dtsi`, whose plausible-looking `canfd-global@400c0000` and
  interrupts `373`/`374` (global) and `375..380` (per channel) belong to a different part.
- **No static NVIC vector exists to write.** RZ/V2N's CM33 gives CAN-FD no dedicated vector at
  all: `bsp_irq_id.h`'s `IRQn_Type` enum has zero CANFD entries, and all 20 CAN-FD sources live
  in the separate `IRQSELn_Type` enum (354..373, including `CANFD_INTRCANGERR_IRQSELn` 366 and
  `CANFD_INTRCANGRECC_IRQSELn` 367). They reach the NVIC only by being routed onto one of the
  selectable slots `SEL0_IRQn`..`SEL126_IRQn` (NVIC 353..479) at run time, through
  `R_BSP_SelectIrqSet()`. Upstream's own dtsi hands those slots out (`adc0` = 403 = SEL50,
  `gpt0` = 406..408 = SEL53..55, on up to 453) and both bindings require `interrupts`, so
  choosing slots here would invent an allocation that collides with whatever upstream picks.
- **No PFC function index for the pads.** The module bonds out two of the SoC's six controllers,
  CANFD2 (CTX2 = P84, CRX2 = P85) and CANFD3 (CTX3 = P86, CRX3 = P87), but
  `metadata/pinmux/v2n.yaml` carries pad <-> signal only, with no alternate-function number.
  `RZV_PINMUX()` needs one, and it lives in the RZ/V2N hardware manual's PFC table.

**One hardware number is worth quoting, because the vendor header carries its own trap.** The
CAN-FD register base on this part is `0x42440000` — `R_CANFD_BASE` in hal_renesas's
`R9A09G056N/iodefines/canfd_iodefine.h`. The `(@ 0x400B0000)` in that same file's `R_CANFD`
struct doc-comment is a template annotation, not this SoC's base. Nothing here writes either
value into a node; both are recorded so a future port does not pick the wrong one.

What *is* already in place, so a port need not re-derive it: the clock path.
`RZ_CLOCK_CANFD(ch)` exists in `dt-bindings/clock/renesas_rzv_clock.h`, and
`clock_control_renesas_rz_cpg.c` already maps `RZ_IP_CANFD` onto
`R_BSP_MODULE_START(FSP_IP_CANFD, ch)`; rzv2n's `bsp_feature.h` declares 6 channels, CAN-FD
support and 96 RX message buffers for this part.

**A carrier fact that changes who owns the transceivers.** `CAN_STBY` is not a Renesas pad — it
belongs to the GD32 IO-MCU on `PB13` (`metadata/pinmux/v2n.yaml:198` ("CAN_STBY")), so taking the
TCAN1044 pair out of standby is a bridge GPIO call on either core, not a pinctrl entry. And
CANFD2/CANFD3 are still unattributed in `metadata/e1m_modules/v2n/core-ownership.yaml`, whose
"absence means not attributed" rule leaves `scripts/check_amp_pad_claims.py` unable to see an
A55-vs-CM33 conflict on those pads until a core claims them.

No code changed, and no devicetree node was added on either core. The analysis lands as two
comment blocks in the repo's existing documented-absence idiom (the `wdt0` block from #1153, the
audio block in the carrier dtsi):
`zephyr/boards/alp/e1m_v2n101_m33_sm/alp_e1m_v2n101_m33_sm_r9a09g056n48gbg_cm33.dts:151-221`
("No &canfd node here") for the CM33, and
`meta-alp-sdk/recipes-kernel/linux/linux-renesas/e1m-x-evk.dtsi:156-184`
("DATA-GATED on the kernel side") for the A55, which upgrades a bare one-line TODO into the three
kernel-side values still missing (the `canfd` node's label and compatible string in the
linux-renesas 6.1.x `r9a09g056` dtsi, the `RZV2N_PORT_PINMUX` function index for P84..P87, and
whether the BSP defconfig builds a CAN-FD driver at all). `<alp/can.h>` behaviour is unchanged
and already correct: `src/backends/can/zephyr_drv.c:167` ("return ALP_ERR_NOT_READY") when no
`alp-canN` alias resolves.

### Added — RZ/V2N OTP recorded in the SoC metadata and the V2N SoM doc (#1148)

`metadata/socs/renesas/rzv2n/n44.json` now counts the SoC's OTP unit
(`"otp": 1`). `docs/soms/v2n.md` gains a "SoC OTP" section with the facts
from the hardware manual (R01UH1071EJ0120 Rev.1.20 §4.10):
- 32 Kbits, supplied from `OTPVDD18`;
- base `0x10450000` (CM33 `0x50450000` / `0x40450000`);
- 16-bit write, 32-bit read, write-once bits;
- the Table 4.10-3 area map: chip product ID `0F3h`-`0F6h`, one-time-read
  enable `12Ah`, boot-device drive strength `12Ch`, user areas `160h`-`1DFh`
  and `1E0h`-`3DFh`.

The SDK does not use it (identity is EEPROM-authoritative). The doc records
that writing it is permanent and out of scope for provisioning.

### Fixed — `docs/os-support-matrix.md` claimed camera GA on V2N/V2N-M1 Cortex-A, wrong core (#1149)

The v0.2.0 Cortex-A (Yocto) table's Camera row read `**GA** (MIPI CSI-2)` for V2N and `**GA**` for
V2N-M1. Neither is true on the A55/Yocto side: the only camera backend `src/yocto/CMakeLists.txt`
links there is `src/backends/camera/zephyr_stub.c` (unconditional, `silicon_ref = "*"`, priority
0), which returns `ALP_ERR_NOT_IMPLEMENTED` for every op on every SoM — a `stub` per this doc's own
status key (`docs/os-support-matrix.md:9`), not `GA`.

The real MIPI CSI-2 ISP-aware camera backend, `src/backends/camera/v2n_n44_isp.c`, does exist and
is registered for `silicon_ref = "renesas:rzv2n:n44"` — but it is a **Zephyr** backend
(`#include <zephyr/drivers/video.h>`, `zephyr/CMakeLists.txt:812`, opt-in via
`CONFIG_ALP_SDK_CAMERA_V2N_N44_ISP`) for the V2N `m33_sm` core, not the A55/Yocto core the table
row claimed it for. Citing a Cortex-M backend to justify a Cortex-A cell is worse than saying
nothing, because it plans a product around a core that never links the code.

Both cells now read `stub`, with a footnote (`[^cam1]`) naming the real Yocto stub backend + its
link site and the real (but wrong-core) Zephyr ISP backend + its link site, so the distinction does
not get re-conflated later.

### Documented — V2N MIPI CSI-2 sensor path: recorded the data gate instead of guessing a sensor (#1149)

`src/backends/camera/v2n_n44_isp.c` is registered for `silicon_ref = "renesas:rzv2n:n44"` and its
capture path is real, but it resolves a device only through the `alp-camera0..3` devicetree
aliases — and no V2N board or overlay in this repo defines one, so the backend's `_devs[]` NULL
check fires and `alp_camera_open()` on V2N hands back `NULL` with `last_error` =
`ALP_ERR_NOT_READY`. No devicetree was written for it here,
because the values a CSI-2 node needs are not in this tree or its pinned dependencies. What landed
is the two comment blocks that say so precisely, so the next attempt starts from the gap rather
than re-deriving it.

That backend's header used to promise that once the SoC port wired MIPI CSI-2 up to
`drivers/video/`, "these calls go to real silicon for free", and closed with "no open tracking
issue exists yet for that follow-up" — both wrong. It now carries a DATA-GATED block, checked
against the pinned Zephyr v4.4.1 and the `hal_renesas` that pin imports, naming four separate
missing facts:

- **No receiver driver.** Zephyr v4.4.1's `drivers/video/` ships no Renesas RZ/V CSI-2 receiver at
  all — `video_renesas_ra_ceu.c` is the RA-family parallel CEU — and `dts/bindings/video/` carries
  CSI-2 receiver bindings only for NXP (`nxp,mipi-csi2rx.yaml`). ADR 0017's consume-upstream rung
  has nothing to consume yet.
- **No register base.** `dts/arm/renesas/rz/rzv/r9a09g056.dtsi` declares no `csi2`/`cru`/`isp`
  node, `hal_renesas`'s rzv2n `bsp_slave_address.h` carries no CRU entry, and
  `metadata/socs/renesas/rzv2n/n44.json`'s `peripheral_instances` block covers i2c/uart/gpt/gtm
  only — so the board generator has no base to emit either. The real value is in the RZ/V2N
  Hardware User's Manual `r01uh1003ej`, CRU + MIPI CSI-2 register chapters.
- **The CM33 interrupt cell is not a datasheet constant.** `hal_renesas`'s rzv2n `bsp_irq_id.h`
  lists `CRU0_CSI2_LINK_INT_IRQSELn = 494` and `CRU1_CSI2_LINK_INT_IRQSELn = 500` in
  `IRQSELn_Type` — IRQSEL *multiplexer selector* numbers. `IRQn_Type`, the enum that actually
  feeds a DT `interrupts` cell, holds no CRU vector at all; it ends at `SEL126_IRQn = 479`. So the
  cell is a free choice of one `SELn` vector plus an IRQSEL programming step no code in this tree
  performs. Contrast `zephyr/boards/alp/e1m_v2n101_m33_sm/alp_e1m_v2n101_m33_sm_r9a09g056n48gbg_cm33.dts`'s
  `mbox1`, whose `interrupts = <293 2>` came straight out of `IRQn_Type` as `MHU_MSG5_NS_IRQn`.
- **No sensor is chosen.** `metadata/boards/e1m-x-evk.yaml` sets `ov5640: false` and names no
  sensor; the E1M-X carrier exposes bare CSI connectors. Without a part there is no compatible, no
  CCI address, no lane count and no link frequency — and the OV5645 pair named in
  `meta-alp-sdk/recipes-kernel/linux/linux-renesas/e1m-x-evk.dtsi`'s header belongs to the Renesas
  EVK, not to this carrier.

The carrier dtsi's one-line `- 2x MIPI-CSI cameras.` TODO grew the same DATA-GATED treatment the
TAS2563 audio entry beside it already had, for the Linux/A55 half. It now records what the carrier
*does* carry — the CAM0 control pads (`XEVK_PIN_CAM0_MUX_SEL` = `E1M_X_GPIO_IO16`,
`XEVK_PIN_CAM0_EN` = `E1M_X_GPIO_IO18`, `XEVK_PIN_CAM0_RST` = `E1M_X_GPIO_IO20`, active-low), the
control buses (`XEVK_I2C_BUS_DSI_CSI0` = `E1M_X_I2C2`, `XEVK_I2C_BUS_DSI_CSI1` = `E1M_X_I2C3`),
and the CRU + ISP DMA pools `meta-alp-sdk/recipes-kernel/linux/linux-renesas/e1m-v2n-som.dtsi`
already reserves (`isp@90000000`, `cru_buffer@b4000000`) — against the four things it does not:
the sensor part; which of the E1M-X edge connector's four CSI instances
(`metadata/e1m/pinout-x-v1.json`, CSI0..CSI3) lands on which of the SoC's two receivers
(`"mipi_csi2": 2`) and on how many lanes, which `metadata/pinmux/v2n.yaml` cannot answer because it
carries no CSI lane row at all; which of the GD32-owned rails in
`metadata/e1m_modules/v2n/gd32-io-mcu-map.csv` (`CAM_EN_LDO0` = `PC3`, `CAM_EN_LDO1` = `PE8`,
`CAM_EN_LDO2` = `PE7`, `CAM_EN_LDO3` = `PE10`) powers which connector; and — for CAM1 specifically
— a Linux I2C master at all, since `E1M_X_I2C3` (`DSI1_CSI_I2C`) terminates on the GD32 IO-MCU
bridge, the same blocker that already defers GT911 touch.

No metadata, schema, Kconfig or CMake changed: the enablement scaffolding was already complete
(`CONFIG_ALP_SDK_CAMERA_V2N_N44_ISP`, `default y if ALP_SOC_RENESAS_RZV2N_N44`, is defined in
`zephyr/kconfigs/power-camera-display.kconfig` and links the backend from `zephyr/CMakeLists.txt`).
Only a sensor decision and the carrier routing are missing, and both are answers, not lookups.

### Added — opt-in Linux MIPI CSI-2 camera path on V2N / V2N-M1, bench-unverified (#1149)

meta-alp-sdk gains an IMX219 + CSI-2 receiver + CRU0 devicetree fragment for
the E1M-X-EVK CAM0 connector, built only when `ALP_ENABLE_CAM0_IMX219 = "1"`
(separate `e1m-v2{n,m}101-x-evk-cam0` dtbs; the default dtb is unchanged).
The sensor is a placeholder and the SoC labels are unverified; nothing has
run on hardware. The Zephyr/CM33 camera backend gap is not addressed. See
`docs/v2n-camera-csi.md`.

### Added — U-Boot reports the SoC reset cause and holds the DX-M1 in reset after a watchdog reset (#1153)

After a SoC-only watchdog reset the peripherals outside the SoC reset domain
kept stale state, and the boot log did not say why the board had restarted.
`meta-alp-sdk/recipes-bsp/u-boot/u-boot/0012-rzv2n-dev-ALP-E1M-reset-cause-and-deepx-reset-hold.patch`
makes `board_late_init()` read `CPG_ERROR_RST2` (`0x10420B40`; bit1 =
WDT_CA55, bit0 = WDT_CM33; RZ/V2N manual R01UH1071EJ0120 Rev.1.20 §4.4.4.15,
and §4.4.6.5.4: it survives an error system reset) before anything else,
print `ALP: reset cause: WDT CA55` / `WDT CM33` / `power-on or software`,
clear the WDT flags, and export the cause as env `alp_reset_cause` and
`/chosen/alp,reset-cause` (`wdt-ca55`, `wdt-cm33`, `wdt-ca55-cm33`,
`por-or-sw`). On a v2n-m1 SoM, a WDT reset also drives M1_RESET (PA6) low
for 10 ms before the existing DEEPX rail / PCIe sequence releases it.

Not done, on purpose: GD32_NRST (P74, shared with PMIC GPIO4, topology
unconfirmed), the Ethernet PHYs and the PMIC are untouched, so a WDT reset
still leaves them in their prior state. The 10 ms hold is a placeholder until
the DEEPX datasheet minimum is confirmed. Bench-verified on E1M-V2M103
(hang injection: `WDT CA55`, DX-M1 held 10 ms, back at 8.0 GT/s x2). A plain
Linux `reboot` also reports `WDT CA55`, because the kernel restarts through
the CA55 watchdog, so `por-or-sw` means power-on only. See
`docs/rzv2n-m33-secure-boot.md` ("Reset cause and watchdog-reset behaviour")
for the test steps. New HIL spec `tests/hil/v2m103-x-evk/v2m103-reset-cause.yaml`.

### Investigated — `metadata/pinmux/v2n.yaml`'s TBD columns confirmed real, with two different causes (#1156)

- `e1m_pad: "TBD"` on all 207 rows is confirmed real, not a bug: the
  E1M-connector edge-ball assignment for RZ/V2N does not exist yet, in this
  repo or the internal metadata repository. Filling it in requires a SoM
  netlist export in the same shape as AEN's `from-alif.tsv`, which has not
  been produced. Left as-is pending that export.
- `e1m_function: "TBD"` on the 145 Renesas-owned rows has a different,
  narrower cause: the internal source TSV carries a third column the public
  one lacks, naming the E1M-standard signal for a subset of rows -- that
  column can populate `e1m_function` for those rows once ingested, but it
  cannot populate `e1m_pad` (it doesn't carry the edge ball either). Left as
  "TBD" pending that ingestion, not blocked on the netlist export above.

### Changed — pinmux `owner` can now name the core that claims a pad, not just the vendor (#1157)

`metadata/pinmux/v2n.yaml` distinguished only `renesas` from `gd32`, so every
RZ/V2N-side pad read `owner: "renesas"` uniformly. V2N is an AMP part: the A55
cluster runs Linux and the CM33 runs Zephyr, and they own different pads. A pad
claimed by one core was therefore invisible to the other's generator, and a
cross-core conflict could only be found on a bench.

That is not hypothetical — `docs/errata-e1m-x-v2n.md:56-111` records the USB
over-current hog regressing when the CM33-owned GD32 supervisor SPI took
`P96`/`SCK7` on 2026-06-03, a collision the metadata had no way to express.

Pads may now carry a `core` alongside `owner`, and the schema enforces the pair:
a row with `core` must have `owner: "renesas"`, since a GD32-side pad has no
RZ/V2N core to attribute. The rule is validated by execution rather than by
reading — mutating the `PA9` row to carry `core: "m33"` produces exactly one
error, and a bogus core value is rejected by the enum.

**Deliberately incomplete, and that is the point.** A core assignment is a
hardware fact per pad, and only the ones this repo establishes are set — `sci7`
(CM33-owned), `gpio9` `P97` (the M33's GD32 chip-select, `..._cm33.dts:110-112`)
and `i2c8`/BRD_I2C (reachable from both, itself the coordination hazard the
issue names). Every other pad is left explicitly unassigned. Guessing an owner
would defeat the purpose of the change, which is to make a conflict a validation
error instead of a bench surprise; a wrong owner produces a confident wrong
answer, which is worse than an honest unknown.

- HIL: E1M-V2M103 `ssh-run` specs for `examples/v2n/v2n-secure-element-sign` (OPTIGA Trust M probe, Coprocessor UID and raw APDU session) and `examples/v2n/v2n-power-monitor` (E1M-X EVK INA236 3V3/1V8/VCAM3 rows). Both pass on E1M-V2M103 silicon (#1160).

- `tests/hil/run_smoke.py` `ssh-run`: the run is now stopped after `serial.duration_s` (an example that loops forever used to hang the runner), and it runs under `ssh -tt` so the stopped example's buffered stdout is not lost (#1160).

- `tests/hil/run_smoke.py` `ssh-run` specs may now carry `ssh_args:` (argv passed to the remote binary) and `ssh_files:` (`{local, remote}` pairs scp'd alongside the binary before it runs) -- an example that takes filename arguments, not just its own binary, previously had no way to get them onto the target. New E1M-V2M103 spec `v2n-drpai-inference.yaml` for `examples/v2n/v2n-drpai-inference` (`<model.tar> <frame0.bin>` argv) documents the expected printouts; not bench-run by this change -- no compiled DRP-AI model bundle exists in-tree yet (#1160, #2236).

New E1M-V2M103 specs `v2n-temp-sensor.yaml` and `v2n-brd-i2c-bringup.yaml` (read-only health check of every on-module BRD_I2C part). - The V2N `v2n-temp-sensor` HIL spec could not run: it targeted the CM33 through `west flash` although the example is an A55 app, and it expected strings (`Alp SDK`, `tmp112`) the example only prints on failure. It now uses `ssh-run` and matches the example's real output.
- `v2n-brd-i2c-bringup` reported the RV-3028 RTC as FAIL (`RTC_RD_TIME: Invalid argument`) on a healthy part. `rtc-rv3028` returns `EINVAL` after reading STATUS over I2C and finding PORF set, so the chip answers but its time is unset. On the E1M-X EVK V2 the RTC's VBACKUP (SoM `VBAT`, pad AQ25 `+S_CAP`) reaches only header P10, so with nothing fitted there the time is lost at every power-off. The row now reads PASS with that explanation.

### Fixed — four HIL spec/runner bugs found by the first V2M103 bench run (#1160)

- **GD32 protocol checks are a floor, not a list.** `v2m103-gd32-bridge-linux`, and `*-gd32-getversion-i2c` for V2M103 and V2N101, hard-coded minor 14 or 15 and failed on a board reporting protocol 0.17.0; they now accept any 0.x with minor >= 14.
- **`ssh_command` goes to `sh -s` on stdin.** Passed as one argv string, Windows `ssh.exe` mangled `$(printf %03o "$v")`-style constructs; `run_smoke.py` now sends the command on stdin.
- **Failed specs print the board output.** The summary showed only the token verdict; it now shows the tail of the captured stdout/stderr.
- **`*-xspi-mtd` no longer passes on an empty read.** BusyBox `head` has no `-c`, so both hashes were md5 of empty input and `HIL_MTD0_STABLE` passed falsely; the specs now read with `dd` and require 4194304 bytes and a non-empty-input hash.
