### Documented — the GD32 bridge HiL soak's quarantine notes still described six rows as skipped, but every row runs active (#1162)

`examples/v2n/v2n-gd32-bridge-hil-soak/src/main.c`'s `tests[]` table has had
every row at `quarantined = false` since the fixes landed, but the comment
block above it and the README's "Quarantine list" section still read as if
`pwm_capture`, `adc_stream`, `qenc`, `tmu`, `ota_get_state` and `trng` were
presently skipped — `adc_stream` most dangerously, since its comment still
described an actively destructive DMA-contention failure mode as "still
quarantined" when the code runs it every cycle.

Both are rewritten to describe what actually happened. Five of the six rows
(`pwm_capture`, `qenc`, `tmu`, `ota_get_state`, `trng`) were never broken HAL
bodies: the `transport_spi.c` slave-cursor rewind bug plus the host masking
every error reply's true status behind `ALP_ERR_IO` made their failures
indistinguishable from real defects, fixed in `2e30b9d09`. `trng` also had a
real hardware fault-latch condition underneath (`TRNG_STAT = 0x48`), now
handled. `adc_stream` was a genuinely separate, genuinely destructive firmware
defect — circular DMA without `CTL1.DDM` plus an unenabled `RCU_DMAMUX`
clock — fixed in `ffdc66ee5`, not merely a transport artefact like the other
five. Both fixes landed 2026-06-04 and were validated 253/253 across a 20-row
soak by 2026-06-06 (`docs/test-plan.md`).

The README's per-test table had drifted the same way, on rows the fixes
above never touched: `adc_stream`'s row still described the pre-fix `>0
samples` DMAMUX regression check instead of the current two-read paced
assertion; `dac`'s row still said `1650 mV` when the setpoint moved to
`600 mV` in `824403359` (jumper-safe under the X-EVK Tier-B bench's ADC0
jumper); `qenc`'s row said the read "reads exactly 0" when the code stopped
asserting a position value once the floating-encoder drift was understood
(round-trip only, value ignored); and `adc_stream_guard` — the fw v0.2.8
converter-ownership guard added in `d1879bcfe` — had no row at all. The
"Reading the output" section's sample log line also still said `19/19 PASS`
for a 20-row table. All four are corrected; the other sixteen rows were
checked against their `t_*` functions and are accurate as written.

No `quarantined` flag or test logic changed — this is a documentation-accuracy
fix only.

### Fixed — the OPTIGA Trust M driver no longer points the next implementer at an upstream Zephyr module that does not exist (#1164)

The Trust M driver has been probe-only since v0.3, and both files that explain
why named the wrong next step. `chips/optiga_trust_m/optiga_trust_m.c` said the
answer was to "vendor the upstream library as a Zephyr module" and sized it at
"~5 KLOC". Neither holds. Infineon's `optiga-trust-m` at `release-v5.8.1` ships
no `zephyr/module.yml` and no library-level CMakeLists, so a west project pin
would be inert for the same reason `vendors/u8g2/README.md:9` ("ships no")
already documents; and its `src/` plus `include/` are 19,777 lines, not five
thousand. The comment now states what consuming it actually costs — vendored
source plus module glue alp-sdk writes itself — and names the two hardware gaps
that bound the work as much as the vendoring does (that comment was
replaced when the host library landed; see `1164-optiga-host-library.md`).

The public header was wrong about the hardware.
`include/alp/chips/optiga_trust_m.h` told the reader the chip "sits on Alif's
LPI2C bus" on E1M-AEN, naming the one family where it is unreachable and
omitting the two where it is populated. AEN's BRD_I2C was believed at the time
to be LPI2C0, where the Alif silicon can only be a slave --
**since corrected by #1848: BRD_I2C is SoC I2C0, master-capable, not LPI2C0**
(`docs/bring-up-aen.md:263` ("so the M55 can master BRD_I2C directly")) -- and
the part is marked `DNI` on the current batch
(`docs/bring-up-aen.md:304` ("DNI on this bench batch")). The chip is populated
on E1M-X V2N / V2M at `0x30` on BRD_I2C with the RZ/V2N as bus master
(`metadata/e1m_modules/E1M-V2N101.yaml:50` ("role: secure_element")). The header
now says so
(`include/alp/chips/optiga_trust_m.h:20-26` ("Populated on E1M-X V2N / V2M")).

Two facts were verified rather than assumed while establishing this, and are
recorded so the vendoring decision can be made without repeating the work.
Licensing is not the blocker: all 57 files under upstream's `src/`, `include/`,
`config/` and `extras/pal/zephyr/` carry a per-file MIT SPDX identifier, and
`MIT` is already on this repo's allowlist at
`metadata/schemas/library-v1.schema.json:35` ("BSD-2-Clause"). And the existing
probe is correct: the register numbers and the four-byte `I2C_STATE` read in
`optiga_trust_m_init()` match upstream's own physical layer, so the probe stays
valid under a real transport.

The in-tree minimal-APDU alternative was costed too, separately from the
vendoring path above. #1164 names two ways off the stub: vendoring Infineon's
host library, costed above, or "an in-tree minimal APDU implementation of the
handful of commands actually needed" — never costed until now. Upstream's
`ifx_i2c_data_link_layer.c` (608 lines, an 11-state retry/resend/ack/nack
machine plus a CRC16 over every frame) and `ifx_i2c_transport_layer.c` (479
lines, cross-frame APDU chaining) are both required before
OpenApplication/CloseApplication (APDU commands `0x70`/`0x71` in upstream's
`src/cmd/optiga_cmd.c`, lines 31 and 33) or any other command APDU can run:
1,087 lines at minimum, hand-derived from the wire spec rather than run against
upstream's tested implementation, for a security element with no silicon in
this dispatch to verify it against even once. `ifx_i2c_presentation_layer.c`
(1086 lines) is not part of that minimum — its entire body is guarded
`#ifdef OPTIGA_COMMS_SHIELDED_CONNECTION`, the optional Shielded Connection
encryption layer, verified against a fresh clone of `release-v5.8.1`.
Vendoring the whole `src/comms/ifx_i2c/` directory instead — the three files
above plus `ifx_i2c_physical_layer.c` (720), `ifx_i2c.c` (315) and
`ifx_i2c_config.c` (140) — totals 3,348 lines, already tested against real
silicon. **Since superseded by `1164-optiga-host-library.md`, same release:** the
host library was vendored (`vendors/optiga-trust-m`) and the driver now
reads the Coprocessor UID and runs raw APDU sessions on silicon, so the
`NOSUPPORT` contract and the deferral recorded in this entry no longer
hold.

### Added

- OPTIGA Trust M now runs Infineon's host library (`vendors/optiga-trust-m`, release-v5.8.3, MIT) through a PAL on the portable `alp_i2c_*` / `alp_uptime_ms` surface, so the same driver serves the A55 and MCU cores. `optiga_trust_m_read_product_info()` returns the 27-byte Coprocessor UID (object `0xE0C2`) and `optiga_trust_m_send_apdu()` runs a raw APDU session; both returned `ALP_ERR_NOSUPPORT` before. Bench, E1M-V2M103 2026W38-0001 (`/dev/i2c-8`, `0x30`): probe, UID read (firmware `80101071`, build `2564`) and a raw OpenApplication + GetDataObject pass 14/14 runs. Read-only: no key or data-object writes; Shielded Connection stays off until binding-secret provisioning is designed.

### Changed

- `optiga_trust_m_product_info_t` now has the real Coprocessor UID layout (`cim_id`, `platform_id`, `model_id`, `rom_mask_id`, `chip_type`, `batch_num`, `x_coord`, `y_coord`, `fw_id[4]`, `esw_build`), replacing a placeholder shape that did not match the chip.

### Fixed

- `optiga_trust_m_init()` could never find a fitted Trust M on silicon: it read `I2C_STATE` with a repeated-start write-read, which the part NACKs every time. It now writes the register address, stops, waits the part's guard time and reads, as upstream's physical layer does, and allows the library's own wake budget (200 tries at 1 ms, `PL_POLLING_MAX_CNT`) instead of 10. The `fake_optiga` emulator now NACKs a repeated start, so the chips suite catches the old form.

### Fixed

- `provision_som.py`'s SoM-presence gate no longer reports the OPTIGA Trust M (`0x30`) as missing on a healthy module. The Trust M NACKs the first I2C access after idle and ACKs one made right after it; one `i2cdetect -r` scan missed it. An expected-but-silent address is now re-probed as wake-then-scan in one shell command, because the part is asleep again by the next SSH round trip. Bench, E1M-V2M103 2026W38-0001: three runs after idle all clean; the old check refused this unit. The `i2cdetect` parser also reads fixed columns now, so a range-limited scan no longer misplaces cells.

### Fixed — ACT88760 Buck5 / Buck6 rail attribution was swapped in the V2N power tree (#1165)

`metadata/e1m_modules/v2n/power-tree.yaml` had `vdd_core_0p75` on
`buck5` and `vdd08_ddr` on `buck6`, both marked TBD-verify and both
inferred only from CMI sequencing timing. Checked 2026-09-25 against the
module design data and a live register read on an E1M-V2M103 (ACT88760
at `0x25` on BRD_I2C): tile `0xC0` (Buck5) reads VSET `0x0C` = 800 mV,
and tile `0xE0` (Buck6) reads VSET `0x0A` = 750 mV. So `VDD08_DDR` is
Buck5 and `VDD_CORE_0P75` is Buck6. The CMI report numbers these two the
other way round, which is how the earlier attribution went wrong.

This was a runtime bug, not only a label: the generated guard table in
`include/alp/chips/v2n_power_tree.h` gave Buck5 a 725–775 mV window and
Buck6 a 775–825 mV window. Both healthy rails therefore read out of
window. The two channels are swapped back, both nets are now named in the
table instead of `TBD`, and the GPIO7 / GPIO10 role text now names Buck6.

Buck6's tile `0xE4` reads `0x3E`: ON bit clear, AUXIN_EN set. The rail
is held up by the PWEN2 sequencer trigger, not by its ON bit, so
`act8760_rail_set_enable()` (which only writes the ON bit) cannot switch
it. That matches `enable_writable: false` for this rail.

### Changed — all 13 ACT88760 rail roles in the V2N power tree are now confirmed against the module schematic (#1165)

The 13 rail roles themselves were filled by the guarded PMIC work (#2483); one
mapping, LDO3 to `VDD_eMMC_3V3`, had been made by elimination and carried a
"confirm against the schematic" note. That is now checked: the LDO3 output
feeds `VDD_eMMC_3V3`, and the seven buck outputs and the other five LDO/load-switch
outputs match the existing `metadata/e1m_modules/v2n/power-tree.yaml` rows
(including the Buck5/Buck6 numbering correction). Only the `evidence:` text
changes; no voltage, window or control value moves.

### Added — Guarded, data-driven readings and control for the V2N-family PMICs: ACT88760, DA9292 and TPS628640 (#1165)

`metadata/e1m_modules/v2n/power-tree.yaml` (new schema
`power-tree-v1`) is now the single source for the V2N / V2N-M1 on-module
power tree. It records every rail's net name (public), target, guard window
(default target +/-5 %, rounded inward to the chip's step), `critical`
flag, control class and owner per boot mode, plus the roles of the eleven
ACT88760 GPIOs. `scripts/gen_power_tree.py` generates
`include/alp/chips/v2n_power_tree.h` from it (`V2N_POWER_*` / `V2N_M1_POWER_*`
brace initialisers, no storage; `--check` for CI). `validate_metadata.py`
cross-checks it against the chip manifests, the SoM presets and
`core-ownership.yaml`.

The three drivers now read everything and control only through that table:

- **Fail-closed.** With no table installed (`act8760_set_limits()`,
  `da9292_set_limits()`, `tps628640_set_limits()`; `*_init()` clears it),
  every control write returns `ALP_ERR_NOSUPPORT`.
- **Window.** A voltage write is encoded in the rail's live range / VSTEP,
  refused with `ALP_ERR_OUT_OF_RANGE` unless the encoded value lies in the
  window, then read back. The ACT88760 compares in µV, so the 12.5 mV LDO
  grid cannot truncate into the window.
- **Critical rails are never disabled.** That covers every ACT88760 rail,
  DA9292 CH1 and TPS628640 `0x4D`. A TPS628640 reset counts as a disable.
- **ACT88760 raw writes** reach only MSTR `0x01`, `0x05`, `0x2B`,
  `0x33`. Everything else is refused: `0x07` (MR / SLEEP / DPSLP / POWER
  OFF / watchdog), `0x09`, `0x0A`, `0x0B` / `0x0C` (IO delays; `0x0C`
  bits1:0 are WDTIME / RETRY TIME), `0x14` (POK_OV / VSYSWARN thresholds --
  a bad value can trip PMIC shutdown, deny until a typed API needs it),
  `0x15`-`0x26`, `0x2D`-`0x32`, every MODEx, every tile register and all
  of ADD2. The DA9292 raw path reaches only `0x02`-`0x05`. The TPS628640
  has no raw write path. No ACT88760 rail on V2N / V2N-M1 is
  enable-writable: every one of them is the PMIC's own CMI hardware
  sequence, not a software on/off switch, so `act8760_rail_set_enable()`
  returns `ALP_ERR_NOSUPPORT` on every rail regardless of `true`/`false`.
  That is a fact about this power tree's installed table, not the driver:
  `act8760_rail_set_enable(true)` itself still refuses
  (`ALP_ERR_OUT_OF_RANGE`) on ANY caller-installed table entry that has
  both `enable_writable` and a window whose live VSET reads outside it,
  the same rule DA9292 / TPS628640 apply.
- **ACT88760 Buck3 / Buck4 range** is decoded from tile +1 bit3 (`0x81` /
  `0xA1`), per the AA82BZ register-map workbook. `metadata/chips/act8760.yaml`
  said `0x86` / `0xA6` bit1, which is DBSTBY: decoding that as the range is
  a 5x setpoint error on `LPD4x_1V1` / `LPDDR_1V8`.
- **ACT88760 GPIOs.** New `act8760_gpio_get()`, toggle peek / clear, and
  `act8760_gpio_set_polarity()` (MODEx bit7 only, GPIO4 `GD32_NRST` only).
  The last one fixes the MODE4 OTP defect (`0x88` -> `0x08`, volatile).
  `act8760_init()` now probes `0x03`, not `0x00`, whose VSYS latches clear
  on read.
- **`da9292_ch2_sequence()`** is the U-Boot `0004` DEEPX rail sequence as an
  OS-agnostic function (caller-opened GPIOs, a delay callback). On top of
  `0004`, it clears CH2_EN before VSTEP, and it propagates a failed event
  clear. After P64 goes high it also requires no CH2 OV / OC in STATUS_00
  and EVENT_00, because the AROVx OTP masks OV out of PG. On a warm reboot
  with CH2 live, it issues zero CTRL_01 writes, and a missing
  `DEEPX_PWR_EN_REQ` leaves the rail and P64 as found. It reports
  PMC_CFG_00 (`0x0E`): the OTP's `0xFF` enables the EN2 / VSEL2 pin
  functions, which bypass every I2C guard.
- **New bench tool:** `examples/v2n/v2n-pmic-inspect` (A55 / Linux). It is
  read-only unless you pass `--write`, and it refuses single-rail disables
  of DEEPX rails.

**ABI.** Removed: `da9292_v2n_base_init()`, `da9292_v2n_m1_enable_deepx_rail()`,
`act8760_rail_set_vset()`, `tps628640_write_reg()`. Added: the three
`*_set_limits()`, `act8760_rail_get_state()` / `_get_voltage_mv()` /
`_set_voltage_mv()` / `_set_enable()`, `act8760_gpio_get()` /
`_toggles_peek()` / `_toggles_clear()` / `_set_polarity()`,
`da9292_get_identity()` / `_get_channel_state()` / `_peek_events()` /
`_ch2_sequence()`, `<alp/chips/pmic_rail_limit.h>` and
`<alp/chips/v2n_power_tree.h>`. Changed: `da9292_set_voltage_mv()` encodes
for the live VSTEP and writes both VSEL registers; `da9292_get_voltage_mv()`
decodes the active VSEL; `da9292_read_and_clear_events()` does not clear
without a table; `tps628640_software_enable(true)` now refuses
(`ALP_ERR_OUT_OF_RANGE`) unless the live VOUT1 *and* VOUT2 setpoints both
lie inside the installed window (the VID strap picks which one is live and
the driver can't read it), instead of blindly energizing whatever is
currently programmed; `tps628640_reset_to_defaults()` now preserves the
caller's FPWM-mode and ramp-speed bits across the chip's own factory reset
instead of silently dropping them to the datasheet default, and -- since
the chip's own reset always re-enables the converter regardless of what
this driver wants -- re-checks VOUT1/VOUT2 against the window and the
rail's prior enable state once the reset lands: it clears SOFTWARE_ENABLE
again and reports `ALP_ERR_OUT_OF_RANGE` when the post-reset setpoint is
out of window, and it also clears SOFTWARE_ENABLE (no error) when the rail
was simply off before the call, so a reset can never spring a
previously-disabled rail back to life. The v2n-pmic-inspect example app has not run on silicon yet.

### Removed — the TAS2562 kernel codec driver was enabled on V2N/V2M with no device-tree node to bind to (#1171)

`meta-alp-sdk/recipes-kernel/linux/linux-renesas/tas2563-audio.cfg` set
`CONFIG_SND_SOC_TAS2562=y` for `e1m-v2m101` and `e1m-v2n101`, pre-staging the
mainline ASoC driver that covers the carrier's two TAS2563 smart amps. Nothing
instantiated it. Each of those machines builds exactly one device tree —
`KERNEL_DEVICETREE = "renesas/e1m-v2n101-x-evk.dtb"` and
`"renesas/e1m-v2m101-x-evk.dtb"`, with V2N102/V2M102 reusing the V2N101 one —
and no `compatible` string starting `ti,tas` appears in any `.dts`/`.dtsi`
under `meta-alp-sdk/recipes-kernel/linux/linux-renesas/`. The fragment's own
comment admitted it: the driver "loads with no DT consumer (harmless no-op)".

The fragment and its two `SRC_URI:append` lines are gone. The BSP defconfig
(linux-renesas 6.1.141-cip43) does not set the symbol, so removing the
fragment returns the kernel to not-built rather than needing an explicit `=n`.
`display.cfg`, `trim-unused-storage-net-fs.cfg` and `no-kernel-audit.cfg` are
untouched.

Everything the fragment knew is now in the audio TODO block at the top of
`meta-alp-sdk/recipes-kernel/linux/linux-renesas/e1m-x-evk.dtsi`, where the
implementer of the codec nodes will be reading, together with one fact that
was not recorded anywhere: landing a kernel codec node claims I2C `0x4D`/`0x4E`
away from the SDK's own userspace `chips/tas2563` driver, which reaches those
addresses over `alp_i2c_*`. That ownership call has to be made in the same
change as the nodes, not discovered afterwards.

### Notes — the missing SSIU/I2S device-tree node on V2N/V2M stays data-gated (#1171)

The other half of #1171 — no SSI/SSIU node on either core, so
`<alp/i2s.h>` falls through to `src/common/stub/stub_i2s.c` and returns
`ALP_ERR_NOSUPPORT` (lines 22, 28, 33, 41, 50) — is **not** fixable from this
repo, and no node was written.

On the Cortex-M33 side the blocker is upstream: Zephyr v4.4.0's
`dts/arm/renesas/rz/rzv/r9a09g056.dtsi`, which the generated M33 board trees
include, contains no SSI or I2S node at all, and the tree's only Renesas I2S
driver is `drivers/i2s/i2s_renesas_ra_ssie.c` behind the
`renesas,ra-i2s-ssie` binding — the RA-family SSIE, not the RZ/V SSIU+SSI. A
node here would need a new driver plus a fabricated register base, interrupt
and clock.

On the Linux side four SoC-side values are absent from this repo: the SSI/SSIU
node label the linux-renesas 6.1.141-cip43 `r9a09g056` dtsi exposes, its
binding (a comment in `e1m-x-evk.dtsi` said `rcar_sound`, an R-Car binding,
unverified for this SoC — now marked as such), the PFC function for the SSIU
pads, and the MCLK source and rate. The pad routing is not assigned either:
`metadata/pinmux/v2n.yaml:126-133` still carries `e1m_pad: "TBD"` and
`e1m_function: "TBD"` on all eight SSIU rows (`SSIU1_SSI1_SCK` on `P44`
through `SSIU4_SSI4_SDATA` on `P15`), and
`metadata/e1m_modules/E1M-V2N101.yaml:190-191` declares both `i2s0` and `i2s1`
with `driver_status: none`. Generating DT/pinctrl from that layer is #655.

The catalog's `peripherals.i2s: true` is left alone: it is derived from
`metadata/socs/renesas/rzv2n/n44.json:62` (`: 10,`), a silicon fact that
is true whether or not a driver binds. Narrowing it to a
driver-availability claim is a catalog-semantics change across every SKU and
peripheral, not a V2N audio fix.

### Documented — the customer onramp's last stale tan-cli version pin, re-verified against the shipped Python `tan` (#1191)

#1191 tracked the Rust-era Quickstart being unexecutable against Python `tan`.
Most of that surface was already fixed by earlier, unrelated PRs by the time
this landed: `README.md`, `AGENTS.md`, `llms.txt`, `pyproject.toml`,
`metadata/bootstrap.json`, `metadata/schemas/bootstrap-v1.schema.json`,
`metadata/schemas/build-plan-v1.schema.json` and `scripts/alp_cli/doctor.py`
(the last one retired outright) no longer mention `--non-interactive` as
unsupported, `tan sdk switch`, Rust/`cargo install`/`rustup`, or a `doctor
--build` check-set distinction — all re-measured here against a real,
installed `tan 0.6.0` (`pip install ./python` from the `alplabai/tan-cli`
`v0.6.0` tag into a clean Python 3.12 venv), not inferred from source or an
older doc:

- `tan init --name my-app --sdk-root <sdk> --non-interactive` → `rc=0`,
  scaffolds the project (the flag is accepted and dropped, not declared).
- `tan sdk switch some-version` → `rc=1`, `sdk.not-ported`, directs the
  caller to `--sdk-root`.
- `tan validate --sdk-root <sdk>` (no `--offline`) → `validate: ./board.yaml
  is clean`, `rc=0`.
- `tan doctor` vs `tan doctor --build` against the same project → both report
  the identical 14 checks (11 passed, 2 warning, 1 failed).
- `tan emit zephyr-conf` → `No such command 'emit'` (`rc=2`); `tan generate
  --target zephyr-conf` is the real front door and wrote its target.

What was still stale: `docs/cli.md`, `docs/getting-started.md`,
`docs/firmware-quickstart.md`, and `docs/cross-platform-setup.md` each named
`v0.5.1` as tan-cli's "current release" and described the interactive
`doctor --fix` sudo-elevation behaviour as landing in a future `v0.6.0-rc1+` —
tan-cli tagged `v0.6.0` on 2026-08-24 (which also removed `tan renode` and
its 27 `renode.*` issue codes, and raised its own alp-sdk floor to `v0.16.0`,
matching this repo's `pyproject.toml` version). All four now cite
[`v0.6.0`](https://github.com/alplabai/tan-cli/releases/tag/v0.6.0) as
current, and the `--fix` paragraphs read "as of tan v0.6.0" rather than a
still-pending `dev`-ahead-of-release framing — re-verified live: `tan doctor
--fix` outside a TTY prints `warning: --fix was requested but not run: no
interactive terminal`, matching the documented behaviour exactly.

Not attempted here: a real hardware build/flash artifact and a CI job
running this onramp end to end (issue #1191's last two checklist items) —
out of scope for a documentation-only pass; tracked for a follow-up.

### Fixed — the U-Boot bootcmd hardcoded the V2N dtb and let a failed kernel load boot a stale image (#1252, #1302)

Two failures in `CONFIG_BOOTCOMMAND`
(`meta-alp-sdk/recipes-bsp/u-boot/u-boot/0002-rzv2n-dev-ALP-E1M-production-boot.patch`),
both of which present as a successful boot:

**The dtb was a literal (#1252).** `boot/e1m-v2n101-x-evk.dtb` was loaded on both
the SD and eMMC branches. V2M MACHINEs build `renesas/e1m-v2m101-x-evk.dtb`
(`meta-alp-sdk/conf/machine/e1m-v2m101-a55.conf:58`,
`meta-alp-sdk/conf/machine/e1m-v2m102-a55.conf:60`), so every V2M
image asked for a filename it does not contain — and each of those machine confs
already carried the note "the U-Boot bootcmd must load this filename (set
fdtfile)". The name is now `CONFIG_ALP_E1M_FDTFILE`, a Kconfig string defaulting
to the V2N basename, overridden for the V2M MACHINEs by `fdtfile-v2m.cfg`
through the same `*.cfg` channel `prod-boot.cfg` uses. This is the mechanism the
patch's own comment specified as the fix; that comment is updated rather than
left describing the work as future.

The override is scoped per MACHINE and not to `rzv2n-family`, because the family
override covers the V2N SKUs too and would invert the bug. A new V2M MACHINE
needs its own line — "which dtb does this image contain" is a per-MACHINE fact
(`KERNEL_DEVICETREE`), and no wildcard is safe.

**The loads were non-fatal (#1302).** Every load was `;`-chained, so a missing
kernel `Image` or dtb left whatever those addresses already held and
`run bootimage` booted it. Cold, that is garbage. Warm, it is the *previous*
boot's image — which looks like a successful boot of the wrong software, and is
the worse of the two. Both loads are now re-issued with `&&`, `bootimage` runs
only if both landed, and the failure branch prints what could not be loaded and
stops at the prompt.

`Image` is re-loaded even though `bootcmd_check`'s vendor `sd2load`/`emmcload`
already tried, because those envs are rewritten by vendor feature layers
(`meta-rz-drpai`, `meta-rz-opencva`) and cannot be relied on to fail loudly. Same
address and mmc spec, so it is a no-op when the vendor path worked.

**Bench-gated.** This changes a production boot path and has not been booted on
silicon. The new failure mode is a U-Boot prompt rather than a wrong-image boot —
recoverable over serial, not a brick — but a real boot on a V2N and a V2M module
is owed before this is trusted.

### Added — opt-in KleidiAI execution provider for the ONNX Runtime recipe (#1258)

`meta-alp-sdk`'s `onnxruntime_1.28.0.bb` gains `PACKAGECONFIG[kleidiai]`, which
maps to `-Donnxruntime_USE_KLEIDIAI=ON` and points ORT's `FetchContent` at a
KleidiAI `v1.20.0` archive staged in `SRC_URI` (the tag ORT's own `cmake/deps.txt`
pins, sha1 identical), so the build stays offline. Enable it with
`PACKAGECONFIG:append:pn-onnxruntime = " kleidiai"`; ORT itself turns the option
off with a warning on a non-aarch64 target.

The knob is **off by default**. The issue asks for a measured win, and no
before/after on real `E1M-V2N101` silicon exists yet, so shipping it on would
put an unmeasured perf claim in every image. Nothing here is a build claim: the
change is recipe-only and awaits a `bitbake onnxruntime` pass with the knob on.

### Added -- ONNX Runtime CPU floor enabled for the V2M and V2N images (#1259)

`alp-sdk` gains an `ort` PACKAGECONFIG (`-DALP_SDK_USE_ORT_CPU=ON
-DALP_SDK_ORT_REQUIRED=ON`, depends on the layer's own `onnxruntime` recipe)
that the V2M101/V2M102/V2M103/V2N101/V2N102/V2N103 MACHINE confs switch on
with `ALP_ENABLE_ORT_CPU`. On V2M the default is `0` while the DEEPX runtime
is on, because dx-rt already installs its own `libonnxruntime` 1.20.1 and the
layer's 1.28.0 would collide; set `1` to force it. `resolve_auto()` still
orders CPU last. Silicon passes per SKU are still owed.

### Changed — the DEEPX DX-M1 inference backend is verified on silicon (#1262)

`src/yocto/inference_deepx.cpp` has been run on real hardware for the first
time: an E1M-V2M103 with DEEPX dx-rt 3.2.0, driver 1.8.0 and DX-M1 FW 2.4.0,
driving a yolo11n `.dxnn` through `<alp/inference.h>`. Results:
- Open works under both `DEEPX_DXM1` and `AUTO`; AUTO selects DEEPX, and the
  two produce bit-identical outputs.
- 50/50 invokes succeed at a mean of 46.93 ms.
- `alp_inference_close()` against an in-flight `invoke()` drains cleanly in
  20/20 rounds, and the next invoke returns `ALP_ERR_NOT_READY`.

The status in `docs/test-plan.md`, `<alp/inference.h>`, the backend header,
`src/yocto/CMakeLists.txt`, the alp-sdk recipe and `docs/os-support-matrix.md`
moves from bench-unverified to verified. Output parity: for a real VOC image,
the decoded `[84, 8400]` output matches ONNX Runtime CPU on the same
`yolo11n.onnx`:
- box correlation 0.9997 and class-score correlation 0.9946;
- the same top detection (class 4 at 0.868 on the NPU, 0.854 on the CPU);
- 10/10 identical anchors above 0.5 confidence.

### Fixed — `ALP_DEEPX_DXRT_HOME` works with a Yocto SDK toolchain file (#1262)

Every Yocto SDK toolchain file sets `CMAKE_FIND_ROOT_PATH_MODE_LIBRARY=ONLY`,
which re-rooted `find_library(... PATHS $ENV{ALP_DEEPX_DXRT_HOME}/lib)` into
the sysroot. A cross build with `ALP_SDK_DEEPX_REQUIRED=ON` therefore always
failed to find `libdxrt`. The lookup now passes `NO_CMAKE_FIND_ROOT_PATH`. The
comment also notes that `<root>/lib/include` must be the installed dx-rt
headers: a dx_rt source clone has no build-generated `dxrt/gen.h`.

### Changed — the DRP-AI3 backend has run on silicon (#1268)

On an E1M-V2M103 (board #1), with the `&drpai0` override applied by hand to
the board DTB and `src/yocto/inference_drpai.cpp` cross-built against the real
MERA2 runtime, YOLOX-S/VOC ran through `<alp/inference.h>`:
- `open()` works under `DRPAI` and `AUTO`, and `invoke()` takes ~40 ms per
  640x640 frame.
- Outputs match the compiler's interpreter reference (correlation 0.996-0.998).
- A VOC-calibrated bundle detects an aeroplane photo as aeroplane at 0.519,
  against 0.525 from ONNX Runtime CPU on the same input.

`docs/bring-up-drpai-v2n.md`'s status banner and the stale "never run on
DRP-AI silicon" comments are updated. A baked `alp-image-edge` doing the same
on its own is still to be confirmed.

### Fixed — `examples/peripheral-io/i2c-master` opened `BOARD_I2C_SENSORS` and expected TMP112, which isn't on that bus (#1269)

The example pinned `E1M_I2C0`/`E1M_X_I2C0` (`BOARD_I2C_SENSORS`) in `board.yaml` and probed for a
TMP112 at 0x48 in `src/main.c`. TMP112 is populated on every AEN/V2N/V2N-M1 SoM per
`metadata/chips/tmp112.yaml`, but on `BRD_I2C`, not on `BOARD_I2C_SENSORS` — neither
`metadata/boards/e1m-evk.yaml` nor `metadata/boards/e1m-x-evk.yaml` lists a TMP112 in the
`i2c_devices:` block for the sensor bus this example opens. A customer running the example on
real E1M/E1M-X EVK hardware got an I2C NACK, never a temperature reading.

Repointing the bus instead of the chip was not an option that works for both boards this example
claims to support: `BRD_I2C` is a different physical controller from `BOARD_I2C_SENSORS` on both
families regardless (on the E1M-AEN family it is SoC I2C0, function C — see #1848), and no example
wired a portable `alp_i2c` bus to it at the time, so there was no portable master path to a TMP112
there yet.

The example now reads the BMP581 barometer instead, which *is* populated on `BOARD_I2C_SENSORS`
at 0x47 on both the E1M EVK (U14) and the E1M-X EVK, per each board's `i2c_devices:` metadata —
keeping the example a working demonstration on every board it claims to support.
`examples/v2n/v2n-temp-sensor` remains the correct, V2N-only pattern for reading TMP112 over
`BRD_I2C`.

### Fixed — `board.schema.json`'s `cores.<id>.app` description omitted the parent-directory fallback (#1294)

`$defs/core_entry/properties/app` said `os: zephyr` requires `app:` to itself contain
`prj.conf` or `CMakeLists.txt`, with no mention of the convention 93 of 98 zephyr example
core entries actually rely on: pointing `app:` at a sources-only subdirectory (e.g. `./src`)
and letting `alp_orchestrate.orchestrator._zephyr_app_dir` fall back to that directory's
parent CMakeLists.txt. The description now states both supported `os: zephyr` conventions
(self-contained app dir, or sources dir with parent fallback) and that `os: baremetal` has
no such fallback. Documentation only -- no validation or runtime behaviour changed.

### Changed — ADR 0026 accepted, with its migration re-scoped: the deletion unit was wrong and would have removed the SDK's refusal to build an unsupported hardware revision (#1341)

ADR 0026 ("Tan owns the planner. alp-sdk stops producing plans.") moves from
`Proposed` to `Accepted`. The decision, its five clauses, the measurement that
motivated them and the rejected alternatives all stand — reading both repos
before executing it strengthened the case rather than weakening it. What did not
survive review is the Migration section.

**Step 3 was not executable as written.** It said to delete
`scripts/alp_orchestrate/` "with `git grep` evidence that nothing references it".
That evidence cannot be produced: the directory is not the planner. It is
simultaneously the planner, the per-slice config emitters, and the `board.yaml`
loader the rest of the SDK imports as a library. `scripts/alp_project.py:179-186`
and `:224-230` (measured at `00627b88`) import `load_board_yaml`, `emit_system_manifest`,
`emit_ipc_contract_h`, `emit_dts_reservations`, `emit_os_topology`,
`_slice_alp_conf`, `_slice_cmake_args` and `_slice_local_conf` from it;
`metadata/emit-registry-v1.json` names its modules as the `owner.module` for
twelve of the twenty emit modes; sixteen `check_*.py` gates import it.

**And the deletion would have removed the SDK's refusal to build an unsupported
hardware revision.**
`SdkRevisionUnknown` / `SdkRevisionNotBuildable` / `SdkRevisionUnsupported` come
from `alp_orchestrate.models`, are raised inside the directory step 3 proposed
to delete (`scripts/alp_orchestrate/loader.py:653,660,702,709,749`, reached from
`load_board_yaml` at `:1238-1260` on every emit), and are imported from outside
it by `scripts/validate_board_yaml.py:21` and
`scripts/gen_catalog.py:93,340,353-359`.
That chain is the SDK declining to build a hardware revision it does not support
rather than producing an image for it. Worse, `validate_board_yaml.py` is the
script **tan itself spawns** on the default `tan validate` path
(tan-cli at `b9aa697`, `python/tan/commands/validate_cmd.py:319`, whose
`subprocess.run` call is `:1508-1519`), so a naive `rm -rf` would break tan's own
default validate path after tan had become the only CLI.

The amendment replaces steps 2-4 with a six-step sequence whose order is
load-bearing, inserting the split step the ADR was missing (separate the planner
axis from the emitter/loader core, keeping the revision gate) before any
deletion. It also records four things the Migration section never decided: who
answers the configure-time `alp_project.py --emit zephyr-conf --core <id>` call
that scaffolded and example `CMakeLists.txt` make (repointing it at `tan` would
make tan a hard dependency of every user project build, including a plain `west
build`, and reaches projects already shipped); who owns rendered-artefact bytes
now that clause 4 retires the parity axis without retiring the duplicated
renderers; where the surviving oracle checks live, since `parity-seam1.yml` diffs
the frozen oracle against a **live SDK emit** and is dead by construction once
the SDK cannot emit; and what `sdkVersion` / `sdkCommit` mean once tan is the
emitter.

Two measured facts also correct the ADR's own text. A cross-repo audit found that
of the 20 `--emit` modes, 19 are re-implemented in tan against alp-sdk's raw
metadata and one (`scaffold`) is a byte-for-byte vendored snapshot — none is
consumed as a schema-validated envelope, so the duplication clause 4 leaves
unpoliced is wider than the planner. And clause 4's second bullet, which
preserves "the frozen `crates/` oracle axis, until `crates/` is deleted on its own
schedule", is already stale: `tan-cli` at `b9aa697` has no top-level `crates/`.
Both implementations are Python, so no language-boundary argument for keeping two
remains.

Finally, the parity axis may be **deleted** rather than merely disabled only once
the second producer exists in no alp-sdk release that tan's supported-version
floor still accepts — until then, an old SDK with a new tan has two producers
again and no gate.

Two consequences of the acceptance are recorded with it. The replacement step 3's
exit condition is **not** "`git grep alp_orchestrate` returns only history and
CHANGELOG" -- that names 263 tracked files on `dev` (`west.yml`,
`include/alp/rpc.h`, `src/zephyr/alp_banner.c`, `zephyr/kconfigs/core.kconfig`,
`meta-alp-sdk/conf/machine/*.conf`) and contradicts the split's own premise that
the emitter/loader core survives; it is instead "no module outside the surviving
core imports `alp_orchestrate`, and `metadata/emit-registry-v1.json` names no
doomed-axis module as an `owner`". And ADR 0027 clause 5 offers to "implement it
once in tan and skip the port" **if 0026 is accepted first** -- 0026 is now
accepted but not executed, so 0027 clause 3's reserved-band refusal still has to
land on both sides for the whole migration window. Skipping it would diverge a
hardware refusal across two producers, the class 0026 exists to close.

Docs only; no code, schema or metadata change.

### Documented — `helper_firmware` said the GD32 bridge was covered by "the customer's flash flow"; it is factory-programmed by Alp Lab (#1349)

`metadata/e1m_modules/E1M-V2N101.yaml`'s `helper_firmware:` header comment said
`gd32_bridge` was registered into the system manifest "so the customer's flash
flow covers them." That is the opposite of the product decision (maintainer,
2026-08-09: *"Gd32 is not a customer path. It should be programmed by us at the
factory and we should supply the api interface details to the customers."*) and
of the entry's own body, which already documented the factory-programmed,
`flash_policy: recovery_only` reality in detail.

Nothing behavioural changes: `firmware_path` was already deliberately absent, so
`tan flash` already declines this helper cleanly rather than spawning a flasher
against a nonexistent path (`python/tan/core/flash_plan.py::helper_flash_gate`).
Only the stale framing comment is corrected, to say the registration is for
Alp Lab's factory/production flash flow and that customers are given the
bridge's command-frame API (SPI + I2C, `docs/gd32-bridge.md`), not a way to
reflash it. `E1M-V2N102.yaml`, `E1M-V2M101.yaml`, and `E1M-V2M102.yaml` never
carried this comment — only `E1M-V2N101.yaml` did.

`alp.lock`'s `digests.metadata` regenerated to match.

Not addressed here: the issue's optional suggestion of an explicit
`audience: factory` field on `helper_firmware` entries so tooling can
distinguish factory-only helpers mechanically instead of by prose. That is a
schema change the issue itself flags as "worth discussing" rather than a
straightforward correction, and is left for a maintainer call.

### Fixed — `gen_zephyr_board`'s `zephyr_peripherals_dtsi` refusal blamed the customer for the SDK's vintage (#1354)

`_aen_peripherals_dtsi()` runs before `_aen_flash_partitions()` in `_aen_dts()`, and `atoc`
(#1289) predates `zephyr_peripherals_dtsi` (#1352), so every checkout that carries the newer
field also carries the older region — `_aen_missing_region_message()`'s carefully-worded `atoc`
vintage branch added by #1352 could never actually fire on a real checkout. The message that
DID fire, for an E8 SoC JSON missing `zephyr_peripherals_dtsi`, told the reader to hand-author
`zephyr/dts/alif/ensemble_e8_peripherals.dtsi` and declare it in the SoC JSON — even though that
64+ KiB overlay already ships in every checkout old enough to be missing the key, because the
overlay predates the key that names it. The consumer was sent to author a file already sitting
in their own tree.

`_aen_peripherals_dtsi()` now distinguishes the two cases the way `_aen_missing_region_message()`
already does for `atoc`: when the key is absent, the SoC is `alif:ensemble:e8`, and
`zephyr/dts/alif/ensemble_e8_peripherals.dtsi` is already present in the checkout, the refusal
names the real cause (this alp-sdk predates #1352) and the real fix (upgrade alp-sdk) instead of
telling the reader to recreate a file they already have. Any other missing-key shape (a
genuinely new Ensemble part with no overlay yet) still gets the original authoring-gap message
unchanged — that refusal is correct and #1352's real point.

Both vintage messages (`atoc` and `zephyr_peripherals_dtsi`) also named an unreleased commit and
said "upgrade alp-sdk to a release that includes it," which no tag could satisfy — no published
tag contained either commit at the time #1352 shipped. `v0.16.0-rc1` is factually the first
published tag that contains both commits, but both messages now name **v0.16.0** as the floor,
with rc1 called out parenthetically as the earliest containing tag: rc1 is a GitHub `Pre-release`,
so the upgrade paths a reader actually follows (`gh release` "latest", a manifest/west bump to a
released tag) skip it and would leave the message pointing at a target normal tooling never lands
on. The "would otherwise tell a reader already on the rc to upgrade further" concern this
changelog previously gave for preferring rc1 does not arise in practice — a checkout at rc1
already carries both commits, so neither vintage branch can fire on it, and the `--metadata-root`
scenario this whole fix is about only ever presents a *pre-rc1* tree (one missing the key), so GA
never over-advises there either.

The `zephyr_peripherals_dtsi` vintage probe also checked the file next to the running script's
own checkout (`REPO`), not the tree the SoC JSON in question was actually loaded from
(`metadata_root`). Those differ under `--metadata-root`, and on the SDK's own default invocation
the vintage branch was provably unreachable — #1352 added the branch and the
`zephyr_peripherals_dtsi` key in the same commit, so no default checkout can have the key absent
while running code that already knows to look for it. The probe reads from
`metadata_root.parent / "zephyr" / "dts" / ...` for the `.is_file()` check, and the raised message
now interpolates that same real path plus the SoC-JSON's actual location (the `soc_json_rel`
idiom `emit_zephyr_board` already uses) instead of two hardcoded repo-relative strings — round one
fixed the probe's read, round two fixed what the message it raises actually says.

`scripts/alp_project_loader.py`'s `_resolve_sku()` — reachable from this same
`--metadata-root` path (`emit_zephyr_board` → `_resolve_sku`) — had an unguarded
`preset_path.relative_to(REPO)` that raised a raw `ValueError` instead of the intended
diagnostic when `metadata_root` sat outside the repo checkout. Its sibling `_resolve_board`
already carried the `is_relative_to(REPO)` guard; `_resolve_sku` now matches it. Same defect
class as the closed #1485.

### Added — declare the on-die flash aperture and each memory region's write authority (#1365, split A)

Two optional metadata fields, authored data only: `soc_spec-v1`'s
`soc_flash_base` (the base address of the on-die non-volatile aperture --
`2147483648` / `0x80000000` on `metadata/socs/alif/ensemble/e3.json`..
`e8.json`) and `som-preset-v1`'s `memory_map[].write_authority` (WHO may
write a region: `customer_image`, `vendor_image`, `customer_runtime`,
`secure_enclave`, `none`, or `composite`), authored on all seven rows of
every AEN preset that declares a `memory_map:` --
`metadata/e1m_modules/E1M-AEN{301,401,501,601,701,801,803}.yaml`, seven
presets, 49 rows. (AEN803 landed on `dev` while this branch was open and is
the SKU currently on the bench; a new AEN SoM whose author omits the field
now fails `validate_metadata.py` instead of shipping, which is the whole
point of the gate.)

This exists to close a real hazard, found on the bench and previously
distinguishable only in a prose comment: `storage` (`0x80560000`, 96 KiB)
and `atoc` (`0x80578000`, 32 KiB) were the same shape in the data --
same `carveout: false`, no other differentiator -- even though one is
customer-mountable at runtime and the other is written by the Secure
Enclave at provisioning, and corrupting the latter can leave the part
unbootable. Bench-observed 2026-08-08: ATOC magic `ckBS` (`0x53426B63`)
read back **intact** at `0x8057EA50` while an app erased `0x80560000`,
which at that time fell inside the SAME `storage` partition -- an erase
of customer storage could reach the boot table, because one partition
spanned both. `atoc` has had its own declared region since; what was
still missing, and is what this change adds, is any machine-readable
statement of the difference between the two.

**Split A changes no allocator behaviour and no emitted bytes.** Both
fields are additive metadata; `scripts/alp_orchestrate/carveout.py`'s
`resolve_carve_outs()` still reads only `carveout:`, and no DTS,
partition table, or other generated artefact moves. `write_authority`
exists so the flash/RAM class can be derived and gated against
`carveout:` in CI (split B), not to change what the allocator does
today.

`mram_main`'s `base:` is deliberately left as the literal string `"TBD"`
and is NOT filled by this change. It is the whole-window alias over the
six fine-grained regions above (`write_authority: composite`), it is the
only authored row on E1M-AEN501/601/701/801 that lists `a32_cluster`, and
it carries no `carveout:` key at all -- and `resolve_carve_outs()` treats
an absent `carveout:` as eligible (`scripts/alp_orchestrate/carveout.py`
reads `if region.get("carveout") is False:`). The unresolved base is
therefore the only thing standing between the allocator and that window
today: the allocator seeds each region's high-water mark from
`base + size` alone and allocates **top-down**, with no knowledge that
six sibling partitions live inside the same extent, so an `ipc:` entry
naming an `a32_cluster` endpoint would place its first carve-out at the
TOP of the window -- inside `atoc` at `0x80578000`..`0x80580000`.

Filling that base is safe only once split B's derived-flash-class
refusal exists to reject the region first. The order is: **derived-kind
refusal first, then the base fill.** Never the reverse.

### Added — `system-manifest-v1` now EMITS `memory[]`, and its rows are typed (#1365 item 3)

The `memory[]` contract landed ahead of its producer in split C (`2fd04541`,
#1984) with `items` left as `{required: ["name"], additionalProperties: true}`
— every other field prose-declared only. Both halves close here, in one diff,
because the order matters: typing a row is free while nothing emits it and
breaking once something does.

**The producer.** `scripts/alp_orchestrate/memory.py`'s `resolve_memory_regions()`
projects `alp_project.resolve_memory_map()`'s effective table into the pane,
alongside the existing `resolve_carve_outs` / `resolve_storage_partitions`
calls in `emit_system_manifest()`. Four of the committed emit snapshots grow a
`memory:` block; the other 33 `--emit` surfaces stay byte-identical.

The key is **OMITTED, never emitted empty**. A SoM that resolves no regions at
all (an unresolvable `silicon_variant`, e.g. NX9101's `TBD`) carries no
`memory:` key, so an absent pane still means "producer older than this change,
or a layout still pending" — never "this SoM has no memory regions". Emitting
`memory: []` would have collapsed exactly the distinction split C's own text
drew.

**Three vocabularies, taken from the shipped derivation rather than from
#1365's issue body**, which predates splits A and B and proposes shapes the
code cannot fill:

- `kind` is `aperture.classify_region()`'s four verdicts verbatim — `flash`,
  `ram`, `unclassified`, `unresolved` — not the issue's two. The two extra
  values exist precisely to say *not proven*: `unclassified` is
  outside-the-aperture AND preset-authored (containment is ONE-DIRECTIONAL, so
  outside proves nothing — an Ensemble OSPI XIP window is outside and still
  flash), and `unresolved` covers both "no extent" and "this SoC declares no
  aperture", which is every non-Alif SoM. A 2-value enum would have to fold one
  of them into `ram`, asserting a class the deriver never returned.
- the authority field is `write_authority` with som-preset-v1's six values,
  passed through verbatim, not the issue's 3-value `owner`. One axis cannot
  separate flash-time from runtime authority: `customer_image` and
  `customer_runtime` would both collapse onto `customer`, which is the exact
  `he_slot0`-vs-`storage` distinction the vocabulary was widened to draw
  (#1365 review). A row that authors none carries no key — absent means
  unresolved, never `customer_runtime` (ADR-0034 clause 4).
- `status` is `ok` / `unresolved`, the word this schema's items description
  already made normative, not `ipc[]`'s `ok` / `blocked`. They are not
  synonyms: `blocked` is a verdict on an allocation request; a region either
  resolved an address or did not.

`status` keys off the **base**, not off the extent, because the schema's rule
is written about `base`. Size resolves independently: AEN's `mram_main` emits
`size_bytes: 5767168` alongside `status: unresolved` and no `base`, with a
`reason` naming the field to declare — `base: TBD` is a placeholder, and
ADR-0034 clause 4 forbids guessing past it.

**`source`** — the field an IDE derives editability from (`alp-sdk-vscode#484`)
— is `som_preset` or `soc_derived`, derived in the emitter rather than tagged
inside `resolve_memory_map()`. That function's precedence is ALL-OR-NOTHING (an
authored `memory_map:` wins the whole table), so provenance is a property of
the table, not of a row; `carveout.py` and `partition.py` already read it the
same way via `bool(som_preset.get("memory_map"))`. Tagging rows in the loader
would also have added a key to dicts that flow into `$defs/memory_region`'s
`additionalProperties: false` validation path. The issue's third value,
`board_yaml`, is dropped as having no producer: board.yaml never AUTHORS a
region, it only NAMES one.

**`dt_label` is deliberately not carried.** #1556 allows it only when verified
against the board `.dts`, and this emitter has no access to that verification,
so emitting it would ship exactly the name-derived fallback the rule forbids.
The schema now says so instead of imposing a rule on a field it does not
declare.

**The row invariant is enforced, not described.** `status: ok` with no `base`,
`status: unresolved` with no `reason`, and `status: unresolved` carrying a
`base` were all schema-legal while that rule lived in the items description —
the same "prose nothing checks" shape typing this pane exists to end. An
`if`/`then`/`else` on `memory[].items` now refuses all three, verified against
the four committed manifests (unchanged, rc=0) and the 37 emit snapshots
(byte-identical).

**The gate.** `scripts/check_system_manifest.py` was jsonschema-only and could
not express the join the schema's prose promises, so it gains one: an
`ipc[].carve_out_region` that names no `memory[].name` now fails. The storage
side stays unenforced on purpose — an `on_module.ospi_memories:` key is a legal
`flash_device` target that gets no region row, and the loader already refuses a
`flash_device` naming neither (`_known_flash_devices`). The check is skipped
when `memory:` is absent.

Two corrections to split C's own text while typing it: the pane description
said the join key was `ipc[].region`, but the emitted key is
`ipc[].carve_out_region`; and it described the key as "DECLARED AHEAD OF ITS
PRODUCER, DELIBERATELY -- no emitter writes this key yet", which stops being
true here.

Consumers pinned to a vendored copy of this schema see one new optional root
key; the root stays `additionalProperties: false`, which is the producer gate
that catches an emitter key typo (`check_system_manifest.py`). Downstream,
`tan`'s planner-oracle corpus regenerates on its next SDK pin bump — alp-sdk's
own CI does not depend on `tan`, so nothing here waits on it.

Refs #1365, #1983, #1984. Does not close #1365 on its own — the issue stays
open until its remaining follow-ups land.

### Fixed — the IPC/flash-partition resolvers now derive flash class from the declared aperture, not just the legacy `carveout:` flag (#1365, split B)

Split A (#1365) added `soc_flash_base` and `write_authority` as additive
metadata and changed no allocator behaviour. Split B makes the two consumers
that matter -- `scripts/alp_orchestrate/carveout.py`'s IPC carve-out resolver
and `scripts/alp_orchestrate/partition.py`'s flash-device resolver -- derive
a region's class against the SoC's declared on-die MRAM aperture
(`alp_orchestrate.aperture`, factored out of `check_atoc_reservation.py`'s
own aperture math so both stay in sync) instead of trusting an authored
`carveout:` flag that, on `mram_main`, was never authored at all.

**IPC carve-out eligibility** (`carveout.py`'s `_region_ipc_eligibility()`)
derives a region's class (`flash` / `ram` / `unclassified` / `unresolved`)
against the aperture, and containment is checked BEFORE authorship: a
region CONTAINED in the aperture is `flash` and refused regardless of who
authored it. A region outside the aperture that the SoM preset did NOT
author is `ram` by construction (needs no authority) -- every V2N/V2M/NX9101
row lands here, which is what keeps their resolution byte-identical. A
region outside the aperture that the preset DID author is `unclassified`
(containment is one-sided: outside proves nothing) and needs
`write_authority: customer_runtime` to be eligible. Where the class can't
be derived at all -- no aperture declared for this SoC (every non-Alif SoM,
handled before this function is ever called), or the region's own `base`
is unresolved (`mram_main`'s `"TBD"`) -- the authored flag decides, and
`carveout:` is honoured FIRST when present, ahead of `write_authority`
(the conservative, pre-split-B signal); `write_authority` is consulted only
when `carveout:` is absent, and the region refuses, naming both, when
neither is present (ADR-0034 clause 4). NOTE: "eligible" here is not the
same predicate as "resolves `base_is_unmapped` fine downstream" -- an
unresolved-base region can pass eligibility on an authored flag alone and
still land `status: blocked` at the separate `_region_top_init()` check
that requires an actual, mapped `base`/`size` to allocate against.

A present `carveout:` that DISAGREES with a resolvable derived class --
`flash`, `ram`, or an `unclassified` row's `write_authority`-derived
answer -- is refused, naming BOTH facts: the derived class (with the
addresses that produced it) and the authored flag. This closes a review-
round regression the first split-B cut of this eligibility function
introduced: a preset-authored row outside the aperture with
`write_authority: customer_runtime` AND an explicit `carveout: false`
used to resolve `status: ok` on the write-authority answer alone, silently
dropping the author's `carveout: false` -- proven end-to-end by appending
`{name: ospi_xip, base: 0xA0000000, size_kib: 1024, carveout: false,
write_authority: customer_runtime}` to a real AEN preset's `memory_map:`.
`tests/scripts/test_orchestrate_carveout_aperture_ordering.py`'s
`TestCarveoutAgreementBlocker` reproduces exactly this probe and asserts
the refusal; `TestUnclassifiedWriteAuthorityLegCoverage` separately proves the
`write_authority == "customer_runtime"` leg on the `unclassified` branch
is still load-bearing on its own -- verified by hand: mutating
`derived_eligible = wa == "customer_runtime"` to `derived_eligible = False`
in `_region_ipc_eligibility()` turns that test red. That test is
positive-only, though, so it catches only that one direction; it does
NOT catch `derived_eligible` mutated to `True` unconditionally (dropping
the requirement rather than inverting it), which leaves the hazard this
same paragraph names -- "a future authored OSPI XIP row must NOT
silently become an IPC candidate" -- unguarded on its own. #2010 closes
that gap with a dedicated negative case.

Closes the ordering hazard split A's changelog entry documented: an
`a32_cluster`/`m55_*` `ipc:` entry can no longer resolve into the on-die
MRAM aperture once `mram_main`'s base is eventually filled in, because the
derived-flash-class refusal does not depend on that base staying
unresolved. `TestMramMainOrderingGuard` (same test file) pins this
directly: with `mram_main`'s base synthetically resolved in-memory, the
`rpmsg-aen` / `mproc-mailbox` examples' `ipc:` entries still block.

**Flash-device eligibility** (`partition.py`'s `_is_flash_sub_partition()`,
P2) is NOT an equality check: a region is a partition INSIDE a flash
device (excluded from `_known_flash_devices()` / `storage[].flash_device:`)
when its resolved extent is a PROPER SUBSET of the aperture
(`aperture.is_partition_inside_aperture()` returns `True`); it is a flash
DEVICE in its own right (kept in the advertised set) only when the extent
equals the aperture exactly (`False` -- e.g. `mram_main` once resolved).
Everything else -- extent outside the aperture, or unresolvable on either
side -- returns `None` and falls back to the legacy `carveout:` flag
(`region.get("carveout") is False`), never reading "not proven inside" as
"is a device" (review-round MAJOR 3).

**Measured, not assumed:** this change's own diff re-baselines exactly
four golden snapshots -- `rpmsg-aen.system-manifest`, `rpmsg-aen.build-plan`,
`mproc-mailbox.system-manifest`, `mproc-mailbox.build-plan`. In every one,
`status:` stays `blocked` and no address ever resolves; only the `reason:`
text changes, from "base is TBD" to naming the actual exclusion (the
fine-grained regions' derived `flash-class` containment, and `mram_main`'s
disqualifying `write_authority: composite`). A later review-round fix
capped the number of per-region details joined into one ineligibility
reason at 6 (`carveout.py`'s `_MAX_EXCLUDED_DETAIL`) -- an uncapped join
was genuinely unbounded (a future preset with more `memory_map:` rows
grows it without limit), reaching ~1.5 kB single-line in the emitted C
comment and DTS comment on the real 5-excluded-region AEN case today.
The cap sits one above that proven ceiling deliberately: every AEN
SKU's `memory_map:` has exactly 7 rows, so no `ipc:` entry on any SoM
declared today ever hits the cap, and excluded regions can carry
DIFFERENT reasons (flash-class containment vs. an unresolved base) --
truncating one silently would misrepresent why it was excluded, which
is why the cap bounds future growth without touching today's output.
`check_emit_snapshots.py` reports all 37 tracked `--emit` surfaces
byte-identical against the (unchanged) goldens.

`carveout:` stays in the `som-preset-v1` schema (removing it would break
every existing `carveout: false` row and any customer copy) but is now
documented, and enforced, as a legacy override that must AGREE with the
derived class where one is resolvable, never silently overridden by
`write_authority` or silently OR'd in -- see
`docs/board-config-features.md`.

### Added — `system-manifest-v1` declares a `memory[]` contract, ahead of its producer (#1365, split C)

`system-manifest-v1` gains an optional root `memory:` array: the resolved
memory-region view of the SoM, one row per region `resolve_memory_map()`
yields, each carrying the flash/RAM class derived from the SoC's declared
aperture (split A) and the region's authored `write_authority`. Rows join
the manifest's existing panes by name — `ipc[].region` and
`storage[].flash_device` each name a `memory[].name`.

**No emitter writes this key yet, and that is deliberate.** The emit half is
deferred on **fixture churn**, not on an open decision: emitting this key
rewrites every `system-manifest.yaml` under tan's planner-oracle corpus — 98
files, 94 of them carrying `ipc: []` — and landing that as its own
single-cause diff is what keeps it reviewable beside a schema addition.

Ownership is already settled. ADR-0026 §D decided that alp-sdk's emitters are
canonical and that `tan` consumes plan-embedded bytes rather than
re-implementing the renderers; and this schema is alp-sdk's under every
migration outcome regardless (ADR-0026 clause 2). What §D leaves open is a
different thing — *"Something must FAIL when tan's copy of the rendered bytes
diverges from alp-sdk's canonical output. That gate is required; its
implementation is not decided here."*

Declaring the contract now moves no emitted byte: `check_emit_snapshots.py`
still reports 37 `--emit` surfaces byte-identical and
`check_system_manifest.py` still validates all four manifests.

So a consumer must read an absent `memory:` as *"this producer does not emit
it yet"*, never as *"this SoM has no memory regions"*. The field description
says so normatively, alongside two other rules worth stating once: a region
whose base does not resolve carries no `base` and says why (`status:
unresolved` plus a `reason`) rather than guessing one (ADR-0034 clause 4),
and `dt_label` appears only when verified against the board `.dts` (#1556),
never as the name-derived fallback.

The join is partial by construction, and the schema now says that too: an
`on_module.ospi_memories:` key is a legal `storage[].flash_device` target
but is a controller-instance name carrying a `capacity_mbit` and no base, so
it lies outside every aperture and gets no `memory[]` row. Partitions stay
in `storage[]` and carve-outs in `ipc[]`; `memory[]` is the set of
SoM-declared regions those two refer *into*, not a third copy of them.

The root stays `additionalProperties: false`. The schema description
previously advised consumers to tolerate unknown fields two lines above that
closed root, which reads as a contradiction; it now states why it is not
one. The closed root is a **producer** gate — it is what makes
`check_system_manifest.py` catch an emitter key typo instead of shipping it
— while tolerating unknown fields is **consumer** advice, for a tool reading
a manifest emitted by a newer SDK than it was built against. Relaxing the
root to accommodate a strict consumer would remove the only gate that
catches emitter typos; the strict consumer is the thing to fix.

### Removed — `scripts/alp_cli/explain.py`; corrected `docs/cli.md`'s two now-false `tan explain` claims (#1367)

`tan explain --code <CODE>` shipped in `alplabai/tan-cli#627` (released
`v0.6.0`), porting the `ALP-Bxxx` / `ALP_ERR_*` diagnostic-code lookup out of
`scripts/alp_cli/explain.py`. That wrapper's only remaining consumer was
`scripts/alp_cli/main.py`'s own `click.group`, itself retired in this
change (#1368); `tests/scripts/test_alp_explain.py` retired with it. The
generator/emitter side is untouched: `scripts/gen_error_catalog.py` and
`metadata/error-catalog.json` stay exactly as before — `explain.py` never
read `docs/diagnostics/*.md` or the `ALP_ERR_*` enum, only the catalog
`gen_error_catalog.py` already produces, so nothing here is orphaned.

`docs/cli.md`'s `explain` comparison row and its `tan explain` verb section
both stated `tan explain` "never takes a diagnostic `CODE` lookup" and that
an `ALP-Bxxx` code "is decoded ... not by `tan explain`". Both are corrected:
`tan explain --code ALP-Bxxx` is documented as the third selector alongside
`--template`/`--target`, the one mode that reads an SDK checkout (via the
`--sdk-root` ladder), verified end-to-end against a real `tan 0.6.0` and this
checkout's own `metadata/error-catalog.json`.

### Removed — the rest of the `alp_cli` command surface: `main.py`, `validate.py`, and every command module reachable only through them (#1368)

Deleted `scripts/alp_cli/{main,__main__,validate,doctor,emit,faultdecode,
generate,init,model,monitor,new_som,run}.py` and their now-orphaned tests
(`test_alp_cli.py`, `test_alp_cli_doctor.py`, `test_alp_cli_emit.py`,

`_run_script()` half against `scripts/validate_board_yaml.py` itself is kept
— it is the only script-level guard that a warning-only ALP-B010 run exits 0,

Every one of these command modules had already been natively ported to
`tan` and released (`doctor`, `emit`'s ground via `tan generate`, `explain`
(#1367), `faultdecode`, `generate`, `init`, `model`, `monitor`, `new-som`,

The AST import scan is genuinely clean — and genuinely incomplete. It
cannot see a `subprocess` argv **string**, and one survived:

`test_new_som_scaffold_still_writes_under_output_root` spawned

rather than re-pointed at a real `tan new-som` subprocess: alp-sdk owns no
