blocks corrected their "Only `tan validate` prints the full diagnostic
frame" overclaim — a checkout-only user has no `tan` install but does have
`scripts/validate_board_yaml.py`, the same script `tan validate` spawns, so
both are now documented. `docs/cli.md` corrects an "All of Tan's 32 verbs are
native" overclaim back to "Most" (three -- `migrate`, `lock`, `quality` --
still forward to the corresponding `west alp-*` command), and its claim that
no `alp` console script was ever installed, which was false — `alp =
"alp_cli.main:cli"` shipped through `v0.11.0` and was removed in `v0.12.0`
(`629aa75fc`), before this retirement began. `docs/bring-up-drpai-v2n.md`
adds an explicit `--sdk-root <alp-sdk>` binding to its `tan model build`
example -- `tan` is a standalone binary with no repo context to infer an SDK
checkout from. `llms.txt` drops its link to the deleted
`scripts/alp_cli/doctor.py`.
`docs/adr/0020-sdk-owns-build-execution.md` gets a new correction item
(appended, not edited in place, per that ADR's own convention) marking its
own point 6 — "11 non-build verbs all still survive in the `alp_cli`
package" — false as of this change.

### Changed — the bridge firmwares live in their own repositories, and alp-sdk's security scope now says so (#1370)

Both bridge firmware trees are extracted, with history preserved, into
`alplabai/cc3501e-bridge-firmware` and `alplabai/gd32-bridge-firmware`. Each is
public and now carries its own CI, `SECURITY.md`, `CONTRIBUTING.md`,
`CODEOWNERS` and a protected `main` — none of which existed at the moment they
became separate repositories.

**`SECURITY.md` was actively wrong, not merely stale.** It declared
`firmware/cc3501e/` and `firmware/gd32-bridge/` in scope for vulnerability
reports, so a reporter following the published policy filed against a repo whose
maintainers no longer own that artifact. It now scopes the HOST halves
(`chips/cc3501e/`, `chips/gd32g553/`) and points at the two firmware repos by
name, with the boundary stated by artifact rather than by subject: a defect in
how the host *parses* a reply is alp-sdk's, the same defect in how the companion
*builds* it is the firmware repo's. Unsure cases are asked to come here rather
than be filed twice in public.

**ADR 0015** ("CC3501E bridge firmware is embedded in alp-sdk") was still
`Status: Accepted` while the tree contradicted it. It is superseded by
**ADR 0031**, which records what actually changed and — more importantly — what
did not: the wire contract stays single-sourced. Neither firmware mirrors the
protocol header; each compiles alp-sdk's canonical one through an explicit
`ALP_SDK_ROOT`, and firmware-side CI fails on drift (cc3501e compares
`protocol-version.txt` against `ALP_CC3501E_PROTOCOL_VERSION`; gd32 regenerates
`tests/protocol_vectors.txt` and diffs it). Vendoring a copy of the header into
each repo was the obvious way to split and was rejected for exactly the reason
0015 existed: a mirrored header that is merely *stale* still compiles.

### Removed — the firmware trees themselves, and the two unit suites that linked them (#1370)

The deletion that the extraction deliberately deferred is now done:
`firmware/cc3501e/` and `firmware/gd32-bridge/` are gone, and every consumer the
extraction listed has been repointed — `tests/fuzz/` takes the GD32 sources from
an `ALP_GD32_BRIDGE_FIRMWARE_DIR` checkout and **`FATAL_ERROR`s** when it is
absent rather than silently dropping the target, the AEN SoM presets no longer
pin `firmware/cc3501e/prebuilt/` as `helper_firmware`, and the doc links,
`Doxyfile`, `check_cross_platform.py`, `check_doc_drift.py`, `.vscode/tasks.json`
and `chips.kconfig` references are updated.

**Three test suites go with them.** `tests/unit/gd32_bridge_ota`,
`tests/unit/gd32_bridge_transport` and `tests/zephyr/cc3501e_bridge_transport`
all deliberately linked the **real** firmware sources rather than mocks, so with
the firmware removed they did not fail an assertion — they failed to configure
at all:

```
alp.unit.gd32_bridge_ota on native_sim/native/64 error
  (CMake Error at CMakeLists.txt:13 (target_sources): Cannot find source file:)
alp_sdk.cc3501e.bridge_transport on native_sim/native/64 error
  (CMake Error at CMakeLists.txt:32 (file): file STRINGS file)
```

They were **moved, not deleted**. Each now runs in its own firmware repository
as a host-only `ctest` job against a small ztest shim, with the suite sources
byte-identical to the originals —
[gd32-bridge-firmware#32](https://github.com/alplabai/gd32-bridge-firmware/pull/32)
and
[cc3501e-bridge-firmware#27](https://github.com/alplabai/cc3501e-bridge-firmware/pull/27).
The CC3501E suite keeps compiling alp-sdk's canonical
`<alp/protocol/cc3501e.h>` through `ALP_SDK_ROOT`, so single-sourcing of the
wire contract survives the move.

Keeping them here and repointing them at an optional external checkout — the way
`tests/fuzz/` now does — would have produced a suite that silently stops running
whenever that checkout is absent. The fuzz harness gets away with that pattern
because it can hard-fail on a missing directory; a twister suite has no
equivalent, so a required shard would simply go green while covering nothing.

Host-side GD32 coverage here is unaffected: `tests/zephyr/chips/gd32g553/` still
exercises the driver against the committed wire vectors, whose regeneration is
now checked by the firmware repo's own CI.

### Documented — ADR-0006 promised MCUboot swap-with-revert on AEN; the AEN family ships single-slot with no secondary or scratch partition (#1393)

`docs/adr/0006-secure-boot-secure-ota.md`'s "Secure OTA" decision commits the
AEN-Zephyr backend to MCUboot's swap-with-revert dual-bank flow. The AEN
family's MRAM partition map has no secondary slot to swap into and no scratch
partition to swap through — confirmed against `zephyr/boards/alp/e1m_aen801_m55_he/
alp_e1m_aen801_m55_he_ae822fa0e5597ls0_rtss_he.dts` and its `m55_hp` sibling on
`origin/dev`:

```
boot_partition     @ 0x0        64 KiB   label "mcuboot"
slot0_partition    @ 0x10000  2688 KiB   label "image-0"   (HE; HP's is @ 0x2b0000)
reserved_partition @ 0x550000   64 KiB   label "reserved"
storage_partition  @ 0x560000   96 KiB   label "storage"
atoc_partition     @ 0x578000   32 KiB   label "atoc"
```

`1ad76193` (#1100, closing #1069, 2026-08-03) removed `slot1_partition` and
`scratch_partition` from AEN801 deliberately, to fit the disjoint dual-core
slot0 budget: the address that was slot1/OTA (`0x802b0000`) became the HP
core's slot0, and the address that was scratch (`0x80550000`) became
`reserved`. #1445 later applied the same disjoint-per-core-slot0 trade to
every other dual-core AEN SoM. `zephyr/sysbuild/aen/sysbuild.conf` records the
same trade and sets `SB_CONFIG_MCUBOOT_MODE_SINGLE_APP`. Neither
`slot1_partition` nor `scratch_partition` exists anywhere in
`zephyr/boards/alp/` — confirmed by `grep -rn 'slot1_partition\|scratch_partition'
zephyr/boards/alp/` on `origin/dev`, which returns nothing; every AEN board
directory (`e1m_aen401_m55_hp`, `e1m_aen601_m55_hp`, `e1m_aen801_m55_he`,
`e1m_aen801_m55_hp`) carries the same no-slot1/no-scratch map.

**The ADR is not rewritten to erase the original decision.** Per the issue, an
ADR is a record: a new "Amendment (2026-08-25)" section states what was
decided (swap-with-revert), what the AEN family actually ships (single-slot,
no revert target), why they diverge (the #1069/#1100 dual-core slot0 trade,
later confirmed family-wide by #1445), and that OTA on the AEN family stays
deferred until a slot budget or a different delivery shape is chosen — a
maintainer call this ADR does not make. The original "Secure OTA" bullet gets
a one-line forward-pointer to the amendment rather than being silently
edited. `docs/ota.md`'s AEN-Zephyr section gets a shorter note to the same
effect, since it was already framed as an open "v0.4 plan".

`examples/aen/aen-mcuboot-smoke/sysbuild.conf:19` carried one stale line —
`slot1 @ 0x802b0000, scratch, storage` — pre-#1100 language naming partitions
the board no longer has (`0x802b0000` is now HP's slot0). Corrected to match
the current map; the file's own `NO A/B YET: ... the swap/upgrade path is
UNTESTED` note was already accurate and is unchanged.

Refs #1066 (the swap mechanism's own no-erase-MRAM defect, re-scoped to block
re-enabling OTA rather than fix it, since it can't be regression-tested on a
single-slot board) and #1069/#1100 (the deliberate change this documentation
now trails accurately).

### Added — provisioning step + bench helper to erase the AEN801 customer storage window (#1430)

A SoM was shipping with another application's bytes in the window the customer's first NVS write
lands in. alp-sdk#1334 measured, on real E8 silicon, ~110 KiB of a **stale previously-flashed
Zephyr application image** in the E1M-AEN801 customer storage window. It is not live data (the
region was erased and the board cold-cycled to `[SES] ATOC ok` / `RESULT PASS`), but a customer
who dumps the part sees another app's shell strings, and the first NVS write silently destroys
bytes that look meaningful. #1334 closed on the measurement and left the shipping question open;
this is the standing "erase before ship" step.

New `scripts/bench/aen/erase-storage.sh` (Flow D, SWD) plus a new
"Before the SoM ships — erase the customer storage window" section in `docs/aen-provisioning.md`.
Three facts drive the implementation, all already established in-tree:

- **The erased value on this MRAM is `0x00`, not `0xFF`** — measured from the running
  application's own flash parameters, `write_block_size=16 erase_value=0x00` (#1430). The written
  pattern is therefore `/dev/zero`, and it doubles as the `verifybin` reference so "erased" is a
  byte-compare rather than a claim.
- **A J-Link `erase` does not clear MRAM on this part** — the GOTCHA in
  `scripts/bench/aen/flash-jlink-mramxip.sh` ("a J-Link `erase` does NOT clear MRAM"). The erase is
  a `loadbin` through the part-number device profile, which is the only profile that unlocks
  J-Link's built-in Alif MRAM loader.
- **The band immediately above is SE-owned.** The window is DERIVED from the `storage` row of
  `metadata/e1m_modules/E1M-AEN801.yaml:288` (`base: 0x80560000, size_kib: 96`), never hardcoded,
  and the script refuses (exit 5) unless it ends exactly at the `atoc` base on the next line
  (`metadata/e1m_modules/E1M-AEN801.yaml:289`, `base: 0x80578000`). SETOOLS top-anchors the signed
  ATOC there and grows it downward, so an overshoot corrupts live SE data and drops the board to
  `No ATOC`. That guard was validated against the known-bad pre-#1289 128 KiB layout, which it
  refuses.

Gates match the sibling Flow D helpers: exit 4 when the SW-DP IDR says this is not the AEN E8
(the bench has three J-Links and two share OEM serial `603000869`), exit 2 when the part profile
cannot connect, exit 3 on a failed verify **or** on no verify result at all (#1488). The script
deliberately does not reset or boot the board.

**`[BENCH-VERIFIED 2026-08-30]`** — run against a real module (off-labgrid E1M-AEN801,
`AE822FA0E5597LS0`, J-Link `000821005680`): `verify successful`, then a cold power-cycle showed
`u VB` on the `ALP-HE` boot row, so the ATOC band was undisturbed by the erase. Transcript and the
Windows-host `cygpath` fix that first run needed are in `docs/aen-provisioning.md` section 7.
`--dry-run` exercises the window derivation and prints the CommanderScript without opening a probe.

### Fixed — `docs/glossary.md` stated the generic Cortex-M33 IDCODE as a GD32G553 measurement (#1440)

The **IDCODE** glossary entry read:

> Documented as `0x6BA02477` for the GD32G553 (Cortex-M33 r0p1 SW-DPv2);
> used by `gd32_swd_connect` to confirm the link reaches the right silicon.

Both halves are contradicted by the header the entry documents.
`include/alp/chips/gd32_swd.h` carries `@warning UNVERIFIED on a GD32G553`
on `GD32_SWD_EXPECTED_IDCODE` and states that "a correctly-wired GD32
therefore fails a comparison against this macro, so do NOT make a mismatch
fatal (`gd32_swd_connect()` deliberately does not)".

So `0x6BA02477` is the **generic** Cortex-M33 r0p1 SW-DPv2 expectation, not
a GD32 reading — and `gd32_swd_connect()` reports the value rather than
confirming the link reached the right silicon. A reader trusting the
glossary would expect a wrong-board refusal that does not exist, and would
read a mismatch on a correctly-wired GD32 as a fault.

The entry now matches the header, names both candidate values with where
they were read (`0x0BE12477` off the GD32 bridge and `0x6BA02477`
off the V2N CM33 DAP, both on the same V2N bench unit), and repeats the header's
guidance that a production test wanting to refuse on a mismatch must match
a value measured on its own board.

No hardware fact is settled here: **neither candidate has been measured on
a GD32 with a probe attached**, which is what #1440 and #1369 are open for.
`metadata/chips/gd32_swd.yaml`'s `target_expected_idcode` gains the same
hedge as a comment **in this slice**. Its value is left unchanged here —
picking between the two candidates would be guessing a hardware fact, and
the field is not consumed as a fatal guard today. The comment records that
it is the generic value, that whether a correct GD32 matches it is
unknown, and that it must not be read as a wrong-board guard until one
candidate is measured.

`scripts/bench/aen/bench-env.sh` and `docs/test-plan.md:176` already
carried this hedge correctly; the glossary and the manifest were the sites
left uncorrected.

**Superseded below:** a later change in this same release (a second
`#1440` entry, "remove `target_expected_idcode`...") goes further and
removes `target_expected_idcode` entirely rather than leaving it
hedged-but-present,
matching the stance `metadata/schemas/soc-spec-v1.schema.json`'s own
`expect_dpidr` guidance takes for every Alif Ensemble SoC variant — an
absent key is the correct published "unknown", not a guessed value
carrying a comment a future edit can silently ignore. See that entry
below (it sorts after this one) for the field's actual final state;
nothing in this entry's `target_expected_idcode` paragraph above should
be read as still current.

### Fixed — `gd32_swd.yaml`'s wrong-board guard presented an unattested value as armed; nothing was ever consuming it (#1440)

Nothing gated on `metadata/chips/gd32_swd.yaml`'s `target_expected_idcode`.
`gd32_swd_connect()` (`chips/gd32_swd/gd32_swd.c`) reads the SW-DP IDR into
`ctx->idcode` and never compares it against anything. The manifest field
itself has no code consumer: it is not read by any generator or by
`validate_metadata.py`, and it was only ever optional in
`metadata/schemas/chip-v1.schema.json`. The only place a comparison
happened at all was `examples/v2n/v2n-gd32-swd-flash/src/main.c`, against
the *header* macro this field mirrored, and that comparison already only
logged and continued on a mismatch — never fatal. So the field read as an
armed wrong-board guard while functioning as inert documentation, and the
value it carried, `0x6BA02477`, was not a GD32 measurement at all:
`CHANGELOG.md` records it as a measurement of a *different* target on the
same board — the V2N CM33 DAP on a V2N bench unit (`Found SW-DP with ID
0x6BA02477`, `Found Cortex-M33 r0p4`). The only other GD32 candidate on
record, `0x0BE12477`, has no attribution at all — no bench transcript, no
datasheet reference, no commit message.

A guard armed at a wrong ID is worse than an unarmed one: if the wrong
value happens to match the other board, it passes on exactly the board it
exists to exclude — and `0x6BA02477` is exactly that other board's own
measured value.

`target_expected_idcode` is now absent from `gd32_swd.yaml`, and
`metadata/schemas/chip-v1.schema.json` no longer declares the property at
all — with the schema's existing `"additionalProperties": false`, that is
a mechanical guarantee against silently repopulating it, not a comment a
future edit can ignore. The precedent this follows is
`metadata/schemas/soc-spec-v1.schema.json`'s own `expect_dpidr` field
guidance for every Alif Ensemble SoC variant (#1355): an absent key is the
correct published "unknown", and a guessed value is strictly worse than
absent (`metadata/socs/alif/ensemble/e8.json`'s `expect_dpidr` note is the
live, actually-measured instance of that stance). This is **not** the same
container as the V2N/V2M `gd32_bridge` SoM helper-firmware entries — those
carry no `flash_method` and no `flash_args` block at all (removed by
#1439), so there was never an `expect_dpidr` key there to leave unset in
the first place; an earlier draft of this fix cited that as the precedent
and it does not hold up.

The header macro `include/alp/chips/gd32_swd.h` mirrored is renamed
`GD32_SWD_GENERIC_CM33_R0P1_IDCODE` (was `GD32_SWD_EXPECTED_IDCODE`) —
keeping the old name while it names a value the manifest now deliberately
refuses to carry, and while the macro's own `@warning` says a correctly-
wired GD32 may not match it, was the same "confident fiction" this fix
otherwise removes. Its value (`0x6BA02477`) is unchanged; it stays only as
an informational generic-architecture reference that
`chips/gd32_swd/gd32_swd.c`'s connect-path comment and the
`v2n-gd32-swd-flash` example log, and neither gates on. `docs/abi/v0.16-snapshot.json`
(the current, not-yet-frozen snapshot) is regenerated for the rename;
every released `docs/abi/v0.*-snapshot.json` before it is untouched.

Also corrected, all without picking a winner between the two candidate
values: `chips/gd32_swd/gd32_swd.c`'s connect-path comment said "The
GD32G553 carries the Cortex-M33 r0p1 IDCODE" as fact — reworded to name it
the generic value, never measured on a GD32. The header's own comment said
"the bench measures the GD32 bridge answering `0x0BE12477`" a few lines
above stating that value has no attribution at all — `scripts/bench/aen/bench-env.sh`
itself says `0x0BE12477` is "NOT bench-verified", so "measures" was wrong;
reworded to match. The `v2n-gd32-swd-flash` example's `main.c` and
`README.md` said a correctly-wired GD32 is "expected to FAIL" the
comparison and that a mismatch is "expected on a real GD32G553" — both
assert a hardware fact only a measurement could establish, which is the
exact premise #1369 denies; reworded to "unknown, and the comparison
proves nothing either way", consistent with the rest of this fix.
`metadata/e1m_modules/README.md` and `docs/gd32-bridge.md` said the
manifest "expects" / "currently arms" its guard with `0x6BA02477`, which
is no longer true now that the field is absent.

`docs/glossary.md`, `docs/bring-up-aen.md`, `docs/test-plan.md` /
`docs/verification-status.md` (generated from it), `docs/_aen-runbook-section.md`,
and `docs/tutorials/07-recovering-a-bricked-bridge.md` already correctly
hedged this from earlier work (#1512, #1999) and needed no further change
here. `scripts/bench/aen/bench-env.sh` and
`scripts/bench/aen/flash-jlink-mramxip.sh` also carry `0x0BE12477` (a
*different*, AEN-Flow-D wrong-board rejection gate, not this manifest
field) and are deliberately left untouched: both are mid-rewrite on the
open #2032/#2064 branch.

**Closes #1440. Refs #1369.** #1440's ask — the manifest presenting an
unattested value as an armed guard — is resolved by removing the field
and closing the enforcement gap in the schema. #1369's ask is not resolved
by anything here and stays open: which of `0x0BE12477` / `0x6BA02477` (if
either) a GD32 actually answers is unknown, and settling it needs a probe
on a GD32G553, which no authorized bench place currently provides.
`alplabai/tan-cli#610` covers only that a `tan flash` consumer must
degrade cleanly when `expect_dpidr` is absent — it does not settle which
value is correct either, and remains not sufficient on its own to close
#1369.

### Fixed — `bump_version.py` left the `--emit` goldens stale after every release cut (#1461)

`scripts/bump_version.py` already regenerated `docs/abi/v<MINOR>-snapshot.json`
and `alp.lock` on every bump, but not `tests/fixtures/emit-snapshots/` — even
though the version is baked into some of them. Measured on the v0.16.0-rc1
cut, `bump_version.py --to 0.16.0` alone left 11 goldens stale: 7
`*.build-plan` goldens (`sdkVersion`, read straight from
`metadata/sdk_version.yaml` by `scripts/alp_orchestrate/buildplan.py`) and 4
`scaffold.*` goldens (a released scaffold's README doc links, pinned to
`v<version>` by `scripts/alp_template.py`). Every release bump therefore
reddened `validate · soc-spec-v1` until a human ran
`check_emit_snapshots.py --update` by hand.

`bump_version.py` now calls `check_emit_snapshots.py --update` as its last
step, the same way it already invokes `abi_snapshot.py` and `alp_lock.py`.

Regression test: `tests/scripts/test_bump_version_guards.py::test_a_full_bump_regenerates_the_emit_goldens_too`
runs `main()` end-to-end against a scratch checkout with `subprocess.check_call`
recorded, and asserts the `check_emit_snapshots.py --update` invocation is
present — it fails if a future change drops the refresh call from `main()`.

Not folded into this fix: the four `scaffold.*` goldens currently DIFF on a
full local clone (e.g. `test-all.sh --target dev`) because
`alp_template.py::_docs_ref()`'s tag-resolution check (#1508) makes the
scaffold README's doc-link pin depend on whether the local checkout has
fetched the release tag — CI's shallow, tag-blind checkout never has it and
stays green, but a full clone that has already fetched `v0.16.0` diverges from
the committed `main`-pinned golden regardless of what `bump_version.py` does.
Refreshing those 4 goldens against a tags-present clone would pin
`v0.16.0` into the golden and immediately break CI (which always computes
`main`), so they were deliberately left alone here; that tag-presence
nondeterminism is a separate, pre-existing defect in `_docs_ref()` itself.

### Fixed — populated the `quick` quality profile (#1463)

`metadata/quality-tasks-v1.json`'s `quick` profile had selected exactly zero
check-script tasks since it was introduced (`cd71de060`, PR #762) — the
tan-cli surface case that runs `tan quality --profile quick` (`tan-cli`
repo, `scripts/tan-surface/cases.sh` around line 326) has been passing
`rc=0` against an empty task set the entire time, silent since PR #1432 gave
that shape its own diagnosis ("NO TASKS SELECTED -- nothing was checked.
This is not a pass.") but never populated the profile itself.

Membership is measured, not guessed: every task in the 60-strong `pr` profile
was timed (median of 3 runs) and classified by whether it shells out
(`subprocess`, including a bare `git`) or needs a build/toolchain dependency.
`quick` = pure-Python, no subprocess of any kind, no toolchain, and a median
under half a second on the real tree — 36 of the 60 `pr` tasks clear that
bar. The other 24 either shell out (`git`, `alp_project.py`, `west`) or
exceed the 0.5 s bar. The bar itself is now written into the registry's own
root `description` so the next gate's author knows which profile it belongs
in without re-deriving this. No task was removed from `pr`/`full`/`release`,
and no gate was added or renamed.

`python3 scripts/alp_quality.py --profile quick` now runs 36/36 and exits 0
on a clean tree.

### Fixed — enforced the `quick` profile's own membership bar (#1463 round 2)

The criterion above was written into `metadata/quality-tasks-v1.json:3` as
prose only — nothing checked it, so `quick` could be silently re-emptied,
or stuffed with a slow/shelling task, and every gate and test would still
pass. `scripts/check_quality_registry.py` now asserts `quick` is non-empty,
`quick ⊆ pr`, and no `quick` member's script executes `import subprocess`
at module load time (a top-level import only — a lazy in-function import
some other, non-`quick` task uses does not count). The subprocess/toolchain
exclusion is a hermeticity rule (must run clean in a dirty tree or a bare
checkout with no `git`/`west` on `PATH`), not a speed proxy — three of the
gates it excludes (`doxygen-output-untracked` 0.041 s,
`emit-kconfig-contract` 0.044 s, `changelog-citations` 0.051 s) are the
fastest in the whole registry, faster than every `quick` member. The root
`description`'s "walks the whole example/doc tree" exclusion clause was
also removed — it was false: `scripts/check_doc_drift.py` and
`scripts/check_example_sdk_root.py` both `rglob()` their whole tree and are
`quick` members; the timing rule already covers what that clause was
trying to say.

### Proposed — ADR-0028: tan should own the model engine; alp-sdk keeps the NPU truth

`docs/adr/0028-tan-owns-the-model-engine.md` (Status: Proposed) records the
case for eventually moving `scripts/alp_model/` (12 modules, 938 lines) to
`python/tan/model/` in `alplabai/tan-cli`, so tan becomes the single
implementation of the host-side model pipeline. `scripts/alp_cli/model.py`
no longer exists on `dev` — #1367/#1368/#1727 already retired the whole
`scripts/alp_cli/` wrapper layer, and tan-cli v0.6.0 carries native ports of
those commands. The migration this ADR proposes is NOT enacted by this
change — `scripts/alp_model/` is untouched and still lives in this repo.

What this change lands now is the half of ADR-0028's decision alp-sdk is
uniquely authoritative for regardless of where the model engine ends up:
`metadata/npu_ops/`, `metadata/schemas/npu-ops-v1.schema.json`, the
`inference_arena_sram_kib` / vela-profile budgets, and the on-device
`.alpmodel` reader (`src/common/alp_model.c`). The `.alpmodel` container
format is the cross-repo seam and is unchanged.

This applies ADR-0026's principle — hardware truth stays in the repo that
owns the hardware; a consumer of it does not — to the second duplicated
surface. The measured trigger for the *proposal* (not yet enacted): `tan
model build` hand-ports 108 lines of this repo's board.yaml and
compile-option logic, that copy never received the alp-sdk#1271
`_PATH_OPT_KEYS` fix, and it currently corrupts DRP-AI's `input_shape`
(`"1,3,224,224"`), `input_name` (`"images"`) and `product` (`"V2N"`) by
resolving them as filesystem paths. A sha256 pin over the now-retired
`scripts/alp_cli/model.py` could not have caught it: a pin proves the
upstream file is unchanged, never that a downstream port is equivalent.

No alp-sdk build path is affected — no CMake, Yocto recipe or example imports
the Python package. The migration itself is not enacted by this change; see
`docs/adr/0028-tan-owns-the-model-engine.md` for the full decision record.

### Added — per-NPU op-support metadata, regenerated as ground truth, keyed by support-table identity (ADR-0028)

Adds per-NPU op-support metadata produced by running the real toolchains, or
transcribed from a cited vendor manual -- never hand-transcribed from memory
(an earlier hand-guessed seed, `metadata/npu_ops/{ethos_u,drpai,deepx_dxm1}.json`
`"version": "2026.08-seed"`, was written from general knowledge during this
change's own development and never reached `dev`; it is superseded here, not
replaced on `dev`). The flat one-file-per-backend
layout is also wrong: a backend can publish more than one distinct table, so
the new shape keys on **support-table identity**, one file per
`metadata/npu_ops/<backend_family>/<variant>@<toolchain>-<toolchain_version>.json`.

- **`ethos_u/u85@vela-5.1.0.json`** (70 ops) and
  **`ethos_u/u55-u65@vela-5.1.0.json`** (53 ops) are parsed programmatically
  from `vela --supported-ops-report` (`ethos-u-vela` 5.1.0's own
  `SUPPORTED_OPS.md`, column 1 of the "Ethos-U85 TFLite Summary Table" and
  the "Ethos-U55 and Ethos-U65 TFLite Summary Table"; the TOSA tables in the
  same report are out of scope -- the alp-sdk adapter accepts only
  `src_format == "tflite"`). Vela publishes exactly these two TFLite tables
  and both are invariant to `--accelerator-config`: regenerating at
  `ethos-u55-32`, `ethos-u55-256`, `ethos-u65-512`, `ethos-u85-128` and
  `ethos-u85-2048` all reproduce the identical `SUPPORTED_OPS.md` (md5
  `93f186ba8653467e46751765d151c3bd`), which is why table identity, not
  silicon-SKU identity, is the file's key. U55/U65 is asserted a strict
  subset of U85, with the delta pinned to exactly 17 ops (`CAST`, `DIV`,
  `EQUAL`, `GATHER`, `GREATER`, `GREATER_EQUAL`, `LESS`, `LESS_EQUAL`,
  `LOGICAL_AND`, `LOGICAL_NOT`, `LOGICAL_OR`, `NOT_EQUAL`, `REDUCE_ALL`,
  `REDUCE_ANY`, `SCATTER_ND`, `SELECT`, `SELECT_V2`); the new
  `scripts/gen_npu_ops.py` re-derives both files from a live `vela` and
  refuses to write anything if a future vela release disagrees with that
  delta.
- **`drpai/onnx-i8@translator-1.12.json`** (47 ops) is hand-transcribed from
  the DRP-AI Translator i8 vendor manual (doc R20UT5336EJ0112 Rev.1.12,
  §4.1.1 "ONNX Operators", table "Supported ONNX Operator List") --
  `authority: vendor-manual`, since the Translator publishes no machine
  report for `scripts/gen_npu_ops.py` to reproduce. A prior extraction pass
  over the same table found only 45 ops, silently dropping `Gather` and
  `Squeeze`; this pass extracts the table programmatically and gets 47, both
  present. One correction against the literal PDF text: the vendor table's
  own entry #38 is spelled "Sofplus" (a documented typo missing the 't');
  it is recorded here as the correct ONNX operator name `Softplus`, which is
  also how the same manual spells it in its own §4.1.2 detail section --
  the vendor's own document is the source for the correction, not an
  assumption.
- **No `deepx` table ships, and that is deliberate, not an omission.** dxcom
  2.3.0 publishes no op-support report of any kind; the only evidence
  available is 15 ONNX ops observed present in a `yolo11n.onnx` it
  demonstrably compiled, which is a lower bound on support, not a support
  table. Shipping a guessed table would mass-produce false "no-fit" verdicts
  on V2M, the SKU where DEEPX is the headline feature. A consuming engine
  (tan's model-fit analyzer, per ADR-0028) MUST treat a backend with no
  table under `metadata/npu_ops/` as `undetermined`, never as "zero ops
  known -> cpu-fallback" -- `test_no_deepx_table_exists` pins the absence so
  it cannot be silently "fixed" back in.

Every file now also carries `applies_to` (the product/toolchain/
toolchain_version it governs, matched mechanically against its own
filename), `authority` (`tool-generated` | `vendor-manual`), `stance`
(currently always `screening`: this data filters candidate ops, it never
certifies that a present op will actually compile), and `provenance` (the
exact reproducing command or the cited doc section, the tool version, and a
content hash of the regenerated report / cited PDF so upstream drift is
detectable without redistributing vendor content).
`metadata/schemas/npu-ops-v1.schema.json` is rewritten for the nested shape
and its `$id` moves to the `github.com/alplabai/alp-sdk` convention the
other 24 sibling schemas already use.

`scripts/validate_metadata.py`'s `_check_npu_ops_semantics` is rewritten to
cross-check, per file: `applies_to` reproduces the file's own path,
`op_namespace` matches its backend-family directory's compiler ingest
format, every `supported_ops` entry is spelled in the vocabulary
`op_namespace` declares (TFLite UPPER_SNAKE vs. ONNX CamelCase/all-caps
acronym, discriminated on the presence of an underscore -- not
`op == op.upper()`, which would false-flag real ONNX acronyms like `LRN`,
`GRU`, `LSTM`), and a `tool-generated` table carries the `_generated`
DO-NOT-EDIT banner while a `vendor-manual` one carries none (there is
nothing to regenerate it from). `tests/scripts/test_npu_ops_metadata.py` is
rewritten to match: every directory-wide check is parametrized over a
recursive glob of `metadata/npu_ops/**/*.json` (not `*/*.json`, which
silently sees nothing if a file is ever reintroduced flat, directly under
`metadata/npu_ops/`), not a hard-coded per-backend list, so a table added
later inherits every check automatically; plus the dedicated
U55/U65-subset-of-U85 invariant and the explicit "no deepx table" test
above. `scripts/test-all.sh`'s `stage_generated_files` now also runs
`gen_npu_ops.py --check`, so table staleness has automated coverage instead
of resting on a human alone.

**That skip is no longer unconditional, because unconditional it was
decoration.** `vela` is on almost no contributor's PATH, so the default local
invocation printed `gen_npu_ops.py --check SKIPPED (vela not on PATH)` and
checked nothing — *including* on a change that edited nothing but
`metadata/npu_ops/` and `scripts/gen_npu_ops.py`, i.e. exactly the tooling
this call is the only local proof of. A gate that cannot run on the one change
it exists for is the proxy-check shape this repo keeps digging out. The stage
now derives the touched set from `git diff --name-only
${DIFF_BASE:-$(git merge-base origin/dev HEAD)}` **plus** `git status
--porcelain` (either probe alone has a blind spot — the
first cannot see uncommitted work, which a local run usually is; the second
cannot see what an earlier commit on the branch already changed), and:
`rc=2` + those paths touched is a **hard failure** naming the files and how to
install vela; `rc=2` with them untouched still skips, now saying so; `rc=1` is
a defect, unchanged. Measured on this branch, all four states: vela unbound +
untouched → SKIP, stage rc=0; vela unbound + a touched
`metadata/npu_ops/ethos_u/u55-u65@vela-5.1.0.json` → stage rc=1; vela unbound +
a touched `scripts/gen_npu_ops.py` → stage rc=1; vela bound
(`ethos-u-vela` 5.1.0) + clean tree → stage rc=0. The `rc=1` path was hit for
real in the process: with vela bound, a deliberately-dirtied op table reported
`STALE metadata/npu_ops/ethos_u/u55-u65@vela-5.1.0.json` and failed the stage.

Nothing consumes this data yet (unchanged from the original landing): it
lands standalone ahead of the `tan.model.analyze` static-fit estimator that
will read it.

### Added — every Ethos-U SoC publishes its Vela memory profile (`npu_toolchain.vela`)

Invoked with neither `--system-config` nor `--memory-mode`, `ethos-u-vela`
5.1.0 picks a default profile per accelerator, and **the failure mode differs
by accelerator** — the U85/U65 one is not the U55 one. Every figure below is
KiB, measured on `ethos-u-vela 5.1.0` against
`tests/fixtures/models/tiny_int8.tflite` (712 B, md5
`07290259e28e1467fa184ef01b71e40a`):

| `--accelerator-config` | flagless `system_config` / `memory_mode` | `sram` | `dram` | `on_chip_flash` | `off_chip_flash` |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `ethos-u85-256` | `Ethos_U85_SYS_DRAM_Mid` / `Dedicated_Sram_384KB` | `0.0` | `0.265625` | `0.0` | `0.0` |
| `ethos-u65-256` | `Ethos_U65_Client_Server` / `Dedicated_Sram_384KB` | `0.0` | `0.109375` | `0.0` | `0.0` |
| `ethos-u55-256` | `Ethos_U55_High_End_Embedded` / `Shared_Sram` | `0.03125` | `0.0` | `0.0` | `0.078125` |
| `ethos-u55-128` | `Ethos_U55_High_End_Embedded` / `Shared_Sram` | `0.03125` | `0.0` | `0.0` | `0.078125` |

…and with the `memory_mode` this block declares:

| `--accelerator-config` | declared `memory_mode` | `sram` | `dram` | `on_chip_flash` | `off_chip_flash` |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `ethos-u85-256` | `Sram_Only` | `0.03125` | `0.0` | `0.234375` | `0.0` |
| `ethos-u55-256` | `Sram_Only` | `0.03125` | `0.0` | `0.078125` | `0.0` |
| `ethos-u55-128` | `Sram_Only` | `0.03125` | `0.0` | `0.078125` | `0.0` |
| `ethos-u65-256` | `Shared_Sram` | `0.03125` | `0.078125` | `0.0` | `0.0` |

**On the U85 and U65 parts** (`e4`/`e6`/`e8` carry a U85; `imx93` a U65) the
flagless default is DRAM-backed and reports `sram_memory_used = 0.0`. On the
Alif parts that number is a fiction twice over:
`metadata/socs/alif/ensemble/e8.json`'s `external_memory_interfaces` lists
only `HexSPI` and `SD/eMMC` — **there is no DRAM on the part** — and a zero
SRAM figure satisfies the on-device fit gate
(`src/backends/inference/alp_model_select.c`: `return e->arena_sram_kib == 0u
|| t->req_sram_kib <= e->arena_sram_kib;`) against ANY arena.

**On the U55-only parts** (`e3`/`e5`/`e7`, and the U55s that sit alongside the
U85 on `e4`/`e6`/`e8`) that is NOT what happens: vela defaults to
`Ethos_U55_High_End_Embedded` / `Shared_Sram`, never touches DRAM, and already
reports a non-zero `sram_memory_used`. The U55 hazard is a different one and
still real — the weights land in `off_chip_flash_memory_used = 0.078125`, i.e.
the OSPI0 NOR — on `E1M-AEN801` a part the preset declares `assembled: false`
and does not carry (see the `#915` fragment; other AEN SKUs' population
differs per preset). Declaring `Sram_Only` moves exactly that
`0.078125` into `on_chip_flash_memory_used`, which on an AEN SKU is the on-die
MRAM the weights actually live in.

An earlier draft of this entry credited `tiny_int8.tflite` with
`dram_memory_used = 5.359375` at `ethos-u85-256`. That figure is real but
belongs to a different fixture — it is `keyword_scrambled_8bit.tflite`
(29632 B, md5 `4e22b1bbb5f1a0eea728ec15d481ff7e`) at the same config,
re-measured here to confirm the mis-attribution rather than guess at it.
`tiny_int8.tflite` is `0.265625`.

The profile is a silicon fact derivable from the SKU, so it lands next to the
`npus[]` array that already says which accelerator is on the die — **not** in a
customer's `board.yaml`, whose `models[].compile` is scoped by
`metadata/schemas/board.schema.json` to config *"the SDK cannot derive"*.

| SoC spec | `memory_mode` | Needs a vendor config? |
|---|---|---|
| `alif/ensemble/e3.json` … `e8.json` | `Sram_Only` | yes — `ensemble_vela.ini` |
| `nxp/imx9/imx93.json` | `Shared_Sram` | no |

Every declared `memory_mode` is a section Arm's own `vela.ini` ships, so the
flag works for a customer with no license. Sourced from
`examples/aen/aen-npu-inference-alp/CMakeLists.txt:43` (`AEN_NPU_MEMORY_MODE   "Sram_Only"`, U85),
`examples/aen/aen-npu-inference-alp-u55/CMakeLists.txt:52` (`AEN_NPU_MEMORY_MODE   "Sram_Only"`, U55) and
`vendors/nxp-imx93/README.md:106` (`--memory-mode Shared_Sram`, U65) — never invented.

**The U65 citation is weaker than the other two, and now says so.** The two
Alif citations point at build files that pass the flag to a real toolchain;
the U65 one points at `vendors/nxp-imx93/README.md`, an **alp-sdk-authored**
page. So `test_every_vela_profile_cites_a_source_that_states_its_memory_mode`
proves alp-sdk agrees with itself on that row — internal consistency, not
vendor grounding. The README does not derive `Shared_Sram` from any named NXP
or eIQ document (its only vendor citation is `AN14413.pdf`, for the PCA9451A
PMIC), so rather than invent a reference the cited section now carries a
provenance note stating plainly that the mode is alp-sdk's own default, what
it was chosen against (measured: the flagless `Ethos_U65_Client_Server` /
`Dedicated_Sram_384KB` reports `sram_memory_used = 0.0`), and that grounding
it in an NXP primary document is open work.

**No Alif part declares a `system_config`, deliberately.** A Vela
`System_Config` section describes ONE accelerator's memory view — on Alif, one
CORE SUBSYSTEM's: the E8's U85 wants `Ethos_U85_SRAM_Only` while its
M55-HE-paired U55 wants `RTSS_HE_SRAM_Only` (*"the Alif ensemble_vela.ini has
no Ethos_U55-specific section; the per-core RTSS_HE config describes the U55's
memory: axi0_port=Sram"*). Every Alif Ensemble part carries two or three
distinct Ethos-U accelerators, so one scalar would be right for one and wrong
for the others. `system_config_requires_vendor_config: true` plus
`vendor_config_filename: "ensemble_vela.ini"` states what is actually known;
a per-accelerator mapping belongs in the slice that has a consumer for it.
Neither name is an Arm built-in, which is why passing one without `--config`
is a hard vela rc=1 (`Section System_Config.Ethos_U85_SRAM_Only not found in
Vela config file`), not a degradation —
`examples/aen/aen-npu-inference-alif/CMakeLists.txt:85-89` ("name sections that live ONLY in the Alif") already states the rule in the repo's own words.

**Which makes `vendor_config_filename` informational today, and the schema now
says so.** Both the schema's `if`/`then` and `_check_soc_vela_memory_profile`'s
rule (4) permit `system_config_requires_vendor_config: true` +
`vendor_config_filename: "ensemble_vela.ini"` with no `system_config` — which
is exactly what the six Alif specs declare — but there is no legal vela command
line for that combination. Measured on ethos-u-vela 5.1.0, `--config <ini>
--memory-mode Sram_Only` with no `--system-config` is rc=1, verbatim: `Error:
Incorrect argument to CLI option --config=[...]: Specifying a configuration
file is not allowed when using a default system configuration`. Requiring a
`system_config` alongside the flag would force the per-accelerator guess the
paragraph above deliberately refuses, so the field's `description:` is where
this lands instead: the filename tells a customer which file to obtain, and is
not yet a `--config` a consumer can emit.

**A `system_config` is NOT cosmetic, and the `memory_mode` description no
longer says it is.** It shipped claiming *"Placement is decided here;
`--system-config` only decides bandwidth (measured: the two are byte-identical
in memory terms)"*. That is true under `Sram_Only` and false under every other
mode, and the measurement behind it could not have told the difference —
both runs compared were `Sram_Only`. Arm's `vela.ini` assigns
`const_mem_area` / `arena_mem_area` / `cache_mem_area` to a **port**
(`[Memory_Mode.*]`), and the system config maps ports to **areas**
(`axi0_port` / `axi1_port`). `Sram_Only` puts all three on `Axi0` and every
Arm section sets `axi0_port=Sram`, so nothing moves; `Shared_Sram` puts
`const_mem_area` on `Axi1` and `Dedicated_Sram*` puts const **and** arena
there. The original measurement behind this claim was taken against
`person_detect_int8.tflite`, which is not an in-tree fixture and cannot be
re-run from a clean checkout; re-measured instead against the in-tree
`tests/fixtures/models/tiny_int8.tflite` (712 B, md5
`07290259e28e1467fa184ef01b71e40a`) with `ethos-u-vela 5.1.0` at
`ethos-u85-256`, comparing the flagless vela-picked default
(`Dedicated_Sram_384KB`) against a declared `Sram_Only` — the same runs
tabulated above: flagless defaults to `dram_memory_used = 0.265625`; declaring
`Sram_Only` moves that weight into `sram_memory_used = 0.03125` /
`on_chip_flash_memory_used = 0.234375`, and `dram_memory_used` drops to `0.0`.
`tiny_int8.tflite`'s single 8-MAC operator is too small to usefully sweep
`--system-config` at fixed `--memory-mode` the way the withdrawn measurement
did, but the placement claim itself — `memory_mode`, not only
`system_config`, decides where weights land — reproduces on the smaller
fixture.

Two consequences, both recorded rather than guessed at. The Alif parts declare
`Sram_Only`, so their missing `system_config` costs no placement — only
bandwidth and, measured, the encoded weight footprint (`on_chip_flash` is
`235.265625` under `Ethos_U85_SYS_{Flash_High,DRAM_Mid}` vs `248.953125` under
`Ethos_U85_SYS_{Flash_Low,DRAM_Low,DRAM_High}` at `ethos-u85-256 --memory-mode
Sram_Only`, while `sram_memory_used` stays `72.0`). But
`metadata/socs/nxp/imx9/imx93.json` declares `Shared_Sram` with **no**
`system_config`, so `E1M-NX9101` currently inherits vela's default
`Ethos_U65_Client_Server` and lands its weights in DRAM where
`Ethos_U65_Embedded` would land them in flash. The U65 is a single
accelerator, so unlike the Alif parts one scalar *could* describe it; what is
missing is a source for which one. That is open work, not invented here.

`scripts/validate_metadata.py`'s new `_check_soc_vela_memory_profile`
cross-checks the block against the rest of the same spec, which JSON Schema
cannot reach: the block is required on every SoC declaring an `ethos-u*` NPU
and forbidden on every SoC that does not; a `Dedicated_Sram*` mode (vela's own
default on the U85/U65 parts is one) is rejected on a SoC whose
`external_memory_interfaces`
declares no DRAM; a scalar `system_config` is rejected on a multi-accelerator
die and, when outside Arm's built-in set, must carry both the
`requires_vendor_config` flag and the filename.
`tests/scripts/test_vela_profile_metadata.py` pins the same invariants
independently. Both were mutation-proved: 12 mutations (dropped mode,
non-built-in mode, vela's DRAM-backed default on the DRAM-less E8, an
unflagged vendor `system_config`, a scalar `system_config` on the
3-accelerator E8, a first/second/out-of-range citation drift, a missing
vendor filename, an absolute path as the filename, a stray profile on the
DRP-AI-only RZ/V2N) each turn both gates red.

**Reading the `source` citations back is `test_vela_profile_metadata.py`'s
job alone**, and deliberately not the metadata gate's — those citations point
into `examples/` and `vendors/`, which do not exist in the metadata-only
scratch clone that `validate_metadata.py` is run against in a bare `board.yaml`
checkout (formerly exercised by `tests/scripts/test_alp_cli_new_som.py`,
deleted along with the rest of `scripts/alp_cli/` by #1727), so a copy there
could only be a silent skip (`scripts/validate_metadata.py:1353-1361`
("deliberately does NOT live here")).
The test requires the FIRST cited line to state the `memory_mode` and that
line's text to appear exactly once in the file. "The cited RANGE contains the
mode somewhere" was two holes at once, both measured: a 1-line shift left the
needle inside the window, and on the six-line window the U65 profile used to
cite (`vendors/nxp-imx93/README.md`, lines 103-108) a seven-line shift slid
that window clean off the vela command onto the provenance note that disclaims
it — the note names `Shared_Sram` too, so the disclaimer satisfied the check it
was written to weaken. Each `source` now cites the single line that states the
mode: `vendors/nxp-imx93/README.md:106` ("--memory-mode Shared_Sram"),
`examples/aen/aen-npu-inference-alp/CMakeLists.txt:43` (`AEN_NPU_MEMORY_MODE   "Sram_Only"`),
`examples/aen/aen-npu-inference-alp-u55/CMakeLists.txt:52` (`AEN_NPU_MEMORY_MODE   "Sram_Only"`).
`soc-spec-v1.schema.json`'s `source` pattern accepts a bare `:<line>`
alongside the old `:<first>-<last>`.

`metadata/catalog.json` is unaffected (regenerated, byte-identical).

### Correction — the Alif Ensemble E8 has three subsystems, not four

An earlier draft of this metadata described the U85 NPU (Alif block name
`NPU_HG`) as living on an "HG subsystem". The E8 has exactly three
subsystems — RTSS-HE, RTSS-HP, and the A32 APSS — and `NPU_HG` is the U85
block's own instance name (`NPU_HG_BASE 0x49042000`, byte-identical in both
M55 cores' generated CMSIS headers), not a fourth subsystem.
`tests/scripts/test_soc_npu_pairing.py::test_no_shipped_metadata_or_schema_claims_an_hg_subsystem`
now pins the absence of that phrase across `metadata/**`, `scripts/**/*.py`
and `zephyr/dts/**`.

### Fixed — `examples/README.md`'s AEN blurb had three wrong counts, and 21 `board.yaml`-carrying examples were missing from the index (#1486)

Measured against the tree (`ls -d examples/aen/*/ | wc -l`, `ls examples/aen/*/board.yaml | wc
-l`): 66 directories, 9 with `board.yaml`, 57 internal — the blurb said "~59 directories total;
the 7 below are the customer-facing catalog ... the remaining ~52 are internal", and the AEN
table one line below already contradicted its own "7" by listing 8 rows. Corrected the blurb's
counts and added the missing 9th row, `aen/aen-cc3501e-gatt-register`.

Separately, 21 `board.yaml`-carrying example directories across `ai/`, `audio/`, `bringup/`,
`connectivity/`, `display/`, `peripheral-io/`, and `v2n/` appeared nowhere in the index — the
whole AI/predictive-maintenance family and the GD32-bridge functional/loopback/soak trio were
invisible in the catalog `docs/getting-started.md`, `docs/README.md`, and `docs/soms/v2n.md` all
point readers at. Added a row for each to its matching existing section, plus a new "Bring-up"
section for `bringup/board-selftest` (the one directory with no existing home). Verified with:
`for f in examples/*/*/board.yaml; do d=$(dirname "$f"); b=$(basename "$d"); grep -q "$b"
examples/README.md || echo "MISSING $d"; done` — now prints nothing.

### Fixed — 25 stale `libraries.py` line-197 citations pointed at an unrelated parameter default (#1491)

Line 197 of `scripts/alp_orchestrate/libraries.py` was the Kconfig-transcription
site (`zephyr_kconfig_lines`) when 25 comments across `metadata/libraries/*.yaml`,
`metadata/library-profiles/README.md` and five `examples/**` files cited it —
and became stale the moment the same release that added them inserted
`scoped_names`, `_check_slice_requires` and `zephyr_library_kconfig` above it,
pushing the cited function down to line 321. Line 197 is now the
`metadata_root: Path,` parameter (no default) inside `resolve_selection`'s
signature, so several of the citations read as self-contradictory: naming
`zephyr_kconfig_lines` next to a line number where that function is not.

Every citation is re-pointed at the function it actually names: the
project-wide emitter `zephyr_kconfig_lines` now cites `:321`, and citations
describing the per-manifest `integration.zephyr.kconfig` transcription (no
function named) now cite `zephyr_library_kconfig` at `:283`.
`git grep -c "libraries\.py:197"` is 0.

### Fixed — `release.yml`'s Release-body draft is now bounded, and its docs stop claiming it's the final body (#1492)

The CHANGELOG-slice step in `.github/workflows/release.yml` always produced a
*draft* Release body -- a maintainer replaces it by hand with a lean summary
right after the tag lands (`docs/release-policy.md`'s release-cut procedure,
`alp-lab:cutting-a-release` steps 0/9) -- but nothing in the repo said so, and
nothing bounded the draft's size. A full `[Unreleased]` section already
exceeds GitHub's 125,000-char release-body limit routinely (`v0.16.0-rc1`'s
slice was 255,413 chars; `v0.15.0` was 159,174), and the
`softprops/action-gh-release@v3` step that publishes it enforces the limit by
silently `substring()`-ing to 124,999 chars right before the API call
(`truncateReleaseNotes()` in its own source) -- no warning, no log line, and a
cut landing wherever the char count happens to fall, mid-word or
mid-code-fence.

- `release.yml`'s slice step now checks the draft body's length itself: at or
  over the 125,000-char limit, it looks for the last complete CHANGELOG entry
  boundary (a `### ` heading, not a wrapped continuation line, and never one
  sitting inside an open ` ``` ` fence) below the limit. When that boundary
  keeps at least half the budget's worth of real content, it truncates
  there, appends a note pointing at `CHANGELOG.md` and the
  hand-written-summary step, and logs a `::warning::` naming the original
  and truncated lengths. When no such boundary exists -- the first entry
  alone is already oversized, or every candidate boundary is fenced off --
  the step **fails the job** instead of publishing a near-empty or
  fence-broken body.
- `.github/workflows/release.yml`'s header comment and
  `docs/release-policy.md`'s release-cut procedure (steps 7-8) now describe
  the real two-stage flow -- a **published** (not draft-state) auto-generated
  body, replaced by hand with a lean summary once the Release page exists --
  instead of documenting the auto-slice as the shipped state.

Scope is prose + the draft's size guard only: no artefact, checksum, SBOM, or
SLSA provenance is affected, and the existing missing-heading / empty-body
`fail(...)` guards and the `## [v<VERSION>]`-first-match contract
`scripts/bump_version.py` depends on are unchanged.

Deviations from #1492's suggested fix, both deliberate: item 1 (read the
notes from a dedicated per-release file, written and hard-required before
the tag push) is not adopted here -- the CHANGELOG slice stays the source,
per `alp-lab:cutting-a-release` steps 0/9 and `docs/release-policy.md` step
8, which already put the lean hand-written body on the Release page
immediately after it exists rather than before the tag. Item 2 (fail the
job on any oversized body) is adopted **only** when no safe entry boundary
exists below the limit -- an oversized-but-truncatable body (the common
case; every real release to date) still truncates-and-warns rather than
blocking the tag on a purely cosmetic overage of a body nobody is meant to
read in full.

### Removed — `board.schema.json`'s `ota.server.tls_ca_bundle` (#1493)

The schema declared `ota.server.tls_ca_bundle` ("Optional pinned CA bundle
for production"), but the string appeared nowhere else in this repo — no
emitter, loader, gate, test or example read it. (The public consumer
`alp-sdk-vscode` still carries three live copies of the key —
`packages/alp-core/src/board/models.ts`, `packages/alp-webview/src/types.ts`,
and `schemas/board.schema.json`, the last registered as VS Code's board.yaml
validation schema — so the editor will keep autocompleting a key this schema
now rejects; tracked separately as
[alplabai/alp-sdk-vscode#589](https://github.com/alplabai/alp-sdk-vscode/issues/589).)
`_hawkbit_server_lines()`
(`scripts/alp_orchestrate/kconfig.py`) derives TLS from `url`'s scheme alone
(`CONFIG_HAWKBIT_USE_TLS=y`, no sec-tag/CA symbol), and the Yocto/Mender
branch of the same file emits no CA variable either. The key validated and
the value silently evaporated: a customer setting it got a build that
succeeded with no trust anchor installed.

This is the same defect class `boot.anti_rollback` was removed for — a field
promising a security guarantee the SDK doesn't deliver — so it is removed
the same way: deleted from the schema, no legacy shim (no active customers),
no `schemaVersion` bump (matching the `anti_rollback` precedent — a bump is
reserved for a real `scripts/alp_migrate` migration step, and a straight
field removal isn't one).

### Fixed — `inference_ort.cpp`'s `open()` leaked every OrtValue created before a throw (#1494)

`alp_inference_ort_open()` drives an `std::unique_ptr<OrtState>` through
several fallible steps — `std::vector::resize`/`assign`, `std::make_unique`,
`std::string` assignment — any of which can throw. The `catch (...)` handler
released `cpu_mem_info`/`session`/`env` but never called `_release_values()`
on the input/output `OrtValue` vectors, so an exception thrown after some
input or output `OrtValue`s had already been created via
`CreateTensorWithDataAsOrtValue` leaked every one of them.

`OrtState` now owns a `~OrtState()` destructor that is the single place
releasing every vendor resource the struct holds (output values, input
values, `cpu_mem_info`, `session`, `env`, each NULL-checked) — the same
routine an early `return rc;` inside `open()`'s `try`, its `catch (...)`
handler, and `alp_inference_ort_close()` all now rely on via the
`std::unique_ptr<OrtState>`/`delete st` destroying it. `open()`'s success
path is the only one that escapes it, via `std::unique_ptr::release()`. This
also deleted three separate hand-rolled copies of the same cleanup sequence
that had to be kept in sync by hand.

### Fixed — board-config docs cited a stale preset-adoption count and a removed `routes_via:` key (#1495)

`docs/board-config-schema.md:254` claimed "66 do today — 46 on `e1m-evk`, 20
on `e1m-x-evk`"; the real counts are 100 `board.yaml` files under
`examples/` (`find examples -name board.yaml | wc -l`), 75 on `e1m-evk`
(`grep -rl '^preset: e1m-evk' examples --include=board.yaml | wc -l`) and 25
on `e1m-x-evk` (same, `e1m-x-evk`). The doc now cites 100/75/25.

Separately, `metadata/templates/board.yaml:160` and
`docs/board-config-schema.md:246` still advertised a `routes_via:` key on
`e1m_routes:` entries. `$defs.route_entry` in `board.schema.json` is
`additionalProperties: false` and does not accept that key — it was removed
from the schema in an earlier release (SoM concern, moved to the SoM
preset's `pad_routes.dispatch:`) — so a customer copying the template and
using the key it advertises got a hard validation rejection. The dead key is
removed from both the template comment and the doc prose.

### Fixed — `docs/gd32-bridge-protocol.md` documented `STATUS_NOMEM` for DSP chain-pool exhaustion; the firmware returns `STATUS_NOSUPPORT` (0x06) (#1496)

`CMD_ADC_DSP_CHAIN_OPEN`'s doc text claimed pool exhaustion returns `STATUS_NOMEM` (`0x07`), but
`bridge_hw_adc_dsp_chain_open()` returns `BRIDGE_HW_ERR_NOTIMPL`, which `status_from_hw()` maps to
`STATUS_NOSUPPORT` (`0x06`) — the same document's own §6 status table already lists `0x07` as
`Reserved`. A host built against the old doc text would branch on a status code it can never
receive, and misread the real `0x06` reply as "opcode unknown to this firmware build" instead of
"pool full, retry". Corrected the doc to `STATUS_NOSUPPORT` (`0x06`) with a note on why (no
NOMEM-equivalent `BRIDGE_HW_ERR_*` exists yet for this path).

Also fixed the stale in-code comments this drifted from: `adc_stream.c`'s pool-exhaustion comment
claimed `STATUS_NOMEM` "doesn't exist on the wire yet", which undersold it slightly — 17 defensive
`reply_cap` guards in `protocol.c` do return it, but both transports pass a 65-byte reply buffer
(`1u + 32u*2u`), above every guard's threshold, so none of them can actually fire on the wire; and
`bridge_hw.h`'s `bridge_hw_adc_dsp_chain_open()` doc comment claimed real builds return a
NOMEM-equivalent mapped to `STATUS_NOMEM`, which they don't. Both now say what's actually missing:
a NOMEM-equivalent `BRIDGE_HW_ERR_*` in `hal/bridge_hw.h`.

### Fixed — `flash-jlink-mramxip.sh` discarded an operator's DPIDR override (#1497)

`scripts/bench/aen/flash-jlink-mramxip.sh` sourced `bench-env.sh` and then re-declared
`AEN_DPIDR` and `GD32_DPIDR` with bare assignments, silently throwing away any export the
operator had made. `bench-env.sh` is the documented single source and declares them
overridable (`export AEN_DPIDR="${AEN_DPIDR:-4C013477}"`), stating in its own header:
"Override any of them by exporting the variable before invoking a helper".

This was the **only** one of the six callers of `bench_jlink_assert_aen_dpidr` that did
so, and `V2N_CM33_DPIDR` was never re-declared here either — so the file used one source
for two IDs and another for the third, which rules out reading it as deliberate hardening.

The declarations now use `${VAR:-default}`. That satisfies both constraints at once: the
operator's export survives (#1497), and the declarations remain in the file rather than
being deleted (#1527 — deleting the pair to silence shellcheck weakened the wrong-board
MRAM-write gate during #1488 and had to be reverted).

**No safety change.** The gate is fail-closed on a *positive* `AEN_DPIDR` match and aborts
before any MRAM write, so the pre-fix behaviour was a misleading hard abort against a value
the operator had explicitly overridden, never a wrong-board write. This makes the script
consistent with its five siblings, it does not loosen the gate.

### Fixed — a stale zcbor citation shipped in `CHANGELOG.md` because the #1416 citation gate stops at `changelog.d/` (#1498)

`CHANGELOG.md:4006` cited
`meta-alp-sdk/recipes-devtools/zcbor/zcbor_0.9.1.bb:90` / `:92` for the
double `SRC_URI`/`SRCREV` pin that broke every A55 image build; the actual
lines are `:102` (`SRC_URI`) and `:104` (`SRCREV`). The citation was correct
against the fragment at authoring time and went stale when a later edit to
the recipe shifted both lines by 12 — `scripts/check_changelog_citations.py`
only ever reads `changelog.d/`, so once `scripts/assemble_changelog.py`
folded the fragment into `CHANGELOG.md` and deleted it, the citation left
gate scope permanently and nothing re-checked it. Fixed in place.

Extending the gate to also scan `CHANGELOG.md` is the real fix, but running
it against the shipped file first (`_check_one` against `CHANGELOG.md`)
surfaces 12 pre-existing broken citations unrelated to this issue — 4
anchored citations whose cited text has moved, and 8 paths that don't
resolve at all. One of those 8 -- a citation into
`python/tests/gates/test_planner_relocation_freshness.py` (line 129) -- is a
cross-repo tan-cli citation; the gate's docstring says another-repo
citations are reported as SKIPPED, but `_FOREIGN_PREFIXES` only matches
`python/tan/`, `crates/` and `contract/`, so this `python/tests/...` path
falls through that check and is caught here as an unresolved path instead.
The rest are mostly short filenames missing their directory prefix, plus a
couple of moved/renamed files. Landing the extension now would redden on
arrival, so it is left as follow-up (#1715); this citation-only fix is the
smaller step.

### Fixed — ADR-0021/0020 amendments corrected for cleared tan blockers; ADR-0003's Status line records the ADR-0023 supersession (#1516)

`docs/adr/0021-toolchain-provisioning.md`'s newest amendment (2026-08-07) named
a Lane-1 P1 blocker -- `build_cmd.py`'s hardcoded `toolchain_root=None`, and
silent `--materialise` demotions -- that is closed as of tan-cli `v0.6.0-rc1`
(`resolve_toolchain_root()` wired at `python/tan/commands/build_cmd.py:1497`; `_demoted_artefact_issues()`
at `:1406`/`:1545`). A new dated amendment records that, per this ADR's own
append-only convention.

**Known coordination conflict, not fixable from this branch alone:**
`origin/fix/1367-1368-alp-cli-retirement` (`212059ea2`, unmerged) also
prepends its own same-dated `## Amendment (2026-08-26 — the dtc/gperf-consumer
citation named a retired file)` at the identical anchor in this same file
(immediately after the `Deciders:` line, before the existing 2026-08-07
amendment) -- both PRs insert new, non-overlapping content at the same
position relative to `origin/dev`, which two independent PRs cannot avoid
colliding on without one of them deviating from the ADR's own
newest-first-at-top convention. This amendment stays at the top per that
convention; whichever of the two PRs merges second will hit a real conflict
on `docs/adr/0021-toolchain-provisioning.md` at rebase time and must resolve
it by keeping both `## Amendment (2026-08-26 — ...)` blocks, in either
relative order (both are same-dated and address unrelated topics, so the
order between them carries no meaning) -- not by dropping either one.

`docs/adr/0003-peripheral-coverage.md`'s bare `Status: Accepted` gave no

the Deferred-classes table) instead of a `(see :44)` line pointer, since a

An earlier draft of this fix also reworded `docs/adr/README.md`'s row 42
from "partially superseded by 0023" to "Ethernet row contested by 0023

("This ADR supersedes") says it supersedes "that one row of ADR 0003 and

"(partially / narrowly) supersede[d]", and row 42 adds an inline "0023

### Fixed — `<alp/inference.h>` claimed no adapter produces `ALP_INFERENCE_MODEL_EXECUTORCH` (#1517)

`ALP_INFERENCE_MODEL_EXECUTORCH`'s Doxygen said "RESERVED -- no adapter produces this format
and no backend consumes it, so a blob claiming it is rejected with `ALP_ERR_INVAL`". Two of
those three claims were false: `ExecutorchAdapter` (`scripts/alp_model/adapters/executorch.py`)
is registered in `build.py`'s default adapter list and produces `format="executorch"` for any
`.pte` source, and `_fmt_enum()` in `src/backends/inference/alp_model_select.c` explicitly
accepts the `"executorch"` string and decodes it to this enumerator instead of rejecting it.

Only "no backend consumes it" holds: none of `tflm.cpp`, `ethos_u_aen.cpp`, `ethos_u_n93.cpp`,
or `sw_fallback.c` under `src/backends/inference/` branch on `cfg->format`, so an ExecuTorch
blob still ends up handed to the CPU/TFLM backend, which tries to verify the raw `.pte` bytes
as a TFLite flatbuffer and fails that verification -- landing on `ALP_ERR_INVAL` by coincidence
of the TFLM backend's own input validation, not a deliberate format-enum rejection.

The comment now describes the real split: the write side (host-side `.alpmodel` build) is live
and produces this format; the read side (on-device execution) has no consumer yet, and the
`ALP_ERR_INVAL` a caller sees comes from the CPU/TFLM backend's flatbuffer verifier, not a
guard on the format enum itself.

### Fixed — `alp_i3c_open()`'s `@return` list in `<alp/i3c.h>` didn't match its dispatcher (#1518)

The `@return` block named `ALP_ERR_NOSUPPORT` among the four codes `alp_i3c_open()` can set via
`alp_last_error`, and omitted two codes `src/i3c_dispatch.c` actually sets: `ALP_ERR_NOMEM` (the
handle-pool-exhausted path, already described in prose but not tied to its code) and
`ALP_ERR_NOT_IMPLEMENTED` (the `ops == NULL || ops->open == NULL` path).

`ALP_ERR_NOSUPPORT` is not a corner case in the doc, either: `src/backends/i3c/zephyr_drv.c`'s
`#else /* !CONFIG_I3C_CONTROLLER */` branch -- taken whenever a build lacks
`CONFIG_I3C_CONTROLLER` (either `CONFIG_I3C=n`, or `CONFIG_I3C=y` with
`CONFIG_I3C_TARGET_ROLE_ONLY` selected, per upstream `choice I3C_MODE` in
`zephyr/drivers/i3c/Kconfig`) -- registers the backend with every op, including `open()`,
hard-wired to return `ALP_ERR_NOSUPPORT`. `I3C_CONTROLLER` itself defaults to `y` once
`CONFIG_I3C=y` (the upstream `choice I3C_MODE` defaults to `I3C_DUAL_ROLE`); the `n` default
comes from `CONFIG_I3C` itself defaulting to `n`. So `ALP_ERR_NOSUPPORT` from `open()` is the
DEFAULT outcome on every alp-sdk Zephyr build that doesn't set `CONFIG_I3C=y` at all, not an
edge case -- `examples/aen/aen-i3c-regcheck` is the counterexample: its `prj.conf` sets only
`CONFIG_I3C=y` and gets the controller role for free, with no extra role opt-in needed. The
Yocto and sw_fallback backends never return it from `open()`, but the Zephyr backend does by
default, so it stays in the list with that caveat instead of being dropped.

The `@return` block now enumerates all six codes against the specific dispatcher/backend branch
each comes from, mirroring the `@ref CODE (reason)` style already used in `<alp/counter.h>`.

### Fixed — `check_tan_docs_surface.py`'s forwarding-verb exclusion never matched the current `tan`'s `--help` output (#1519)

`_has_legacy_passthrough_args()` skipped flag verification for a legacy
FORWARDING verb (`lock`/`migrate`/`quality`) by checking whether its `Usage:`
line ended in `[ARGS]...` — the frozen Rust/Clap spelling. The current Python
`tan` renders the same catch-all through Typer/Click as `[ARGS...]`, so the
check never fired against a real, installed `tan`: `endswith("[ARGS]...")` is
`False` for every verb tan ships today. Latent rather than a live break — the
failure direction was fail-safe (stricter, never falsely green), and
`docs/cli.md` has no section for any of those three verbs yet — but the first
one added would hit a hard flag-mismatch failure with no working escape
hatch.

Both spellings are now accepted. Also corrected the out-of-scope docstring
bullet that named `tan new-som` as the example forwarding verb whose
tabulated flags can't be mechanically checked — `new-som` is native
`[OPTIONS]`-only and its thirteen `docs/cli.md` flags are in fact this
check's main verified surface; the example is now `tan lock`/`migrate`/
`quality`. Test fixtures re-pointed at a real forwarding verb (`lock`, with
the `[ARGS...]` spelling) plus a new regression test proving `new-som`'s
`[OPTIONS]`-only usage line is checked, not skipped as forwarding.

### Added — tier-2 model-perf: the bench-measured perf-point contract (schema + validator + capture doc) (#1520)

Lands the *contract* half of the tier-2 edge-AI fit/perf lifecycle
(docs/superpowers/specs/2026-07-24-edge-ai-lifecycle-roadmap.md sub-project
1): `metadata/schemas/model-perf-v1.schema.json` defines one bench-measured
performance point, keyed on **measurement identity** rather than on a model
or a SoM alone — SKU, hw_rev, compile target (backend + accel_config + core
+ the exact compiler build), the exact source-model bytes, and the vela
profile when one applies. Compiler build (`target.compiler_version`, e.g.
`vela 4.1.0`) is in the identity key because a compiler upgrade alone can
move `arena_bytes`/`latency_ms` for otherwise-identical everything else —
without it, a re-capture under a newer compiler silently overwrites the old
point at the same filename.

A dedicated collector (`_collect_model_perf_files`,
`scripts/validate_metadata.py:2753` ("def _collect_model_perf_files(root: Path) -> tuple[list[Path], list[tuple[str, list[str]]]]:")) walks the whole
`metadata/model_perf/` tree and FAILS on anything that isn't exactly
`<SKU>/<hash>.yaml` two levels deep — a stray file, a `.yml` sibling, or a
point nested one level too deep (`<SKU>/_fixture/<hash>.yaml`, the precise
evasion the `_fixture` refusal below exists to catch) — rather than the
one-level glob it replaces silently never opening it.
`scripts/validate_metadata.py:2914` (`_check_model_perf_semantics`) adds the
semantic cross-checks a schema can't express: the path reproduces the body
(directory == `sku`, filename == a content hash of the identity fields —
`scripts/validate_metadata.py:2808` ("def _model_perf_identity_hash(doc) -> str:"), `_model_perf_identity_hash`); the SKU
exists; the `(backend, accel_config)` pair and `core` are ones the SKU
actually resolves (cross-checked against `alp_project_loader.resolve_targets`
and `npus[].paired_core`); `hw_rev` is a key in the family
`hw-revisions.yaml`; an `ethos_u` point records its `vela:` system/memory
profile (vela otherwise silently falls back to its own DRAM-backed default,
`Ethos_U85_SYS_DRAM_Mid` / `Dedicated_Sram_384KB`, on silicon with no DRAM)
and a non-`ethos_u` point carries no leftover `vela:` block; `req_sram_kib`
covers `arena_bytes`; `p95` is never below `mean` and `p50` is never above
`p95`; a `latency_ms` block needs at least
`scripts/validate_metadata.py:2749` (`_MODEL_PERF_LATENCY_RUN_FLOOR = 30`)
runs; `capture.date` parses as ISO-8601; and any `_fixture`-named SKU
directory or filename is refused outright in the published tree.

`tests/scripts/test_model_perf_metadata.py` carries one real fixture point
(E1M-AEN801's actual `ethos-u55-256` target on its actual paired `m55_hp`
core and its actual `r1` hw_rev, under `tests/fixtures/model_perf/`) plus a
one-field mutation per rule above, so none of the eleven checks can go
quietly vacuous. `docs/bench/model-perf-capture.md` is the capture recipe,
written before any bench time is spent: it names its own two open
blockers plainly (which vela profile a module should compile under, and
whether `req_sram_kib` should also cover the model's const/weight region),
and its step 3 now spells out `req_sram_kib` as `ceil(arena_bytes / 1024)`
-- rounding down (as vela's own summary CSV and the `.alpmodel` manifest's
`Target.requires.sram_kib` both do) fails the "covers arena_bytes" check
on almost any real capture.

**`metadata/model_perf/` stays empty.** This PR lands the contract only — a
perf point comes off real Alp Lab bench silicon or it does not exist, and
none has been captured. The two blockers above gate that follow-on bench
work, not this PR.

### Fixed — `tests/parity/README.md` described tan-cli's `parity.yml` as alp-sdk's own CI wiring (#1521)

The "CI wiring" section, plus two other spots (the seam-1 coverage-table row
and a `seam2` placeholder claim), named `.github/workflows/parity.yml`'s
`seam1-plan-shape` job, its `PINNED_SDK_TAG` pin, and an inbound
`repository_dispatch` — none of which exist in alp-sdk. That file, job id,
pin, and dispatch all belong to **tan-cli's** `.github/workflows/parity.yml`.
alp-sdk's own half of the gate is `.github/workflows/parity-seam1.yml` (job
id `seam1`), path-filtered to `pull_request`/`push` on
`scripts/alp_orchestrate/**`, `metadata/**`, `examples/**/board.yaml`, and
`tests/parity/**` — not "on every pull request" — with no pin and no inbound
dispatch. alp-sdk is the dispatch *sender* (`dispatch-tan-parity.yml`, event
type `alp-sdk-planner-change`), not a receiver. The README, and the matching
stale reference in `tests/parity/seam1_field_diff.py`'s module docstring,
now describe alp-sdk's actual wiring and point the pin/dispatch/`seam2` half
at tan-cli by name — including correcting the `seam2` claim itself:
tan-cli's `.github/workflows/parity.yml` `seam2` job is a working
materialise + `tan build` + Renode-boot-smoke check today, not a
placeholder.

### Fixed — `check_changelog_citations.py` hard-failed correct citations into tan-cli's `python/tests/`/`python/scripts/` trees (#1522, #1525)

`_FOREIGN_PREFIXES` recognised only `python/tan/`, `crates/`, and
`contract/` as belonging to another repository; every other path under
`python/` fell through to the "no such file in this tree" hard error and
failed the blocking `pr-metadata-validate` gate on a correct citation. alp-sdk
has no `python/` directory of its own at all, so the distinction between
`python/tan/` (skipped) and `python/tests/` (hard error) was never a real
property of this tree — it was an incomplete list, and the routine prose
form of citing tan-cli's hash-pinned `python/tests/gates/
test_planner_relocation_freshness.py` was exactly what it rejected.

`_FOREIGN_PREFIXES` now matches the whole top-level directory
(`"python/"` instead of `"python/tan/"`), since alp-sdk has none of
`python/`, `crates/`, or `contract/` and every subpath under them is equally
unresolvable here. Verified against the gate's own reproduction from #1522
(`python/tests/gates/test_planner_relocation_freshness.py:129` and
`python/scripts/foo.py:10`, both now SKIPPED, not errors) and
mutation-proven: reverting to the old prefix list re-fails both cases with
the original "no such file in this tree" message, while a genuinely bogus
in-tree path still hard-fails as before.

### Fixed — `check_changelog_citations.py`'s foreign-repo skip list was incomplete, hard-failing correct cross-repo citations (#1525)

Same defect and same fix as #1522: `_FOREIGN_PREFIXES`'s `python/tan/` entry
widened to the whole top-level `python/` directory (`crates/` and
`contract/` were already whole top-level dirs, unchanged), so any citation
into tan-cli's `python/` tree — `python/tan/...`, `python/tests/...`,
`python/scripts/...` — is SKIPPED as foreign instead of hard-failing as "no
such file in this tree". A gate that fails correct input trains people to
strip the citation rather than trust the gate; see `changelog.d/1522.md` for
the full evidence and the mutation-proof.

### Fixed — an unverified AEN update-log image was booted before the verify could gate it (#1526)

`flash-update-log-firewall-probe.sh` and `flash-update-log-dual.sh` put `loadbin`,
`verifybin`, `RSetType 2`, `r` and `g` into **one** JLinkExe CommanderScript. JLinkExe
finished the whole script before the shell could read the verify result, so the SE had
already pin-reset and booted the image. The gate that followed could only suppress the
false "flash complete" report and the beacon read-back — it could not stop an unverified
image being booted, and the booted image is what appends to (or overwrites)
`alp_ulog_partition`.

Both scripts now use **two** CommanderScripts: `loadbin` + `verifybin` + `exit`, then the
shell evaluates the result, and only on success a second script carrying
`RSetType 2` / `r` / `g`. The gate is load-bearing rather than advisory.

The MRAM write itself still happens before the verify — that *is* `loadbin`, and it cannot
be otherwise. What is now prevented is **acting** on an image that failed to verify: with
`"flags": ["load", "boot"]` on the ATOC entry, not booting is exactly what keeps the HE
probe (firewall-probe) or the HP owner and the HE client it releases (dual) from running
and touching the update-log partition.

The exit-3 messages said "DATA LOSS: the board was already pin-reset and released ...
alp_ulog_partition may ALREADY have been overwritten". That is no longer true and would
now send an operator to re-verify a partition that is intact, so both copies in each
script are rewritten to say the board was not booted and the partition is untouched — the
correct remaining action being to reflash before booting. The "does NOT and CANNOT prevent
the write, or the boot" comment blocks are likewise corrected rather than left to rot.

### Added — CI gate: assert every ALP-Bxxx emission site has a doc page (#1569)

`scripts/check_diagnostic_narratives.py` and `scripts/gen_error_catalog.py`
both walk `docs/diagnostics/ALP-B*.md` -- neither walks the
`scripts/alp_cli/validator.py` `code="ALP-Bxxx"` emission sites, so a code
the validator starts emitting without ever getting a page stayed invisible
to CI. That is exactly how `ALP-B000` and `ALP-B099` went undocumented
until #1511 caught it by inspection.

New `scripts/check_diagnostic_emission_coverage.py` greps the emission
sites and fails if any has no `docs/diagnostics/<code>.md` page. Today's 11
emitted codes (`ALP-B000`-`ALP-B008`, `ALP-B010`, `ALP-B099`) already match
the 11 doc pages exactly, so this gate guards a currently-quiescent gap
against future drift rather than fixing a live one.

### Changed — stop committing `alp.lock`; generate it on demand (#1576)

`alp.lock`'s `digests.metadata` (`scripts/alp_lock/__init__.py:158-166`) is a
single sha256 over the entire `metadata/**` tree, so any two PRs touching
*different* metadata files rewrote the same JSON line from different bases
and conflicted by construction, sharing no other file. Measured: #1576's body
recorded four PRs simultaneously DIRTY, three sharing no other file; in a
2026-08-25 merge campaign, #1676, #1678 and #1694 were each ejected from the
`dev` merge queue with `alp.lock` as the ONLY conflicting file — #1678 twice,
once per predecessor merge. Precedent: `sdk.revision` was retired in #1615
for exactly this conflict class. A `.gitattributes` merge driver can't fix
it either — the executable it names lives in local `git config`, which never
lives in the repo, and GitHub's server-side merge can't run it.

`alp.lock` is now generated on demand and no longer tracked. `build_lock` is
a pure function of tracked files, so any consumer regenerates the identical
document from the commit it needs it for:

- `git rm alp.lock`; `.gitignore` keeps a locally-regenerated `/alp.lock` out
  of any future commit.
- `west alp-lock --check` (`scripts/west_commands/alp_lock.py`) no longer
  diffs against a committed copy — there isn't one. It now builds a lock in
  memory and schema-validates it against `metadata/schemas/alp-lock-v1.schema.json`,
  still failing on a broken generator or a local/abs-path leak
  (`_reject_local`). Both `.github/workflows/pr-metadata-validate.yml`'s
  "alp.lock generator self-check" step and `scripts/test-all.sh`'s
  `stage_alp_lock` call the same unchanged CLI invocation, so only its
  internal behaviour moved. This is a real, not cosmetic, reduction in what
  `--check` catches: a `build_lock` regression that stays schema-valid --
  a narrowed `_METADATA_DIGEST_GLOBS`, a dropped west project, a digest
  over the wrong directory (the #1045 bug class) -- no longer fails CI. The
  `digests.metadata` glob-coverage half of that is still held by
  `tests/scripts/test_alp_lock_metadata_coverage.py`; nothing now holds
  `_west_projects`/`_libraries` regressing the same way. `scripts/test-all.sh`
  now guards `stage_alp_lock` with the same `require_jsonschema_2020` probe
  as the other jsonschema-2020-12 stages (`alp_lock.py` imports `jsonschema`
  at module scope with no fallback, so a too-old jsonschema previously
  reddened the stage instead of SKIPping, #1396/#1423's exact harm).
- `scripts/check_sbom.py` builds the lock in memory (`alp_lock.build_lock`)
  instead of reading a committed `alp.lock` from disk.
- `.github/workflows/release.yml` generates `alp.lock` before packaging the
  source tarball and appends it into the tarball (`tar --append` after
  `git archive`, since `git archive` only knows tracked files) so a consumer
  with only the tarball -- not a git checkout -- still gets one; `gen_sbom.py`
  reads it from there for the SBOM step, unchanged. The append pins
  `--owner=root:0 --group=root:0 --mode=644` and a `--mtime` derived from the
