  read `cfg->parity`/`cfg->baudrate` either), so they compile against the
  wider struct with no behaviour change.

**Not wired up by this change, and deliberately so:** which E1M/carrier pads
actually carry RTS/CTS is per-SoM metadata that does not exist in the tree
today -- no board currently routes those lines. Emitting Zephyr's
`hw-flow-control` devicetree property or the corresponding pinmux
(`scripts/alp_project.py`) needs that real pad data first; inventing it would
violate this repo's "never invent hardware facts" rule. A caller drives
`flow_control` through the portable API today only on a board whose own
`boards/*.overlay` already routes and pin-muxes RTS/CTS for the target UART
node.

Labelled `needs-silicon`: proving flow control actually prevents overrun
needs a real run at a high baud rate against a real peer, which `native_sim`
cannot show and this change was not bench-verified against. Failure-path and
mapping coverage lands with the code (native_sim ztest for the
`ALP_UART_FLOW_XON_XOFF` NOSUPPORT-on-Zephyr path; a pure-function unit test
for the Linux termios bit mapping); the RTS/CTS overrun-prevention claim
itself remains a bench-gated follow-up.

### Changed — `<alp/cap_instance.h>` reshaped to a two-word vocabulary that can say "not reported" (#1640)

`alp_capabilities_t` had one problem no bit could fix: `flags == 0` meant both
"the backend has nothing" and "the backend never spoke", and the ADC-only
`ALP_INSTANCE_CAP_HW_OVERSAMPLE` / `HW_TRIGGER` / `DIFFERENTIAL` bits lived in
the universal enum, one class away from colliding with an unrelated class's
future bit at the same position.

**`flags` is now universal-only.** `ALP_INSTANCE_CAP_DIFFERENTIAL` and
`ALP_INSTANCE_CAP_HW_TRIGGER`/`HW_OVERSAMPLE` are gone from
`alp_instance_cap_t`; the equivalent ADC facts are `ALP_ADC_CAP_HW_OVERSAMPLE`
/ `ALP_ADC_CAP_HW_TRIGGER` / `ALP_ADC_CAP_DIFFERENTIAL` in `<alp/adc.h>`,
carried in a new `alp_capabilities_t.class_flags` word whose meaning belongs
to the class header of the handle you queried. A new universal bit,
**`ALP_INSTANCE_CAP_REPORTED`**, disambiguates the old zero: unset means "the
backend never populated this descriptor", set means every other bit — in
`flags` or `class_flags` — and `channel_count == 0` is now an affirmative
answer, not silence. `alp_backend_t` grows a matching `base_class_flags`
field so a registry entry can seed `class_flags` the same way `base_caps`
already seeds `flags`; every `src/*_dispatch.c` that pre-seeds `flags` from
`base_caps` now pre-seeds `class_flags` from `base_class_flags` too, in
lockstep. `alp_capabilities_t.max_sample_rate` is renamed `max_rate_hz` to
match what it actually gates (ADC samples/s, I2C/SPI bus clock, PWM carrier).

**The 97-site trap this closes:** across `src/backends/**`, 77 backend
`open()`/`probe()` functions unconditionally wrote `caps_out->flags = 0u;`
into a `caps_out` the dispatcher had *already pre-seeded* from the registry's
`base_caps` (`src/adc_dispatch.c:108` ("alp_capabilities_t caps = { .flags = be->base_caps"),
`src/i2c_dispatch.c:74` ("alp_capabilities_t caps = { .flags = be->base_caps"), and every
sibling `*_dispatch.c`) — a backend "with nothing to say" was clobbering
whatever the registry had already declared, silently. Wave 1 deletes every
one of those 97 lines; the fix is deletion, not population — a backend that
has nothing to add now leaves the pre-seeded descriptor alone. No capability
is lost *today*: of those 77 files, none had a non-zero `base_caps` to
clobber — only `src/backends/adc/alif_e7.c` and `alif_e8.c` (never touched
`caps_out->flags`) and `src/backends/gpu2d/alif_dave2d.c` (re-asserted the
same value it was seeded with) had anything real to report, and all three now
set `ALP_INSTANCE_CAP_REPORTED` explicitly. This closes a **latent** trap —
the next backend to declare a non-zero `base_caps` for a class whose backend
still zeroed `flags` would have had it silently discarded — and fixes a
real ambiguity, not a live data-loss bug.

`include/alp/counter.h`'s capability doc no longer describes the
GD32-bridge-only `channel_count` ambiguity as unavoidable: it now points at
`ALP_INSTANCE_CAP_REPORTED` as the disambiguator, noting that no counter
backend sets it yet so the two cases still collapse to "not reported" today.

Regression coverage: `tests/unit/backend_registry/src/test_capabilities.c`
(the reported/not-reported/affirmative-absence contract directly),
`tests/unit/adc_registry/src/test_adc_registry.c` and
`tests/unit/backend_registry/src/test_registry.c` (`base_caps`/
`base_class_flags` survive to the public getter), and
`tests/unit/i2c_registry/src/test_i2c_registry.c::test_sw_fallback_leaves_preseeded_caps_untouched`,
which seeds a sentinel `alp_capabilities_t` before calling the real
`sw_fallback` `ops->open()` and fails if a future edit re-introduces a
`caps_out->flags = 0u;` clobber.

### Added — dispatcher-side guard on the 41 previously-unguarded ops-vtable call sites (#1641)

15 of the 33 `src/*_dispatch.c` class dispatchers called an op-table function
pointer (`h->state.ops->read`, `->write`, `->start`, ...) with only `open`/
`close` checked `!= NULL` at backend registration — every other slot was
trusted to be populated. This is **not a live crash fix**: every in-tree ops
table that leaves a non-`close` slot NULL is protected structurally at open
today — `src/backends/spi/testing_drv.c`'s `target_open`/`target_transceive`/
`target_close` are all NULL, but `alp_spi_target_open()` rejects a NULL
`target_open` with `ALP_ERR_NOSUPPORT` before a target handle ever exists
(same pattern in `src/backends/i2c/testing_drv.c` and
`src/backends/usb/yocto_drv.c`), so no reachable NULL-deref existed in-tree
before this change. It closes a **contract gap** in the dispatcher/backend
ABI — the first partial vendor port that leaves a *reachable* op slot unset
would have hit it.

`adc_dispatch.c`, `camera_dispatch.c`, `counter_dispatch.c`, `dac_dispatch.c`,
`display_dispatch.c`, `gpu2d_dispatch.c`, `i2c_dispatch.c`, `i3c_dispatch.c`,
`jpeg_dispatch.c`, `power_dispatch.c`, `qenc_dispatch.c`, `rtc_dispatch.c`,
`spi_dispatch.c`, `uart_dispatch.c` and `wdt_dispatch.c` now guard all 41
sites the same way `storage_dispatch.c` already did: `ops->foo == NULL` ->
`ALP_ERR_NOSUPPORT`, exactly one `alp_handle_op_leave()` per exit path.
`<alp/adc.h>`, `<alp/counter.h>`, `<alp/dac.h>`, `<alp/rtc.h>` and
`<alp/wdt.h>` gained `ALP_ERR_NOSUPPORT` on the `@return` lists of the
functions where it is now a reachable outcome (the other seven headers
already documented it).

`tests/zephyr/conformance/src/main.c` adds a guard-mutation proof: it opens a
real UART handle, points it at a local copy of its own backend's ops table
with `write` NULLed, and asserts `alp_uart_write()` returns
`ALP_ERR_NOSUPPORT`. Reverting the guard under test turns a pass into a
SIGSEGV (`rc=-11`) that blocks the two ZTESTs after it — proof the guard is
load-bearing, not decorative. This exercises 1 of the 41 guarded sites; all
41 are the identical `ops->foo == NULL -> ALP_ERR_NOSUPPORT` shape, so the
one case stands for the class, but it is not per-site test coverage.

### Fixed — DAC/I3C admission now consults the backend registry, not a SoC cap-table count that inverted itself to zero (#1642)

`alp_dac_open()` and `alp_i3c_open()` carried a dispatch-level admission gate
shaped `if ((ALP_SOC_<CLASS>_COUNT > 0) && id >= ALP_SOC_<CLASS>_COUNT) reject`.
The `> 0` term meant the gate went permissive exactly when a SoC's count was
`0` — the one case a "reject an unsupported instance" gate exists to catch.
Both guarding comments were also wrong: `src/dac_dispatch.c` claimed
`ALP_SOC_DAC_COUNT` is `0` under `CONFIG_ALP_SOC_NONE` (it is `UINT16_MAX`,
the accept-any sentinel, in `include/alp/soc_caps.h`), and
`src/i3c_dispatch.c` claimed the `> 0` term rejects "a SoC that genuinely has
no I3C" when it does the opposite — skips the check entirely there.

A naive fix (flip the condition to reject when the count is `0`) is wrong too:
`src/backends/dac/gd32_bridge.c` registers an *exact* `silicon_ref` match for
`renesas:rzv2n:n44`, a SoC whose `ALP_SOC_DAC_COUNT` is `0` (it has no on-die
DAC), and serves channels 0/1 over the GD32 IO-MCU bridge. Rejecting on the
cap-table count would refuse a DAC that genuinely works on that SoM.

Both gates are deleted. Admission is now the backend registry alone —
`alp_backend_select()` plus each backend's own `open()`-time bound check —
matching the pattern every other class dispatcher (`adc`, `counter`,
`inference`, ...) already uses; none of them ever had a dispatch-level
instance-count gate. `src/dac_dispatch.c` and `src/i3c_dispatch.c` were the
only two sites in `src/` with this shape (confirmed by grep across `src/`
for the `_COUNT > 0` pattern — no other class dispatcher shares it, so no
sibling fix is needed).

Two `tests/zephyr/peripheral/` scenario tests that pinned the old gate's
behaviour (`test_dac_out_of_range_channel`, `test_i3c_out_of_range_bus`) are
updated: the specific `ALP_ERR_INVAL` assertion under a finite, non-`NONE`
SoC count is dropped, since which error a now-selected backend returns for
an out-of-range instance (`NOSUPPORT` if it declines outright, `INVAL` if it
bounds-checks the instance itself) is backend-specific, not a dispatch
contract. A new test,
`test_dac_bridged_channel_admitted_despite_zero_soc_count` (gated on
`CONFIG_ALP_SDK_V2N_SUPERVISOR`), pins the corrected decision directly: on
`renesas:rzv2n:n44` (`ALP_SOC_DAC_COUNT == 0`), `alp_backend_select("dac",
ALP_SOC_REF_STR)` still resolves to `gd32_bridge`, and opening channel 0
reaches that backend's `open()` and fails for the real hardware reason (no
GD32 bus configured — supervisor `ALP_ERR_NOT_READY`), not a cap-table
refusal. Confirmed this test (and `test_v2n_supervisor_dac_open_not_ready_
without_buses`) both fail under the naive "reject on count == 0" fix, then
reverted that probe.

Per ADR-0002 as amended (`docs/adr/0002-error-mechanism.md`), the deleted
gate's `ALP_ERR_INVAL` for an out-of-range instance was itself the wrong
code for "config exceeds hardware caps" (the ADR's original decision reserves
`ALP_ERR_OUT_OF_RANGE` for that, distinct from `ALP_ERR_INVAL` "programmer
error") — moot now that the gate is gone rather than recoded, since the
still-existing `be == NULL` branch (`ALP_ERR_NOT_PRESENT_ON_THIS_SOC`) and
each backend's own bound check are unchanged and outside this fix's scope.

The broader redesign the issue also describes — a declarative
`instance_count` field on `alp_backend_t` plus honoring the existing
`probe()` hook's return value as the admission verdict across all 16
dispatchers that currently discard it — needs its own design pass and is not
part of this change.

### Added — `<alp/rpc.h>` link-liveness signal (issue #1643)

A far core resetting or crashing used to be invisible: nothing surfaced the
transport's own bind/unbind signal, so `alp_rpc_send()` kept returning
`ALP_OK` into a dead vring forever, indistinguishable from an idle peer.

- **`alp_rpc_link_state_t`** (`ALP_RPC_LINK_DOWN` / `_UP` / `_LOST`),
  **`alp_rpc_link_cb_t`**, **`alp_rpc_set_link_callback()`**, and
  **`alp_rpc_link_state()`** — new, purely additive `<alp/rpc.h>` surface
  (ABI-STABLE, minor bump).
- The dispatcher's internal `alp_rpc_notify_link()` hook
  (`src/backends/rpc/rpc_ops.h` / `src/rpc_dispatch.c`) enforces the header's
  documented invariant with a compare-and-swap: `ALP_RPC_LINK_LOST` is only
  ever accepted from `ALP_RPC_LINK_UP`, so a link that never bound stays
  `DOWN` rather than getting permanently poisoned by an out-of-order notify.
- `src/backends/rpc/yocto_drv.c` (Linux/A-class chardev backend) reports UP
  once `/dev/rpmsg<N>` opens — strictly **before** its rx thread starts, so
  an already-dead peer's first `poll()`/`read()` failure can't have its LOST
  clobbered back to UP by a late UP notify — and LOST on either a `poll()`
  failure or a `read()` EOF/error (both end the same thread, so both now
  report the same state; only the wake-pipe close-side branch stays silent).
- `src/backends/rpc/zephyr_drv.c` wires `ipc_service`'s `bound` + `unbound` +
  `error` endpoint callbacks (previously only `bound` + `received`), all
  three bracketed by the same `rpc_recv_enter()`/`rpc_worker_leave()`
  closing-gate `received` already used — closing a same-channel-close-from-
  inside-the-link-callback hole `bound()` had before this fix (see below).
  **However**: the ONLY `ipc_service` backend `CONFIG_ALP_SDK_RPC` permits
  (`depends on IPC_SERVICE_BACKEND_RPMSG && OPENAMP`) is the pinned Zephyr
  v4.4.1 RPMsg static-vrings backend, which invokes `bound`/`received` only
  — never `unbound`/`error` (confirmed against the pinned tree; those two
  are invoked exclusively by the ICMsg backend family, which this Kconfig
  does not select). **So in this revision, on Zephyr, `ALP_RPC_LINK_UP` is
  reliably reported but `ALP_RPC_LINK_LOST` is NOT observable at all** — the
  wiring is real, tested, and forward-compatible (it goes live the day
  upstream propagates ns-unbind through `ipc_service`, or a future backend
  swap lands), but structurally unreachable today. See
  `src/backends/rpc/zephyr_drv.c`'s `@par Link liveness` file comment.
- **Net effect for the two SoM families this issue names**: neither AEN
  (an all-Zephyr M55↔M55 pair) nor V2N's A55 (whose `silicon_ref` selects
  `src/backends/rpc/yocto_uio_drv.c`, not wired for link liveness at all —
  see below) can produce `ALP_RPC_LINK_LOST` in this revision. The only
  backend that can today is the plain Linux chardev path
  (`yocto_drv.c`) on a peer that isn't V2N's A55.
- `src/backends/rpc/yocto_uio_drv.c` (RZ/V2N's userspace-virtio path, which
  wins over `yocto_drv.c` on every V2N `silicon_ref`) is **not** wired in
  this revision — its remoteproc/virtio teardown shape has no equivalent to
  the chardev backend's poll()+read() EOF signal, and this issue is
  `needs-silicon`; tracked as follow-up. This is the primary remaining gap
  for V2N, not a footnote: it is the one backend that would let V2N's A55
  detect its CM33 peer dying.
- `src/backends/rpc/sw_fallback.c` stays DOWN forever (no synthetic peer
  under native_sim); `src/common/stub/stub_rpc.c` returns `ALP_ERR_NOSUPPORT`
  for both new functions on the bare-metal build.

**Two correctness fixes alongside the above, both covered by new/extended
tests:**
- `zephyr_drv.c`'s `rpc_ept_bound()` (the UP notify) is now bracketed by the
  same `rpc_recv_enter()`/`rpc_worker_leave()` gate `unbound`/`error` use.
  It previously ran unbracketed on the theory that `bound()` "cannot
  plausibly race a self-close" — refuted by the very next line, which
  invokes the app's registered link callback, and that callback closing its
  own channel from inside `bound()` was misclassified as an external close
  (reentrant `ipc_service_deregister_endpoint()` from inside `ipc_service`'s
  own `bound` callback) and left `bound` uncounted against a concurrent
  external close racing the same slot.
- `alp_rpc_call()` gains the same entry-only `ALP_RPC_LINK_LOST` gate
  `alp_rpc_send()` already has — a NEW call is rejected before reaching the
  backend once the link is known LOST. This does not wake a call already in
  flight (see below).

**Behaviour change on the existing surface (documented, not slipped in):**
once a channel has observed `ALP_RPC_LINK_LOST`, `alp_rpc_send()` and a NEW
`alp_rpc_call()` now fail with `ALP_ERR_NOT_READY` instead of accepting into
the dead queue — the SAME return value the header already documented for a
NULL/closed channel, now also covering a known-dead link. An
ALREADY-in-flight `alp_rpc_call()` is unaffected: it keeps its own
`timeout_ms` defense and is not woken early by a link-loss notification
(unblocking an in-flight call from a transport callback crosses the
GHSA-xhm8-7f87-93q5 close-protocol's handle-lifetime rules and needs its
own, separately-reviewed change).

Bench-gated (`needs-silicon`): whether `yocto_drv.c`'s rx thread reports
`ALP_RPC_LINK_LOST` within a bounded time against a real peer's chardev EOF,
without a false positive on a merely-busy link, has not been attempted on
real hardware. (Whether Zephyr's `unbound` vs `error` fires for a far-core
reset is *not* a needs-silicon question in this revision — neither is
reachable under the pinned RPMsg static-vrings backend; see above.)

### Fixed — BLE self-close and mbox close left two use-after-free-shaped gaps (#1644)

`alp_ble_scan_start()`'s deferred self-close branch — taken when `alp_ble_close()`
is called reentrantly from inside a scan callback (#756) — called `_free_radio(h)`
with **no `_conn_pool` walk at all**. #1697 added that walk to `alp_ble_close()`
only, so a radio closed from inside its own scan callback while connections were
live left every `c->state.radio` back-pointer dangling at a recycled radio slot.
The walk is now factored into a shared `_disconnect_radio_conns()` helper called
from both `alp_ble_close()` and the self-close branch, at the same point in each
(after the op drain, before `ops->close()`), so the two teardown paths cannot
drift apart again the way they just did.

`src/backends/mproc/zephyr_drv.c`'s `z_mbox_close()` disabled the channel and
freed its `mbox_be` state, but never called `mbox_register_callback(..., NULL,
NULL)` first — `z_mbox_set_callback()` registers that same `mbox_be` pointer as
the Zephyr mbox driver's callback `user_data`, so the registration outlived the
memory it pointed at. `z_mbox_close()` now unregisters before freeing (disable →
unregister → free). This is defence-in-depth restoring the documented invariant
("stop backend callbacks before the slot is released"), not a demonstrated live
crash — with the channel already disabled the stale registration is not known to
be reachable.

Regression coverage: `tests/yocto/ble_dispatch_conn_pool_orphan.c` gains a fourth
scenario (`test_self_close_releases_conn_slots`) driving the self-close path with
a live connection and asserting the conn slot is released and the peer link
disconnected through the backend — mutation-tested by reverting only the new
`_disconnect_radio_conns()` call on the self-close branch (fails 2/2 assertions)
and restoring it (passes 24/24 in that binary).

### Fixed — six caller- or peer-supplied lengths reached a memcpy or a DMA master with no bound (#1645)

A standing-code audit of `src/` + `include/alp/` found six sites where a
length that came from the caller or from the far side of a link reached a
copy or a hardware DMA master unchecked against the destination it actually
described. Two more sites in the same class are tracked separately (#1619,
and the CAN `payload_len` site) and are not restated here.

- **`src/jpeg_dispatch.c`** now rejects, before either JPEG backend ever
  sees the request: a nonzero `y_stride`/`u_stride`/`v_stride` smaller than
  the row it claims to describe (`ALP_ERR_INVAL`), and `width`/`height`
  beyond the opened backend's own advertised `max_width`/`max_height`
  (`ALP_ERR_OUT_OF_RANGE`) — previously unenforced, so a caller-chosen
  width/height had no upper bound before the length derived from it (a
  plane stride, or `alif_hantro.c`'s DMA span) reached a backend. A backend
  advertising 0/0 caps (the `ALP_ERR_NOT_IMPLEMENTED` stub in
  `zephyr_stub.c`, which has no real bound to advertise) is exempt from the
  max-dimension check, so it still reaches its own `encode()` and returns
  its documented `ALP_ERR_NOT_IMPLEMENTED` instead of every request being
  rejected here with `ALP_ERR_OUT_OF_RANGE` first. A zero stride stays a
  valid "tightly packed" sentinel; the dispatcher now normalizes it to
  `width` (`width`/2 for chroma) **once**, in the one place both backends'
  encode paths route through, instead of leaving each backend to
  reimplement the default — `sw_baseline.c`'s vendored TooJpeg encoder
  never did, so `y_stride == 0` used to alias every output row onto row 0
  (`ALP_OK`, silently wrong image, not a crash).
- **`src/backends/jpeg/alif_hantro.c`** derives the Hantro DMA engine's
  input span from that same now width/height-bounded frame before asking
  `_is_dma_reachable()` whether the range is safe to program into the AXI
  master's registers — `_is_dma_reachable()` itself only checks the range
  against the core-local TCM windows, never against the caller's real
  allocation, so an unbounded width previously made that check pass on a
  range the caller did not own. Width/height are now bounded by the
  backend's own advertised max; an explicit `y_stride`/`u_stride`/
  `v_stride` is only floor-checked (>= the row it claims to describe), both
  here and in `src/jpeg_dispatch.c` — a stride larger than the caller's
  real plane allocation still reaches a backend unchanged, because neither
  the dispatcher nor a backend is handed the plane's real buffer length to
  check a larger stride against (see the updated `@note` on
  `alp_jpeg_encode()` in `include/alp/jpeg.h`). The duplicate `pitch =
  (y_stride != 0 ...) ? ... : width` at the `video_set_format()` call site
  now reuses the one `in_stride` computed above instead of re-deriving it,
  so the two can no longer diverge.
- **`src/backends/rpc/yocto_uio_drv.c`** (`uio_ept_cb()`) and
  **`src/backends/rpc/yocto_drv.c`** (`rpc_rx_main()`) used to silently clip
  an inbound rpmsg frame larger than `ALP_RPC_TX_FRAME_MAX` (1024 B) and
  dispatch the truncated prefix as a complete message — `alp_rpc_call()`
  returned `ALP_OK` with a partial response and no signal anything was
  dropped. Both now drop the frame instead: a per-channel
  `rx_oversized_drops` counter (visible only in the `stderr` log line each
  drop emits — there is no `<alp/rpc.h>` accessor for it) plus that log
  line, rather than a guessed-at partial parse. The chardev path
  (`yocto_drv.c`) has no `len` field to compare against — `read()` never
  reports more than the buffer it was given — so its read buffer is now
  sized one byte past `ALP_RPC_TX_FRAME_MAX`, and only a read that actually
  fills that extra byte (`n > ALP_RPC_TX_FRAME_MAX`) counts as oversized; a
  legitimate exactly-`ALP_RPC_TX_FRAME_MAX`-byte frame is no longer dropped.
- **`src/backends/mqtt/zephyr_drv.c`**'s `MQTT_EVT_PUBLISH` handler read a
  broker payload larger than `rx_buf` up to `rx_buf`'s capacity and then
  sent the QoS-1 PUBACK without draining the remainder off the wire.
  Zephyr's `mqtt_client::internal.remaining_payload` never reached 0, so
  every subsequent `mqtt_input()` returned `-EBUSY` — one oversized publish
  permanently wedged the connection, *after* the broker had already been
  told delivery succeeded and would not retry. A new `mqtt_drain_remaining()`
  helper (shared with the existing `msg_cb == NULL` branch, which already
  drained correctly) now reads and discards the excess before the PUBACK.
- **`src/yocto/inference_deepx.cpp`**'s `alp_inference_deepx_invoke()` hands
  dx_rt's `Run()` a single pointer, `input_bufs[0].data()`, which dx_rt
  treats as the base of one contiguous blob concatenating every input
  tensor. This backend stages each input in its own *separate*
  `std::vector` allocation, so any model declaring more than one input
  would have made dx_rt read past `input_bufs[0]`'s real allocation and DMA
  whatever unrelated heap memory follows it over PCIe to the DX-M1.
  `alp_inference_deepx_open()` now refuses (`ALP_ERR_NOSUPPORT`) any model
  with more than one declared input until a real concatenating staging
  buffer exists, rather than mis-run on first multi-input DEEPX bring-up.

`include/alp/jpeg.h`'s `alp_jpeg_encode()` doc comment is updated for the
new `ALP_ERR_OUT_OF_RANGE` return, the expanded `ALP_ERR_INVAL` case, and to
state precisely what the new dispatcher checks bound: `width`/`height`
against the backend's advertised max, and stride only against a floor —
never an upper bound, since a caller-supplied stride is checked against no
buffer-length parameter the SDK is ever given. New regression coverage:
`tests/unit/jpeg_registry` (native_sim ztest) locks down the max-dimension
reject, the undersized-stride reject, and — by comparing an implicit
(`y_stride == 0`) encode byte-for-byte against an explicit-stride encode of
the same distinguishing-content frame — that the zero-stride sentinel now
normalizes instead of aliasing every row onto row 0;
`tests/yocto/inference_deepx_regression.cpp` (built against the existing
clean-room dx_rt fake, no real DEEPX hardware) locks down the multi-input
open() refusal and confirms a single-input model is unaffected;
`tests/unit/jpeg_zero_caps_exempt` (native_sim ztest, its own executable so
its priority-255 test-double backend can't hijack `jpeg_registry`'s
arbitration) locks down that a backend advertising 0/0 `max_width`/
`max_height` is exempt from the `ALP_ERR_OUT_OF_RANGE` check and still
reaches its own `encode()`.

**Bench-gated:** the `alif_hantro.c` and `inference_deepx.cpp` fixes cannot
be verified end-to-end without E1M-AEN801 (Alif E8, Hantro JPEG) and
E1M-V2M101/102 (DEEPX DX-M1 over PCIe) silicon respectively — both are
reviewed by inspection and, for DEEPX, against the fake-dx_rt regression
harness, not proven on real hardware. The jpeg-dispatcher and rpc fixes
are logic reviewed and compiled (`gcc`/`g++ -Wall -Wextra`, real
macro-gated code paths, not the NOSUPPORT stub arm) outside `native_sim`;
`tests/unit/jpeg_registry` additionally passes 9/9 under
`twister -p native_sim/native/64` (`-s alp.unit.jpeg_registry`). The mqtt
fix's real `CONFIG_ALP_SDK_IOT_MQTT` arm is logic reviewed only: it needs
Zephyr's own headers (`<zephyr/net/mqtt.h>`), which a bare `gcc`/`g++`
cannot resolve, and no `prj.conf`/`board.yaml` in this repo turns that
symbol on for `native_sim`, so no gate here compiles it.

### Fixed — 12 of 122 `alp_handle_op_enter()` failure sites returned `ALP_ERR_INVAL` instead of `ALP_ERR_NOT_READY` (#1646)

`alp_handle_op_enter()` returning `false` means exactly one thing: the handle is closed or
closing. 110 call sites across `src/` already reported that as `ALP_ERR_NOT_READY`; twelve
sites in `src/update_log_dispatch.c`, `src/dsp_dispatch.c`, and `src/i2c_regfile.c` reported
`ALP_ERR_INVAL` instead, indistinguishable from a genuine caller bug (a bad argument). All
twelve now return `ALP_ERR_NOT_READY`, matching the other 110. `dsp_dispatch.c`'s four sites
carried a comment saying the `ALP_ERR_INVAL` was deliberately preserved "to match this op's
pre-#629 null/not-in-use contract" -- `git log -S` confirms #629 itself (`8d861decf`) wrote
that comment, choosing at the time to keep the pre-#629 `ALP_ERR_INVAL` contract rather than
adopt the `ALP_ERR_NOT_READY` convention it was introducing everywhere else. That was a real,
deliberate decision, not stale leftover -- but this repo has no active customers to protect
from the behaviour change, so #1646 drops it same as the other eleven sites.

**NULL-handle rule, decided here:** `src/ble_dispatch.c`'s `alp_ble_gatt_notify()` originally
fused `conn == NULL` (a caller bug) with the `op_enter` failure (a normal disconnect racing
this notify) into one `if`, both mapped to `ALP_ERR_INVAL` -- an early draft of this fix split
the two, keeping `conn == NULL` on `ALP_ERR_INVAL` per ADR-0002's "`ALP_ERR_INVAL` = programmer
error" framing. That draft was self-contradictory: `i2c_regfile.c`'s two sites and
`dsp_dispatch.c`'s four keep their `X == NULL ||` fused with the `op_enter` check and now map
NULL to `ALP_ERR_NOT_READY` too -- so the same PR would have shipped two different answers to
"what does a NULL handle return" depending on which of the twelve sites you're looking at.
Resolved by **matching the dominant house convention instead of inventing a third rule**: ~104
of the 110 already-compliant call sites fuse `X == NULL ||` into the `op_enter` check and return
`ALP_ERR_NOT_READY` for both. `ble_dispatch.c`'s split is reverted; `conn == NULL` now falls
through the same fused check as every sibling and returns `ALP_ERR_NOT_READY`. ADR-0002's
"`ALP_ERR_INVAL` is a programmer error" rule is not actually implemented at 104 of 110 existing
op_enter sites -- retrofitting real ADR-0002 compliance across the codebase is a separate,
much larger change than #1646 (which is scoped to op_enter-status *drift*, i.e. making the
sibling sites agree with each other). Introducing a fresh split at exactly the site this cluster
touches would be the same kind of drift #1646 exists to fix. Next person: if you want to revisit
NULL -> `ALP_ERR_INVAL` codebase-wide, that's a new issue against all ~114 fused sites, not a
re-litigation of cluster 1.

`src/ble_dispatch.c`'s new `ALP_ERR_NOT_READY` leg (a live `conn` whose owner disconnected
between `alp_ble_gatt_notify()`'s argument check and its `op_enter`) had no test coverage --
`tests/zephyr/ble/src/main.c` only ever exercised `alp_ble_gatt_notify(NULL, NULL, 0, NULL, 0)`,
which returns at the earlier `h == NULL` gate and never reaches this leg. Added
`tests/zephyr/ble_gatt_notify_op_enter/`, a small dedicated suite that registers a fake `ble`
backend (priority 200, ahead of `zephyr_drv`'s 100) so it can drive
`alp_ble_open()`/`alp_ble_connect()`/`alp_ble_disconnect()` through the real
`src/ble_dispatch.c` on `native_sim` (which ships no real BLE controller) and assert both the
`conn == NULL` leg and the post-disconnect `op_enter`-failure leg return `ALP_ERR_NOT_READY`.
Kept out of `tests/zephyr/ble` so this always-succeeds fake backend never leaks into that
suite's "no controller -> `ALP_ERR_NOSUPPORT`" smoke test.

Also fixed six stale `@return` docs this change would otherwise have left behind (issues
#1517/#1518's defect class): `include/alp/i2c_regfile.h` (`alp_i2c_regfile_set_write_window`,
`alp_i2c_regfile_stats`) and `include/alp/dsp.h` (all four `alp_dsp_chain_apply_*` variants)
did not list `ALP_ERR_NOT_READY` at all; `include/alp/update_log.h`'s
`alp_update_log_append`/`alp_update_log_append_boot` omitted it, and
`alp_update_log_verify`/`_count`/`_get` had no `@return` error-code documentation whatsoever
for a reachable `ALP_ERR_NOT_READY` (and, for `_count`/`_get`, no `@return` tag at all) -- all
eight now document the real contract.

Cluster 1 of #1646 (`op_enter`-status drift); clusters 2 and 5 remain open.

Cluster 1's fix (`changelog.d/1646.md`'s original entry, folded into `CHANGELOG.md` at release)
normalized `op_enter`-status drift but deliberately left ADR-0002's own text unamended, noting
"retrofitting real ADR-0002 compliance across the codebase is a separate, much larger change
than #1646." This entry is that separate, docs-only follow-up: it does not touch dispatcher
code, it writes down what the code (as landed by cluster 1) actually does.

`docs/adr/0002-error-mechanism.md` gained a dated Amendment (2026-08-27, original text left
intact) with two parts. First, a **scope correction**: the ADR's "programmer error" parenthetical
(split across the Context section's `bus_id` bullet and the Decision section's
`ALP_ERR_OUT_OF_RANGE` sentence) contrasts three `open()`-time codes only — it never defined
`ALP_ERR_INVAL` for the whole public API, so the ~115 non-`open()` sites returning
`ALP_ERR_NOT_READY` for a NULL primary handle were never in violation; they were simply outside
what the ADR governed. Second, the **convention as measured**: `ALP_ERR_NOT_READY` for a handle
(primary, or a secondary handle threaded through the same `alp_handle_op_enter` lifecycle guard —
`alp_ble_gatt_notify`'s `conn`, per cluster 1's fix above, is the only such site in the whole
surface); `ALP_ERR_INVAL` for a malformed argument outside that guard (NULL `cfg`, a NULL
out-buffer with nonzero length); `ALP_ERR_NOSUPPORT` for a missing capability. A wider set of
pre-existing, deliberate per-site outliers (`src/adc_dispatch.c`'s two sites plus its
`alif_e7`/`alif_e8` vendor-extension twins, `src/jpeg_dispatch.c` plus its build-stub twin,
`src/update_log_dispatch.c`'s five unfused NULL-handle checks, and a dozen more `alp_<vendor>_*`
ext entry points) are named and left unchanged — two of the three families are pinned by
`tests/unit/adc_registry` and `tests/unit/jpeg_registry` assertions, which argues *for*
grandfathering rather than the earlier (wrong) claim that nothing consumes the distinction.
Separately, the Yocto/Linux peripheral backend (`src/yocto/peripheral_{gpio,i2c,spi,uart}.c`)
turns out to answer `ALP_ERR_INVAL` for a closed handle too, not just NULL — a whole-backend
divergence from the Zephyr dispatchers' `ALP_ERR_NOT_READY`, recorded as a known, unresolved gap
rather than folded into the per-site outlier list. `docs/adr/README.md`'s ADR-0002 row notes
the amendment.

`metadata/error-catalog.json`'s `ALP_ERR_NOT_READY` summary changed from "Peripheral not
initialised." (too narrow — a closed or mid-operation handle is "not ready" without ever having
been uninitialised) to "The handle is not in a state to perform this operation." No cross-repo
follow-up needed: tan-cli's `explain`-command tests assert a locally-defined fixture string, not
this catalog value.

signex could not be checked for a dependency on these status codes — no signex checkout exists on
the host this amendment was written from. Noted as an open gap in the Amendment text rather than
asserted clean.

### Fixed — `alp_gpu2d_format_t` no longer collides numerically with `alp_pixfmt_t` (#1647)

`alp_gpu2d_format_t` (`include/alp/gpu2d.h`) and `alp_pixfmt_t`
(`include/alp/peripheral.h`) are two public pixel-format enums that share three
member names -- `RGB565`, `RGB888`, `ARGB8888` -- but disagreed on two of their
numeric values: `ARGB8888` was 0 in one and 3 in the other, `RGB888` was 3 in one
and 2 in the other. A caller wiring `alp_display_get_caps()`'s advertised
`alp_pixfmt_t` straight into an `alp_gpu2d_surface_t.format` got a silently
relabelled format -- garbled rendering, not a crash, since every wrong value was
still in range.

`alp_gpu2d_format_t`'s three shared members are renumbered to agree with
`alp_pixfmt_t`. `A8` and `RGBA8888` have no `alp_pixfmt_t` counterpart, so they
take the remaining values in the (still contiguous 0..4) enum.

`gpu2d.h` is `[ABI-EXPERIMENTAL]` and has no active customers, so this is a plain
value renumber, not a symbol removal -- no `docs/abi/removed-symbols.json` entry
applies. `scripts/abi_snapshot.py --diff` reports it as `CHANGED`, which is a
pass-with-warning on an experimental header.

### Fixed — `alp_display_config_t.allow_modeset` read as an unconditional promise the MCU backends do not keep (#1648 tier 2)

`include/alp/display.h`'s doxygen for `allow_modeset` states that
`alp_display_open` "returns `ALP_ERR_INVAL` unless the caller sets this
explicitly". Only the Yocto/Linux backend enforces that: the identifier appears
nowhere in `src/backends/display/zephyr_drv.c` or
`src/backends/display/zephyr_stub.c`, so a default-constructed config that is
refused on A55 opens normally on M55/M33. A customer reading the header on a
Zephyr target expects a refusal that never arrives.

The behaviour is correct; the documentation was not. The whole rationale in that
comment is KMS-specific -- the SDK becomes DRM master and issues
`DRM_IOCTL_MODE_SETCRTC`, and the kernel does not refuse when master is merely
unheld, so opening a display can silently take over an idle framebuffer console
or a VT-switched session. None of that exists on a Zephyr backend, which drives a
dedicated panel it already owns: there is no master to take and no session to
displace, so there is nothing for the flag to protect. Now stated as
Yocto-only, the same way `alp_storage_config_t.allow_unsafe_write` already
documents its own scope with "(ignored elsewhere)".

**Deliberately NOT changed: `allow_unsafe_write`.** #1648 tier 2 lists it as the
same defect, but it is not one -- `include/alp/storage.h` already documents it as
Yocto-only, and the asymmetry is load-bearing. On Linux
`/dev/mmcblk<N>` is the whole-disk node carrying GPT/MBR and the bootloader, and
on some boards `/dev/mtd0` IS the bootloader/FIP partition, so a defaulted config
must not be able to write. A Zephyr backend addresses a dedicated flash
partition, where writing is the ordinary intended operation. Making the Zephyr
backends "honour" the flag would refuse writes by default on every MCU target and
break every existing storage caller -- a regression dressed as a consistency fix.

Documentation only; no behaviour change and no ABI change (the snapshot
regenerates clean).

### Fixed — three portable config fields were accepted, never applied, and returned `ALP_OK` (#1648 tier 1)

`alp_audio_out_set_volume()` on a handle opened `ALP_AUDIO_FMT_S24_LE` / `ALP_AUDIO_FMT_S32_LE`
recorded the requested volume and returned `ALP_OK`, but both the Yocto/ALSA
(`src/backends/audio/yocto_drv.c`) and Zephyr/I2S (`src/backends/audio/zephyr_drv.c`) backends can
only software-scale `ALP_AUDIO_FMT_S16_LE` — so the handle kept playing at full scale regardless
of what the caller asked for, with no error anywhere. Both backends now refuse a non-unity volume
on a format they can't scale with `ALP_ERR_NOSUPPORT` at the `out_set_volume` entry point
(`src/backends/audio/yocto_drv.c:758`, `src/backends/audio/zephyr_drv.c:562`); setting 255
(full-scale, always a no-op) still succeeds on every format.

`src/backends/audio/yocto_drv.c`'s `configure_pcm()` also kept only the return code from
`snd_pcm_hw_params_set_rate_near()`, discarding the rate ALSA actually negotiated. Asking for a
rate the device doesn't support used to `open()` successfully while silently playing at the wrong
speed; `configure_pcm()` now compares the negotiated rate against the request and fails `open()`
with `ALP_ERR_NOSUPPORT` on a mismatch, logging both numbers (`src/backends/audio/yocto_drv.c:289-294`).
The negotiated *period* is deliberately **not** enforced the same way: `frames_per_block` is a
buffering hint, not a contract (`include/alp/audio.h:70`), and `snd_pcm_readi()` / `snd_pcm_writei()`
accept any frame count per call regardless of the device's period. `configure_pcm()` adopts whatever
ALSA negotiates for buffer sizing and only logs when it differs
(`src/backends/audio/yocto_drv.c:309-314`).

The ADC oversampling backends (`src/backends/adc/alif_e7.c`, `alif_e8.c`) converted the portable
`oversampling_ratio` (a RATIO) to Zephyr's `adc_sequence.oversampling` (a log2 EXPONENT) via
`__builtin_ctz()`, which silently rounds a non-power-of-two ratio down instead of failing — e.g. a
requested 3x or 6x both landed on 1x / 2x, `ALP_OK` either way. Both now refuse **any**
`oversampling_ratio` greater than 1x, not just a non-power-of-two one
(`src/backends/adc/alif_e8.c:170`, `src/backends/adc/alif_e7.c:157`): their vendored Alif driver
rejects every non-zero `adc_sequence.oversampling` outright, with no power-of-two carve-out
(`zephyr/drivers/adc/adc_alif.c:779` is `if (sequence->oversampling != 0U) { ... return -ENOTSUP;
}`), so a power-of-two ratio that passed the old, narrower guard still faulted every subsequent
`alp_adc_read_uv()` with `ALP_ERR_IO`. `ALP_INSTANCE_CAP_HW_OVERSAMPLE` is no longer advertised by
either backend's capability set — advertising a capability the vendor driver refuses outright was
the same silent-wrong-answer bug one layer up. The portable Zephyr ADC backend
(`src/backends/adc/zephyr_drv.c`) hardcoded `.oversampling = 0`, dropping the field entirely for
every vendor driver it might run against; it now refuses any ratio greater than 1x with
`ALP_ERR_NOSUPPORT` (`src/backends/adc/zephyr_drv.c:158`) rather than honouring a log2 mapping this
generic, multi-vendor backend has no single driver contract to trust — no ADC backend in this tree
honours a hardware oversampling ratio via that mapping today.

`src/backends/adc/gd32_bridge.c` (E1M-X V2N/V2M, one of four backends touching
`oversampling_ratio`) forwarded a non-power-of-two ratio straight to the GD32 firmware, which floors
it to the nearest power of two rather than refusing it (`docs/gd32-bridge-protocol.md:540`) — so
`oversampling_ratio = 6` returned `ALP_OK` and silently applied 4x, on the one backend where HW
oversampling actually works on real silicon. It now refuses a non-power-of-two ratio with the same
shared `alp_adc_oversampling_ratio_ok()` guard (`src/backends/adc/gd32_bridge.c:92`), which also
gained a `<= 256` ceiling: an unbounded power-of-two check let 512/1024/... pass despite sitting
above every ratio `include/alp/adc.h` documents as supported. The GD32 firmware's flooring behaviour
is unchanged — it is documented as intended and needs bench time to revisit.

No new capability was added: every one of these families becomes an honest `ALP_ERR_NOSUPPORT`
refusal (or, for the ALSA period, an adopted negotiated value) in place of the previous silent wrong
answer, per ADR-0002.

### Fixed — the Yocto/ALSA I²S backend threw away the negotiated sample rate, so an unsupported rate opened successfully and streamed at the wrong speed (#1648 tier 1)

`src/backends/i2s/yocto_drv.c`'s `_configure_pcm()` kept only the return code from
`snd_pcm_hw_params_set_rate_near()`, discarding the rate ALSA actually negotiated back through
its `&rate` argument. Asking for a rate the DAI doesn't support used to let `alp_i2s_open()`
succeed while every subsequent `alp_i2s_write()`/`alp_i2s_read()` streamed at whatever rate ALSA
picked instead — silently wrong, and in direct contradiction of `alp_i2s_open()`'s own doc
comment, which promises "an unsupported sample rate ... returns NULL here, not later."
`_configure_pcm()` now compares the negotiated rate against the request and fails open with
`ALP_ERR_NOSUPPORT` on a mismatch, logging both numbers.

**Scope: I²S class only.** `src/backends/audio/yocto_drv.c`'s `configure_pcm()` has the identical
`set_rate_near`-discards-`&rate` shape and carries the same silent-wrong-rate defect today — this
change does **not** touch it. That fix is scoped to a separate, still-open, bench-held PR (#1790)
that has not merged to `dev`. Until it lands, `alp_audio_out_open()`/`alp_audio_in_open()` on the
Yocto/ALSA path can still silently accept an unsupported rate and stream wrong.

The negotiated *period* is deliberately **not** enforced the same way, for the same reason the
audio backend's period is a hint rather than a contract there too: `block_frames` is a DMA-block
sizing hint, `snd_pcm_writei()` accepts any frame count per call regardless of the device's
period (`snd_pcm_readi()` likewise — it reports whatever count it actually read through
`bytes_out`, not a fixed period-sized chunk), and a `default` ALSA device commonly negotiates its
own fixed period (e.g. a dmix plugin) regardless of what `block_frames` asks for — refusing on a
period mismatch would fail `ALP_I2S_CONFIG_DEFAULT`'s 256-frame request against exactly that kind
of device. `_configure_pcm()` adopts whatever ALSA negotiates for buffer sizing and only logs
when the period differs from the request.

**Known gap, not touched here.** `alp_i2s_write()`'s doc comment (`include/alp/i2s.h`) also
promises that a `bytes` argument larger than the block size negotiated at open is "refused with
`ALP_ERR_OUT_OF_RANGE` rather than truncated," and `src/backends/i2s/zephyr_drv.c`'s `z_write()`
enforces exactly that. `y_write()` does not: it loops `snd_pcm_writei()` across as many ALSA
periods as `bytes` needs, so an oversize write still completes correctly instead of being
refused — a real, if benign, deviation from the documented contract that this change does not
fix.

No new capability, no ABI change: an honest `ALP_ERR_NOSUPPORT` refusal in place of a silent wrong
answer, per ADR-0002. `src/backends/i2s/zephyr_drv.c` was checked as the sibling backend and needs
no equivalent fix — Zephyr's `i2s_configure()` takes `frame_clk_freq` as an exact request and
fails outright rather than silently substituting a nearby rate, so it never had this defect.

**Bench-unverified.** This changes accepted behaviour on real hardware: a config that previously
opened successfully and streamed at a substituted rate now refuses at `alp_i2s_open()` with
`ALP_ERR_NOSUPPORT` when the negotiated rate doesn't match the request — for example,
`ALP_I2S_CONFIG_DEFAULT`'s 48000 Hz against a minimal Yocto image whose `/etc/asound.conf` aliases
`default` straight to a 44.1 kHz-only DAI with no resampling plugin. That refusal is the intended,
documented behaviour, but it is a behaviour change that has not been exercised on a Yocto target
with a real I²S DAI. Like the rest of `src/backends/i2s/yocto_drv.c`, this path is real-ALSA-device
code with no existing hermetic test harness (see the file's own `STATUS: ... BENCH-UNVERIFIED`
note) — bench time on real hardware is needed to observe the refusal firing correctly, matching
the `needs-silicon` label already on #1648. No bench evidence is claimed for this change.

### Fixed — `alp_pwm_configure()` refuses undefined `break_cfg` bits instead of passing them through (#1648)

`break_cfg` only defines `ALP_PWM_BREAK_EXTERNAL`. The dispatcher forwarded
any other bit to the backend unchecked: the GD32 bridge wrote it straight
into its break field, and a caller got `ALP_OK` for a request nothing
honoured. The dispatcher now returns `ALP_ERR_INVAL` for a bit outside the
`ALP_PWM_BREAK_*` flags, the same way it treats an out-of-range
`align_mode`. The non-GD32 backends (Zephyr, Yocto, software fallback,
stub) already return `ALP_ERR_NOSUPPORT` for `alp_pwm_configure()`, so no
other `break_cfg` path accepts a request without effect.

### Added

- `scripts/alp_project.py --emit scaffold` now accepts `--cores core_id:os[,core_id:os...]` as an alternative to `--template`: a selector that picks whichever catalog template's own `cores:` topology matches exactly, so an IDE wizard can name a core/OS mapping it already knows instead of hand-writing the scaffold's directory convention. `--template` is unchanged and remains fully supported; `--cores` resolves to the same template id and renders through the same `render_to_envelope()` path, so nothing already working changes. No exact topology match names the topologies that are on offer; more than one match asks for `--template` to disambiguate.

### Fixed — the ABI freeze gate read a header split as a removed symbol (#1661)

`scripts/abi_snapshot.py --diff` keys every symbol as `header::symbol`, so
relocating one between public headers — a header split, or lifting a hand-written
block into its generated `*_routes.h` sibling — read as `REMOVED` + `ADDED`. The
"ABI freeze gate vs the last released snapshot" step in
`.github/workflows/pr-generated-files.yml` greps for `^  REMOVED ` and fails the
PR, so a move that cost no consumer anything blocked as if a symbol had been
dropped.

The workflow already documents this shape against its own predecessor: comparing
to `v0.1` left *"~200 REMOVED/CHANGED entries ... none of them a real
regression"*, citing "header splits e.g. `dac.h` out of `adc.h` in v0.8.0".
Moving the baseline to the last release fixed the accumulation but not the
move-blindness, so every future split hit it again.

`--diff` now reports `MOVED` when the symbol name and category are unchanged,
its recorded hash is unchanged, **and** the old header still `#include`s the new
one — so a translation unit including the old header still sees it. `MOVED` does
not trip the gate; `REMOVED` still does.

**Reachability is proven from the tree, not assumed, and two restrictions on how
it is proven both err toward `REMOVED`.**

The first was a live security defect in the first cut of this change, not a
theoretical one. A naive scan recorded `#include` lines inside a false `#if` arm
that the preprocessor would never follow — a parser differential between this
scanner and `cpp`. `include/alp/board.h` selects between
`alp/boards/alp_e1m_x_evk_routes.h` and `alp/boards/alp_e1m_evk_routes.h` with
mutually exclusive arms and an `#else #error`; both were recorded as edges. A
symbol moved out of `board.h` into either routes header therefore read as `MOVED`
while every consumer building the **other** board had genuinely lost it — a real
ABI break, reported safe, by the gate whose only job is catching exactly that.
Demonstrated end-to-end before the fix, `rc=0` with the gate silent. Only
unconditional includes now count. The condition is never evaluated, only its
presence: *is this include unconditional?* is answerable from the text, *is this
arm taken?* is not, and guessing would rebuild the same differential one level up.

The include guard is **discovered** rather than assumed to be the outermost
conditional. A `#pragma once` header has no guard, so its first `#if` would
otherwise be mistaken for one and its conditional includes would count again; a
header opening a top-level `#if` above its guard would push real conditionals
down a level and lose its unconditional includes instead. Both shapes are pinned
by tests.

The second restriction is that reachability is **one hop**. A symbol moving to a
header reachable only transitively stays `REMOVED` — 136 transitive-only header
pairs exist in `include/alp/` today, so this is a real limit, and it is a false
`REMOVED`: noise a human resolves at review rather than a silent break.

The persisted snapshot schema is deliberately unchanged. The include graph is
computed fresh from disk inside `--diff` and never written, because
`pr-generated-files.yml` byte-diffs the regenerated current snapshot against the
committed copy — any schema addition would redden that gate regardless of
content. `--output` writes byte-identical bytes to before.

`docs/abi/README.md` documents the `MOVED` verdict and both restrictions, and
`tests/scripts/test_abi_snapshot_freeze_gate.py` runs the workflow's own step
against a real relocation, so the `MOVED` ↔ `grep -q '^  REMOVED '` coupling is
pinned at the gate level and not only in `diff()`'s unit tests.

### Added — CI gate: no two I2C devices may declare the same 7-bit address on the same bus (#1675)

`scripts/check_i2c_address_uniqueness.py` groups every declared I2C device by bus and by
7-bit address across `metadata/e1m_modules/*.yaml`'s `on_module.i2c_devices.<bus>.devices[]`,
`metadata/boards/*.yaml`'s flat top-level `i2c_devices:` list, and `metadata/boards/*.yaml`'s
`audio.codecs[]` list, and fails on any address claimed more than once on the same declared
bus. `assembled: false` devices are excluded; `assembled: optional` devices are NOT --
a part fitted only on some board variants still occupies its address when it is fitted.

The two pre-existing, open collisions this catches on the real tree (#1163: TMP112 vs
TPS628640, both on `brd_i2c` address `0x48` — TMP112 at
`metadata/e1m_modules/E1M-V2M101.yaml:51` and TPS628640's `deepx_lpddr_0v85` at
`metadata/e1m_modules/E1M-V2M101.yaml:57`, with the identical pair at
`metadata/e1m_modules/E1M-V2M102.yaml:47` and `metadata/e1m_modules/E1M-V2M102.yaml:53`)
are allowlisted in the script with the tracking issue named; the gate does not guess an
I2C address to make itself green.

Wired into `pr-metadata-validate.yml`'s `validate` job; `metadata/**` was already in that
workflow's `paths:` filter so both `metadata/e1m_modules/**` and `metadata/boards/**` already
retrigger it, and `scripts/check_i2c_address_uniqueness.py` itself is now added to the filter
too.

An `ALLOWLIST` entry excuses **one known set of claimants, not the address
forever**. The first cut of this gate keyed the allowlist on
`(file, bus, address)` alone; adding a third device at the allowlisted #1163
address then returned exit 0 with no output, so the gate silently accepted a
brand-new instance of the very collision it exists to catch. Each entry now
records the exact claimant set it excuses, and a collision whose claimants
differ from that set is reported normally. Covered by a regression test that
seeds a third claimant at an allowlisted address.

**Three defects found in review of the first two cuts, fixed here.**

The allowlist's claimant set was compared as a `frozenset`, which collapses
duplicates. `devices` has no `uniqueItems`, so two rows may legitimately carry
the same `chip=`/`role=` label -- and a THIRD claimant whose label matched one
already excused was therefore accepted silently at an allowlisted address.
Reproduced by duplicating the `tmp112` row in
`metadata/e1m_modules/E1M-V2M101.yaml`: three devices on `brd_i2c` `0x48`, gate
exit 0, no output. That is the same hole the per-address allowlist exists to
avoid, one level down. Now compared as a multiset, with a regression test that
seeds a duplicate-label third claimant.

A declared address above `0x77` is no longer treated as a distinct address. The
schema's pattern allows up to `0xFF`, so a device entered in 8-bit write-address
form -- `0xD0` for the 5L35023B, the form its own chip YAML quotes -- compared
unequal to the real `0x68` claimant and could never collide with it.

The docstring claimed to read "three declared-device shapes ... all three". That
overclaimed: `metadata/chips/*.yaml` instance tables carry an `addr_7bit` with a
free-text `scope:` rather than a machine-readable bus key, and
`examples/**/board.yaml` carries `hw_info.eeprom.{bus,addr_7bit}`. Both are now
named as deliberate exclusions with the reason, alongside a new, honest statement
that **cross-file joins are not performed**: a carrier's flat `i2c_devices:` and a
mounted SoM's `e1m_i2c*` bus can be the same physical bus
(`XEVK_I2C_BUS_SENSORS` is `ALP_E1M_X_I2C0`), but they live in different files and
the gate compares within a file only. Closing that would need a declared
SoM-to-carrier bus mapping the tree does not have.

A partially-declared `audio.codecs[]` entry is now reported instead of skipped.
`audio:` is a wholly open object in `metadata/schemas/board-preset.schema.json`
(`additionalProperties: true`, no inner shape) and this gate is its only reader
under `scripts/`, so a renamed key drifts unnoticed in both directions. An entry
carrying an address but no `i2c_bus` was dropped by a bare `continue` -- quietly
removing a real claimant from the comparison, which is how the gate goes green on
a collision it never saw. The failure summary now says "problem(s) ... (collisions
and/or uncomparable entries)" rather than calling an uncomparable entry a
collision.

### Changed — aen-cc3501e-socket-throughput sweeps STREAM_WRITE to the 4092-byte ceiling (#1677)

The bridge-only sweep used to stop at 512 B. An earlier bench, run on
mismatched host/firmware protocol revisions, had failed 1024 B and 4092 B
with `rc=-5` and a link that never recovered. Re-measured on 2026-09-28 on
E1M-AEN803 2026W36-0009, with this tree's host and a CC3501E on the bridge
firmware's main branch (`GET_VERSION` v1024): 512, 1024, 2048 and 4092 B
each pushed the full 1 MiB window, in 3 of 3 runs, with no `rc=-5` and no
wedge. The sweep now covers 64 to 4092 B. Rates: 44947 B/s at 64 B,
185654 B/s at 512 B, 226034 B/s at 1024 B, 268893 B/s at 4092 B. The send
buffer is now sized for the largest entry: it was 512 B, and the loop
refuses anything larger than the buffer.

### Changed — CC3501E bridge: the shared CRC-16 is table-driven, +22% STREAM_WRITE throughput

`alp_crc16_ccitt_false_update()` (`include/alp/protocol/crc16.h`) ran an
8-step bit loop per byte. The CC3501E bridge CRCs every request once the
link negotiates wire v4, and bulk frames reach 4 KiB, so on the M55-HE that
loop cost about 1.3 ms per 4092-byte `STREAM_WRITE` frame. It now uses a
256-entry lookup table (512 bytes of const data): identical output, about
0.3 ms per 4 KiB frame at `-O2`.

Measured on an E1M-AEN803 (2026W36-0009), `aen-cc3501e-socket-throughput`
bridge sweep, D-cache on and `CONFIG_SPI_DW_ALIF_PACK32=y`: 4092-byte frames
went from 561 KB/s to 687 KB/s, 2 of 2 runs identical.

A new ztest (`test_crc16_bytewise_matches_bitwise`) compares the helper
against the bit loop over every 97th length up to 4096 bytes, from
non-default starting registers and across a header/payload split, next to
the existing `123456789` -> `0x29B1` check vector. The GD32 bridge uses the
same helper and gets the same output.

### Fixed — CC3501E power presets never configured the radio (#1679)

`CMD_POWER_POLICY` (0x62), its four presets and the host driver have existed for a
while, and the MCU core half was a real implementation. But nothing in
`cc3501e-bridge-firmware:` ever called `Wlan_Set()`, so the Wi-Fi radio stayed fully awake
under every preset — DEEP_SLEEP included. On a Wi-Fi part that is the dominant
term: an associated station that never enters power save keeps its receiver up
continuously, which costs far more than any core idle state saves. In practice the
four presets differed only in core state, which is why the code documented
LOW_POWER and DEEP_SLEEP as sharing one reachable state.

The presets now drive the radio too, via the three knobs `wlan_if.h` exposes:
`WLAN_SET_POWER_SAVE` (active / auto / power-save), `WLAN_SET_POWER_MANAGEMENT`
(always-active / ELP) and `WLAN_SET_LSI` (wake every DTIM vs every Nth DTIM).
LSI is what makes LOW_POWER and DEEP_SLEEP genuinely different, and it gives
`idle_ms_before_sleep` a meaning — that field was previously accepted and discarded
because the vendor Power driver exposes no idle-hysteresis setter.

`Wlan_Set()` is rejected while the radio is down, so the policy is latched and
re-applied once `Wlan_RoleUp(STA)` succeeds; without that, a policy set before
Wi-Fi came up was silently dropped.

**Trade-off.** Waking only every Nth DTIM queues inbound frames at the AP until the
next wake, so DEEP_SLEEP adds hundreds of ms of inbound latency and will cut bulk
throughput hard. That is the preset working as intended, and it is why BALANCED
remains the default.

Also corrects the public header, which described DEEP_SLEEP as "radios off;
wake-on-host only". That was never what the firmware did and still is not — the
station stays associated in every preset.

The radio half runs on the firmware's task, not in the SPI-dispatch ISR the
handler is called from: `Wlan_Set()` is a blocking vendor radio call, and running
it inline failed every preset AND wedged the bridge on silicon (`POWER_POLICY ->
-4`, then `PING -> -5`). A `RESP_OK` to POWER_POLICY therefore means QUEUED, not
APPLIED — the same semantic `OTA_BEGIN` turned out to have.

Because of that, the reply now carries one data byte reporting whether the
PREVIOUS radio apply was realised, and `cc3501e_power_policy()` takes an optional
`bool *radio_ok_out`. Without it a host cannot distinguish an accepted-and-applied
policy from an accepted-and-silently-rejected one — which is exactly how a broken
radio apply went unnoticed on the bench until the return value was checked.

Bench-verified on an AEN EVK bench unit: all four presets report `radio_ok=1` and the
bridge survives each (`PING -> 0`). Bulk throughput under DEEP_SLEEP tracks the
default (798000 vs 799383 B/s), which is correct — 802.11 power save keeps the
station awake while downlink traffic flows and sleeps in the idle gaps, so the
saving is in idle current, not a throughput cut.

**Not measured:** this bench has no way to meter CC3501E current (the only
instrument is a carrier-wide 15 V rail at 1 mA resolution), so no power figure is
claimed. **One unexplained observation:** a single early run showed DEEP_SLEEP
throughput collapse to 617 B/s, and one later run had the DEEP_SLEEP policy call
itself return non-OK. Neither reproduced across the following runs. Recorded here
rather than omitted.

### Added — `cc3501e_power_off()` for long-idle duty cycles (#1679)

The presets are for short gaps. For a node that uplinks once an hour or once a
day, what matters is that the companion draws essentially nothing in between —
`WIFI_EN` gates VPA (3.3 V) through the board's load switch, so cutting it removes
the radio's power rather than idling it, far below anything `PowerWFF3_SLEEP`
reaches.

This deliberately is not a fifth preset: `CMD_POWER_POLICY` travels over the very
link the action kills, so it is a host-side GPIO action alongside
`cc3501e_reset()`. It is **explicit only** — nothing in the driver powers the
device down on its own, because only the application knows when the next uplink is
due and whether anything is in flight.

While off, calls fail `ALP_ERR_NOT_READY` immediately instead of clocking frames
at an unpowered slave. `cc3501e_reset()` is the wake; all device state (the
association, the BLE host, open sockets) is lost with the cold boot. Never call it
with an OTA in flight — it destroys the partially staged image.

Fixing this exposed three recovery defects, one of them long-standing:
`cc3501e_reset()` and `cc3501e_hard_reset()` gated on `initialised`, which made a
downed context unrecoverable; nothing re-armed that flag; and the re-arm has to
happen **before** the `GET_VERSION` compat gate, because that gate reads through
`cc3501e_get_version()`, which itself refuses on a downed context. The last one
also silently bricked any context downed by a version mismatch — there was no way
back through the API.

### Fixed — power presets could wedge the bridge when BLE was enabled (#1683)

Wi-Fi and BLE share the CC3501E's HIF, and `DEEP_SLEEP`'s `WAKE_UP_EVENT_N_DTIM`
long sleep interval starved BLE with it: with BLE advertising, the bridge could
stop answering (`PING -> -5`) and stay that way until a reset.

The long sleep interval is now withheld while BLE is enabled — `DEEP_SLEEP` keeps
`POWER_SAVE_MODE` + ELP but falls back to waking every DTIM, which is
`LOW_POWER`'s radio behaviour. Wi-Fi-only builds keep the full interval.

Two other real defects were found and fixed while isolating this, neither of them
the trigger: both halves of the policy ran in the SPI-dispatch ISR, and the core
half swapped the Power policy function pointer at runtime, racing the idle loop.
The presets now select behaviour purely through Power constraints, which
`PowerWFF3_sleepPolicy` is documented to read, so there is no swap to race.

Bench-measured with BLE advertising between presets, three consecutive runs: the
bridge never wedged (`PING -> 0` throughout). **Not a clean sweep** — one run still
lost a single BLE advertising call with the bridge alive, so a residual
intermittent BLE-op timeout under power presets remains and #1683 stays open for
it. What is fixed is the unrecoverable wedge.

### Fixed — the V2N `ipc:` carve-out deferred reconciliation to a closed issue (#1685)

`zephyr/boards/alp/e1m_v2n101_m33_sm/alp_e1m_v2n101_m33_sm_r9a09g056n48gbg_cm33.dts`'s
OpenAMP carve-out comment said the paper `ipc:` carve-out in `board.yaml`
("still `ocram_low` pending a follow-up that reconciles the two") would be
reconciled by alp-sdk #683. #683 is closed, and it settled a different
question — bench-validating the real `/dev/rpmsg` transport for the GHSA-xhm8
close-protocol redesign — not this address reconciliation. The deferral
pointed at an issue that never covered it, so the open question had nothing
tracking it.

The comment is now self-contained: it explains directly that
`resolve_carve_outs()` (`scripts/alp_orchestrate/carveout.py`) allocates the
`ipc:` entry from `ocram_low` only because that is the sole non-cacheable
region reachable from both `a55_cluster` and `m33_sm`
(`metadata/socs/renesas/rzv2n/n44.json`), that nothing consumes the address
it resolves to, and that the real transport instead uses a hand-authored DDR
window sized from the OpenAMP resource table's vring math. It also spells
out the resulting exhaustion instead of leaving it implicit: `carve_out_kb:
512` in both `examples/multicore/rpmsg-v2n/board.yaml` and
`examples/multicore/heterogeneous-offload/board.yaml` is the *entire*
512 KiB of `ocram_low`, so a second `ipc:` entry on this SoM has no headroom
left there once the paper allocation becomes load-bearing.

No carve-out was resized. Whether the fix is teaching the resolver about the
real DDR window or shrinking the examples' paper `carve_out_kb` values is a
sizing decision on real SoM memory, left for a follow-up that actually picks
one.

### Fixed — cold-chain-monitor README's `models/`/`tests/` references dead-ended a scaffolded customer (#1688)

`scripts/alp_project.py --emit scaffold`'s doc-link rewriter (`scripts/alp_template.py`'s
`_scaffold_readme`) only rewrites markdown link syntax (`](../...)`) into an absolute
GitHub URL; it cannot reach a bare code span or a bare CLI argument. The `edge-ai` template
(`metadata/templates/catalog-v1.json`) vendors only `examples/ai/cold-chain-monitor`'s
`board.yaml`/`prj.conf`/`CMakeLists.txt`/`src/*`/`README.md` -- neither the example's own
`models/` subdirectory nor the repo-root `tests/unit/cold_chain/` ships with it -- so a
`tan init --template edge-ai` (or the equivalent `alp_project.py --emit scaffold`) customer's
README pointed at `models/README.md` and `tests/unit/cold_chain` with no way to resolve either.

Both referents are now real markdown links the rewriter picks up (verified against
`tests/fixtures/emit-snapshots/scaffold.edge-ai-v2n101.snap`, regenerated by
`check_emit_snapshots.py --update`): the Model section links `models/README.md`, and a new
sentence ahead of the Tests fence links `tests/unit/cold_chain` -- the `twister` invocation
itself is untouched. `examples/ai/cold-chain-monitor/src/main.c`'s two `models/README.md`
comments (lines 20 and 154 before this change) are unreachable by the rewriter either way and
are spelled out as the full repo-relative path instead, so the comment stays unambiguous once
the file is vendored away from its directory.

Same fix class as `examples/peripheral-io/i2c-master/README.md`'s dangling `i2c-scanner`
reference (#1705).

Filed from `tan-cli#821(a)`, which worked around the dead pointers with a
`DELIBERATE_EDITS` standing exception in `tests/parity/scaffold_byte_parity.py`; that
entry is declared to retire once this lands and tan-cli re-vendors this tree. The shipped
link text here does not byte-match tan-cli's own local correction, so the re-vendor's
parity capture (`scaffold.edge-ai-v2n101.snap` and its tan-cli-side counterpart) must be
regenerated, not assumed identical.

### Fixed — cold-chain-monitor's Model section rendered as two paragraphs, dangling the sentence before its own link

An adversarial review caught a rendering regression this fix's own commit introduced: the
explanatory `<!-- The ../cold-chain-monitor/ detour is deliberate: ... -->` comment landed
mid-sentence, at column 0 on its own line, between "No model is shipped (stub +
deterministic classifier/fallback). See" and the `models/README.md` link that completes it.
CommonMark treats an HTML comment at column 0 as an HTML block, which -- like a blank line --
can interrupt a paragraph; GitHub and every emitted scaffold README rendered the sentence and
its link as two separate `<p>` tags instead of one. The comment now sits above the paragraph
as its own block, separated by a blank line, so the sentence and its link render as a single
paragraph; the comment's wording is unchanged.
`examples/connectivity/mqtt-telemetry/README.md` carried the same defect, copied from this fix
by a later commit; see `changelog.d/1794.md` for that repair, including the strengthened pinning
tests and the regenerated `scaffold.edge-ai-v2n101.snap` golden this half of the fix also moves.

### Fixed — `mqtt-telemetry`'s `board.yaml` still told customers to `west build` (#1689)

`#1016` rewrote the `Customer workflow:` comment header in every example
`board.yaml` from "copy this directory ... and `west build`" to the
`tan init --from-example <category>/<name>` / `tan build` form that ADR-0020
makes the whole command surface. It missed
`examples/connectivity/mqtt-telemetry/board.yaml` -- `git log` on that file
shows only `c830dc3d` (#903/#904), never #1016's `cdfe1368` -- so it kept
telling customers to copy the directory by hand and build with `west`.

Rewritten to match, keeping the example's own SSID/PSK + broker-URI guidance:
`tan init --from-example connectivity/mqtt-telemetry`, set the credentials in
`src/main.c` (or wire them from provisioning), then `tan build` for the AEN
board target. The path matches the sibling convention already used by
`connectivity/iot-connected-camera`, and `mqtt-telemetry` is present in
`metadata/catalog.json`, so the command as written resolves.

Scope checked, not assumed: a wrap-tolerant sweep (the old text wrapped as
`` `west\n# build` ``, which a plain grep for "west build" misses) over every
example `board.yaml` confirms this was the last `Customer workflow:` header
naming `west`. The ~95 example `README.md` files that mention `west build` are
left alone deliberately -- those document the underlying Zephyr command that
`scripts/alp_project.py` delegates to, which is still accurate.

### Fixed — `alp_ble_close()` orphaned connection back-pointers (#1697)

`alp_ble_connect()` stores a raw back-pointer into the conn slot (`c->state.radio = h`),
but `alp_ble_close()`'s only teardown call was `_free_radio(h)` — it never walked
`_conn_pool`. Any still-claimed connection therefore outlived the radio it points at, and
the next `_alloc_radio()` was free to recycle that slot underneath it. Reachable on the
shipping Zephyr backend with a plain open → connect → close → reopen; no partial vendor
port required.

`close()` now force-disconnects its own radio's connections before the controller goes
away. **This was the design decision the issue flagged for a maintainer**: the alternative
was refusing the close while links are live, but every other `alp_*_close()` in the tree
returns `void`, so there is no channel to report a refusal and diverging here would be an
API change. Consistency won; a caller that wants to keep a peer link must not close its
radio.

The sweep calls `alp_ble_disconnect()` rather than open-coding the teardown, so it inherits
the existing #629 sleep-poll drain, the backend disconnect, the lifecycle reset and
`_free_conn()` — and its `ALP_ERR_NOT_READY` on a lost CAS already handles another thread
tearing the same conn down. Ordering is after the radio's own drain (no new connect can be
admitted past it) and before `ops->close()` (the backend disconnect needs a live
controller). The #1118 refcount work and the #629/#756 self-close drain are untouched.

Adds `alp_slot_is_claimed()` — the acquire-load counterpart to `alp_slot_try_claim()` —
documented as safe for *sweeping* a pool but never for gating a claim.

### Fixed — LVGL could draw onto a recycled display handle (#1698)

`alp_gui_lvgl_attach()` caches the `alp_display_t *` in LVGL's user-data and has no
matching detach, so `_flush_cb()` reads it back on every frame forever.

**The filed diagnosis was that this dereferences a closed handle. It does not, and the
real hazard is worse.** `alp_display_blit()` already gates on the lifecycle byte and
returns `ALP_ERR_NOT_READY`, and the handle pool is `static`, so a closed display yields a
silently dropped frame and never a use-after-free. What actually bites is **slot reuse**:
`alp_display_close()` followed by `alp_display_open()` hands the same address to a
*different* display, whose lifecycle reads `OPEN` — so the blit **succeeds, against
somebody else's screen**. Silent wrong-display corruption, not a crash.

A raw pointer therefore cannot identify a display across a close/open pair. `struct
alp_display` gains an `epoch` generation counter, bumped on every fresh claim and placed
*after* `in_use` so the allocator's `memset(..., offsetof(..., in_use))` cannot reset it.
`attach()` snapshots the epoch alongside the pointer and `_flush_cb()` re-compares before
blitting, skipping the frame on a mismatch — `lv_display_flush_ready()` is still called
either way, so the render loop never wedges, matching the existing failed-blit contract.

This needs **no new public API**, which sidesteps the decision the issue was blocked on:
its three options were adding `alp_gui_lvgl_detach()` (new surface on an `[ABI-STABLE]`
contract), refusing the close (impossible — `alp_display_close()` returns `void`), or
documenting the footgun. The corrected diagnosis makes a fourth option available that none
of the three required.

Also closes a leak on the new `NOMEM` path: the render buffer is freed when the binding
allocation fails, since a bind-up that never completed has no "persistent for the process
lifetime" claim on it.

### Documented — the SERAM ↔ services-library version pairing on E1M-AEN, and the API break below v109 (#1700)

Alif Semiconductor, answering our escalation on a customer AE822 (2026-08-28):

> there is an API break between SERAM v106 and v109 for E8 devices. v106 is a
> really early version for E8 platform, and you definitely need to update SERAM
> on your HWs to a newer version (v110 is recommended). It works ok with also
> with services library v109. General guideline is that you should always use a
> matching SERAM and services library.

This is the answer to the first of the five questions we escalated, and it is a
constraint no part of this repo previously stated. The SE firmware image (SERAM,
what `se_service_get_se_revision()` reports) and the services library (the
hal_alif `se_services` client this SDK links, `hal_alif v2.3.0` at the current
`west.yml` pin) are versioned together and are not independently upgradable.
Nothing in the SDK could have told a reader that, and the failure mode of
getting it wrong does not name itself: the customer's module runs SERAM
**1.106.2** (Jul 14 2025) against a services library from SETOOLS **1.109**,
which straddles the break.

`docs/aen-se-services.md` gains §0.1 with the pairing rule, a supported-pairs
table, the one read-only call that tells you what a module is running
(`se_service_get_se_revision()`, already in §1's zero-risk set), and the remedy
— a System Package update over the SE-UART, not an application change.

It also records the symptom seen on the mismatched pair, because that is what a
reader will arrive with rather than a version number: the *first* SE service
request stops HFXTAL and unlocks the PLL, and the M55-HP drops from 400 MHz to
76.8 MHz and stays there. It reproduced through `SERVICE_CRYPTOCELL_GET_RND`
(reached from a DHCP client's randomness source) but is not RNG-specific —
shifting application code by `0x100` changes the outcome. Alif has **not** said
the break causes this fault, and §0.1 does not wait on that: across an API break
any behaviour is permissible, so nothing measured on a mismatched pair is
evidence about anything and a workaround built on one is unsafe to ship even
when it appears to work. Fix the pairing first, triage after. #1700 stays open
for the causal question.

**ADR 0030** records the standing position the answer forces: SERAM and the
services library are one versioned pair that moves together, and E1M-AEN tracks
Alif's latest released SERAM — floor and current baseline **v110** — rather
than sitting on whatever a module shipped with. A `hal_alif` bump stops being a
routine dependency bump under that rule: it moves the services library, so it
moves the required SERAM floor with it. The ADR also records why the two obvious
alternatives lose — pinning a known-good older pair means standing on v106, the
version Alif are telling us to leave, and leaving the pairing to each module
owner is the status quo that produced #1700.

`docs/aen-provisioning.md` gains the same check as a prerequisite note ahead of
§2, since the SE-UART a reader is already wiring is the channel the SERAM update
travels over.

§1's `se_service_get_se_revision()` row carried `SES A0 v1.106.2 Jul 14 2025` as
its bench value — a capture taken before the reference board's System Package
update, and now precisely the version Alif says to move off. Left alone it
advertised a pre-break baseline as this SDK's reference. The row now reads
`SES A0 v1.110.0 Mar 4 2026` with the old capture kept alongside it, so the
change is legible rather than silent.

Two facts checked against upstream while writing this, both recorded: hal_alif
documents `se_service_get_se_revision()` as "Retrieve SERAM version banner"
(`se_services/include/services_lib_protocol.h`), which is what makes it the right
call to name; and `hal_alif v2.3.0` is already the newest `hal_alif` release tag,
so the services-library half needs no bump — the work is entirely module-side.

One thing this does **not** settle, and the pin cannot answer it: hal_alif
versions its services library independently of SETOOLS — `v2.3.0` declares
`SE_SERVICES_VERSION_STRING "0.50.10"`, a number with no stated relation to SERAM
v106/v109/v110 — and Alif publish no mapping between the two schemes. So which
SERAM floor this SDK's pin actually requires is unknown. §0.1 and ADR 0030 both
say so, and take v110 as the module baseline on the strength of Alif's own
recommendation and the reference board running it.

### Added — a diagnostic warning when a module's SERAM sits below the ADR-0030 floor (#1700)

`docs/aen-se-services.md` section 0.1 and ADR 0030 record the SERAM/services-
library pairing rule and the v110 floor, but until now that check was purely
manual: a reader had to call `se_service_get_se_revision()` themselves and read
the banner. `src/backends/soc_info/alif_se.c` now runs that same check on every
`alp_soc_info_read()` / `alp_soc_secure_fw_ping()` and logs one `LOG_WRN` the
first time it sees a SERAM version below v110, naming ADR-0030 and #1700.

This is a **diagnostic, not a fix**. The customer report behind #1700 is a
mismatched SERAM (v106) against a services library from SETOOLS v109: the first
SE service request stopped HFXTAL and unlocked the PLL, and M55-HP fell from
400 MHz to 76.8 MHz and stayed there. Alif confirmed a real API break below v109
for E8; across a break of that kind any SE behaviour is possible, so this
backend does **not** attempt to re-establish the clock itself -- the same
"no workaround is safe to ship" reasoning `docs/aen-se-services.md` already
states for a mismatched pair rules that out. What it does instead is turn a
silent 76.8 MHz stall into an actionable, one-shot log line, so a mismatched
module gets caught before a customer spends time debugging an application on
top of undefined SE behaviour.

The check only runs on this backend's own read path -- whichever `se_service_*`
call an application issues first (the customer's own trigger was
`SERVICE_CRYPTOCELL_GET_RND`, not a soc-info read) is not intercepted, so
`docs/aen-se-services.md` still leads with calling `se_service_get_se_revision()`
explicitly as the first diagnostic step regardless of whether the warning fired.

`tests/unit/alif_se_seram_floor_warning/` adds white-box native_sim coverage
(the `#include`-the-real-TU technique `tests/unit/se_cryptocell_hash_bounds/`
already uses) for the banner parser and the warn-once behaviour, on both the
customer's failing capture (SERAM v106) and the healthy reference-board capture
(SERAM v110).

Still open, unchanged by this PR: whether the API break *causes* the HFXTAL/PLL
drop is an Alif-side question this repo cannot answer from software alone --
see #1700 for the live escalation and the bench plan to demonstrate it.

### Documented — bound a relayed, uncorroborated Alif statement on `app-device-config.json` to what it actually established, and to the firewall carve-out this repo already ships (#1701)

SETOOLS **1.110.00** ships no AE822-specific device config: the stock
`build/config/app-device-config.json` declares `"device": "AE722F80F55D5AS"`,
an **E7** part, not the E1M-AEN801's `AE822FA0E5597LS0`. Every customer
provisioning an AEN801 was either using a config named for different silicon
or hand-editing one with no documented basis for the edit.

A maintainer relayed the following from Alif, second-hand — it was **not**
posted to alp-sdk#1700 or alp-sdk#1701, and as of this writing (2026-09-02)
it appears nowhere else in this repo either:
