> The provided app-device-config.json works with either E7 or E8. The part
> number field is just a text field for your own usage. The important thing
> to note is the part number selected when you execute tools-config, as that
> is what app-gen-toc and app-write-mram use.

The previous version of this entry presented that quote as Alif's settled,
confirmed answer and closed the issue on the strength of it, and generalized
"the part-number field doesn't matter" further than the relay supports.
Neither holds up: the quote has no repo-internal corroboration, and this
repo already ships a firewall-policy-sensitive path
(`examples/connectivity/firmware-update-log`'s hardware-firewall proof, via
`scripts/bench/aen/flash-update-log-firewall-probe.sh`) whose own comments
warn that swapping in a generic device config there "can remove the very
firewall rule you are trying to prove" — the opposite of "this field never
matters."

`docs/aen-provisioning.md` §3 now:

- attributes the quote as relayed and uncorroborated, not settled;
- keeps only what is independently bench-established as bench-established —
  **`device` is very likely cosmetic, not silicon-relevant** (the SE reports
  the correct part identity from OTP, `ALIF_PN = AE822FA0E5597LS0`,
  regardless of which part the config file names) and **the HFXO trim fields
  already matched our AE822** (`XO_REG1` readback agrees with the stock
  file's `HFXO_CAP_CTRL`/`HFXO_PFET_GM_CTRL`/`HFXO_NFET_GM_CTRL`);
- marks the "`tools-config -a` binds the ATOC to a part, not this file"
  claim as resting on the relay alone;
- states the firewall exception explicitly: the stock file is fine
  unmodified for the boot/identity path this section covers, but that does
  not extend to firewall-policy-sensitive flows, which already require a
  board-specific `ALP_AEN_DEVICE_CONFIG_JSON` instead of the stock file.

**No new device-config file ships with this change**, in either `alp-sdk` or
`alp-sdk-internal`. `app-device-config.json` remains a licensed SETOOLS
deliverable carrying Alif-owned configuration beyond the `device` string, so
a hand-produced copy would still be inventing vendor-owned content rather
than qualifying it.

The documented guidance for the boot/identity path: use the stock
`app-device-config.json` unmodified, as the reference board does; do not
hand-edit its `device` field. alp-sdk#1701 is item 3 of the Alif escalation
tracked at alp-sdk#1700 and stays **open** pending a citable Alif answer on
the issue thread — this entry no longer claims it closed.

### Fixed — `i2c-master`'s README pointed at a sibling example as bare prose a scaffold cannot resolve (#1705)

`examples/peripheral-io/i2c-master/README.md`'s troubleshooting bullet named
`examples/peripheral-io/i2c-scanner` as a bare inline code span rather than a
markdown link. tan-cli's scaffold vendoring runs `--emit scaffold` through a
doc-link rewriter that only rewrites markdown link syntax (`](...)`) and is
documented as intentionally not normalising bare prose cross-references, so once
vendored into a customer project -- which carries neither `scripts/` nor the
sibling example -- that bullet became a dead pointer with no path the reader could
follow.

Now a real relative link, matching the two links to the same referent this README
already carried at its top and in its "see also" list. `scaffold.sensor-v2n101.snap`
embeds this README and is regenerated: exactly one line changes, and every changed
character is the link syntax itself.

This completes #1705. Its first half (`examples/bringup/board-selftest/README.md`'s
`scripts/program_eeprom.py` reference) landed earlier; this half was deliberately
deferred because #1269 was concurrently regenerating the same golden, and fixing
both at once would have collided on that fixture.

### Fixed — `--emit scaffold --template multicore-rpmsg` emitted a tree that could not build standalone (#1712)

Materialising the catalog's `multicore-rpmsg` template (`tan init`/`alp_project.py
--emit scaffold --template multicore-rpmsg --sku <SKU>`) produced a project
that failed immediately: `metadata/templates/catalog-v1.json`'s
`files.user_owned` list for the record was missing the project root's own
`CMakeLists.txt` (the multi-slice marker directing a customer at `linux/` and
`m55_hp/`) and `linux/src/main.c` — a file `linux/CMakeLists.txt`'s
`add_executable(rpmsg_aen_consumer src/main.c)` already required. `cmake -S .
-B build` at the scaffold root failed with "does not appear to contain
CMakeLists.txt"; configuring `linux/` past that failed again at
`add_executable` with "Cannot find source file: src/main.c". Both paths are
added to the record now (`board.yaml`, `CMakeLists.txt`, `m55_hp/prj.conf`,
`m55_hp/CMakeLists.txt`, `m55_hp/src/main.c`, `linux/CMakeLists.txt`,
`linux/src/main.c`, `README.md`).

Separately, `examples/multicore/rpmsg-aen/linux/CMakeLists.txt`'s
`ALP_GENERATED_DIR` fallback resolved
`${CMAKE_CURRENT_SOURCE_DIR}/../../build/generated` — two levels up from
`linux/`, landing in the scaffold's *parent* directory, outside the project
entirely, instead of the project root's own `build/generated/` one level up.
Fixed to `../build/generated`; verified by resolving both forms against a
materialised scaffold path.

Reproduced by emitting the template, materialising the JSON envelope to disk,
and running `cmake` against both the project root and `linux/` — see
`tests/scripts/test_alp_project_scaffold_emit.py::
test_scaffold_via_cores_selects_multicore_rpmsg`, whose pre-fix assertion
pinned exactly the missing-file set this fixes.

### Fixed — a citation stopped being checked the moment it shipped (#1715)

`check_changelog_citations.py` enumerated only `changelog.d/*.md`, so a citation was
verified while it sat in a fragment and then **never again** once that fragment was folded
into `CHANGELOG.md` at release time — which is exactly when it starts to rot. #1498 was the
symptom; the hole that let it ship is fixed here.

`CHANGELOG.md` is now scanned too, but its two halves carry different contracts and are
graded differently:

- **`[Unreleased]`** describes the current tree, so a broken citation there is an **error**,
  same as a fragment.
- **A released section is a historical record** of a tree that no longer exists. Some of its
  citations are unfixable by construction, and rewriting them to suit today's tree would
  falsify what shipped. Those are reported as **warnings** — visible, never silently passed,
  never blocking.

Grading released history as errors would have made this gate unlandable without editing
shipped release notes, which is the opposite of what a changelog is for. Three such
citations exist on `dev` today and are now surfaced as warnings (quoted in a fenced block
below because they are dead paths by construction — writing them as live citations here
would trip this very gate, which is itself the behaviour working):

```
alp_cli/new_som.py:154   -- deleted with the alp_cli retirement (#1367/#1368)
docs/Overview.md         -- deleted
docs/abi/README.md:157   -- anchor "no final v0.15.0 tag exists yet", correctly
                            removed once v0.15.0 GA shipped
```

Eight citations that *were* genuinely fixable are corrected in the same change: three
anchor drifts re-resolved to where the code moved
(`include/alp/protocol/cc3501e.h` 447 -> 534, `cc3501e-bridge-firmware:hal/ti/cc3501e_hw_ti_wifi.c`
715 -> 781, `src/zephyr/console/alp_console_companion_wifi.c` 348 -> 416), and five bare
filenames rewritten as repo-relative paths so the resolver can find them at all. Citation
count went 74 resolved / 11 errors to 77 resolved / 0 errors + 3 warnings.

### Fixed — the GD32 bridge protocol doc no longer says a second FFT `chain_bind` is accepted (#1717)

`docs/gd32-bridge-protocol.md` §3.x and the `CHAIN_BIND` section still said
the firmware did not guard the single FFT block, so two streams could both
bind FFT chains. Since protocol v0.10 (`gd32-bridge-firmware` PR #121), a
second FFT-terminal bind returns `STATUS_NOSUPPORT`, exactly like the FAC
guard, and the refused chain stays open so the host can retry the same
`chain_id`. Both sections now say so, matching the doc's own v0.10 history
entry.

### Fixed — a model tensor with rank > 4 was silently truncated to rank 4 by the ONNX Runtime, DEEPX DX-M1, and TFLM backends (#1729)

`alp_inference_tensor_t`'s `shape` field has exactly 4 slots. All three of
`src/yocto/inference_ort.cpp`, `src/yocto/inference_deepx.cpp`, and
`src/backends/inference/tflm.cpp` used to hand back a tensor descriptor
truncated to its first 4 dims whenever a real tensor's rank exceeded that —
sized correctly via `size_bytes`, but with a `shape[]` that no longer matched
the model and no signal to the caller that anything was wrong. Confidently
wrong tensor geometry is worse than a refusal — and, before this fix, the
*same* rank-5 model was silently truncated on TFLM while being refused on
ORT/DEEPX, so a portable app got a different answer per backend.

All three backends now reject such a model at `alp_inference_open()` with
`ALP_ERR_NOSUPPORT` instead: ORT's `_gather_tensor_info()` refuses any tensor
whose `GetDimensionsCount()` exceeds 4 (kept as a SEPARATE check from the
pre-existing hostile/corrupt-ndim ceiling — a corrupt ndim is `ALP_ERR_INVAL`,
a well-formed model this descriptor can't represent is `ALP_ERR_NOSUPPORT`,
and collapsing the two would misreport a hostile rank-1000 `ndim` as merely
"unrepresentable"), DEEPX's `open()` checks every input/output tensor's
`shape().size()` right after `GetInputs()`/`GetOutputs()` before staging any
buffers, and TFLM's `tflm_open()` checks every input/output tensor's
`dims->size` right after `AllocateTensors()` succeeds, before handing state
to the caller.

DEEPX's `get_output()` also re-checks the LIVE tensor `Run()` hands back
(`last_outputs`) — the open()-time check only sees the DECLARED
`GetOutputs()` metadata, which does not cover a model whose live output rank
differs (e.g. a dynamic/data-dependent shape).

**A sibling of the same defect, found while fixing this one and fixed with
it.** The rank cap is not the only place a real dimension was quietly
reshaped to fit the descriptor: `alp_inference_tensor_t.shape[]` is
`uint16_t`, and `inference_deepx.cpp` cast each `int64_t` extent straight
into it with no bounds check — a dim above 65535 wrapped (100000 became
34464) and a symbolic/dynamic `-1` became 65535, in both cases a
plausible-looking wrong extent, exactly the failure mode this issue is
about. `inference_ort.cpp` already refused such dims at load time in
`_gather_tensor_info` ("reject here instead of lying to the caller"); its
sibling never got that check.

The rank-vs-extent decision for ORT and DEEPX is now shared:
`src/yocto/inference_tensor_shape.h`'s `alp_inference_shape::fill_fixed_shape()`
copies a shape when it fits (rank <= 4 AND every dim in `[0, UINT16_MAX]`)
and refuses — leaving the descriptor untouched — otherwise. It has zero
dependency on the ONNX Runtime C API or dx_rt, mirroring the
`src/yocto/drpai_deploy_shapes.h` (#1635) precedent of splitting a
vendor-independent decision into its own testable header. ORT's
`_gather_tensor_info()` still does its own open()-time extent check (and
pins a non-positive/symbolic dim to 1, a documented ORT-specific choice);
`get_input()`/`get_output()` call `fill_fixed_shape()` as the actual
write path and as defense-in-depth. DEEPX's `fill_tensor_descriptor()` now
returns `bool` and calls `fill_fixed_shape()` directly, so both the
declared-shape path (`get_input`/`get_output`) and the live post-`Run()`
path are covered — DEEPX deliberately does **not** copy ORT's "pin to 1"
behaviour: that is a documented load-time choice ORT makes for symbolic
dims, and silently inventing an extent on a backend that never made that
choice would be the same lie in a new place. `UINT16_MAX` itself is
representable and still passes.

TFLM's `fill_tensor_descriptor()` still casts `t->dims->data[i]` to
`uint16_t` with no per-extent bounds check — the same sibling defect,
unfixed on that backend. Not addressed here (out of scope for this batch);
worth its own follow-up.

`include/alp/inference.h`'s `alp_inference_open()` doc and
`docs/tutorials/16-inference-mobilenet.md`'s troubleshooting section both
document the new refusal. Regression coverage:
`tests/yocto/inference_ort_regression.cpp` and
`tests/yocto/inference_deepx_regression.cpp` drive the real backend bodies
against clean-room stand-in vendor headers (`tests/yocto/fakes/`) since
neither ONNX Runtime nor DEEPX dx_rt is available in CI (#1747);
`tests/yocto/inference_tensor_shape.cpp` unit-tests `fill_fixed_shape()`
directly (rank and extent boundaries, including the 65535/-1 wrap cases),
registered as `alp_test_inference_tensor_shape` — no vendor SDK, so it is
the surface where these decisions actually run today.

### Fixed — the GD32 PWM ceiling was documented as the unprescaled ~303 us (#1730)

`docs/gd32-bridge-protocol.md` and `metadata/chips/gd32g553.yaml` both
stated a "~4.63 ns LSB" and a "~303 us" longest period as the achievable
GD32 PWM figures. Both numbers are arithmetically right for the timer
running **unprescaled** off the 216 MHz CK_TIMER — and neither is what the
firmware surfaces, because it always programs a fixed 216:1 prescale to a
1 MHz tick. The real figures are a **1 us LSB and a 65.536 ms** longest
period at full 16-bit count.

The protocol document already contradicted itself on this: a dozen lines
below the ~303 us claim it correctly describes a channel reporting "the
boot default (65.536 ms period, 0 duty)".

The stale figure was not inert. #1730 was found while reviewing
`fix/1635-pwm-status-parity`, whose new comment cited the ~303 us number
as the `OUT_OF_RANGE` mechanism — a wrong justification reached for
precisely because the documented ceiling was wrong. `gd32g553.yaml`'s
`pwm_routing.notes` also claimed periods beyond ~303 us "require the
firmware's repetition-counter / prescaler logic", implying a longer period
is reachable by some other path; it is not.

Both sites now give the prescaled figures, name the unprescaled ones as
what they are, and record the consequence a caller can actually hit:
**a period longer than 65.536 ms is currently clamped by the firmware and
still reported as success**, so it cannot be detected from the return code
— read back with `CMD_PWM_GET`.

Documentation only; no behaviour changes here. The clamp itself is a
firmware defect and is not fixable from this repo — `firmware/gd32-bridge/`
has zero tracked files on `dev` and lives in the separate
`gd32-bridge-firmware` repo (ADR-0031). The `PWM_TIMER_PRESCALER` /
`PWM_TIMER_TICK_NS` / `PWM_TIMER_ARR_MAX` constants the 65.536 ms figure
derives from are in that repo; the value is corroborated in-tree by the
protocol document's own boot-default line. #1730 tracks the firmware-side
refuse-don't-clamp fix, which is bench-owed.

### Fixed — the shipped CC3501E prebuilt answered a wire protocol the host refuses (#1733)

`cc3501e-bridge-firmware:prebuilt/` shipped `cc3501e-v0.3.0.bin`, built at wire
protocol **4**. The protocol moved to **5** in #1610/#1655 (`OTA_UPDATE_MODE`,
opcode `0x47`) but `firmware-version.txt` was never bumped, so the repo kept
shipping a blob that a host built from this tree rejects outright at
`GET_VERSION` — and two different builds both called themselves `0.3.0`. All
six AEN SoM presets pinned that blob as their `helper_firmware.cc3501e_otp`
payload.

- New prebuilt `cc3501e-v0.4.0.bin` (+ `.sig`, `.sha256`) at wire protocol 5,
  signed with the VALIDATION vendor key; `firmware-version.txt` is now `0.4.0`
  and the image reports `fw_version=0x0400`.
- `E1M-AEN{301,401,501,601,701,801}.yaml` repointed at the new blob.
- `cc3501e-bridge-firmware:README.md` leads with the prebuilt flashing recipe
  (verify signature → drop into the flash-set → `programmer -i XDS110`), with
  building from source as the fallback it should be. Building previously
  required TI ticlang 5.1.1 + SimpleLink Wi-Fi SDK 10.10.01.08 + SysConfig
  1.28.0 + Wi-Fi toolbox 4.2.4 just to obtain a working companion.
- `docs/cc3501e-bridge.md` gains the **GPE anti-rollback stamp** as a fourth
  version axis. It is not the SemVer, it is burned irreversibly into the part
  as a monotonic floor, and a stamp below that floor makes the programmer
  report success while the device keeps the old image.
- Documented that `ti/regen_flashset.sh`'s epoch-derived version is not a
  release scheme: its high byte wraps every ~194 days, so it is not monotonic
  over a part's life (run today it yields `0.144.51.196`, below the
  `0.149.63.0` floor already burned into the bench unit).
- Flagged an unresolved contradiction: `prebuilt/CHANGELOG.md` and
  `regen_flashset.sh` require GPE `major = 0`, while
  `ti/package_cc3501e_prod.ps1` and `ti/validate_gpio_bench.ps1` default to a
  `major = 1` stamp and comment that major must be `>= 1`. Releases use `major = 0`;
  the `>= 1` path is unverified and left untouched rather than guessed at.

### Fixed — `alp_gpio_write()` (and every other op) on a closed pin answered NOT_READY on Zephyr and INVAL on Yocto (#1734)

`src/yocto/peripheral_gpio.c` gated every GPIO op on `pin == NULL || !pin->in_use`
and returned `ALP_ERR_INVAL` for both a NULL handle and a closed (non-NULL,
`in_use == false`) one, while every Zephyr dispatcher -- and ADR-0002's
2026-08-27 amendment recording the convention -- treats a NULL-or-closed
handle as a lifecycle condition and returns `ALP_ERR_NOT_READY`. The same
public symbol, `alp_gpio_write(closed_pin, ...)` among them, answered
differently depending on which backend the build selected.

`alp_gpio_configure`, `alp_gpio_write`, `alp_gpio_read`, `alp_gpio_irq_enable`,
and `alp_gpio_irq_disable` in the Yocto backend now return `ALP_ERR_NOT_READY`
for a NULL-or-closed pin, matching the Zephyr dispatch layer. Where a
lifecycle check was previously fused into the same condition as a malformed-
argument check (a NULL `level` out-param on read, a NULL `cb` on IRQ enable),
the two are now split: the lifecycle check runs first and short-circuits to
`NOT_READY`, and the malformed-argument check only runs once the handle
itself is known good, still returning `ALP_ERR_INVAL`. `include/alp/peripheral.h`'s
doc comment for `alp_gpio_write` is corrected to state the NULL-or-closed
case explicitly instead of attributing `ALP_ERR_NOT_READY` solely to a pin
not configured as output.

`src/yocto/peripheral_i2c.c`, `peripheral_spi.c`, and `peripheral_uart.c` gated
the same way and returned `ALP_ERR_INVAL` for a NULL-or-closed handle too --
named in ADR-0002's amendment alongside the GPIO case. That divergence is
resolved separately by #1834 (landed independently on `dev`); with both
changes in, all four Yocto peripheral families now match the Zephyr
convention.

### Fixed — `check_emit_snapshots` failed on any checkout that had the release tag (#1738)

Four scaffold goldens (`scaffold.minimal/peripheral/sensor-v2n101`,
`scaffold.multicore-mailbox-aen801`) failed the gate on a clean `dev`, with no code
change in sight. The cause was not stale goldens — it was that the emitted bytes
depend on the **checkout**, not the commit.

A scaffolded README pins its doc links to a ref chosen by `alp_template._docs_ref()`:
`v<version>` when `metadata/sdk_version.yaml` says `status: released` **and** that tag
resolves locally, else `main`. `_tag_resolves()` is a local `git rev-parse`, so a clone
that fetched origin's tags emits `blob/v0.16.0/` while a shallow, `--no-tags`, or
tarball checkout of the same commit emits `blob/main/`. The goldens were written from a
tagless checkout, so every tagged checkout failed — unwinnable either way, since fixing
it for one host breaks the other.

That is the same machine-specific class this module already tokenises (`<SDK_ROOT>`,
`<PYTHON_EXECUTABLE>`, `<SDK_COMMIT>`), so the ref is now tokenised as `<DOCS_REF>` and
the goldens pin the link *shape* — which is what the gate is for. `main`, `v0.16.0`,
`v1.0.0` and `v0.16.0-rc1` all collapse to the same token, so this also stops the
goldens re-drifting at every release tag; non-`blob` GitHub links are left alone.

The ref appears in two link shapes — `blob/<ref>/` for files and `tree/<ref>/` for
directories (`alp_template.py` picks `kind` per target) — and only the `sensor-v2n101`
scaffold emits a `tree/` link, so covering `blob/` alone left exactly that one snapshot
failing in CI. Both kinds are normalised; `blob` vs `tree` is preserved, since only the
ref is host-dependent.

This gate runs in CI as a step of the `validate · soc-spec-v1` job, and also inside
`scripts/test-all.sh`. It sat red on `dev` because the job was already failing, so one
more red step in it drew no attention.

### Fixed — an idle CC3501E delivered ~5.8 phantom events per second (#1740)

Every `cc3501e_poll_events()` on an **empty** event ring dispatched three events with
opcode `0x00`, length 0 — continuously, with no Wi-Fi or BLE activity at all. `0x00` is
not a defined `ALP_CC3501E_EVT_*` opcode.

Reply padding added in #1610/#1655 pads a reply up to an 8-byte multiple for DMA burst
alignment and folds the pad **into the declared payload length**. Its own comment states
the invariant it breaks: *"The pad bytes are never interpreted: every reply carries its
own length"* — true only for a self-delimiting payload. `GET_PENDING_EVENTS` returns a
packed `{opcode(1) | len(1) | payload[len]}` list with no count and no terminator, so the
pad is indistinguishable from entries. An empty ring produced `reply_payload = 1`,
`rem = 1`, `pad = 7`, declared 8 — the host then walked 7 zero bytes as three
`{opcode 0, len 0}` entries. Measured on an E1M-AEN801: `[evtdbg] got=7 raw=00 00 00 00`
every poll.

`#1724`'s fan-out meant every subscriber received each phantom. Fixed-size replies
(`GET_VERSION`, `GET_MAC`) were unaffected because the host reads a known byte count.

The walk now stops at a zero opcode, treating it as the padding it is — no wire-format
change, and the DMA-alignment win is kept. Bench A/B on AEN801: 117 phantom events per
20 s before, **0** after, with the padding still arriving unchanged (`got=7`).

Not a regression from #1721/#1724 — the walk loop is byte-identical before #1724.

Also noted while tracing, not changed here: `cc3501e_request()` writes `*rx_len` only when
`data_len > 0`, so a caller that does not pre-initialise its length variable reads stale
stack on a bare-OK reply. `cc3501e_poll_events()` initialises `got = 0`, so it was not the
cause, but it is a live trap for the next caller.

### Fixed — `alp companion sock tcp-get` overflowed the shell stack and halted the board (#1743)

Every `alp` console command runs on the Zephyr shell thread, and the companion verbs
descend `shell` -> `cc3501e_request()` -> the SPI transport and then format the result
back out through `shell_print()`. Zephyr's default `CONFIG_SHELL_STACK_SIZE=2048` does
not leave enough room for that chain: with data actually flowing through `sock tcp-get`'s
receive loop it overflowed and took the system down —

```
E:   Stack overflow (context area not valid)
E: >>> ZEPHYR FATAL ERROR 2: Stack overflow on CPU 0
E: Current thread: 0x200001d0 (shell_uart)
E: Halting system
```

Sized from measurement rather than guessed. With `CONFIG_THREAD_ANALYZER` on an
E1M-AEN801:

| path | `shell_uart` peak |
|---|---|
| `alp companion ver` alone | 1044 / 2048 (50 %) |
| after `sock tcp-get` | 1156 / 2048 (56 %) |

Under 900 bytes remained for the receive loop's own formatting, and printf under picolibc
is stack-hungry. `configdefault` now raises the default to **4096 whenever
`ALP_SDK_CONSOLE` is enabled**, which measures 1156 / 4096 (28 %) on the same board —
headroom goes from 892 to 2940 bytes. It costs 2 KB of RAM (~0.8 % of the AEN801's
256 KB) and only on builds that opt into the console; `configdefault` leaves an
application free to choose its own value.

Note the receive buffer was never the problem — it is `static uint8_t rx[512]`, off-stack.
The only stack arrays in that translation unit are `ip[4]` and `req[160]`. The overflow is
call-chain depth, which is why raising the thread's stack is the proportionate fix rather
than shrinking a local.

### Fixed — a `sock` send could report failure on a transfer the peer received in full (#1746)

Two distinct defects produced the same symptom, and both are now closed.

**1. No request identity, so a lost reply re-executed the send.** `poll_by_repeat()`
re-sends the identical frame on every poll, and the companion's
`handle_worker_routed_payload_reply()` treats a poll that finds an idle worker as a
brand-new request. Once a send completed and the slot was freed, the host's next
byte-identical poll **re-transmitted the payload**, and one lost `RESP_OK` became an
endless re-execute ending in a `-4` timeout on a send that had succeeded. Fixed by
giving `CMD_SOCK_SEND` a `seq` in the byte at offset 3 of
`alp_cc3501e_sock_send_t` — previously `reserved`, always written 0 — assigned once
per logical send so it is constant across the retry loop
(`chips/cc3501e/cc3501e_sockets.c:388` (`p[3] = ++ctx->sock_send_seq`)). Wire
protocol 6 -> 7; companion side is cc3501e-bridge-firmware#89, shipped as its
prebuilt v0.6.0.

**2. The request payload phase raced the companion's re-arm.** A request is two
SS0-framed transfers — a header declaring the length, then the payload — and the gap
between them is `CC3501E_PHASE_SETTLE_US`. `cc3501e_reply_gate()` only waits on the
READY line when it has been proven, and on the measured unit it never is: READY is
CC3501E `GPIO_17` -> Alif `P2_6`, and `P2_6` is `SPI1_SCLK_A`, so enabling its input
buffer degrades the link it would gate. That pad conflict is an Alif pad function,
not a board-revision property, so the fallback applies to any module routing READY
to `P2_6` — r1 as measured here, and R2 unless its netlist moves the line, which
has not been checked. Every phase therefore fell back to a blind
40 us, which the payload phase intermittently out-ran — the payload landed short or
shifted and the companion rejected the frame with `RESP_ERR_INVALID`, surfacing as
`send failed (-1)`. Raised to 250 us
(`chips/cc3501e/cc3501e_core.c:1607` (`#define CC3501E_PHASE_SETTLE_US 250u`)).

Bench-measured on E1M-AEN801 serial `2617-0001` (board rev **r1**), protocol 7, against a bare
`accept()` listener, 10 consecutive `alp companion sock tcp-get`:

| phase settle | end-to-end successes | `send failed` |
|---|---|---|
| 40 us | 6/10 | 4/10 |
| 250 us | **10/10** | **0/10** |

**Cost, and why it matters to #1677:** that gap is paid per payload phase, so it is a
throughput tax on anything that streams (OTA_WRITE's 260 B chunks, bulk socket
sends). Any throughput figure taken before this change is not comparable. The value
is empirical, not derived — the real fix is a readable READY line, which needs a
board revision that does not put it on `SPI1_SCLK_A`.

**Measure this surface with a bare `accept()` listener, never an HTTP server.** An
HTTP server logs only a *parsed* request, so it cannot see a connection whose bytes
it never parses — which is exactly the trial that works. That instrument is what
kept this issue mis-characterised as "cannot connect to anything".

### Fixed — the DRP-AI Yocto inference backend now has CI compile coverage; ORT and DEEPX already gained it as a side effect of #1900 (#1747)

`src/yocto/inference_ort.cpp`, `inference_deepx.cpp`, and `inference_drpai.cpp`
default OFF (`ALP_SDK_USE_ORT_CPU` / `ALP_SDK_USE_DEEPX_DXM1` /
`ALP_SDK_USE_DRPAI_V2N`) because their real vendor SDKs (ONNX Runtime,
DEEPX dx_rt, the EdgeCortix MERA2/DRP-AI TVM runtime) are license- or
account-gated and unobtainable in CI — so none of the three was compiled by
any PR gate, and a change to any of them could ship broken straight into a
release with nothing to catch it.

`#1900` already closed the gap for ORT and DEEPX incidentally, adding
`tests/yocto/inference_ort_regression.cpp` and
`inference_deepx_regression.cpp`, which compile those two backends' real
`.cpp` bodies against clean-room stand-in vendor headers
(`tests/yocto/fakes/onnxruntime/`, `tests/yocto/fakes/dxrt/`) and are wired
into `tests/yocto/CMakeLists.txt` as ctest targets — reachable by
`pr-plain-cmake.yml`'s existing `yocto` (and `strict-warnings`) jobs on
every PR touching `src/**`, no vendor SDK required.

This closes the same gap for DRP-AI: `tests/yocto/inference_drpai_regression.cpp`
compiles `src/yocto/inference_drpai.cpp` against a new
`tests/yocto/fakes/drpai/` (a clean-room stand-in for
`MeraDrpRuntimeWrapper.h`, plus a fake `linux/drpai.h` for the DRP-AI
driver uapi struct/ioctl this file also hard-`#include`s), also wired into
`tests/yocto/CMakeLists.txt`. Unlike ORT/DEEPX, DRP-AI's `open()` resolves
its reserved-memory arena via a real `::open("/dev/drpai0", ...)` +
`::ioctl()` before ever touching the vendor C++ API, so no CI runner (there
is no such device) ever reaches `LoadModel()`/`GetInputInfo()`/`Run()` —
these tests instead cover what IS host-independent: the `model_data`/
`model_size` input-validation guard, the documented "device absent ->
`ALP_ERR_IO`, not a guess" contract, and the NULL-`be_state` guards on
every other hook. All three backends now fail a PR's build the moment a
change to them breaks compilation, closing the "ships unbuilt" risk this
issue named even though full behavioral coverage of the DRP-AI vendor
surface still requires real silicon.

### Fixed — cold-chain-monitor README sent every DEEPX customer to the wrong SKU (#1749)

`examples/ai/cold-chain-monitor/README.md` told a reader to "Flip `som.sku` in
`board.yaml` to `E1M-V2M101` for the DEEPX DX-M1 path" -- correct advice for an
`E1M-V2N101`/`E1M-V2N102` customer, but misleading for an `E1M-V2M102`
customer, whose SKU already carries the DEEPX DX-M1 NPU
(`metadata/socs/deepx/dx/m1.json`'s `variants[0].alp_module_skus` lists both
`E1M-V2M101` and `E1M-V2M102`; `metadata/e1m_modules/E1M-V2M102.yaml` sets
`on_module.npu: deepx_dxm1`, `inference.preferred_backend: deepx_dxm1`, and
`capabilities.deepx_dxm1: true`).

The sentence now states the SKU-neutral fact -- the DEEPX DX-M1 NPU is
populated on `E1M-V2M101`/`E1M-V2M102` and absent on `E1M-V2N101`/
`E1M-V2N102`, the same PCB without it -- and leaves the `som.sku` pick to the
reader either way.

Filed from `alplabai/tan-cli#946`, which had already locally corrected its
vendored copy of this file via `DELIBERATE_EDITS`
(`tests/parity/scaffold_byte_parity.py`, same pattern as tan-cli#814/#821(a)/
#912) pending this upstream fix; that entry retires once tan-cli re-vendors
this tree. The wording landed here does not byte-match tan-cli's own local
correction, so the re-vendor's parity capture must be regenerated, not
assumed to already match.

### Fixed — a citation whose path starts with a dot was silently unchecked (#1755)

`scripts/check_changelog_citations.py`'s `_CITATION` path group began
`[A-Za-z0-9_]`, so a path whose first character is a dot never matched the regex
at all. Every `.github/workflows/*.yml:NNN` citation was therefore invisible to
the gate -- not reported, not skipped, simply never seen, while the summary line
reported a confident count that excluded them.

#1750 widened the blast radius by extending this gate to scan `CHANGELOG.md`,
where several such citations already ship. It also set a trap for anyone fixing a
citation correctly: rewriting a bare workflow-filename citation into its real repo-relative
`.github/...` path REMOVED it from the gate's view, so doing the right thing
reduced coverage.

The path group now accepts an optional single leading dot. The regex is anchored
on backticks at both ends, so this cannot widen it into prose. With the
previously-invisible citations now in scope the gate resolves 109 citations across
55 fragments plus `CHANGELOG.md` with zero errors -- every one that had been
shipping unchecked resolves correctly. Two unit tests pin the dotted and undotted
forms.

### Fixed — a repo-wide documentation sweep corrected 27 claims that contradicted the tree (#1757–#1783)

Twenty-six docs stated something the current tree disagrees with, and one
example directory promised a `.gitignore` that did not exist. Every claim was
checked against its source of truth before editing.

Two mattered more than the rest.

`docs/tutorials/02-i2c-scan.md` told the reader to expect OPTIGA Trust M
(`0x30`), TMP112 (`0x48`) and RV-3028-C7 (`0x52`) to ACK on the bus the
scanner opens. `BOARD_I2C_SENSORS` resolves to `ALP_E1M_I2C0` (SoC I2C2), and
`metadata/e1m_modules/E1M-AEN801.yaml` puts only the 24C128 EEPROM at `0x50`
on `e1m_i2c0:`; the other three sit on a separate bus, `brd_i2c:`, that this
scan never opens. Three of the four documented ACKs
could never appear, so a reader chasing them was debugging a bus that was
never there. The page now agrees with `docs/bring-up-aen.md`, including that
`0x48` on I2C2 is U32 INA236B (+V_CAM0 rail) on pre-respin carriers, not the
TMP112.

`examples/connectivity/iot-connected-camera/certs/README.md` told the reader
that `client.key` was covered by a `.gitignore` in that directory. There was
no `.gitignore` there at all — `git check-ignore` on the path exited 1, and
the directory tracked only `README.md`. A customer generating a key beside it
and running `git add -A` would have committed a TLS private key. The missing
`.gitignore` is now present and the sentence describes what it actually does.

The remainder were stale identifiers and versions: the GD32 bridge protocol
documented as `0.2.0` where `gd32-bridge-firmware:src/protocol.h` defines
`0.9.0`; `ALP_ERR_NOSUPPORT` printed as `-5` in two expected-output blocks
where `include/alp/peripheral.h` defines `-6`; `v0.15-snapshot.json` named as
the current ABI snapshot while `metadata/sdk_version.yaml` declares `0.16.0`;
AEN and NX9101 described as E1M-X when they are E1M (35x35 mm); console
samples showing `EVK_PIN_*` names that `gpio-button-led` never prints; and a
`west build` line missing the `/r9a09g056n48gbg/cm33` board qualifiers.

Three ADRs keep their decisions intact and gained corrections instead:
ADR-0009 records in a dated amendment that the AEN sysbuild overlay ships
`SB_CONFIG_MCUBOOT_MODE_SINGLE_APP=y` rather than swap-using-scratch,
ADR-0022's status block now says the Renode models it called "still present"
were deleted, and ADR-0015's prebuilt-blob claim points at a path that exists.

### Removed — `coreMQTT-SN` is dropped: its upstream repository no longer exists (#1784)

`west.yml` pinned `coreMQTT-SN` to `v1.0.1` on the `freertos-org` remote, but
`github.com/FreeRTOS/coreMQTT-SN` has been deleted upstream. Anyone running
`west update --group-filter +extras-tier1` could not fetch it, so the whole
`extras-tier1` group was unfetchable rather than just this one library.
`examples/connectivity/mqtt-sn-publish/README.md` already recorded the
disappearance in prose while the manifest kept pointing at the dead remote.

A second break came with it: `metadata/libraries/coremqtt-sn.yaml` cited
`metadata/library-profiles/coremqtt_sn/`, a directory that does not exist.

Rather than repoint at an unofficial mirror of an abandoned library, the
library is removed: its west project and the now-unused `freertos-org` remote,
`metadata/libraries/coremqtt-sn.yaml`, the `coremqtt_sn` entry in
`metadata/library-aliases-v1.json`, the `ALP_MQTTSN_MBEDTLS` /
`ALP_MQTTSN_BEARSSL` / `ALP_MQTTSN_NO_TLS` Kconfig knobs, the
`examples/connectivity/mqtt-sn-publish` example, and its `ws6c-emit-parity`
fixture. `metadata/catalog.json` and `docs/portability-matrix.md` are
regenerated (the library × SKU cell counts move from 248/252 to 241/245 and
from 144/144 to 140/140; the four incompatible cells are unrelated and
unchanged).

MQTT itself is unaffected — `<alp/iot.h>`'s `alp_mqtt_*` surface and the
libmosquitto-backed Yocto implementation do not depend on this library. The
`VERSIONS.md` roadmap line offering MQTT-SN as a future secondary protocol on
that same surface also stands: it describes an Alp Lab API we have not built
yet, not this third-party package.

### Fixed — mqtt-telemetry README pointed a scaffold customer at `native_sim.conf` outside their tree (#1794)

`examples/connectivity/mqtt-telemetry/README.md` referenced `native_sim.conf` twice: a bare
markdown link the scaffold doc-link rewriter (`_RELATIVE_LINK_RE` in `scripts/alp_template.py`,
`../`-prefixed links only) never touched because the file is a *child* of the example dir, not a
sibling; and a `west build` instruction naming the same file. The `iot` template's envelope
(`metadata/templates/catalog-v1.json`) does not include `native_sim.conf`, so both references
dead-ended for a `tan init --template iot` customer.

The link now uses the same `../mqtt-telemetry/native_sim.conf` detour already established for
`examples/ai/cold-chain-monitor/README.md`'s `models/README.md` link, with the same one-line HTML
comment naming the rewriter's `../`-only regex so it survives future tidying. The Build section
now states the native_sim leg is in-tree only, matching cold-chain's reworded Tests section; the
build command itself is unchanged.

`tests/scripts/test_alp_template.py::test_scaffold_readme_mqtt_native_sim_conf_link_survives_scaffolding`
pins the emitted-envelope link so a future edit back to the natural-looking `](native_sim.conf)`
fails loudly instead of shipping a silent regression.

Deliberately out of scope: adding `native_sim.conf` to the `iot` template's file envelope. That
would fix the underlying gap for real, but it changes a published template's file set, moves
goldens, and affects tan-cli's vendored parity capture — a maintainer call, not a doc fix.

### Fixed — mqtt-telemetry's TLS-status sentence rendered as two paragraphs, and its Build lead-in over-scoped a native_sim caveat onto the working real-silicon command

An adversarial review of #1798 caught a rendering regression that shipped on `dev` in that PR
and was then copied into this file's own `native_sim.conf` link (the change above) by the same
commit that added it here: the explanatory `<!-- The ../mqtt-telemetry/ detour is deliberate:
... -->` comment sat at column 0 on its own line, which CommonMark parses as an HTML block that
CAN interrupt a paragraph. It split "the native_sim leg turns mbedtls off (see" from the
`native_sim.conf` link that completes the sentence into two separate `<p>` tags, both on GitHub
and in every emitted scaffold README. The comment now sits above the paragraph as its own block,
separated by a blank line, which keeps the sentence in one `<p>`.
`examples/ai/cold-chain-monitor/README.md` carried the identical defect from the same #1798
commit; its fix is in `changelog.d/1688.md`.

The Build section's lead-in also over-promised and over-scoped: "In the alp-sdk tree, the
native_sim leg builds against the in-tree `native_sim.conf` ... and runs with:" prefaced the
WHOLE fenced block, including the real-silicon leg a scaffold customer CAN run, casting doubt on
the one command that works; and it never said outright that a scaffold customer cannot run the
native_sim leg as shown, while the scaffold rewriter turns the command's own path argument into
`.` -- the customer's own directory -- directly contradicting "in the alp-sdk tree". The lead-in
prose is now gone; the caveat is a comment inside the fenced block, attached only to the
native_sim leg, explicit that `native_sim.conf` is not in the scaffold and naming the one fix
that is actually runnable from the emitted scaffold form (copy the file in from the link above)
-- an earlier draft also offered "build this leg from an alp-sdk checkout", but that remedy
doesn't match what a scaffold customer sees: the command's own path argument and
`EXTRA_ZEPHYR_MODULES` value are already rewritten to `.` and `$ALP_SDK_ROOT`, i.e. run FROM the
scaffold, not from an alp-sdk checkout. The real-silicon leg carries no caveat. The `west
build`/`west flash` command lines themselves are byte-identical to before this fix.

`test_scaffold_readme_cold_chain_models_link_survives_scaffolding` and
`test_scaffold_readme_mqtt_native_sim_conf_link_survives_scaffolding` in
`tests/scripts/test_alp_template.py` previously asserted only that the rewritten URL substring
was present in the emitted README -- true even with the paragraph split, which is exactly why the
regression shipped past them. Both now also assert the lead-in text and the link land in the same
rendered block. `markdown_it` (the library that would let a test render CommonMark directly) is
not a declared project dependency -- absent from `pyproject.toml` and `scripts/requirements.txt`,
so not installed by the `pip install -e ".[dev,model-compile]"` step that runs `pytest
tests/scripts/` in CI -- so the added assertion is a small stdlib-only helper that pins the same
CommonMark fact (no blank line, no column-0 HTML block opener, between the two markers) without
adding one. `tests/fixtures/emit-snapshots/scaffold.edge-ai-v2n101.snap` moved to match the
cold-chain-monitor README fix; regenerated with `check_emit_snapshots.py --update`, not
hand-edited.

### Fixed — i2c-master's remaining bare `i2c-scanner` referents, orphaned when #1792 closed #1705 early (#1795)

`examples/peripheral-io/i2c-master/README.md`'s bare cross-reference to

`src/main.c` ("you may want to run ...", "Use i2c-scanner to enumerate ...")

### Fixed — `docs/aen-se-services.md` listed a second AEN bench board that does not exist (#1797)

ADR 0030 sets the supported SERAM floor for E1M-AEN at **v110** and says a board
below it "is updated before it is trusted to produce evidence". The per-board
table this doc added to record that
(`docs/aen-se-services.md:170` ("SERAM version, per physical board (#1797)"))
carried two rows: the bench unit, and "the second AEN bench board (on the
internal board farm)" marked `TBD` / **Unverified**.

There is no second board. That board-farm place definition is stale —
every resource on it reports `avail: False` with `port: None` and
`path: None`, the exporter host has no `/dev/ttyUSB*` attached at all, and the
exporter's own udev match rules name `ID_SERIAL_SHORT` `BG01028C` and
`BG04503B`, which are the same two FTDI adapters the bench enumerates as its
SE-UART and app-console ports. One board, moved off the farm.

The remaining row is now identified by module revision and serial rather than by
which host it happens to be plugged into, and re-confirmed on a cold power-on
reset: `SEROM v1.105.65 0x000002A0`, `SES A0 v1.110.0 Mar  4 2026`, both SERAM
banks `1.110.0`, `LCS=1`
(`docs/aen-se-services.md:179` ("The AEN bench unit")).

**v110 meets the floor exactly**, so every AEN board in existence is above it and
no SE-touching result is taken on a pairing ADR 0030 calls untriageable.

The same cold-POR capture also settled #1702, which had recorded that the SERAM
offset record at `0x805ffff0` does not survive a cold power-on and that the unit
must therefore be run warm-reset only. It survived a full 20 s power-off: SEROM
handed off to a valid SERAM bank, `ATOC ok`, and slot0 booted in 31.09 ms. That
constraint is not in force, which matters because it was written into every AEN
and CC3501E bench harness.

### Fixed — the CC3501E firmware docs called async-event delivery future work eight months after it shipped (#1799)

Slave->master async-event delivery landed in **#1721** (merged 2026-08-27,
closing **#130**): the CC35 pulses an attention edge on the existing READY wire
(`GPIO17` -> Alif `P2_6`), the host arms with `cc3501e_attn_arm()` and drains on
the edge, and it was validated on silicon at 135 of 135 firmware pushes across a
40 s armed window with the console timer poll at 60 s — so no timer delivery
could have accounted for it. Eight places in `cc3501e-bridge-firmware:` still described
the whole mechanism as unbuilt.

Two of those were worse than stale. `src/protocol_gpio.c` and
`hal/ti/cc3501e_hw_ti_gpio.c` both said `EVT_GPIO_INTERRUPT` delivery "needs the
next-rev host-IRQ line". The line exists; `gpio_irq_cb()` simply never calls
`event_ring_push()`. A reader following those comments would have specified a
board change to buy something an existing one-line call already reaches. They now
name the real blocker.

`DESIGN.md`'s section is rewritten around what shipped, including the three
properties of the shared wire that are load-bearing rather than incidental —
sticky arm intent (unconditional re-arming in `lock_release()` hangs the device
after `WIFI_SCAN`), the 50 ms empty-drain backoff (the wire also carries READY
flow control, so a transaction end is indistinguishable from an attention pulse;
without the backoff 86 events cost 11888 ISRs instead of 220), and that a full
ring must still pulse (16 boot-time Wi-Fi events fill the ring, and pulsing only
on a successful push is unrecoverable on an idle host). A *dedicated* HOST_IRQ
pad on a later board rev stays documented as future work, which is what would
remove the shared-wire ambiguity in the first place.

**Correcting the prose surfaced two limits that were written down nowhere.**

The firmware pulse is a **build-time opt-in**: `build_ti.ps1 -AttnPulse` sets
`-DCC3501E_ATTN_PULSE=1` and is default OFF, because the wire is a rev-1 bodge
absent on the stock EVK. `ti/package_cc3501e_prod.ps1` builds with
`build_ti.ps1 -Ble` and does not pass it, so the production recipe produces an
image whose attention call links a no-op stub — a host that arms attention never
sees an edge and silently falls back to its timer poll. `prebuilt/CHANGELOG.md`
nonetheless listed the attention edge as a plain 0.4.0 feature; it now records
that whether the shipped `cc3501e-v0.4.0.bin` carries the pulse is **unverified**,
and says to assume it does not until an edge is observed on silicon. The
host-side subscriber fan-out (#1724) is unconditional and unaffected.

And only Wi-Fi events have a producer: `EVT_WIFI_CONNECTED` and
`EVT_WIFI_DISCONNECTED` are the only `event_ring_push()` call sites in the tree.
`EVT_GPIO_INTERRUPT` and every BLE event have none, so they never reach the host
whatever the transport does. `BRINGUP_STATUS.md` §4 and §8 now say so instead of
implying the transport is the gap.

`BRINGUP_STATUS.md` also carried the accuracy fixes made in the extracted
`alplabai/cc3501e-bridge-firmware` repo but never ported back here, which matters
because this copy is the one alp-sdk consumers read: the TL;DR table still
advertised a single **"Wi-Fi connect-STA / soft-AP / sockets … socket APIs
shipped"** row. Sockets do not connect at all on fw 0.4.0 / protocol 5 (#1746),
and soft-AP association is unresolved (#1562, #1385). Those are now three
separate rows carrying their real state and evidence, plus the §0.5 current-state
section (shipping versions, what #1740 and #1743 fixed, open items with
measurements, bench traps). The header date moves 2026-07-08 -> 2026-08-28.

No behaviour changes: comments, docs and one changelog bullet only.

### Fixed — `alp_power_configure_wake_source()` lied about arming a wake source it could never honour on stock AEN builds (#1812)

On a default `alp_e1m_aen801_m55_he/ae822fa0e5597ls0/rtss_he` build, pinned
upstream Zephyr 4.4.0's Alif E8 SoC does not `select HAS_PM`, so `CONFIG_PM`
is unreachable and `src/backends/power/zephyr_pm_policy.c` (gated `depends
on PM`) never compiles in. `src/backends/power/zephyr_stub.c`'s wildcard
priority-0 fallback wins `alp_backend_select("power", ...)` instead.
`alp_power_open()` and `alp_power_configure_wake_source()` both returned
`ALP_OK`; only `alp_power_request_sleep()` returned `ALP_ERR_NOSUPPORT` — a
caller found out its setup was pointless only after asking to sleep. No AEN
example called the portable `<alp/power.h>` surface at all, so nothing in CI
noticed.

Shipping the full `alif_aipm` SE-backed power backend the issue's "Proposed
resolution" describes (`SERVICES_power_wakeup_config` /
`_mem_retention_config` / `_stop_mode_request` / the VTOR-save calls for warm
resume) is out of scope for this change: it needs bench time on real E8
silicon this pass didn't have, and faking a sleep path that has never
actually entered STOP on hardware would be worse than the bug it replaces.
Landing that backend is tracked as follow-on work; #1813 settles the
`<alp/power.h>` shape it needs first.

What lands now is the issue's accepted minimum: the failure moves to
configuration time, enforced once in the dispatcher rather than duplicated
per backend. `src/power_dispatch.c`'s `alp_power_configure_wake_source()`
rejects any bit outside what the active backend reported at `open()` time
via the new `alp_power_wake_capabilities()` accessor — `ALP_ERR_NOSUPPORT`,
not `ALP_OK` — before the backend's own op ever runs.

The fix closes this gap on every backend registered for the `power` class
today, and each reports ONLY what it can genuinely deliver:

- `zephyr_stub.c` reports zero armable wake bits — it can arm nothing.
- `zephyr_pm_policy.c` reports `ALP_POWER_WAKE_TIMER` ONLY. Its `_wake_sem`
  has exactly one giver in the whole file, `_timer_expiry` (armed by its own
  `k_timer` when `wake_after_ms > 0`); there is no out-of-band signaller for
  a GPIO IRQ, UART RX, or RTC-alarm-as-distinct-source. An earlier draft of
  this fix advertised RTC/GPIO/UART_RX on the theory that the caller's own
  peripheral setup would cover them — review caught that this backend never
  actually wakes on any of them, so a caller following exactly the protocol
  the header prescribes (check `alp_power_wake_capabilities()`, configure
  the advertised bit, call `request_sleep` with `wake_after_ms == 0`) would
  park on `K_FOREVER` forever: the #1812 shape, reincarnated on a second
  backend. `z_request_sleep` now also refuses `wake_after_ms == 0` outright
  with `ALP_ERR_NOSUPPORT` — belt-and-suspenders, since the dispatcher's own
  INVAL guard only rejects an *empty* bitmap paired with `wake_after_ms ==
  0`, not a non-empty one (e.g. `ALP_POWER_WAKE_TIMER` configured, but
  `wake_after_ms` still passed as `0` by mistake).
- `yocto_drv.c` reports `ALP_POWER_WAKE_RTC` ONLY — the one bit its
  `_program_wakealarm` genuinely arms. Every other bit has no matching
  sysfs knob at all, and even `ALP_POWER_WAKE_RTC` itself only arms
  anything when `wake_after_ms > 0` (the wakealarm is programmed lazily at
  `request_sleep()` time, not by the bitmap) — a caller configuring
  `ALP_POWER_WAKE_RTC` with `wake_after_ms == 0` arms nothing here and
  falls through to whatever the kernel's own already-enabled wakeup
  sources do, unrelated to this backend. **Behaviour change for
  out-of-tree callers**: before this fix EVERY bit besides `RTC` returned
  `ALP_OK` from `alp_power_configure_wake_source()` on a Yocto build and
  was silently ignored; those now return `ALP_ERR_NOSUPPORT`. A caller
  wanting a guaranteed wake on this backend must pass `wake_after_ms > 0`.

A bitmap the dispatcher rejects is now never mirrored into the handle
either, so `alp_renesas_power_supervisor_mode_set`
(`src/backends/ext/renesas/power.c`), which reads that mirror directly and
forwards it to `gd32g553_power_mode_set()`, can never receive one hardware
never agreed to arm.

The three backends also now agree on `alp_power_wake_info_t::realised_mode`
when a call fails outright: `zephyr_stub.c` and `zephyr_pm_policy.c`
(`wake_after_ms == 0`) both report `ALP_POWER_MODE_RUN`, matching
`yocto_drv.c`'s pre-existing failure-path behaviour — none of them echo
back the requested mode as if it had been realised.

`examples/aen/aen-power-smoke` now calls `alp_power_open()` /
`alp_power_wake_capabilities()` / `alp_power_configure_wake_source()` /
`alp_power_request_sleep()` (the exact repro from this issue) and logs the
result, informationally, AFTER its existing WFI/SysTick proof has already
printed its own RESULT line (a real backend's DEEP_SLEEP success would
reboot the core via the SE and skip everything after it, so the probe runs
last, not first). Its `prj.conf` gained `CONFIG_ALP_SDK=y`, without which
`<alp/power.h>` isn't even on the include path. This is now exercised by the
AEN801 board-target build gate. `tests/zephyr/peripheral/src/main.c`'s
native_sim power-mode ZTESTs (the same stub-backend path, no `CONFIG_PM`)
assert the new configuration-time contract directly, and
`tests/unit/power_registry` gained matching coverage for the pm_policy
backend: `ALP_POWER_WAKE_TIMER`-only capability, the `wake_after_ms == 0`
refusal, and a STOP-mode round-down assertion mirroring the yocto test.

### Changed — `<alp/power.h>` mode ladder, retention, and wake-source contract settled while still `[ABI-EXPERIMENTAL]` (#1813)

`<alp/power.h>` could not express what the Alif Ensemble E8 actually offers,
and it is `[ABI-EXPERIMENTAL]` precisely so this can be fixed before an AEN
power backend freezes against it (`docs/abi-markers.md` confirmed before
touching the header — no ABI-snapshot major-bump gate applies pre-1.0 to an
experimental symbol; `docs/abi/v0.16-snapshot.json`, the CURRENT snapshot
per `metadata/sdk_version.yaml`'s still-0.16.0 `version:`, is regenerated in
place for the new symbols, following the same-week precedent set by
`bc6974d3` — see the ABI-snapshot note at the end).

- **`ALP_POWER_MODE_STOP`** — a fifth rung on `alp_power_mode_t`, below
  `STANDBY`. The E8's STOP ladder (datasheet Table 5-5) runs from a ~900 nA
  floor at STOP_5 (nothing retained AND no wake source armed) up through
  low-uA levels depending on what's retained and armed (e.g. STOP_2 retains
  the 4 KB Utility SRAM at ~1.1 uA; pairing `ALP_POWER_RETAIN_NONE` with a
  real wake source is actually STOP_4 at ~1000 nA — LPRTC/LFXO — or STOP_3
  at ~1050 nA — LPTIMER/BOD/LPCMP/LPGPIO — 11-17% above the STOP_5 number, a
  real gap for anyone sizing a battery off it); the SDK had no way to name
  any of this. The two generic backends registered for the `power` class
  today, `zephyr_pm_policy.c` and `yocto_drv.c`, have nothing deeper than
  `PM_STATE_SUSPEND_TO_RAM` / `"mem"` to offer, so both now round STOP DOWN
  to that state explicitly (not through their `default:` case, which
  rounded to the SHALLOWEST state instead) and report
  `alp_power_wake_info_t::realised_mode` as `STANDBY`, never `STOP` — a
  caller is never told the backend reached a depth it never proved. All
  three backends (`zephyr_stub` included) now also agree that a call which
  fails outright reports `realised_mode == ALP_POWER_MODE_RUN`, never an
  echo of the mode that was requested but never realised.
- **`alp_power_configure_retention()` + `alp_power_retain_t`** — a portable
  retention descriptor (`ALP_POWER_RETAIN_NONE` / `_UTILITY` / `_TCM` with a
  `retain_kb` field / `_FULL`), not a raw vendor bitmask, mapping onto
  `SERVICES_power_mem_retention_config`'s bitmask on a real E8 backend.
  `ALP_POWER_RETAIN_TCM` always rounds UP to the backend's own retention
  granularity — never `ALP_ERR_NOSUPPORT` for a `retain_kb` that doesn't land
  exactly, which the header's first draft contradicted itself on.
  `{ALP_POWER_RETAIN_TCM, retain_kb=0}` is rejected as `ALP_ERR_INVAL` (not a
  valid spelling of "retain nothing" — use `ALP_POWER_RETAIN_NONE`).
  Optional on the backend vtable (`alp_power_ops_t::configure_retention` may
  be `NULL`): a backend with no opinion accepts `ALP_POWER_RETAIN_NONE` as a
  no-op and returns `ALP_ERR_NOSUPPORT` for anything else. Mirrored into the
  handle only on `ALP_OK`, same reasoning as the wake bitmap below — which
  means a `configure_retention` implementation sees the STALE `state->retain`
  during its own call (the new request is the `retain` parameter, not yet
  mirrored); `power_ops.h`'s vtable doc now says so explicitly, so the first
  real implementer isn't trapped by it. A `{ALP_POWER_RETAIN_TCM,
  retain_kb=0}` regression test now backs this (`tests/zephyr/peripheral`) —
  the verification ledger previously claimed this path was covered when
  nothing actually exercised it.
- **`alp_power_wake_capabilities()`** — a new dedicated accessor reporting
  which `ALP_POWER_WAKE_*` bits the active backend can arm. Deliberately
  NOT a field on `alp_power_capabilities()`'s existing `alp_capabilities_t`:
  that struct's `flags` is the cross-class `alp_instance_cap_t` bitmap every
  peripheral class shares (`cap_instance.h`), and its bit values collide
  numerically with `ALP_POWER_WAKE_*` one-for-one (`ALP_INSTANCE_CAP_DMA` ==
  `ALP_POWER_WAKE_RTC` == bit 0, `HW_OVERSAMPLE` == `WAKE_GPIO`, and so on) —
  overloading it would have made `alp_capabilities_has(caps,
  ALP_INSTANCE_CAP_DMA)` return true for a power handle that merely armed an
  RTC wake. `alp_power_ops_t::open()` gained a dedicated `wake_caps_out`
  output parameter (a separate channel from the existing `caps_out`) so
  every backend reports it without touching the shared struct.
- **`ALP_POWER_WAKE_COMPARATOR` / `ALP_POWER_WAKE_BROWNOUT`** — two wake
  bits with no earlier portable equivalent (the E8 LPCMP analog threshold
  wake and brown-out detect).
- **Reported-capability + error contract for wake sources, enforced
  centrally.** `<alp/power.h>` previously documented "unsupported bits are
  silently ignored" on the `ALP_POWER_WAKE_*` bitmap, directly contradicting
  `alp_power_configure_wake_source()`'s own already-documented
  `ALP_ERR_NOSUPPORT` return. That contradiction is resolved in the honest
  direction: `src/power_dispatch.c`'s `alp_power_configure_wake_source()`
  now rejects, for EVERY registered `power`-class backend in one guard, any
  bitmap containing a bit outside what `alp_power_wake_capabilities()`
  reports — not a per-backend duplicated check. All three backends
  registered today report exactly what they can genuinely deliver, not what
  seemed plausible: `zephyr_stub` (0, the AEN-default — #1812), `yocto_drv`
  (`ALP_POWER_WAKE_RTC` only — the one bit its wakealarm genuinely arms;
  everything else has no sysfs knob), and `zephyr_pm_policy`
  (`ALP_POWER_WAKE_TIMER` only — its `_wake_sem` has exactly one giver, its
  own `k_timer`; an earlier draft of this change advertised RTC/GPIO/
  UART_RX here too on the theory that the caller's own peripheral setup
  covered them, which review caught as #1812 reincarnated on a second
  backend — see #1812's changelog entry for the fix). `src/backends/ext/
  renesas/power.c` implements no `power`-class vtable of its own (it's a
  vendor-ext bypass reading the dispatcher's mirrored bitmap directly), so
  it inherits the fix automatically once a rejected bitmap is no longer
  mirrored into the handle on failure.

**ABI-snapshot precedent.** `metadata/sdk_version.yaml` still reads
`version: 0.16.0` / `status: released`, and `v0.16.0` is tagged, so naively
regenerating `docs/abi/v0.16-snapshot.json` looked like rewriting shipped
history. It isn't: `bc6974d3` (`feat(cc3501e): host driver + console for the
SPI1 bridge passthrough (#1842)`), merged to `dev` on 2026-08-30 — a week
after the `v0.16.0` tag, with `sdk_version.yaml` unchanged — directly edited
`docs/abi/v0.16-snapshot.json` in place for its own new public symbols
("The ABI snapshot is regenerated for the new fields", per its commit
message). The tagged commit itself is untouched; the file literally named
`v0.16-snapshot.json` on `dev`'s HEAD is a rolling ledger of the CURRENT
`[ABI-EXPERIMENTAL]`+`[ABI-STABLE]` surface, not a frozen artifact of the
tag, until whatever cuts v0.17.0 renames/regenerates it. This change follows
that exact precedent rather than inventing a new one or bumping the version
file unilaterally.

### Fixed — the AEN calendar ran on the errata-bound LPRTC with no caveat, and the SoM's own `rv3028c7` workaround turned out to be unreachable (#1814)

`AERR0012` v2.0 leaves no Ensemble revision without an RTC accuracy quirk, and
`src/backends/rtc/lprtc_calendar_shim.c` — the AEN calendar path — carried
neither erratum. ER001 (Rev **A0**, the bench silicon, fixed in A1): a POR_N
assertion or a wake from STOP resets the RTC clock pre-scaler divider, and
re-programming it afterwards does not recover the lost accuracy. ER002 (Rev
**A1**, no fix planned): while POR_N is asserted the clock source falls from
the 32 kHz LFXO to the ~5%-accurate LFRC. Both are now recorded at the shim
(`src/backends/rtc/lprtc_calendar_shim.c:44` ("SILICON CAVEAT (#1814)")) and in
both AEN RTC example READMEs
(`examples/aen/aen-rtc-calendar/README.md:38` ("see alp-sdk#1814")).

Alif's own stated ER002 workaround is "use an external real-time clock
source", and the `E1M-AEN801` SoM already carries one — an `rv3028c7` at
7-bit `0x52` on `BRD_I2C`, driver already at `chips/rv3028c7/rv3028c7.c`
(`metadata/e1m_modules/E1M-AEN801.yaml:119` ("chip: rv3028c7")). It is
**not** switched to here, and the reason recorded in an earlier draft of this
fragment was wrong. That draft said the pads "carry no documented I2C function
at all". They do: `BRD_I2C_SCL` is `P7_1` and `BRD_I2C_SDA` is `P7_0`, and
`ADTS0013` v1.2 Table 3-16 gives those pads `I2C0_SCL_C` / `I2C0_SDA_C` --
I2C0, which HWRM 15.4.1 documents as master-or-slave capable. The slave-only
`0x40` constraint belongs to `LPI2C0` on `P7_4`/`P7_5`, which is not where this
bus is wired.

What that r1 run actually measured was two floating pins, and the conclusion
drawn from it does not carry. On an **r1** module the RTC and the TMP112 sit on
LPI2C0 (`P7_4`/`P7_5`) and **nothing is attached to `P7_0`/`P7_1`** -- so
nothing could have ACKed there whatever the pad biasing. The `-116`
(`-ETIMEDOUT`) with `E: User Abort on i2c@49010000` at High-Z, and the `-5`
(`-EIO`) with the pad's internal pull-up enabled, characterised an empty net
rather than a populated bus. The "no usable pull-up, the two 0 ohm jumpers are
not stuffed" reading and the open-drain-vs-push-pull inference both came from
that same floating net, and neither survives.

Bench-settled again on 2026-09-05 on **2626-R2** silicon -- the revision that
actually routes `BRD_I2C` to I2C0 -- the bus works on the SoC's **internal
pull-up alone**. The `rv3028c7` ACKs at `0x52` (ID register `0x28` = `0x44`,
seconds `0x01` -> `0x02`, so the oscillator runs), and every non-response is a
clean `rc=-5` (`-EIO`) NACK with zero `-ETIMEDOUT` across the whole run.
`R93`/`R94` stay DNP and are not needed. The withdrawal of the "not usable as
built" verdict, and the customer-facing writeup of the bus, are recorded in
this release's #1848 fragment.

**Later correction:** the `0x28` = `0x44` reading above was written up as if
it confirmed the part's identity outright. Per the RV-3028-C7 Application
Manual Rev. 1.4 §3.14, register `0x28` splits into an HID nibble (hardware
identity) and a VID nibble (production-line version); only HID `0x4` is an
identity claim -- VID `0x4` is a separate, production-line-scoped field, not
additional confirmation.

So nothing electrical blocks `rv3028c7` from backing the AEN calendar any
more. **#1814 stays open as a deliberate backend-selection change, not a board
change** -- and it is not a free upgrade. `VDD_BAT`/`VBACKUP` has no supply
fitted on this batch (`R4`/`R68` both DNP), so the external RTC loses the time
on a cold boot exactly as the LPRTC does; switching backends buys accuracy
while running, not persistence across power.

The LPRTC shim therefore stays the AEN calendar source for now. Its counter
keeps advancing across a reset; it is the *elapsed* time across one that is
untrustworthy on both silicon revisions, so a caller that needs accuracy must
re-set the time from an external source after any POR
(`src/backends/rtc/lprtc_calendar_shim.c:103`
("selection deliberately (#1814)")).

A follow-up review round flagged 4 majors against a different framing bug:
every comment and doc line above described the LFXO-to-LFRC fallback as
happening only "while POR_N is asserted" -- accurate as errata text, but the
bench module's own SE boot header reports `[SES] No LF XTAL` on *every* boot,
meaning this board has no 32 kHz LFXO fitted at all and LFRC is its
permanent LPRTC clock source, POR_N or not. That is not a transient
startup state; it is the steady state, and it means the calendar drifts
continuously at LFRC's ~5% offset from LFXO -- roughly 72 minutes per day --
for as long as the shim runs, not only across a reset. The shim comment, both
example READMEs, and `docs/aen-se-services.md` are corrected to say so
(`src/backends/rtc/lprtc_calendar_shim.c:59` ("BENCH FACT (goes beyond the errata text above")).

### Added — promote DMA0 + EVTRTR0 into the shared E8 devicetree, add EVTRTR2 (#1815)

The E8 ships three PL330 DMA controllers and three Event Routers (AE822 HWRM §3.13.4: "EVTRTR0,
dedicated to DMA0 controller and UTIMER... EVTRTR1, dedicated to DMA1 controller... EVTRTR2,
dedicated to DMA2 controller and LPUTIMER"), but `evtrtr0`/`dma0` were declared only inside FIVE
example board overlays (`aen-cc3501e-bringup`, `aen-usb-firstlight`, `aen-cc3501e-gatt-register`,
`aen-cc3501e-companion-tour`, `aen-cc3501e-ble-gatt`) — the CC3501E bridge SPI1's only DMA
consumer — with no way for a second consumer to reach the same nodes without copy-pasting the
`ALIF_DMA_ENCODE()` cells and peripheral-request numbers by hand. `dma2` (the RTSS-HE-local
controller) already existed in `zephyr/dts/alif/ensemble_e8_peripherals.dtsi`, but its paired
event router, `evtrtr2`, did not — `alif,dma-event-router.yaml`'s own doc-comment example already
named it, unused.

`dma0` + `evtrtr0` are now declared in the shared dtsi, `status = "disabled"` like every other
block, content unchanged from the five overlays (bench-exercised there, not re-derived); the five
overlays now just flip `&dma0`/`&evtrtr0` to `status = "okay"` instead of redeclaring the nodes.
`evtrtr2` is added paired 1:1 with the existing `dma2` (`dma-controller = <&dma2>`, `dma-groups =
2`, per HWRM Table 12-31's own text: "DMA requests to DMA2 controller are routed via 2-to-1
multiplexers... The selection of group 0-1 can be done independently for each DMA request"), at
its HWRM-sourced local address `0x400E2000` (Table 10-8 M55-HE Local Memory Map).

No separate `evtrtr1`/`dma1` node is added: per the HWRM, each M55 core's local PL330 + event
router sit at the SAME core-local register window (`0x400C0000` / `0x400E2000`) regardless of
which core reaches it — `dma2`'s own existing comment already documents that the RTSS-HP core
sees this identical address as "DMA1". A second, identically-addressed node would collide with
`dma2`/`evtrtr2`, not extend them; `evtrtr2`'s comment now states this explicitly, discharging the
"EVTRTR1 appears only in prose comments" gap without inventing a duplicate node.

Left undone: `dmas`/`dma-names` wiring onto the I2S, PDM, ADC, CPI and HexSPI nodes named in the
issue. Most of those peripheral nodes (`i2s0..3`, the main-domain `pdm`) do not exist in the
shared dtsi yet — they are declared per-example, matching this repo's established pattern that
`dmas` wiring is overlay-level (the CC3501E bridge's own `dmas` property lives in its overlay, not
on `spi0`/`spi1` in the shared dtsi) — so wiring them here would be scope creep past what a single
dtsi-file change can responsibly source. `evtrtr2`'s comment records the confirmed peripheral-
request numbers found while researching this (`DMA2_REQ[12]`/`[13]` LPSPI RX/TX, `DMA2_REQ[10]`
ADC24_DONE0 -- HWRM Table 12-31; `DMA2_REQ[4]` is `ADC120_DONE0_DMA_REQ`, the main-domain
12-bit ADC, not ADC24) for whichever board overlay picks this up next.

### Added — the E8 low-power peripheral bank has a devicetree presence (#1816)

`zephyr/dts/alif/ensemble_e8_peripherals.dtsi` declared `lpgpio`, `lpi3c0`, `lptimer0` (channel 0
only) and `rtc0` from the low-power domain and nothing else, even though the AE822 Datasheet
(Alif_E8_Datasheet_v1.2) Table 3-3's footnote names this bank as precisely the survivor set for
STANDBY and STOP: "If RTSS-HE is powered down, then the LPI3C, LPUTIMER, LPI2C1, LPCPI, LPI2S,
LPPDM, and LPSPI0/1 in the same subsystem are also powered down" — i.e. the peripherals that keep
running while the rest of the chip sleeps had no way to be named in a devicetree at all.

Added, all `status = "disabled"` matching every other block in the file: `lpuart` (reuses the
upstream `ns16550` driver already binding `uart0..7`, since the HWRM states "all information
related to UART in this section also applies to LPUART"), `lpi2c1` (master-only, reuses the
upstream `snps,designware-i2c` driver already binding `i2c0/i2c1/i2c2` — distinct from the
slave-only, SE-mastered LPI2C0 the file already excludes for a documented reason), `lpspi0` +
`lpspi1` (the same `alif,dwc-ssi-spi` driver as `spi0`; per the HWRM the pair shares device pins
and forms a single channel, master-only on LPSPI0 and slave-only on LPSPI1, and shares ONE IRQ
line), `lpi2s` (`snps,designware-i2s`, the same driver as the main-domain `i2s3` example node),
`lppdm` (the driver + Kconfig already existed — `zephyr/drivers/audio/alif_pdm.c` — only the node
was missing; its single OR'ed IRQ line is documented against the main-domain `pdm` node's three
discrete lines), `lpcam` for LPCPI (`alif,cam`, whose binding already carried an `lp-cam` property
anticipating exactly this instance), and `lptimer1`/`lptimer2`/`lptimer3` (the three sibling
channels `lptimer0`'s own comment already documented how to add). Every reg/IRQ value is
transcribed from the HWRM's Table 10-5 Low Power Peripherals Memory Map and the M55-HE local
interrupt-number table, cross-checked against the three already-verified entries in this file
(`lpi3c0`=50, `rtc0`=58, `lptimer0`=60) rather than read cold. Three new clock IDs
(`ALIF_LPUART_CLK`, `ALIF_LPCPI_CLK`, `ALIF_LPI2S_76M8_CLK`) were added to
`alif-ensemble-clocks-ext.h`; `ALIF_LPSPI_CLK` and `ALIF_LPPDM_76M8_CLK` already existed, unused
by any node until now.

`lpcmp0` (LPCMP, the STOP-mode wake source the datasheet gives 20 µA / 10 µs response) is a
genuinely different, simpler IP from the four HSCMP instances `alif,cmp` already binds — no
driver exists for it, so a new binding (`zephyr/dts/bindings/comparator/alif,lpcmp.yaml`) declares
the node without claiming it is usable from application code.

Left undone: the LPSPI0/LPSPI1 master/slave mode-select bit (`HE_CLK_ENA[SPI_MODE]`) has no DT
property yet, and neither does LPI2C1's own software clock gate (`HE_CLK_ENA[I2C_CKEN]` bit 13) —
a board enabling either must handle these registers itself, which is driver-level follow-up, not
blocked by these disabled nodes. `lpuart` has a real, currently-unresolved correctness gap, not
just an unwired nice-to-have: none of the three `ALIF_PARENT_CLK_*` options is the LPUART's real
PCLK source (`RTSS_HE_CLK`, boot-time selectable, not a `fixed-clock` node), so the first board to
enable it gets a garbled baud rate until `clock_control_alif.c` grows a real `RTSS_HE_CLK` case or
an enabling overlay pairs a `clock-frequency` override with its own UART_CKEN-gate handling (see
`ALIF_LPUART_CLK`'s own comment for why neither is done here). LPI2C0's precision-reference/VREF
and BOD/die-temperature companions are tracked separately (#1817).

### Added — BOD gains a devicetree node; TSENS documented as an ADC channel, not a new node (#1817)

Four E8 analog blocks the datasheet lists as features had no path in alp-sdk. Of the four:

- **ADC24** already had a node (`adc24_0` in `ensemble_e8_peripherals.dtsi`) — the gap is that no
  example enables it, which is example-authoring work outside a single dtsi-file change; left
  undone here.
- **On-die temperature sensor**: the HWRM (§19.5 TSENS Overview) states it has no register block
  of its own — "The TSENS is connected internally to input channel 6 of ADC120 and ADC122" — so
  there is no devicetree node to add. A comment on `adc12_0`/`adc12_2` now records this so a future
  reader does not go looking for a `tsens@...` node that was never going to exist. Surfacing it as
  a named temperature reading (vs. raw ADC counts) is backend/application work, left undone.
- **Internal precision reference (VREF_P/VREF_N)**: the issue itself scopes this to
  `metadata/socs/alif/ensemble/e8.json` and board metadata, not `ensemble_e8_peripherals.dtsi` —
  outside this change's file scope. Left undone.
- **BOD (Brown-Out Detect)**: added a disabled node, `bod0`, at the shared `BOR_BOD` register
  block (HWRM Table 10-4 + Table 19-32, base `0x4200_4000`) with `interrupts = <100 3>`
  (`M55HE_IRQS[100]` `BOD_IRQ`, HWRM Table 8-5). No Zephyr brown-out class API exists upstream and
  alp-sdk carries no vendored one, so a new minimal binding
  (`zephyr/dts/bindings/misc/alif,bod.yaml`) declares the node without a driver — matching this
  batch's `alif,lpcmp.yaml` precedent (#1816). BOD is distinct from BOR (outright reset, not
  modelled by this node) and from the external supervisor errata ER004 requires (out of scope,
  filed elsewhere). The Datasheet's own §3.7.4/Table 3-5 (not the HWRM, which has no §3.7.4 —
  the same content is at HWRM §8.1.5) also documents `BOD_DMA_REQ`; the actual request number,
  `DMA2_REQ[7]`, is HWRM Table 8-6. DMA wiring is #1815's territory, not modelled here.

### Reverted — a #1818 follow-up briefly programmed the reduced DMA burst length into DMATDLR instead of the unreduced FIFO default; that write is now back to the unreduced default (#1818)

A pass over `spi_dw_dma_setup_tx_channel()` (`zephyr/drivers/spi/spi_dw_alif.c`)
found that DMATDLR (the DW_SSI TX DMA watermark register) got the raw,
unreduced half-FIFO default while the PL330 `dma_cfg` burst length —
computed separately — could be smaller, for a dummy-TX chunk or for
`ALP_CC3501E_OTA_MAX_CHUNK` (4092, not a multiple of the default burst of 8).
A first pass made the two match by writing the reduced burst length into
DMATDLR as well. That is reverted here: DMATDLR is a **low watermark**, not a
burst count — it asserts `dma_tx_req` once the TX FIFO holds `<= DMATDLR`
entries, and the only hardware constraint is `DMATDLR + burst <= fifo_depth`.
With `fifo_depth = 16` (`zephyr/dts/alif/ensemble_e8_peripherals.dtsi:624`)
the existing `DMATDLR = 8` with `burst <= 8` already satisfied that, so the
mismatch this closed was never a correctness bug by that measure. Moving
DMATDLR to 4 (the OTA tail) or 1 (a dummy-TX chunk) instead makes the PL330
refill in much smaller increments against a DW_apb_ssi master that gates
SCLK on TX underrun — an unproven, potentially-regressive behavioural change
with no bench evidence either way, so it is not made.

`write_dmatdlr(dev, dw_spi_txftlr_dflt)` (`zephyr/drivers/spi/spi_dw_alif.c`)
is back to the unreduced default. The extracted, host-tested burst-length
helper (`zephyr/drivers/spi/spi_dw_alif_dma_burst.h`,
`tests/unit/spi_dw_alif_dma_burst`) is kept: it still supplies the PL330
`dma_cfg` burst length for both directions, which does need to match the
actual burst, unlike DMATDLR.

Still open, and not resolvable from source reading alone: `spi_dw_dma_enable_channels()`
leaves `SSIENR = 1`, so every `write_dmatdlr()` / `write_dmardlr()` call runs
with the controller already enabled, and whether the DW_apb_ssi honours a
watermark-register write in that state is unverified. See the
`CONFIG_SPI_DW_ALIF_DMA_MIN_LEN` comment in
`examples/aen/aen-cc3501e-bringup/prj.conf` for the full note and the
one bench read-back (`read_dmatdlr()`/`read_dmardlr()`) that would settle it.

### Fixed — CC3501E OTA writes: limit each frame to 64 data bytes while the bridge is in update mode (#1818)

Host workaround for a firmware limitation in the update-mode polled SPI slave.
That slave mis-receives any request payload phase longer than 70 bytes: 70 B or
fewer is received intact, 71 B or more is lost (the host sees `-5` with an
all-zero reply header), and 1024 B or more misframes. Splitting one payload
phase across several SS0-framed transfers does not help. Every `OTA_WRITE`
chunk of more than 64 data bytes therefore failed, while the tiny `OTA_BEGIN` /
`OTA_STATUS` payloads worked. Normal (callback SPI) mode is unaffected.

- While the peer is polled, `cc3501e_ota_write()` splits a larger buffer into
  consecutive `OTA_WRITE` frames of at most `CC3501E_POLLED_OTA_CHUNK` (64) data
  bytes, advancing the offset per frame (4 offset + 64 data + 2 CRC = 70 B, the
  largest frame on the proven side of the boundary). Callers that pass 508 or
  1024 B chunks keep working unchanged. Outside update mode a write is still one
  frame.
- `cc3501e_ota_update()` clamps its own chunk to one polled-safe frame, so a
  BUSY/IO hold-off retry re-sends exactly the chunk that was refused.
- The `cc3501e_host_ota` fake slave now records frame count and size; new cases
  pin a 1024 B write as 16 frames with the image landing in order, a 130 B write
  as 64 + 64 + 2, and normal mode as a single frame.

Bench, E1M-AEN803 serial 2026W36-0009, clean bridge firmware, with FINISH
removed so nothing was ever staged. The first 64-byte `OTA_WRITE` now lands
(device cursor 64), where every earlier run failed with `-5` at cursor 0. With
the window holding the manifest's worth of bytes, the bridge calls
`psa_fwu_start`. That call correctly rejects the example's *inert* demo blob,
which carries no valid signed manifest: the device latches OTA ERROR, fault
stage 1 (`psa_fwu_start`), and replies `RESP_ERR_BUSY`. The link stays healthy
before and after. A complete OTA on silicon needs a signed TI image and a real
FINISH, which this change does not exercise.

### Changed — the AEN ADC driver now says out loud that `ADC_CLK` is out of spec, instead of reading silently (#1823)

Every ADC conversion on E8 runs the SAR roughly twice as fast as the part is
characterised for, and nothing said so. HWRM Table 19-2 sources `ADC_CLK` from
`PERIPH_CLK`, and 19.1.5.3.4 `ADC_CLK_DIVISOR` accepts only `0x2`..`0x10`
(divide by 2..16). `PERIPH_CLK` is bench-measured at ~156.5 MHz on `AE822` —
twice independently, from ADC conversion timing over 2000 reads and from the
SE's own boot line `[SES] SE frequency is 78.31 MHz`, exactly half. So even the
maximum divisor 16 gives ~9.8 MHz against the `ADTS0013` v1.2 maximum of
**5000 kHz**. The DT nodes already carry `clock_div = <16>`, the lowest
`ADC_CLK` reachable
(`zephyr/dts/alif/ensemble_e8_peripherals.dtsi:1402` ("lowest ADC_CLK reachable")).

`adc_alif.c` now emits one `LOG_WRN` per instance at init naming the datasheet
limit and stating that its ENOB and linearity figures do not apply to these
readings
(`zephyr/drivers/adc/adc_alif.c:1219` ("ADC_CLK is out of spec")).

It warns rather than clamping or refusing, deliberately: there is no in-spec
setting to clamp **to**, and refusing would break every working ADC caller for a
limitation the hardware cannot avoid. Conversions complete and the readings are
usable — this is an accuracy caveat, not a failure. What changes is that a
caller can now see it, instead of trusting a number whose stated accuracy does
not hold.

This does not close #1823. Resolving it needs Alif: either a `PERIPH_CLK`
prescaler that is not in `AHRM0012NDA` v0.3, or a divisor above 16 with a
constraint the manual omits. Until then the warning is the honest state.

### Fixed — DMA data buffers were never cache-maintained on the AEN E8, and the `<alp/peripheral.h>` SPI contract never said whose job it was (#1830)

The PL330 is programmed non-cacheable and non-snooping —
`dma_pl330_config_channel()` writes `CC_CCTRL_MODIFIABLE_VALUE = 0x2` into both
cache-control fields of `DMA_CCRn`, i.e. `AxCACHE = 0b0010`, Normal
non-cacheable non-bufferable (HWRM 12.2.4.3.15,
`zephyr/drivers/dma/dma_pl330_alif.c:219`). It therefore neither snoops nor
allocates, and software maintenance is mandatory for any buffer in cacheable
memory. Two of its consumers did none on caller data: `spi_dw_alif.c` held no
cache call at all, and `video_alif.c` had a single clean+invalidate at
