*enqueue* — before the CPI writes the frame — and nothing after completion.
Neither direction produces an error; the wire carries pre-eviction bytes on TX
and the CPU reads pre-DMA bytes on RX.

Both are now maintained. `spi_dw_alif.c` cleans TX before `dma_start()`
(`:503`), clean+invalidates the RX destination before the transfer (`:431`),
and invalidates RX again once the transfer completes
(`zephyr/drivers/spi/spi_dw_alif.c:729`) — the second invalidate drops lines
speculative prefetch pulled in during the transfer window, which the
pre-transfer call cannot cover. `video_alif.c` invalidates the frame buffer on
the dequeue path (`zephyr/drivers/video/video_alif.c:842`). The policy this
settles is "buffers may be cacheable, the driver maintains them", not "callers
must allocate non-cacheable" — so no `BUILD_ASSERT` region check was added.

That policy is now written down where a caller can find it, on
`alp_spi_transceive` (`include/alp/peripheral.h:738` ("DMA and the data cache")), together with the one part that is **not** the driver's to fix:
maintenance operates on whole cache lines, so a partially-covered line is
invalidated in full. An `rx` buffer sharing a cache line with other live data
can lose a CPU write to that neighbour made during the transfer window. Give a
DMA-sized `rx` buffer its own cache line(s); `tx` is only ever cleaned, never
invalidated, so it is unaffected.

### Fixed — AEN E8 OSPI/HexSPI `core_clk` fell back to `bus-speed`, silently disabling OSPI_SCLK instead of driving it at the real 400 MHz core clock (#1831)

`zephyr/drivers/flash/flash_ospi_alif.c`'s `OSPI_ALIF_INIT` macro fed `core_clk` from `DT_INST_PROP_OR(inst, clock_frequency, DT_INST_PROP(inst, bus_speed))` — the node never set `clock-frequency`, so `core_clk` fell back to `bus-speed` (100 MHz). `alif_hal_ospi_initialize()` writes the whole `OSPI_BAUDR` register from `core_clk / bus_speed`, so `core_clk == bus_speed` wrote `OSPI_BAUDR = 1`. HWRM `AHRM0012NDA v0.3` §16.1.5.3.5 defines `OSPI_BAUDR[SCKDV]` as bits 15:1 (bit 0 is RESERVED and forced to 0 on every write): "If this field is set to all 0s, the serial output clock (OSPI_SCLK) is disabled." A written value of 1 leaves `SCKDV` all zero — **the old fallback disabled `OSPI_SCLK` entirely. It was a dead bus, not an overclock.** (An earlier revision of this PR, its changelog fragment, and both touched header comments claimed the old fallback would overclock an external device past its rating; that claim was wrong and is corrected here. HWRM §16.1.4.2 also makes `SCLK ≤ OSPI_CLK/2` a hardware property of Master mode, so an overclock past the core clock was structurally impossible regardless.) Latent on this batch only because no such part is populated on the E1M-AEN801 (bench module is board rev r1, `2617-0001`; E1M-AEN801 populates neither external OSPI memory on any revision -- E1M-AEN803 is the SKU that fits OSPI0, measured in #2041 as an ISSI `IS25WX256-JHLE`, not the Macronix part this fragment originally named -- corrected per #2062).

The file's own header comment justified the placeholder as "must come from the Alif Ensemble E8 TRM, not be invented" — stale: HWRM Table 16-2 sources HEXSPI0's internal core clock (OSPI0_CLK) from "SYST_ACLK or 266M_CLK", selected by `MISC_CLK_CTRL[SEL_OSPI_CLK]` (`zephyr/drivers/flash/flash_ospi_alif.c:97-102` ("the true OSPI core-clock source is NOT an unavailable HW")); HWRM §8.3.2.3.7 gives that bit's silicon reset value 0x0 as "400 MHz (SYST_ACLK)" (`AHRM0012NDA v0.3`). `zephyr/dts/alif/ensemble_e8_peripherals.dtsi` now declares `clock-frequency = <400000000>` (`zephyr/dts/alif/ensemble_e8_peripherals.dtsi:751` ("That was UNSAFE on Flow D")), and the driver macro now reads it with a plain `DT_INST_PROP(inst, clock_frequency)` (`zephyr/drivers/flash/flash_ospi_alif.c:1283` ("the exact dead-bus failure this file fixed for a MISSING")) — no fallback: a board/SoM that omits `clock-frequency` on its `ospi0` node now fails to build instead of silently programming a disabled clock. Worked through: `400000000 / 100000000 = 4`, `SCKDV = 2`, `BAUDR = SCKDV × 2 = 4`, `SCLK = 400/4 = ` **100 MHz** — exactly the node's `bus-speed`, and half the §10.5 200 MHz HEXSPI controller cap. The example that independently exercises this same call, `examples/aen/aen-ospi-regcheck/src/main.c`, carried the identical `DT_PROP_OR` fallback one file over from the driver fix; it is corrected the same way (`examples/aen/aen-ospi-regcheck/src/main.c:390` ("instead of quietly re-growing the same fallback")).

`zephyr/drivers/flash/flash_ospi_alif.c:481` adds `OSPI_ALIF_CHECK_SCLK()`, three `BUILD_ASSERT`s beside the macro so a *present but wrong* `clock-frequency`/`bus-speed` ratio fails the build the same way a *missing* `clock-frequency` now does: the effective divider (`clock-frequency / bus-speed`, HAL-truncated, bit 0 forced to 0 by `OSPI_BAUDR[SCKDV]`) must be ≥ 2 (else `SCKDV` is all zero and `OSPI_SCLK` is disabled, per §16.1.5.3.5 above), the raw ratio must be even (else the bit-0 truncation rounds the divider **down**, so `SCLK` silently **overshoots** the requested `bus-speed` -- e.g. a ratio of 3 becomes a divider of 2), and the resulting `SCLK` must stay ≤ 200 MHz (HWRM §10.5).

**Not addressed here.** The driver still does not program `MISC_CLK_CTRL[SEL_OSPI_CLK]` itself, so 400 MHz is correct only for as long as whatever boot stage runs before it (ROM/SE) leaves that mux at its documented reset value; HWRM §8.3.2.3.7 also documents a 0x1 selection (266 MHz from `266M_CLK`/PLL). Making `core_clk` unconditionally correct means the driver owning that selection itself — a distinct change to a system-level clock-mux register (`MISC_CLK_CTRL` is not OSPI-instance scoped) that needs bench confirmation of its placement relative to the existing `CLKCTL_PER_SLV->OSPI_CTRL` clock-enable sequence in the same file, which this change does not attempt. **Not verified on silicon and cannot be on the current bench**: board rev r1 (`2617-0001`) has no OSPI memory assembled to clock.

### Added — `alp companion spi1` + `cc3501e_spi1_configure/_transfer/_release`: host passthrough onto the E1M connector's SPI1 (#1841)

The E1M connector's SPI1 pins (AG10 SCK / AG9 MOSI / AG8 MISO / AH9 CS0 / AH8
CS1) land on the CC3501E, not the Alif -- a carrier device on that bus was
previously unreachable from the host. A new proto v6 opcode family
(`0x55..0x57`, worker-routed) relays the host's bytes onto the coprocessor's
own SPI1 controller: `CONFIGURE` acquires the bus and pins clock/mode/CS,
`TRANSFER` clocks one full-duplex chunk (up to `ALP_CC3501E_SPI1_MAX_XFER` =
4088 B, with `NO_TX`/`NO_RX`/`CS_HOLD` flags to drop a direction or chain
chunks into one device transaction), and `RELEASE` is the escape hatch back
to a known-free bus.

New host API: `cc3501e_spi1_configure()` / `cc3501e_spi1_transfer()` /
`cc3501e_spi1_release()` in
[`<alp/chips/cc3501e/core.h>`](include/alp/chips/cc3501e/core.h). New
console group: `alp companion spi1 configure|xfer|read|release` (see
[`cc3501e-companion-commands.md`](docs/cc3501e-companion-commands.md#alp-companion-spi1)).

TRANSFER carries a `seq` byte for wire-level duplicate suppression: the
firmware caches the last completed `(seq, result)` and replays it for a
matching seq instead of re-clocking the bus, which is what makes the host's
ordinary transport-level retry safe on a bus that can drive flash. The host
driver additionally requires a CONFIGURE to have succeeded in the *current*
session before it will send a TRANSFER -- the firmware's `g_configured`
latch and cached result are file statics that outlive an Alif reboot, so a
freshly initialised host context is forced through a real round trip (whose
own poll discards any stale cache left by a session the firmware outlived)
rather than risk a fresh ctx's first TRANSFER colliding with one and handing
back a previous session's RX bytes as `ALP_OK` with the bus never re-clocked.

Not yet silicon-validated; see `cc3501e-bridge-firmware:`'s test suite and
`docs/cc3501e-bridge.md`'s "SPI1 host passthrough" section for the wire
contract and the v0.x roadmap entry.

### Fixed — tas2563 driver no longer accepts init at the write-only broadcast address (#1846)

`tas2563_init()`'s `addr_is_valid()` accepted `TAS2563_I2C_ADDR_BROADCAST`
(`0x48`) as a valid instance address, which init's own probe, and every
later `tas2563_read_revision()`/`tas2563_set_mode()` call, then both read
AND wrote through `ctx->addr` (`select_page()` writes the page register
before every read). `0x48` does not pin down one physical chip the way a
strap address does; on a bus where an unrelated device is strapped there
(e.g. an INA236 current monitor), those reads/writes land on that device's
registers instead of the amp -- a real EVK pre-respin had exactly this
collision (see `metadata/boards/e1m-evk.yaml`'s U28/U32 notes, #1163/#1659).

`tas2563_init()` now rejects `TAS2563_I2C_ADDR_BROADCAST` with
`ALP_ERR_INVAL`; only the four documented per-chip AD0/SPICLK straps
(`TAS2563_I2C_ADDR_GND_DIRECT` .. `TAS2563_I2C_ADDR_VDD_DIRECT`) are
accepted. The check runs once, in `tas2563_init()`, before `ctx->addr` is
ever assigned; every other function gates on `ctx->initialised` rather
than re-validating the address, so this one admission check covers the
context's whole lifetime -- confirmed no other path (dispatch
registration, board/SoM preset, example) constructs a live context at
`0x48`. The broadcast address stays defined for reference (it is a real,
datasheet-documented write-only global-call address a future
group-write-only helper could use) but is no longer usable through this
per-instance driver context.

### Fixed — E1M-AEN801's BRD_I2C is SoC I2C0, not the slave-only LPI2C0; unblocks the on-module `rv3028c7` RTC (#1848, unblocks #1814)

`BRD_I2C` (the on-module housekeeping bus carrying the RV-3028-C7 RTC, the
OPTIGA Trust M secure element, and the TMP112 temperature sensor) was
documented, and wired nowhere, on the assumption that it sat on the Alif
LPI2C0 (`P7_4`/`P7_5`) -- a bus the SoC can only be a *slave* on (TRM
§3.17.4, hardcoded slave address `0x40`), so those three parts were treated
as Tier-3 SE-mediated and unreachable as an ordinary I2C master.

That routing was wrong. `BRD_I2C_SCL`/`BRD_I2C_SDA` land on SoC pins
`P7_1`/`P7_0` (the `E1M-AEN-2626-R2` netlist, balls B3/B8); Alif's
`ADTS0013` v1.2 Table 3-16 gives those pads the alternate function
`I2C0_SCL_C`/`I2C0_SDA_C` -- **SoC I2C0**, one of the four shared-peripheral
I2C modules the HWRM (§15.4.1) documents as master-or-slave capable, not
LPI2C0. The M55 masters BRD_I2C directly, the same as any Tier-1 upstream
`i2c_dw` bus.

**What changed:**

- `zephyr/dts/alif/ensemble_e8_peripherals.dtsi` -- corrects the LPI2C0/i2c0
  comment blocks; no behavior change to the SoC-level node population.
- `examples/aen/aen-secure-element-sign`'s board overlay -- adds the
  `pinctrl_i2c0` group (`I2C0_SCL_C`=P7_1, `I2C0_SDA_C`=P7_0), enables
  `&i2c0`, and aliases it to **portable bus 2** (`alp-i2c2`, not 0) --
  0 and 1 are already the E1M edge I2C buses (`BOARD_I2C_SENSORS` /
  `EVK_I2C_BUS_DSI_CSI`), and this SoM's own board files already default
  `alp-i2c0` to the EVK sensor bus in other projects (e.g.
  `aen-eeprom-manifest`), so BRD_I2C could not reuse bus 0 without
  silently repointing the stock `i2c-scanner`/`i2c-master` examples at a
  bus carrying a secure element. Only the HE overlay wires it -- HP never
  touches `&i2c0`, so the two cores never race the same controller. The
  generated E1M-AEN801 SoM board files are UNCHANGED: this SoM's on-module
  buses are wired per-example, matching the existing I2C2/EEPROM
  convention, not baked into the shared board file.
- No `bias-pull-down` (deliberately High-Z instead): the R2 components CSV
  shows this net's pull-up jumpers (R93/R94) DNP, unlike I2C2/EEPROM's
  (R95/R96, stuffed) -- a pull-down here would park the bus low through the
  pad's own ~50 kOhm Rpd. Whether that even matters is an open question the
  datasheet and the HWRM disagree on (open-drain needing a pull-up vs.
  push-pull by design); see the overlay's pinctrl comment and the ADR
  amendment. Do not add a bias without a bench answer.
- `metadata/e1m_modules/E1M-AEN801.yaml` -- `on_module.i2c_devices.brd_i2c`
  now carries `bus_master: alif-ensemble` and a corrected, cited comment.
  The five sibling AEN presets (301/401/501/601/701) share this SoM PCB but
  keep `bus_master` OMITTED, pending a per-part datasheet check that their
  Alif silicon variant backs `I2C0_SCL_C`/`I2C0_SDA_C` the same way --
  their stale "SE masters it" comments are corrected without asserting the
  routing for them.
- `docs/adr/0017-alp-sdk-over-the-vendor-sdk.md` -- the original Tier-3
  rationale for this trio is left legible (not silently rewritten); a new
  "Amendment (2026-08-30)" section supersedes it for the E1M-AEN801
  specifically, records the open pull-up question and OPTIGA's DNI status,
  and does not reopen Tier-3 in general or reverse the (still-correct)
  LPI2C0-is-genuinely-slave-only finding.
- `docs/bring-up-aen.md`, `docs/soms/aen.md`, `docs/aen-bench-bringup.md`,
  `docs/cc3501e-bridge.md`, `docs/glossary.md`, `docs/troubleshooting.md`,
  `docs/tutorials/02-i2c-scan.md`, `docs/tutorials/13-eeprom-provisioning.md`,
  `examples/aen/aen-secure-element-sign/{board.yaml,README.md,src/main.c,testcase.yaml}`,
  `examples/aen/aen-eeprom-manifest/{README.md,src/main.c}`,
  `examples/aen/aen-i2c2-eeprom-regcheck/src/main.c`,
  `examples/aen/README.md`,
  `examples/peripheral-io/i2c-master/{board.yaml,README.md,src/main.c}`,
  `include/alp/chips/optiga_trust_m.h`,
  `changelog.d/1269.md`, `changelog.d/1761.md` -- reconcile every prose site
  that repeated the LPI2C0/`P7_4`/`P7_5` claim for E1M-AEN801's BRD_I2C.

**Not done here, and said plainly:** this is bus plumbing, not RTC-source
selection. The AEN calendar backend (`src/backends/rtc/lprtc_calendar_shim.c`,
selected by `silicon_ref` on `alif:ensemble:e8`) still wins dispatch over the
now-reachable `rv3028c7` -- wiring the RTC dispatcher to prefer the external
part when BRD_I2C is present, with the internal LPRTC as documented fallback,
is a separate, larger change and is not part of this fix.

**Verification status: R2-sourced, NOT bench-verified.** Every routing fact
above comes from the `E1M-AEN-2626-R2` netlist + `ADTS0013` v1.2. No R1
netlist is available, and the only AEN801 bench unit on hand identifies as
r1 (`alp board` -> `E1M-AEN801 r1`, serial `2617-0001`). Probe `P7_0`/`P7_1`
on that unit before treating BRD_I2C as confirmed there -- both the pad
routing and the pull-up question above it are open until that probe runs.
`OPTIGA` also lives on this bus at `0x30` -- do not blind-scan it; probe
known addresses only.

**Bench-settled 2026-08-31** on the r1 module (`E1M-AEN801`, serial `2617-0001`),
`i2c0` at 100 kHz, read-only `i2c_write_read` of register `0x00`:

| pad bias | result on `0x48` (TMP112), `0x52` (RV-3028-C7), `0x30` (OPTIGA) |
|---|---|
| High-Z, no bias | `rc=-116` (`-ETIMEDOUT`) with `E: User Abort on i2c@49010000` |
| same build + internal pull-up (~50 kΩ) | `rc=-5` (`-EIO`), no abort |

A bias-only edit changing the error class proves the pinctrl is correct and the
controller reaches the wire, and that the net has **no usable pull-up**. It also
settles the open-drain question against the HWRM's push-pull note: had these pads
driven push-pull, the High-Z run would have worked. The I2C IP tri-states for the
high phase, so an **external pull-up is required**. Nothing ACKed under the internal
pull-up either, which is expected — ~50 kΩ is far too weak for 100 kHz rise time.

**So this bus is not usable as built.** It needs `R93`/`R94` stuffed — bridging
BRD_I2C into the segment the carrier already pulls up via `R137`/`R144` — or
dedicated pull-ups on the net. That is a board change, not a firmware one, which is
why #1814 stays open.

### Added — the E1M-AEN801's on-module housekeeping I2C bus (BRD_I2C) is documented, and the "not usable as built" verdict on it is withdrawn (#1848, #1814)

[`docs/soms/aen.md`](docs/soms/aen.md) gains **"On-module housekeeping I2C
(BRD_I2C)"** — the customer-facing reference for the two parts every AEN801
carries and nothing on the carrier is needed to use: the Micro Crystal
**RV-3028-C7** RTC at `0x52` and the TI **TMP112** thermometer at `0x48`
(design address, ADD0 strapped to GND), both fitted. The OPTIGA Trust M at
`0x30` is DNP on this batch and must not appear in a shipped devicetree. The
bus is **SoC I2C0 function C** on `P7_0`/`P7_1`, isolated from the
I2C2/EEPROM segment (`R93`/`R94` DNP), so the manifest EEPROM is not on it.
Both parts are driven by upstream Zephyr — `CONFIG_RTC_RV3028` and
`CONFIG_TMP112`, both `default y` off their devicetree nodes — with
`examples/aen/aen-rtc-alarm` and `examples/aen/aen-temp-sensor` as the worked
examples, and the bus, the child nodes and the `alp-i2c2` / `rtc` /
`ambient-temp0` aliases generated into the board devicetree from
`metadata/e1m_modules/aen/on-module-links.yaml`, and the RTC alarm path documented end to end (`/INT` →
`P15_0` → LPGPIO bit 0 → IRQ 171, open-drain active low, `R98` 100 kΩ to
`+1V8` fitted).

Four limitations are stated up front rather than left to be discovered on a
bench, because each of them surprises people:

* **The RTC does not keep time across a power cycle.** `VDD_BAT`/`VBACKUP`
  has no supply fitted on this batch (`R4`/`R68` both DNP) — no backup cell,
  no trickle source. Hence `backup-switch-mode = "disabled"` (the binding
  requires the property) and no `trickle-resistor-ohms`. Persistence is a
  populate change, not a firmware setting.
* **`RTC_CLKOUT` reaches only the E1M edge connector (pin `AH16`)**, not the
  SoC, so it is a carrier-designer's clock and firmware cannot consume it.
* **`MODULE_STBY`/`EVI` (edge pin `O2`) is a carrier-driven event input.**
* **One bench module answered at `0x40` instead of `0x48`.** At the time,
  `0x40` looked like it could not be a legal TMP112 address at all, and that
  part fingerprinted as a genuine TMP112 on three of three registers
  (`CONFIG` `0x60a0`, `T_LOW` `0x4b00`, `T_HIGH` `0x5000` — the datasheet
  power-on defaults), so the working theory was that its ADD0 was not
  actually at GND: check **U20 pin 3 continuity to GND** on that unit.
  **Later correction (alp-sdk#1978):** per TI SBOS473L p.44, the BOM's exact
  orderable MPN for U20, `TMP112DIDPWR`, is X2SON (DPW), 5 pins ONLY — no
  SOT563-6 orderable carries that MPN — and per SBOS473L Table 7-4 the
  X2SON-5 "Address Variant Only" row straps ADD0→GND to `0x40`, so `0x40` is
  the DESIGN address for the part this board specifies, not an anomaly the
  open-joint theory needs to explain; the fingerprint matches that design.
  What is *not* established is *as-built*: nobody has confirmed the fitted
  package marking on a physical module, and BOM is not as-built. The anomaly
  is since confirmed on 2 of 2 modules tested, so it reads as a **batch**
  property, not the per-module defect first suspected. The devicetree still
  keeps `0x48`, unchanged here — it now contradicts the `0x40` design
  address above, a separate decision left visible rather than silently
  resolved; the examples, not the DT, tolerate and report the anomaly.

### Fixed — a bench verdict measured on r1 hardware was recorded as a property of the bus, and said it was unusable (#1848)

`zephyr/dts/alif/ensemble_e8_peripherals.dtsi`'s BRD_I2C/`i2c0` comments
carried a "BENCH-SETTLED 2026-08-31 … this bus is NOT usable as built …
needs `R93`/`R94` stuffed" block, and `docs/bring-up-aen.md` §5.1,
`docs/glossary.md`, `src/backends/rtc/lprtc_calendar_shim.c` and
`examples/aen/aen-brd-i2c-scan` all repeated it. That run was taken on an
**r1** module, where the RTC and TMP112 sit on LPI2C0 (`P7_4`/`P7_5`) and
**nothing is attached to `P7_0`/`P7_1`** — so nothing could have ACKed there
whatever the pad biasing, and the run characterised two floating pins rather
than a populated bus. Its open-drain-vs-push-pull inference came from the
same floating net.

Bench-settled again on 2026-09-05 on **2626-R2** silicon (Flow A, cold-cycle
proven), the revision that actually routes BRD_I2C to I2C0: the bus works on
the SoC's **internal pull-up alone**. The RV-3028-C7 ACKs at `0x52` (ID
register `0x28` = `0x44`, seconds `0x01` → `0x02`, so the oscillator runs),
the TMP112 fingerprints correctly and reads 28.062 °C, and every
non-response is a clean `rc=-5` (`-EIO`) NACK — **zero `-ETIMEDOUT`, zero
`User Abort on i2c@49010000`** across the whole run. `R93`/`R94` stay DNP and
are not needed.

The r1 measurement is kept as history everywhere it appeared, marked with
why its conclusion does not carry, rather than deleted. The RTC shim's own
comment is corrected too: nothing electrical blocks `rv3028c7` from backing
the AEN calendar any more, only a deliberate backend-selection change
(#1814) — and that is not a free upgrade, since with no `VBACKUP` supply the
external RTC loses the time on a cold boot exactly as the LPRTC does.

**Later correction:** the `0x28` = `0x44` reading above reads like a full
identity confirmation; it is only a partial one. Per the RV-3028-C7
Application Manual Rev. 1.4 §3.14, register `0x28` splits into an HID
nibble (hardware identity) and a VID nibble (production-line version) —
only HID `0x4` is documented as an identity check, VID `0x4` is a separate,
production-line-scoped field.

### Changed — `soc-spec-v1`: an `ethos-u*` NPU entry must declare `mac_per_cycle` (#1849)

`$defs/npu` required only `type` plus `anyOf(gops, tops)`, so

```json
{ "type": "ethos-u55", "gops": 100 }
```

validated cleanly while carrying nothing to build the vela
`--accelerator-config` string (`<type>-<mac_per_cycle>`, e.g. `ethos-u55-256`)
from. Schema validation on a consumer's read path cannot catch this, because
the document already passes the schema — the gap was in the schema itself.

The issue framed this as a downstream tan-cli concern that degrades to a
silent skip. **In this repo it is worse than that, and in three different
ways**, which is the argument for fixing it here rather than adding a fourth
guard:

- `scripts/alp_project_loader.py:751` ("raise KeyError(") raises `KeyError`, deliberately —
  `scripts/alp_project_loader.py:743-745`
  ("it must never be silently masked into a") chose a crash over emitting
  the truncated `ethos-u55-`.
- `scripts/alp_orchestrate/kconfig.py:1374`
  (`n.get("mac_per_cycle")`) filters the incomplete entry out, which makes it
  indistinguishable from an absent `npus[]` block, and
  `scripts/alp_orchestrate/kconfig.py:1405`
  (`mac = macs[0] if macs else 256`) then defaults to **256**. On a part whose
  U55 is really 128-MAC that emits `CONFIG_ETHOS_U55_256=y` — a legal
  `ETHOS_U_NPU_CONFIG` member, so neither the `_valid_accel` guard nor
  anything downstream refuses it, and a 256-MAC command stream errors a
  128-MAC NPU at invoke (the #909 mis-size the surrounding code goes to some
  length to avoid).
- tan-cli skips the NPU entirely (its own `isinstance` guard, tan-cli#965).

Crash, silent mis-size, silent skip. None of the three is wrong on its own;
what was wrong is that the document was accepted at all. `$defs/npu` now
carries an `if`/`then` (`metadata/schemas/soc-spec-v1.schema.json:351-357`)
that refuses an `ethos-u*` entry without `mac_per_cycle` at authoring time,
where there is exactly one answer. The consumer-side guards stay: schema
validation and a downstream guard are complementary, not substitutes.

The requirement is **conditional** on purpose. `drp-ai` and `deepx-dx-m1` are
not compiled through vela and legitimately carry no `mac_per_cycle`; an
unconditional `required` would refuse two committed documents. The `if` also
carries its own `required: ["type"]`, without which it would match *vacuously*
on an entry that has no `type` at all and refuse it for the wrong field.

**Zero metadata churn**, verified rather than asserted: all 16 `ethos-u*`
entries across the nine `metadata/socs/**/*.json` documents (Alif Ensemble
e3–e8, i.MX 93) already declare `mac_per_cycle`, and the only two entries in
the tree that omit it are the two non-Ethos ones.

`tests/scripts/test_soc_spec_npu_mac_per_cycle.py` is mutation-proven in both
directions, because a conditional rule can ship broken two ways: deleting the
`if`/`then` fails the three refusal cases (u85/u55/u65, parametrised because
the rule keys on the `^ethos-u` prefix rather than an enumerated list), and
replacing it with an unconditional `required` fails a *different* three — the
two non-Ethos documents plus the zero-churn sweep.

Schema, tests and changelog only; no metadata, script or code change.

### Fixed — `hw-revisions-v1.schema.json` closes its root; it was the last schema that accepted an undeclared top-level key (#1850)

`metadata/schemas/hw-revisions-v1.schema.json` carried `"additionalProperties": true` at
its root -- the only one of the 29 schemas under `metadata/schemas/` that did, with no
rationale recorded anywhere for the exception. Swept against the tree, nothing needs the
door: all four governed files (`metadata/e1m_modules/{aen,imx93,v2n,v2n-m1}/hw-revisions.yaml`)
carry exactly the three declared top-level keys `display_name`, `family` and `hw_revisions`,
and all three are already `required`, so no optional key could be hiding behind it either.
Closed to `false`.

This is narrower than it may sound, and the narrowing is worth recording because the issue
that opened it overstated the hole. A typo *inside* a revision entry was never accepted:
`$defs.hw_rev_entry` is `additionalProperties: false` over `board_rev`, `changes`,
`max_sdk_version`, `min_sdk_version`, `pad_route_overrides`, `released`, `status` and
`summary`, and `hw_revisions` constrains its own keys with
`propertyNames: {"pattern": "^r[0-9]+$"}`. Only a stray key at the top level was admitted.

Nothing downstream depended on the open root. `scripts/validate_metadata.py:92`
("HWREV_SCHEMA = REPO") loads this schema and validates every
`metadata/e1m_modules/*/hw-revisions.yaml` against it --
`scripts/validate_metadata.py:3494-3506`
("# Per-family hw-revisions files (YAML) against hw-revisions v1.") -- and reports
`4 hw-revisions file(s) ... 0 failure(s)` after the change. No
generator in this repo writes these files; tan reads them and touches only `hw_revisions`
(`tan-cli` `python/tan/commands/new_som_cmd.py:401-426`, `_family_hw_revisions`), and
creating a family file is a manual porting step. The customer-facing path in
`docs/porting-new-som.md` §7 appends a revision row *inside* `hw_revisions:`, which was
already strict.

Schema only; no metadata, code or generated-file change.

### Documented — ADR 0034: the SDK declares support policy as data, and exactly one normative evaluator applies it (#1851)

The SDK refuses builds on grounds it presents as facts about silicon, and some of them are
not. `board.yaml` setting the other class's runtime -- `zephyr` on a Cortex-A, `yocto` on a
Cortex-M -- is refused at `scripts/alp_orchestrate/validate.py:296-307`, reached from
`scripts/alp_orchestrate/loader.py:910`, with an error telling the customer its runtime "is
determined by the core class". Upstream Zephyr at the pinned v4.4.1 ships
`arch/arm/core/cortex_a_r/`, so Zephyr does run on Cortex-A: alp-sdk **chose** to carry two
OSes and pair one to each core class, which is a product decision, not physics.
`scripts/alp_orchestrate/topology.py:92`'s "A Cortex-A can't run Zephyr" states it as
impossibility and is inaccurate as written.

`docs/adr/0034-support-policy-is-declared-data-with-one-normative-evaluator.md` records the
shape: support policy is declared as versioned, schema-backed data; exactly **one** normative
evaluator turns a declared policy into a verdict; consumers call it or carry a hash-pinned
audited port rather than re-deriving it from prose. The evaluator stays in alp-sdk `scripts/`
because 96 configure-time `CMakeLists.txt` invocations of
`${ALP_SDK_ROOT}/scripts/alp_project.py --emit zephyr-conf --core <id>` and the four
`west alp-*` commands reach `load_board_yaml` with no tan in the process -- so a plain
`west build` keeps every refusal it has today. Declared policy is constrained (exact values
only, derived closed codomain, `required` + `additionalProperties: false` + `schemaVersion`,
no catch-all entry, totality proved by a gate rather than by ordering, normative miss
semantics) so the evaluator stays a small total lookup and a second-language port is provable
rather than trusted. And a refusal that enforces a support decision must say so.

Three measurements motivate it. The rule is restated three times
(`scripts/alp_orchestrate/topology.py:28-43`, `scripts/alp_orchestrate/topology.py:80-87`, `tan-cli` `python/tan/core/os_class.py`) and the
copies have **already diverged**: on an unresolved core type alp-sdk `_allowed_os_for_core("")`
returns `["baremetal", "off"]` while tan returns `[]`, and `_default_os_from_core_type(5)`
raised `AttributeError` where tan normalises -- tan took the tan-cli#914 / tan-cli#957 fix and
alp-sdk did not (#1852, closed by #1888, merged 2026-09-01 as `f5c7ff5b`). That the divergence
existed undetected until someone looked is the argument; closing one instance does not close the
class. The field built to carry the decision is unused: all **26**
`topology.<core>` entries across the eleven `metadata/e1m_modules/*.yaml` presets omit `os`,
and `som-preset-v2.schema.json` `$defs.topology_entry` has `required: []`, so
`scripts/alp_orchestrate/loader.py:555`'s preference for the declared value is never reached
from a *preset* -- a customer's own `board.yaml cores.<id>.os` still reaches it through the
merge at `scripts/alp_orchestrate/loader.py:165-179`, as 53 in-tree `board.yaml` files do. And
`metadata/` already carries decisions alongside hardware truth (`emit-registry-v1.json`,
`quality-tasks-v1.json`, `toolchains.json`, `bootstrap.json`, `library-aliases-v1.json`,
`registries/`), which is why "policy metadata" has been naming two different things.

`docs/board-config-schema.md`'s "OS inference from core type" section is rewritten for
customers: the refusal is kept, but named as a support boundary with the exact error text, and
the previous claim that the runtime is "mapped to the silicon class, not chosen" is corrected.
The seam spec records the same correction plus the distinction the earlier draft blurred --
prong (b) can mean "the SDK evaluates at emit time and stamps the outcome" or "the decision is
authored once and read back", and only the second removes evaluation from the build path.

ADR 0034 narrows ADR 0026 clause 2's *justification*, not its decision: clause 2 keeps
`metadata/` in alp-sdk because "Those are hardware truth", which describes only half the
directory. Docs only; no schema, metadata or code change -- `docs/README.md`'s ADR count moves
31 -> 32.

### Fixed — an unresolved `cores[].type` no longer crashes or gets guessed at; alp-sdk now answers what tan answers (#1852)

alp-sdk and tan carry the same core-class-to-runtime rule in two repos, and they had diverged
on the one input neither schema constrains: a `cores[].type` that is absent, empty, or not a
string. tan took the fix (tan-cli#914 / tan-cli#957 / tan-cli#962); alp-sdk did not, in the one
direction `test_planner_relocation_freshness.py` cannot see -- tan's copy lives at
`python/tan/core/os_class.py`, outside `tan/planner/` and outside `HAND_PORT_SOURCES`, so the
hash pin never looked at it.

Measured on `dev` before this change:

```
alp-sdk  _allowed_os_for_core("")       -> ["baremetal", "off"]      tan -> []
alp-sdk  _default_os_from_core_type(5)  -> AttributeError            tan -> "off"
alp-sdk  _runtime_class(5)              -> AttributeError            tan -> "other"
```

Two failure modes, not one. `AttributeError: 'int' object has no attribute 'lower'` aborts
`--emit os-topology` with a bare traceback rather than a diagnostic; and `["baremetal", "off"]`
for a core whose class nobody established is a plausible-but-wrong answer that tan's own
docstring rejects by name.

The bare `(core_type or "").lower()` idiom was in **three** functions in
`scripts/alp_orchestrate/topology.py` -- `_default_os_from_core_type`, `_runtime_class` and
(via `_cross_class_os`) `_allowed_os_for_core` -- reached from one caller,
`core_os_topology`, whose `soc_types` comprehension took `c.get("type", "")` unvalidated
against `soc-spec-v1.schema.json`'s own `"type": {"type": "string"}`. That value also went
verbatim into the emitted `core_type` field, so a non-string was a wire leak into the
document as well as a crash. Those four sites are fixed: the caller normalises to the same `""`
unresolved sentinel a missing `type` already produces, and each helper keeps an `isinstance`
backstop so a future caller does not inherit the same crash-or-leak choice.

**A fifth site, found on review (#1888), and the reason the count moved.** The scope above came
from a prose list of three functions plus their caller, not from an antipattern grep — the
failure this repo has a named rule against. An actual grep of every `cores[].type` read finds
`scripts/alp_orchestrate/kconfig.py` carrying the same
`(c.get("type") or "").lower()` in `_emit_inference`, reading the same field on the same
schema-invalid-`--metadata-root` precondition, and still raising: driving it with
`soc_spec={"cores":[{"id":"c0","type":5}]}` gives `AttributeError: 'int' object has no
attribute 'lower'`. So `--emit os-topology` was fixed while `--emit kconfig` was left crashing.
Every other reader in the tree (`scripts/alp_orchestrate/loader.py:865`,
`scripts/alp_orchestrate/libraries.py:83`, `scripts/alp_orchestrate/libraries.py:95`,
`scripts/gen_portability_matrix.py:550` ("): str(c.get("), `scripts/validate_metadata.py:1520` ("), str) and str(c.get(")) coerces with
`str(...)` and cannot raise.

The neighbouring `vector_extension` read is guarded in the same change: it is the identical
idiom on the identical object one line above, is declared `"type": "string"` by the same
`$defs/core`, and that line is its only read in the tree — fixing one and not the other would
repeat the partial scope this review caught. An unresolved value now falls through to
`CONFIG_ALP_SDK_INFERENCE_TFLM_KERNEL_REF=y`, the scalar-safe kernel, rather than being guessed
into NEON.

Both review findings are pinned by mutation, not by reading. Reverting `_runtime_class`'s guard
alone previously left the suite byte-identically green — every assertion reached it through
`core_os_topology`, which had already normalised the value — so
`test_runtime_class_never_raises_on_an_unresolved_type` now asserts the helper's own contract
directly, and `test_emit_kconfig_never_raises_on_an_unresolved_type` does the same for the fifth
site. Reverting either guard turns four parametrised cases red.

`_cross_class_os` is deliberately left unguarded, matching tan. It feeds the REFUSAL at
`scripts/alp_orchestrate/validate.py::_enforce_os_matches_core_class`, where declining both
real runtimes for an unclassified core is the conservative answer. Only the *advertised*
`allowed_os` set was wrong.

The distinction the fix preserves is **unresolved** versus **unclassified**: a real type
string matching neither `cortex-a*` nor `cortex-m*` (a future RISC-V companion, say) still
resolves to `off` with `["baremetal", "off"]` on offer, in both repos. Collapsing those two is
what produced the wrong answer in the first place.

No emitted bytes change for any shipping SoM -- every `cores[].type` in all nine
`metadata/socs/**` files is `cortex-a*` or `cortex-m*`, and both `os-topology` emit snapshots
are byte-identical after the change.

### Fixed — the boot banner now warns when the compiled SoM `hw_rev` disagrees with the live EEPROM manifest (#1853)

Every build resolves a `hw_rev` (`board.yaml`'s `som.hw_rev`, falling back to
the SKU preset's `default_hw_rev`), and separately the SDK reads the SoM's
*actual* revision from the on-module EEPROM manifest at boot — but nothing
compared the two. On the AEN family, three E1M pads (`E1M_GPIO_IO8`,
`E1M_GPIO_IO10`, `E1M_GPIO_IO21`) physically sit on a *different chip*
depending on which revision is right, and `alp_hw_info_assert_matches_build()`
existed to catch exactly this — but had zero call sites in the tree, so a
build could disagree with its module silently. (It still has zero call
sites: this fix adds a boot-time check, not a caller of that function — see
`alp_hw_info_build_hw_rev_mismatch()` below.)

The boot banner (`CONFIG_ALP_SDK_BANNER`, on by default) now compares the
live manifest's `hw_rev` against the newly-emitted
`CONFIG_ALP_SDK_SOM_HW_REV` (`scripts/alp_orchestrate.py`, the same `hw_rev`
the build resolved — not a derived pad-routing table; nothing in a compiled
firmware image derives one from `pad_routes`/`pad_route_overrides` today,
that data is read only by the debug/BOM `--emit composed-route-table` /
`--emit carrier-netlist` surfaces) via the new, independently-testable
`alp_hw_info_build_hw_rev_mismatch()`, and prints a loud warning on a
disagreement. This is a warning, not a boot refusal, by default: a
factory-fresh module with no EEPROM manifest yet (`ALP_ERR_NOT_PROVISIONED`)
is an expected state and never trips it, and bricking a developer's board
over a revision string is a worse failure mode than a possibly-wrong pin. A
production build that would rather halt closed opts in via the new
`CONFIG_ALP_SDK_HW_REV_MISMATCH_FATAL`.

Not implemented here: refusing to *dispatch* only the specific pads whose
route actually differs between hw_revs (the issue's "stronger guard"). No
peripheral-class dispatcher consults any pad-route table today, so there is
nothing to retrofit — filed as **#1859** instead: generate a per-hw_rev
`cc3501e_gpio_routes[]` from the composed route table, plus one `hw_rev`
guard in the GPIO proxy (GPIO-only, much smaller than a dispatch-layer
change). #1859 is also why this fix, by itself, does not close the loop on
the bench module that reported #1853: `examples/aen/aen-cc3501e-gpio/src/
cc3501e_gpio_routes.c` (and the same table duplicated in
`aen-cc3501e-bringup` and `aen-cc3501e-companion-tour`) hardcodes the r2 map
— `{ALP_E1M_GPIO_IO8, 30u}` / `{ALP_E1M_GPIO_IO10, 35u}`, no IO21 entry — with
no `hw_rev` awareness at all. On the r1 bench module, this fix's banner
prints the warning correctly, but the hardcoded GPIO table is still wrong;
nothing here changes what pin actually gets driven.
`CONFIG_ALP_SDK_HW_REV_MISMATCH_FATAL` is today's coarser mitigation for
that gap: it halts before any pad is ever dispatched.

Bench-gated: verified against a crafted manifest under native_sim
(`tests/zephyr/hw_info`); not yet re-verified against the physical bench
module (`E1M-AEN801 r1`, serial `2617-0001`) that reported the original
mismatch.

### Fixed — an unrouted E1M pad can now be modelled and is refused loudly, not opened silently as a normal GPIO (#1854)

`metadata/schemas/som-preset-v2.schema.json`'s `pad_routes:` block had exactly
two states: routed through a SoM-side mediator chip, or the implicit `direct`
default. A pad that is physically open on a given hardware revision -- wired to
neither the mediator nor the main silicon -- had no way to say so, so it fell
into the `direct` default and emitted as an ordinary, openable GPIO. The
concrete instance: `metadata/e1m_modules/aen/hw-revisions.yaml` records that AEN
r2 leaves `E1M_GPIO_IO21` unrouted (it was CC3501E `GPIO_30` on r1, moved to
`IO8` on r2), yet `--emit composed-route-table` for r2 emitted
`{ "e1m": "E1M_GPIO_IO21", "dispatch": "direct" }` with no marker at all -- the
revision where the pad is dead looked identical to a working one.

`pad_route_entry.dispatch` gains a third value, `unrouted`, and the schema's
`pad_routes:` description (the exact prose the issue quoted) now says so:
pads not listed still default to `direct`, but a dead pad MUST carry an
explicit `unrouted` entry -- there is no implicit `unrouted`. An `unrouted`
entry requires a `doc:` (schema `allOf`, mirroring the existing
`mailbox.driver_status: partial` -> `notes:` pattern), so the model can't just
say "dead" without saying why. `metadata/e1m_modules/E1M-AEN{301,401,501,601,
701,801}.yaml` each gain the one new row recording IO21 on r2; r1's existing
`pad_route_overrides` (`dispatch: cc3501e, dispatch_pin: 30`) is untouched, so
`--emit composed-route-table` still differs correctly between the two
revisions -- confirmed by diffing the full composed table before/after for
both AEN r1/r2 and a V2N SKU: the ONLY change anywhere is IO21 on r2.

The runtime side closes the loop where every caller actually meets it: the
CC3501E GPIO proxy backend (`src/backends/gpio/cc3501e_proxy.c`) is the single
chokepoint every `alp_gpio_open()` call on an AEN target passes through
(it registers above the platform GPIO backend and fans out per-pin
internally), so the check lives there, not in one example. A new
board-provided `cc3501e_gpio_unrouted[]` list (WEAK empty default, same
pattern as the existing `cc3501e_gpio_routes[]` table) is checked in
`px_open()` before the route/delegate decision; a listed pin_id returns
`ALP_ERR_NOSUPPORT` instead of falling through to the platform driver and
silently opening a pin that reaches nothing. `include/alp/chips/cc3501e/gpio.h`
declares the new table. A new `tests/unit/gpio_cc3501e_unrouted` ztest suite
(native_sim, its own local strong override, its own controlled optimization
level) proves both directions: with the check reverted,
`alp_gpio_open(ALP_E1M_GPIO_IO21)` genuinely succeeds against a real emulated
`alp,pin-array` node (not an accidental failure from a missing DT node); with
the check in place, the same call returns `NULL` and `alp_last_error() ==
ALP_ERR_NOSUPPORT`, and an ordinary pin (`IO20`) is unaffected.

**The model and the guard ship; no pad is refused on real hardware yet.**
`aen-cc3501e-bringup` / `aen-cc3501e-companion-tour` / `aen-cc3501e-gpio`
deliberately do NOT populate `cc3501e_gpio_unrouted[]` with IO21, so those
examples' behaviour is unchanged. Two reasons, both pre-existing and both
already filed:

- The examples' route tables are not revision-aware -- they encode ONE
  hardware revision's wiring, hand-picked to match whatever board the
  example was written against, with no way to select r1 vs r2 at build
  time. The only AEN hardware on the bench today is r1, where
  `hw-revisions.yaml`'s `pad_route_overrides` route IO21 to CC3501E
  `GPIO_30` -- IO21 genuinely works on r1; only r2 leaves it open. A
  static `ALP_E1M_GPIO_IO21` entry in these examples would refuse a pad
  that works on the only board that can prove it. Fixing this needs the
  examples' tables to be generated from the (revision-selected) composed
  route table, which is issue #1859.
- Independently, the WEAK-default-array override pattern itself
  (`cc3501e_gpio_unrouted[]`, and the pre-existing `cc3501e_gpio_routes[]`
  it mirrors) does not reliably work on the real ARM target: under `-Os`,
  GCC constant-folds the WEAK definition's own initializer into every
  read inside `cc3501e_proxy.c` before the linker ever resolves which
  definition wins, so a strong override in another translation unit is
  never referenced and both symbols are garbage-collected out of the
  final ELF (`nm`/`objdump` evidence) -- issue #1860. Populating the
  examples today would either be silently inert (folded away) or, once
  #1860 is fixed, wrong on r1 -- worse than leaving it unpopulated.

Both issues are prerequisites for populating this list in real firmware,
not for the model or the guard, which are correct and land here as-is.

The mechanism is schema-general -- any SoM family (V2N/V2M's GD32 bridge
included) can now record a genuinely dead pad the same way -- but only AEN's
concrete IO21 fact is recorded here, per the no-inventing-values rule; no
V2N/V2M pad is known to need it today.

### Fixed — scaffolded `board.yaml`/`src/*.c` comments named an alp-sdk-only path bare, unresolvable outside the SDK tree (#1855)

`--emit scaffold`'s content-adaptation pass (`alp_template.render_to_envelope`)
only ever rewrote a bare alp-sdk-tree-relative cross-reference
(`docs/cc3501e-bridge.md`, `examples/v2n/v2n-temp-sensor`, ...) inside
README.md — via `_scaffold_readme`'s markdown-link rewriter. A `board.yaml` or
`src/main.c` **comment** names the same kind of reference in plain prose, with
no `[...](...)` around it, so it was never touched and survived a scaffold
verbatim: `iot`'s board.yaml/src/main.c both said "(see
docs/cc3501e-bridge.md)"; `sensor`'s board.yaml/src/main.c both said "see
examples/v2n/v2n-temp-sensor for ..."; `edge-ai`'s src/main.c said "(see
examples/ai/cold-chain-monitor/models/README.md)" — none of those paths exist
in a customer's copied-out project.

`multicore-mailbox`'s README carried a related but separate bug: its
`west build -b <board> examples/multicore/mproc-mailbox/peer` line names a
*subpath* of the template's own `example_path`, which the existing bare-
mention rewrite (`example_path` -> `.`) never matched (its right-hand `\S`
boundary failed on the trailing `/peer`), so it survived un-rewritten too.

Added `_scaffold_bare_repo_paths()` — the same `docs/*.md`/`examples/<...>` ->
absolute GitHub URL rewrite `_scaffold_readme` already gives a markdown link,
now also run on `board.yaml` and every `src/*.c`/`src/*.h` in
`render_to_envelope()` — and widened `_scaffold_readme`'s bare `example_path`
match to capture and keep a trailing `/<subpath>`, rewriting it to
`./<subpath>`. `diagnostics` and `minimal` were checked against the same
methodology and carry no such reference today; left unchanged.

`tests/fixtures/emit-snapshots/scaffold.{peripheral,sensor,edge-ai}-v2n101.snap`
and `scaffold.multicore-mailbox-aen801.snap` regenerated via
`scripts/check_emit_snapshots.py --update` to match (`peripheral`, not named
in the original report, carries the same bug class in its `board.yaml` and is
fixed by the same general pass).

### Fixed — the CC3501E GPIO proxy route table was hand-triplicated, non-revision-aware, and routed a bridge-reserved pad (#1859)

`examples/aen/{aen-cc3501e-gpio,aen-cc3501e-bringup,aen-cc3501e-companion-tour}/src/cc3501e_gpio_routes.c`
hardcoded the r2 (production) map -- `{ALP_E1M_GPIO_IO8, 30u}`,
`{ALP_E1M_GPIO_IO10, 35u}`, no `IO21` entry -- with none of the three
`board.yaml` files setting `som.hw_rev`. On the r1 bench module `IO8` and
`IO10` are direct Alif GPIOs and `IO21` reaches the CC3501E instead, so
now that #1860 makes the table's contents actually reach the proxy
backend, a board built for r1 would have started driving the wrong
chip's pins. Separately, the table carried
`{ ALP_E1M_GPIO_IO16, 17u }` -- CC3501E `GPIO_17`, the bridge's own
READY/host-IRQ line (`metadata/e1m_modules/aen/from-cc3501e.tsv`; the
bridge firmware's `gpio_pad_reserved()`, in the separate
`alplabai/cc3501e-bridge-firmware` repo, rejects pads 16 and 17). `IO17`
(-> `GPIO_16`, the bridge's own SPI0 CS) was correctly hand-omitted with
a comment explaining why; `IO16` was not.

Both defects share a root cause: the table was hand-maintained instead of
derived from the metadata that already fully describes it. Replaced with
`scripts/gen_cc3501e_gpio_routes.py`, a generator matching this repo's
"board files are generated from YAML" convention
(`scripts/gen_board_header.py`, `--emit zephyr-board`): for every AEN
example whose `prj.conf` sets `CONFIG_ALP_SDK_GPIO_CC3501E_PROXY=y`, it
resolves `alp_project.py --input <board.yaml> --emit composed-route-table`
(which already applies `metadata/e1m_modules/aen/hw-revisions.yaml`
`pad_route_overrides:` for the board's `som.hw_rev`, falling back to the
SoM's `default_hw_rev` when unset -- `scripts/alp_project_loader.py`'s
`_hwrev_pad_route_overrides()`), filters to `dispatch: cc3501e` GPIO
rows, and excludes any row whose target pad is in
`RESERVED_CC3501E_PADS`. That set is DERIVED from
`metadata/e1m_modules/aen/from-cc3501e.tsv`'s `BRIDGE_READY` /
`BRIDGE_SPI_CSN` peripheral-claim column, not hand-typed against the
firmware's `gpio_pad_reserved()` (which lives in a separate repo this
one can't see drift in) -- as one rule applied to every row, not a
per-instance hand omission. A dropped row is printed, not silently
discarded; a `dispatch: cc3501e` GPIO row with no `dispatch_pin` (a
metadata defect -- typo'd `dispatch:`, a missing pin in a
`pad_route_overrides` entry) now fails the generator outright instead of
silently delegating that pad to the platform driver, and
`metadata/schemas/hw-revisions-v1.schema.json`'s `pad_route_overrides[].dispatch`
now carries the same enum the SoM preset schema already enforces, so a
typo can't validate in the first place.
`.github/workflows/pr-generated-files.yml` and
`scripts/test-all.sh`'s `stage_generated_files` regenerate and diff-gate
the three committed tables the same way every other single-sourced
artifact in this repo already is, scoped to `examples/aen` so a future
fourth proxy-enabled example is covered without another edit here.

The three examples still resolve to `hw_rev=r2` (none set `som.hw_rev`,
so the SoM's `default_hw_rev: r2` applies) -- their generated tables are
unchanged in board-revision terms, just corrected (`IO16` dropped, 9
routes instead of 10) and now regenerable. A board.yaml that sets
`som.hw_rev: r1` gets the r1 map automatically; verified both by hand
(feeding the generator a `som.hw_rev: r1` copy of `aen-cc3501e-gpio`'s
board.yaml and confirming `IO8`/`IO10` resolve `direct` and `IO21`
resolves `cc3501e`/`30`) and by a new committed regression test,
`tests/scripts/test_gen_cc3501e_gpio_routes.py::test_r1_board_yaml_produces_the_r1_map_not_r2s`.
`tests/scripts/test_aen_cc3501e_routes.py`'s cross-check against SoM
metadata was itself pinned to `from-cc3501e.tsv` (r2-only) before this
round; it now builds its expectation from each example's own
`--emit composed-route-table`, so it can validate a per-example
`som.hw_rev` instead of only ever proving r2.

**Also added: a runtime hw_rev guard, GPIO-only** (the "stronger guard"
#1853's boot-banner fix explicitly deferred to this issue). Before this,
nothing stopped a firmware image compiled against one hw_rev's route
table from running on a module of a DIFFERENT hw_rev -- exactly the risk
above, just moved from "the table is wrong" to "the table is right for
the wrong module." `alp_gpio_cc3501e_attach()` now reads the on-module
EEPROM manifest once (via `alp_hw_info_read()` +
`alp_hw_info_build_hw_rev_mismatch()`, landed on `dev` with #1862) and
caches whether the live module's `hw_rev` disagrees with
`CONFIG_ALP_SDK_SOM_HW_REV` (the rev this build's table was generated
for); `route_lookup()` refuses to proxy anything for the rest of the run
when it does, falling through to the platform driver -- the same safe
fallback an empty/unpopulated route table already gets, instead of
driving a different physical pin than the caller asked for. Stays
inert (never refuses) when the manifest can't be read (unprovisioned
EEPROM, or -- true for all three examples today -- no
`CONFIG_ALP_SDK_HW_INFO_EEPROM_I2C_BUS_ID` wired for AEN yet), matching
the boot banner's own floor: known limitation, not fixed here.

`fix/1854-unrouted-pad` (#1863) is unaffected: it deliberately leaves
`cc3501e_gpio_unrouted[]` unpopulated pending #1860's own-TU fix landing
first; this change does not touch that table, and -- unlike
`cc3501e_gpio_routes[]` -- `cc3501e_gpio_unrouted[]` is NOT covered by
`scripts/gen_cc3501e_gpio_routes.py` (different shape entirely). Whoever
populates it will be hand-writing entries the same way this table used
to be, with the same drift risk; a generator for that table is a
follow-up, not part of this fix.

### Fixed — the CC3501E GPIO proxy's weak route table was constant-folded at `-Os`, so a board's strong override was never read (#1860)

`src/backends/gpio/cc3501e_proxy.c` defined `cc3501e_gpio_routes[]` /
`cc3501e_gpio_route_count` as `__attribute__((weak)) const` objects in the
same translation unit that read them in `route_lookup()`'s loop bound. At
`-Os` (`CONFIG_SIZE_OPTIMIZATIONS=y`, the default on
`alp_e1m_aen801_m55_he/ae822fa0e5597ls0/rtss_he`) the compiler could see
its own zero initializer for `cc3501e_gpio_route_count` at the read site
and folded the loop away entirely -- a board's strong override in another
translation unit (e.g. `examples/aen/aen-cc3501e-gpio`) still linked, but
nothing ever read it. Measured on the real target build: the example
object carried the strong `R cc3501e_gpio_routes` symbol, the proxy
object carried only the weak `V` definition with zero relocations
against either symbol in its disassembly, and the final ELF contained
neither symbol. Every `alp_gpio_open()` call fell through to the
platform backend, so pads that exist only on the CC3501E (`IO13`, `IO15`,
`IO18`, `IO19`, `IO20`) could not be driven at all, silently, at any
optimization level the repo ships.

Fixed by splitting the weak default into its own translation unit,
`src/backends/gpio/cc3501e_proxy_routes_weak.c` (gated the same way as
`cc3501e_proxy.c`, `CONFIG_ALP_SDK_GPIO_CC3501E_PROXY`, in
`zephyr/CMakeLists.txt`). `cc3501e_proxy.c` now only ever sees the
`extern` declaration already in `<alp/chips/cc3501e/gpio.h>`, so
`route_lookup()` always compiles a genuine indirect load through
whichever definition the linker resolves. Re-measured on the same target
build after the fix: the proxy object's disassembly now carries real
`R_ARM_ABS32` relocations against both symbols, and the final ELF
carries the strong 9-entry table (verified against the raw `.rodata`
bytes, not just symbol presence).

The same weak-array-read-in-its-own-TU shape is the bug, not this one
instance -- `#1854`'s `cc3501e_gpio_unrouted[]` table (currently parked,
unpopulated, on `fix/1854-unrouted-pad`) will need the identical
own-TU split before it can safely carry real entries.

### Fixed — `aen-cc3501e-gpio` and `aen-cc3501e-companion-tour` stack-overflowed in `main()` on boot and halted (#1868)

Both examples declared their `cc3501e_t fw;` driver context as a plain
automatic (stack) local in `main()`. `sizeof(cc3501e_t)` is ~32 KB — `rx_scratch`
/ `tx_scratch` / `wifi_scan_buf` / `ble_scan_buf` / `evt_buf` / `sock_buf` /
`spi1_tx_buf` / `spi1_rx_buf` are each sized off `ALP_CC3501E_MAX_PAYLOAD`,
4096 since the v5 protocol bump — against `CONFIG_MAIN_STACK_SIZE=4096` in
both examples' `prj.conf`. The compiler's frame-reservation instruction for
`main()`'s prologue alone (`sub sp, #framesize`) therefore moved `SP` below
`PSPLIM` before a single statement of `main()` ran, and the M55 raised a
UsageFault immediately: `E: ***** USAGE FAULT ***** / E: Stack overflow
(context area not valid)`, faulting PC resolving (`arm-zephyr-eabi-addr2line`
against the built ELF) to `main()`'s own entry
(`examples/aen/aen-cc3501e-gpio/src/main.c:205`, the line the compiler
attributed the prologue to), with `LR` resolving to `z_setup_new_thread`
(upstream Zephyr's own `kernel/thread.c` at the v4.4.1 pin — not a path in
this tree, so deliberately not cited as one) — i.e. `main()` never got past its own
prologue, consistent with the captured boot log showing the SDK banner but
never `main()`'s own first `printf`. Confirmed via `sizeof(cc3501e_t)` = 32888
bytes (host GCC build) and, post-fix, via `arm-zephyr-eabi-nm` on a rebuilt
ELF: `fw` now lands in `.bss` (`20000650 00008040 b fw.0`, gpio; `...b fw.4`,
companion-tour) and `main()`'s prologue drops to `sub sp, #28`.

Same defect, same fix already established in `aen-cc3501e-bringup`'s own
`fw` (that example's comment: *"STATIC, not a stack local: ... as a local
the prologue crosses PSPLIM and the M55 raises STKOF -> UsageFault at
main+4 ... Bench-proven: as a local this image never boots."*) — it just
never propagated to its two siblings. `aen-cc3501e-gpio` and
`aen-cc3501e-companion-tour` now declare `static cc3501e_t fw;` too, moving
the context to BSS instead of the main thread's stack. Both rebuilt clean
(`west build`, `alp_e1m_aen801_m55_he/ae822fa0e5597ls0/rtss_he`); no
`CONFIG_MAIN_STACK_SIZE` change needed for either — the GPIO/camera-enable
and diagnostic/socket helpers these two call all use small fixed-size wire
structs or (companion-tour's socket buffers) are already `static`, so 4096 B
of real stack is ample once the 32 KB context is off it.

**Second symptom investigated, not fixed here.** The same boot capture shows
the banner printing the raw `CONFIG_BOARD` target (`alp_e1m_aen801_m55_he`)
instead of the live SoM identity (`E1M-AEN801 r1`, as `alp-console` prints on
the same physical module) — the original issue's two guesses (`CONFIG_ALP_SDK_HW_INFO`
never enabled, or a fault before the manifest read) are both wrong.
`CONFIG_ALP_SDK_HW_INFO` defaults to `y` and is on; `scripts/alp_orchestrate`
auto-emits `CONFIG_ALP_SDK_HW_INFO_EEPROM_I2C_BUS_ID=0` (+ address/offset/
bitrate) into every AEN build from the SoM preset's `on_module.eeprom`,
regardless of the app's own `peripherals:` list — confirmed present and
correctly resolved in `aen-cc3501e-gpio`'s own `.config`. The read still
fails because the underlying devicetree node it targets, `i2c2`, is
`status = "disabled"`: none of `aen-cc3501e-gpio` / `aen-cc3501e-bringup` /
`aen-cc3501e-companion-tour`'s board overlays enable it or declare the
`alp-i2c0` alias `alp_hw_info_read()`'s `alp_i2c_open(bus_id=0)` needs — only
`alp-console`'s overlay does (its own `&i2c2 { status = "okay"; ... };` +
`alp-i2c0 = &i2c2;`, bench-validated pad config). So on all three CC3501E
examples the EEPROM read structurally cannot succeed, the banner falls to
the `CONFIG_BOARD` fallback, and the `#1853`/`#1859` `hw_rev`-mismatch guard
(keyed on that same read) is inert on all three, not just this one. Wiring
`i2c2` into three example overlays is a distinct, bench-validated hardware
change (pad config, pull direction, possible pin interaction with each
example's existing SPI1/LP-GPIO wiring) outside this fix's scope — left as a
follow-up.

### Fixed — the three CC3501E examples never enabled `i2c2`, so the EEPROM manifest read structurally could not succeed (#1870)

`alp_hw_info_read()` opens `bus_id = 0`, which resolves through the
`alp-i2c0` alias to the SoC's `i2c2` (the on-module EEPROM manifest bus,
disabled by default in the base dtsi). `examples/aen/aen-cc3501e-gpio`,
`aen-cc3501e-bringup` and `aen-cc3501e-companion-tour` never enabled that
node or declared the alias — zero references in all three, versus two in
`examples/peripheral-io/alp-console`'s bench-validated overlay — so the
manifest read failed for a *configuration* reason on modules that are
otherwise fully provisioned. The banner fell back to the raw board target
instead of the SoM identity, and, more importantly, the hw_rev-mismatch
guard added for #1853/#1859 keys off exactly this read: with it inert, a
compiled-vs-actual revision mismatch on these examples — which carry the
CC3501E GPIO proxy route table, i.e. exactly where a mismatch drives the
wrong chip's pins — went undetected.

Each of the three real-board overlays now carries the same `i2c2` pinctrl
group, `&i2c2 { status = "okay"; ... }` and `alp-i2c0` alias as
`alp-console`'s overlay, byte-for-byte the same pad config (SCL `P5_6`
/ SDA `P5_7`, input-enable, bias-pull-down — the pad DSC value Alif's
reference uses, do not "correct" to pull-up). `i2c2` is the EEPROM/manifest
bus that exits at the connector and is pulled up on the carrier
(`R95`/`R96` populated); it is a different bus from the on-module BRD_I2C
housekeeping bus (#1848), whose pull-ups are absent.

Verified with `west build` (`alp_e1m_aen801_m55_he/ae822fa0e5597ls0/rtss_he`)
for all three: the resolved `zephyr.dts` shows `i2c2` `status = "okay"`
with `pinctrl-0 = <&pinctrl_i2c2>` and the `alp-i2c0` alias resolving to it.
`aen-cc3501e-bringup`'s `CONFIG_MAIN_STACK_SIZE=32768` is unchanged by the
new bus. Bench-gated: not yet re-verified against a physical E1M-AEN801.

### Changed — ADR 0026 §C and §D decided: alp-sdk keeps the configure-time call and stays canonical for rendered bytes (#1892)

ADR 0026's 2026-08-30 amendment raised §C and §D as open questions and stopped
short of answering them — §C ends "Decide which, here, before step 3", and §D
warned that leaving the render-artefact owner implicit "recreates the #320 →
#485 drift class one layer down, now undetected." Both are now decided and
recorded in the ADR.

**§C — who answers `alp_project.py --emit zephyr-conf --core <id>` at
cmake-configure time: alp-sdk does, via a surviving emitter core. The call is
not repointed at `tan`.** Alp Lab ships SoMs; a customer running a plain
`west build` must not thereby acquire a hard dependency on a second tool that
was nowhere in their loop, and repointing the call at `tan` would do exactly
that for every user project build, including ones already shipped to
customers that no repo-side change can reach. This is the same direction
ADR-0017 and ADR-0020 already set: the SDK ships with the hardware, the build
CLI is optional convenience layered above it.

**§D — single owner for rendered-artefact bytes: alp-sdk's emitters are
canonical.** `tan` consumes plan-embedded bytes instead of re-implementing the
renderers. Rendering `alp.conf` / sysbuild / kconfig / headers / secure bytes
is hardware-truth generation from `metadata/`, and the producer and renderer
of hardware truth belong in the same repo. The 19-of-20 `--emit` modes
currently re-implemented in tan against alp-sdk's raw metadata are what goes
away under this decision; the parity apparatus shrinks to a render-envelope
gate rather than being deleted with the planner axis. That gate's
implementation is not decided here.

Neither decision reverses the ADR: `tan` still owns the planner outright and
alp-sdk still stops being a second plan producer. Only the renderers — the
`alp.conf` / sysbuild / kconfig / headers / secure emitters and the
configure-time `--emit zephyr-conf` call — stay in alp-sdk. §G's replacement
migration sequence is updated to match: step 3 now repoints only the
plan-producer consumers at `tan`, leaving every renderer-owned emit-registry
entry resolving to alp-sdk's surviving core, and step 6 clarifies that
deleting the planner parity axis in tan does not touch the separate
render-envelope gate §D requires.

One concrete consequence, named so it does not need rediscovering: tan-cli's
eleven vendored `CMakeLists.txt` templates that spawn
`${ALP_SDK_ROOT}/scripts/alp_project.py --emit zephyr-conf` at build time
(tan-cli#1079) are correct as written under this decision and stay unchanged.

Docs only; no code, schema or metadata change.

and **v0.15.0**, narrowing the gap to two releases (**v0.10.0** and

### Added — the first tier-2 bench perf points in `metadata/model_perf/` (#1894)

Three points were measured on E1M-V2M103 2026W38-0001 on 2026-09-28. Each follows `docs/bench/model-perf-capture.md`: 5 warm-up invokes discarded, then back-to-back good invokes timed with `alp_inference_last_invoke_latency_us()`:

| backend | model | mean | p95 | runs |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `deepx_dxm1` | yolo11n (dx-com 2.3.0) | 45.47 ms | 46.16 ms | 50 |
| `drpai` | YOLOX-S/VOC sparse70 (DRP-AI Translator i8 v1.12) | 40.05 ms | 40.09 ms | 50 |
| `cpu` (ONNX Runtime 1.20.1) | YOLOX-S/VOC | 1668.5 ms | 1674.1 ms | 30 |

All three run on the A55 cluster with the model in DDR, so there is no on-chip SRAM arena (`req_sram_kib` / `arena_bytes` = 0). The unit is bench-only, and each point's `capture.notes` records that. No Ethos-U point is included: the vela-profile question in the capture doc still blocks those.

### Fixed — a prerelease tag declared itself as its GA version, so an rc checkout was indistinguishable from the release (#1902)

`scripts/bump_version.py --to <X.Y.Z-rcN>` already parsed a SemVer
pre-release suffix (`SEMVER_RE`'s `(?:-([\w.]+))?` group) and
`scripts/alp_lock/__init__.py`'s version regex already tolerated one too --
but nothing actually let the suffix reach a build. `.github/workflows/release.yml`'s
"Parse tag + verify against metadata" step compared `metadata/sdk_version.yaml`'s
`version:` against the TAG's core (stripped-of-suffix) version with no
stripping on the metadata side, so a `version:` carrying `-rc1` failed the
release outright -- the only way to pass was to bump metadata to the bare
GA version and let just the git tag carry `-rcN`, which is exactly why an rc
checkout's `ALP_VERSION_STRING`, `alp_version_string()`, `alp.lock`'s
`sdk.version`, and the build plan's `sdkVersion` all read identically to the
eventual GA build. (This is what forced the manual CHANGELOG retitle in the
v0.15.0 window, #1292: the metadata never distinguished the rc from the GA
it never shipped.)

Fixed at the root: `release.yml` now strips DECLARED's own suffix
(`DECLARED_CORE="${DECLARED%%-*}"`) before comparing to the tag's core, so
`metadata/sdk_version.yaml` can legitimately carry the SAME suffix as the
tag being cut. A second guard closes the gap that alone would have opened:
a GA tag (no suffix of its own) now REFUSES a metadata `version:` that
still carries a leftover rc suffix -- otherwise a forgotten final bump
after the last rc would ship a GA build silently reporting itself as an
rc, #1902 in the other direction. `scripts/bump_version.py --to 1.0.0-rc1` now writes the FULL
`1.0.0-rc1` into `metadata/sdk_version.yaml`'s `version:` and
`include/alp/version.h`'s `ALP_VERSION_STRING` (`ALP_VERSION_MAJOR/MINOR/PATCH`
stay the plain core integers) -- SemVer's own pre-release syntax, not a new
field. `pyproject.toml`'s `[project]` version and the `alp_banner.c` sample
line stay pinned to the core triple (PEP 440 doesn't accept a bare `-rc1`
suffix, and neither is the self-identification surface -- the banner's
*code* always prints the live `ALP_VERSION_STRING`). `CHANGELOG.md` is left
untouched by a pre-release bump: an rc has no GA section of its own yet, and
slicing one would starve `release.yml`'s documented `## [Unreleased]`
fallback of content; the later GA bump (`--to 1.0.0`, no suffix) does the
real slice.

Two more consumers had the same `\s*$`-anchored regex and would have
silently broken (or gone blind) the first time this was actually exercised:
`scripts/check_version_doc_sync.py`'s `declared_version()` now accepts the
suffix and checks `ALP_VERSION_STRING` against the FULL declared string
(`declared_version_full()`) while every other copy -- pyproject.toml,
alp_banner.c, VERSIONS.md -- still checks the core triple only; and
`scripts/abi_snapshot.py`'s `_SDK_VERSION_RE` (used by
`current_snapshot_version()` / `--print-current-version`, which
`scripts/test-all.sh`'s `abi_current_snapshot()` and `pr-abi-snapshot.yml`
both call) now tolerates the suffix too -- pre-fix it returned `None`
("can't verify"), silently skipping `stage_abi_strict` for the whole rc
window instead of running it.

`status: released` in `metadata/sdk_version.yaml` is deliberately left
alone: overloading it for this was already proposed and rejected once
(this CHANGELOG's v0.15.0 entry and #1508, both citing alp.lock churn) --
the pre-release suffix is the narrower, additive fix `scripts/alp_lock/__init__.py`,
`scripts/alp_orchestrate/sdk_compat.py`, `scripts/alp_orchestrate/buildplan.py`
and `scripts/alp_cli/__init__.py` already tolerated with zero code changes.

### Fixed — `diagnostic_format.py`'s SARIF/LSP `_uri()` emitted a bare filesystem path, not a URI reference (#1909)

`_uri()` fed both `to_machine_json` (LSP `uri`, diagnostic-v1) and `to_sarif`
(`artifactLocation.uri`) with `diag.path.as_posix()` — a bare path, not a
URI. Both SARIF 2.1.0's `artifactLocation.uri` and LSP's `DocumentUri`
define this field as a URI reference: on an absolute Windows-spelled root
this rendered `C:/w/proj/board.yaml` (forward-slashed, still no `file:`
scheme, still invalid at the drive-letter-colon position), and a POSIX
absolute root rendered with no scheme either — a consumer resolving either
fails or matches nothing, silently.

`_uri()` now renders an absolute path as an absolute `file:` URI and keeps a
relative path relative (already a legal RFC 3986 §4.2 URI reference), judged
Windows- vs POSIX-spelled from the path string itself
(`scripts/alp_cli/diagnostic_format.py:61-100`, `_is_windows_spelled` /
`_path_to_uri_reference`) rather than the rendering host's own OS — the host
formatting a diagnostic may not match the path's own spelling. Ported from
tan-cli's `path_to_uri_reference` (alplabai/tan-cli#1111,
`python/tan/core/uri_reference.py`), the reference implementation for the
identical defect in tan's own SARIF/LSP exporters, so the two emitters of
`schemaVersion: 1` documents agree on `uri` again.

Left out of scope, matching tan-cli's own reverted attempt at it
(alplabai/tan-cli#1117): declaring `originalUriBaseIds`/`uriBaseId` on
`to_sarif`'s output so a relative `artifactLocation.uri` has a base to
resolve against — tan-cli found no sound anchor for it yet (a `root="."`
vs. a `--project` override disagree on what the relative path is even
relative to) and reverting an authoritatively wrong base was judged safer
than shipping one.

### Fixed — `alp_template.py` crashed with a bare `TypeError` on a schema-valid catalog record declaring `constraints.minimum`/`maximum` on a non-integer parameter (#1916)

`_check_constraints` (`scripts/alp_template.py:267`) compared a parameter's
`default` against `constraints.minimum`/`maximum` without first checking the
bound applies to the parameter's declared `type`. A **schema-valid**
`templates[].parameters[]` record —

```json
{"name": "knob", "type": "string", "default": "a", "constraints": {"minimum": 5}}
```

— died with `TypeError: '<' not supported between instances of 'str' and
'int'`, surfacing an internal crash on input the tooling itself said was
acceptable.

`_check_constraints` now refuses `minimum`/`maximum` on any non-`integer`
type — string, enum **and** boolean (boolean deliberately: `bool < int`
never raises, so there is no crash, but the bound is still meaningless) —
and raises the same curated `ParameterError` every other check in this
function already uses
(`scripts/alp_template.py:284` ("only applies to type 'integer'")),
matching the shape tan-cli's own fix settled on
(tan-cli#1123) so the two implementations agree on this input class again.

`metadata/schemas/template-catalog-v1.schema.json`'s `$defs/parameter` gained
an `if`/`then` pair (the same construct the record already uses for
`status: preview` requiring `note`) rejecting `constraints.minimum`/`maximum`
on a non-`integer` `type` at the schema level too, so the crashing record
above no longer validates in the first place.

`constraints.enum` on a non-`string`-coerced type (e.g. `integer` +
`constraints.enum`, unsatisfiable rather than crashing) is the same
inapplicability class the issue also flagged — left out of scope here as
lower priority; tracked in the issue for follow-up.

### Fixed — `_dxcom_version()`'s probe-failure fallback carried a different vendor token than its success path (#1923)

`scripts/alp_model/adapters/deepx.py`'s `_dxcom_version()` returned
`"DX-COM <version>"` on the success path but the bare lowercase
`"dxcom"` (the console-script name) when the version probe failed, so a
perf point published during a probe failure carried a different
`target.compiler_version` vendor token than one published during a
successful probe -- for the same compiler, on the same backend. tan-cli
matches a bench perf point to a build by that token, case-folded, so the
mismatched fallback silently produced "no bench data for this build"
instead of a match.

`_dxcom_version()`'s fallback is now `"DX-COM <unknown>"` -- the token
stays `DX-COM` on every path; only the version segment varies. Checked
both sibling adapters for the same shape: `ethos_u.py`'s `_vela_version()`
falls back to the bare `"vela"` (no version suffix) and
`drpai.py`'s `_compiler_version()` falls back to the bare `"drp-ai_tvm"`
-- both already share their first token with their success-path string,
so neither had this divergence.

Added `tests/scripts/test_alp_model_adapters.py::test_dxcom_version_fallback_matches_success_vendor_token`
(probes a simulated `dxcom` failure and asserts the token) and
`::test_vela_and_drpai_version_fallback_already_matches_success_token`
(pins the two sibling adapters' existing, already-correct behaviour so a
future edit can't reintroduce the split).

### Added — listening sockets on the CC3501E, so a host can serve over the soft-AP (#1925)

The CC3501E socket API was client-only — `cc3501e_sock_open` / `_connect` /
`_send` / `_recv` / `_close`, opcodes `0x20`-`0x24`. A product could not
terminate an inbound TCP connection over the module's own soft-AP even though
the bridge firmware already runs lwIP with `bind`/`listen`/`accept` available:
the AP path starts a DHCP server through that same stack. This is the host half
of cc3501e-bridge-firmware#104 — serving an embedded web console over the
module's AP so the product needs no Ethernet PHY.

Wire protocol **8 → 9** (`ALP_CC3501E_PROTOCOL_VERSION`):

| Opcode | Name | Payload |
|---|---|---|
| `0x25` | `ALP_CC3501E_CMD_SOCK_BIND` | `alp_cc3501e_sock_bind_t` — the `SOCK_CONNECT` layout with the LOCAL endpoint |
| `0x26` | `ALP_CC3501E_CMD_SOCK_LISTEN` | `alp_cc3501e_sock_listen_t` |
| `0x2c` | `ALP_CC3501E_EVT_SOCK_ACCEPTED` | `alp_cc3501e_sock_accepted_evt_t`, async |
| `0x17` | `ALP_CC3501E_CMD_WIFI_GET_IP` | gains an optional `alp_cc3501e_wifi_iface_t` byte |

New host API in `<alp/chips/cc3501e/sockets.h>`: `cc3501e_sock_bind()`,
`cc3501e_sock_listen()` and `cc3501e_sock_accepted_decode()`.

**There is deliberately no accept opcode.** `accept()` blocks, and the firmware
worker holds READY low across a worker body, so an accept opcode would black the
whole bridge out — every opcode, not just sockets — for as long as no client
connected. An inbound connection arrives instead as an entry on the existing
polled event queue (`cc3501e_poll_events`), carrying a handle the host uses with
the ordinary `SOCK_RECV` / `SOCK_SEND` / `SOCK_CLOSE`.

The accepted-connection event is a compact 12-byte IPv4 form, not a 20-byte
`alp_cc3501e_sock_addr_t`: the firmware event ring caps a per-entry payload at
`ALP_CC3501E_EVENT_PAYLOAD_MAX` (16) and **clamps** anything longer, i.e.
silently truncates it on the wire, so `_Static_assert`s pin the size against
that cap (`include/alp/protocol/cc3501e.h:1941`
(`sock_accepted must fit ALP_CC3501E_EVENT_PAYLOAD_MAX`)). Use
`cc3501e_sock_accepted_decode()` rather than casting the callback's payload
pointer — it aims into the driver's event buffer at whatever offset the entry
landed on, so the cast is unaligned.

**Breaking:** `cc3501e_wifi_get_ip()` takes the interface as a parameter
(`cc3501e_wifi_get_ip(ctx, iface, ip)`), rather than gaining a second entry
point beside a permanently-STA one. Pass `ALP_CC3501E_WIFI_IFACE_STA` to keep
existing behaviour; `ALP_CC3501E_WIFI_IFACE_AP` reports the module's own
soft-AP address — the bind address a serving application needs before any
client has associated.

`alp companion sock serve <port> [seconds]` is the worked reference: it binds,
listens, and answers inbound HTTP, printing the AP-side address to aim a client
at.

Bench-verified on an E1M-AEN801 (2026-09-03, firmware GPE `0.149.83.0`,
`GET_VERSION` → protocol v9): an associated client holding a DHCP lease from the
CC3501E's own server received `HTTP/1.0 200 OK` on 16/16 requests across 5 serve
runs at ~0.45 s each, each connection arriving as `opcode 0x2c (len 12)`, with
the bridge still answering `GET_VERSION` afterwards.

Not fixed here and not caused here: socket operations in AP mode are unreliable
when they race radio activity — back-to-back **client** ops, and `bind`/`listen`
issued while a client is still associating. The first shape reproduces
identically on the pre-change protocol-8 firmware with no listening socket in
play; both are cc3501e-bridge-firmware#106. The send direction is also unbounded
(cc3501e-bridge-firmware#107).

### Fixed — gd32-bridge protocol spec said the frame CRC is MSB first; both implementations transmit it LSB first (#1926)

`docs/gd32-bridge-protocol.md:796` claimed the CRC-16/CCITT-FALSE trailer is
transmitted MSB first. Verified against `chips/gd32g553/gd32g553.c`'s four
CRC sites (`:213-214` SPI request, `:255-256` SPI reply parse, `:275-276`
short-error-envelope parse, `:366-367` I2C write) -- all four store the low
byte at the lower index, confirming LSB first, silicon-verified and matching
the gd32-bridge-firmware side. The spec sentence was the deviant party, and
it had already caused a downstream defect twice: the firmware's wire-vector
generator followed this sentence and emitted every vector big-endian
(gd32-bridge-firmware#68, fixed by gd32-bridge-firmware#88).

The doc now states the CRC is LSB first, with the worked example from the
issue -- CRC-16/CCITT-FALSE over the PING request body `A5 00` is `0xFF84`,
which goes on the wire as `84 FF` -- and a note that this is the one
little-endian field in an otherwise big-endian envelope, which is what made
the mistake easy. Grepped the repo for every other site repeating an
MSB-first claim for this protocol's CRC; found none (`docs/gd32-bridge.md`,
`docs/adr/0016-cross-core-peripheral-proxy-wire-schema.md`, and the other
gd32-bridge docs don't state a byte order for the CRC at all). Neither
implementation changed.

### Changed — the CC3501E wire protocol is versioned MAJOR.MINOR, and features are discovered by capability (#1927)

The wire protocol went **v5 to v9 in a single week**, and every bump forced a
lockstep reflash of both halves, because the host refused the link on any
mismatch. Sorted by the only question that matters — would an *unchanged host*
be **misread**? — only two of those four bumps qualify:

| Bump | Change | Old host misread? |
|---|---|---|
| v6 | SPI1 passthrough opcodes `0x55`..`0x57` | No — additive |
| v7 | `alp_cc3501e_sock_send_t::reserved` → retry seq | **Yes** |
| v8 | frame-header flags bits 3..7 → retry seq | **Yes** |
| v9 | `SOCK_BIND`/`SOCK_LISTEN`/`EVT_SOCK_ACCEPTED` | No — additive |

Two real breaks presented as four. The cause was one integer doing two jobs — a
compatibility gate *and* a feature marker — tested with exact equality, so the
feature half kept firing the gate half.

Per **ADR 0033**:

- `ALP_CC3501E_PROTOCOL_MAJOR` / `ALP_CC3501E_PROTOCOL_MINOR` replace the flat
  integer. `CMD_GET_VERSION` carries `(MAJOR << 8) | MINOR` in the same 2-byte LE
  reply. Retroactively v5=`1.0`, v6=`1.1`, v7=`2.0`, v8=`3.0`, v9=`3.1` — and the
  current wire `3.1` is **byte-identical** to what shipped as "v9".
- `cc3501e_reset()` refuses on **MAJOR only**
  (`chips/cc3501e/cc3501e_core.c:854` (`if (!cc3501e_fw_major_is_acceptable(fw_major))`)).
  A differing MINOR now connects, which is safe *because* MINOR is defined as
  additive: the host never sends an opcode it does not know, and the firmware
  never emits an event nobody armed.
- `MAJOR 0` is reserved, so a firmware predating the scheme — answering with its
  raw v1..v9 integer — stays distinguishable from one that disagrees about frame
  layout. `cc3501e_t::fw_proto_major` / `::fw_proto_minor` are recorded on both
  the accept and the refuse path.
- New `CMD_GET_CAPABILITIES` (`0x06`) and `cc3501e_get_capabilities()` report
  which opcode families a **build** implements, composed from the same
  compile-time switches that decide which HAL bodies link. That is something a
  version number cannot express: a build without Wi-Fi still carries every socket
  opcode and answers `NOTIMPL` to all of them.
- `alp companion ver` now leads with the release version — `fw 0.6.0 (wire 3.1)`.
