  address above — a separate decision, deliberately left visible here
  rather than silently resolved.

`XEVK_I2C_ADDR_TCAL9538` (E1M-X-EVK) is deliberately left at `0x72`: that is a
different board and no measurement covers its strap. Changing it to match the
E1M-EVK would ship an unverified address.

### Fixed — `0x58` on the SoM EEPROM bus is documented instead of unexplained (#1976)

An I2C census of SoC I2C2 sees an ACK at `0x58` that no metadata claimed, which
is an address a future part could be assigned to and collide with
(alp-sdk#1976). It is the **same physical N24S128** as the `0x50` array
answering its second device-select header (`1010` → `0x50`, `1011` → `0x58`) —
one part, nothing extra to source.

All **eleven** SoM presets that populate `eeprom_24c128` now record it, not just
the one it was measured on: the E1M-AEN line is a single shared PCB differing
only in SoC MPN, and the onsemi `N24S128C4DYT3G` is equally the fitted default on
E1M-V2N/V2M, so the collision hazard was identical on every SKU. The measurement
provenance stays singular and honest — bench-measured on `E1M-AEN803` serial
`2026W36-0003`, cited as one measurement rather than eleven.
`examples/aen/aen-eeprom-manifest` demonstrates reading it through the new
`eeprom_24c128_read_identity()`, and the bench/test/verification docs no longer
present their device census as a closed account that omits it.

### Added — `eeprom_24c128_read_identity()` reads the N24S128's second I2C device-select header (#1976)

The on-module 24C128 EEPROM (Onsemi N24S128) answers at both `0x50` (the 16 KB
array) and `0x50 + 0x08` — one part, a second device-select header exposing a
64-byte Secure Data Page, a 16-byte factory Unique ID, a Lock Status byte, and
the Device Configuration Register. `eeprom_24c128_read_identity()` reads all
four in one call into a new `eeprom_24c128_identity_t`, with a per-field
`_valid` flag rather than an all-or-nothing error: the approved
footprint-compatible second source (STMicro M24128-BFMH6TG, DNP) has no such
header, so on that part every read NACKs and the function still returns
`ALP_OK` with every `_valid` false.

Read-only by design — a stray write at the Device Configuration Register
selector would move the EEPROM off its strapped I2C address and can
permanently write-protect the array, so this change adds no write/lock path.
Bench-verified 2026-09-06 on an E1M-AEN803 (serial 2026W36-0003) over SoC
I2C2 — the shipped function itself was executed on silicon, not just linked.
It returned `ALP_OK` with all four objects answering at `0x58`: the Secure
Data Page erased (64 bytes of `0xFF`), a stable 16-byte Unique ID, Lock Status
reporting unlocked, and the Device Configuration Register reading the
datasheet delivery state `0x1D`. `0x58` was confirmed to be a distinct address
space rather than an alias of the manifest in the array at `0x50`, and the
three documented error paths each returned their documented status on the same
run.

### Fixed — the on-module TMP112 answers at `0x40`, not the declared `0x48` (#1978)

An I2C census on `E1M-AEN803` serial `2026W36-0002` found the on-module
temperature sensor ACKing at `0x40` while every metadata declaration in the tree
said `0x48`. It reproduced on two of two modules, so this is the part's actual
address on this SoM, not a one-board anomaly.

`0x48` was not an arbitrary guess — it is the TMP112's address when `ADD0` is
tied to `GND`, and it is the address most reference designs use. On the E1M-AEN
modules `ADD0` lands in the `0x40..0x43` row of the datasheet's address table
(TI SBOS473L Table 7-4) instead, which nothing in the tree had captured.

* `metadata/e1m_modules/E1M-AEN{301,401,501,601,701,801,803}.yaml` and
  `metadata/e1m_modules/aen/on-module-links.yaml` now declare
  `address_7bit: 0x40`, with the node named `tmp112@40`.
* `chips/tmp112/tmp112.c` and `include/alp/chips/tmp112.h` accept the
  `0x40..0x43` row (`TMP112_I2C_ADDR_ADDRVAR_*`) alongside the `0x48..0x4B` row
  the driver already knew, and the three-row Table 7-4 is documented at the
  enum rather than left implicit.

The address is the whole bug: a driver pointed at `0x48` on these modules gets
no ACK and reports the part missing, which is indistinguishable from a
depopulated or dead sensor.

### Documented — `docs/bring-up-aen.md` still called the TMP112's `0x40` address a per-unit defect after #1978 fixed the metadata (#1978)

`metadata/e1m_modules/E1M-AEN*.yaml`, the generated devicetree, `metadata/chips/tmp112.yaml`
and `docs/soms/aen.md` all already carry the corrected design address --
`0x40`, not the earlier-declared `0x48` -- for the on-module TMP112. The fix
that landed under #1978 (`fix(aen): repair five E1M-EVK drivers, correct the
TMP112 address, and add the phased EVK demo (#2036)`) did not touch
`docs/bring-up-aen.md`, which still called `0x40` a "per-unit TMP112 defect",
listed `0x48` as the "DECLARED address" that "does NOT answer on the 2026W36
batch", and reported the bench-settled BRD_I2C table's ACK for the TMP112 at
`0x48` instead of `0x40`. All three are corrected to match the rest of the
tree: `0x40` is the TMP112DIDPWR's (X2SON-5) design address per TI SBOS473L
Table 7-4 (ADD0->GND), not a batch anomaly.

### Added — build-time knobs for Alif TF-A's console UART base and pads (#1979)

Alif's TF-A port hardcodes its BL32 console to the DevKit's UART2 in two
independent places that must move together: the register base
(`platform_def.h`) and the pinmux (`devkit_e7_sp_min_setup.c`). A carrier
routing a different UART got no console output and no error -- BL32 ran
(confirmed via PSCI answering SMCs) while the console stayed at zero bytes,
as happened during the 2026-09-05 E8 A32 Linux bring-up (#1972).

`meta-alp-sdk/recipes-bsp/trusted-firmware-a/trusted-firmware-a/`
gains `alif-console-uart-build-knobs.patch`, adding six `#ifndef`-guarded
macros defaulted to the unmodified DevKit UART2 values, so an unset build is
byte-identical. The bbappend wires the E1M-AEN801 EVK's verified console
routing (SoC UART5, `P3_4`/`P3_5`, alternate function 2) behind an
`:e1m-aen801` override.

The `:e1m-aen801` and `:e1m-aen701` knobs are inert today:
`MACHINE=e1m-aen801-a32`/`e1m-aen701-a32` does not yet parse (no public
Scarthgap `meta-alif-ensemble`/`devkit-e8.conf` exists, #1968 #1971), so
nothing currently reaches this recipe. The patch is verified (`patch -p1
--dry-run`, `git apply --check`) against the real upstream source
(`alifsemi/trusted-firmware-a_alif`, branch `alif_lts-v2.10.8`), not against
real E1M-AEN801/E1M-AEN701 silicon -- that needs the Scarthgap layer to land
first. Both MACHINEs get the same UART5 knobs: they are the same AEN carrier
PCB (`metadata/pinmux/aen.yaml`) and share the `PLAT=devkit_e7` TF-A plat
directory this patch touches.

**This fixes only the TF-A/BL32 half of #1979.** The issue names a second,
independent trap on the Linux side (`UART2_STATUS "okay"` making
`serial@4901a000`/`ttyS0` win over the UART5 console at the `aliases`
level) that this change does not touch. Refs #1979 -- does not close it.

### Fixed — E1M-AEN EVK Linux device tree no longer lets UART2 win the console over UART5 (#1979)

PR #2485 fixed the TF-A/BL32 half of #1979 only (the console UART base
+ pinmux hardcoded to the Alif DevKit's UART2 in
`trusted-firmware-a_%.bbappend`). This fragment adds the Linux-side
half the same issue describes: Alif's `devkit_ex_dct_defines.h`
hardcodes `UART2_STATUS "okay"`, so `serial@4901a000` (UART2)
enumerates as `ttyS0` and takes `console=ttyS0` regardless of what
`aliases { serial0 = ...; }` names — the 8250 driver assigns `ttySN`
by probe order, not by the DT alias. The E1M-AEN EVK (E1M-AEN801/
E1M-AEN701 share one carrier PCB) does not bring UART2 out; its real
console header is SoC UART5 (`serial@4901d000`, `P3_4`/`P3_5`,
alternate function 2).

New `meta-alp-sdk/dynamic-layers/meta-alif-ensemble/recipes-kernel/linux/linux-alif/e1m-aen-evk-console.dtsi`
(`meta-alp-sdk/dynamic-layers/meta-alif-ensemble/recipes-kernel/linux/linux-alif/e1m-aen-evk-console.dtsi:34`
("&uart2 {")) disables `&uart2`, enables `&uart5`, sets
`aliases { serial0 = &uart5; }`, and `chosen { stdout-path =
"serial0:115200n8"; }`. New
`meta-alp-sdk/dynamic-layers/meta-alif-ensemble/recipes-kernel/linux/linux-alif_%.bbappend`
(`meta-alp-sdk/dynamic-layers/meta-alif-ensemble/recipes-kernel/linux/linux-alif_%.bbappend:32`
("SRC_URI:append:e1m-aen801 = \" file://e1m-aen-evk-console.dtsi\"")) gates
the fragment on `:e1m-aen801`/`:e1m-aen701`, mirroring the TF-A
bbappend's per-carrier knobs.

**INERT TODAY, same reason as the TF-A half.** No Scarthgap
`meta-alif-ensemble` exists publicly (#1968), and even the one public
branch (`devkit-ex-b0`) is Scarthgap-incompatible (#1971), so neither
`MACHINE=e1m-aen801-a32` nor `e1m-aen701-a32` parses. There is no
`linux-alif` recipe in any layer on `bblayers.conf` for this bbappend
to attach to, so it never runs, and `KERNEL_DEVICETREE` in
`e1m-aen801-a32.conf`/`e1m-aen701-a32.conf` is itself still
`# TBD(alif-hw-config)` — no board dts exists yet to `#include` this
fragment from.

**Verification is static only, and incomplete.** `dtc` is not
installed in this environment
(`which dtc` exits non-zero), and no vendor devkit-e8/-e7 dts is
vendored in this tree, so the fragment could not be compiled against a
real base — a brace-balance check (`{` == `}`) is the only mechanical
check run. `&uart2`/`&uart5` are the conventional lowercase node
labels (matching `e1m-x-evk.dtsi`'s own `serial0 = &scif;` idiom for
the V2N side) but are NOT confirmed against a real vendor dtsi, which
does not exist publicly yet (#1968, #1971) — the fragment's own header
comment flags this and says a wrong label fails loudly at `dtc` time,
not silently. Confirm both labels once a Scarthgap `linux-alif` recipe
lands before relying on this fragment.

### Fixed — the generated board header defined an address macro for I2C parts that are not on the board (#1980)

`scripts/gen_board_header.py` never read the `assembled` key #1977 added to
`i2c_device_entry` (`metadata/schemas/board-preset.schema.json:389-392`), so
every `i2c_devices:` entry got a plain `#define EVK_I2C_ADDR_<NAME> 0x..u`
regardless of whether the part is actually fitted. On the E1M-EVK, U37 (the
PCIe I/O expander) is `assembled: false` (`metadata/boards/e1m-evk.yaml:295`)
— confirmed absent on both bench boards and from the maintainer's I2C
schedule (`changelog.d`'s own #1974 entry) — but the header still defined
`EVK_I2C_ADDR_TCAL9538_PCIE 0x71u` as if it were real. Firmware that reads
"the header defines an address" as "the part is there" would address
silicon that does not exist and get a clean `-EIO`.

**Decision: rename, don't delete or guard.** Deleting the macro breaks any
existing caller at compile time with no explanation, and #1977 kept the
entry rather than deleting it because the footprint is real and other
revisions populate it — the same is true one row down:
`EVK_I2C_ADDR_TCA6408A_MAIN` (`metadata/boards/e1m-evk.yaml:297`) is the
*alternate* population of the same U35 footprint, bench-confirmed on an
earlier EVK revision and a clean NACK on both current boards, and is now
ALSO marked `assembled: false` here (leaving it plain would be the exact
class this fix exists to close). `examples/peripheral-io/i2c-device-hub/src/main.c` already and
correctly probes it at runtime alongside `EVK_I2C_ADDR_TCAL9538_MAIN` as a
legitimate cross-revision fallback, so its caller now spells the renamed
`EVK_I2C_ADDR_TCA6408A_MAIN_NOT_ASSEMBLED` macro. A compile-time `#if 0`
guard or outright omission would make that fallback pattern impossible to
write for a newly-unfitted part without hand-editing a generated file. So
`_emit_i2c_devices()` (`scripts/gen_board_header.py`) now renames every
macro an `assembled: false` entry contributes — address, `alias`, and any
`calibration` shunt/max-current pair — with a `_NOT_ASSEMBLED` suffix via
the new `_tag()` helper (`scripts/gen_board_header.py`) rather than
emitting the plain name. The plain name a reader would reach for out
of habit is no longer defined at all, so accidental use is a compile error
instead of a silent bus probe against nonexistent silicon; the address and
the `doc:` reason both survive under the renamed macro for anyone who
deliberately wants to probe for an earlier/other revision's population.

**Naming, unresolved:** issue #1980 itself flagged three candidate suffixes
as "worth a decision rather than assuming" and suggested `_NOT_FITTED`.
This change keeps `_NOT_ASSEMBLED` (it matches the `assembled:` key name
directly, and the doc-comment prose #1974/#1977 already wrote), but that
choice was made unilaterally, not by the maintainer — flagging it here so
it can still be revisited before the macro name ships in a release.

A second consumer of `assembled` had the same bug in a different shape:
`scripts/alp_orchestrate/slugs.py`'s `_slugs_from_on_module()` (feeding

### Fixed — `aen_atoc.py` rejected every valid Cortex-A32 boot config (#1981)

`scripts/aen_atoc.py`'s `SLOT0_WINDOWS` (the #1069 slot0-XIP window guard)
only recognised `cpu_id` values `M55_HE`/`M55_HP`, so any `mramAddress` ATOC
entry declaring `cpu_id: "A32_0"` — what the Alif Secure Enclave requires for
an A32 Linux boot chain — raised `AtocValidationError` unconditionally. No
in-tree flash path could stage an A32 Linux image. The rejected config is the
one #1981 reproduces: a `BOOTLOAD` (TF-A BL32) entry at `cpu_id A32_0`, boot
address `0x80002000`, plus an `A32_APP` kernel entry — the shape Alif's own
APSS application note specifies for an A32 Linux chain.

**The `0x80002000` floor is NOT verified on silicon in this tree, and this
change does not claim it is.** It is taken from that application-note config,
which is the only source for it here: nothing under `docs/` or
`metadata/e1m_modules/` carries the address, `docs/test-plan.md` has no A32 row,
and #1972 — the issue that owns this work — says in its own words that it
"tracks the first-light boot" and defers everything downstream until "a kernel
banner has been read on this silicon". Linux has not been booted on the A32
cluster of any AEN module. Note also that `0x80002000` falls INSIDE the `mcuboot`
region every AEN preset declares (`{ base: 0x80000000, size_kib: 64 }`), 8 KiB
in — consistent with an A32 chain the Secure Enclave boots directly without
MCUboot, but a real overlap a reader should see rather than discover. Confirming
the floor against a Secure Enclave boot table on real silicon is **bench-owed**
and belongs to #1972's first-light boot. Until that happens the floor is a
documented assumption, and the guard is no tighter than that assumption.

Added an `A32_0` window, floor `0x80002000` (that application-note `BOOTLOAD`
boot address) through `0x80578000` (5592 KiB) — the base of the SE-owned
`atoc` band, verbatim from every AEN preset's `memory_map:` `atoc` region
(`metadata/e1m_modules/E1M-AEN801.yaml`, `E1M-AEN803.yaml`, and five other
AEN SKUs, all `{ base: 0x80578000, size_kib: 32 }`). This is a fixed
reservation band, not the true per-build ceiling — the signed ATOC's own
start address moves with ATOC package size (SETOOLS
`build/app-package-map.txt`) and this module has no per-build input to
re-derive it — the same #1289/#1482 decision `scripts/check_atoc_reservation.py`
already enforces for every other AEN partition table: never derive the exact
ATOC start, reserve a band whose base is a committed static value instead.
An earlier version of this window used the raw System MRAM end
(`0x80580000`) as its ceiling instead of the atoc band's base, which
silently accepted an `A32_0` `mramAddress` entry anywhere inside that 32 KiB
SE-owned band — exactly the vacuous-hardcode shape
`check_atoc_reservation.py`'s own docstring warns against. `SLOT0_WINDOWS`'s
ceiling is now derived from that band's size rather than hand-copied, and
`check_atoc_reservation.py` gained a fourth check asserting every
`SLOT0_WINDOWS` ceiling stays at or below each preset's `atoc` band base, so
this specific regression can't recur unnoticed.

An A32 Linux chain's `mramAddress` span runs from TF-A BL32 through the
kernel and so covers **both** M55 windows entirely — the A32 window above is
not a third disjoint slice, it deliberately overlaps the M55 ones.
`validate_atoc_entries()` therefore also rejects any config mixing an
`A32_0` `mramAddress` entry with an `M55_HE`/`M55_HP` `mramAddress` entry
(mixing them would stage an M55 slot0 image into memory the A32 chain is
executing from); `loadAddress` (ITCM) M55 stub entries — the shape the
issue's own example config uses for its `HP_APP`/`HE_APP` stubs — stay
exempt, as before. That mutual-exclusivity check only fires when an M55
`mramAddress` entry is present alongside an A32 one; a **pure** A32-only
config (the shipped shape) is constrained by the window bounds alone, not by
that check — worth stating plainly, since an earlier version of this
module's own comment claimed the opposite.

Fixed a second, sibling defect this window addition exposed in
`scripts/west_commands/runners/alif_flash.py::_select_app_shape()`: its
`vector_suffix = 'HE' if vector_cpu_id == 'M55_HE' else 'HP'` ternary assumed
`SLOT0_WINDOWS` held exactly two keys. With `A32_0` added, a reset vector
landing in the sliver above the old `M55_HP` ceiling (`0x80550000..0x80578000`,
inside the `A32_0` window but outside both real M55 windows) would have
silently matched `A32_0`, fallen into the `else` branch, and been mis-staged
to burn at `M55_HP`'s window base (`0x802b0000`) — a wrong address. An
earlier version of this fix special-cased `A32_0` to reject it with a
message claiming the address was "staged by a different flash path" — a
regression in its own right: this runner is Zephyr `west flash`-only and
never legitimately stages an A32 image, so a genuine M55 mis-link landing
in that sliver (e.g. `0x80560000`) got a misleading "nothing to see here"
message instead of the correct refusal. `_select_app_shape()` now excludes
`A32_0` from its window lookup entirely, so any reset vector outside the two
real M55 windows gets the plain "outside every declared slot0 window —
refusing to burn" diagnostic.

Also fixed: the mutual-exclusivity check itself tested `cpu_id != 'A32_0'`
to decide "is this an M55 entry", which would mislabel a future second
A32-cluster key (the Alif E8's A32 cluster is dual-core) as an M55 entry and
wrongly trip mutual exclusion against `A32_0`. It now tests membership
against an explicit `{M55_HE, M55_HP}` set instead.

### Fixed — the orchestrator no longer emits `bitbake alp-image-edge` for a MACHINE that cannot build (#1982)

Five SoM presets declare the A32 cluster's stock app as the `STOCK_IMAGE_APP` token
(`alp-image-edge`): `metadata/e1m_modules/E1M-AEN{501,601,701,801,803}.yaml`. Every one of them,
`scripts/alp_orchestrate/orchestrator.py` turned straight into a `bitbake alp-image-edge` /
`MACHINE = "<machine>"` build-plan command — silently, because the stock-image token is
deliberately exempt from the `recipe:` requirement that would otherwise flag an app-only Yocto
slice. All five MACHINEs are known-non-buildable, split into two failure classes (do not conflate
them): `e1m-aen801-a32` / `e1m-aen701-a32` ship a `meta-alp-sdk/conf/machine/*.conf` whose `require`
is either broken (#1968: names a file absent from every branch of the public meta-alif-ensemble) or
commented out pending that layer being vendored at all; `e1m-aen501-a32` / `e1m-aen601-a32` /
`e1m-aen803-a32` ship **no conf at all**, strictly more unbuildable since BitBake fails before it
can parse a single `require`. All five sit on a meta-alif-ensemble base that is Yocto-series-
incompatible with this repo's Scarthgap baseline regardless (#1971) — so every project naming any
of these five SoMs' A32 cluster received a confidently-emitted command that could not have
succeeded. E1M-AEN803 is the bench module #1982 itself names.

`_slice_command` now refuses all five MACHINEs before considering `image:`/`app:`/`recipe:` at
all, raising a new `UnbuildableYoctoMachineError` that `emit_build_plan` turns into a
`command: null` slice plus a `yocto-machine-unbuildable` warning naming the blocking issues and
#264 — the same "carry the slice, never emit a broken command" convention `board-tree-missing`
and `command-unrooted` already use. The `STOCK_IMAGE_APP` exemption comment now says explicitly
that it assumes the image recipe is buildable for the slice's MACHINE. A new CI gate,
`scripts/check_yocto_machine_tree_parity.py`, consults this SAME denylist (`YOCTO_MACHINE_UNBUILDABLE`)
so a `machine:` with no conf and no denylist entry can never fall through undeclared. It is
modelled on — but is deliberately NOT the full self-cleaning mirror of —
`check_board_target_tree_parity.py` (issue #999): it is a one-way absence check only, since a
shipped `.conf` is weaker proof of buildability than a resolving Zephyr `board.yml` (both
`e1m-aen801-a32.conf` and `e1m-aen701-a32.conf` exist and are still unbuildable). Removing an entry
once its MACHINE genuinely resolves stays a human call; see the gate's own module docstring for the
full division of labour.

The two `tests/parity/oracle/*.build-plan.json` fixtures affected (`multicore_rpmsg-aen`,
`audio_i2s-tone`, both via `E1M-AEN801`) are re-frozen at their `a32_cluster` slice's `command` ->
`null` plus the new warning — the same class of hand-reviewed oracle correction alp-sdk#999 made
for `board-tree-missing`, recorded in `tests/parity/oracle/ORACLE-PROVENANCE.txt` — rather than a
seam-1 comparator allowance, per ADR-0020's own post-mortem of why that shortcut is the failure
mode to avoid. Every emit-snapshot fixture and unit test whose plan included an AEN801 A32-cluster
slice (no shipped example uses the other four SKUs) was regenerated/updated to reflect the new
`command: null` + warning shape.

**Refs #1982, does not close it.** This stops the planner from handing out a command it already
knows cannot succeed — it does **not** close #1968 or #1971 (the underlying layer/machine-conf
defects, owned by #264's rebuild), and it does not touch #1982's other, bench-gated half: an A32
target this small still gets `IMAGE_ROOTFS_EXTRA_SPACE`/`IMAGE_ROOTFS_SIZE` sized for hardware it
isn't (`meta-alp-sdk/recipes-images/alp-image-common.inc:183-184`), tracked behind #1970/#1973.

**tan-cli is out of sync until tan-cli#1223 lands.** `tan-cli`'s vendored copies of
`tests/parity/oracle/multicore_rpmsg-aen.build-plan.json` and `audio_i2s-tone.build-plan.json` still
carry the pre-fix `bitbake alp-image-edge` shape with no warning, and `tan-cli`'s own planner
(`python/tan/planner/buildplan.py`) has no `YOCTO_MACHINE_UNBUILDABLE` port at all — so `tan build`
still hands out the doomed command for all five AEN A32 SKUs until that issue's re-vendor + port
lands. This alp-sdk change alone does not make `tan build` honest about it.

### Fixed — `cc3501e_wifi_ap_start()`'s role-confirmation loop now bounds by wall time, not a manual sleep-only budget (part of #1985)

Follow-up to #1953, which fixed the identical antipattern in
`poll_by_repeat()` (`chips/cc3501e/cc3501e_core.c`) but deferred two call
sites that ran the same pre-fix shape. This lands one of the two:
`cc3501e_wifi_ap_start()`'s GET_DIAG_INFO role-confirm loop in
`chips/cc3501e/cc3501e_wifi.c`. The loop tracked a `uint32_t remaining`
budget by hand: a successful-but-not-yet-AP read debited only the 50 ms
`CC3501E_WIFI_STATUS_POLL_GAP_MS` gap it slept for, and a *failed* read
debited a defensive ESTIMATE of the attempt's worst-case cost
(`CC3501E_REQ_TMO_MS`, 100 ms) instead of what the attempt actually took —
`cc3501e_request()` does not itself bound an attempt to `CC3501E_REQ_TMO_MS`,
so nothing capped how long a genuinely hung attempt could run. Same false "a
read either costs nothing or costs its declared worst case" premise #1953
disproved for `poll_by_repeat()` itself.

**Converted to the `alp_uptime_ms()`-deadline shape** `poll_by_repeat()`
already uses: a deadline read once at entry (`alp_uptime_ms() + timeout_ms`),
a real-time check after every attempt (`now_ms >= deadline_ms`), and the
final back-off gap clamped to whatever's left before the deadline — no more
`attempt_cost` estimate. The loop keeps its existing fixed 50 ms cadence
(`CC3501E_WIFI_STATUS_POLL_GAP_MS`); it did not grow the exponential
back-off `poll_by_repeat()` itself uses, since that constant already existed
specifically to duplicate `poll_by_repeat()`'s cadence for a *different*
opcode (GET_DIAG_INFO) than the one it bounds (WIFI_AP_START).

**Quantified, not just asserted, what changes:** the old manual accounting
deliberately over-charged every failing iteration relative to real wall
time — 100 ms phantom `attempt_cost` plus the real 50 ms gap = 150 ms
debited per iteration, against the ~50 ms that (in this repo's own
fake-clock host harness, where a failed attempt costs 0 simulated time)
actually elapsed — so it converged to `ALP_ERR_TIMEOUT` faster than real
time, making fewer GET_DIAG_INFO attempts than a real deadline permits for
the same declared `timeout_ms` against a permanently wedged transport.
Measured directly (both directions of a mutation test: the converted loop
reverted to its pre-fix shape, run, then restored) against
`tests/zephyr/cc3501e_host_driver`'s fake-clock harness, `timeout_ms = 200`,
`CC3501E_REQ_TMO_MS = 100`, gap = 50 ms:

| | GET_DIAG_INFO attempts | budget accounted per iteration |
|---|---|---|
| pre-fix (manual `remaining -=`) | 2 | 150 ms (100 ms phantom + 50 ms real) |
| post-fix (`alp_uptime_ms()` deadline) | 5 | 50 ms (real gap only) |

This loop makes no read before entering the loop, so the post-fix count has
a clean closed form: exactly `ceil(timeout_ms /
CC3501E_WIFI_STATUS_POLL_GAP_MS) + 1` every time (200 -> 5, 10000 -> 201).
This does not change how long `timeout_ms` bounds the call to (both models
still return `ALP_ERR_TIMEOUT` no later than the caller's declared budget),
only how many GET_DIAG_INFO frames land on the wire while getting there.

**No accounting difference on a healthy poll:** the pre-fix code already
charged a successful-but-non-AP read nothing extra, and the deadline model
preserves that — a healthy multi-poll AP role-up still spends only its real
gap time either way.

**Tests:** added `test_wifi_ap_start_bounds_diag_attempts_on_wedged_
transport_1985` to `tests/zephyr/cc3501e_host_driver/src/test_host_driver.c`,
against a new `g_diag_io_down_remaining` / `slave.diag_info_attempt_count`
fixture pair (the GET_DIAG_INFO analogue of the existing
`g_status_io_down_remaining` / `slave.wifi_status_attempt_count` used for
WIFI_STATUS), asserting the exact `== 5u`. Mutation-proven: reverting the
loop to its pre-fix `remaining -=`/`attempt_cost` shape drops the count to
2 and reddens the assertion; restoring the fix turns it green again at 5.

**`cc3501e_wifi_connect()`'s identical WIFI_STATUS antipattern is NOT
touched by this change** — it was converted separately, on real
E1M-AEN801 silicon, on `feat/2035-cc3501e-wedge-and-throughput` (merged to
`dev` as part of #2035, PR #2050). That conversion uses a different shape
than this one: an `elapsed_ms` accumulator that only ever grows by the poll
gap actually slept, rather than this change's `alp_uptime_ms()` deadline —
`cc3501e_wifi_connect()`'s own comment explains the choice. Both shapes hit
the same category of off-by-one (an unconditional pre-loop read that adds
one to the closed form): this file's independent derivation for the
ap_start case first predicted 5 attempts and confirmed it by test; the
connect-side derivation predicted 5 before its own run corrected it to 6.
Both #1953-deferred call sites are now converted; #1985 tracked exactly
these two.

**Bench-owed:** this touches `chips/cc3501e/cc3501e_wifi.c`, held per #1937.
The CC3501E is activated only on one AEN EVK bench place, which is not among the
boards reservable for this work this session — no silicon measurement backs
the attempt-count table above, which is native_sim / host-harness only, same
caveat #1953 already carries for `poll_by_repeat()` itself.

### Fixed — `cores.<id>.app:` no longer crashes the orchestrator on an unresolvable path (#1987)

`scripts/alp_orchestrate/orchestrator.py` resolved a user-supplied
`cores.<id>.app:` with a bare `(Path(base_dir) / p).resolve()`, and
`_zephyr_app_dir()` then called `.is_file()` twice on the result with no
`try` at all. That is the third instance of the antipattern #1961 closed
for `extra_libraries.<name>.profile:` in `validate.py` and for the
`--input` board.yaml in `loader.py`: a `board.yaml` whose `app:` reaches
a symlink loop crashes the CLI with an unhandled exception instead of a
clean `OrchestratorError`.

All three call sites now catch `(OSError, RuntimeError)` and re-raise
`OrchestratorError` naming the offending `app:` value.

Both platform shapes are covered, because they are genuinely different
and one test cannot see both:

* POSIX -- a symlink loop makes `Path.resolve()` raise `RuntimeError`
  (ELOOP).
* Windows -- `.resolve()` returns *without* raising and `.is_file()`
  raises a plain `OSError` (`WinError 1920`, "The file cannot be
  accessed by the system"), which is neither `RuntimeError` nor
  `PermissionError`.

Mutation-proven, one mutant per guard, each killed by exactly one test:

* deleting the `try`/`except` around `_resolve_app_path()`'s `.resolve()`
  fails `test_resolve_app_path_posix_symlink_loop_clean_error` with the
  raw `RuntimeError` escaping, and leaves the Windows test green;
* narrowing `_zephyr_app_dir()`'s first `except (OSError, RuntimeError)`
  back to `(RuntimeError, PermissionError)` fails
  `test_zephyr_app_dir_windows_symlink_loop_clean_error` with
  `OSError: [WinError 1920] The file cannot be accessed by the system`,
  and leaves the POSIX test green.

Closes #1987.

### Fixed — the RTC-alarm port-15 register-layout warning was family-scoped, not part-scoped, and would have misdirected non-E8 AEN SKUs (#1988)

`metadata/e1m_modules/aen/on-module-links.yaml` carries `families: [aen]` —
it is the single on-module-pad authority shared
by every AEN SKU (E1M-AEN301/401/501/601/701/801/803). Its `rtc_alarm.risk`
string, though, was evidenced against exactly one document:
`metadata/e1m_modules/aen/on-module-links.yaml:255` ("The AE822 DFP warns for port 15").
AE822 is the E8's own part number — there is no citation against the
E3/E4/E6/E7 DFPs, and `scripts/gen_zephyr_board.py`'s `_aen_brd_i2c_dts()`
(`scripts/gen_zephyr_board.py:1300` ("def _aen_brd_i2c_dts")) emitted that
string into every AEN SKU's generated `.dts` unconditionally — the function
took no part parameter at all.

Nothing had shipped wrong yet only because every non-E8 AEN SKU is refused
earlier in the pipeline, for one of two reasons. E1M-AEN301, E1M-AEN501 and
E1M-AEN701 (E3/E5/E7) are driven out at `_board_naming()`: none of their SoC
JSONs' `m55_hp`/`m55_he` core entries declares `zephyr_cpucluster` at all, so
board naming itself raises before this code is ever reached. E1M-AEN401 and
E1M-AEN601 (E4/E6) clear that guard but are then refused by
`_aen_peripherals_dtsi()`, since neither `e4.json` nor `e6.json` declares
`zephyr_peripherals_dtsi`. Either way, none of the five reaches this code
path today. The moment any of E3/E4/E5/E6/E7 clears its own guard, its
generated devicetree would carry AE822-specific register-layout guidance for
silicon whose port-15 layout was never checked — actively misdirecting a
bring-up engineer toward suspecting the wrong register on a fault they
cannot attribute to that DFP.

Fixed by scoping the DATA, not by hardcoding a part check in the generator:
`rtc_alarm.risk` is now a map keyed by the SoC's own `part` designator
(`metadata/e1m_modules/aen/on-module-links.yaml:247` ("Keyed by the SoC"))
with a single `E8:` entry carrying the existing AE822 text.
`_aen_brd_i2c_dts()` now takes `part` and looks up `risk.get(part)`
(`scripts/gen_zephyr_board.py:1360` ("risk_text = (alarm.get(")) — a part
with no entry gets no risk paragraph at all, silence rather than a hedged
restatement, because no DFP has been checked for it. `docs/soms/aen.md`'s
own prose already scoped this section "E1M-AEN801 only", so no doc change
was needed there — only the generator was unconditional.

`tests/scripts/test_gen_zephyr_board.py`'s
`test_rtc_alarm_risk_is_scoped_to_the_part_it_was_evidenced_against` forces
E1M-AEN801 down this same emit path with its SoC JSON's `part` mutated to
`E4` (the narrowest stand-in for onboarding E1M-AEN401, which is refused
earlier for lacking `zephyr_peripherals_dtsi`) and asserts the AE822 sentence
is absent from that `.dts` while still present in the genuine, unmutated
E1M-AEN801 build. Every committed AEN board file is byte-identical after
this change (E1M-AEN801 is genuinely E8, so its own generated `.dts` is
unaffected). `_load_aen_on_module_links()` also now shape-checks
`rtc_alarm.risk` itself (a bare string, the pre-#1988 shape, used to reach
the `.get(part)` lookup and crash with an uncaught `AttributeError` instead
of the file-naming `ZephyrBoardEmitError` its sibling checks already raise).

NOT closed by this fix: the SAME family-vs-part shape survives, unattributed,
in `_aen_i2c_pinctrl_group()`'s "Alif's own DFP sets PADCTRL_READ_ENABLE on
{sda} AND {scl}" comment
(`scripts/gen_zephyr_board.py:1162` ("Alif's own DFP sets")) — it is
evidenced only against the AE822 DFP but is emitted into
every AEN SKU's `-pinctrl.dtsi` unconditionally, taking no `part` parameter
at all. `test_part_designator_is_read_from_the_soc_json` now also asserts
`"AE822 DFP"` is absent from a part-mutated board (pinning the CLASS, not
just the one string this fix scopes), so this residue will fail loudly the
day a non-E8 board is onboarded rather than silently inheriting E8 wording;
scoping the pinctrl comment itself is left as a follow-up.

### Fixed — five AEN SoM presets still declared the OSPI0 NOR/HyperRAM chip-selects inverted, and the schema let a stray chip-select value through silently (#1990)

Auditing the `ospi_memories:`/`hyperram:` scaffold question for #1944 turned
up a real hardware-fact bug: `metadata/e1m_modules/E1M-AEN301.yaml`,
`E1M-AEN401.yaml`, `E1M-AEN501.yaml`, `E1M-AEN601.yaml` and
`E1M-AEN701.yaml` all still had `ospi_memories.ospi0.chip_select: 0` (NOR)
and `hyperram.chip_select: 1` (HyperRAM) — exactly the inverted mapping
that `E1M-AEN801.yaml` (and `E1M-AEN803.yaml`) already document as
corrected: the shared E1M-AEN-2626-R2 netlist routes U9 (the RAM footprint)
to `OSPI0_SS0` (CS0) and U10 (the NOR footprint) to `OSPI0_SS1` (CS1), and
per the family's own `metadata/e1m_modules/aen/CHANGELOG.md` invariant
("all AENs have the same revision, only SoC changes") every AEN SKU ships
one shared module PCB, so the corrected mapping applies family-wide, not
only to the SKU where it was first caught. Fixed to `ospi0.chip_select: 1`
/ `hyperram.chip_select: 0` on all five, with the same corrected-mapping
comment `E1M-AEN801.yaml` carries. `chip_select` on these blocks has no
generator consumer today (`scripts/alp_orchestrate/*` reads
`ospi_memories`/`hyperram` for capacity and key presence, not
`chip_select`), so this is a metadata correctness fix with no generated-file
fallout, not a behaviour change.

**Bench-owed.** The corrected `chip_select` mapping is not an electrical
measurement on E1M-AEN301/401/501/601/701 silicon — it is inferred from
the E1M-AEN-2626-R2 netlist notes recorded against E1M-AEN801/E1M-AEN803
plus the family's "one shared PCB" invariant. That inference is strong
(one PCB, one netlist; the U9/U10 footprints don't move with SoC tier or
population) but nobody has probed OSPI0_SS0/OSPI0_SS1 on E3–E7 silicon to
confirm it.

The same audit found the five presets' `hyperram:` blocks omitted
`assembled:` entirely — the exact key `som-preset-v2.schema.json`'s own
description calls "load-bearing" (defaults `true`, and E1M-AEN801 is on
record for advertising 256 Mbit of external RAM it does not populate
because of this same omission). This fragment's first pass made it
explicit as `assembled: true`, citing each file's own `memory.dram_mbit`
derivation comment ("populated on every AEN BOM variant") as the source.
Round-2 review caught that this is the same boilerplate comment present
verbatim in `E1M-AEN801.yaml`, whose own HyperRAM is `assembled: false` —
so it falsifies the claim for at least one family member and cannot stand
as evidence either way for E3–E7. No BOM, netlist, or bench measurement
backs `true` on these five, so it is now `assembled: optional` (the same
per-BOM-variant shape as `ospi0` above), with `memory.dram_mbit`
correspondingly `TBD`, not `256`. `E1M-AEN803.yaml`'s `hyperram:` — left
with `assembled:` omitted entirely by this fragment's first pass, the very
antipattern the fix targets — is now explicit `assembled: true`, sourced
from that file's own header ("both parts fitted ... IS the E1M-AEN803 SKU
contract").

**A stray value would have passed every gate anyway.** `chip_select` was
`{"type": "integer", "minimum": 0}` with no upper bound, on a bus that only
ever wires two chip-select lines (`OSPI0_SS0`/`OSPI0_SS1` — no shipped
preset, including `E1M-AEN803.yaml`'s 2-CS OSPI0 controller, ever declares
a third). Setting `chip_select: 9` on `E1M-AEN803.yaml` and re-running
`validate_metadata.py` left every check green. Added
`"maximum": 1` to both `$defs/ospi_memory.chip_select` and
`$defs/hyperram.chip_select` in `metadata/schemas/som-preset-v2.schema.json`,
and `tests/scripts/test_ospi_chip_select_bound.py` to pin the boundary (0/1
accepted, 2/9 rejected) so the next typo fails schema validation instead of
shipping silently.

### Added — a gate requiring a changelog.d/ hex/serial silicon claim to be corroborated outside the fragment (#1993)

On 2026-09-05 `changelog.d/1981.md` shipped "Bench-verified on two
E1M-AEN803 modules on 2026-09-05: the Secure Enclave's own boot table
booted `BOOTLOAD` (TF-A BL32) at `cpu_id A32_0`, boot address
`0x80002000`, flags `u VB`." None of it happened: no such bench session
ran, no AEN803 module is on any bench, and `0x80002000` was carried over
verbatim from an Alif application-note config, not measured. The
identical fabricated sentence was also the sole comment justifying
`0x80002000` as a production constant in `scripts/aen_atoc.py`'s
`SLOT0_WINDOWS`, and reached two issue bodies besides.
`check_changelog_citations.py`, `check_atoc_reservation.py`,
`validate_metadata.py`, `check_doc_drift.py` and the ATOC pytest suite
were all green throughout — none of them ask whether a hardware claim is
true. Withdrawn in `b1de21838` and `5597f8265` (see #1991).

`scripts/check_silicon_claim_provenance.py` closes the one piece of this
that is mechanically checkable: a `changelog.d/*.md` sentence asserting
bench/silicon verification ("bench-verified", "bench-proven",
"bench-measured", "measured on", "confirmed on N of N", "silicon-verified",
"verified on silicon") that also names a concrete hex address or a
`YYYYWnn-nnnn` bench-serial token must have that literal value appear
somewhere under `docs/` or `metadata/` outside `changelog.d/` — the exact
standard the retraction commit itself applied ("the address appears
nowhere else in the tree — not in docs/, not in metadata/e1m_modules/, not
in docs/test-plan.md"). A sentence carrying an explicit negation ("not",
"never", "unverified", ...) is read as a disclaimer, not a claim, and is
exempt — the withdrawn fragment's own "NOT verified on silicon" text next
to the same address stays green. Deliberately, a second copy of the value
in `scripts/*.py` / `chips/**` / `src/**` / `include/**` does NOT count as
corroboration: this incident planted the identical unsourced sentence in
`scripts/aen_atoc.py` at the same time as the changelog fragment, so
treating that as proof would have passed the real defect rather than
caught it.

This is narrower than a general "every bench claim needs a citation" gate
on purpose. That shape was tried against this tree first and flagged
roughly 20 of 24 existing, correctly-sourced changelog fragments — most
`changelog.d/` bench narratives have no matching `docs/test-plan.md` row
per issue number, and a claim with no hex/serial anchor at all
(`"Bench-verified on an AEN EVK bench unit: all four presets report radio_ok=1"`,
`changelog.d/1679.md`) is exactly this shape. That is the same
noisy-gate failure #1963 was rejected for, so this gate checks only the
hex/serial-anchored subset — the shape of the actual incident — and says
so in its own docstring, along with the rest of what it does not catch
(a claim with no anchor at all; a claim planted only in source-code
comments, never a changelog fragment; and that a corroborated value is
merely *sourced*, not *true* — the reviewer `inventedHardwareFacts`
verdict this issue also calls for is unaffected). `CHANGELOG.md` (a
byte-for-byte fold of `changelog.d/` via `assemble_changelog.py` — scanning
or corroborating against it would be circular) and `docs/superpowers/**`
(raw planning/session dumps, not a reviewed hardware record) are excluded
from both claim-scanning and corroboration.

Verified against the known-bad build first, per the debugging rule the
gate itself models: run against the tree at commit `b1de21838^` (the
fabricated text still present), the gate exits 1 and names
`changelog.d/1981.md` and `0x80002000`; run against the current tree, it
exits 0. `tests/scripts/test_check_silicon_claim_provenance.py` embeds
the actual shipped fragment text as a regression fixture rather than a
synthetic stand-in.

### Fixed — `scripts/test-all.sh` could never pass on Windows (#1995)

`bash scripts/test-all.sh` always failed its `[yocto-build-and-ctest]`
stage on a Windows host:

```
src/yocto/inference_drpai.cpp:117:10: fatal error: sys/ioctl.h: No such file or directory
[yocto-build-and-ctest] FAIL (exit=1)
```

`src/yocto/inference_drpai.cpp:115-118` hard-includes `<fcntl.h>`,
`<linux/drpai.h>`, `<sys/ioctl.h>` and `<unistd.h>`, and
`tests/yocto/CMakeLists.txt` compiled it into
`alp_test_inference_drpai_regression` on every host. `sys/ioctl.h` does
not exist on Windows, so the stage — and therefore the whole script —
could not go green there.

That block's own comment named the assumption behind it: "no platform
guard here beyond the one this whole `yocto` leg already implies (issue
#1747's CI gate runs on ubuntu-latest)". The implication holds for CI
and not for `test-all.sh`, which at
`scripts/test-all.sh:1621` ("--target dev (release-grade build)")
skips the yocto leg only for `--target dev` and otherwise runs it
wherever it is invoked.

This mattered beyond a cosmetic red. The repo's workflow is local-first
CI on **both** Windows and WSL; a stage that can never be green on one
of them trains the reader to treat its `FAIL` as noise, which is exactly
how a genuine failure in that stage would be waved through. It also made
a Windows run's `REAL_RC` useless as a single go/no-go signal.

The `alp_test_inference_drpai_regression` target is now defined only
when `CMAKE_SYSTEM_NAME STREQUAL "Linux"`. The target is guarded rather
than the whole leg on purpose: the sibling `alp_test_inference_ort_
regression` and `alp_test_inference_deepx_regression` targets are
host-portable and still build and run on Windows, so the leg keeps its
coverage there. On a non-Linux host CMake now prints a named skip
pointing at the ubuntu-latest job that does cover it, matching how
`[bash32-parse]` and the stage's own `zcbor not found` gap already
report themselves.

Verified on Windows 11 (MSYS2/Git Bash) at `2b9001176` + this change:
`cmake -B <dir> -S . -DALP_OS=yocto -DALP_BUILD_TESTS=ON -G "Unix
Makefiles"` configures with the skip message, `cmake --build` exits 0,
and `ctest --output-on-failure` reports `100% tests passed, 0 tests
failed out of 10` — the same stage that previously died at
`make: *** [Makefile:101: all] Error 2`.

### Fixed — `pr-plain-cmake` compiled `tests/**` without watching it (#1997)

`.github/workflows/pr-plain-cmake.yml` builds with `-DALP_BUILD_TESTS=ON`,
and `CMakeLists.txt:311` does `add_subdirectory(tests)` — so files under
`tests/` decide which targets that workflow compiles and which of its 54
ctest cases run. `tests/**` was not in either `paths:` block, so those
files could not trigger the workflow that exercises them.

Surfaced by #1996, which guards `alp_test_inference_drpai_regression`
behind `CMAKE_SYSTEM_NAME STREQUAL "Linux"` (so `scripts/test-all.sh` can
pass on Windows, #1995). That is exactly a change to which targets the
plain-CMake build produces, and `pr-plain-cmake` did not run on it at all;
the evidence that the target still builds on Linux exists only because the
run was dispatched by hand.

Two changes, because the path filter alone does not close the class:

* `tests/**` added to both `paths:` blocks, so the workflow runs.
* The `yocto backend + tests` job now asserts by name that
  `alp_test_inference_drpai_regression`,
  `alp_test_inference_ort_regression` and
  `alp_test_inference_deepx_regression` are still listed by `ctest -N`
  before running them.

The second matters because a vanished target is silent: CMake produces a
smaller build and ctest a shorter list, both exit 0, and nothing compares
either against an expectation — a guard that wrongly excludes a target on
the platform that owns it looks identical to a guard that works. Those
three are asserted because their definition is conditional; presence is
checked by name rather than by counting tests, so adding a test never
trips it. This is the same posture the `yocto-zcbor` leg already states
for its own `ALP_SDK_MODEL_ZCBOR_REQUIRED=ON` flag: fail loudly rather
than degrade quietly.

Verified in both directions. On Linux all three are present — run
`34021819100`, job `plain-cmake · yocto backend + tests`:
`Built target alp_test_inference_drpai_regression` and
`8/54 Test #8: alp_test_inference_drpai_regression ... Passed`. On a
Windows host, where `inference_drpai.cpp` cannot compile and #1996
deliberately drops the target, the same assertion reports
`MISSING: alp_test_inference_drpai_regression` and exits 1.

### Fixed — the provisioning example no longer records a real module under the wrong SKU (#2001)

`examples/aen/aen-eeprom-provision/` used the real allocated serial
`2026W36-0001` with `mfg 2026-09-04`, alongside `sku=E1M-AEN801` taken from the
example's own `board.yaml`. Both the command block and the expected-output
transcript did it, so the file read as a record that the module with that serial
had been provisioned as an `E1M-AEN801`.

It has not. **The maintainer confirmed the unit is an `E1M-AEN803`** — which is
what `changelog.d/1974.md:3`, `metadata/boards/e1m-evk.yaml:278` and
`src/zephyr/alp_banner.c:204` already say. Those three were corrected when #1977
landed; this example was the last place on `dev` still pairing that serial with
`E1M-AEN801`.

The SKU here is **not** changed to `E1M-AEN803`, deliberately. It comes from
`som.sku` in the example's `board.yaml`, and the per-example overlay filename is
required to be the fully-qualified Zephyr board id
(`alp_e1m_aen801_m55_he_ae822fa0e5597ls0_rtss_he.overlay`). No `E1M-AEN803`
board tree exists under `zephyr/boards/alp/` — only the SoM preset
`metadata/e1m_modules/E1M-AEN803.yaml` — so renaming the SKU would break the
example's build to fix a documentation defect.

Instead the unit identity is now `<SERIAL>` / `<MFG-DATE>`, which is what a
worked example should have carried in the first place: step 1 of the same README
already says *"The serial must come from the allocation ledger, not from your
head."*

**Bench-owed, and not claimed here:** whether the physical module was ever
actually written with `sku=E1M-AEN801` is unverified. The transcript was
illustrative, but if that provisioning run really happened against
`2026W36-0001`, its EEPROM holds the wrong SKU and `alp_banner.c` will print it.
Reading the manifest back off that unit settles it in one line; nothing in this
change asserts either way.

Closes #2001.

### Fixed — `sw_fallback` audio backend accepted and discarded any volume, and its #1648 regression test never called the entry point it guards (#2002)

`c19c3bc75` (#1790) closed #1648 tier 1 on the Yocto and Zephyr audio-out
backends: `alp_audio_out_set_volume()` now returns `ALP_ERR_NOSUPPORT`
instead of accepting a volume it can never apply. The fix did not reach
the third backend. `src/backends/audio/sw_fallback.c:161`
(`sw_out_set_volume`) discarded both arguments and returned `ALP_OK`
unconditionally — the exact accept-and-discard shape #1648 exists to
close. `sw_fallback` is a null sink (`out_write` discards every frame),
so unlike the Yocto/Zephyr siblings — which can scale `S16_LE` and only
refuse `S24_LE`/`S32_LE` — it can scale **no** format, so `include/alp/
audio.h:230-237`'s contract was false for every format on this backend,
not just 24/32-bit.

`sw_out_set_volume` now returns `ALP_OK` only for `vol == 255` (full
scale, a no-op on every format) and `ALP_ERR_NOSUPPORT` otherwise,
regardless of the open format.

Second, separate defect: `tests/unit/audio_volume_guard/src/
test_audio_volume_guard.c` was the only shipped regression test for
#1648, and it exercised `alp_audio_volume_settable()` — the extracted
guard predicate shared by the Yocto/Zephyr backends — but never any
backend's actual `out_set_volume`. Counted on `origin/dev`: 14 calls to
the guard, 0 to `alp_audio_out_set_volume()` or any backend's real op.
That circularity survives a backend forgetting to call the guard, a
backend passing the wrong format into it, the dispatcher discarding the
backend's return code, or (after this fix) `sw_out_set_volume`
regressing back to unconditional `ALP_OK` — each reintroduces #1648
exactly, and the old test would stay green through all of them.

The dispatcher's `alp_audio_out_open()` selects exactly one backend via
`alp_backend_select()` with no fallback, and `zephyr_drv` registers
unconditionally at priority 100 for the `"*"` wildcard
(`zephyr/CMakeLists.txt`) — so it always wins arbitration ahead of
`sw_fallback` (priority 0), and its own `out_open()` needs a real I2S
device or refuses outright. No live `alp_audio_out_t` handle backed by
`sw_fallback` is reachable through the public API on `native_sim`. The
test now fetches `sw_fallback`'s registered `out_set_volume` directly
from the backend registry (`alp_backend_select()` +
`alp_backend_select_next()`, the same pattern `tests/unit/
audio_registry` already uses) and calls that real function pointer —
the exact one `alp_audio_out_set_volume()` dispatches to — for
`S16_LE`/`S24_LE`/`S32_LE` at both refused and full-scale volumes,
asserting both the return code and that a refused call does not record
the requested volume.

Mutation-killed: reverting only `sw_out_set_volume`'s body to the old
`(void)state; (void)vol; return ALP_OK;` in an isolated copy of the tree
turns `test_sw_fallback_real_out_set_volume_refuses_non_unity_every_
format` red —
`Assertion failed ... test_audio_volume_guard.c:151: (rc not equal to
ALP_ERR_NOSUPPORT) format 0 vol 0: sw_fallback can scale nothing,
expected ALP_ERR_NOSUPPORT, got 0` — while the original guard-only tests
stay green, confirming they alone would have missed the regression.

Refs #1648.

### Added — `metadata/catalog.json` publishes each SoM's single-slot boot fact (#2004)

`scripts/alp_orchestrate/secure.py::_boot_target_is_single_slot` already
computed, per project, whether a target's MCUboot chain is single-slot
(no `slot1`/scratch partition to swap into) — but the answer was computed
in-process at `emit_sysbuild_conf` time and published nowhere. A consumer
outside this repo (the VS Code Configurator, via `tan`) had no way to
know a given SoM would reject `boot.swap_algorithm: move` until the build
itself raised `OrchestratorError`.

Every `soms[*]` entry in `metadata/catalog.json` now carries:

```json
"boot": {
  "single_slot": true,
  "default_swap_algorithm": "none",
  "allowed_swap_algorithms": []
}
```

(the second of the two shapes weighed in the issue — the resolved default
plus the legal set, not just the bare boolean). On a two-slot target this
reads `single_slot: false`, `default_swap_algorithm: "scratch"`,
`allowed_swap_algorithms: ["scratch", "move", "overwrite"]` — mirroring
`scripts/alp_orchestrate/secure.py:239-269`'s `swap_algorithm` →
`SB_CONFIG_MCUBOOT_MODE_*` mapping exactly, the sole owner of that rule.

**What the field means for a SoM, not just a project.** The real predicate
answers a per-project, per-core question (does THIS project's chosen
`m55_he`/`m55_hp` core have its own `<role>_slot0` region?), and a catalog
entry has no project, only a SoM preset. `scripts/gen_catalog.py`'s new
`_boot()` answers the SoM-level version of the same question: does EVERY
m55 role this SoM's own `topology:` declares have a `<role>_slot0`
`memory_map:` region? On the current corpus this is never a mixed answer —
each dual-M55 AEN SoM's preset declares disjoint `he_slot0`/`hp_slot0`
windows or neither (#1069/#1445) — so `single_slot` is never a lie by
omission. A `memory_map:` authored for one m55 role but not its sibling
would be a half-authored preset; `gen_zephyr_board._aen_role_slot0_map`
raises for that state instead of guessing, and `_boot()` checks EVERY
declared m55 role (not just the first, unlike `_boot_target_is_single_slot`'s
short-circuit) so a future half-authored preset fails the regen loudly
instead of resolving to an order-dependent answer.

**No second implementation of the predicate.** `_boot()` calls the SAME
`gen_zephyr_board._aen_role_slot0_map` resolver `_boot_target_is_single_slot`,
`_aen_dts`, `_aen_flash_partitions` and `loader._resolve_slot0_load_address`
already share — never a scan of `memory_map:` region names for the
substrings `slot1`/`scratch`, which `secure.py`'s own docstring documents
as disagreeing with the real resolver in general.

**Corpus result**, verified against a direct call into
`alp_orchestrate.secure._boot_target_is_single_slot` (not just re-derived):
single-slot — `E1M-AEN301`, `E1M-AEN401`, `E1M-AEN501`, `E1M-AEN601`,
`E1M-AEN701`, `E1M-AEN801`, `E1M-AEN803`; two-slot (no `m55_he`/`m55_hp`
core, so the predicate never fires and explicit `boot.swap_algorithm`
values are accepted) — `E1M-NX9101`, `E1M-V2M101`, `E1M-V2M102`,
`E1M-V2N101`, `E1M-V2N102`.

`metadata/catalog.json` carries no JSON Schema in `metadata/schemas/`
today (only `metadata/templates/catalog-v1.json` has one, a different
file) — none was extended, since none exists.

The downstream leg — `tan` forwarding this field to the extension — is
tracked separately; this closes only the SDK-side publication the issue
asked for.

### Fixed — carve-out refusal told the reader to make an edit it would still refuse (#2009)

`scripts/alp_orchestrate/carveout.py`'s IPC-eligibility refusal told the
reader to "Add a region whose resolved base sits outside the ... aperture
(or, if inside it, one that resolves `write_authority: customer_runtime`)".
The parenthetical was false: `_region_ipc_eligibility()`'s `cls == "flash"`
branch refuses a region CONTAINED in the SoC's declared on-die MRAM aperture
unconditionally — `write_authority` is consulted only on the unclassified
(outside-aperture) branch. A region inside the aperture could never be made
IPC-eligible by adding `write_authority: customer_runtime`, exactly what the
remedy instructed. `docs/board-config-features.md` carried the same
inversion in prose.

Both now say what actually unblocks the case: outside the aperture, and —
only for a region the SoM preset authors itself — carrying
`write_authority: customer_runtime`. A contained region is flash-class and
refused regardless of `write_authority`.

Re-baselined the four affected golden snapshots
(`tests/fixtures/emit-snapshots/{mproc-mailbox,rpmsg-aen}.{build-plan,system-manifest}.snap`)
— the reason text changed, `status: blocked` did not. Added
`TestContainedRegionWriteAuthorityNeverRescues` to
`tests/scripts/test_orchestrate_carveout_aperture_ordering.py`, pinning the
behaviour rather than the wording: a region matching the issue's exact
repro (contained, `write_authority: customer_runtime`) still refuses, a
`mram_main`-shaped end-to-end case simulating a customer following the old
remedy stays blocked, and a region matching the corrected remedy (outside
the aperture, preset-authored, `write_authority: customer_runtime`) does
resolve eligible.

Found by a post-merge review of #1983 (#1365 split B, merged as
`2fd045411`); the reviewed text moved and this repo has advanced since,
so file/line references in the original finding no longer match `dev`
verbatim.

### Fixed — pinned all 12 mutants that survived a post-merge review of #1365 split B, corrected a false size-precedence history and a false mutation-testing claim (#2010)

A mutation review of #1365 split B (#1983, merged as `2fd045411`) ran 30
mutants against `pytest tests/scripts/` plus `check_emit_snapshots.py`,
`check_atoc_reservation.py`, and `check_system_manifest.py`. 12 survived
(A8, A9, A10, M1, C3, C4, C6, C9, C11, C12, P1, P4). All 12 are closed here
— each with a new or extended test that goes red under the exact mutant and
green once reverted.

**`scripts/alp_orchestrate/memregion.py`'s `_region_size_bytes` (mutant M1)**
— the comment justified checking `size_kib` before `size_mib` as "matching
this module's one prior caller (`check_atoc_reservation.py`'s now-retired
`_region_size_kib`)". False: on `origin/dev` before split B, this module's
only two callers were `carveout.py` and `partition.py`, both mib-first via a
key-presence check (`if "size_mib" in region: ...`); `check_atoc_reservation.py`
was NOT a caller then — it carried its own private, unrelated
`_region_size_kib` (kib-first), which split B retired in favour of importing
this module. Restored mib-first precedence to match the module's real prior
behaviour and corrected the comment. The `memory_region` schema permits both
`size_mib` and `size_kib` on one region and no shipped preset sets both, so
this has no real-preset evidence either way — pinned by
`TestRegionExtent::test_size_mib_wins_when_both_fields_are_valid_ints`
(`{size_mib: 2, size_kib: 64}` must resolve via `size_mib`) rather than left
to change silently again.

**`scripts/alp_orchestrate/carveout.py`'s `_region_ipc_eligibility`
(mutant C4)** — `derived_eligible = wa == "customer_runtime"` dropped to
`= True` unconditionally survived every gate because
`TestUnclassifiedWriteAuthorityLegCoverage` was positive-only. Added
`test_outside_aperture_authored_row_with_wrong_write_authority_blocks` and
`..._with_no_write_authority_blocks`: an outside-aperture, preset-authored
row with `write_authority` anything other than `customer_runtime` (or
absent) must refuse — exactly the hazard the function's own docstring names,
"a future authored OSPI XIP row must NOT silently become an IPC candidate".
`changelog.d/1365-split-b.md` claimed this leg was "mutation-tested:
dropping it turns that test red" — true only for the opposite direction
(mutant C5, already killed); corrected that fragment in place.

**The other 10 mutants, by ID:**
- **C3 / C11** (`ram` leg of `_region_ipc_eligibility`) — likely
  UNREACHABLE on any SoM shipped today: `cls == "ram"` requires
  `not is_preset_authored`, but every Alif preset that resolves an aperture
  also authors an explicit `memory_map:` block, and no non-Alif SoM ever
  resolves an aperture at all (`git grep -n "carveout:" metadata/socs/` is
  empty). Kept, not deleted — a future minimal Alif SoM port relying
  entirely on SoC-level `memory_regions:` would reach it for real — and
  documented in place with the reachability precondition. Pinned by direct
  call (`TestRamLegReachability`), the only way to exercise it today.
- **C6** (unresolved-base ordering) — `carveout:` must be checked before
  `write_authority` (#1365 split B review MAJOR 2); no preset authors both
  fields on an unresolved-base row, so this was defensive-only and unpinned.
  `TestUnresolvedLegOrdering::test_unresolved_base_honours_carveout_false_over_customer_runtime`
  closes it with `{"base": "TBD", "carveout": False, "write_authority":
  "customer_runtime"}`.
- **C9** (`_MAX_EXCLUDED_DETAIL`, 6) — unpinned by any behavioural test;
  pinned directly (`TestMaxExcludedDetailCap`). The reasoning stands:
  `board.schema.json`'s `/$defs/ipc_entry` sets `endpoints.minItems: 2`, and
  every AEN SKU's `memory_map:` has exactly 7 rows, so 5 is the true
  ceiling on any SKU shipped today.
- **C12** (terminal ADR-0034 clause-4 refusal) — one direct-call assertion
  (`TestUnresolvedLegOrdering::test_unresolved_base_with_neither_flag_refuses_terminal`).
- **A8** (`is_partition_inside_aperture`'s low-edge boundary,
  `lo >= full_lo` vs `lo > full_lo`) — untested and live: `mcuboot` is flush
  with the aperture base on all 7 AEN SKUs. Added
  `test_true_for_a_proper_subset_flush_with_the_low_edge`.
- **A9** (`resolve_aperture`'s `isinstance(base, bool)` guard on
  `soc_flash_base`) — the module docstring claimed the move from
  `check_atoc_reservation.py`'s original `_resolve_aperture` was "unchanged
  in behaviour"; false, the original guarded only `mram_mb` against a
  Python `bool`, not `base` itself. Corrected the docstring ("moved and
  hardened") and pinned the guard with a synthetic SoC spec
  (`test_none_when_soc_flash_base_is_a_bool`) since no real
  `metadata/socs/**` file can carry a JSON boolean there.
- **A10** (`region_extent`'s `isinstance(base, bool)` guard) —
  pre-existing behaviour, carried over verbatim; folded into
  `TestRegionExtent` (`test_unresolved_when_base_is_a_bool`).
- **P1** (`partition.py`'s legacy `carveout: false` fallback in
  `_is_flash_sub_partition`) — the fallback the docstring's "MAJOR 3" and
  the non-Alif no-op argument both rest on had no test; no non-Alif preset
  authors `carveout: false` today. Direct-call pin with an explicit
  `aperture=None` (`TestLegacyCarveoutFallback`).
- **P4** (`resolve_storage_partitions`'s hoisted `aperture`) — P2/P3 were
  killed only via a direct-call sentinel path, so the derived verdict was
  never proven load-bearing through the actual production entry point. Added
  one synthetic `memory_map:` row (strictly inside the declared aperture, no
  `carveout:` key authored) where the derived and legacy verdicts genuinely
  disagree, and drove it through `resolve_storage_partitions()` itself
  (`TestDerivedVerdictLoadBearingEndToEnd`). Under the mutant the entry still
  blocks, but for the WRONG reason (the unrelated #1556 unverified-dt_label
  gate catches it instead) — proving the derived aperture-containment check
  is the one actually deciding it.

Every fix above was verified by re-applying its exact mutant in a disk copy
of the tree (never the branch) and confirming the new test goes red with
the assertion text quoted in its own docstring/message, then reverting.

**Not fixed here, flagged for a follow-up issue:**
`tests/scripts/test_check_emit_snapshots.py` unit-tests only
`_normalize_host_paths` — the four `.snap` fixtures are guarded solely by
`scripts/check_emit_snapshots.py` running inside `test-all.sh`. Running
`pytest tests/scripts/` alone and reading green gives no snapshot coverage
at all (this is how mutants A2/A3 survived `pytest` entirely in the

Refs #1365, #1983. #2009 (the remedy-text inversion from the same review)
was already fixed and merged separately — not touched here.

### Fixed — the build-plan CWD-independence test compared the whole envelope, including the live git commit, and could redden on a race that had nothing to do with CWD (#2014)

`tests/scripts/test_orchestrate_buildplan.py::test_emit_build_plan_app_paths_independent_of_cwd`
calls `emit_build_plan()` twice from two different working directories and
asserted that the two returned envelopes were equal in full. That included
`sdkCommit`, which `scripts/alp_orchestrate/buildplan.py::_sdk_commit()`
resolves with a live `git rev-parse --short HEAD` on every call. Any
concurrent git operation in the same worktree between the two calls — a
commit from another agent, a rebase, a branch switch — moved `sdkCommit`
between them and failed the assertion for a reason unrelated to the
CWD-independence property the test exists to guard (issues #596 and #865).
It fired for real on 2026-09-06:

```
AssertionError: {'sdkCommit': '3dadd4584'} != {'sdkCommit': 'a284f7647'}
```

The CWD-independence comparison now excludes exactly the envelope keys
whose value is read from ambient process/repository state rather than
derived from the test's inputs, via a new module-level
`_ENV_DERIVED_ENVELOPE_FIELDS` constant. Tracing `emit_build_plan()`'s full
call graph turned up exactly one such key: `sdkCommit`. Its sibling
`sdkVersion` (`_sdk_version()`, read from `metadata/sdk_version.yaml`) is
deliberately left in the comparison — it only moves on a deliberate
release-version bump, never as a side effect of ordinary concurrent
commit/rebase/branch-switch activity, the same asymmetry
`scripts/check_emit_snapshots.py` already encodes for the golden-snapshot
gate (a comment on the new constant also reconciles this against
`tests/parity/seam1_field_diff.py`, which drops `sdkVersion` too, but for
the opposite reason: that harness diffs a frozen cross-release oracle
against the current checkout, where `sdkVersion` is guaranteed to differ
by construction — not the same-checkout, two-in-process-calls case this
test is making). Every path, token, and slice the test actually exists to
pin is still compared byte-for-byte via plain dict equality. `sdkCommit`'s
own shape (a lowercase-hex string, or `None` when `git` genuinely isn't
available) is not re-checked in this test; that check already lives, and
now stays, in `test_emit_build_plan_carries_sdk_provenance` alone, so the
two tests don't carry two independent copies of the same assertion.

`test_emit_build_plan_deterministic`, a sibling in the same file that calls
`emit_build_plan()` twice back-to-back and compared the raw JSON strings for
byte-identity, was exposed to the same race. It is fixed more directly:
`_sdk_commit` is pinned to a constant for the duration of the test via
`monkeypatch`, so the original byte-for-byte string comparison — including
`sdkCommit`, and including the serialization details (key order, `indent=2`,
the trailing newline) an exclusion-based fix would stop covering — is kept
exactly as it was. No other whole-envelope comparison of `emit_build_plan()`
output was found elsewhere in `tests/scripts/`.

### Fixed — retract the corrupted-tree V2N supervisor / DEEPX rail claims from #2021 / a4ff0e3a (#2021)

#2021 claimed the `CONFIG_ALP_SDK_V2N*` Kconfig symbols were undefined; its
own author retracted it once the cause surfaced -- the claim came from a
worktree holding a binary-corrupted copy of
`zephyr/kconfigs/v2n-supervisor.kconfig`. Before the retraction, `a4ff0e3a`
(#2019) had already rewritten `docs/v1.0-readiness.md`'s
`src/zephyr/v2n_power_mgmt.c` bullet from that corrupted tree, adding text
that the two symbols "do not exist" / "are not defined anywhere" and that
the `#else` stub "wins on every build". The Kconfig-symbol claims do not
hold against a clean `20fec7a7` checkout: both symbols resolve `=y` on
`alp_e1m_v2m101_m33_sm` and `alp_e1m_v2n101_m33_sm` once the generated
`alp.conf` sets `CONFIG_ALP_SOC_RENESAS_RZV2N_N44=y`,
`CONFIG_ALP_SDK_CHIP_GD32G553=y` and `CONFIG_ALP_SDK_CHIP_DA9292=y`. The
NOSUPPORT-stub claim is right for the wrong reason: the stub still wins
on both in-tree boards, but through `v2n_power_mgmt.c`'s DT-alias guard,
not the Kconfig guard the retracted text named.

`docs/v1.0-readiness.md`, `docs/console.md`,
`docs/cc3501e-companion-commands.md`, the `v2n-m1-deepx-inference` example
(README, `board.yaml` comment and `main.c` comments, which no longer
claim this `m33_sm` image brings the DEEPX rail up, calls
`deepx_dxm1_bring_up()` or has a Zephyr DEEPX backend), the
`src/zephyr/v2n_power_mgmt.c` / `v2n_power_mgmt.h` comments, and
`zephyr/kconfigs/v2n-supervisor.kconfig`'s help text now describe the real
mechanism: the module's DT aliases are `v2n-deepx-pwr-en-req` /
`v2n-deepx-core-0p75-en` (not a `-gpios` property naming convention), and no
in-tree board defines them, so DEEPX rail bring-up compiles to its
`ALP_ERR_NOSUPPORT` stub on `alp_e1m_v2m101_m33_sm` -- tracked as #2045.
Separately, the V2N supervisor's `CONFIG_ALP_SDK_V2N_SUPERVISOR_SPI_BUS_ID`
/ `_I2C_BUS_ID` both default `-1` and nothing in-tree overrides them, so the
supervisor singleton never opens a bus and `alp companion` commands would
fail `ALP_ERR_NOT_READY` on a stock build (derived from source, not run on
silicon) -- tracked as #2044.

`zephyr/kconfigs/chips.kconfig`'s DA9292 help text is also corrected: the
PMIC's 7-bit I2C address is `0x1E` (`include/alp/chips/da9292.h`), not the
stale `0x1C` it carried.

### Fixed — the `--emit` goldens are now guarded by `pytest tests/scripts/`, not only by `test-all.sh` (#2023)

`tests/scripts/test_check_emit_snapshots.py` unit-tested only
`_normalize_host_paths`, so every committed golden under
`tests/fixtures/emit-snapshots/` was guarded **solely** by
`scripts/check_emit_snapshots.py` running inside `scripts/test-all.sh`.
Running `pytest tests/scripts -q`, reading green and pushing gave no
snapshot coverage at all.

Measured, not theorised: in the mutation review of #1365 split B (#2010),
mutants **A2** and **A3** survived `pytest tests/scripts/` entirely and were
killed only by that script. The fixtures carry the exact refusal text that
ships into `build/generated/alp/system_ipc.h` and `dts-reservations.dtsi`,
which is how #2009 — a refusal instructing an edit the same function
refuses — reached committed goldens and customer-visible generated output.

`tests/scripts/test_emit_snapshot_goldens.py` closes it the way the issue
prefers: it INVOKES the gate rather than reimplementing a fixture diff, so
there stays one source of truth for what "in sync" means. Five checks, and
the refusing direction of each is pinned rather than assumed —

- the gate itself runs under pytest and must report every surface
  byte-identical (mutation-proven: appending one line to
  `rpmsg-aen.system-manifest.snap` turns it red, reverting turns it green);
- a perturbed golden and a missing golden each return 1, exercised against
  a COPY under `tmp_path` with `CASES` narrowed to a single entry, so the
  committed fixtures are never written to and the check costs one emit
  rather than 37;
- `CASES` and the goldens on disk must be the same set in BOTH directions —
  a new case with no committed golden, and an orphaned golden no case emits
  any more, are drift that never shows up as a `DIFF`;
- both `--emit` surfaces that reach generated output (`system-manifest` and
  `build-plan`) keep at least one golden.

Costs ~10 s in a suite that already runs ~760 s, and that cost is the point:
without it the suite said nothing about the goldens.

One correction to the issue text while closing it: it describes "the four
golden fixtures under `tests/fixtures/emit-snapshots/`". There are **37**
`.snap` files there; four of them are the `.system-manifest` goldens. The
gap was wider than the issue stated, and this guard covers all 37.

Refs #2010, #2009, #1365. Closes #2023.

### Changed (BREAKING for out-of-tree presets) — som-preset schema is now v2: `write_authority` required, `npu_population` removed (#2024)

`metadata/schemas/som-preset-v1.schema.json` is renamed `som-preset-v2.schema.json` and
`schema_version` is pinned to 2 (`metadata/schemas/som-preset-v2.schema.json:56` ("schema_version")).
There is no v1 compatibility path: a preset still declaring `schema_version: 1` fails validation.

`memory_region` now lists `write_authority` in `required`
(`metadata/schemas/som-preset-v2.schema.json:724` ("write_authority")), so a `memory_map:` row
that omits it is rejected by the schema itself, per ADR-0034 clause 4 (absence is a validation
failure, never a permissive default). The semantic gate `_check_som_write_authority_present` in
`scripts/validate_metadata.py` existed only to cover the v1 gap and is deleted with its test.
`inference.npu_population` and the `npu_instance` definition are deleted; Ethos-U instances are
derived from the SoC JSON `npus[]`.

Regions the loader derives when a preset declares no `memory_map:` now state their authority
explicitly (`scripts/alp_project_loader.py:504` ("def resolve_memory_map(")): SRAM/TCM and SoC-level
RAM regions are `customer_runtime`, the derived `mram_main` whole-device alias is `composite`. The
`rpmsg-v2n` and `hetero-offload` system-manifest emit snapshots gain that field.

**Migrating an out-of-tree preset:** set `schema_version: 2`, add `write_authority` to every
`memory_map:` row (values in the schema's `write_authority` description), and delete any
`inference.npu_population` block.

### Fixed — Flow D's `flash-jlink*.sh` write a replacing ATOC with no way to warn what it delisted (#2025)

`app-write-mram -p` and a J-Link `loadbin` of a hand-authored ATOC both
REPLACE the resident ATOC rather than merging it — any boot entry not
named in the config being written is silently delisted, and the SES
prints `[SES] ATOC ok` afterwards with nothing to say otherwise. On
2026-09-07 this destroyed a diagnostic BL32 (md5
`94aa473453271b58160146ceaa828a5f`) plus an A32 Linux boot chain on
an AEN EVK bench unit.

PR #2026 guards the four SE-UART (Flow A) scripts with
`bench_atoc_replace_guard()`, which queries the resident TOC via SETOOLS
`maintenance -c $SE_UART -opt gettoc` before writing and refuses (exit 5)
unless `--replace-atoc` is passed. Flow D has no `SE_UART` dependency at
all — that is the point of Flow D, and on a no-SE-UART bench place
it is the only load path — so it cannot run that same query.

**Interim step only** (this change): `flash-jlink.sh`, `flash-jlink-hp.sh`
and `flash-jlink-mramxip.sh` now require an explicit `--atoc-unqueryable`
flag before writing anything; without it they abort (**exit 8**, chosen
to collide with none of these scripts' existing 1–7) with a message
naming the replace, the missing SE-UART channel, and the class of entry
that would be delisted (an A32 chain, an HP app). This is a deliberately
DIFFERENT flag from Flow A's `--replace-atoc`, not merged or aliased to
it: an operator on a no-SE-UART slot passes `--atoc-unqueryable` on every
single run, and that habit must never also unlock `--replace-atoc` on a
board where the resident TOC genuinely can be read.

**Open question, blocking the full (query-based) guard on Flow D:** does
`maintenance -c $SE_UART -opt gettoc` itself reset the target? If it
does, `AP[3] (APAddr 0x00300000)` — the AHB-AP carrying the M55 debug
domain — disappears (per `flash-jlink-mramxip.sh`'s own `#1902` notes:
0 of 8 post-reset scans found it), and that script's pre-programming `h`
halt gate (exit 5, unrelated to this change's exit 8) would then fail on
every run regardless of SE-UART availability. Reading the ATOC over
SWD/J-Link instead was assessed and rejected: MRAM reads on this part can
return an uncommitted shadow (a `loadbin` that verifies but does not
persist, so a same-power-cycle read shows the just-written package while
persisted MRAM holds a different, foreign one) and the debug-AP read path
has also returned a flatly false `Verify successful.` against data never
written (2026-09-05, 5/5 `verifybin` calls). Wiring the SE-UART `gettoc`
guard into Flow D needs the reset question answered on silicon first.

### Fixed — several `scripts/bench/aen/` helpers silently REPLACED the whole ATOC instead of adding to it, deleting resident boot entries with no warning (#2025)

`flash-run.sh` generates a fresh SETOOLS ATOC config with exactly two
entries (`DEVICE` + `ALP-HE`) and burns it with `app-write-mram -p`, which
**replaces** the device's entire Application Table of Contents rather than
merging into it — the header comment's "keeps the factory DEVICE cfg" was
true but incomplete: it kept `DEVICE` and silently dropped everything else.
This destroyed a live A32 Linux boot chain (`BOOTLOAD`/`A32_APP`/`HP_APP`/
`HE_APP`) on an AEN EVK bench unit on 2026-09-07 — one Flow A run left only
`DEVICE` and the new `ALP-HE`, with no error and no SES warning (`[SES]
ATOC ok` prints either way).

Added a GUARD that runs before the write: query the currently-resident ATOC
with SETOOLS' `maintenance -c $SE_UART -opt gettoc` (a non-destructive TOC
read, not a merge engine), log the pre-write table unconditionally, and
refuse to proceed (exit 5) if any resident entry other than `DEVICE`/
`ALP-HE` is found, naming what would be delisted. Also refuses if the query
itself can't be verified (tool missing, no parseable table, and no `No
ATOC` state either) rather than assuming it is safe to write blind. A new
`--replace-atoc` flag opts out of the guard for an intentional replace.
Updated the step-1 header comment to say the ATOC is REPLACED, not kept.

The same hazard exists in every other `scripts/bench/aen/` helper that
commits a freshly-generated `app-gen-toc` package: `loadbin $PKG $ATOC_ADDR`
over J-Link burns the identical signed ATOC structure `app-write-mram -p`
does, at the same MRAM location, so it replaces rather than merges too.
Factored the guard out of `flash-run.sh` into a shared
`bench_atoc_replace_guard()` in `bench-env.sh` (query + parse + allow-list +
abort logic, parameterized by the entries the caller is itself about to
write) and applied it to:

- `flash-run-dualcore.sh` — allows its own `ALP-HP`/`ALP-HE` two-entry write
  (the whole point of that script), refusing only a genuinely foreign
  resident entry. New `--replace-atoc` flag.
- `flash-update-log-dual.sh` — allows `HP-OWNER`/`HE-CLIENT`. New
  `--replace-atoc` flag (combinable with the existing `--package-only`).
- `flash-update-log-firewall-probe.sh` — allows `HE-PROBE`. Same new flag.

`flash-run.sh` itself now calls the shared function instead of carrying its
own copy.

Swept the rest of `scripts/bench/aen/` for the same shape: `erase-storage.sh`
never touches the ATOC band (writes only the customer `storage` window and
asserts it is adjacent to, not overlapping, `atoc`); `ram-run.sh` is a
RAM-only Flow C run with no MRAM write; `flash-all-flowd.sh` has no ATOC
generation of its own, it only invokes `flash-jlink.sh` in a loop.
`flash-jlink.sh`, `flash-jlink-hp.sh`, and `flash-jlink-mramxip.sh` generate
and burn a replacing ATOC the same way (Flow D, `DEVICE`+`ALP-HE`/`HP-APP`
only) but currently have no SE-UART dependency at all — extending this guard
to them means deciding whether they should newly depend on `SE_UART` for a
read-only `gettoc` query, a design tradeoff against their "no SE-UART" Flow D
premise that this change does not resolve. Refs #2027.

**Validated against real silicon captures** off an AEN EVK bench unit (2026-09-07,
ANSI intact), and three defects the earlier synthetic-fixture coverage
missed fixed as a result: the transcript path (`${TMPDIR:-/tmp}/<tag>-atoc-
before.log`) was NOT run-unique, so two concurrent runs of the same script
against different boards could interleave and one could read the other's
transcript — now `mktemp`-generated per run; `getbanner`'s real line has a
LEADING SPACE ("` SES A1 v1.110.0 ...`"), which a bare `^SES` anchor
rejected outright, aborting every run on real hardware — anchor now
tolerates leading whitespace; SETOOLS colours the WHOLE LINE, not just the
cell text, so the ANSI-stripped `gettoc` row also keeps a leading space,
which the table-row match (`/^\|/`) never matched at all — `resident`
silently computed empty on every real coloured transcript. Also: `SERAM0`/
`SERAM1` (the two on-module SE firmware banks, never touched by
`app-write-mram -p`) are resident on every real board regardless of the
