`examples/aen/aen-evk-demo/prj.conf` had been patching this with
`CONFIG_TMP112=n`, a per-app fix over a per-board defect — the next app to
enable `CONFIG_SENSOR` alongside alp-sdk's own chip driver on this board
would have hit the identical link error with no CI gate to catch it first.

`scripts/gen_zephyr_board.py`'s `_aen_kconfig_defconfig()` now emits a
`config TMP112` / `default n` stanza into both boards' generated
`Kconfig.defconfig`, the same `if BOARD_<sym> ... endif`-scoped pattern that
function already uses for `ROM_START_OFFSET`. This is a board-scoped
default, not a hard disable: Kconfig.zephyr sources a board's
`Kconfig.defconfig` ahead of subsys/Kconfig, so this default only supplies
the value nothing else assigns — an app that genuinely wants the upstream
driver still sets `CONFIG_TMP112=y` explicitly and that assignment overrides
the board default regardless of source order. Confirmed on the real board
target, not just by mechanism: `west build -p always -b
alp_e1m_aen801_m55_he/ae822fa0e5597ls0/rtss_he examples/aen/aen-temp-sensor`
links `zephyr/drivers/sensor/ti/tmp112/libdrivers__sensor__ti__tmp112.a`,
and the resolved `.config` carries `CONFIG_TMP112=y`, `CONFIG_SENSOR=y` and
`CONFIG_DT_HAS_TI_TMP112_ENABLED=y` with the board's `default n` in force.
`examples/aen/aen-temp-sensor` is exactly that app (it reads TMP112 through
the upstream sensor API, not alp-sdk's chip driver); its `prj.conf` and
`README.md` now say so explicitly instead of relying on the
devicetree-triggered default that no longer fires on this board. `examples/aen/aen-evk-demo/prj.conf`'s now-redundant
`CONFIG_TMP112=n` line and its explanatory comment block are deleted — the
board default already does that job.

The other thirteen parts the issue's `find` turned up (bme280, bmi323,
bmp581, lis2dw12, lps22hb, lsm6dso, hx711, max31855, max31865, veml7700,
tsl2591, vl53l1x, icm42670) have no board-level `.dts` node today — only
per-example carrier overlays declare them, which `Kconfig.defconfig` cannot
see — so they stay latent and undefaulted here; the naming-convention fix
(a chip-driver symbol prefix) the issue calls out as "Not in scope" is still
not in scope.

### Fixed — V2N/V2M CM33 supervisor now comes up by default (#2044)

`CONFIG_ALP_SDK_V2N_SUPERVISOR_SPI_BUS_ID` defaulted to `-1` and nothing set it, so on both in-tree RZ/V2N CM33 boards the GD32 supervisor singleton latched `ALP_ERR_NOT_READY` and every bridge-routed open (ADC/PWM/DAC/QENC/counter, ADC streams, TMU, TRNG poll, the Renesas power ext, `alp companion`) failed. It now defaults to `1` whenever the board enables the `alp-spi1` devicetree alias, which both `alp_e1m_v2n101_m33_sm` and `alp_e1m_v2m101_m33_sm` do (`alp-spi1 = &gd32_spi`). Boards without the alias keep `-1`.

### Fixed — `docs/v1.0-readiness.md` no longer lists the removed CM33 DEEPX rail module as delivered (#2045)

The readiness log still recorded §C.28 (`src/zephyr/v2n_power_mgmt.c`, the
P65-driven CM33 DEEPX-rail sequence) as delivered and DONE. That module is not

### Fixed — U-Boot fixes the on-module clock generator's SE1/SE3 OTP routing so the SoC RTC starts (#2045)

The on-module Renesas 5L35023B programmable clock generator (RIIC8/BRD_I2C,
7-bit `0x69`) ships an OTP image whose single-ended output routing is wrong
for this SoM: SE1 (feeds the SoC RTXIN and the Wi-Fi module's 32k LPO input)
outputs `24.576 MHz` instead of `32.768 kHz`, and SE3 (audio clock) outputs
`22.5792 MHz` instead of `24.576 MHz`. Bench-confirmed on E1M-V2M103 board
#1: with the as-shipped OTP values the SoC RTC (RTCA-3) fails to start
(`error -ETIMEDOUT: Failed to setup the RTC!`).

Two volatile register writes fix it (5L35023B datasheet register map,
"Byte 36: SE1 and DIV4 control" = reg `0x24`, "Byte 33: SE3 and DIFF1
Control Register" = reg `0x21`):

* register `0x24` `0x9c` (`1001_1100`) -> `0x8e` (`1000_1110`): clears bit 4
  `SE1_Freerun_32K` (`1`->`0` — 0 means SE1 is sourced from the 32.768 kHz
  DCO instead of free-running) and sets bit 1 `DIV4_CH3_EN` (`0`->`1` — DIV4
  channel 3 output enabled). Bit 7 `I2C_PDB`, bit 6 `Ref_free_run`, bit 5
  `free_run_output_config`, bit 3 `SE1_CLKSEL1`, bit 2 `REF_EN` and bit 0
  `DIV4_CH2_EN` are all unchanged.
* register `0x21` `0x80` (`1000_0000`) -> `0xc0` (`1100_0000`): sets bit 6
  `SE3_CLKSEL1` (`0`->`1` — SE3 now sourced from DIV4 = PLL2 `122.88/5` =
  24.576 MHz, was DIV2). Every other bit is unchanged, including both
  `DIFF1_CMOS2_FLIP`/`DIFF2_CMOS2_FLIP` bits that also live in this
  register. Neither write touches the separate DIFF1/DIFF2 registers
  (`0x22`/`0x23`) -- those are untouched.

With them applied, the SoC RTC counts at 32.768 kHz (bench-verified against
an NTP-slewed reference, ~±100 ppm). Both are OTP-shadow registers -- the
writes take effect immediately but **revert on power-cycle** (the OTP
itself cannot be re-burned in-system), so they must be re-applied on every
boot.

`meta-alp-sdk/recipes-bsp/u-boot/u-boot/0007-rzv2n-dev-ALP-E1M-clkgen-otp-fixup.patch`
adds `alp_clk5l_fixup()`, run first in `board_late_init()` -- ahead of
and independent of the `0004` DEEPX rail step -- for the whole rzv2n-family
(this clock generator is present on every V2N/V2M SoM, not just
DEEPX-populated V2M units). Guarded to single-byte reads only (matching the
constraint `0005`/`0006` document for this RIIC family) and to writing only
these two registers: register `0x00` (General Control) must first read
`0xa0` (OTP-burned, `I2C_addr[1:0]=01` -> 7-bit `0x69`). Register `0x24`
is then handled first, then `0x21` -- each independently: its as-shipped
OTP value writes the fix and reads it back, its already-fixed value skips,
and any other readback is left untouched and only reported (rather than
requiring both registers to read the OTP pair before either is touched,
which would report a half-applied prior run as "unexpected" instead of
completing it). If `0x24`'s write/readback fails, `0x21` is never touched.
Each write is read back before the next register is touched.

Logs one line: `ALP: 5L35023B clock: SE1 32.768 kHz, SE3 24.576 MHz
(0x24=0x8e 0x21=0xc0)` on success, or a per-register `... already ... --
skip` / `... is neither ... -- not touching` line otherwise.

**Kernel devicetree (`meta-alp-sdk/recipes-kernel/linux/linux-renesas/e1m-v2n-som.dtsi`):**
the SoC RTC (`&rtc`) is now enabled and its `rtc_clk` fixed-clock node set
to the corrected `clock-frequency = <32768>` -- the previously deployed dtb
carried `clock-frequency = <0>` (the vendor SoC dtsi's own unset-placeholder
default; no ALP override had ever set it, on the earlier, incomplete
understanding that RTXIN had no reference at all). RTXIN in fact has no
*discrete crystal*, but it is fed by SE1 of the on-module clock generator
once U-Boot corrects it, and DT enablement now depends on that runtime fix
having already run before Linux probes `&rtc`. The on-module RV-3028-C7
remains the RTC of record (`rtc0` alias, unchanged) -- the SoC RTC is a
second, SoC-internal timebase, not a replacement. Because `&rtc` (the SoC
RTC, `rtc-rtca3`) is now enabled, it probes on every boot alongside
`rv3028`, and Linux's `/dev/rtcN` numbering follows probe order, not the
`aliases` block -- without a fixed id the SoC RTC (which probes before
`rv3028` on this bus) would take `/dev/rtc0` and displace `rv3028` to
`/dev/rtc1`, breaking `RTC_HCTOSYS`. A new `rtc1 = &rtc;` alias pins the
SoC RTC to `/dev/rtc1` so `rv3028` keeps `/dev/rtc0`. Stale "no crystal,
nothing to enable" comments in `e1m-x-evk.dtsi` and `rv3028-rtc.cfg` are
corrected to match.

This is a runtime workaround; **production builds should use a Renesas
factory dash code that carries the corrected OTP image** instead of relying
on the U-Boot fixup.

`docs/soms/v2n.md` gains an "On-module clock-generator fixup" section (plus
a corrected "Real-time clock" section) and `docs/bring-up-v2n-m1.md` cross-
references it from the DEEPX-rail step, noting the fixup's log line appears
first and is unrelated to DEEPX sequencing.

**Patch md5 (current):** `0007` `422cb294103c4a3878bd7ad43150e35b`. Applies
cleanly on top of `0006`, against `renesas-u-boot-cip` `bcf29d98` plus the
meta-renesas PMIC-I2C-removal patch and `0001`-`0006`. Cross-built
(`ARCH=arm CROSS_COMPILE=aarch64-linux-gnu- rzv2n-dev_defconfig` +
`no-dirty-version.cfg`/`gigadevice-xspi.cfg`/`deepx-rail.cfg`/
`fdtfile-v2m.cfg`); `strings u-boot | grep 'ALP: 5L35023B'` confirms all
eleven log lines link, `u-boot.bin` md5 `9f23a19d1afdf69179319921b6327470`.
Not yet flashed/bench-booted -- register-write values are bench-proven
(2026-09-24, E1M-V2M103 board #1) but this patch's own build was verified
as a clean cross-compile + string-link only, not (yet) an on-silicon boot.

### Fixed — U-Boot routes the on-module clock generator's SE2 from DIV4 so the GD32 HXTAL gets 24.576 MHz (#2045)

SE2 of the on-module 5L35023B (BRD_I2C, 7-bit `0x69`) drives the GD32
supervisor's OSCIN (net `GD32_OSC`). The as-shipped OTP has register `0x1F`
= `0x46`; its bit 7 `SE2_Freerun_32K` = 0 makes SE2 free-run at 32.768 kHz,
which is why the GD32 HXTAL never starts.

U-Boot patch `0013-rzv2n-dev-ALP-E1M-clkgen-se2-gd32-hxtal.patch` extends
`alp_clk5l_fixup()` with two more volatile register writes (never OTP; register
`0x00` is never written), in this order, each read back and skipped when
already correct:

* register `0x24` `0x9c` -> `0x8f`: the existing `0x8e` plus bit 0
  `DIV4_CH2_EN`, so DIV4 channel 2 is live before SE2 selects it.
* register `0x1F` `0x46` -> `0xc7`: sets bit 7 `SE2_Freerun_32K` and bit 0
  `SE2_CLKSEL1` (DIV4, was DIV5); `VDD2_SEL` is unchanged.

SE2 is then DIV4 = 24.576 MHz, the same source SE3 already uses. U-Boot logs
`ALP: 5L35023B clock: SE1 32.768 kHz, SE2 24.576 MHz, SE3 24.576 MHz
(0x24=0x8f 0x1f=0xc7 0x21=0xc0)`. SE2 must not change afterwards: the GD32
locks its PLL to it once the host triggers the switch. The `clkgen_verify`
provisioning step now expects `0x1F` = `0xC7` and `0x24` = `0x8F` and reports
`SE2 24.576 MHz`. The GD32 firmware's IRC8M `SystemInit()` override is
unchanged. The next build's corrected OTP image (ledger item 24) should carry
`0x1F` = `0xC7` and `0x24` = `0x8F` so SE2 is valid from power-on-reset.

Not yet bench-verified: scope TP88 should read 24.576 MHz at 1.8 V.

### Added — U-Boot sequences the V2N-M1 DEEPX 0.75 V core rail before releasing `M1_RESET` (#2045)

The V2N-M1 SoM's DEEPX DX-M1 core rail (DA9292 CH2, 0.75 V) had no
sequencing step: `board_late_init()` released `M1_RESET` and enabled the
PCIe mux purely on the on-module EEPROM manifest match, with nothing
bringing CH2 up first. The DA9292-AROVx OTP variant this SoM uses boots
with `CH2_VSTEP=1` (doubled voltage range, `PMC_CTRL_01` reset `0x80`);
releasing `M1_RESET` before CH2 is confirmed at 0.75 V and power-good
risked an over-voltage event on the DEEPX core rail, not merely a
brownout.

`meta-alp-sdk/recipes-bsp/u-boot/u-boot/0004-rzv2n-dev-ALP-E1M-DEEPX-rail-bringup.patch`
adds `alp_deepx_rail_bringup()`, run in `board_late_init()` before
`alp_deepx_pcie_bringup()` (patch 0001). It programs CH2 to 0.75 V over
DM I2C bus 8 (RIIC8/BRD_I2C, DA9292 at `0x1E`), verifies every write by
read-back, is idempotent across a warm reboot (never clears a validly-up
`CH2_EN`), then enables the channel and releases P64
(`DEEPX_CORE_0P75_EN`) only after polling P65 (`DEEPX_PWR_EN_REQ`) and
confirming `CH2_PG` with no UV/OV/OC. `alp_deepx_pcie_bringup()` now runs
only when the rail step succeeds. Gated on the new
`CONFIG_ALP_E1M_DEEPX_RAIL` (default `n`, wired via `deepx-rail.cfg` for
the V2M MACHINEs only) OR the existing EEPROM-manifest check, so V2N base
images touch nothing on the DA9292.

Three hardening fixes on top of the first draft: the P65 read now uses
the dedicated PFC terminal-input register (`PFC_BASE+0x0820+n`) instead
of the P output-latch register (which returned the last value
*written*, not the live pin level); every program-phase abort forces P64
low / `M1_RESET` asserted via a shared `alp_deepx_rail_safe_off()`
helper; `CH2_VSTEP` is re-checked immediately before the `CH2_EN` write
and aborts if it is ever found set -- the exact over-voltage condition
this sequence exists to prevent; and the PG-timeout failure message now
names a possible EN2-gates-CH2 hardware-wiring question (see
`docs/bring-up-v2n-m1.md` §2).

**Maintainer decision carried through in full:** Cortex-A55/Linux is the
sole master of RIIC8/BRD_I2C; the CM33 must never master it or claim
P64/P65.

- `src/zephyr/v2n_power_mgmt.c`/`.h`, `CONFIG_ALP_SDK_V2N_POWER_MGMT`, and
  the V2N supervisor's BRD_I2C transport are deleted outright -- the
  CM33's only GD32 transport is SPI now.
- `chips/da9292`'s driver stays; the V2N helpers
  `da9292_v2n_m1_enable_deepx_rail()`/`da9292_v2n_base_init()` were later
  removed (#1165).
- The generated CM33 Zephyr board files no longer claim RIIC8 (`&i2c8`
  `status = "disabled"`, `alp-i2c0` alias removed;
  `metadata/e1m_modules/v2n/supervisor-links.yaml`'s `brd_i2c` link
  flips to `status: disabled`).
- `metadata/pinmux/v2n.yaml` attributes `DEEPX_CORE_0P75_EN` (P64) and
  `DEEPX_PWR_EN_REQ` (P65) to `core: "a55"`.
- `meta-alp-sdk/recipes-kernel/linux/linux-renesas/e1m-v2m-deepx.dtsi`
  drops its `deepx-m1-reset-release-hog` (U-Boot is the sole `M1_RESET`
  owner); the P80/P95 PCIe-mux hogs are unchanged.
- `examples/v2n/v2n-rtc-multi-alarm` is retired -- it addressed the RTC
  over CM33 I2C, now forbidden (the on-module RV-3028-C7 is Linux's
  `/dev/rtc0`).
- `0001-clk-renesas-r9a09g056-keep-CM33-owned-RSCI7-on.patch` (retitled,
  was `...-RSCI7-RIIC8-on.patch`) drops its `riic_8_ckm`
  `DEF_MOD_CRITICAL` hunk -- Linux is RIIC8's real consumer now. The five
  `rsci_7_*` hunks (SCI7 SPI, still CM33-owned) are unchanged.

**Two unrelated BRD_I2C address corrections, bench-confirmed on
E1M-V2M103 (`alp i2c scan`/`i2cdetect`):** `CLK_5L35023B_I2C_ADDR_DEFAULT`
(`include/alp/chips/clk_5l35023b.h`) changed `0x68u` -> `0x69u` (the
fitted part straps `I2C_addr[1:0] = 01`, not the previously assumed
`00`), and `metadata/chips/tmp112.yaml`'s address entry changed `0x48`
-> `0x40` (the fitted TMP112DIDPWR straps `ADD0 = GND` to `0x40`, the
same class of bug already fixed for AEN #1978). Both are the actual
strapped address; every example and doc citing either is updated in the
same slice.

**`deepx_lpddr_0v85` strap resolved: `0x48` (#1163, #1845).** `0x48`
ACKs on `BRD_I2C` only after `P64` is driven high, and its VOUT register
reads back `0x5A` (= 0.85 V: 0.4 V + 90 x 5 mV), matching the role;
`0x44` (`deepx_ddr5_vdd`) and `0x4F` (`deepx_ddr5_vddq`) are present on
the same scan. `metadata/e1m_modules/E1M-V2M101.yaml`/
`E1M-V2M102.yaml`/`E1M-V2M103.yaml` change `address_7bit: "TBD"` ->
`"0x48"`; `docs/bring-up-v2n-m1.md` and `docs/soms/v2n-m1.md` are
updated to match and no longer warn against hardcoding `0x48`.

**`0005-i2c-rzg2l_riic-combined-register-read.patch`** makes every RIIC
register read on this driver (all nine RIIC instances) a single
repeated-START transaction. `dm_i2c_read()` always builds a register
read as two `struct i2c_msg`s (write-the-offset, then the paired read),
and the unpatched `riic_xfer()` ran each as its own independent
START..STOP transaction with a spurious STOP between them, instead of
the one combined transfer `riic_read_common()` already implements. The
fast path now packs the offset for any 1-4 byte width, which also fixes
the on-module 24C128 EEPROM's 2-byte-offset reads on RIIC0.
`riic_check_busy()` gains a one-shot BBSY-timeout recovery (clock SDA
free, full `ICE=0+IICRST` reset, retry), since `riic_ops` implements no
`dm_i2c` bus-recovery op, and `riic_wait_for_icsr2()`'s timeout
diagnostic now prints unconditionally instead of only in DEBUG builds.
Writes were unaffected (`dm_i2c_write()` always built one combined
message). This runs on silicon in the bench-passing chain described
below (v4..v6) -- it is not isolated as a fix for one symptom.

**`0006-rzv2n-dev-i2c-rzg2l_riic-p06-p07-pullup-clock-fix.patch`**
carries two independently bench-proven fixes for a repeated-START
arbitration-lost failure (`ICSR2 = 0x0a`, `STOP|AL`) that `0005` alone
did not clear, each sufficient on its own: (1) the SoC-internal pull-up
on P06/P07 (`PUPD_H` = `0x03030000`, matching what Linux already
programs -- U-Boot left it at the POR value of 0), and (2) a slower
RIIC8 SCL. `riic_set_clock()`'s CKS table (shared by every SoC this
driver builds for) is tuned for a 50 MHz RIIC input clock; R9A09G056/057
(RZ/V2N, RZ/V2H) run RIIC off a 100 MHz input, so the upstream value
(`CKS(3)` standard / `CKS(1)` fast) actually ran the bus at roughly
double rate. The nominal-100 MHz-correct value, `CKS(4)`/`CKS(2)`, still
lost bit 7 on long reads over the heavily-loaded BRD_I2C bus (~13
populated branches) from about byte 13 onward on bursts longer than
~12 bytes. `0006` ships one step slower still, `CKS(5)` standard /
`CKS(3)` fast, as deliberate margin: bench-confirmed, 32-byte bursts
come back clean and repeatable at `CKS(5)`. FAST-rate `CKS(3)` is
carried by the same margin reasoning but was not itself bench-tested
(only STANDARD/RIIC8 was exercised). External 2.2 kOhm pull-ups to the
1.8 V rail are fitted on this bus; the SoC-internal pull-up was
bench-confirmed required at the unpatched (faster) clock,
and is carried alongside `CKS(5)` -- either the pull-up or the slower
clock alone was sufficient to fix this arbitration-lost failure, and
both are kept.

`0006` also adds: `riic_read_common()` polls `ICCR1.SDAI` (SDA
released) before the repeated START, since restarting while a slave
still holds SDA low from its ACK is the arbitration-lost race seen on
the bench; `riic_check_busy()` clears stale `ICSR2` `AL|STOP|NACKF|
START` bits before the busy-bus check; `riic_wait_for_icsr2()`'s timeout
diagnostic now always prints `ICSR2`/`ICCR2`/`ICCR1`; and
`riic_i2c_raw_read()`'s `ICMR3.ACKBT`/`ICCR2.SP` register-set ordering
is fixed to set-then-read (matching the RIIC master-receive flowchart
and the already-correct `drivers/i2c/rz_riic.c riic_receive_data()`).
That last change is protocol correctness, not the cure for a
separately-observed bit-7 loss on long reads (bytes at offset
`0x0D`/`0x0E` losing bit 7 on a 16-byte burst) -- a systematic sweep
across CKS values (above) reproduced the identical corruption with and
without the reorder, so the reorder is kept on its own merits but the
bit-7 mechanism itself is unconfirmed pending a scope capture of the
affected bytes.

**DEEPX rail bench-PASSED on silicon, E1M-V2M103 (v6).**
`board_late_init()` ran for real and brought CH2 up on its own. Console:
`ALP: DA9292 programmed CTRL_01=0x01 VOUT_CH2=0x96/0x96` then `ALP:
DEEPX rail 0.75V up (PG)`. Read back after boot: `CTRL_01` `0x03`,
`VOUT_CH2` `0x96/0x96`, `STATUS_00` `0x03` (`CH2_PG` set, no UV/OV/OC),
`STATUS_01` `0x00`; the DEEPX bucks surfaced on `BRD_I2C` once `P64`
went high, all present and matching their known roles: `0x44` `0x82`,
`0x48` `0x5a`, `0x4F` `0x14`.

The PCIe step (`alp_deepx_pcie_bringup()`, patch `0001`) did not run on
this pass -- the on-module EEPROM manifest is blank, so the
EEPROM-manifest gate never opens; `CONFIG_ALP_E1M_DEEPX_RAIL` on its own
is enough to run the rail step, but the PCIe path still needs a
programmed manifest, unrelated to this patch. BENCH-PENDING: PCIe, once
a programmed EEPROM manifest is available to test against.

**Patch md5s (current):** `0002` `c546f00cabca346e335febd21ecbc440`,
`0004` `269fc80793f33514871704d3c1f4fc73`, `0006`
`79cce6934ecf6b205e5017866634d8bd`. `0004` applies cleanly on top of the
corrected `0002` and the meta-renesas PMIC-I2C-removal patch, against
`renesas-u-boot-cip` `bcf29d98`.

The `0005`/`0006` comments in
`meta-alp-sdk/recipes-bsp/u-boot/u-boot_%.bbappend` and the pull-up
comment in
`meta-alp-sdk/recipes-kernel/linux/linux-renesas/e1m-x-evk.dtsi` are
updated to match this state.

### Fixed — AEN I2C pinctrl comments contradicted each other on pull direction, and an E8-only bench citation leaked into every AEN board tree (#2046)

`scripts/gen_zephyr_board.py`'s two on-module I2C pinctrl groups explained
the same DSC pull-direction encoding two different ways. The BRD_I2C group
said `bias-pull-up` is DSC=1, a real pull-up; the `e1m_i2c0` group said the
opposite — that upstream `pinctrl_soc.h`'s encoding "reads inverted vs the
Alif pad hardware" and that `bias-pull-up` gives a dead bus, a claim
`examples/aen/aen-eeprom-manifest`'s overlay repeated verbatim. Reading
Zephyr's actual `soc/alif/ensemble/pinctrl_soc.h` settles it: its
`ALIF_PINCTRL_BIAS_CFG()` macro (lines 44-48) maps `bias-pull-up` -> DSC=1
and `bias-pull-down` -> DSC=2 unconditionally, exactly matching the field's
own comment at line 24 — there is no inversion anywhere in that file. The
BRD_I2C group's reading was right; the `e1m_i2c0` group's "inverted
encoding" explanation was not, and is retracted. The dead-bus report that
explanation was invented to justify is left UNCONFIRMED, not disproven —
nobody has re-run `bias-pull-up` on that bus in a controlled trial since —
because an honest open question is the right outcome here, not a second
invented explanation. Both groups (`scripts/gen_zephyr_board.py:1101` and
`scripts/gen_zephyr_board.py:1172`), the checked-in `E1M-AEN801` board
trees, the three verbatim-copied example overlays (`aen-eeprom-manifest`,
`aen-i2c2-eeprom-regcheck`, `aen-eeprom-provision`), and
`docs/aen-bench-bringup.md`'s matching bullet now carry the corrected
explanation. No emitted pad VALUE changed: `bias-pull-up` on P7_0/P7_1 and
`bias-pull-down` on P5_6/P5_7 are unchanged and still bench-proven correct.

Separately, the `e1m_i2c0` group cited "bench-validated 2026-06-15 on the
E8" unconditionally, so an `E1M-AEN301` (E3) board tree would carry an
E8-only bench result as if it were family-wide the moment E3 gains a
`zephyr_peripherals_dtsi` — the same class of leak #1988 fixed for
`rtc_alarm.risk` with a per-part map.
`metadata/e1m_modules/aen/on-module-links.yaml:195-198`'s `e1m_i2c0` entry
now carries a `bench_validation:` map keyed by the SoC's own `part`
designator, same pattern as `rtc_alarm.risk`. Unlike that fix, a part with
no entry does NOT get silence: the E8 citation still appears, qualified
with an explicit "NOT been independently repeated on the `<part>`"
statement, because the emitted pad value is unchanged and correct for
every part — only the claim of which silicon it was measured on was wrong.
Found while hand-porting alp-sdk#2036 into tan-cli
(alplabai/tan-cli#1251), where tan's own regression guard against E8 facts
in non-E8 trees tripped on the citation.

### Fixed — SD peripheral clock gate was never enabled; SD is now disabled entirely on the E1M-EVK 2626-R2 (#2051)

**Renamed:** `examples/aen/aen-sdcard-readout` is now
`examples/aen/aen-sdhc-probe` — the maintainer's call, so the name says
what the app actually is (register-level SD controller probes, inert
until the EVK's SD mux is reworked) rather than implying a working
card-readout path. Every live reference (docs, `testcase.yaml` ids, the
bench app list, the app's own `CMakeLists.txt` project name) moved with
it; only already-released/historical mentions of the old name (e.g. in
other closed issues' own changelog fragments) were left as-is.

**SD is disabled entirely on the E1M-EVK 2626-R2 — a hardware defect, not a
firmware gap.** The 74LVC157 SDIO mux (`U38`/`U39`) has **no
high-impedance state**: with its `/E` ENABLE input HIGH, its Y outputs are
FORCED LOW, not released — this part's datasheet gives no Hi-Z condition
in its function table at all. `U38`/`U39`'s outputs are the **SoC-facing**
nets (`E1M_CLK`, `E1M_CMD`, `E1M_D3..D0`, `E1M_SDIO_RST`), so those nets
are held low by the mux whenever it is powered, **regardless of ENABLE**.
Two in-tree comments previously claimed the opposite (`/E = 1` → Hi-Z,
"isolated, safe-default") — corrected in
`include/alp/boards/alp_e1m_evk.h` and `docs/cc3501e-bridge.md`. Given
that, leaving the SD host controller enabled and merely avoiding the mux
ENABLE write (an earlier revision of this fix) was not enough: applying SD
pinctrl and starting the identification clock at `POST_KERNEL` would still
fight the mux's held-low outputs. `sdhc0` now stays
`status = "disabled"` (the shared SoC dtsi's own default) on both
`examples/aen/aen-sdhc-probe` and `examples/aen/aen-evk-demo`'s board
overlays for this board, so no SD pinctrl is applied and no SDCLK is ever
emitted.

**Pins the firmware now leaves untouched, on both examples:** `P14_1`
(`SD_CLK`), `P14_0` (`SD_CMD`), `P13_0..P13_3` (`SD_D0..D3`), `P14_2`
(`SD_RST`), and E1M `IO20` (the mux ENABLE, → CC3501E `GPIO_26`). In
`aen-sdhc-probe` specifically, the CC3501E inter-chip SPI1 link
(`P14_4..P14_7`), `WIFI_EN`/`E_WIFI.NRST` (LP-GPIO) and `READY` (`P2_6`)
are ALSO untouched now — removed from the overlay entirely, not merely
undriven, once the bridge bring-up they existed for was dropped from
`main()` (see above). **Still muxed to a peripheral:** `aen-evk-demo`'s
other thirteen phases are unaffected, including its own use of the same
CC3501E bridge (phase 8) for Wi-Fi/BLE.

**Root cause, still real and still fixed independent of the above:**
`CLKCTL_PER_MST.PERIPH_CLK_ENA` bit 16 (`SDC_CKEN`) was never gated on, so
the DWC SDHC block was entirely unclocked — every register, including
read-only `CAPABILITIES1`, read `0x00000000`. Fixed by declaring `sdhc0`
once, in the shared SoC dtsi with `clocks = <&clockctrl ALIF_SDC_CLK>`
(`zephyr/dts/alif/ensemble_e8_peripherals.dtsi:665` ("sdhc0: sdhc@48102000 {")),
and calling `clock_control_on()` as the first action in `sdhc_dwc_init()`
(`zephyr/drivers/sdhc/sdhc_dwc.c`). **This explains the all-zero
readback on E1M-AEN803 serial 2026W36-0002 only** — it does not close the original open question, a
`SW_RST_CMD`=1 reading on a block this app's own earlier diagnostics show
was clocked. **Nothing here has been run on real hardware as of this
head.**

**Reset-path hardening**, found while chasing the symptom before the clock
gate was identified: `sdhc_dwc_hw_reset()` polls only the reset bit(s) it
wrote and names which bit is stuck on a timeout; `sdhc_dwc_reset()`
reconfigures and syncs its `data->ios` cache even on a timeout, under
`data->lock`, and on failure now sets the cached clock to `UINT32_MAX`
rather than `0` — `0` is itself a real, requestable "disable the clock"
value, so leaving it there could make a later real request for `0` compare
equal to the invalidated cache and skip reprogramming
(`zephyr/drivers/sdhc/sdhc_dwc.c:772-786`); `sdhc_dwc_set_io()` takes the
same lock for its whole read-modify-write.

**Example rework.** Both examples' overlays drop the now-pointless `P14_2`
GPIO mux group, the `gpio14` enable, and (in `aen-sdhc-probe`) the
`alp,pin-array` `SD_RST` slot. `aen-sdhc-probe`'s probes are now
compile-time conditional on `sdhc0` being enabled
(`examples/aen/aen-sdhc-probe/src/main.c:423` ("int main(void)")) — with
it disabled (as on this board), `main()` compiles down to the clock-gate
proof below rather than the full probe set. The CC3501E bridge bring-up,
PING wait, meta handshake, and SE clock-cycle diagnostic are removed
entirely from this app: nothing downstream needs the bridge once the mux
is never touched.

**Clock-gate proof, added after review, still pad-free.** The fix above
(`clock_control_on()` in `sdhc_dwc_init()`) had not been run on real
silicon on any previous head of this branch, and `sdhc0` staying disabled
means the normal probe set never reaches it either. `main()`'s disabled-
board branch
(`examples/aen/aen-sdhc-probe/src/main.c:423` ("int main(void)")) now
reads `CLKCTL_PER_MST` (`0x4903F00C`) and `CAPABILITIES1`
(`0x48102040`), calls `clock_control_on()` for `ALIF_SDC_CLK` against the
`clockctrl` device directly, re-reads both registers, and prints an
explicit, grep-able verdict on whether bit 16 (`SDC_CKEN`) went clear to
set and whether `CAPABILITIES1` went `0x00000000` to non-zero. Neither
register access nor the `clock_control_on()` call applies SD pinctrl or
touches a single SD pad: `CLKCTL_PER_MST` is a SoC-level system-control
register, gating the block's internal clock only, and pinctrl is applied
solely by the SDHC driver's own init, which is never built while `sdhc0`
stays disabled. No expected capability word is asserted anywhere in this
code -- the silicon's own value is printed and left to stand as the
evidence, so a guessed constant never masquerades as a real measurement.
This proves the controller becomes addressable; it does **not** prove a
card enumerates, and says so in its own printed output and in
`examples/aen/aen-sdhc-probe/README.md`.
`examples/aen/aen-sdhc-probe/prj.conf` gains `CONFIG_CLOCK_CONTROL=y`
(the `clockctrl` device is otherwise only pulled in via `CONFIG_SDHC_DWC`
itself, which never selects while `sdhc0` is disabled), and
`sdhc-build-coverage.overlay` gains an explicit, spelled-out hazard
comment (SoC driving HIGH into `U38`/`U39` driving LOW on six pads at
once) so the build-only, never-flashed status of that overlay cannot be
missed. `sdhc0` stays `status = "disabled"` on both real board overlays;
nothing flashable enables it.

**Measured values from a bench run against this head:**
`<PLACEHOLDER -- bench run pending; fill in `CLKCTL_PER_MST`/`CAPABILITIES1`
before/after and the printed verdict line verbatim once the bench agent
reports it>`.
`aen-evk-demo`'s SD phase is unchanged from the previous revision of this
fix (still an unconditional `SKIPPED`,
`examples/aen/aen-evk-demo/src/main.c:2855` ("static phase_verdict_t phase_sdcard(demo_ctx_t *ctx)")) —
it drops its now-dead `<zephyr/storage/disk_access.h>` /
`<zephyr/drivers/disk.h>` / `<zephyr/fs/fs.h>` / `<ff.h>` includes and the
disk/FatFs `prj.conf` block, which also drops this app's dependency on the
`fatfs` west module entirely.

**Driver build coverage.** With `sdhc0` disabled in both examples' real
overlays, neither build reaches `CONFIG_SDHC_DWC` any more, so the #1097
orphan-section link regression (`CONFIG_SDHC_DWC_ADMA`'s descriptor table
landing in an empty-named linker section) lost its only coverage. Restored
via a second, build-only twister scenario,
`alp_sdk.examples.aen.sdhc_probe.aen.sdhc_build_coverage`
(`examples/aen/aen-sdhc-probe/testcase.yaml`), which layers a new
`sdhc-build-coverage.overlay` on top of the real board overlay to
re-enable `sdhc0` for that scenario only — never the app's real
configuration, never flashed. Verified locally: this scenario builds and
links clean with `CONFIG_SDHC_DWC=y`.

### Changed — CC3501E bridge reaches 2 MB/s: settles counted from the last transfer, the CRC hidden inside them, and shorter gates for fast firmware (#2052)

On E1M-AEN803 2026W36-0009, 4092-byte `STREAM_WRITE` frames went from
1.27 MB/s to about 2.01 MB/s against cc3501e-bridge-firmware #155 (TCM
per-frame path, slicing-by-4 request CRC, SPI driver in code TCM).

- **New `alp_uptime_us()`.** It is a microsecond counterpart of
  `alp_uptime_ms()`: cycle-counter backed on Zephyr where a 64-bit cycle
  counter exists (AEN), `CLOCK_MONOTONIC` on Linux, and the stub's
  microsecond clock elsewhere.
- **Inter-phase settles count from the end of the previous transfer**, not
  from the moment the gate is called. `cc3501e_t` records
  `last_xfer_end_us`, so host work done between two phases counts toward the
  settle instead of adding to it.
- **The request CRC is split around the header.** The header and the first
  half of the payload are CRC'd before the request header, and the rest
  after it, so most of the ~150 µs CRC runs inside the two settles.
- **The shared CRC-16 uses slicing-by-4 with one 32-bit load per step.**
  About 150 µs per 4 KiB frame on the M55-HE (179 µs single-table,
  ~280 µs before that).
- **Firmware reporting `ALP_CC3501E_CAP_FAST_REPLY` gets shorter waits:**
  a 50 µs phase settle (was 250 µs), and a reply gate rising from 200 µs at
  536 B to 450 µs at 4092 B (was 800 µs). Measured need: 10 to 25 µs for
  the settle, and 300 to 400 µs for the reply at 4092 B. Firmware without
  the capability keeps 250 µs and the 2048 B / 2000 µs plateau.

Per-frame breakdown at 4092 B (µs): settle and first half-CRC 77, header 11,
second half-CRC plus copy 15, payload 1317 (25 MHz wire), reply gate 450,
reply header 11, settle 50, reply 14.

### Changed — CC3501E bridge reaches 1.27 MB/s: faster host path, a SPI FIFO fix, and a shorter reply gate for fast firmware (#2052)

On E1M-AEN803 2026W36-0009, 4092-byte `STREAM_WRITE` frames went from
561 KB/s to 1,276,266-1,277,817 B/s (3 of 3 clean sweeps). That needs this
change plus cc3501e-bridge-firmware `perf/bridge-hot-path-ram`.

Host side, per 4092-byte frame:

- **`spi_dw_alif`: the polled loops no longer overflow the RX FIFO.** The
  refill budget counted the TX and RX FIFO levels but not the frame sitting
  in the shift register. A loop fast enough to keep the TX FIFO full (seen
  at `-O2`) then had one frame more in flight than the RX FIFO holds. RX
  never completed, and the transfer ended in `packed transfer stalled` /
  `rc=-4`.
- The request payload is clocked TX-only (`rx = NULL`), because nothing
  reads the slave's dummy bytes. Without RX drains the polled loop runs at
  wire speed: 1.31 ms for 4094 B at 25 MHz, down from 1.91 ms.
- Only the bytes each read phase clocks are cleared. A `memset` of the whole
  4100-byte scratch buffer cost up to 165 µs per request under `-Os`.
- The shared CRC-16 uses a lookup table (see the #1677 CRC fragment).

Reply-header gate:

- Old firmware: the 2000 µs plateau now starts at 2048 B. Interpolated,
  2048 B only got about 970 µs, and 2048-byte frames caused 4 of the 6
  `rc=-5` wedges seen on 2026-09-28.
- New firmware: firmware that reports the new
  `ALP_CC3501E_CAP_FAST_REPLY` capability (bit `0x00001000`) runs its
  per-frame path from RAM and arms the reply for a 4 KiB frame in 300 to
  600 µs. `cc3501e_reset()` reads the capability, and the gate then rises
  from 200 µs at 536 B to 800 µs at 4092 B, about 1.8× the measured need.
  Firmware without the bit keeps the conservative gate.
- The flag is stored in `cc3501e_t::fw_fast_reply`, in padding, so the
  struct layout does not move.

`aen-cc3501e-socket-throughput` now builds the way a product runs:
`CONFIG_DCACHE=y` (the board default), `CONFIG_SPEED_OPTIMIZATIONS=y` and
`CONFIG_SPI_DW_ALIF_PACK32=y`. With the D-cache off, the same link measures
~563 KB/s, because the host becomes CPU-bound. `aen-bench-shared.conf` still
forces the cache off, so a Flow C measurement must pass `-DCONFIG_DCACHE=y`.

New host-driver ztests pin the 2048 B plateau and the fast-reply table.
All nine CC3501E suites pass (535 cases).

### Documented — AEN `memory_map:` gaps investigated; #1975's per-unit evidence corrected (#2053)

`E1M-AEN803.yaml` and `E1M-AEN801.yaml` both carry `mram_main.base:
"TBD"` and neither represents the external OSPI0 HyperRAM/NOR in
`memory_map:`. Both were investigated for this issue; neither ships a
data change here, because both collide with real invariants elsewhere
in the tree rather than a false positive in a check:

- Resolving `mram_main.base` to `0x80000000` is correct for IPC
  carve-out purposes (`scripts/alp_orchestrate/aperture.py`'s
  `classify_region()` already has a whole-device-alias exception for
  it), but trips `scripts/gen_zephyr_board.py::_aen_check_map_overlaps()`,
  which has no such exception and reads the resolved region as
  overlapping `mcuboot` -- a real collision that function's own
  docstring silently relied on `mram_main.base` staying non-integer to
  avoid. Needs a fix to that function before `base` can resolve.
  `metadata/e1m_modules/E1M-AEN801.yaml`/`E1M-AEN803.yaml` document the
  finding in place.
- A `hyperram` `memory_map:` row for `E1M-AEN803` (base `0xa0000000`,
  64 MiB, confirmed against Alif's own Linux devicetree) was tried and
  reverted: its end address `0xa4000000` becomes the highest
  `base + size` across the whole table, and
  `scripts/check_atoc_reservation.py`'s ATOC top-anchor rule requires
  whichever region owns that file-wide maximum to be named `atoc`
  regardless of aperture -- filed as alp-sdk#2069. Both external
  memories' population facts stay correctly recorded in
  `on_module.hyperram` / `on_module.ospi_memories.ospi0`.

What does ship: `metadata/boards/e1m-evk.yaml`'s alp-sdk#1975 record now
also carries a second data point -- a second board (serial
`2026W36-0002`) censused 2026-09-12 found all six INA236
answering, confirming the missing-INA236 condition is per-unit, not
batch-wide or design-level.

### Fixed — `mram_main.base` resolved from the `"TBD"` sentinel to `0x80000000` on all seven AEN presets (#2053)

`mram_main.base` stayed the literal string `"TBD"` in every AEN SoM preset
(`metadata/e1m_modules/E1M-AEN301.yaml:198`,
`metadata/e1m_modules/E1M-AEN401.yaml:187`,
`metadata/e1m_modules/E1M-AEN501.yaml:184`,
`metadata/e1m_modules/E1M-AEN601.yaml:191`,
`metadata/e1m_modules/E1M-AEN701.yaml:219`,
`metadata/e1m_modules/E1M-AEN801.yaml:290`,
`metadata/e1m_modules/E1M-AEN803.yaml:236` ("name: mram_main, base: 0x80000000")), blocked twice over: first by
`scripts/gen_zephyr_board.py::_aen_check_map_overlaps()` having no
whole-device-alias exception (fixed by #2073), then by
`scripts/check_atoc_reservation.py`'s top-anchor rule being unscoped to the
SoC's declared MRAM aperture (fixed by #2069). With both landed on `dev`,
`base` now resolves to `0x80000000` on all seven presets — not copied
across, but confirmed independently per SoC: every
`metadata/socs/alif/ensemble/{e3,e4,e5,e6,e7,e8}.json` declares
`"soc_flash_base": 2147483648`, and `scripts/gen_zephyr_board.py`'s own
`_AEN_MRAM_BASE` constant carries the same value, sourced from upstream
Zephyr's `mram: flash@80000000` node present in every Ensemble SoC dtsi.

**Measured effect, re-run across all seven presets, not assumed from the
#2073 single-preset (E1M-AEN801) measurement:** identical across all
seven. No `ipc:` entry moves off `status: blocked` on any of them — but
*why* it stays blocked changes, and that change broke three tests that
asserted the old reason (see "Test fallout" below). Before this change,
`mram_main`'s `base: "TBD"` made its derived class `unresolved`, and it
was disqualified there by its authored `write_authority: composite`
(never `customer_runtime`) — `scripts/alp_orchestrate/carveout.py`'s
`_region_ipc_eligibility()` `cls == "unresolved"` tail. After, its
resolved extent equals the SoC's declared App MRAM aperture exactly (the
whole-device alias), so `classify_region()` calls it `flash` outright and
the `cls == "flash"` branch disqualifies it **unconditionally** —
`write_authority` is not even consulted once `base` resolves. No existing
carve-out candidate (`mcuboot`, `he_slot0`, `hp_slot0`, `reserved`,
`storage`, `atoc`) gains or loses an address; those six rows are
unchanged on every preset. What changes on all seven: `mram_main`'s own
`memory_map` row (`kind`/`status` go from `unresolved`/`unresolved` to
`flash`/`ok` and it gains `base: 2147483648`), and the *reason text*
every blocked AEN `ipc:` entry cites for `mram_main`, from "has an
unresolved base ('TBD') so containment against the declared MRAM
aperture can't be verified, and its authored write_authority is
'composite', not 'customer_runtime'" to "[0x80000000, 0x80580000) is
flash-class (contained in the SoC's declared on-die MRAM aperture) --
not safe as an IPC carve-out target". Same verdict, different (and now
unconditional) reason. Confirmed against `E1M-AEN301/401/501/601/701`
and `E1M-AEN803` by hand (no shipped example `board.yaml` declares an
`ipc:` carve-out for any of these six SKUs -- `E1M-AEN301` and
`E1M-AEN401` each have an example targeting them, but neither one
exercises `ipc:`) using a synthetic `m55_hp`+`m55_he` rpmsg `board.yaml`
per SKU; not committed, since it duplicates coverage this repo doesn't
otherwise ship for those SKUs.

**Test fallout, root-caused and fixed, not papered over.** Three tests
asserted the pre-change reason/verdict against a REAL preset that no
longer produces it:
`tests/scripts/test_orchestrate_memory_regions.py::test_a_region_whose_base_does_not_resolve_is_kind_unresolved`
and `::test_an_unresolved_base_carries_status_and_reason_but_no_base`
(both against `E1M-AEN301`'s `mram_main`) and
`tests/scripts/test_orchestrate_memory.py::test_resolve_carve_outs_blocks_on_unmapped_base`
(against `E1M-AEN701`'s, asserting `"write_authority is 'composite'" in
entry.reason`, which no longer appears). Re-pointed at synthetic rows
(`memory._resolved_row()` / `carveout._region_ipc_eligibility()` direct
calls, the file's own established pattern) rather than flipped to assert
the new value against the same real preset — flipping would have
deleted the ADR-0034-clause-4 "unresolved base" witness entirely, since
no shipped preset authors one any more. A fourth test,
`test_size_is_emitted_even_when_the_base_is_unresolved`, kept passing but
had gone vacuous for the same reason and is moved onto the same synthetic
row. A fifth gap — `carveout.py`'s `write_authority`-present-but-wrong
refusal on the `cls == "unresolved"` tail (the exact leg `E1M-AEN701`'s
`mram_main` used to exercise) — had no OTHER test in the tree covering
it once that real-preset producer disappeared; added
`test_unresolved_base_with_write_authority_not_customer_runtime_refuses`
to `tests/scripts/test_orchestrate_carveout_aperture_ordering.py`'s
`TestUnresolvedLegOrdering`, proven to fail under a mutation that always
grants eligibility on that branch.

**Coverage gap this leaves, not silently absorbed.** Resolving the last
`"TBD"` base removed the only shipped preset that ever authored an
unresolved `memory_map:` base, so it also removed the only end-to-end
path through the unresolved-base legs of `memory.py::_resolved_row()`
and `carveout.py::_region_ipc_eligibility()`'s `cls == "unresolved"`
tail. The three tests above now pin those legs by calling the private
helpers directly instead of through a real preset, which proves the
legs themselves still behave correctly but no longer proves the WIRING
that routes an unresolved row into them — a future change that filtered
unresolved rows out earlier (e.g. in `carveout.py::_candidate_regions()`,
before `_region_ipc_eligibility()` is ever reached) would leave every
current pin green while the guard on a live preset went dead. alp-sdk#2096
proposes a synthetic *preset* fixture (not a synthetic row) that keeps an
unresolved base in the tree purely to exercise that routing again,
without reintroducing a real unresolved sentinel into any shipped SoM.

Regenerated and diffed rather than assumed cosmetic: the `rpmsg-aen` and
`mproc-mailbox` `system-manifest` and `build-plan` `--emit` snapshots
(`tests/fixtures/emit-snapshots/`) are the only four of the gate's 37
cases that changed, exactly as #2073 predicted. Every other `--emit`
surface — `soc_caps.h`, board routes headers, the CC3501E GPIO route
tables, the pinmux/support-matrix/portability-matrix/catalog/error-catalog
docs, and the ABI snapshot — regenerates byte-identical; none of them
consume `memory_map.mram_main`. A bench build
(`scripts/bench/aen/build.sh examples/aen/aen-adc-regcheck` for
`alp_e1m_aen801_m55_he/ae822fa0e5597ls0/rtss_he`,
`-DCONFIG_COMPILER_WARNINGS_AS_ERRORS=y`) produces a byte-identical
`zephyr.dts` and the same 81848 B / 31.22% FLASH usage before and after —
`mram_main` is excluded from the disjoint-slot0 partition table (only the
six fine-grained regions feed it), so resolving its `base` has no DTS
effect at all.

`tests/scripts/test_gen_zephyr_board.py`'s `TestAenMemoryMapValidation`
whole-device-alias tests (added by #2073) mutated `E1M-AEN801.yaml`'s
`"TBD"` line to a resolved one as their own setup; with the preset now
resolved on disk that substitution's anchor text no longer exists, so the
four tests are updated to start from the already-resolved fixture instead
of re-deriving it.

`changelog.d/1430.md` cited two lines inside `E1M-AEN801.yaml` (the
`storage`/`atoc` rows) that shifted when this change's comment edit
shrank the block above them (298/299 → 288/289); re-resolved in the same
change per the fragment convention.

Prose swept for the same reason across every file that narrated the
`"TBD"`/`write_authority`-composite state as current:
`examples/multicore/rpmsg-aen/board.yaml`,
`examples/multicore/mproc-mailbox/board.yaml` (both claimed `mram_main`

`scripts/check_atoc_reservation.py`, `scripts/alp_orchestrate/aperture.py`,

External OSPI0 memories (`hyperram`, `ospi0` NOR) remain a deliberate

### Fixed — `docs/bench/model-perf-capture.md`'s blocker 3 claimed `<alp/inference.h>` has no latency accessor; it has had one since #1541 (#2054)

The tier-2 model-perf capture doc listed three open blockers gating a bench
capture campaign. The third, "No timing harness," said `<alp/inference.h>`
"exposes no latency accessor" and that "the first capture campaign has to
lift one" itself before it could fill any `perf.latency_ms` field. That
stopped being true on 2026-08-18: commit `409e4c31`
("`feat(inference): add alp_inference_last_invoke_latency_us accessor
(#1541)`") added `alp_inference_last_invoke_latency_us(alp_inference_t *inf,
uint64_t *out_us)` at `include/alp/inference.h:481`, and
`docs/abi-markers.md:69` already names it "the model-perf-capture latency
accessor" in the `inference.h` classification row. The accessor is wired
into both dispatchers (`src/inference_dispatch.c` for Zephyr/M-class,
`src/yocto/inference_yocto.c` for Yocto/A-class) and the stub
(`src/common/stub/stub_inference.c`), so the doc was describing a gap that
had already closed.

Verified the accessor's actual contract before rewriting anything, rather
than trusting the doc's paraphrase: it reports only the LAST successful
`alp_inference_invoke()` call — no history, no running statistics, so a
caller building a distribution reads it once per invoke and keeps the
samples itself. `out_us` is filled in whole MICROSECONDS, rounded to
nearest. It returns `ALP_OK` with a real duration once any invoke has
completed `ALP_OK` on the handle, or one of `ALP_ERR_INVAL` (`out_us` is
NULL), `ALP_ERR_NOT_READY` (`inf` is NULL/closed, or no invoke has ever
completed `ALP_OK` on this handle — never returned merely because the last
invoke was slow), or `ALP_ERR_NOSUPPORT` (a stub build with no inference
backend compiled in at all, so there is no timing mechanism to have
populated). It carries a function-level `[ABI-EXPERIMENTAL]` marker; the
file-level marker on `inference.h` stays `[ABI-STABLE]`.

Blocker 3 had no residual real blocker once the false claim was removed —
the recipe's step 4 now names the exact API and header instead of "once it
exists," and review of the first draft of this fix surfaced three
correctness traps in that step that needed closing before it could be
trusted, so the shipped step 4 also covers all three. First, checking only
the accessor's own return code is not enough: `alp_inference_invoke()` can
itself return `ALP_ERR_TIMEOUT` (NPU stuck) or `ALP_ERR_IO` (NPU error),
and a failed invoke does not update the accessor's stored value, so
reading it after a failed invoke silently returns the PREVIOUS successful
invoke's duration with `ALP_OK` — recording that as the new sample
duplicates an old value and drops exactly the invoke that blew its timing
budget, biasing `p95` low in a way `scripts/validate_metadata.py` cannot
detect. The step now requires checking `alp_inference_invoke()`'s own
return first and discarding/re-running on anything but `ALP_OK`, never
recording. Second, "divide by 1000" without a type/rounding contract
invites `out_us / 1000` as C integer division on the `uint64_t` reading,
which truncates every value to a whole millisecond (a 1500 us invoke
under-reports as `1` ms instead of `1.5`, a 33% error that still passes
`metadata/schemas/model-perf-v1.schema.json`'s `latency_ms` block — its
fields are typed `number` with only a positivity/non-negativity floor, no
precision requirement — and can even collapse `stdev` to `0` on a tight
distribution). The step now spells out a floating-point division by
`1000.0` with the fractional result kept, mirroring step 3's existing
worked-example standard of care for its bytes→KiB conversion. Third,
`ALP_OK` from the accessor is necessary but not sufficient: on a target at
60 MHz or below under stock Kconfig, or any target without
`CONFIG_TIMER_HAS_64BIT_CYCLE_COUNTER`, the hardware cycle counter wraps
modulo 2^32 and the accessor reports `ALP_OK` with a plausible-looking but
too-small duration, not an error — now called out explicitly, alongside a
pointer at the two in-tree examples (`examples/camera-vision/ai-object-detection-realtime/src/main.c`
and `examples/camera-vision/ai-camera-viewer/src/inference_loop.c`) NOT to
copy, since both predate this accessor, hand-roll `k_cycle_get_32()` /
`k_cyc_to_us_floor32()`, and discard `alp_inference_invoke()`'s status via
`(void)`.

The doc's "three blockers" language was renumbered to "two blockers"
throughout `docs/bench/model-perf-capture.md`; blockers 1 (the vela
profile question) and 2 (the const-region question) are untouched and
remain open — neither was re-checked as part of this change.
`metadata/schemas/model-perf-v1.schema.json`'s `latency_ms` field
description carried the same stale claim ("no AEN example times an
inference today and `<alp/inference.h>` exposes no latency accessor") and
is corrected too; the field stays schema-optional, now because no bench
capture has run yet rather than because no accessor exists. The pending,
still-unreleased `changelog.d/1520.md` fragment repeated the identical
false "three blockers" / "no latency accessor" claim in its own prose (it
folds into the same `[Unreleased]` section as this fragment and #1541's),
so it is corrected in place to "two blockers" with the accessor clause
dropped, rather than left to ship a self-contradicting release note.

This is a documentation-only correction. No `perf` data was added, changed,
or measured on silicon, and `metadata/model_perf/` still ships empty — this
issue is deliberately separate from the bench data campaign tracked under
#1894.

### Fixed — the ATOC unwritable-TMPDIR test now skips where its precondition cannot be built, instead of failing (#2055)

`test_atoc_guard_aborts_when_tmpdir_is_unwritable`
(`tests/scripts/test_bench_jlink_connect_guard.py:1041`) builds its
precondition with `unwritable.chmod(0o500)` and then expects
`bench_atoc_replace_guard()`'s `mktemp` to fail inside that directory. On
Windows that precondition never holds: `os.chmod` only toggles
`FILE_ATTRIBUTE_READONLY`, and that attribute does not stop a directory from
accepting new entries. Measured on Windows 11 with Python 3.12.10, a
directory chmod'ed `0o500` reads back `0o555`, `os.access(dir, os.W_OK)`
returns `True`, and a file writes into it without complaint. `mktemp`
therefore succeeded, the guard returned `0`, and the assertion demanding `5`
failed with the transcript path — `unwritable-tmp/test-tag-atoc-before.BoNwrZ`
— naming the very file that proves the directory was still writable.

This never reddened CI, and the reason it did not is unrelated to the defect:
GitHub's `windows-latest` resolves `bash` to the WSL launcher with no
distribution installed, so `_NEEDS_BASH`
(`tests/scripts/test_bench_jlink_connect_guard.py:60`) skips the whole module
there before this test is reached. On a Windows developer box with a real
`bash` on `PATH` — Git Bash or MSYS2, the setup `docs/cross-platform-setup.md`
describes — the module does not skip, and this one test fails among 43 that
pass.

The fix follows the discipline the file already sets for `bash` itself:
probe the capability by performing it rather than by trusting the platform.
`_dir_still_accepts_a_new_file()`
(`tests/scripts/test_bench_jlink_connect_guard.py:68`) creates a probe file
in the directory after
the `chmod`; if the write succeeds, the unwritable-TMPDIR precondition does
not hold on this host and the test skips with a reason that says so, naming
this issue. Where `chmod` does make the directory refuse a write, the probe
fails, and the test runs and asserts exactly what it asserted before —
including the specific `cannot create the pre-write ATOC transcript` abort
message that distinguishes this failure mode from the unrelated downstream
redirect failures an earlier revision of the test could not tell it from.

Because a skip is a weaker outcome than a run, the same `mktemp`-failure
branch now also has a sibling test that needs no mode bits at all:
`test_atoc_guard_aborts_when_tmpdir_does_not_exist`
(`tests/scripts/test_bench_jlink_connect_guard.py:1097`) points `TMPDIR` at a path
that does not exist, which drives the identical `mktemp ... || return 5` line
in `bench_atoc_replace_guard()` and asserts the same two things — the `5` and
the `cannot create the pre-write ATOC transcript` message. That one runs
wherever `bash` runs, so the branch stays covered on the hosts where the
`chmod` route is unavailable, rather than only on POSIX.

A sweep of `tests/scripts/` found one other test building a precondition out
of a restrictive `chmod` —
`tests/scripts/test_kconfig_extra_library_profile_never_raises.py:115`'s
`os.chmod(p, 0)` — and it is already guarded, skipping both on Windows and on
a root caller, so it carries no latent platform dependence. Of the remaining
`chmod` calls, most add the execute bit to a fixture script;
`tests/scripts/test_verify_west_patches.py:119` restores the write bit before
an `rmtree` rather than adding execute. None of them depends on a directory
refusing an entry.

### Fixed — `sdhc_dwc_card_busy()` tested a five-bit CMD+DAT mask for any-bit-high, so an ordinary DAT0-low busy card reported not-busy (#2057)

`sdhc_dwc_card_busy()` (`zephyr/drivers/sdhc/sdhc_dwc.c:986-1015`) tested
`DWC_SDHC_CMD_DATA_LINE_STATUS_Msk` (`0x01F00000U` — DAT`[3:0]` Line Signal
Level at bits `[23:20]` plus CMD Line Signal Level at bit 24, SD Host
Controller Simplified Specification Present State Register, offset `024h`,
section 2.2.9 in v3.00, unchanged through v4.20) and returned "not busy" the
moment *any* of those five bits read high. SD busy signalling — an R1b
response, or write programming — is DAT0 held low while DAT1..DAT3 and CMD
sit high (SD Physical Layer Specification 4.2.4.2). That reads back as
`0x01E00000U`: non-zero, so the old check declared the card not busy while it
was busy. The five-bit group is still the correct test for the CMD11
low-phase check in `sdhc_dwc_set_voltage()` (all five genuinely go low
there); it was simply the wrong test for this function.

`sdhc_dwc.h` gains a DAT0-only accessor derived from the existing
`DWC_SDHC_DAT_LINE_LVL_Pos` field (added in #2042):

```c
#define DWC_SDHC_DAT0_LINE_LVL_Msk BIT(DWC_SDHC_DAT_LINE_LVL_Pos)
```

`sdhc_dwc_card_busy()` now tests that mask alone, and its comments name DAT0
specifically instead of "DAT lines" against a mask that also covered CMD.

**Precedent, for a reader who wants a second data point.** Linux's
`sdhci_card_busy()` masks `SDHCI_DATA_0_LVL_MASK` (`0x00100000`) — cited from
general knowledge, not read from disk; the Linux kernel is not vendored in
this tree. This repo's own `zephyr/drivers/sdhc/sam_sdmmc.c` checks a single
bit, `SDMMC_PSR_DATLL_Pos`, the same DAT0-alone convention.

**Masked, not harmless.** Upstream Zephyr's `sdmmc_wait_ready()`
(`subsys/sd/sd_ops.c`, not vendored in this alp-sdk tree) falls through to
CMD13 polling when `sdhc_card_busy()` says not-busy, so the generic write path
has a backstop and no data-corruption path is named by this fix. The sharper
consequence is the CMD11 post-switch check in `sdmmc_switch_voltage()` (upstream Zephyr
`subsys/sd/sd_ops.c`, not vendored in this alp-sdk tree, around line 397),
which would have accepted "switched successfully"
on a CMD-high/DAT-low reading — exactly the false-positive this defect could
produce. Today the only thing standing between that false success and the bus
is the driver-internal DAT`[3:0]`-all-high poll inside
`sdhc_dwc_set_voltage()`, and that poll is itself unreachable — see #2058.

**Untested on silicon.** No `PSTATE` value has ever been captured from AE822
hardware (`snps,dwc-sdhc` is instantiated by exactly two E1M-AEN801 board
overlays, and SD enumeration has never completed on either — see #2051, the
`SW_RST_CMD` self-clear defect that currently blocks `disk_access_init()`
before any command reaches the busy path). This fix is spec-and-precedent
reasoning, not a bench measurement. Whether the DWC block reports DAT0
identically to the generic SDHCI convention cited above is not established by
this change and should be labelled `untested-on-silicon` until a bench run
reads the register.

Refs #2042, #2058, #2051.

### Fixed — the 1.8V voltage switch polled the line levels with the internal clock stopped, discarded a clock-gate error, and dropped bus power for the whole switch (#2058)

`sdhc_dwc_set_voltage()` (`zephyr/drivers/sdhc/sdhc_dwc.c:196-309`) could not
complete a 1.8V signal-voltage switch even on hardware that reaches it. Three
separate defects sat in the same sequence; this entry fixes all three and
keeps them distinct, because they are not the same bug.

**Defect 1 (the reason the switch cannot complete) — the DAT-line poll ran
with the internal clock stopped.** The generic SD subsystem's
`sdmmc_switch_voltage()` (upstream Zephyr `subsys/sd/sd_ops.c`, not vendored
in this alp-sdk tree) first sets `card->bus_io.clock = 0` and calls
`sdhc_set_io()`, which lands in `sdhc_dwc_set_io()`'s `ios->clock == 0` branch
and calls `sdhc_dwc_disable_clock(regs)`
(`zephyr/drivers/sdhc/sdhc_dwc.c:1094`) — clearing **both**
`DWC_SDHC_CLK_EN_Msk` and `DWC_SDHC_INTERNAL_CLK_EN_Msk` together
(`zephyr/drivers/sdhc/sdhc_dwc.c:169`). `sdmmc_switch_voltage()` then makes a
second `sdhc_set_io()` call to change `signal_voltage`, which clears the
already-clear `DWC_SDHC_CLK_EN_Msk` once more
(`zephyr/drivers/sdhc/sdhc_dwc.c:1071`) and calls `sdhc_dwc_set_voltage()`.
Inside the 1.8V case, the poll's clock re-enable previously set only
`DWC_SDHC_CLK_EN_Msk` — the internal clock was still off from the earlier
call — and the poll ran immediately after. `sdhc_dwc_enable_clock()`, the
function that sets `DWC_SDHC_INTERNAL_CLK_EN_Msk` and waits for
`DWC_SDHC_INTERNAL_CLK_STABLE_Msk`, did not run until `sdhc_dwc_set_io()`
called it *after* `sdhc_dwc_set_voltage()` had already returned
(`zephyr/drivers/sdhc/sdhc_dwc.c:1077`).

Per the SD Host Controller Simplified Specification's Clock Control register,
SD Clock Enable must not be set before Internal Clock Stable reads 1, and
SDCLK is derived from the internal clock. With the internal clock stopped
there is no SDCLK on the bus; per SD Physical Layer Specification 4.2.4.2 the
card drives CMD and DAT`[3:0]` low and only releases them high within 1ms of
SDCLK appearing at the new voltage. The poll therefore observed the lines
still low and timed out after `DWC_SDHC_1P8V_TIMEOUT_US` regardless of which
bits it tested — unconditionally, independent of the #2042 and #2057 fixes.

Fixed by calling `sdhc_dwc_enable_clock(regs)` — which enables the internal
clock, waits for it to report stable, and only then sets
`DWC_SDHC_CLK_EN_Msk` — in place of the bare `DWC_SDHC_CLK_EN_Msk |=` before
the poll, and propagating `-EIO` if the internal clock never reports stable.
The existing 1ms settle (`k_busy_wait(1000)`) and the `DWC_SDHC_1P8V_TIMEOUT_US`
poll loop are otherwise unchanged.

**Defect 2 — `sdhc_dwc_disable_clock()`'s return value was discarded in
`sdhc_dwc_set_io()`'s `ios->clock == 0` branch**
(`zephyr/drivers/sdhc/sdhc_dwc.c:1094`; the other call site,
`zephyr/drivers/sdhc/sdhc_dwc.c:366` inside `sdhc_dwc_clock_set()`, already
checked it). `sdhc_dwc_disable_clock()` returns `false` when
`DWC_SDHC_CMD_INHIBIT_Msk` or `DWC_SDHC_DAT_INHIBIT_Msk` is set — exactly the
state the controller may report while a card holds DAT`[3:0]` low after
CMD11. The gate could then silently not happen while `data->ios.clock` was
still recorded as `0`, leaving the driver's idea of the clock state and the
hardware's diverging with no error anywhere. Fixed by checking the return
value and propagating `-EIO`, matching the existing `:366` call site.

**Defect 3 — bus power (Vdd1) was dropped for the whole switch.**
`sdhc_dwc_set_voltage()` clears `DWC_SDHC_PC_BUS_PWR_VDD1_Msk` unconditionally
on entry, before the `switch (voltage)`. The 1.8V case then wrote
`DWC_SDHC_PC_BUS_VSEL_1V8_Msk` (which does not include the Vdd1 bit) and did
not restore Vdd1 until *after* the `>= 5ms` `DWC_SDHC_1P8V_TIMEOUT_US` gate —
so Vdd1 was off for the whole gate. The SD Host Controller Simplified
Specification's voltage-switch procedure (3.6.1) never has the host remove
Vdd here; only the signalling level changes. If `sd_vdd1_on` gates a load
switch on a given carrier, the previous sequence would have power-cycled the
card mid-CMD11, and any subsequent "success" would be a freshly reset card at
idle rather than a switched one — whether that is the case on any Alp carrier
is not established by this change. Fixed by folding the Vdd1 restore into the
same write that sets the 1.8V VSEL bits, before the gate starts, so Vdd1
stays continuously applied through the switch.

**Not fixed here, and not claimed fixed.** The specification's 3.6.1 also has
the host re-read the 1.8V Signaling Enable bit in `HOST_CTRL2` after the
`>=5ms` gate (abort if the controller cleared it — regulator failure) and,
on any switch failure, fully power-cycle the SD bus before re-initialising at
3.3V. This driver does neither; it returns `-ETIMEDOUT`/`-EIO` and leaves
recovery to the generic layer (upstream Zephyr `subsys/sd/sdmmc.c`, not
vendored in this alp-sdk tree, sets `vol_180_support = false` and returns
`SD_RESTART` — a graceful outcome but not the specification's own one). Left
as TBD — out of scope for this fix, not evaluated here.

**Unreachable on current hardware, for two independent reasons.** SD
enumeration has never completed on E1M-AEN801, the only in-tree consumer of
`snps,dwc-sdhc` — the currently-tracked root cause is #2051 (`SW_RST_CMD`
never self-clears; `SW_RST_R` at register `0x4810202F` stays `0x02`, so
`disk_access_init()` returns `-116`), so `sdmmc_switch_voltage()` is never
reached at all today. **UPDATE (#2051):** the 74LVC157 SDIO mux has no
high-impedance state at all — its outputs face the SoC and are held low
whenever it's powered, regardless of ENABLE — so #2051 went further than
`no-1-8-v;` and disabled `sdhc0` outright (`status = "disabled"`) on both
real board overlays
(`examples/aen/aen-evk-demo/boards/alp_e1m_aen801_m55_he_ae822fa0e5597ls0_rtss_he.overlay`
and
`examples/aen/aen-sdhc-probe/boards/alp_e1m_aen801_m55_he_ae822fa0e5597ls0_rtss_he.overlay`,
renamed from `aen-sdcard-readout`). Neither real overlay sets `no-1-8-v;` any
more; that property now lives only in the build-only, never-flashed
`sdhc-build-coverage.overlay` that keeps `CONFIG_SDHC_DWC` compiling. The
driver still honours the property when it is set
(`zephyr/drivers/sdhc/sdhc_dwc.c:1183-1184` ("props->host_caps.vol_180_support = config->no_1_8_v ? 0 :")),
so the generic SD subsystem would never call `sdmmc_switch_voltage()` for a
build that sets it, even once enumeration completed — the 74LVC157 SDIO mux
on the E1M-AEN801 EVK cannot pass a 1.8V logic level. This fix is correct by
construction against the cited specification text, not verified against
silicon: no `PSTATE` or `CLK_CTRL_R` value has ever been captured from AE822
hardware, and this change was not run on a bench.

Refs #2042, #2057, #2051.

### Fixed — scope the OSPI0 NOR/HyperRAM identity, population, and chip-select claims to the SKU each is actually true for (#2062)

`git grep -n 'R2 BOM'`, `git grep -n MX25UM25645`, and `git grep -n
W958D8NB` against `origin/dev` found sites stating in the present tense
that the E1M-AEN OSPI0 NOR is a Macronix `MX25UM25645GXDI00` populated
(`DNP = 0`) on "the R2 BOM," that its HyperRAM sibling is a Winbond
`W958D8NBYA5I`, or both. Measured contradiction (issue #2041): on
`E1M-AEN803` serial `2026W36-0002`, Flow C ITCM RAM-run, the NOR answered a
JEDEC ID read on OSPI0 **CS1** with `9d 5b 19 10` at `BAUDR=20` (20 MHz),
repeated on the alternate ISSI ReadID opcode `0x9E`. `0x9d` is the ISSI
manufacturer ID; `5b 19` is the `IS25WX256` type/capacity pair -- matching
`metadata/e1m_modules/E1M-AEN803.yaml:59-72`'s `IS25WX256-JHLE` NOR and
`:75-94`'s `S80KS5122GABHM02` (Infineon/Cypress) HyperRAM. Macronix's
manufacturer ID is `0xc2`.

The greppable part-name sites were not the whole defect: `scripts/gen_zephyr_board.py` could still print a population
claim contradicting its own preset (a generated E1M-AEN803 board said
"populated" in its banner and "not populated on this batch" two paragraphs
later, from two separately-hardcoded sentences), and several population
claims the part-name greps cannot reach -- `dram_mbit`/`flash_mbit` values,
a preset's own cross-reference to its sibling SKU -- were left standing.
The list below covers **25 distinct sites across 17 hand-edited
files**, plus 2 regenerated `.dts` files.

Four separate errors were mixed into these sites and are corrected
independently:

1. **Part identity.** Macronix `MX25UM25645GXDI00` -> measured ISSI
   `IS25WX256-JHLE`; Winbond `W958D8NBYA5I` -> measured
   `S80KS5122GABHM02` (Infineon/Cypress) -- cited to #2041, everywhere the
   claim named a SKU/footprint that actually populates OSPI0.
2. **Population.** `metadata/e1m_modules/E1M-AEN801.yaml:60-88` declares
   *both* external memories `assembled: false` (`memory.dram_mbit: 0`,
   `memory.flash_mbit: 0` at `:155-156`) -- E1M-AEN801 runs from the SoC's
   on-die MRAM and populates neither device on any revision as this repo
   models it. "The R2 BOM populates only OSPI0" is false for that SKU;
   every corrected site now says which SKU (E1M-AEN803) the claim is
   actually true for.
3. **Chip select.** Several sites placed the NOR on CS0. The netlist puts
   `U10` (NOR) on `OSPI0_SS1` and `U9` (HyperRAM) on `OSPI0_SS0`; metadata
   was corrected to match in `44200cab` (#1944, #1990, PR #2007); #2041
   confirmed it by distinguishing three `ser` values -- `0x00000002` (CS1)
   drains `9d 5b 19 10`, `0x00000001` (CS0) drains `00 00 00 00`,
   `0x00000000` drains 0/4 with `SR = 0x00000002`.
4. **HyperRAM capacity.** `metadata/e1m_modules/E1M-AEN803.yaml:92`
   measures the fitted HyperRAM at `512` Mbit (64 MiB), not the `256` Mbit
   the Winbond part's own datasheet capacity would have implied --
   `S80KS5122GABHM02` is a larger part than the Winbond one it replaces.

**A true fact used to draw a false conclusion, plus four
population-completeness gaps:**

- **Major.** The populated-case banner and MRAM-only text said "neither
  is used for XIP boot here (OSPI_XIP_SER does not exist on this die
  ...)" and "MRAM-only regardless: ...; OSPI_XIP_SER does not exist on
  this die ..., so ...". "OSPI_XIP_SER does not exist" is a real, cited
  fact for AE822 (Alif `soc_features.h` `SOC_FEAT_OSPI_HAS_XIP_SER (0)`;
  `zephyr/drivers/flash/flash_ospi_alif.c:275-291` cites the same chain)
  -- but it does not prove XIP is impossible on this silicon: Alif's own
  vendor `drivers/source/ospi_psram_xip.c` (around lines 169-173,
  verified against the Alif reference DFP -- not vendored into this
  repo, so not a resolvable in-tree citation) compiles `ospi_control_xip_ss()` out under that
  exact guard and STILL calls `aes_enable_xip()`, and the SDK's own
  `zephyr/drivers/flash/flash_ospi_alif.c:285` -- verified in-tree --
  says AE822 does XiP "through a single FIFO location." The missing
  register rules out only hal_alif's own
  `alif_hal_ospi_xip_enable()`, not XIP on this part -- so the day an
  E1M-AEN803 board tree is committed (#2084), both paragraphs would have
  told customers XIP is impossible on that SKU's real, populated part,
  which is false. Fixed: `_AEN_OSPI_XIP_GAP` now states the real,
  non-overreaching reasons -- hal_alif's `alif_hal_ospi_xip_enable()`
  targets the absent `XIP_SER` register, and `flash_ospi_alif.c` ships
  no `flash_driver_api` at all (#915) -- true regardless of the die's
  own XIP capability, so it can never overreach the way the die-level
  fact alone did. `tests/scripts/test_gen_zephyr_board.py`'s populated-
  preset test, which had locked in the old wording, updated to match and
  to assert the die-level fact is never followed by a bare "so".
- **Minor 1 -- an undeclared device block read as populated.** The
  schema only requires `on_module.silicon`; omitting `hyperram:` or
  `ospi_memories:` entirely is valid. The old code's `on_module.
  get("hyperram") or {}` collapsed an absent block to `{}`, which then
  hit the `assembled` default `true` the same as a DECLARED block with
  the key merely omitted -- an undeclared HyperRAM printed "HyperRAM is
  populated". Fixed: `_aen_ospi_device_state()` now takes `dev: dict |
  None` and returns state `"absent"` for `None`, which
  `_aen_ospi_population_clause()` excludes from the clause text
  entirely -- an absent device is never named "populated" OR "not
  populated".
- **Minor 2 -- "optional" fell into the "no device" branch.** Both
  devices `"optional"` produced "... are BOM-optional, not assumed
  populated, so there is no external XIP / flash device" -- asserting
  flatly that no device exists contradicts "not assumed populated" (a
  BOM-optional part MAY be fitted). Fixed: the `"optional"` category now
  says "so no external XIP / flash device is **assumed** -- even if
  fitted, the same gap applies (`_AEN_OSPI_XIP_GAP`)."
- **Minor 3 -- three untested branches.** Changing `dev.get("assembled",
  True)` to `dev.get("assembled")`, or deleting the `is_tbd()` guard, or
  reverting the absent-block fix, all stayed green. Added
  `test_ospi0_storage_banner_assembled_key_absent_reads_as_populated`,
  `test_ospi0_storage_banner_chip_tbd_prints_no_part_name`, and
  `test_ospi0_storage_banner_omits_an_undeclared_device_block`, each
  mutation-checked by hand against the specific line it pins (flip the
  default / delete the guard / drop the absent-block handling; each
  test went red, then green again on restore).
- **Minor 4 -- awkward mixed-case sentence.** "OSPI0 NOR (N) is
  populated; HyperRAM (R) is not populated; neither is used for XIP
  boot here" used "neither" immediately after calling one device
  unfitted. Fixed: when exactly one of two declared devices is
  populated, the sentence now says "the populated device is not used
  for XIP boot here" instead; "neither" is reserved for the case where
  both declared devices are actually populated.

**Why AEN801 keeps ISSI/Infineon-Cypress part names on an unpopulated
footprint (scope decision):** E1M-AEN801 and E1M-AEN803 are the same SoC
(`AE822FA0E5597LS0`) on the same PCB, and E1M-AEN803 is E1M-AEN801's
*populated BOM variant* -- not a different design, the same U10/U9
footprint stuffed. Its measured parts are therefore the parts that
footprint takes on this SoC, whether or not any individual E1M-AEN801 unit
carries them. E1M-AEN{301,401,501,601,701} are **different SoCs** (E3-E7,
not E8) with no populated BOM variant ever measured -- the 24-ball OSPI
footprint they share with AEN801/803 accepts several different vendors'
parts, and which one a stuffed unit of those SKUs would carry is a real
open BOM question, not a PCB fact the way AEN801/AEN803's shared-SoC case
is.
