the same guard for a different reason than the aperture branch: with no SoC aperture declared,
SETOOLS's real ATOC anchor point can't be confirmed at all — the file-wide max is only a
fail-closed stand-in (an out-of-window OSPI0 HyperRAM row can sit far above the real window, the
same hazard the aperture-scoped rule guards against), so the fallback's own failure message says
so instead of claiming a confirmed SETOOLS anchor address. `customer_runtime`
(`_RUNTIME_WRITABLE_AUTHORITY`, `scripts/check_atoc_reservation.py:154` ("customer_runtime")) is
the ONLY `write_authority` value the schema defines as writable by the application at runtime;
every other declared value (`customer_image`/`vendor_image`: flash-tool only, `secure_enclave`: SE
at provisioning, `none`: no writer, `composite`: a whole-device alias deferring to its contained
rows — `mram_main`'s own tag today) stays exempt, unchanged. A row that IS runtime-writable now
fails naming the row and its authority (`_runtime_writable_top_failure()`,
`scripts/check_atoc_reservation.py:157` ("def _runtime_writable_top_failure")); the remedy it
suggests depends on the same exact-extent test 4b/4c already use to spot a whole-device alias —
`composite` only for an alias (`lo == floor and hi == top`), `secure_enclave` for the atoc band
itself, since suggesting `composite` for a mis-authored `atoc` partition would let an author retag
it that value and pass (`composite` is itself exempt). ABSENT `write_authority` stays exempt too —
the schema says absent means unresolved, never `customer_runtime` (ADR-0034 clause 4) — but is now
SKIP-noted by name rather than silent, since the schema also says a consumer must treat it as
ineligible for runtime write and say so.

No committed preset is affected: the only real whole-device alias, `mram_main`, already carries
`write_authority: composite`.

Checked `scripts/alp_orchestrate/partition.py` for the same hazard on the `storage[].flash_device:`
path per the issue's open question — it never reads `write_authority`, and its allocator only
avoids OTHER named `memory_map:` siblings with a resolved base, not the alias's own authority.
Two OTHER, unrelated mechanisms mask it today, not this gate: the #1556 Devicetree-label gate
(`_has_real_dt_label()`, `scripts/alp_orchestrate/partition.py:706` ("def _has_real_dt_label"),
enforced at `scripts/alp_orchestrate/partition.py:1096` ("verified_dt_label")) refuses `status: ok`
for any `memory_map:`-sourced `flash_device:` — alias or not — that lacks an explicit `dt_label:`
override, which nothing in the tree declares yet (`on_module.ospi_memories:` devices skip this gate
entirely, `scripts/alp_orchestrate/partition.py:918` ("is_ospi_device or _has_real_dt_label")); and
`check_atoc_reservation.py` itself only ever walks the in-tree `metadata/e1m_modules/` preset
directory (run with no metadata-root argument at
`.github/workflows/pr-metadata-validate.yml:621` ("python3 scripts/check_atoc_reservation.py")), so a customer
preset loaded through a `--metadata-root` override (`effective_metadata_root()`,
`scripts/alp_orchestrate/models.py:406` ("effective_metadata_root")) never runs through this CI
gate at all. #2088 tracks `partition.py`'s own gap as a follow-up.

### Fixed — `partition.py` placed a runtime mount on any `memory_map` region without checking `write_authority` (#2088)

`_resolve_flash_device()` (`scripts/alp_orchestrate/partition.py:480` ("def _resolve_flash_device("))
resolved a `storage[].flash_device:` reference to any named `memory_map:` region -- including a
whole-device alias like `mram_main` -- purely on name and size, never reading `write_authority`.
The schema is explicit that `customer_runtime` is "the ONLY value ... a row may claim DIRECTLY for
... a runtime mount to land on" (`metadata/schemas/som-preset-v2.schema.json`); nothing in the
allocator enforced it. `scripts/check_atoc_reservation.py` closed the equivalent hole for rows
covering the ATOC band (#2086); this closes the allocator's own gap, flagged as a follow-up in
that fix's changelog entry.

The guard lives in `_resolve_flash_device()` itself
(`scripts/alp_orchestrate/partition.py:539` ("if wa is not None and wa not in (")), the one place
every caller routes through -- the main allocator (`resolve_storage_partitions()`,
`scripts/alp_orchestrate/partition.py:816` ("def resolve_storage_partitions(")) and both
alt-device remedy scans (`_verified_alt_devices()`, `scripts/alp_orchestrate/partition.py:768`
("def _verified_alt_devices("); the inlined overlap-block scan,
`scripts/alp_orchestrate/partition.py:1038` ("d not in reserved_names")) all resolve through it,
so one guard covers every path a customer preset can reach, not just the board.yaml-driven one. A region
whose authored `write_authority` is neither `customer_runtime` nor `composite` is refused outright,
naming the region, the offending value, and the remedy. An ABSENT value is refused too, but only
where an on-die MRAM aperture resolves for the SoM (Alif) -- mirrors `carveout.py`'s own
`_region_ipc_eligibility()` gate; a no-op on every non-Alif SoM, none of which author
`write_authority` on a derived region today.

`composite` -- the tag a whole-device alias like `mram_main` carries, meaning "consult the
contained rows instead" (the schema's own words) -- is not an unconditional pass: refusing it
outright would break `examples/connectivity/production-deployment/board.yaml`'s
`flash_device: mram_main`, the only whole-device alias any committed preset declares. Instead
`_composite_alias_coverage_gap()` (`scripts/alp_orchestrate/partition.py:300`
("def _composite_alias_coverage_gap(")) actually consults
the contained rows the tag promises: every resolved `memory_map:` row CONTAINED in the alias's own
address window must declare its own `write_authority`, and together the contained rows must
CONTIGUOUSLY tile the window -- no gap, no overlap -- before the alias is accepted; a row whose
own base or size doesn't resolve is deferred rather than an immediate refusal (it is named as a
candidate only if a gap remains for it to plausibly explain), and a row outside the window is
ignored as unrelated. Placement itself routes through a SEPARATE, older function
(`_reserved_spans()`) with its own weaker origin/window derivation, so a composite alias whose
contained rows verify safe is refused anyway if that function can't actually reserve them.

Review round 1 found the first cut of this fix skipped the consultation entirely (a blanket
`composite` exemption) and reproduced the hole three ways against the real E1M-AEN801 preset with
only `memory_map:` swapped, landing a `storage[]` entry inside the live Secure-Enclave-owned
`atoc` band (bench-observed at 0x80578000..0x80580000,
`scripts/alp_orchestrate/carveout.py:100-104`) or at MCUboot's own address. Review round 2 found
the consultation itself was two more of the same class of hole:

- **Sum, not tiling.** The first cut of the consultation summed contained rows' sizes and compared
  the total to the alias's capacity -- an overlap of N bytes plus a hole of N bytes passes a sum
  check while the hole itself stays unprotected. Reproduced by deleting `atoc` and widening
  `he_slot0` by exactly `atoc`'s size (2688 -> 2720 KiB): the sum still matched, and
  0x80578000..0x80580000 stayed undeclared. The consultation now sorts the contained spans and
  walks them, refusing a gap OR an overlap and naming the offending pair.
- **The allocator's own degradation went unnoticed.** `_reserved_spans()` -- the function placement
  actually uses -- derives its own window top as `max(hi)` across every `memory_map:` row with a
  resolved base, INCLUDING a row entirely unrelated to this alias; an out-of-window sibling pushes
  that derived top past the alias's real one, failing `_reserved_spans()`'s own identity check and
  degrading it to reserving NOTHING -- not even `mcuboot` -- with only a stderr warning. The
  consultation verifying the contained rows individually didn't make placement itself safe. Fixed
  by treating that degradation as a refusal for a `composite` target: an alias whose contained rows
  can't actually be reserved can't be consulted either, the same principle already applied to an
  unresolved base.

No committed preset's behaviour changes: every AEN SKU's `memory_map:` already resolves,
authorizes, and contiguously tiles `mram_main`'s declared capacity with no gap and no overlap, so
`_resolve_flash_device("mram_main", ...)` still succeeds on all seven of them -- `_reserved_spans()`
still reserves every named sibling regardless of authority (including `storage` itself), so
`mram_main` remains 100% tiled with zero free bytes for a new entry either way
(`test_fully_tiled_device_blocks_with_an_actionable_reason`, unchanged). `carveout.py`'s
`_region_ipc_eligibility()` independently refuses `mram_main` as an IPC carve-out target outright
in every state it can resolve to (`composite` != `customer_runtime` while unresolved; flash-class,
never eligible, once resolved) -- the two enforcers agree in effect that a `customer_runtime`
write never lands broadly across `mram_main` on real metadata today, even though `partition.py`
now resolves the alias as a device (an explicit pin still needs somewhere to point) where
`carveout.py` never treats it as one eligible carve-out target.

### Fixed — AEN bench builds default to AEN803, and refuse a board overlay that would silently not apply (#2094)

Zephyr auto-applies a per-app devicetree overlay only when its filename
matches the fully-qualified board target with `/` replaced by `_` (the full
stem; #2235 found Zephyr also accepts a second, SHORT stem -- see
`changelog.d/2235.md`), and `scripts/bench/aen/build.sh` never forces
`EXTRA_DTC_OVERLAY_FILE`. So an app
that ships overlays for a *different* target built with **no overlay applied
at all** and said nothing about it — the operator got a binary shaped for the
wrong module, and the first symptom was a peripheral misbehaving on real
silicon. `scripts/bench/aen/bench-env.sh`'s `AEN_BOARD` note already
described this hazard; nothing enforced it.

The build now checks the app's `boards/` directory before invoking `west`
(`scripts/bench/aen/build.sh:274` ("$APP_DIR/boards")) and
refuses when that directory holds overlays but not the one this board target
would pick up (`scripts/bench/aen/build.sh:257`
("ships AEN board $label files, but none for")). The refusal prints the exact
filename it expected, every overlay that *is* present, and the
`AEN_BOARD=<fully-qualified board>` override to build anyway
(`scripts/bench/aen/build.sh:268`
("refusing to build with no $label applied")). #2235 later extended this
check to board-qualified `.conf` files through one shared function
called once per extension,
`scripts/bench/aen/build.sh:203`
("bench_build_require_board_qualified() {"), then refined the guard further
-- see `changelog.d/2235.md` for what changed.

An app with no `boards/` overlays at all still builds: there is nothing to
miss, so only a non-empty overlay set that lacks this board's file is an
error (of any kind, at the time -- #2235 narrowed this to
`alp_e1m_*_rtss_h[ep]`-shaped sets plus this board's own bare and
board+SoC near-miss names, so a `native_sim`-only overlay set no longer
counts; see `changelog.d/2235.md`).

**The `AEN_BOARD` default is now repointed to E1M-AEN803, closing the issue.**
Every module on the Alp Lab AEN bench farm is an E1M-AEN803. That rests on
the maintainer's account, not on anything readable from silicon (the same
part number is on both SKUs), as
`metadata/e1m_modules/E1M-AEN803.yaml:203`
("so it rests on the maintainer's word") records. The repoint
waited on the guard above landing first, then on #2214 backfilling every
`examples/aen/*` overlay that previously existed only for AEN801 with an
AEN803 twin, so the guard does not strand most of `apps.txt`. The default is
now
`scripts/bench/aen/bench-env.sh:105` ("alp_e1m_aen803_m55_he/ae822fa0e5597ls0/rtss_he"),
confirmed a real, generated board target at
`zephyr/boards/alp/e1m_aen803_m55_he/alp_e1m_aen803_m55_he_ae822fa0e5597ls0_rtss_he.yaml:4`
("identifier: alp_e1m_aen803_m55_he/ae822fa0e5597ls0/rtss_he") since #2084;
`AEN_BOARD` still overrides for genuine AEN801 or off-default work.

**Verification: every `apps.txt` app built for both targets.** All 23 apps in
`scripts/bench/aen/apps.txt` were built directly with `west build`, the same
flags `build.sh` uses, once for
`alp_e1m_aen801_m55_he/ae822fa0e5597ls0/rtss_he` and once for
`alp_e1m_aen803_m55_he/ae822fa0e5597ls0/rtss_he`. All 23 build on both
targets. `aen-npu-inference-alif` needs a Vela compiler, which `build.sh`
does not supply: without one it fails the same way on both targets
(`ERROR: vela not found at vela`), and with `-DAEN_NPU_VELA=<venv>/bin/vela`
it builds on both. For every app, the pair was then compared three ways:

- **`zephyr.dts`**: after stripping the `/* in <file>:<line> */` source-location
  comments, which name the board tree each node came from, the only
  differences are the root `model` and `compatible` strings. No node,
  register value or property differs, OSPI0 included. This matches the
  issue's own prediction that a safe repoint changes nothing observable
  until #915 lands OSPI0 driver support.
- **`.config`**: only the board-identity symbols differ: `CONFIG_BOARD`,
  `CONFIG_BOARD_TARGET`, and `CONFIG_BOARD_ALP_E1M_AEN80{1,3}_M55_HE[...]`.
- **`zephyr.bin`, byte for byte**: 3 apps are identical, and the other 20
  differ in exactly one byte. That byte is the `1` to `3` of the embedded
  `alp_e1m_aen80{1,3}_m55_he` board-name string. Image sizes are equal in
  all 23.

`scripts/bench/aen/README.md` and the `build.sh` overlay-name comment are
updated to match the new default;
`scripts/bench/aen/README.md:171` ("Qualified board target.") and
`scripts/bench/aen/README.md:224` ("west build -b alp_e1m_aen803_m55_he")
now show the AEN803 target.
`scripts/bench/aen/aen-flowc-itcm.conf:21`
("boards/alp_e1m_aen801_m55_he_ae822fa0e5597ls0_rtss_he.conf") named only the
AEN801 file at the time: `examples/peripheral-io/alp-console` had no
AEN803-qualified twin of that board-scoped `.conf`, so an app built under the
new AEN803 default without an `AEN_BOARD` override would have tripped
`build.sh`'s own overlay preflight (it also shipped only an AEN801
`.overlay`). #2235 resolved that gap: `alp-console` now ships both twins —
`boards/alp_e1m_aen803_m55_he_ae822fa0e5597ls0_rtss_he.conf` and the matching
`.overlay` — so a build under the AEN803 default no longer trips the guard.

### Added — gpio-qdec input-subsystem backend for the portable QENC API (#2095)

The Alif E8's UTIMER QEC hardware channel is a measured edge counter, not a
quadrature decoder (#2037), so a quadrature encoder wired to plain GPIOs
needs Zephyr's `gpio-qdec` input driver (`compatible = "gpio-qdec"`, emits
`INPUT_EV_REL` events) instead of the sensor-class channel
`src/backends/qenc/zephyr_drv.c` already speaks. That backend's own comment
anticipated exactly this ("Real pulse counts come via the v0.3
input-subsystem fast-path") but nothing implemented it until now.

`src/backends/qenc/gpio_qdec.c` is a new QENC backend, registered at
priority 110 (`src/backends/qenc/gpio_qdec.c:141`
(".priority    = 110,")) — above `zephyr_drv`'s 100 — so it is tried
first. For each `alp-qenc<N>` alias whose devicetree node is compatible
`gpio-qdec`, it registers an `INPUT_CALLBACK_DEFINE_NAMED` that
atomically accumulates `INPUT_EV_REL` events into a per-index position
(thread-safe: `atomic_add`/`atomic_get`/`atomic_set`). `alp_qenc_open()`
baselines each handle to that shared accumulator's value at open time, so
`get_position()`/`reset_position()` are relative to the handle's own
baseline instead of the raw accumulator — two handles opened at different
times don't zero each other out. An alias that is NOT a `gpio-qdec` node
makes `open()` decline with `ALP_ERR_NOSUPPORT`
(`src/backends/qenc/gpio_qdec.c:101`
("if (dev == NULL) return ALP_ERR_NOSUPPORT;")).

`src/qenc_dispatch.c`'s `alp_qenc_open()` gained the same open-time
fall-through `src/security_dispatch.c`'s `hash_open()` already uses (issue
#239): on `ALP_ERR_NOSUPPORT` it walks to the next-priority backend
(`src/qenc_dispatch.c:107`
("be = alp_backend_select_next(")) instead of
failing the whole open — so a sensor-class `alp-qenc<N>` alias still lands
on `zephyr_drv` exactly as before; the new backend never breaks it. The
walk stops before the vendor `sw_fallback` candidate: a real backend's
`ALP_ERR_NOSUPPORT` means "wrong shape for this alias", not "no real
backend exists", so it must not silently land on the software fallback's
fake counter.

Compiled only under `CONFIG_INPUT`
(`zephyr/CMakeLists.txt:1130`
("zephyr_library_sources_ifdef(CONFIG_INPUT")), selected purely by the
alias's devicetree `compatible` — no new Kconfig knob to choose between the
two qenc backends.

`tests/unit/qenc_gpio_qdec` (new native_sim ztest) aliases `alp-qenc0` to a
`gpio-qdec` node and `alp-qenc1` to native_sim's plain `gpio0` controller
(a real, ready, non-`gpio-qdec` device), and drives the backend with
`input_report_rel()` directly (the same event shape the real driver posts)
to check position accumulation, reset, that a non-`REL` event type is
ignored, and that the `alp-qenc1` open falls through to `zephyr_drv`.

This only partially addresses #2095: the AEN `aen-qenc-readout` example's
own migration onto `alp_qenc_open()` is still open (its UTIMER QEC channel
is sensor-class, not a plain-GPIO pair this backend serves).

### Added — `qenc-readout` builds and runs on the E1M EVK with an AEN SoM (#2095)

`examples/peripheral-io/qenc-readout` gains board overlays for the
AEN801/AEN803 M55-HE and M55-HP targets
(`examples/peripheral-io/qenc-readout/boards/alp_e1m_aen801_m55_he_ae822fa0e5597ls0_rtss_he.overlay`,
and the AEN803 twin) that bind `alp-qenc0` to a `gpio-qdec` node on the
EVK rotary encoder's phase pads, so the portable `alp_qenc_*` calls reach
the encoder through the gpio-qdec backend added in #2506. A new
build-only twister scenario, `alp_sdk.example.qenc_readout.aen`, keeps the
two targets building. Bench, E1M-AEN803 serial 2026W36-0001, M55-HE RAM-run:
`alp_qenc_open` and `alp_qenc_reset_position` return `ALP_OK` and the
position reads `0` at rest; a turn of the knob has not been captured yet.

Also fixes the AEN twister matrix on `dev`: `src/backends/qenc/gpio_qdec.c`'s
input callback was unreferenced in any AEN build whose `alp-qenc<N>` aliases
name no `gpio-qdec` node (`examples/aen/aen-qenc-readout`), which
`-Werror=unused-function` turned into a build failure; it is now
`__maybe_unused`.

### Added — synthetic SoM preset fixture covers the unresolved-base routing #2053/#2102 removed (#2096)

`mram_main.base` resolves to `0x80000000` on all seven AEN presets (#2053,
#2102), so no shipped preset authors an unresolved `memory_map:` base any
more. That was the only shipped-preset producer of that shape anywhere in the
tree, so it was also the only end-to-end path through
`scripts/alp_orchestrate/memory.py::_resolved_row()`'s unresolved-base leg
and `scripts/alp_orchestrate/carveout.py::_region_ipc_eligibility()`'s
`cls == "unresolved"` tail. The tests that cover those legs are direct calls
into the private helpers, which keep the legs green in isolation but prove
nothing about the WIRING that routes an unresolved row into them in the
first place -- a change that filtered unresolved rows out earlier (say in
`carveout.py::_candidate_regions()`, before `_region_ipc_eligibility()` is
ever called) would leave every direct pin green while the live guard went
dead.

`tests/scripts/_orchestrate_support.py` gains
`_synthetic_aen_unresolved_base_root()`, a sibling of the existing
`_synthetic_nx9101_root()`: a scratch metadata root carrying a synthetic
`E1M-AEN899` preset (not a real SKU) under `alif:ensemble:e3` -- an Alif SoC
that DOES declare an on-die MRAM aperture, so the aperture-dependent branches
are reached rather than short-circuited by `aperture is None`. Its
`memory_map:` is a verbatim copy of `metadata/e1m_modules/E1M-AEN301.yaml`'s
seven rows as they stood before #2053/#2102, `mram_main`'s `base: "TBD"`
included. Two new tests drive it through the full `load_board_yaml` ->
`resolve_memory_regions()` / `resolve_carve_outs()` pipeline rather than
calling the private helpers directly, so the routing into both legs stays
covered end to end alongside (not replacing) the direct-call pins.

### Fixed - `aen-evk-demo`'s TAS2563 amp-fault pin print was inverted (#2097)

`phase_sound()` (`examples/aen/aen-evk-demo/src/main.c`) configures
`AMP_FAULT_PIN` (`IRQ_N`, P5_0) plain `GPIO_INPUT` -- no `GPIO_ACTIVE_LOW` --
so `gpio_pin_get()` returns the raw electrical level, not `IRQ_N`'s logical
sense. `IRQ_N` is open-drain, active-low, so raw `1` (pulled high by `R124`)
is idle and raw `0` is the fault. Both baseline and post-shutdown prints had
this backwards: raw `0` printed `"high (no fault)"` and raw `1` printed
`"LOW (asserted!)"`. A healthy, idle-high board printed the opposite word.

Bench evidence (SWD, read-only, E1M-AEN803 serial 2026W36-0002): `EXT_PORTA` (`0x49005050`)
read `0x000000C1`, pad `P5_0` electrically high, both amps' latched-fault
words `0x00000000` -- the line was idle-high throughout; there was never a
fault.

Fixed by swapping the print's interpretation to match the pin's real
polarity, and printing the raw level alongside the verdict so a reader can
always tell which is which: `raw=%d (%s)`, `raw=1` -> `"high, no fault
(IRQ_N idle)"`, `raw=0` -> `"LOW, fault asserted (IRQ_N active-low)"`.

Not routed through `tas2563_fault_asserted()` (`chips/tas2563/tas2563.c`,
already correct): that call needs an `alp_gpio_t *` from `alp_gpio_open()`,
which only resolves pin ids present in this app's `alp,pin-array`
devicetree node (a 3-entry array for the SoM-internal CC3501E nets only --
see the overlay's Phase-11 header for why `AMP_FAULT`/`AMP_ENABLE` reach
`gpio5` directly instead of through that array). Extending the array to
reach this pad was explicitly avoided when the phase was written, to skip
~50 unused placeholder entries; this fix does not reverse that.

Review follow-up: the mapping itself is pulled into a new
`examples/aen/aen-evk-demo/src/amp_fault_verdict.h` (`amp_fault_pin_verdict()`),
same pure-predicate-in-a-header pattern as `bmp581_verdict.h`/
`sound_verdict.h` in that directory, with three new cases in
`tests/zephyr/chips/src/test_audio.c` (`raw=1` idle, `raw=0` asserted, a
negative-errno read failure counted as neither) -- this exact ternary was
inverted once already; a unit test now fails before a bench run does.

### Fixed - `aen-evk-demo`'s I/O-expander phase asserted a configuration the SDK deliberately never creates (#2098)

`phase_io_expander()` (`examples/aen/aen-evk-demo/src/main.c`) read the
TCAL9538's configuration register (`0x03`) and printed it against a
hardcoded `0xF0` expectation. Nothing in the tree ever writes that register
for `P0-P3` -- deliberately, per #2035: they are carrier display/camera
control lines (`LCD_PWR_EN`/`LCD_RST`/`CAM_EN`/`CTP_RST`), not this SDK's to
own -- so a fresh board reads the power-on default `0xFF` every time, and
the polarity round-trip's own write (`tcal9538_set_polarity_inversion(&io,
0xFFu)`) inverted the register for all 8 pins, including the four the SDK
does not own.

Fixed: the config read is now printed as a found direction, per nibble
(`P0-3`/`P4-7`, `input`/`output`/`mixed`), never compared against an
expected value and never gated on. The polarity round-trip now only ever
writes `IOEXP_POLARITY_TEST_MASK` (`P4-P7`, the sensor-interrupt pins
`aen-sensor-int-probe` already legitimately drives). `PASS` requires `P4-P7`
to flip on invert (a fixed, nonzero compile-time mask, so this can't pass
vacuously the way #2037 found) AND the WHOLE byte to come back to `before`
on restore.

Two corrections from review, both against the same first draft of this fix:

- **The restore check was itself vacuous.** It compared only the bits this
  phase never writes (`P0-P3`), so a chip that ACKs the restore write but
  never actually clears register `0x02` still passed: `before=0xF3,
  inverted=0x03, restored=0x03` (invert genuinely took effect, restore
  never did) read as a `PASS` under the old mask. Comparing the whole byte
  catches it -- see `test_ioexp_polarity_vacuous_restore_now_fails` in the
  new `tests/zephyr/chips/src/test_ioexp_verdict.c`.
- **A strict single-attempt check can fail a healthy board.** `P4-P7` are
  live sensor-interrupt lines, and phase 2 leaves the ICM42670 running
  accelerometer output at 100 Hz for the rest of this app's run (it is
  never deinitialised) -- a real interrupt edge landing mid-round-trip can
  cancel one bit's forced flip. The predicate itself
  (`ioexp_polarity_check()`, new `examples/aen/aen-evk-demo/src/
  ioexp_verdict.h`) stays strict per attempt -- loosening it would also let
  a genuinely wedged expander pass -- so the phase instead retries the
  whole before/invert/restore sequence up to `IOEXP_ROUND_TRIP_ATTEMPTS`
  (3) times and accepts the first attempt that passes outright.

Both writes (`IOEXP_POLARITY_TEST_MASK` on invert, `0x00` on restore) are
still whole-register writes to `0x02` only (`tcal9538_set_polarity_
inversion()` has no read-modify-write) -- so `P0-P3`'s own polarity bits do
get written, always to 0, on every attempt. That is harmless today (`0x02`
sits at its POR default and nothing else in this tree ever writes it), and
is exactly what the now-whole-byte restore check would catch if it ever
stopped being true. What this phase never does, on any attempt or any
board revision, is touch the DIRECTION register (`0x03`) or the OUTPUT
register (`0x01`) for `P0-P3` -- it never drives or reconfigures those
pins, which is the ownership boundary #2035 actually cares about.

Does not reverse the #2035 decision.

Also extracts the AMP_FAULT (IRQ_N) raw-pin polarity mapping from #2097's
fix into `examples/aen/aen-evk-demo/src/amp_fault_verdict.h`, covered by
three new cases in `tests/zephyr/chips/src/test_audio.c` -- the same
predicate-in-a-header pattern as `ioexp_verdict.h`, so a re-inverted
ternary in either place now fails a unit test before it fails a bench run.

### Added — CC3501E `WIFI_STATUS` surfaces the reason/status code for the most recent connect attempt (#2099)

`alp_cc3501e_wifi_status_t`'s 4th wire byte was an unused `reserved` field,
always 0. It is renamed `last_reason` and documented: the low byte of the
802.11 REASON code from a DISCONNECT event, or the 802.11 STATUS code from an
ASSOCIATION_REJECTED/AUTHENTICATION_REJECTED event — two different code
tables, and nothing on the wire says which one, so `fail_reason == REJECTED`
does not disambiguate them. Requires bridge firmware that publishes the
reason (`cc3501e-bridge-firmware`); older firmware still sends 0, so this is
purely additive — no wire-version bump needed.

Recorded ONLY while the connect attempt's state is CONNECTING, then frozen
and PERSISTS through every later state publish — including a subsequent
`cc3501e_wifi_disconnect()` call (WIFI_DISCONNECT), which republishes this
same frozen value rather than a fresh one — until the next connect attempt
starts and clears it back to 0. `cc3501e_wifi_connect()` itself issues that
same disconnect at entry, before submitting a new attempt, whenever the latch
still shows a FAILED attempt (the pre-existing #1435/#1437 stale-association
cleanup), so that internal disconnect republishes the OLD attempt's value
too. `0` means nothing was recorded for that attempt, not "no cause": a clean
success or a bare timeout also reads `0`. `CONNECTED` always publishes `0`,
unconditionally, even over a since-succeeded transient rejection recorded
earlier in the same attempt. Never holds vendor reason 200
(`WLAN_DISCONNECT_USER_INITIATED`). Known residual: a late event from the
PREVIOUS attempt landing in the brief window right before the new attempt's
own connect call can still be recorded against the new one; the converse also
holds — a reject arriving after an attempt has already been declared TIMEOUT
is lost. The firmware also runs one bounded, transparent retry on a first-pass
status-30 rejection: the retry normally reports its own outcome, but the byte
reports the FIRST pass's outcome (e.g. REJECTED/30) when the retry's connect
call is refused, when the retry times out, or when the retry ends with reason
3 or 0, which carry no AP verdict. Scope is the connect
attempt only: a deauth after a successful `CONNECTED` is not recorded, because
the state is no longer CONNECTING.

`alp companion wifi status` prints `reason: <N>` after `fail:  <N>` when
`last_reason` is non-zero. `wifi connect`'s async result line does the same
on both a failure and a timeout, fetched via the new `cc3501e_wifi_status_once()`
— a single, non-retried WIFI_STATUS read (public API, alongside the existing
down-window-retrying `cc3501e_wifi_status()`; its real bound is the shared
request lock's bounded acquire plus the per-phase READY wait, not a
`timeout_ms` argument, which the transport ignores) so a wedged transport
cannot turn this best-effort diagnostic fetch into an extra ~10 s delay with
the connect result held back. The console only trusts the fetched
`last_reason` when the latch's own `state` reads `CONN_FAILED` -- a
`DISCONNECTED`/`CONNECTING` state there means no failure of THIS attempt
ever landed (the submit was bounced `BUSY` by a concurrent worker op, or lost
to a transport IO fault, and the outer loop's own `timeout_ms` simply ran
out), so the byte would otherwise still hold an UNRELATED prior attempt's
stale value. The fetch is skipped entirely when `cc3501e_wifi_connect()`
returned `ALP_ERR_INVAL`: no attempt started, so the latch still holds the
previous attempt's value. This is the host-visible half of the bench gap this
issue tracks: roughly half of `alp-console` station connects were failing
`-5` (`REJECTED`) with nothing to say why.

`rssi_dbm`'s `@warning` (issue #1387, closed) is updated to say so: the wire
slot that would have carried an RSSI-validity flag is the same byte now
carrying `last_reason`, so that option is no longer available on this reply.
No replacement channel is decided here.

### Added — a gate catching a testcase.yaml platform_allow entry with no matching boards/ overlay (#2101)

`scripts/check_example_board_overlay_parity.py` already caught a `board.yaml`-declared core with a missing overlay (#1009); it now also catches the sibling case #2101 reported: a `testcase.yaml` `platform_allow` entry for a real E1M SoM board target (`alp_e1m_*`) with no matching `boards/<target>.*`, while `boards/` ships an `alp_e1m_*`-qualified overlay for a different target in the same file. Zephyr's board-overlay auto-apply resolves a qualified target to its overlay filename by joining the board name and every `/`-separated qualifier with `_`, and separately accepts a SHORT form that drops the SoC-id segment (confirmed against `cmake/modules/configuration_files.cmake` and `cmake/modules/extensions.cmake` in a real Zephyr v4.4 checkout, not inferred from this repo's filenames); a target with no matching file in either form silently builds with no board overlay at all — no error, no warning. The precondition for "does this example use per-target overlays" is keyed off `boards/` content on disk, not off which `platform_allow` entries happen to be declared — the declaration-keyed form misses the defect's own fully-declared shape (`aen-brd-i2c-scan` on the AEN803 branch: `platform_allow` swapped to the AEN803 target, the AEN801 overlay left in place, zero declared-entry matches).

Measured on the AEN803 board-tree branch (counting directories, not files): 81 example directories under `examples/aen/`, 73 ship an `alp_e1m_aen801*` overlay, 1 (`aen-adc-regcheck`) ships `alp_e1m_aen803*`, 72 ship 801-but-not-803. This gate covers **0** of those 72 — none of them declares an AEN803 `platform_allow` entry at all, so a `platform_allow`-keyed check has nothing to compare against for them; closing those needs the overlays themselves (owned by #2100/#2103) or a broader repo-state-keyed check (below). On `origin/dev` today the check also finds 0 problems, but that means "nobody has declared a second SKU's `platform_allow` entry yet," not that this class is absent — `zephyr/boards/alp/` already ships preliminary `e1m_aen401_m55_hp` / `e1m_aen601_m55_hp` trees with no sibling overlay across the 12 examples that ship an `alp_e1m_aen801_m55_hp` one, reachable the moment any of those 12 declares an AEN401/AEN601 `platform_allow` entry. This gate is scoped to `alp_e1m_*` targets only, so an example whose only `boards/` content is a `native_sim` overlay/conf for a vendor reference-board `platform_allow` entry (a real, common, legitimate pattern) is never flagged — with one known exception outside this scope, filed separately: `examples/peripheral-io/drone-autopilot` ships a real `alp_e1m_aen801_m55_hp` overlay but declares only `ensemble_e8_dk` for its hardware scenario, so its build silently drops the overlay's `alp-i2c0`/`alp-uart1`/`alp-pwm0..3` aliases today.

`pr-metadata-validate.yml` is not among `dev`'s required merge-queue contexts (those are the `twister-shard` jobs, `clang-format · diff-only`, and `distro install · all`), so this gate does not hold the queue.

A broader, deferred alternative that would close all 72 plus the AEN401/AEN601 gap: key off `zephyr/boards/alp/` tree membership instead of `testcase.yaml` declarations — for every `boards/<SKU>_<quals>.overlay` an example ships, if a sibling SKU's board tree names the same core in its own `metadata/e1m_modules/<SKU>.yaml` `topology.<core>.board:`, require the sibling overlay or an explicit allow-list entry. Fully computable from committed metadata, but red on `dev` today (the 12 HP examples above), so deferred rather than landed here.

### Fixed — cc3501e READY gate trusted a level read as proof the slave had re-armed, clocking phases into a stuck-HIGH pad near-instantly (#2105)

**Before:** `cc3501e_reply_gate()` (`chips/cc3501e/cc3501e_core.c`) read
`ctx->ready_pin` once per phase and, on HIGH, skipped its fixed inter-phase
settle outright — a HIGH read was trusted as proof the slave's SPI slave was
armed+idle. On an R2 AEN EVK bench module, the pad AEN example bridges
opened for this (Alif P2_6) is not the CC3501E's GPIO17 READY net at all: it
is E1M pad AH7 / I2S1_SCLK, which the EVK carrier maps to the Arduino
header's `CK_RST` (`metadata/boards/e1m-evk.yaml`) — a reset line that idles
HIGH — while the real READY net lands on E1M pad G3 / IO16 instead
(`metadata/e1m_modules/aen/from-cc3501e.tsv`, `from-alif.tsv`). Reading
`CK_RST`'s constant HIGH as "armed" produced near-zero settles on every
phase; with the gate trusting it, station connect never associated in 4 of 4
bench boots (run8), against 5 of 7 with the gate disabled.

**After this commit:** the line may only ever ADD delay, never remove it.
When `ctx->ready_pin` is populated, `cc3501e_reply_gate()` waits (bounded by
`CC3501E_READY_WAIT_US`) for the pin to read HIGH, and then **always** pays
the same fixed `fallback_us` settle a `NULL` `ready_pin` pays with no wait at
all — a HIGH read decides only how much *extra* time to wait before that
unconditional settle, so however wrong the read is, the worst case is
"waited a bit longer than necessary", never "clocked early". A stuck-HIGH
pad is found on the very first, zero-delay poll, so it costs exactly the
`ready_pin == NULL` timing and can never make a gate faster than gate-off; a
noisy or glitching pad cannot shorten a settle either; a genuinely
slower-than-the-fixed-settle slave (e.g. mid radio op) is the one case READY
still helps, by waiting out the real re-arm instead of guessing a fixed
number.

A new `CC3501E_READY_STUCK_LOW_STREAK` (3) bounds the cost of a genuinely
stuck-LOW (or disconnected) `ready_pin`: after 3 consecutive gates each burn
the full `CC3501E_READY_WAIT_US` without ever seeing HIGH, this process
stops *waiting* on it (`g_ready_ignored`, file-global — not per-`ctx`, and
`cc3501e_ready_line_was_stuck()` latches for diagnostics) and falls back to
paying only the fixed settle from then on. **The latch recovers:** firmware
can legitimately hold READY LOW across an entire radio op spanning several
gates, so once latched, each gate still takes one zero-wait read; a HIGH
there clears the latch and the streak so the next gate resumes the real
bounded wait. Each time the latch sets, the number of consecutive timeouts
needed to set it again doubles (3, 6, 12, then capped at 24, never reset), so
a line that is mostly LOW with an occasional HIGH read cannot keep re-buying
3 full waits under the transport lock. This can only ever remove a wasted *wait* — the settle itself
is always paid unconditionally, so none of this can make a gate return
early.

`ctx->ready_pin` is opt-in and left `NULL` by default on every AEN example
bridge on the R2 module: a board (or hand-reworked unit) that genuinely
wires GPIO17 to some Alif pin sets `fw->ready_pin` in its own
`cc3501e_bridge_bringup()`. Doing so while holding a stale assumption about
the wiring is safe for *link timing* (READY can never clock a phase early),
but not free: the wait runs while `cc3501e_request()` holds its internal
transport lock, so a wrong or slow `ready_pin` can make another caller see
`ALP_ERR_BUSY` after `CONFIG_ALP_SDK_CC3501E_REQUEST_LOCK_TIMEOUT_MS` —
documented on `ready_pin` itself (`include/alp/chips/cc3501e/core.h`), the
Kconfig (`zephyr/kconfigs/chips.kconfig`), and every example's opt-in
comment.

`tests/zephyr/cc3501e_host_driver` coverage asserts plain delay accounting,
never wall-clock time: stuck-HIGH pays exactly the 3 fallbacks (700 us);
stuck-LOW pays the bounded wait plus fallback on each of the first 3 gates,
then fallback only once the latch trips, recovering back to the full bounded
wait the moment a read comes back HIGH; a HIGH between two shorter runs of
timeouts resets the streak instead of letting it accumulate across the gap;
a noisy (flips-every-read) pad and a slower-to-arm slave both pay AT LEAST
the fallback total, never less. Mutation-verified: an early return on HIGH
(the pre-fix bug shape) turns the stuck-HIGH, noisy, and slow-to-arm cases
red; deleting the stuck-LOW latch turns the stuck-LOW case red; deleting the
streak reset on HIGH turns the timeout/HIGH/timeout/timeout case red;
reverting the latch-recovery read turns the latch-clears-on-HIGH case red;
disabling the threshold doubling turns the re-latch hysteresis case red —
each mutation turns exactly its own regression(s) red and nothing else.

**Out of scope for this fix, noted for follow-up:** on the E1M EVK, CC35
GPIO17 (the CC3501E's real READY output) is wired out to E1M pad G3 / IO16,
which the EVK carrier also exposes as `EVK_PIN_W_DISABLE2` — the M.2 E-key
slot's Bluetooth-disable line (`metadata/boards/e1m-evk.yaml`). READY
toggling (and the separate async-event attention pulses, `#1721`/`#130`)
may therefore also toggle that M.2 signal on a board with an M.2 E-key card
fitted; this was not investigated further here.

### Fixed — `drone-autopilot`'s hardware scenario named a board target it ships no overlay for, silently dropping every `alp-*` alias and driver (#2106)

`examples/peripheral-io/drone-autopilot`'s only board overlay is
`boards/alp_e1m_aen801_m55_hp_ae822fa0e5597ls0_rtss_hp.overlay`, written for
#1383 item 2 to close the same devicetree-alias gap
`examples/peripheral-io/pwm-led-fade` closed for #1375. `testcase.yaml`'s
`alp_sdk.examples.drone_autopilot.aen` scenario declared a different board
target, `ensemble_e8_dk/ae822fa0e5597ls0/rtss_hp`: introduced at `4a1c1a732`
as `alif_e7_dk_rtss_hp` (an E7 dev kit against an E8 `board.yaml` even then),
then retargeted to the E8 vendor DevKit by `560b256e5` (#1266/#1316,
"documentation for a dev kit CI never builds" by its own commit message) --
three months before `4a375045f` (#1383) added the overlay. That commit never
corrected the scenario. Zephyr resolves a `boards/` overlay by
fully-qualified board target name, so building for `ensemble_e8_dk/...`
picked up no overlay at all, with no error or warning (the scenario is
`build_only: true`, so nothing ever ran to surface it).

The loss was not just the six `alp-*` aliases. Confirmed against both
targets' generated `.config`: on `ensemble_e8_dk/...` `CONFIG_PWM_ALIF_UTIMER`,
`CONFIG_I2C_DW` and `CONFIG_GPIO_DW` are all absent and `pwm_alif_utimer.c`
is never compiled into the image -- the whole driver set the overlay's
`&utimer10`/`&utimer11`/`&i2c2`/`&uart3` nodes pull in was gone, not just the
aliases pointing at it.

`board.yaml` names `som.sku: E1M-AEN801` / `preset: e1m-evk`, the README's
"Hardware" section says E1M-AEN801 + E1M-EVK, and the sibling
`examples/aen/aen-pwm-utimer-pwmleds` / `examples/aen/edgeai-vision-aen`
scenarios that target the same overlay both use the fully-qualified
`alp_e1m_aen801_m55_hp/ae822fa0e5597ls0/rtss_hp` form -- and dual-targeting
the DevKit as well would be actively wrong, since it does not carry the
E1M-EVK pad routing the overlay encodes. So the overlay was right and the
scenario's `platform_allow` was wrong. Corrected `testcase.yaml`'s
`platform_allow` to `alp_e1m_aen801_m55_hp/ae822fa0e5597ls0/rtss_hp`, and
updated the three stale `ensemble_e8_dk/...` mentions that agreed with the
old value -- the README's `[UNTESTED]` banner and `west build -b ...`
command, and `docs/local-ci.md`'s Windows cross-compile example -- to match.

Added `examples/peripheral-io/drone-autopilot` as a third, bounded
`--testsuite-root` on `pr-twister-aen.yml` (same #1101 precedent as the
existing `firmware-update-log` root): before this the corrected target was
built by no CI job -- `pr-twister-aen.yml` only covered `examples/aen` and
`firmware-update-log`, and `pr-twister.yml` filters the AEN scenario out via
`-p native_sim/native/64` -- so a regression back to the wrong target would
have gone unnoticed again.

Verified against the generated devicetree rather than a green build alone: on
the corrected target `build/zephyr/zephyr.dts` carries `alp-i2c0 = &i2c2`,
`alp-uart1 = &uart3`, and `alp-pwm0`..`alp-pwm3 = &esc0`..`&esc3`, all
attributed back to the overlay; on the old `ensemble_e8_dk/...` target none
of the six aliases appear anywhere in the generated tree.

Checked, not assumed, whether the same overlay-vs-declared-target mismatch
recurs elsewhere: of the 20 other `examples/*/*/testcase.yaml` files that
declare `ensemble_e8_dk/...` (across `ai/`, `audio/`, `camera-vision/`,
`connectivity/`, `display/`, `multicore/`), none ships an `alp_e1m_*` overlay
under its `boards/` directory -- every one of those 20 is either genuinely
DevKit-targeted or (where a `boards/` directory exists at all) carries only a
`native_sim_native_64` overlay, so none pairs a real `alp_e1m_*` overlay with
a wrong `ensemble_e8_dk` declaration. #2120's declared-target-with-no-overlay
gate scopes to `alp_e1m_*` `platform_allow` entries and would not have caught
this one, since the declared (wrong) target here was the vendor
`ensemble_e8_dk` board, not an `alp_e1m_*` one; not widened here.

### Fixed — CC3501E reply-header gate is now sized by the real expected byte count, not a flat 200 us or the caller's rx_cap (#2107)

The host used to wait a fixed, blind 200 us (`cc3501e_reply_gate(ctx, 200u)`)
before clocking the CC3501E bridge's reply header on every request, regardless
of how much reply data that request expected back or how much request data it
just sent. Two bench findings show 200 us is too short for a large exchange
either direction:

- **Reply side (measured for this fix).** `dispatch_frame` composes a large
  reply (ring copy, a CRC over ~4100 bytes, a ~4100-byte memcpy) inside the
  CC3501E's SPI transfer-complete ISR before it re-arms the reply-header
  phase. A `SOCK_RECV` asking for 512 bytes (`want` = 512, wire reply =
  `sizeof(alp_cc3501e_sock_recv_resp_t)` (24 B) + 512 = 536 B) was clean 3/3 at
  200 us; the SAME op asking for 4071 bytes wedged the link on the very first
  call, 2/2 runs at both 1 MHz and 25 MHz. Widening only that gate to 2000 us
  made the 4071 B `want` succeed 3/3, including a streamed 262144 B download
  with a matching CRC. The want=4071 reply is NOT 24 + 4071 = 4095 B: a bridge
  command handler's writable capacity is the 4100 B frame minus its own 5 B
  header minus the 2 B CRC trailer = 4093 B, so the actual wire reply the
  firmware produced was capped at 4093 B.
- **Request side (inferred, not directly measured for this fix).**
  `dispatch_frame` runs in the SAME ISR the instant the request PAYLOAD phase
  finishes -- it CRCs up to ~4094 request bytes and runs the opcode's handler
  before arming the reply header, so a large REQUEST should pay the same
  composition cost even when its reply is tiny.
  `examples/aen/aen-cc3501e-socket-throughput/README.md` (~159-165) records a
  512 B `STREAM_WRITE` request clean 4/4 at the old flat 200 us gate, while
  1024 B and 4092 B requests both failed `rc=-5`, 3/3 each. No run has
  measured what gate value actually fixes the request side -- this fix's
  `max(expected_reply, wire_tx_len)` is CONSISTENT WITH that failure boundary
  (a 1024+ B request now gets more than 200 us), not proven to close it the
  way the reply-side fix was proven on `SOCK_RECV`.

**The key is not `rx_cap`.** `cc3501e_sock_recv()` always passes
`rx_cap == sizeof(ctx->sock_buf) == ALP_CC3501E_MAX_PAYLOAD` (4096 B)
regardless of the `want` it actually asked the peer for -- rx_cap is a fixed
local staging buffer, and the bridge sizes its reply from the wire request,
not from how big a buffer the host happens to have allocated. An earlier
version of this fix keyed the gate on rx_cap directly, which would have put
every `SOCK_RECV` -- including the 512 B one proven fine at 200 us -- at the
2000 us ceiling, taxing every small read for no reason.

`cc3501e_expected_reply_bytes()` (`chips/cc3501e/cc3501e_core.c`)
reconstructs the real expected reply size per opcode from `(cmd, tx_payload,
tx_len)` instead of trusting rx_cap:

- `SOCK_RECV`: `sizeof(alp_cc3501e_sock_recv_resp_t)` (24 B) + `want` (the
  wire `max_len` field the request actually carries) -- EXCEPT `want == 0`,
  which the bridge treats as "no limit" (it clamps the reply to `max_len`
  only when `max_len != 0`), not "expect nothing back". A caller-supplied
  `cap` of 0 reaches the wire as literally that "no limit" value, so `want ==
  0` falls back to rx_cap instead of computing a tiny 24 B reply.
- `SPI1_TRANSFER`: `sizeof(alp_cc3501e_spi1_transfer_resp_t)` (4 B), plus the
  request's own `len` unless it set `ALP_CC3501E_SPI1_XFER_NO_RX` (reply is
  then the bare 4 B header).
- Every other opcode, `GET_PENDING_EVENTS` included: `rx_cap`, unchanged.

**`GET_PENDING_EVENTS` was NOT special-cased**, though its firmware-side
event ring is a documented fixed 16 entries (288 B worst case) well under
this rx_cap (`sizeof(ctx->evt_buf)`, 4096 B). An earlier version of this fix
keyed it to that 288 B ring so every poll stayed at the 200 us floor; that
case was removed because it depends on a firmware-internal constant
(cc3501e-bridge-firmware `src/event_ring.h`) this driver has no way to verify
stays 16 -- a silent ring-depth change on the firmware side would silently
under-gate this poll again, exactly the class of bug this fix exists to
close. `cc3501e_poll_events()` now pays the full ~2000 us ceiling every call:
measured at roughly 1.8 ms added per poll, about 0.36% additional
transport-lock hold at a realistic 2 polls/s cadence -- accepted as the cost
of not trusting a number this file cannot verify, rather than risking a
silent wedge if the ring ever grows.

`cc3501e_reply_header_gate_us()`'s input is then `max(expected_reply,
wire_tx_len)` -- whichever side of the exchange is larger -- so a large
REQUEST (`STREAM_WRITE`, `OTA_WRITE`, a big `SPI1_TRANSFER` TX, or a large
`SOCK_SEND`/`BLE_GATT_REGISTER`/`BLE_GATT_NOTIFY`/`BLE_GATT_WRITE` payload)
gates just as long as a large reply does -- these are NOT unchanged from the
old 200 us floor when their payload is large; see the table below. The
proven 200 us floor holds at or below 536 B (the measured `SOCK_RECV`
`want`=512 point); the gate grows linearly to the proven 2000 us at
`ALP_CC3501E_MAX_PAYLOAD - ALP_CC3501E_HEADER_BYTES` (4092 B) -- the largest
single-frame byte count any opcode in this driver can ever present in either
direction, 1 byte short of the measured 4093 B ceiling, which only ever hands
out the proven 2000 us slightly sooner, never less delay than a naive
interpolation would. Only those two points (536 B at 200 us, 4093 B at
2000 us) were bench-measured; every byte count strictly between them is
linearly interpolated, not separately measured.

Per-op-class worst-case added latency (vs. the old flat 200 us):

| Class | Bytes | Gate | Added latency |
|---|---|---|---|
| `PING`, `GET_VERSION`/`GET_CAPABILITIES`, `GET_DIAG_INFO`/`DIAG_GET_STATS`, most BLE control, `SOCK_OPEN`/`BIND`/`LISTEN`/`CLOSE`, `GET_MAC`, `WIFI_GET_RSSI`/`GET_IP`/`STATUS`, most `OTA_*` control, `GPIO_CONFIGURE`/`SET_INTERRUPT`, `POWER_POLICY`, camera control | <= 536 B | 200 us | none |
| `SOCK_RECV` with `want` near its 4071 B protocol ceiling or `want == 0` ("no limit"), a near-max `SPI1_TRANSFER`, `GET_PENDING_EVENTS` (rx_cap 4096 B, no longer floored), or a near-max `STREAM_WRITE`/`OTA_WRITE`/`SOCK_SEND`/`BLE_GATT_REGISTER`/`BLE_GATT_NOTIFY`/`BLE_GATT_WRITE` payload | >= 4092 B | 2000 us | +1800 us |
| Anything strictly between | 536-4092 B | interpolated | up to +1800 us |

Two documented, deliberately-unfixed limits remain, both pre-existing and
both left alone rather than special-cased:

- **`BLE_GATT_READ` can be OVER-gated.** `src/backends/ble/cc3501e.c` (~324)
  passes the portable API caller's own `out_cap` straight through as rx_cap,
  and a caller sized generously for "any GATT value" pays the large-reply
  gate even though most real attribute values are a few bytes.
- **A raw `WIFI_SCAN_START`/`BLE_SCAN_START` call with `(NULL, 0)` can be
  UNDER-gated.** rx_cap bounds only how much the driver copies into the
  caller's buffer, not what the firmware actually sends back on the wire --
  a cached scan result can still return a large reply even when the caller
  asked to copy out nothing.

**Caveat.** On `dev` without alp-sdk#2105, a READY pin that reads CONSTANT
HIGH -- a stuck-high pad, not a genuinely wired-and-idle one -- proves itself
on the very first read and then bypasses this fallback gate entirely via the
level-gated READY path. This fix only changes behaviour on the fixed-wait
fallback path (every CS-less r1 board, and any board whose READY pin never
proves itself); it does nothing for a board already misbehaving on the READY
path #2105 addresses.

Does not touch `CC3501E_PHASE_SETTLE_US` (the request-header, request-payload,
and reply-payload phases' own settle) or the READY-line edge-wait path --
both stay exactly as they were; only the reply-header phase's blind-fallback
computation changed.

### Changed — CC3501E `SOCK_RECV` gets its own request-seq counter for the firmware's replay-safe receive (#2108)

Bench evidence: one run downloaded 262144 B over 4071 B `cc3501e_sock_recv()`
calls, every call returned `ALP_OK`, and exactly one 4069 B block never
arrived -- a GAP, not a duplicate -- sitting exactly on a reply boundary.
Root cause: the bridge firmware commits its receive-ring advance EAGERLY,
before the host has actually received anything, so a reply that then fails
CRC on the wire has already consumed that chunk firmware-side. Today's
firmware cannot tell a retry of that exact request apart from a brand-new
one, so `poll_by_repeat()`'s identical re-issue gets answered with the NEXT
chunk instead of the lost one.

The real fix is firmware-side
(`cc3501e-bridge-firmware#138`, merged, not yet in a released blob): the ring
advance becomes lazy, keyed on (header seq, socket handle) recorded on every
`SOCK_RECV` dispatch -- a request whose seq and handle match the immediately
preceding dispatch is a replay, the ring does not advance again; any other
request commits and serves the next chunk. That mechanism only works if the
key it reads is unambiguous.

This change is the host-side groundwork for that key: `cc3501e_sock_recv()`
now allocates its wire-header retry seq (proto v8, 5 bits, 1..31) from its
own dedicated `ctx->sock_recv_seq`, not the shared `ctx->req_seq` every other
worker-routed opcode also draws from. One counter per ctx, shared across
every socket handle, is enough -- the firmware records its key on every
`SOCK_RECV` dispatch regardless of handle and compares only against the
single most recent entry, never against history, so two recvs that are
adjacent in the `SOCK_RECV` stream can never carry the same seq regardless of
which handles they're on. Drawing from the shared `req_seq` instead would not
have that property: unrelated opcode traffic can land between two recvs
without ever touching a dedicated counter, so two recvs that are adjacent in
the firmware's `SOCK_RECV`-only view could still end up exactly 30 unrelated
commands apart in `req_seq`'s cycle and numerically identical -- exactly the
bench failure above.

`cc3501e_sock_recv()` also only commits its candidate seq into
`ctx->sock_recv_seq` once its own call reaches `ALP_OK` with the reply fully
decoded -- never after `ALP_ERR_TIMEOUT`, `ALP_ERR_IO`, or a short header. A
caller whose call fails keeps the SAME candidate on its next attempt, so once
`fix/sock-recv-retry-safe` ships, an immediate retry of the SAME handle will
recover the chunk that call's lost or corrupted reply already committed,
instead of the bridge treating the retry as a new request and skipping past
it. Recovery holds only for an immediate retry of the same handle: a
different handle called first also gets that same candidate, but with its
own handle, so it correctly starts fresh rather than colliding with the
failed call's entry -- and once that different-handle call commits, the
original handle's next retry gets a genuinely new seq and can no longer
recover the original lost chunk.

`poll_by_repeat()`'s retry loop is unchanged in behaviour; its body moved to
a new `poll_by_repeat_seq()` that takes the seq as an explicit parameter,
letting `SOCK_RECV` supply its own while every other caller still goes
through `poll_by_repeat()`, which allocates from `ctx->req_seq` exactly as
before.

Harmless against firmware without that replay logic: it ignores the
seq bits for `SOCK_RECV` exactly as it already does for every opcode that
never checks them.

### Fixed — the `alp companion wifi connect` console command budgeted a CC3501E STA connect at a 50 s budget, under the 70 s bound (#2111)

The CC3501E bridge firmware's own worst case for one STA connect is 10 s
`Wlan_RoleUp` + 30 s L2 association + 30 s DHCP-lease poll = 70 s
(`cc3501e-bridge-firmware:hal/ti/cc3501e_hw_ti_wifi.c`), which documents
75000 ms as the caller budget that clears it. `src/zephyr/console/
alp_console_companion_wifi.c`'s `ALP_COMPANION_WIFI_CONN_MS` was `50000u`,
under that bound, so a genuinely slow-but-healthy association could time out
before the firmware's own connect finished.

`ALP_COMPANION_WIFI_CONN_MS` `50000u` → `75000u`, matching
`SOCKTP_CONNECT_TIMEOUT_MS` / `CONNTWICE_CONNECT_TIMEOUT_MS`. The same
constant is also passed to `cc3501e_wifi_ap_start()`. That call submits
WIFI_AP_START once and then confirms via an independent channel -- polling
`GET_DIAG_INFO`'s role field until it reports `ALP_CC3501E_ROLE_WIFI_AP`,
bounded by `timeout_ms` (`chips/cc3501e/cc3501e_wifi.c`) -- and the
firmware's own worst case there is a single 10 s `Wlan_RoleUp`
(`CC3501E_WIFI_ROLE_TIMEOUT_MS`), so kept shared rather than split: 75 s is a
harmless (if generous) upper bound on that confirmation poll, not an
incorrect one.

The console's `wifi ap` command handler carried stale comments and a stale
shell error string describing a firmware version that could never confirm
AP_START at all. Corrected to the current behaviour (submit once, confirm via
the diag role within the budget): `ap start "%s" unconfirmed (%d) -- firmware
v4 has no AP status latch (#1385); check for the SSID out of band` →
`ap start "%s" failed (%d)`, with `(not confirmed within the budget)`
appended when the failure is `ALP_ERR_TIMEOUT`. The block comment justifying
the success branch as unreachable dead code is removed -- it is the live
path. `chips/cc3501e/cc3501e_wifi.c`'s own block comment above the CONFIRM
step, which said AP_START "has no such channel" and "`timeout_ms` is
therefore currently unused", is corrected to describe the GET_DIAG_INFO
confirmation poll that follows it, and `docs/cc3501e-companion-commands.md`
describes `wifi ap` the same way.

The same under-provisioned budget existed on more callers wired to the same
CC3501E backend: `examples/aen/aen-cc3501e-bringup`'s
`CC3501E_CONN_TIMEOUT_MS` `15000u` → `75000u` (a 5-try bounded retry loop
re-issues `WIFI_CONNECT_STA` on timeout, so a short budget there let a retry
land on top of the previous attempt's still-running connect);
`examples/connectivity/mqtt-telemetry`'s `WIFI_CONNECT_TIMEOUT_MS` `10000u` →
`75000u`; `examples/connectivity/iot-fleet-ota` / `iot-dashboard` moved an
unnamed `10000u`/`5000` literal onto a named `WIFI_CONNECT_TIMEOUT_MS`
`75000u`; and `examples/connectivity/iot-connected-camera`'s inline `30000` →
`75000u` (its `overlay-aen.conf` wires the same CC3501E path on an E1M-AEN
target, so it is not exempt). All four now read that on E1M-AEN801 with the
CC3501E bridge attached the bridge's worst case is 70 s, and on any other
Wi-Fi backend the value is only an upper bound, not a derived worst case.

`docs/cc3501e-bridge.md`'s bench table said a stuck association blocks the
console "for the full `ALP_COMPANION_WIFI_CONN_MS = 75000u` (75 s)"; reworded
to "up to 75 s; a firmware-reported failure returns sooner" -- the budget is
a ceiling on a hung link, not the duration of every failure.

`chips/cc3501e/cc3501e_wifi.c`'s scan-window comment ("the same shape the
55 s connect budget uses over its own 40 s") is corrected to "75 s ... 70 s".

Comments in `examples/aen/aen-cc3501e-socket-throughput` (`SOCKTP_CONNECT_
TIMEOUT_MS`'s derivation, and `SOCKTP_VERDICT_WAIT_MS`, which is now defined
as `SOCKTP_CONNECT_TIMEOUT_MS` instead of a separately-drifting `45000u`
literal), `aen-cc3501e-connect-twice-probe` (source and README), `aen-cc3501e-
wedge-postmortem` (source and README), and `aen-cc3501e-companion-tour` are
corrected from a stale DHCP/total figure to the current 150-try / 30 s DHCP
figure and the 70 s / 75000 ms bound, without changing any of those files'
already-correct `75000u` values.

### Fixed — connectivity examples never attached the CC3501E bridge on E1M-AEN801, so `alp_wifi_open()` returned NULL (#2112)

On E1M-AEN801, the portable `<alp/iot.h>` Wi-Fi API only reaches the on-module
CC3501E bridge once an application has attached a live `cc3501e_t` handle:
`cc35_open()` returns `ALP_ERR_NOT_READY` while the backend's static bridge
context is unset
(`src/backends/wifi/cc3501e.c:39` ("return ALP_ERR_NOT_READY;")), and
`alp_wifi_open()` (`src/wifi_dispatch.c:70` ("alp_wifi_t *alp_wifi_open(void)"))
then returns NULL. None of `mqtt-telemetry`, `iot-fleet-ota`, or
`iot-dashboard` called `cc3501e_bridge_bringup()` or `alp_wifi_cc3501e_attach()`
before `alp_wifi_open()`, so on real AEN801 silicon all three failed at
`alp_wifi_open()` and never reached `alp_wifi_connect()` — only the
`examples/aen/aen-cc3501e-*` apps and `iot-dashboard`'s own doc comment
already showed the working pattern
(`examples/aen/aen-cc3501e-bringup/src/cc3501e_bridge.c:124`
("(void)alp_wifi_cc3501e_attach(fw);")).

Fixed at the example level, not the backend: each of the three AEN-targeted
connectivity examples now copies the same `cc3501e_bridge.{c,h}` bring-up
template every `examples/aen/aen-cc3501e-*` app uses and calls
`cc3501e_bridge_bringup()` once before its first `alp_wifi_open()` —
`examples/connectivity/mqtt-telemetry/src/main.c:141`
("alp_status_t bridge_rc = cc3501e_bridge_bringup(&bridge);"),
`examples/connectivity/iot-fleet-ota/src/main.c:400`
("alp_status_t     bridge_rc = cc3501e_bridge_bringup(&bridge);") — called
once in `main()` before the poll loop, not inside `fleet_wifi_up()`, which
runs every tick and would otherwise re-run the WIFI_EN/nRESET reset sequence
on every poll — and
`examples/connectivity/iot-dashboard/src/main.c:159`
("alp_status_t     bridge_rc = cc3501e_bridge_bringup(&s_bridge);"). The
portable backend itself is unchanged: `docs/cc3501e-bridge.md` already
documents that the bring-up helper, not the dispatcher, is what attaches the
bridge, so the fix stays at the application layer that owns SoM bring-up.
`mqtt-telemetry` and `iot-fleet-ota`'s `board.yaml` gained the
`peripherals: [spi, gpio]` block the bridge helper needs (`iot-dashboard`
already carried it, anticipating this exact gap) —
`examples/connectivity/mqtt-telemetry/board.yaml:55`
("peripherals:") and `examples/connectivity/iot-fleet-ota/board.yaml:53`
("peripherals:").

No new gating mechanism: `alp_gpio_open()`/`alp_spi_open()` return NULL fast
(no backend registered for that SoC ref) when the bring-up call runs under
`native_sim`, so `cc3501e_bridge_bringup()` fails with
`ALP_ERR_NOT_PRESENT_ON_THIS_SOC` and each example falls through to the same
NULL/NOT_READY framing path it used before this fix — bench-verified via a
local `native_sim` run of all three (`[mqtt] wifi: cc3501e_bridge_bringup ->
ALP_ERR_NOT_PRESENT_ON_THIS_SOC`, then the unchanged `alp_wifi_open() -> NULL
(ALP_ERR_NOT_READY)` framing path, ending on the harness's `[mqtt] done`
marker). `examples/connectivity/iot-connected-camera` is deliberately left
untouched: its `board.yaml` targets `E1M-V2N101` only (no AEN scenario is
built anywhere in-tree) and its own README documents that choice —
`examples/connectivity/iot-connected-camera/README.md` ("## Why V2N rather
than AEN?") — and its `alp_wifi_open()` NULL there is V2N's Linux-owned radio
being unreachable from the M33 Zephyr core, not a missing bridge attach.

**Verification.** `main.c` + `cc3501e_bridge.c` compile cleanly for both
`native_sim/native/64` and the real `alp_e1m_aen801_m55_hp` board target in
all three examples (`app/libapp.a` links with no warnings from the new
files). The real-board link itself is blocked by three pre-existing defects
this fix does not touch and does not attempt to fix: mbedtls's
`ssl_misc.h` `mbedtls_error_pair_t` include-order error (`mqtt-telemetry`,
`iot-fleet-ota`), undefined `z_impl_sys_rand_get` with TLS off
(`mqtt-telemetry`, `iot-fleet-ota`), and `iot-dashboard`'s lvgl finding no
`zephyr,display` node — all three reproduced locally, unchanged by this
fix, on `origin/dev` before this branch.

### Documented — `docs/soms/aen.md` claimed every non-`E1M-AEN801` preset still carried the pre-#1848 LPI2C0 assumption; none do (#2118)

The paragraph above the `## On-module housekeeping I2C (BRD_I2C)` heading in
[`docs/soms/aen.md`](../docs/soms/aen.md) said "the other AEN SKUs still carry
the pre-#1848 LPI2C0 assumption in their own preset files pending the same
netlist evidence." False on `dev`: `metadata/e1m_modules/E1M-AEN301.yaml`,
`E1M-AEN401.yaml`, `E1M-AEN501.yaml`, `E1M-AEN601.yaml`, and `E1M-AEN701.yaml`
each explicitly reject the LPI2C0 reading ("HELD, NOT the disproven LPI2C0
claim (#1848, ADR 0017 amended ...)"), and `E1M-AEN803.yaml` carries the
corrected `I2C0_SDA_C = P7_0` / `I2C0_SCL_C = P7_1` mapping outright. Reworded
to say what is true: #1848 disproved the LPI2C0 reading for the whole family,
not just `E1M-AEN801`, and no shipped preset carries it -- the other SKUs
still await their own per-part datasheet confirmation of the corrected
mapping, which the presets' own comments already say (`bus_master` held
pending that check).

### Added — auto-recover a wedged CC3501E bridge link (#2126)

Before, a bridge wedge (observed ~3 times per 50 Wi-Fi connects on
an AEN EVK bench unit) left every request failing (`ver` → `-4`/`-5`) until the
whole board was power-cycled — the host-side warm-reset fix
(`cc3501e_recover()`) existed but nothing called it automatically.

Now `cc3501e_link_check_and_recover()` is wired into the driver's own
worker-routed failure exits and into `cc3501e_wifi_connect()`'s timeout
exit: when a top-level op exhausts every attempt with no status ever
decoded off the wire (a genuinely busy bridge that answers late no longer
false-triggers), it probes with `PING` for up to 12 s and, only if every
probe fails, warm-resets and re-confirms the link — guarded against an
open OTA/update session (tracked by an explicit per-link flag, not the
transport's peer-polled bit), an attempt-based cooldown with exponential
back-off (30 s doubling to 5 min on repeated failure, reset on success),
and `CONFIG_ALP_SDK_CC3501E_AUTO_RECOVER` (default `y`, genuinely
Kconfig-gated off — not just defaulted — when disabled). `alp companion
recover` shares the same guarded path for manual use instead of bypassing
it.

The whole reset-through-reconfirm sequence now holds the link's request
lock so no concurrent request desyncs the CS-less wire mid-reset, and only
one recovery runs at a time. A successful recovery bumps the link's epoch;
any socket handle opened before that epoch fails closed
(`ALP_ERR_NOT_READY`) instead of silently addressing a socket that no
longer exists on the other side of the reset. Subscribe to
`cc3501e_set_recover_callback()` for recovery notifications.

Measurement and post-mortem apps keep the old behaviour on purpose:
`aen-cc3501e-wedge-postmortem`, `aen-cc3501e-command-sweep` and
`aen-cc3501e-silent-scan-probe` set `CONFIG_ALP_SDK_CC3501E_AUTO_RECOVER=n`,
because a reset mid-capture destroys the evidence they exist to record.

**Breaking:** socket handles now carry the link epoch in their upper byte,
so a handle is no longer the firmware's small integer — print it as
`0x%04x`, and mask with `& 0xFF` before comparing against a firmware-side
number. A handle minted before a recovery now returns `ALP_ERR_NOT_READY`
from every socket op instead of addressing whichever socket now holds that
number. `cc3501e_sock_accepted_decode()` takes the owning link's epoch as a
new parameter, so callers decoding an accepted-socket event must pass it.
A failing op can also now take longer than its own `timeout_ms`: the
probe-and-reset sequence adds up to ~12-18 s of probing plus ~3.5 s of
reset before the call returns.

### Added — AEN803-qualified board overlays backfilled across the AEN example set (Refs #2128)

`scripts/bench/aen/build.sh` (#2094) now refuses a build whose app ships
`boards/` overlays but none matching the resolved board target, and every
module on the bench farm is an E1M-AEN803. But `_qualified_target_to_stems()`
(`scripts/check_example_board_overlay_parity.py:395-410` ("def _qualified_target_to_stems")) keeps the SKU
verbatim in both the full and short overlay stem, so a single filename cannot
serve both `alp_e1m_aen801_*` and `alp_e1m_aen803_*` — repointing
`bench-env.sh`'s `AEN_BOARD` default to AEN803 (#2094, still open) would have
stranded ~18 of 23 `apps.txt` entries behind an explicit `AEN_BOARD=` export.

71 example directories that shipped an `alp_e1m_aen801_*`-qualified overlay
or `.conf` now also ship the `alp_e1m_aen803_*` counterpart — 77 `.overlay`
files (65 single-core dirs + 6 dual-core dirs' HE+HP pair:
`aen-alp-rpc`, `aen-dualcore-doorbell`, `aen-dualcore-he-master`,
`aen-dualcore-ipc`, `aen-dualcore-master`, `aen-rpc-pingpong`) and 3
`.conf` files (`aen-analog-validate`, `aen-dualcore-he-master`,
`aen-jpeg-regcheck`), 80 new files total.

Body content is SoC-level, not SKU-level, so it copies across unchanged; only
each banner's board-target name and SKU digit were updated. Two banner
sentences were corrected rather than propagated, since they were tied to a
specific bench run on an actual AEN801 unit, not a generic SoC-pad fact:
`examples/aen/aen-rtc-alarm/boards/alp_e1m_aen803_m55_he_ae822fa0e5597ls0_rtss_he.overlay:51`
("BENCH-PROVEN 2026-09-05 on E1M-AEN801 2626-R2") and
`examples/aen/aen-cc3501e-gpio/boards/alp_e1m_aen803_m55_he_ae822fa0e5597ls0_rtss_he.overlay:17`
("SPI1 DATA PATH BENCH-VALIDATED 2026-06-20 (E1M-AEN801, M55-HE)") both keep
naming the AEN801 unit that was actually bench-run and now say the SoC-pad
behavior is expected to carry to AEN803's identical die but has not itself
been separately bench-proven there.

**Excluded: `examples/aen/aen-ospi-regcheck`.** It is the only app whose
overlay substantively touches `&ospi0`, and the board tree's own banners
diverge exactly there —
`zephyr/boards/alp/e1m_aen801_m55_he/alp_e1m_aen801_m55_he_ae822fa0e5597ls0_rtss_he.dts:14-16`
says OSPI0 NOR + HyperRAM "are not populated, so there is no external XIP /
flash device", while
`zephyr/boards/alp/e1m_aen803_m55_he/alp_e1m_aen803_m55_he_ae822fa0e5597ls0_rtss_he.dts:14-18`
says they "are populated; neither is used for XIP boot here ... #915" — so
its regcheck pass/fail semantics may assume a floating bus that stops
floating on AEN803. That needs a human call and is deliberately left out of
this PR; the issue stays open. `examples/aen/aen-adc-regcheck` was also
skipped — it already ships both `alp_e1m_aen803_m55_he_*` and
`alp_e1m_aen803_m55_hp_*` overlays.

None of these new overlays have been bench-built or run on real AEN803
silicon as of this PR — the AEN803 bench gate run is what first compiles
them.

### Fixed — `EVK_PIN_SDIO_MUX_SEL` doc string and `evk_sdio_select_t` enum had the SDIO mux select polarity inverted (#2129)

`metadata/boards/e1m-evk.yaml:140` ("SDIO mux S") (the `EVK_PIN_SDIO_MUX_SEL` `doc:` field) said
"0 = M.2 E-key SDIO, 1 = microSD slot" -- the opposite of the carrier
netlist. `E1M-EVK-2626-R2_pinmap.csv` (internal repo, `grep -a ',U38,'`)
shows `SD_D3` on U38 pin 2 (`1|0`) and `M2E_SDIO_D3` on pin 3 (`1|1`); U39
carries the same shape for CLK/CMD. A 74LVC157/3257-type part's `x|0`
inputs are selected when `S` is LOW, so `S` LOW routes the microSD slot
and `S` HIGH routes the M.2 E-key, not the reverse the doc string
claimed. Confirmed on real hardware, not just the netlist: on
E1M-AEN803 serial 2026W36-0002, header P18 open pulls `S` low through `R27` (100k to
`0V`) via `R198` (0 ohm to `NetP18_2`), and a microSD card in `J7`
enumerated and read a real sector 0 with the `55 AA` boot signature --
proving `S` LOW is the microSD slot on this hardware.
`metadata/boards/e1m-evk.yaml:140` ("SDIO mux S") (the pin's IDE hover doc string) is
corrected and now carries the full r1/r2 split rather than just r2: on
r1 `S` IS firmware-drivable, via CC3501E `GPIO_30`
(`metadata/e1m_modules/aen/hw-revisions.yaml:46`
("r1: CC3501E GPIO_30 (r2 unrouted).")), with a warning never to drive
it LOW while header P18's jumper is fitted (see the hazard below); on
r2 it is `dispatch: unrouted`
(`metadata/e1m_modules/E1M-AEN801.yaml:358-359`
("Physically open on board 2626-R2")), #1854) and hardware-strapped via
`R198`/`R27`/header `P18` instead.

The same inversion was baked into the generated `evk_sdio_select_t` enum:
`metadata/boards/e1m-evk.yaml:372-373`
 ("MUX_SEL.SDIO low.") paired `EVK_SDIO_M2E_KEY` with `value: 0` and
`EVK_SDIO_SDCARD` with `value: 1` (now swapped, so `EVK_SDIO_SDCARD = 0`
/ `EVK_SDIO_M2E_KEY = 1`, matching `MUX_SEL.SDIO low`/`high` in the same
block). **Public ABI change:** no in-tree code consumes
`evk_sdio_select_t`'s values today (the pin isn't software-drivable at
all on r2, and no example opens it on r1 either), so this changes no
behaviour in this repo -- but out-of-tree code that passes
`EVK_SDIO_SDCARD` or `EVK_SDIO_M2E_KEY` as a raw `0`/`1` literal, rather
than the symbolic name, now gets the opposite value.
`docs/abi/removed-symbols.json` needs no entry for `evk_sdio_select_t`:
the typedef's header move (`alp_e1m_evk.h` -> `alp_e1m_evk_routes.h`,
#637) together with this fix's enumerator swap is exactly the
moved-and-value-changed shape #2139 taught `scripts/abi_snapshot.py
--diff` to report as `MOVED` plus `CHANGED` (merged as `1648f3f8b`), so
the v0.15 diff carries no `REMOVED` line and the
`pr-generated-files.yml` freeze gate stays green without an allowlist
entry. `docs/abi/v0.16-snapshot.json` (the
CURRENT snapshot, `metadata/sdk_version.yaml` pins `version: 0.16.0`) is
regenerated via
`scripts/abi_snapshot.py --version v0.16 --output docs/abi/v0.16-snapshot.json`
to carry the new hash -- and, after this branch rebased onto `origin/dev`
(which landed #2126's `cc3501e_t` recover fields in the meantime), was
regenerated again so BOTH the recover fields and the swapped
`evk_sdio_select_t` hash are present. (A follow-up is filed separately to
make `abi_snapshot.py diff()` report this shape as `MOVED`+`CHANGED`
instead of requiring an allowlist entry.)

`include/alp/boards/alp_e1m_evk_routes.h` is regenerated from both
metadata changes via `scripts/gen_board_header.py` (GENERATED, never
hand-edited);
`tests/fixtures/emit-snapshots/proj-aen.carrier-netlist.snap` and
`proj-aen.composed-route-table.snap` were refreshed via
`scripts/check_emit_snapshots.py --update` in the same pass.

**`include/alp/boards/alp_e1m_evk.h:96-157`
 ("SDIO multiplexer (M.2 E-key SDIO vs microSD card slot).")'s
hand-written SDIO mux block carried the same inverted `S` mapping, plus
a deeper problem: it presented `/E = 0` as a working route on the stock
74LVC157, which it never was.** Per the authoritative 2626-R2 carrier
netlist, the mux's `Y` pins land on the SAME nets the SoC's own
peripheral pins are wired to (U39 `3Y` = `E1M_CLK`, `4Y` = `E1M_CMD`,
`2Y` = `E1M_SDIO_RST`; U38 `1Y`..`4Y` = `E1M_D3`..`E1M_D0`). A 74LVC157
is UNIDIRECTIONAL and always actively drives `Y` -- the selected `A`/`B`
input at `/E` = LOW, forced LOW at `/E` = HIGH -- so it fights the SD
host controller's own CLK/CMD output (and the SD_RST GPIO output
`aen-sdcard-readout` drives on `E1M_SDIO_RST`) in EITHER state, not just
when disabled: SD, and SoC-to-amp I2S through the same-shape U46 mux,
can never work through the stock part at all. A 3257-type FET
bus-switch rework of U38/U39 -- now the standard fit going forward for
THOSE two ICs -- IS a genuine bidirectional switch: `/E` = LOW connects
(does not drive) the selected side, so the SoC's own driver passes
through cleanly, and `/E` = HIGH is real Hi-Z. That fixes SDIO (U38/U39,
both on `+3V3`) -- proven, SD reads 4-bit at 25 MHz, after a U38 solder
fix, on the hand-reworked E1M-AEN803 serial 2026W36-0002, though only with the
unmerged enable path (see the SD row correction below; dev's own SD
path is unverified until #2122 and the `test/2051-sdhc-enable-on-reworked-mux`
ADMA/SRAM0 work land).

**U46's failure mode was itself misdiagnosed for several passes of this
fix.** As-built, U46 is a `74LVC157ABQ,115`
(`E1M-EVK-2626-R2_components.csv`, internal repo) -- its `VCC` range is
1.2-3.6 V, so `+VIO` at 1.8 V is IN SPEC for it. Undervoltage was never
the stock part's problem: like U38/U39, it fails by DIRECTION (a
one-way mux whose `Y` outputs drive the SoC side), so it can NEVER pass
SoC-to-amp I2S at any `VCC` -- moving the stock part's `VCC` alone
fixes nothing. A working U46 needs the part REPLACED with a 3257-type
bus switch, same as U38/U39, though "the standard fit going forward"
does not (yet) apply to U46 the same way -- AND that switch's `VCC` on
a rail within ITS spec. A 3257-type part was fitted at U46 on
E1M-AEN803 serial 2026W36-0002 with `VCC` initially left on `+VIO`. `+VIO` is NOT a
carrier-selected rail -- it is the plugged-in SoM's own `VIO_OUT`
(`E2` pins P1/P2 feed `+VIO_C`, which reaches `+VIO` through U33's
shunt monitor). MEASURED with the E1M-AEN SoM (same unit)
(maintainer, 2026-09-15): `+VIO` = 1.8 V, below a 3257-type bus
switch's 2.3-3.6 V `VCC` spec (unlike the stock 74LVC157, which
tolerates 1.8 V), and with both amps ACTIVE, every I2S/I2C call
returned `ALP_OK` but the TAS2563s produced no audible output. On
that same unit (2026-09-15 ~14:05Z), the fitted 3257-type part's
`VCC` was moved from `+VIO` to `+3V3` between that silent run and an
audible run -- a continuous 1 kHz PROBE_LISTEN tone through I2S3 was
then clearly audible on both TAS2563 amps, confirmed by ear. This is
NOT established as the only difference between the two runs; MEASURED
is the rail move and the audibility change, INFERRED is that the rail
move caused it. SCOPE: only amp PLAYBACK audibility was checked this
way -- PDM mic capture and M.2 E-key I2S through this mux remain
unverified. The SAME run also showed an open `INT_LTCH0` bit 2 (TDM
clock error) latch during playback and open issue #2146 (amps
auto-shut down ~1 s after I2S stops, stay off after restart) -- a
working mux does not mean the audio path is otherwise clean. NEW
CAVEAT, untested: at `VCC` = 3.3 V a CBT-type switch's control-input
VIH (~2.0 V) may not reliably register a 1.8 V HIGH on `/E` or `S` from
the CC3501E -- the amp path only needs both LOW, which is why it
worked, but disabling the mux (`/E` HIGH) or selecting M.2 (`S` HIGH)
may not switch reliably. A working U46 therefore needs BOTH a
3257-type swap AND `VCC` on `+3V3` (subject to the `/E`/`S` HIGH
caveat and the open TDM-latch/#2146 findings) -- `VCC` alone is NOT
the gate, since a stock 74LVC157 on `+3V3` still fails by direction.
The untested alternative is a switch rated for 1.8 V `VCC` -- e.g. TI
TMUX1574 (1.5-5.5 V), which keeps the SN74CBTLV3257 pin numbering ONLY
in its TSSOP-16/SOT-23-THIN-16 packages (its UQFN pinout differs, and
none of TMUX1574's packages fit U46's NXP DHVQFN-16 2.5x3mm land
pattern without an adapter or flying leads) -- UNTESTED in-house. The
SDIO block's truth table is now scoped to "with a 3257-type switch
fitted" rather than presented as universal, and the I2S block
(`include/alp/boards/alp_e1m_evk.h:159-260`
 ("I2S0 multiplexer (TAS2563 amplifier vs M.2 E-key I2S).")) gets the
same per-part contention wording for `/E` PLUS this `+VIO`/`+3V3`
power-rail finding, alongside a separate pre-existing bug in that
block: it claimed I2S_EN is unconditionally "driven from Alif via
alp_gpio_*", true only on r1 -- on r2 it is CC3501E `GPIO_30`
(`metadata/e1m_modules/aen/from-cc3501e.tsv:21`
 ("AG33	IO8	GPIO30")), contradicting the block's own r1/r2 summary
two paragraphs above it.

The SDIO block's claim that IO21 is CC3501E-proxied is
revision-dependent, not simply wrong: r2
(`metadata/e1m_modules/E1M-AEN801.yaml:358-359`
 ("Physically open on board 2626-R2")) leaves it `dispatch:
unrouted` and hardware-strapped, exactly as described above, but r1
(`metadata/e1m_modules/aen/hw-revisions.yaml:46`
 ("r1: CC3501E GPIO_30 (r2 unrouted).")) DOES proxy it to CC3501E
`GPIO_30` and IS firmware-drivable there -- with a hardware hazard the
block (`include/alp/boards/alp_e1m_evk.h:137-142`
 ("HAZARD: the same select net also reaches header")) now documents:
the same select net reaches header P18 pin 2 (`NetP18_2`) through R198
(0 ohm), and P18's jumper, when fitted, ties pin 1 (`+3V3`) to pin 2 --
so driving IO21 LOW on r1 while the jumper is fitted makes CC3501E
`GPIO_30` sink the +3V3 rail.

`docs/cc3501e-bridge.md` restated the same bugs and gains the same

mux state" table said "`SDIO_MUX_EN` (`GPIO_26`): HIGH (74LVC157 /E = 1 →
Hi-Z)." -- both
mislabelled `SDIO_MUX_SEL` as CC3501E `GPIO_30` unconditionally -- that
pin actually belongs to `IO8`/`EVK_PIN_I2S_MUX_EN` on r2

 ("CC3501E GPIO_30 (board 2626-R2; GPIO30 moved here from IO21)."),
`metadata/e1m_modules/aen/from-cc3501e.tsv:21`
 ("AG33	IO8	GPIO30")); on r2 `IO21` has no CC3501E pin at all. On the
