bullets at `:553-575`  ("- `SDIO_MUX_EN`") and the `I2S_MUX_EN` bullet
specifically at
`:576-612`  ("- `I2S_MUX_EN`")), which: states the same
neither-`/E`-state-is-safe-or-working fact as the header above for
`SDIO_MUX_EN` on a stock 74LVC157 (dropping the old "safe-default"
framing entirely); gives `SDIO_MUX_SEL` its r1 (firmware-drivable,
`GPIO_30`, same P18-pin-2 hazard) vs r2 (hardware-strapped, not a
CC3501E pin) split; and adds the previously-missing `I2S_MUX_EN` row
(`GPIO_30` on r2 only -- r1's `IO8` is a direct Alif GPIO, not
CC3501E-proxied at all) with its boot-time HIGH (disabled) level, the
`/E` contention caveat, and the `+VIO`-to-`+3V3` power-rail finding
above (VCC moved between a silent and an audible run, `/E`/`S` HIGH
caveat included), since it controls the same family of mux on U46.

**Two separate, wrong claims about the same rail description, both now
fixed.** First: at dev `5b7f1f3c6`, `docs/boards/e1m-evk.md` said `+VIO`
is selectable via header P17 -- the `+VIO` "(selectable" rails bullet and
the IO-voltage-select table's "jumper between" row. Now corrected at
`docs/boards/e1m-evk.md:49-53` ("the plugged-in") and
`docs/boards/e1m-evk.md:176` ("jumper connects"): P17 selects `+V_ANA`
(2626-R2 netlist, `P17`
pins 1/3/5 = `+5V`/`+3V3`/`+1V8`, pins 2/4/6 = `+V_ANA`), and `+VIO` is
the plugged-in SoM's own `VIO_OUT` (`E2` pins P1/P2), unaffected by
P17. **A pin-order hazard survived one pass of this fix**: at an
earlier pass of this same branch, `docs/boards/e1m-evk.md` briefly said
"one of `+1V8`/`+3V3`/`+5V`
(pins 1/3/5)" -- reversed. Per the netlist, pin 1 = `+5V`, pin 3 =
`+3V3`, pin 5 = `+1V8`, confirmed for BOTH P17 and P9
(`E1M-EVK-2626-R2_pinmap.csv`, internal repo, `grep -a ',P17,\|,P9,'`).
A user jumpering pins 1-2 expecting 1.8 V would have put 5 V on
`+V_ANA` instead. Fixed the order to "`+5V`/`+3V3`/`+1V8`" at
`docs/boards/e1m-evk.md:49-52`
 ("the plugged-in"), with the pin numbers (pins 1/3/5) at `:142`
 ("jumper connects"); every other P17/P9 pin statement in the tree
was checked against the netlist and already had the correct order.

Second: it implied `+V_ANA`/P17 also feeds the Arduino/mikroBUS
expansion IO ("for the user interface and Arduino expansion"). Per the
2626-R2 netlist, `+V_ANA` feeds only DAC header J15 and the OPA189 DAC
buffers U23/U24's `V+` (pin 5) -- nothing else. The Arduino/mikroBUS
LSF0108 level shifters U18/U22/U40 have `VREF_A` = `+VIO` and `VREF_B`
pulled to a DIFFERENT rail, `+VARD`, through R176/R177/R178; `+VARD` is
selected by header **P9** (netlist: pins 1/3/5 = `+5V`/`+3V3`/`+1V8`,
pins 2/4/6 = `+VARD` -- the same shape as P17/`+V_ANA`). Added as a new
`docs/boards/e1m-evk.md:177`  ("same shape as P17") table row and folded
into the rails bullet (`:49-63`  ("the plugged-in")) and the
"Expansion" bullet (`docs/boards/e1m-evk.md:360-362`
 ("Expansion:**"), reworded from "the IO-voltage select rail" to
name `+VARD`/P9 specifically). **`+VARD`'s own scope was ALSO
under-stated on the first pass**: it is not only the Arduino/mikroBUS
level-shifter reference (verified against the netlist,
`grep -a ',J17,\|,J18,\|,P3,\|,R146,\|,R147,\|,R173,\|,R174,\|,R175,\|,U16,\|,U17,\|,R95,\|,R96,\|,R97,\|,R98,\|,R99,\|,R100,\|,R101,\|,R102,'`):
U22 also carries `UART0.TX`/`RX` to Arduino UART header J17 (via
R95/R96) and `ENC1..3_X`/`Y` to encoder header J18 (via R97-R102), and
`+VARD` directly supplies J17 pin 1, J18 pin 1, header P3 pin 2, the
`CK_SCL`/`CK_SDA` pull-ups R146/R147, and U16/U17's `REFB` via
R173/R174. Setting P9 to `+5V` therefore puts 5 V on J17, J18, and
those I2C pull-ups too, not just the Arduino/mikroBUS shifters --
folded into the same `docs/boards/e1m-evk.md:49-63`
 ("the plugged-in") and `:143`  ("same shape as P17") edits.

**A second, later pass over `+VARD` found one more load the netlist grep
above had missed: `R175` is a `+VARD` pull-up on `CK_RST`**
(`E1M-EVK-2626-R2_pinmap.csv`, internal repo: `"CK_RST",R175,1` /
`"+VARD",R175,2`), and `CK_RST` itself reaches mikroBUS header P7 pin

Two small gaps left behind by #2033 (#2032, #2064), found in review of its
final commit `0f97f6c1a`. Neither is a regression from that PR, and neither
blocked it.

**No test proved an empty `swd` resource still refuses.** `0f97f6c1a` split
`bench_labgrid_resolve()`'s two resource checks: a place exporting no
`seuart` became legal (two of the three AEN places have no SE-UART at all), while a
place exporting no `swd` stays fatal
(`scripts/bench/aen/bench-env.sh:247-250` ("exports no 'swd' resource path")).
Only the relaxed half was tested
(`tests/scripts/test_bench_labgrid_resolver.py::test_place_with_swd_but_no_seuart_resolves_successfully`)
-- nothing constructed a place whose `acquired resources:` block omitted

(`tests/scripts/test_bench_labgrid_resolver.py:386-411` ("The mirror image")),
mirroring the
`seuart` test's fixture-construction technique (an executable stub written

### Fixed — SDHC DWC R2 (CID/CSD) response realignment (#2131)

`CONFIG_SDHC_RSP_136_HAS_CRC` (`zephyr/kconfigs/vendor-alif-peripherals.kconfig:629`
("config SDHC_RSP_136_HAS_CRC")) gates the 8-bit realignment shift the DWC_mshc
R2 (CID/CSD) response needs, but nothing defined the symbol, so `IS_ENABLED()`
was always 0 and the shift never ran. Once defined, the realignment loop
(now `sdhc_dwc_realign_r2_response()`, `zephyr/drivers/sdhc/sdhc_dwc.h:351`
("static inline void sdhc_dwc_realign_r2_response")) also carried the
shifted-out byte from the wrong neighbour -- `response[i + 1]` instead of
`response[i - 1]` -- which truncated a v2 CSD's `C_SIZE` to its low 16 bits.

Bench evidence (E1M-AEN803 serial 2026W36-0002), same Samsung microSD, whose MBR ends at
sector `0x0EEC0000` = 250,347,520 sectors:

- symbol undefined (dead code): `524800` sectors reported (256 MiB).
- symbol defined, wrong carry direction: `49020928` sectors reported
  (`C_SIZE` `0x3BAFF` truncated to `0xBAFF`).
- both fixes: the correct `250347520` sectors (122240 MiB), CID/CSD read
  correctly, sector 0 read back with its `55 AA` boot signature.

The realignment is now a small `static inline` helper so it is host-testable
independent of hardware; see `tests/unit/sdhc_dwc_r2_realign` (native_sim
ztest), which builds the 4 RESP words a DWC controller would hold for a real
CSD v2 register (`CSD_STRUCTURE = 1`, `READ_BL_LEN = 9`, `C_SIZE = 0x3BAFF`)
and asserts the decode matches the same field positions Zephyr's `sd_ops.c`
v2 CSD decode uses (that file lives in the Zephyr tree, not this repo) --
including `response[0]` (the least significant word), which the old carry
direction polluted with data from the wrong neighbour even though it has no
lower word to carry from.

### Fixed — `alp_audio_out_start()` / `alp_i2s_start()` before the first write failed on the Alif DesignWare I2S driver (#2132)

`alp_audio_out_start()` called before the first `alp_audio_out_write()` — the
open, set_volume, start, then stream order every in-tree caller uses
(`examples/aen/aen-evk-demo/src/main.c`, `examples/audio/audio-loopback`,
`examples/audio/audio-noise-suppression`, and the bench-only
`aen-i2s-tas2563-probe` on branch `test/2149-underrun-bench`) —
failed `ALP_ERR_NOMEM` (`-7`) on the Alif DesignWare I2S driver
(`snps,designware-i2s`). Traced to `zephyr/drivers/i2s/i2s_dw.c`'s
`tx_stream_start()` dequeuing a block from its TX ring buffer at
`I2S_TRIGGER_START` time and returning `-ENOMEM` when the buffer is empty
(`zephyr/drivers/i2s/i2s_dw.c:304` ("Ring buffer is empty")) — the `-7`
there does not mean out of memory, it means "START with nothing queued".
`examples/audio/i2s-tone` calls `alp_i2s_start()` the same way and hits the
same trap on the same silicon; its "TX starts fronting underrun silence"
comment was wrong for this driver and is corrected alongside the fix.
**Proven on silicon** (E1M-AEN803 serial 2026W36-0002, measured on `820692b7e`):
`alp_audio_out_open+set_volume(4)+start(I2S3)` now returns `0` (was `-7`),
the priming writes succeed, and both TAS2563 amps go ACTIVE. `z_start()`
and `z_stop()` have both been rewritten twice since that run (issue #2132
review round 4's lock/NOMEM-stale-flag handling, then issue #2137's
`I2S_STATE_ERROR` recovery) — see that issue's own changelog entry for the
newer same-unit (image `41d4acff9e9d6aa73d65380395208dc6`) data,
which is itself measured on `2e92da60a` (the first #2137 round), not any
round since — review rounds 2 and 3 of #2137 have not been re-run on
silicon at all.

Fixed once at the lowest shared layer both `<alp/i2s.h>` and `<alp/audio.h>`
route through — `src/backends/i2s/zephyr_drv.c`, not the audio backend above
it. `z_start()` defers the real `I2S_TRIGGER_START` when the TX side has
nothing queued yet, instead returning `ALP_OK` with a `tx_pending_start` flag
set (`src/backends/i2s/zephyr_drv.c:495`
("if (h->cfg.direction == ALP_I2S_DIR_TX && !s->tx_block_queued)")).
`z_write()` retries the real trigger every time a block is queued while
still pending. Write-then-start — a block already queued when
`alp_i2s_start()` is called — still triggers immediately via `z_start()`'s
own trigger call, unchanged.

Stopping a stream that never really started (`tx_started` false, whether
because `start()` was deferred and never fired, or never called at all)
used to forward straight to `I2S_TRIGGER_DRAIN`: `i2s_dw.c`'s `STOP`/`DRAIN`
refuse a trigger on a stream that never reached `I2S_STATE_RUNNING`
(`zephyr/drivers/i2s/i2s_dw.c:491` ("STOP trigger: invalid state"),
`zephyr/drivers/i2s/i2s_dw.c:522` ("DRAIN trigger: invalid state")), even
though real blocks may still be sitting in the TX ring holding slab memory.
`z_stop()` now falls back to `I2S_TRIGGER_DROP` when `DRAIN` fails, which
works from `READY` too and releases everything queued
(`src/backends/i2s/zephyr_drv.c:634`
("rc = _errno_to_alp(i2s_trigger(dev, _to_dir(h->cfg.direction), I2S_TRIGGER_DRAIN));")).
(This fallback was broadened further under issue #2137 to also cover a
stream stuck in `I2S_STATE_ERROR`; see that issue's own changelog entry.)

A second, related defect in the same area: `z_close()` only issued
`I2S_TRIGGER_DROP` when the dispatcher's `h->started` was true, so a TX
handle that only ever queued blocks (write before start, or a start whose
retry never fired) left real slab-block pointers in the driver's TX ring /
in-flight `mem_block` when its slab was `k_free()`'d. The next `open()` on
that device would dequeue a pointer into freed memory, and the completion
path would free it into the NEW handle's slab — memory corruption, not just
a leak. `z_close()` now DROPs unconditionally for TX; RX stays gated on
`h->started` exactly as before, byte-identical to `i2s_dw`'s own
`rx_stream_disable()`, which only ever ran when RX had actually been
triggered (`src/backends/i2s/zephyr_drv.c:881`
("if (dev != NULL && (h->cfg.direction == ALP_I2S_DIR_TX || h->started))")).

**Two defects found in a second review round, after the first fix landed
and was re-reviewed against reusable probe apps:**

- **A write could report frames as pushed that were never actually
  queued.** A failed START retry inside `z_write()` used to return the
  failure without releasing the block it had just queued, so the audio
  layer's chunked write loop (and a caller reading `out_frames`) could not
  tell "nothing was queued" apart from "queued, but the deferred start
  still failed" — both came back `ALP_ERR_IO`. Reproduced: write, write
  (fills the 2-block slab, stream never started), write with a short
  timeout returns `ALP_ERR_TIMEOUT` with `out_frames` still reporting 32
  frames pushed — audio that was never queued. Fixed: a failed retry now
  issues `I2S_TRIGGER_DROP` on the block it just queued before returning
  the error — while a start is pending the ring holds only that one block,
  so DROP releases exactly it, never a sibling write's
  (`src/backends/i2s/zephyr_drv.c:814`
  ("_errno_to_alp(i2s_trigger(dev, _to_dir(h->cfg.direction), I2S_TRIGGER_DROP));")).
  An I2S write that returns an error now NEVER leaves a block queued, so
  the audio backend's chunked loop again counts a chunk toward
  `out_frames` ONLY on `ALP_OK`, restoring `out_frames`'s original "frames
  actually pushed" meaning (`include/alp/audio.h`, `include/alp/i2s.h`).
  This also makes `alp_i2s_write()`'s doc claim "every subsequent write
  retries the trigger until it succeeds" literally true: the slab can no
  longer fill up with un-started blocks under sustained START failures.

- **A successful START didn't always clear the pending flag.** Sequence:
  start (deferred) → write (START retry fails, block dropped by the fix
  above) → start (explicit retry; nothing is queued yet post-fix, so this
  defers again rather than triggering) → write (fires the real trigger).
  Before this fix, `z_start()`'s immediate-trigger success path set
  `tx_started` without clearing `tx_pending_start`, so if that path were
  ever reached with `tx_pending_start` still true (e.g. before the DROP
  fix above closed off the specific sequence that exposed it, or via any
  future code path that queues a block without going through the retry
  logic), the next write would retry a START on an ALREADY-RUNNING stream
  and get `i2s_dw`'s `-EIO` — every later write into a stream that is
  actually playing would then fail. Fixed by construction, not by patching
  one call site: `_mark_tx_started()` clears `tx_pending_start` in the
  same assignment as setting `tx_started`, and is now the ONLY place
  either can be set true; `_mark_tx_stopped()` is the ONLY place a TX
  stream returns to FULLY idle, clearing all three flags together
  (`src/backends/i2s/zephyr_drv.c:453` ("static void _mark_tx_started(alp_z_i2s_side_t *s)"),
  `src/backends/i2s/zephyr_drv.c:463` ("static void _mark_tx_stopped(alp_z_i2s_side_t *s)")).
  The invariant
  `tx_started ⇒ !tx_pending_start` now holds regardless of which path
  reaches it. (Issue #2137 review round 2 added a second, narrower
  function, `_mark_tx_needs_restart()`, for a stream that is idle but
  owes a restart rather than fully idle -- `tx_pending_start` ends up
  `true` there instead of `false`, so it could not simply reuse
  `_mark_tx_stopped()`; it still clears `tx_started`, so the invariant
  holds via either of the two named functions, not one. See that
  issue's own changelog entry.)

**Concurrency (found in the second review round, closed across two more):**
an earlier draft of this fix's docs added a "calls on one handle must not
run concurrently" restriction to the `[ABI-STABLE]` `<alp/i2s.h>`/
`<alp/audio.h>` headers. That draft never reached `dev`, so dropping the
restriction again narrows no shipped contract — it is simply wrong: the
dispatcher deliberately only counts in-flight ops (`src/i2s_dispatch.c`), it
does not serialize them, so real cross-thread races exist and needed fixing,
not documenting around.

Two separate races, two separate fixes. A `k_spinlock` in the sidecar
(`src/backends/i2s/zephyr_drv.c:320` ("struct k_spinlock lock;")) guards the three `tx_*` flags and the
`i2s_trigger()` calls that change them in `z_start()`/`z_write()`/`z_stop()`
— never held across `k_mem_slab_alloc()` or the Zephyr `i2s_write()` API
call, both of which can block. This closes thread A's write() queuing a
block racing thread B's stop() DROPping it (or vice versa) once both sides
are inside the lock. It does NOT close a second race: write()'s
`k_mem_slab_alloc()`/`i2s_write()` genuinely run unlocked, so a write can
queue a real block, then a concurrent stop() can lock, see the stream never
started, DROP that exact block for real, and clear the flags — all before
the write reaches its own lock acquisition to (now falsely) record
`tx_block_queued = true`. The next `start()` then sees that stale flag, takes
the immediate-trigger path, and hits `i2s_dw`'s real empty-ring `-ENOMEM` —
the original `-7` symptom, reappearing via a race. Closed on the READ side
instead of trying to close the write/stop timing gap: on TX, `z_start()`
now treats an `ALP_ERR_NOMEM` from the real START trigger as "the flag was
stale", not a hard failure — a failed START changes no other `i2s_dw` driver
state (`i2s_dw.c` returns before touching `stream->state`), so it clears
`tx_block_queued`, defers instead of failing, and lets the next `write()`
queue for real and fire the trigger normally
(`src/backends/i2s/zephyr_drv.c:540`
("} else if (rc == ALP_ERR_NOMEM) {")). Reproduced deterministically without
real threads via a new `fake_i2s_set_write_hook()` that runs synchronously
from inside the fake's `write()` callback — i.e. from inside the real
`i2s_write()` call `z_write()` makes, before it reaches its own lock — and
calls `alp_i2s_stop()` right then, standing in for a second thread winning
the race.

A related fix in the same function: the failed-retry path in `z_write()`
used to discard `I2S_TRIGGER_DROP`'s own return code and clear
`tx_block_queued` regardless. If DROP itself ever failed, that would silently
break the "an error means nothing is queued" invariant — a write would
return an error while its block might still be queued. `tx_block_queued` is
now cleared ONLY when DROP returns success; a DROP failure is surfaced to
the caller instead of the original START failure, so the state is visibly
unresolved rather than confidently wrong
(`src/backends/i2s/zephyr_drv.c:815` ("if (drop_rc != ALP_OK) {")).

The RX side does not carry the empty-queue trap: `i2s_dw.c`'s
`rx_stream_start()` allocates a fresh block from its own `k_mem_slab`
instead of dequeuing from a caller-filled ring buffer, so RX `start()` is
never deferred. The Yocto/ALSA and sw_fallback audio-out backends already
returned `ALP_OK` for a start before any write (ALSA's `snd_pcm_prepare()`
needs no queued data either); this fix makes the Zephyr/I2S backend
observably match them instead of diverging by backend.

One related, smaller behaviour change falls out of routing everything
through `tx_started`/`tx_pending_start` rather than the dispatcher's
`h->started`: `alp_i2s_stop()`/`alp_audio_out_stop()` on a TX handle that
was opened but never started or written to now returns `ALP_OK` via `DROP`
instead of the pre-existing `-EIO` a bare `DRAIN` used to surface in that
case. (Issue #2137 review round 2, finding 3: the current code goes
further still and skips the doomed `DRAIN` attempt entirely for a TX
handle `tx_started` already says is not running, rather than issuing it
and discarding a known-in-advance `-EIO` — avoids that trigger's own
`LOG_ERR` on every such call. See that issue's own changelog entry for the
current `z_stop()` shape and why "a harmless `DROP` no-op" undersold it:
`DROP` is not a no-op when blocks are genuinely queued, see the stranded-
blocks case two paragraphs up.)

Regression tests: `tests/unit/i2s_start_defer/` proves the deferred-start
state machine directly against `<alp/i2s.h>` with a fake I2S device that —
unlike `tests/unit/i2s_write_bounds`'s always-succeeds fake — models the
DesignWare driver's empty-queue `TRIGGER_START` refusal, its `-EIO` on an
already-running `START` and a not-running `STOP`/`DRAIN`, and `DROP`'s
unconditional release of every queued block back to the real `k_mem_slab`
captured at `configure()` time; covers start-then-write, write-then-start
(now also pinning that a follow-up write doesn't spuriously retry),
stop-with-no-write, the stranded-blocks repro, a running-stream
stop/restart cycle, close-then-reopen with no stale block, a forced START
failure retrying across 5 consecutive writes (past the 2-block slab depth,
proving the slab can no longer exhaust), fault-clear recovery, the
explicit-restart-after-failed-retry sequence, and the write-vs-stop race
above (reproduced single-threaded via the new `fake_i2s_set_write_hook()`).
The fake's forced-failure
knob (`fake_i2s_force_start_fail()`) pins this backend's own retry/DROP
bookkeeping under an injected fault — it does not claim that exact
sequence is reachable on real `i2s_dw`, which only fails `START` on an
empty ring or an already-running stream; see `fake_i2s.c`'s own header
comment. `tests/unit/audio_out_start_defer/` proves the `<alp/audio.h>`
composition on top, including the volume-scaled chunked write loop
(stereo, more than 128 frames per block, `set_volume(4)` — the exact shape
the silicon repro used) and that a failed deferred-start retry does NOT
count toward `out_frames`.

### Fixed — `alif_pdm.c` ignored the Zephyr `dmic` contract; `<alp/audio.h>` PDM capture returned `ALP_OK` then read nothing (#2133)

`alp_audio_in_open()` + `alp_audio_in_start()` returned `ALP_OK` on the E1M-AEN801's HP PDM mics, then every `alp_audio_in_read()` timed out with an empty FIFO. `dmic_alif_pdm_configure()` (`zephyr/drivers/audio/alif_pdm.c`) broke the standard Zephyr `dmic` API contract two ways: it read `req_chan_map_lo`'s low byte VERBATIM as the hardware channel-enable mask instead of decoding the standard `dmic_build_channel_map()` nibble encoding, and it never left the PDM clock-mode field `MICROPHONE_SLEEP` nor programmed per-channel FIR/gain. The portable `src/backends/audio/zephyr_drv.c` backend used the standard encoding correctly, so it was the one broken by the driver's divergence: for its 2-channel request the verbatim read produced `0x10` (hardware channel 4 only) instead of `0x03` (hardware channels 0 and 1, where the EVK's mics actually are).

Fixed by making the driver honour the contract itself: a dependency-free translation header, grounded in the register layout and HWRM 15.7.4.3.1's even/rising-odd/falling edge rule (`zephyr/drivers/audio/alif_pdm_chanmap.h:21` ("hw_channel = (pdm_controller * 2) + lr")), replaces (not ORs) the channel-enable field and rejects a duplicate/out-of-order map the ISR cannot honour; per-channel FIR/gain defaults are primed in `configure()`, with the actual `PDM_MODE` write deferred to `DMIC_TRIGGER_START` so `configure()` alone cannot start the block sampling. `configure()` validates the requested `pcm_rate` against a HWRM/DFP-grounded clock-mode table (`zephyr/drivers/audio/alif_pdm.c:452` ("{ 8000U, PDM_MODE_STANDARD_VOICE_512_CLK_FRQ, 512000U },"), `zephyr/drivers/audio/alif_pdm.c:465` ("{ 16000U, PDM_MODE_HIGH_QUALITY_1024_CLK_FRQ, 1024000U },"), `zephyr/drivers/audio/alif_pdm.c:474` ("{ 32000U, PDM_MODE_WIDE_BANDWIDTH_AUDIO_1536_CLK_FRQ, 1536000U },"), and `zephyr/drivers/audio/alif_pdm.c:518` ("{ 48000U, PDM_MODE_FULL_BANDWIDTH_AUDIO_3071_CLK_FRQ, 3072000U },")) AND the board's own mic clock range, a board-level DT fact (`clk-frequency-min`/`clk-frequency-max` on `alif,alif-pdm.yaml`) rather than something the driver or an app invents -- the portable backend's own generic clock window is unchanged (`src/backends/audio/zephyr_drv.c:331` (".min_pdm_clk_freq = 1000000,")). HWRM 15.7.5.3.1's back-to-back `PDM_CTL0` write-spacing requirement is honoured by `pdm_ctl0_write_spacer()` (`zephyr/drivers/audio/alif_pdm.c:541` ("static void pdm_ctl0_write_spacer(const struct device *dev)")) before every `PDM_CONFIG_REGISTER` write; `pdm_force_sleep()` (`zephyr/drivers/audio/alif_pdm.c:563` ("static void pdm_force_sleep(const struct device *dev)")) forces the block's channel-enable and clock-mode fields inert on a genuine cold boot only, so a fresh image no longer silently inherits whatever mode/channels the PREVIOUS image left running.

**Drop reporting.** On `dev`, `alif_pdm.c` had no overflow detection at all: a slab-alloc miss, a delivery-queue overflow (oldest block evicted), or a genuine hardware FIFO overflow (`PDM_ERROR_IRQ`'s status-register bit 0, `zephyr/drivers/audio/alif_pdm_reg.h:85` ("#define PDM_ERROR_IRQ_FIFO_OVERFLOW_STAT (0x1U << 0U)")) all passed silently. Fixed: each site now sets a new sticky `overrun` flag (`zephyr/drivers/audio/alif_pdm.c:377` ("bool overrun;")) -- the slab-alloc miss (`zephyr/drivers/audio/alif_pdm.c:1279`), the hardware FIFO overflow (`zephyr/drivers/audio/alif_pdm.c:1219`), an unplannable burst (`zephyr/drivers/audio/alif_pdm.c:1442`), and the delivery-queue overflow (`zephyr/drivers/audio/alif_pdm.c:1474`) -- checked by `dmic_alif_pdm_read()` before every `k_msgq_get()` so a caller gets `-EIO` instead of silently splicing the next block onto the gap (`zephyr/drivers/audio/alif_pdm.c:1168` ("if (pdata->overrun) {")); the flag clears only in `DMIC_TRIGGER_STOP`, after it frees the in-progress block and drains the queue, so a restart without a prior `STOP` cannot erase the report. `DMIC_TRIGGER_START`/`dmic_alif_pdm_configure()`'s refuse/no-op/proceed decisions are pure functions, `pdm_decide_start()`/`pdm_configure_allowed()` (`zephyr/drivers/audio/alif_pdm_trigger_state.h:56` and `zephyr/drivers/audio/alif_pdm_trigger_state.h:93`), mirroring `dmic_mcux.c`'s `DMIC_STATE_ACTIVE`/`DMIC_STATE_ERROR` handling (ZEPHYR_BASE `zephyr/drivers/audio/dmic_mcux.c`): START refuses `-EIO` when unconfigured or still flagged `overrun`; `configure()` refuses `-EBUSY` while a capture is active, so a second `configure()` call can no longer force-sleep the hardware or swap `mem_slab` out from under an in-progress capture.

**Resume/suspend hygiene.** On `dev`, `PM_DEVICE_ACTION_SUSPEND` left `record_data`/`overrun`/the in-progress buffer/the queue exactly as an active session left them -- SUSPEND left capture running, so a post-resume `DMIC_TRIGGER_START` could silently NOOP over a block nothing was sampling into. Fixed: `pdm_hw_bringup(dev, cold_init)` (`zephyr/drivers/audio/alif_pdm.c:1514` ("static int pdm_hw_bringup(const struct device *dev, bool cold_init)")) only force-sleeps on a genuine cold boot, so `PM_DEVICE_ACTION_RESUME` no longer wipes a prior session's hardware channel-enable field; `PM_DEVICE_ACTION_SUSPEND` (`zephyr/drivers/audio/alif_pdm.c:1641` ("case PM_DEVICE_ACTION_SUSPEND: {")) now runs the same free/drain/record_data=0/overrun=false cleanup `DMIC_TRIGGER_STOP` does, and resets `clk_mode` to `PDM_MODE_MICROPHONE_SLEEP` (`zephyr/drivers/audio/alif_pdm.c:1708` ("pdata->clk_mode = PDM_MODE_MICROPHONE_SLEEP;")) as a fail-safe against the hardware channel-enable/FIR/GAIN registers NOT surviving the low-power transition -- a post-resume `DMIC_TRIGGER_START` now always refuses as "not configured" rather than risk proceeding over dead register state. Latent today (`CONFIG_PM_DEVICE` is off on every board this driver ships on).

**Errno mapping.** `alp_audio_in_read(..., timeout_ms=0)` reaches `k_msgq_get(K_NO_WAIT)`, which returns `-ENOMSG` for "nothing queued yet"; the shared `alp_status_from_zephyr_errno()` baseline has no arm for it and falls through to `ALP_ERR_IO` ("dropped data, sticky") instead of `ALP_ERR_TIMEOUT`. Fixed with a local override in `src/backends/audio/zephyr_drv.c`'s `errno_to_alp()` (`alp_status_from_zephyr_errno_ex()`, `src/backends/audio/zephyr_drv.c:140`), kept local rather than touching the shared baseline header to stay minimal against `fix/2132-audio-out-start-defers-until-first-block`'s concurrently in-flight edits to the same file's `out` paths.

**Gain clamp.** `pdm_set_ch_gain()`'s `ch_gain` is only meaningful in `PDM_CH_GAIN`'s 12-bit field; a caller-supplied value above `PDM_CH_GAIN_MAX` (`0xFFF`) used to be written unclamped, truncating to bits [11:0] -- `0x1000` exactly truncates to 0 (mutes the channel), the opposite of what a caller raising gain would expect. Since the function returns `void` (existing public API), it now clamps through `pdm_ch_gain_clamp()` (`zephyr/drivers/audio/alif_pdm_reg.h:59` ("static inline uint32_t pdm_ch_gain_clamp(uint32_t ch_gain)")), called from `pdm_set_ch_gain()` (`zephyr/drivers/audio/alif_pdm.c:884` ("ch_gain = pdm_ch_gain_clamp(ch_gain);")) and from `pdm_apply_channel_defaults()`'s `cfg->channel_gain` application (`zephyr/drivers/audio/alif_pdm.c:608` ("pdm_set_ch_gain(dev, hw_ch, cfg->channel_gain);")), with a `LOG_WRN` instead of a silent truncation. `PDM_INIT`'s `BUILD_ASSERT` independently bounds the DT `channel-gain` property to `0x001..PDM_CH_GAIN_MAX` at build time (`zephyr/drivers/audio/alif_pdm.c:1760` ("BUILD_ASSERT(DT_INST_PROP_OR(n, channel_gain, 0x200) >= 0x001 && \")); an inverted `clk-frequency-min`/`clk-frequency-max` DT range is independently caught the same way (`zephyr/drivers/audio/alif_pdm.c:1742` ("BUILD_ASSERT(!(DT_INST_NODE_HAS_PROP(n, clk_frequency_min) && \")).

`examples/aen/aen-pdm-mic-alif` moves onto the standard contract: it measures the ACHIEVED sample rate (frames delivered / elapsed wall-clock time, excluding the first read's startup latency) rather than only checking "PCM varies", requires it within ±5% of the requested rate, treats a driver-reported drop (`dmic_read()` returning `-EIO`) as an outright `FAIL` regardless of what the surviving blocks measured (`examples/aen/aen-pdm-mic-alif/src/main.c:414` ("verdict = "), `examples/aen/aen-pdm-mic-alif/src/main.c:423` ("verdict = "), and `examples/aen/aen-pdm-mic-alif/src/main.c:432` ("verdict = ")), and gates `PASS` on at least one channel's AC RMS clearing a documented floor above idle noise, derived directly from silicon (see below) rather than assumed (`examples/aen/aen-pdm-mic-alif/src/main.c:141` ("((4U * 15U * DT_PROP(PDM_NODE, channel_gain)) / PDM_GAIN_BASELINE_0X200)")) -- peak-to-peak is still measured and printed per channel but is no longer gated on, since a single transient spike can clear a peak-to-peak floor without sustained signal. `PASS` (`examples/aen/aen-pdm-mic-alif/src/main.c:440` ("verdict = ")) is worded as "above the idle-noise AC-RMS floor", not "live audio": this example has no controlled stimulus of its own, so the actual acoustic verification is the loopback below, scoped to mic ch0/ch1 only. `examples/aen/aen-evk-demo`'s sound-baseline loop reads `SOUND_BASELINE_BLOCKS + 1` blocks and skips the first (settling transient), preserving the full `SOUND_BASELINE_BLOCKS` in the baseline (`examples/aen/aen-evk-demo/src/main.c:4584` ("for (unsigned b = 0; b < SOUND_BASELINE_BLOCKS + 1u; b++) {")). That path needs a mic sample rate whose PDM clock is >= 1.2 MHz on this EVK: at the example's `SOUND_SAMPLE_RATE_HZ` (16000, mode 4's 1024 kHz clock) the board overlay's `clk-frequency-min = <1200000>` rejects it with `-EINVAL`, so the baseline/correlation path is exercised only once a mic-capable rate is available independent of the speaker rate (issue #2134, software resample). `<alp/audio.h>` documents the settling requirement generically -- discard at least the first block, and more if the backend documents a longer settling duration (`include/alp/audio.h:134` ("-- discard at least the first block, and more if the backend")) -- with the measured figure (see below) kept in the Alif binding, not the portable header.

New host-testable regression: `tests/unit/alif_pdm_chanmap` (12 cases) locks the channel-map translation against the portable backend's and the example's exact requests, plus `pdm_ch_gain_clamp()`'s boundary (`0xFFF` passes through unchanged; `0x1000` and `0xFFFFFFFF` both clamp to `PDM_CH_GAIN_MAX`) -- mutation-checked: removing the clamp (`return ch_gain;` unconditionally) fails exactly the two out-of-range cases, 10/12; restored, 12/12. `tests/unit/alif_pdm_trigger_state` (6 cases) locks `pdm_decide_start()`'s refuse/no-op/proceed decision and `pdm_configure_allowed()`'s active-capture refusal (`tests/unit/alif_pdm_trigger_state/src/test_alif_pdm_trigger_state.c:79` ("ZTEST(alif_pdm_trigger_state, test_configure_refused_while_active)") and `tests/unit/alif_pdm_trigger_state/src/test_alif_pdm_trigger_state.c:84` ("ZTEST(alif_pdm_trigger_state, test_configure_allowed_while_idle)")); mutation-checked per case. `tests/unit/errno_mapping` (`test_zephyr_enomsg_baseline_is_io_not_timeout`, `tests/unit/errno_mapping/src/test_errno_mapping.c:86`) pins the shared baseline's `-ENOMSG` answer; `tests/unit/audio_in_enomsg_timeout` (`test_nonblocking_empty_read_is_timeout_not_io`, `tests/unit/audio_in_enomsg_timeout/src/test_audio_in_enomsg_timeout.c:30`) exercises `zephyr_drv.c`'s override end to end against a fake DMIC backend -- deleting the override fails this test; restoring it passes.

**Silicon evidence, E1M-AEN803 serial 2026W36-0002.** Register-level configuration: `PDM_CONFIG_REGISTER` read back matching the requested channel map and mode, held throughout capture; the 16 kHz build's DT-range guard is confirmed (`dmic_configure -> -EINVAL`, register never written). 48 kHz mode 7: `measured_rate_hz=48000` exactly, `slab_missed=0`, `overrun=0`, no `-EIO` for the full run (commit `68a169977`). Acoustic capture at 48 kHz on mic ch0/ch1 (PDM controller 0) ONLY is separately verified by a speaker-to-mic loopback -- the `PROBE_LOOPBACK` mode of `examples/aen/aen-i2s-tas2563-probe` on branch `test/u46-i2s-tas2563-on-reworked-mux` (commit `56631094d`, issue #2143), NOT this driver's own example, which has no controlled stimulus: TAS2563 speakers (independently verified audible) played known tones at gain `0x200` (readback-confirmed); Goertzel-bin analysis (2 s windows, first 200 ms discarded) found the 1 kHz bin at 9.3/0.1 dB (ch0/ch1) in silence rising to 43.4/48.8 dB at volume 16 and 57.8/57.6 dB at volume 48, a 500 Hz bin at 54.7/56.6 dB that only lit up during the 500 Hz stimulus window (staying within -9.8..+5.3 dB everywhere else), and peak-to-peak (the probe's own `loop_chan_result_t.p2p`; per channel, 960 ms window, after `zephyr_drv.c`'s `dc_block_s16()` high-pass, hence not a multiple of 32) rising from 128/128 in silence to 266/292 at 1 kHz/volume 16 and 651/652 at 1 kHz/volume 48. **The D2 pair (HW 4/5) is register-level verified only, never acoustically tested.** An early raw hex dump of the capture-start transient (from the same unattended 30 s bench build) showed roughly 7 zero samples followed by ~25 samples of ring-down at 48 kHz -- under 1 ms total; documented in `zephyr/dts/bindings/audio/alif,alif-pdm.yaml`'s decimator-settling description (its comma-bearing filename isn't a checkable `path:NNN` citation).

The example's signal-level gate was re-derived from AC RMS instead of peak-to-peak: a probe loopback silence window measured peak-to-peak 545 on one channel with the room silent, above the prior 512 floor, from a transient spike rather than sustained signal. The new floor (`examples/aen/aen-pdm-mic-alif/src/main.c`'s `MIN_SIGNAL_RMS_AC_LSB` = 4 x 15 = 60 at gain `0x200`) is derived directly from this example's OWN idle measurement (E1M-AEN803 serial 2026W36-0002, 2026-09-15 19:51Z, 48 kHz, `channel-gain` `0x200`, raw `dmic_read()`, 3 runs / 12 channel readings over blocks 1-3, n=14400 samples/channel): `rms_ac` read 15 on every channel in every run (one earlier, interrupted attempt read 18-19), and every run read `RESULT INCONCLUSIVE` (idle only; ambient sound during those runs is unknown). **Still unmeasured on this example:** a `PASS` at a real sound level -- a PREDICTION from the probe loopback's AC-RMS estimate (roughly 20 in silence, 68 at volume 16, and 195 at volume 48, all above the 60 floor), not yet confirmed by a run of this example itself.

### Added — `<alp/dsp>` streaming integer-ratio decimator: anti-alias FIR + keep-1-in-N (#2134)

Phase 1 of #2134 only: this adds the standalone decimator to the portable
`<alp/dsp>` layer. It does **not** wire it into the audio-in backend yet —
`alp_audio_in_open(.sample_rate_hz = 16000)` on a board whose PDM can't be
clocked for 16 kHz still fails the same way it did before this change. That
wiring is a separate, later phase (Refs #2134; blocked on #2132 / #2133
landing first, since both touch `src/backends/audio/zephyr_drv.c` and
`include/alp/audio.h`, which this phase deliberately did not touch).

Reuse check first: `<alp/dsp.h>`'s existing `alp_dsp_chain_t` FIR/IIR/window/FFT
pipeline (`include/alp/dsp.h:247`
("alp_dsp_chain_t *alp_dsp_chain_open(const alp_dsp_stage_t *stages, size_t n_stages);")) has no
rate-changing stage — its contract is `got <= min(in_n, out_cap)`
(`include/alp/dsp.h:262-263` ("Receives the number of output samples written")),
which a decimator (`out < in`) cannot satisfy without redefining that shared
contract. Nothing else under `<alp/dsp>` filters or resamples. New API added
instead of extending the chain.

New public surface (`alp_dsp_decimator_t` + `alp_dsp_decimator_init` /
`_process` / `_reset`, `include/alp/dsp.h:602`
("alp_status_t alp_dsp_decimator_init(alp_dsp_decimator_t *dec, uint32_t ratio, uint8_t n_channels);")):
caller-allocated, no heap (`include/alp/dsp.h:515-520`
("@par Allocation: caller-owned, no heap")) — unlike the pool-backed
`alp_dsp_chain_t`, this is a plain value type the caller declares on the
stack/static/embedded in another struct. At 1104 bytes on M55 it is larger
than Zephyr's default `CONFIG_MAIN_STACK_SIZE` (1024 B), so the Doxygen
recommends `static` storage or embedding it in backend/app state rather than
a thread's own stack (`include/alp/dsp.h:522`
("@par Size: 1104 bytes on M55")). Supports ratios 2, 3, 4, 6 (covering
48000->16000/8000 Hz and
32000->16000/8000 Hz) and 1..2 interleaved int16 channels with independent
per-channel filter state. `alp_dsp_decimator_process`
(`src/dsp_decimator.c:194` ("const size_t exact_out = (dec->phase + in_frames) / dec->ratio;")) computes the
exact output frame count for a call up front from the running phase before
touching any state, so an undersized `out_cap` is rejected with the decimator
left completely unchanged (no partial consumption) — arbitrary block sizes
across calls give bit-identical output to one big call, with the keep-1-in-N
phase preserved across the boundary.

Filter: one Q15 fixed-point, 135-tap, Kaiser-windowed-sinc (beta 6.976)
anti-alias low-pass (`src/dsp_decimator.c:136`
("static const int16_t *_alp_dsp_decim_lookup(uint32_t ratio)")), designed by
the committed `scripts/gen_dsp_decimator_coeffs.py` and re-verified against
the embedded tables via its `--check` mode
(`scripts/gen_dsp_decimator_coeffs.py:168` ("def check():")). The passband
edge is held at a fixed offset below the output Nyquist (`fs_in /
(2*ratio)`); the stopband edge sits at `fs_out - passband_edge` (`fs_out =
fs_in / ratio`) rather than at the output Nyquist itself — the wider
transition band that buys is what lands stopband attenuation around 70 dB
at this tap count instead of ~40. Content between the output Nyquist and
`fs_out - passband_edge` is therefore NOT stopband-attenuated; it folds into
the transition band above the stated passband (ratio 3: 8.0-8.8 kHz folds
into the 7201.6-8798.4 Hz transition). Each table's centre tap is nudged so
it sums to exactly 32768 — unity DC gain in Q15, not just in the float
design (`scripts/gen_dsp_decimator_coeffs.py:95-96`
("centre = (N - 1) // 2")). Measured on the shipped Q15 taps: ripple
0.0044-0.0062 dB, stopband attenuation 65.46-70.31 dB across the four ratios
(worst case is ratio 3 — its wider fs_in gives it the tightest transition
band of the four) — full per-ratio numbers are in `alp_dsp_decimator_init`'s
Doxygen (`include/alp/dsp.h:559-587`
("@par Filter design")). Convolution runs in an int64 accumulator with a Q15
rescale and explicit int16 saturation (`src/dsp_decimator.c:230-240`
("int64_t acc = (int64_t)coeffs[half] * (int64_t)window[half];")); no CMSIS-DSP
dependency: `arm_fir_decimate_q15` requires its block size to be a multiple
of the decimation ratio, which conflicts with the arbitrary-block-size
requirement here, so this stays on the portable-C path for phase 1. A CMSIS
Helium path is a possible phase-2 optimisation if board measurement warrants
it, following the same chunking approach the SW fallback backend already
uses for CMSIS FIR input, `src/backends/dsp/sw_fallback.c:225`
("while (off < in_n) {").

CPU: the tap table is symmetric (odd-length linear-phase FIR), so the
convolution is folded to 68 multiplies instead of 135
(`src/dsp_decimator.c:232-235` ("acc += (int64_t)coeffs[j] * (int64_t)(window[j] + window[taps - 1u - j]);")),
`coeffs` / `n_channels` are hoisted to locals once per call instead of
re-reading `dec->` each iteration, and the circular-buffer wrap uses a
compare (`src/dsp_decimator.c:210` ("if (widx == taps) {")) instead of `%
taps` (the write index only ever steps by 1, so a full udiv+mls was wasted
work). The fold is bit-identical to the unfolded form: integer addition and
multiplication are exact (no floating-point reordering), and re-deriving the
symmetric-sum identity `sum(c[j]*w[j])` == `c[half]*w[half] +
sum(c[j]*(w[j]+w[N-1-j]))` for j in [0,half) holds for any symmetric table,
which was confirmed against the shipped tables over 20 random windows per
ratio. No ABI change (int64 accumulation is unchanged; `32768 * sum(|c|)`
still exceeds 2^31 for ratios 2, 3, and 4, so it stays int64).

Host tests (native_sim, `tests/unit/dsp_decimator/`): a table-driven test
covers EVERY supported ratio (`tests/unit/dsp_decimator/src/test_dsp_decimator.c:92-100`
("static const decim_ratio_spec_t k_ratio_specs[] = {")) — a tone at ~0.9x
the ratio's passband edge must stay within a generous tolerance of the
injected amplitude, and a tone just above the ratio's stopband edge must be
attenuated by at least (stated stopband - 0.5 dB), which catches a
wrong-ratio table (the #2134 review's case-3u-serves-the-ratio-6-table
mutation: a swapped table's actual cutoff sits at the wrong ratio's edge, so
the passband tone lands out of band). Exact frame counts across 1/7/256/1023-frame
blocks match a single-block run bit-for-bit AND match the absolute `n_in /
ratio` count (`tests/unit/dsp_decimator/src/test_dsp_decimator.c:206`
("zassert_equal(got_ref, n_in / ratio,"));
stereo channels stay independent
(`tests/unit/dsp_decimator/src/test_dsp_decimator.c:242`
("ZTEST(alp_dsp_decimator, test_stereo_channels_independent)")); an
unsupported ratio is rejected
(`tests/unit/dsp_decimator/src/test_dsp_decimator.c:292`
("ZTEST(alp_dsp_decimator, test_unsupported_ratio_rejected)")); and reset
reproduces a fresh `init` exactly
(`tests/unit/dsp_decimator/src/test_dsp_decimator.c:348`
("ZTEST(alp_dsp_decimator, test_reset_reproduces_fresh_init)")).

Mutation-checked, each confirmed red then reverted: (1) swapping ratio 3's
table lookup to serve the ratio-6 table reddened
`test_every_ratio_passband_and_stopband_tones`'s passband assertion for
ratio 3 (its actual cutoff moved to the wrong edge); (2) the phase-wrap
off-by-one `dec->phase < dec->ratio` -> `<=` reddened both the new absolute
`n_in / ratio` assertion and the existing chunked-vs-single-block comparison
in `test_exact_frame_counts_across_odd_blocks`. The suite is green again
after both reverts.

`scripts/gen_dsp_decimator_coeffs.py --check` parses the tables embedded in
`src/dsp_decimator.c` and re-derives them from the design parameters, failing
if they've drifted (`scripts/gen_dsp_decimator_coeffs.py:168`
("def check():")); a pytest exercises both the pass and a deliberately
corrupted-tap fail case
(`tests/scripts/test_gen_dsp_decimator_coeffs.py:35`
("def test_check_fails_when_a_tap_is_wrong(tmp_path):")), skipping if numpy
isn't installed (`tests/scripts/test_gen_dsp_decimator_coeffs.py:16`
("pytest.importorskip")).

ABI: `docs/abi/v0.16-snapshot.json` unchanged vs `HEAD` (`abi_snapshot.py
--diff` reports no diff) — the decimator surface (3 new functions, 2 new
macros, 1 new struct) was already captured in this phase-1 slice.

### Added — PDM capture at 8 and 16 kHz on boards whose mics can't be clocked for it (#2134)

`alp_audio_in_open(.sample_rate_hz = 16000)`, and 8000, used to fail with
`ALP_ERR_INVAL` on the E1M-EVK. Its MP34DT05TR-A mics need a PDM clock of
at least 1.2 MHz, and the Alif modes for 8 and 16 kHz run slower than that.

The Zephyr audio-in backend now tries the requested rate first. If the PDM
refuses it (`-EINVAL`), the backend opens at the lowest native rate that is
an integer multiple of the request: 32 kHz, then 48 kHz. It then decimates
each block with the `<alp/dsp.h>` decimator from phase 1 (#2160).
- Reads still return frames at the requested rate.
- `frames_per_block` still counts frames at that rate.
- Only S16 is supported.

The decimator moved out of `src/dsp_dispatch.c` into `src/dsp_decimator.c`.
PDM capture now links it without pulling in the DSP chain's handle pool;
`gen_dsp_decimator_coeffs.py` and its test follow the move.

Bench-verified on E1M-AEN803 2026W36-0009 (Flow C, M55-HE, one EVK PDM
mic), each from a cold boot:
- 16000 Hz: `ALP_OK`, 16042 Hz delivered (32 kHz native, ratio 2), live
  signal. On unmodified `dev` the same open returns `ALP_ERR_INVAL`.
- 8000 Hz: 8021 Hz delivered (32 kHz native, ratio 4).
- 48000 Hz: native and unchanged, 48139 Hz delivered.

### Added — CC3501E host-side link-failure ring (#2136)

**Before:** a bridge wedge left no usable evidence. `cc3501e_request_locked()` overwrote
`ctx->rx_scratch[0]` on every pre-decode failure, and the firmware side could not fill the gap
either — a wedge-probe build's warm `nRESET` does not preserve retained RAM across the reset
(cc3501e-bridge-firmware#148).

**After:** `cc3501e_t` carries an 8-entry `link_log` ring (`<alp/chips/cc3501e/core.h>`),
filled only when a request bails with no reply status decoded. Each entry records the opcode,
which wire phase the attempt reached, the mapped status, the request- and reply-header bytes,
READY-line evidence, and the recovery-attempt count — enough to tell a deaf-armed slave apart
from a desynced or crashed one. Read it via `cc3501e_link_log_count()` /
`cc3501e_link_log_get()`, or `alp companion linklog`; the recovery callback also dumps it right
before printing its own recovery line.

The ring now survives the very recovery it exists to outlive:
`cc3501e_link_check_and_recover()`'s own up-to-24-PING probe used to overwrite the whole ring 3x
over before a bench operator ever saw it, evicting the original wedging op's entry in favour of
8 identical PING failures. The probe now suppresses ring writes for its own duration
(`ctx->link_log_suppress`) and counts its failures separately
(`cc3501e_link_log_probe_fail_count()`, surfaced in the recovery-notify dump) instead of evicting
anything. Each entry's `hdr_bytes` / `reply_hdr` are now zeroed and flagged invalid
(`CC3501E_LINK_LOG_HDR_BYTES_VALID` / `CC3501E_LINK_LOG_REPLY_HDR_VALID`) unless that phase's own
transceive actually returned `ALP_OK` — previously a bail could present a prior attempt's stale
`rx_scratch` residue as if it were this attempt's wire data. `cc3501e_link_log_count()` /
`_get()` now take the driver's request lock so a read can never observe a torn write, with
`cc3501e_link_log_fail_streak()` and `cc3501e_link_log_recover_streak()` (the streak as it stood
before the confirming PING that follows a warm reset resets it) added alongside for the same
reason. The never-reachable `CC3501E_LINK_LOG_PHASE_VERDICT` macro was removed rather than kept
as documented dead code.

### Fixed — `alp_i2s`/`alp_audio_out` stop/start/write returned `ALP_ERR_IO` forever after a TX underrun or RX overrun (#2137)

Once an I2S stream started and then went quiet for longer than its queued
audio, `alp_i2s_stop()`, `alp_i2s_start()`, and `alp_i2s_write()` all failed
`ALP_ERR_IO` (`-5`) until the process restarted — `alp_audio_out_*` sits on
top of `<alp/i2s.h>`, so the same gap broke `alp_audio_out_stop()` /
`alp_audio_out_start()` too. **Proven on silicon** (E1M-AEN803 serial 2026W36-0002): on the
previous image (pre-`#2137`), the U46 probe's `alp_audio_out_stop(I2S3)`
followed by `alp_audio_out_start(I2S3)` both returned `-5` on the same
sequence. On a build of the `#2137` fix (`2e92da60a`, merged into test
branch `273b34e76`, image md5 `41d4acff9e9d6aa73d65380395208dc6`), the SAME
sequence printed `alp_audio_out_stop(I2S3) [stop-control, amps still
ACTIVE] -> 0` then `alp_audio_out_start(I2S3) [restart ...] -> 0` --
`stop()` and `start()` each returned `0` on silicon. The bracketed text
is the probe's own fixed label, not a measurement: audibility was NOT
checked in that run, and the underrun precondition itself (the stream
actually reaching `I2S_STATE_ERROR` before that stop) was NOT observed
either -- nothing in the probe prints it. This data is measured on
`2e92da60a` specifically -- the rest of this fragment's content
was not re-run on silicon; the image's test branch (`273b34e76`) contains
`2e92da60a` only. The
`write()`-path recovery and the RX-side fix below are unit-tested only,
never run on this bench at any commit.

Root cause: the Alif DesignWare I2S driver follows Zephyr's own trigger
contract, and the backend never issued the ONE trigger that gets a stream
back out of it. When the TX queue runs dry while `RUNNING`, the TX IRQ
drops the stream into `I2S_STATE_ERROR`
(`zephyr/drivers/i2s/i2s_dw.c:743-769` ("tx_stream_park_keep_clock(stream, dev);"));
RX does the same on slab/queue exhaustion
(`zephyr/drivers/i2s/i2s_dw.c:875-911` ("stream->state = I2S_STATE_ERROR;")).
From `ERROR`: `DRAIN`/`STOP` need `RUNNING` and `-EIO`
(`zephyr/drivers/i2s/i2s_dw.c:465-501` ("stream->state != I2S_STATE_RUNNING")), `START` needs
`READY` and `-EIO`s too
(`zephyr/drivers/i2s/i2s_dw.c:443-463` ("stream->state != I2S_STATE_READY")), and TX
`i2s_write()` needs `RUNNING` or `READY` and `-EIO`s as well
(`zephyr/drivers/i2s/i2s_dw.c:578-599` ("dev_data->tx.state != I2S_STATE_READY")).
Zephyr's `enum i2s_trigger_cmd` (`include/zephyr/drivers/i2s.h`) gives
exactly two ways out: `I2S_TRIGGER_PREPARE`, valid ONLY from `ERROR`, which
moves to `READY` and drops the queue
(`zephyr/drivers/i2s/i2s_dw.c:496-503` ("stream->queue_drop(stream);")); and
`I2S_TRIGGER_DROP`, valid from any state but `NOT_READY`, which also moves
to `READY`
(`zephyr/drivers/i2s/i2s_dw.c:533-542` ("I2S_STATE_NOT_READY")). `src/backends/i2s/
zephyr_drv.c` used neither.

Fixed at the same shared layer #2132 already routes every `<alp/i2s.h>` and
`<alp/audio.h>` caller through — using only the documented Zephyr trigger
contract, never driver-private state:

- **`z_stop()`** falls back to `DROP` when `DRAIN` fails — covering both the
  pre-existing `#2132` "never really started" case and the new `#2137`
  "underran/overran into `ERROR`" case with one fallback in both
  directions, since `DRAIN` refuses both `READY` and `ERROR` for the
  identical reason (`state != RUNNING`). For TX, when the sidecar's
  `tx_started` already says the stream is not genuinely running, the
  doomed `DRAIN` attempt is skipped entirely rather than issued just to
  watch it fail — `i2s_dw`'s own `DRAIN` refusal logs its own `LOG_ERR`
  (`zephyr/drivers/i2s/i2s_dw.c:522` ("DRAIN trigger: invalid state")), so this also removes a log line on
  an already-known, already-handled path.
  The `DROP` fallback is gated on `h->started` for RX only, matching
  `z_close()`'s own gate — `DROP` tears down real RX clock hardware
  (`zephyr/drivers/i2s/i2s_dw.c:1437-1486` ("i2s_clock_disable(i2s);")), and must not run for an RX
  handle that was never started. A
  never-started RX handle returns `ALP_OK` in that case — NOT `DRAIN`'s own `-EIO`, which the finding-8 gate would
  otherwise have surfaced as a user-visible regression from the
  pre-`#2137` behaviour (an unconditional `DROP` that also returned
  `ALP_OK`): stopping something that was never started, or already
  stopped, is benign by the same convention the TX side already follows.
  Otherwise, either trigger succeeding marks the TX flags stopped and
  returns `ALP_OK`; both failing (or `DROP` being skipped for a genuinely
  never-started TX stream, or the RX case above) surfaces `DRAIN`'s own
  failure
  (`src/backends/i2s/zephyr_drv.c:634` ("rc = _errno_to_alp(i2s_trigger(dev, _to_dir(h->cfg.direction), I2S_TRIGGER_DRAIN));")).
  `alp_audio_out_stop()`'s `@return` now documents the both-refused
  `ALP_ERR_IO` case
  (`include/alp/audio.h:265` ("both the primary stop trigger and")).
- **`z_start()`** retries a real `START` that fails `ALP_ERR_IO` with one
  `PREPARE`-then-retry cycle, in both directions; a failed `PREPARE` leaves
  the ORIGINAL `START` error as the reported failure, not `PREPARE`'s own.
  Since `PREPARE` drops the ring (normally already empty for a TX
  underrun; it also frees any block that raced in, since
  `i2s_dw_write()` checks state separately from `queue_put()`,
  `zephyr/drivers/i2s/i2s_dw.c:590-622` ("queue_put(&dev_data->tx.mem_block_queue, mem_block, size);")), the
  retried `START` on TX correctly lands in the pre-existing `#2132`
  empty-queue deferral instead of failing again
  (`src/backends/i2s/zephyr_drv.c:505` ("if (rc == ALP_ERR_IO) {")). That
  deferral branch now also clears `tx_started` via a new
  `_mark_tx_needs_restart()` helper instead of leaving it stale (see the invariant paragraph below). A successful
  recovery logs one `LOG_WRN` — otherwise-silent evidence a `PREPARE`
  actually ran.
- **`z_write()`** (TX) retries an `i2s_write()` that fails `-EIO` with the
  same `PREPARE` shape, and retries the write ONCE REGARDLESS of whether
  its own `PREPARE` succeeded (finding 4): a CONCURRENT call (another
  writer's own `PREPARE`, or a `stop()`'s `DROP`) may already have taken
  the stream out of `ERROR` between this write's own trigger failing and
  its own `PREPARE` running, so a refused `PREPARE` here does not prove
  the stream is still stuck — only that it was not FROM `ERROR` at that
  exact instant. If the stream genuinely still is in `ERROR`, the retry
  just gets the same `-EIO` and falls into the existing free-and-report
  path, no new failure mode; previously this case gave up immediately and
  could drop a write a concurrent recovery would otherwise have accepted.
  The TX flag reset (via `_mark_tx_needs_restart()`) runs ONLY when THIS
  CALL's own `PREPARE` succeeded -- making it unconditional would assume that the ORIGINAL `i2s_write()`
  failing already proves `tx_started` stale regardless of what this
  `PREPARE` reports. That misses that a CONCURRENT call updates
  the very same flags under the very same lock as part of its own
  trigger, so by the time this call's own `PREPARE` observes a refusal,
  the flags already reflect whatever that concurrent call actually did —
  correctly. The race reproduces on real API interleavings
  (`fake_i2s_set_write_fail_hook()`, firing a genuine `alp_i2s_write()` /
  `alp_i2s_stop()` / `alp_i2s_start()` call from inside this fake's own
  `-EIO` return, the actual race window): a second writer whose `PREPARE`
  lost the race to a first writer's own recovery had the unconditional
  version clear the first writer's valid `tx_started` and queue its own
  retry, firing a spurious `START` on an ALREADY-RUNNING stream
  (`i2s_dw`'s real `-EIO`) and DROPping the first writer's still-good
  audio (`writerB=-5` observed); a writer whose `PREPARE` lost the race
  to a concurrent `stop()` had it re-arm a restart the caller never asked
  for, resuming playback without an explicit `start()`
  (`running_after_writer=1` observed on a stream the caller had just
  stopped). Reverted to the conditional reset; only the `LOG_WRN` was
  ever conditional on this call's own `PREPARE` succeeding, unchanged.
  The retry itself always runs, with the SAME slab block (never freed
  before the retry, never double-freed after it either way)
  (`src/backends/i2s/zephyr_drv.c:779` ("err = i2s_write(dev, slab_block, bytes);")).

**The RX-side leak:** the RX ISR's own
`I2S_STATE_ERROR` entry
(`zephyr/drivers/i2s/i2s_dw.c:875-911` ("stream->state = I2S_STATE_ERROR;")) orphaned
the just-filled block on EITHER of its two error exits — a failed
`k_mem_slab_alloc()` for the next block (`k_mem_slab_alloc()` sets `*mem =
NULL` on failure, so the just-filled block's own pointer, held only in a
local, was never freed), or a failed `queue_put()` of the one just filled
(the fresh block the alloc just returned replaces `stream->mem_block`,
so `rx_stream_disable()`'s own free — which only ever frees
`stream->mem_block` — never sees the orphaned one either). With the
2-block slab `src/backends/i2s/zephyr_drv.c` allocates, two overruns
exhausted it and the third `rx_stream_start()` returned `-ENOMEM`
permanently — RX has no NOMEM-as-stale-flag branch (that is TX-only).
Fixed at the actual source, `zephyr/drivers/i2s/i2s_dw.c`: both error
exits now `k_mem_slab_free()` the block they would otherwise have
orphaned, with an inline `alp-sdk issue #2137` note alongside the file's
existing ADR 0017 Tier-2 provenance header. No `zephyr_drv.c` change was
needed for this half of the fix — RX carries no sidecar flags to begin
with (`z_start()` never defers for RX).

**A second, pre-existing RX bug on the same recovery path:** `rx_stream_start()` never reset `mem_block_offset`,
which the ISR's own `alloc`-failure exit above leaves at the full block
size (set at `zephyr/drivers/i2s/i2s_dw.c:871` ("stream->mem_block_offset = offset;")),
right before that exit). `I2S_TRIGGER_PREPARE` doesn't touch it either
(`zephyr/drivers/i2s/i2s_dw.c:543-550` ("case I2S_TRIGGER_PREPARE:")).
So the first ISR firing after
ANY recovery inherited a stale "already full" offset on a block that was
never actually filled, computed zero frames to read, and queued it as a
"complete" frame anyway — stale/garbage sample data delivered silently on
literally the first frame after every recovery, not a leak or corruption,
but wrong data with no error returned anywhere. Fixed by resetting
`mem_block_offset` to `0` in `rx_stream_start()`
(`zephyr/drivers/i2s/i2s_dw.c:1225` ("stream->mem_block_offset = 0;")),
mirroring `tx_stream_start()`'s own
reset. The fake now mirrors the fixed driver's exact exit order too
(alloc the next block first, free the filled one on either error exit,
enter `I2S_STATE_ERROR` when its own ring is full) — see
`fake_i2s_rx_complete_block()`.

**The `tx_started` invariant:** the file
header's own `tx_started => !tx_pending_start` invariant broke on this
exact sequence: deferred `start()` → `write()` fires the real `START` →
underrun → `start()`: the real `START` `-EIO`s, `PREPARE` succeeds, the
retried `START` `-ENOMEM`s (the ring is empty again, per the `#2132`
empty-queue deferral) — the NOMEM branch cleared `tx_block_queued` and set
`tx_pending_start`, but left `tx_started` untouched at `true`. `tx_started`
had gone write-only after the original `#2137` fix (nothing read it), so
this went unnoticed until `z_stop()`'s new skip-`DRAIN` check above gave it
a reader again. Fixed by routing that branch through the new
`_mark_tx_needs_restart()` (`src/backends/i2s/zephyr_drv.c:478`
("static void _mark_tx_needs_restart(alp_z_i2s_side_t *s)")) instead of a
manual two-field assign; the invariant now holds via either that function
or `_mark_tx_stopped()` — the file header comment names both.

`include/alp/i2s.h`'s `alp_i2s_start()`/`alp_i2s_stop()`/`alp_i2s_write()` and
`include/alp/audio.h`'s `alp_audio_out_start()`/`alp_audio_out_stop()`/
`alp_audio_out_write()` document that an underrun/overrun is recovered
transparently — the caller does not need to detect or clear the condition
itself before calling any of them again.

Regression tests: `tests/unit/i2s_start_defer/` extends its fake I2S device
to enforce the same state machine — a new `fake_i2s_tx_simulate_underrun()`
(the deterministic, single-threaded stand-in for the real IRQ's "ring found
empty" transition, since native_sim has no interrupt timeline to reach it
asynchronously) drops the fake into `I2S_STATE_ERROR`, from which `START`/
`STOP`/`DRAIN`/write() all refuse exactly as real `i2s_dw` does, and only
`PREPARE`/`DROP` recover it. Covers: start, write, underrun, then stop
returns `ALP_OK`; underrun, then start (re-defers) plus write (fires the
real trigger) plays again; underrun, then write alone resumes playback with
no slab leak or double free (proven against the REAL `k_mem_slab`'s own
free-block count via a new `fake_i2s_slab_free_count()`, not just the fake's
bookkeeping); and PREPARE refused propagates the ORIGINAL error rather than
PREPARE's own, proven via a new `fake_i2s_prepare_call_count()` so the test
can't pass merely by coincidence on a backend with no recovery logic at all.

The tests add: `fake_i2s_rx_simulate_overrun()` / RX state modeling
(`fake_i2s_rx_running()`, `fake_i2s_rx_in_error()`,
`fake_i2s_rx_slab_free_count()`, `fake_i2s_rx_complete_block()`) and
`test_rx_overrun_recovers_no_slab_leak`, which runs three overrun-and-
recover cycles against the REAL RX `k_mem_slab`'s free-block count, then a
genuine completed-frame `read()` -- this does NOT prove the driver-level
leak fix itself: `zephyr/drivers/i2s/i2s_dw.c` is read-verified and
modelled by the fake (which mirrors the fixed driver's exact free-on-both-
error-exits behaviour), but is not compiled by any test in this suite (or
any other) -- native_sim has no DesignWare I2S hardware for it to target.
The test's own red proof reverted the FAKE's own model back to
the pre-fix (leaky) behaviour, not `i2s_dw.c`, to demonstrate the test
catches that class of bug at all;
`fake_i2s_drain_call_count()` and `test_underrun_start_retry_clears_
started_invariant`, which proves the `tx_started` invariant fix by
observing that `z_stop()` skips the real `DRAIN` trigger rather than
issuing a doomed one; `fake_i2s_force_write_fail()` and
`test_underrun_write_retry_fails_after_prepare_succeeds_no_leak`, which
proves a RETRY failure (distinct from the original underrun) surfaces as
itself with the block freed exactly once; `test_underrun_start_prepare_
refused_propagates_original_error`, the `start()`-side sibling of the
existing `write()` PREPARE-refused case; `fake_i2s_force_drop_fail()` and
`test_stop_both_drain_and_drop_refused_surfaces_drain_error`, which makes
`z_stop()`'s both-refused return path reachable in a test; and
`tests/unit/audio_out_start_defer`'s `test_mono_underrun_stop_start_write_
recovers`, proving the same recovery sequence composes correctly through
`<alp/audio.h>`, not just `<alp/i2s.h>` directly.

The concurrent-recovery race is exercised with `fake_i2s_set_write_fail_hook()`,
which fires a genuine `alp_i2s_*` call from inside `fake_i2s_write()`'s
own `-EIO` return — the actual unlocked race window `z_write()` has, no
knob required — and three tests built on it that DO discriminate:
`test_ilv_a_second_writer_after_concurrent_writer_recovery` (RED on
`4d50eb653`: `writerA=0 running_after_A=1 writerB=-5
running_after_B=0`; GREEN: `writerB=0 running_after_B=1`),
`test_ilv_b_writer_does_not_undo_concurrent_stop` (RED on `4d50eb653`:
`stop=0 running_after_stop=0 writer=0 running_after_writer=1`; GREEN:
`running_after_writer=0 start2=0 running_after_start2=1`), and
`test_ilv_d_writer_resumes_after_concurrent_start_recovery` (passes on
both -- additional coverage, not a discriminator for this specific bug).

### Fixed — aen-evk-demo no longer drives CC3501E GPIO_30 as I2S_EN on r1 modules (#2138)

`examples/aen/aen-evk-demo/src/cc3501e_gpio_routes.c` (`examples/aen/aen-evk-demo/src/cc3501e_gpio_routes.c:84`
("{ ALP_E1M_GPIO_IO8, 30u },")) is a hand-written, standalone route table --
this app has no `board.yaml`, so it never reaches
`scripts/gen_cc3501e_gpio_routes.py`'s per-revision generation the way
`aen-cc3501e-bringup`/`aen-cc3501e-gpio`/`aen-cc3501e-companion-tour` do. Its
`IO8 -> CC3501E GPIO_30` entry is correct only on **r2**
(`metadata/e1m_modules/E1M-AEN801.yaml`'s base `pad_routes`). On **r1**,
`metadata/e1m_modules/aen/hw-revisions.yaml:44`
(`e1m: E1M_GPIO_IO8,  dispatch: direct,`)
moves IO8 to a direct Alif GPIO and re-routes IO21 -- not IO8 -- onto
CC3501E GPIO_30 instead. On an E1M-EVK 2626-R2 carrier, that GPIO_30 net (the
SDIO mux SELECT) reaches `NetP18_2` through R198 and a fitted P18 jumper ties
it to +3V3, so phase 11's `AEN_EVKDEMO_SOUND_PLAYBACK=1` path -- which drives
"I2S_EN" LOW through GPIO_30 -- would short a CC3501E output against +3V3 on
an r1 module with P18 fitted. The default `AEN_EVKDEMO_SOUND_PLAYBACK 0` kept
default builds from hitting this.

The route table is not deleted or regenerated: this app is intentionally a
standalone Zephyr app with no `board.yaml` for the generator to resolve
against (see the table's own file header), and its IO8 entry is still the
correct one for the r2 hardware most of this phase's bring-up ran on. Instead,
phase 11 now refuses to drive the pin at all unless it can positively confirm
the live module's hw_rev, over a fresh `alp_hw_info_read()` (independent of
phase 5's own read, so this guard holds regardless of whether phase 5 ran or
passed)
(`examples/aen/aen-evk-demo/src/main.c:4198`
("/* --- 0. Refuse unless the live module is CONFIRMED hw_rev 2626-r2 -- */")).
A read failure, an unprovisioned/corrupt manifest, or any `hw_rev` string
other than exactly `"2626-r2"` all FAIL the phase before `ALP_E1M_GPIO_IO8`
is ever opened
(`examples/aen/aen-evk-demo/src/main.c:4231`
("refused: hw_rev != 2626-r2 (#2138)")) -- not just a
recognised r1, so an unprovisioned module or a future r3+ board fails safe
here too.

The decision lives out of `main.c` into
`examples/aen/aen-evk-demo/src/hw_rev_verdict.h`'s
`aen_evkdemo_hw_rev_confirms_io8_safe()` -- a pure function, same pattern as
`sound_verdict.h`/`amp_fault_verdict.h` in that directory -- so it is
unit-tested directly rather than trusted by inspection; `main.c` calls
`alp_hw_info_read()` (the SDK's own EEPROM-manifest surface, which already
validates magic + `schema_version` + CRC32 via
`alp_hw_info_classify_manifest()`) so the schema and CRC checks come from
that classifier rather than a hand-rolled `eeprom_24c128` read.
`examples/aen/aen-evk-demo/prj.conf` now sets
`CONFIG_ALP_SDK_HW_INFO_EEPROM_I2C_BUS_ID=0` (the SAME portable bus id --
`EVK_I2C_BUS_SENSORS`/`ALP_E1M_I2C0` -- phase 5's own `ctx->carrier_bus`
already reads this identical 0x50 manifest over, confirmed against
`metadata/e1m_modules/E1M-AEN801.yaml`'s `e1m_i2c0:` block) and
`CONFIG_ALP_SDK_HW_INFO_EEPROM_I2C_BITRATE_HZ=100000` (matching that same
bus's existing rate -- both opens reconfigure the one physical controller on
`open()`, so leaving them mismatched would reclock every other phase's
carrier-bus traffic to whichever ran most recently).
`tests/zephyr/chips/src/test_hw_rev_verdict.c` adds nine `native_sim` ZTEST
cases proving the header end to end through
`alp_hw_info_classify_manifest()`: r2 confirms, r1/blank-erased/bad-magic/
bad-schema/bad-CRC/a `"2626-r"` prefix all refuse, plus two cases that call
the verdict function directly (not through the classifier) -- an
unterminated, field-filling `"2626-r2X"` and a raw read-error status -- to
prove its own bound doesn't trust an unterminated buffer or a status the
classifier never actually returns for a real read failure.

The table's own "REVISION SCOPE" comment
(`examples/aen/aen-evk-demo/src/cc3501e_gpio_routes.c:39`
("* IO8 AND IO13 -- the I2S mux ENABLE and SELECT phase 11 drives -- are BOTH"))
is corrected to say IO8 is revision-scoped (and now guarded at runtime)
instead of claiming, as before, that the table "needs no per-revision
variant" and that the pinout's own `EVK_PIN_I2S_MUX_EN` / `Alif P7.1` prose
was simply stale -- that prose was right for r1, wrong for r2.

Every other `examples/**/cc3501e_gpio_routes.c` was audited for the same
hazard. `aen-sdcard-readout`'s hand-written table only routes IO20 (the SD
mux ENABLE), which `hw-revisions.yaml` does **not** move on any AEN
revision, so it carries no r1 hazard and is unchanged.
`aen-cc3501e-bringup`/`aen-cc3501e-gpio`/`aen-cc3501e-companion-tour` are all
generator-composed (`scripts/gen_cc3501e_gpio_routes.py`) so their route
tables ARE resolved per the revision each build's `board.yaml` declares --
but that resolution is per BUILD, not per module, so it alone would not have
caught the exact #2138 shape (a table built for one revision's hw_rev
running on a live module of a different one). Their real safety reason is
narrower and does not depend on that: none of the three ever calls
`alp_gpio_open()` on `ALP_E1M_GPIO_IO8`, `IO10`, or `IO21` -- the only pads
`hw-revisions.yaml` moves between chips -- in the first place.
`aen-cc3501e-bringup`'s `main.c` opens no GPIO proxy pad at all;
`aen-cc3501e-gpio` only opens `ALP_E1M_GPIO_IO13`
(`examples/aen/aen-cc3501e-gpio/src/main.c:217`
("the GPIO proxy backend (so a portable alp_gpio_open(ALP_E1M_GPIO_IO13)"));
`aen-cc3501e-companion-tour` only opens `ALP_E1M_GPIO_IO15`
(`examples/aen/aen-cc3501e-companion-tour/src/main.c:799`
("alp_gpio_t *io = alp_gpio_open(ALP_E1M_GPIO_IO15);")) -- neither pad is
revision-dependent. No hazard, no change.

`tests/scripts/test_aen_cc3501e_routes.py:716`
("def test_standalone_app_route_table_guards_revision_dependent_pads(path):")
adds a regression check: it reads every `e1m` pad
`hw-revisions.yaml`'s `pad_route_overrides` ever moves, and for any
standalone hand-written table that routes one of those pads, asserts the
app's `phase_sound()` guards it before opening it, via a per-pad checker
function looked up in `PAD_GUARD_CHECKERS`
(`tests/scripts/test_aen_cc3501e_routes.py:710`
("PAD_GUARD_CHECKERS = {")).

The check must do more than grep `main.c` for the guard function's NAME before the
`alp_gpio_open()` call, which would pass a `/* TODO: add the check here
*/` stub left in the guard's place, or the guard's own condition inverted
(`if (guard_ok)` instead of `if (!guard_ok)` -- refuses r2, drives the pin
on r1, the exact short this issue exists to prevent). It also must check that
the guard actually runs before the open, not just its text; mutants it rejects include: the guard wrapped in a dead `#if 0`, wrapped in a dead `if
(0) { ... }`, wrapped in a branch that does not dominate the open (`if
(ctx->carrier_bus == NULL) { ... }`), `&& (0)` appended to the condition
(swallowed by the old `[^{};]*` argument class), a dead `if (0) return
PHASE_FAIL;` as the block's last statement, `return PHASE_FAIL;` sitting
only inside a `printf()` string literal, and the guard called with
hardcoded, always-safe constant arguments (`ALP_OK, "2626-r2"`) instead of
the real `hwrev_rc`/`hwrev_info.som_hw_rev`.

`_check_phase_sound_io8_guard()`
(`tests/scripts/test_aen_cc3501e_routes.py:395`
("def _check_phase_sound_io8_guard(phase_sound_body: str) -> tuple[bool, str]:"))
closes all seven mutants: it strips comments AND string/char literals first (not
just comments, closing the string-literal case); requires the exact
`hwrev_rc = alp_hw_info_read(&hwrev_info);` and `if
(!aen_evkdemo_hw_rev_confirms_io8_safe(hwrev_rc, hwrev_info.som_hw_rev))
{` -- pinned to the real variable names, no extra operators -- each at
brace depth 1 (directly in `phase_sound()`, not nested in any further `{
}`); rejects any preprocessor conditional between the function's start and
the open other than the app's own known `#if AEN_EVKDEMO_SOUND_PLAYBACK`
wrapper; and finds the guard block's closing brace with a depth scan
(not a lazy "up to the first return-shaped substring" regex) so `return
PHASE_FAIL;` must be that block's own FINAL statement, not merely present
somewhere inside it.

A second, later, unguarded open -- e.g. a debug re-open added after the
properly guarded first one -- must not pass either. `_check_phase_sound_io8_guard()` uses
`re.finditer()` and rejects outright the moment more than one occurrence exists, even one
that looks textually dominated by the guard's `return PHASE_FAIL;` in
straight-line code -- proving that in general needs real control-flow
analysis, which this checker deliberately does not attempt (a stricter,
simpler rule than trying to prove dominance case by case). It also rejects any `goto` inside `phase_sound()` outright, for
the identical reason -- a `goto` jumping around the guard would defeat a
text-order/brace-depth checker undetected, and the real file has none.
`tests/scripts/test_aen_cc3501e_routes.py:694`
("def test_check_phase_sound_io8_guard_synthetic_cases(body, expected_ok):")
feeds this checker sixteen hand-built synthetic `phase_sound()` bodies --
the seven named mutants above, six more (a TODO stub, the inverted condition, the guard moved
after the open, the guard removed to an unrelated helper, IO8 opened
before the guard), the second-unguarded-open and goto cases, plus two
that must be ACCEPTED -- entirely independent of whatever `main.c`
currently contains, so this suite proves the CHECKER's own correctness
rather than just today's file.

Proven against real `main.c` mutations too, not just the synthetic
cases: reverting the guard to a bare TODO comment, and separately
inverting its condition, each reproduce a red failure; a
13-mutant script (`#if 0`, dead `if (0)`, the
non-dominating branch, moved-after-open, extracted-to-a-helper, `&& (0)`,
the dead conditional return, the string-literal-only return, the
constant-args call, opened-before-the-guard, the TODO stub, the inverted
condition, and a full swap for the real pre-#2138 `main.c` at `cf4fcb239`)
all reproduce red against this checker, with the real fixed file the only
`GREEN`. Restoring the real guard, or reverting any
synthetic mutant back to a passing case, brings the suite back to green
(33 passed, 1 skipped).

**`prj.conf` side effects**: `CONFIG_ALP_SDK_HW_INFO_EEPROM_I2C_BUS_ID=0`
is a single, image-wide Kconfig, not a phase-11-scoped one -- it also turns
on the boot banner's own EEPROM read (`alp_sdk_banner()`,
`src/zephyr/alp_banner.c`) and `alp_gpio_cc3501e_attach()`'s hw_rev read
(`src/backends/gpio/cc3501e_proxy.c`, phase 8, issue #1859's
`g_hw_rev_mismatch` guard). Both are harmless only because this app leaves
`CONFIG_ALP_SDK_SOM_HW_REV` at its default `""` -- a real mismatch there
would make the CC3501E GPIO proxy refuse EVERY proxied pad (including
phase 9's IO20 SD mux ENABLE, which is actually safe on both revisions),
and `CONFIG_ALP_SDK_HW_REV_MISMATCH_FATAL` would halt boot outright.
`examples/aen/aen-evk-demo/prj.conf` now documents both side effects and
that `ALP_SDK_SOM_HW_REV` must stay unset on this app; issue #2144 tracks
giving the CC3501E GPIO proxy its own PER-PIN guard so a real mismatch
there stops blocking pads (like IO20) that are actually safe.

### Fixed — `abi_snapshot.py --diff` reported a moved+value-changed symbol as `REMOVED` + `ADDED`, hiding the real change (#2139)

MOVED detection (`_diff()`'s REMOVED/ADDED pairing) required an identical content
hash between the disappearing and reappearing symbol, so a header split that also
changed the symbol's value — #2129's `evk_sdio_select_t` enumerator swap
(`EVK_SDIO_SDCARD` 1->0, `EVK_SDIO_M2E_KEY` 0->1) riding along with the
`alp_e1m_evk.h` -> `alp_e1m_evk_routes.h` split — read as a plain removal plus an
unrelated addition. The freeze gate in `.github/workflows/pr-generated-files.yml`
blocks on any `REMOVED` line, so the only way through was a false
`docs/abi/removed-symbols.json` entry claiming the typedef no longer exists, and
the enumerator swap itself never showed up anywhere a reviewer would see it.

`diff()` now prefers an exact-hash MOVED match as before, and falls back to a
value-may-differ match when the symbol name is **unambiguous** — exactly one
header lost it, exactly one header gained it, reachable via the same one-hop
`#include` graph MOVED already used. That reports `MOVED` plus an accompanying
`CHANGED` line
(`scripts/abi_snapshot.py:1225` ("CHANGED {r_cat[:-1]} {a_header}::{r_sym} (moved from {r_header})"))
with the same per-field/enumerator detail a same-header CHANGED already gets, or a
"content hash changed" fallback for a record schema with nothing more descriptive
than the hash
(`scripts/abi_snapshot.py:790` ("content hash changed")). Several headers losing or
gaining the same name at once is left alone rather than guessed at — it falls back
to the pre-fix REMOVED + ADDED behaviour
(`scripts/abi_snapshot.py:1198` ("value_changed = False")). The freeze gate's own
`^  REMOVED ` grep is unaffected: a true removal (no reachable candidate at all)
still reports a bare `REMOVED` and still fails the gate. `CHANGED` follows the
existing pre-1.0 policy already documented for a same-header value change — it
prints for review but does not trip the freeze gate, only `--diff`'s own exit code
(`docs/abi/README.md:154` (`(issue #2139) -- a consumer of the`)).

**Round 2 (review):** the unambiguous-name check above keyed only on
`(category, symbol)`, so a struct `alp_x_t` REMOVED from one header and an
unrelated ENUM (or fnptr) `alp_x_t` ADDED in a header the first still reaches
paired as a false MOVED + CHANGED — hiding a genuine removal from the freeze
gate. The pairing and its ambiguity counts now also key on the typedef's own
`kind` (struct/union/enum/opaque/fnptr/alias; `None` for every non-typedef
category, so functions/macros/variables are unaffected)
(`scripts/abi_snapshot.py:1215` ("and a_kind == r_kind")), refusing to pair
across a kind change even when the bare name is unambiguous.

Seven regression cases in `tests/scripts/test_abi_snapshot.py` total: moved+changed
reports MOVED + CHANGED, not REMOVED + ADDED
(`tests/scripts/test_abi_snapshot.py:531` ("def test_diff_reports_moved_and_changed_when_value_also_changed(tmp_path):")),
the concrete `evk_sdio_select_t` enumerator-swap shape reports the enumerator-level
detail, a genuine deletion still reports a bare REMOVED (existing
`test_diff_reports_genuine_deletion_as_removed`, unchanged), an ambiguous
same-name multi-header case falls back to plain REMOVED + ADDED for all of them
(`tests/scripts/test_abi_snapshot.py:618` ("def test_diff_falls_back_when_moved_name_is_ambiguous(tmp_path):")),
a struct-disappears/enum-appears same-name pair still reports REMOVED + ADDED
(`tests/scripts/test_abi_snapshot.py:649` ("def test_diff_reports_removed_added_when_typedef_kind_changes_across_headers(tmp_path):")),
the same for struct-to-fnptr
(`tests/scripts/test_abi_snapshot.py:681` ("def test_diff_reports_removed_added_when_struct_becomes_fnptr_across_headers(tmp_path):")),
and a same-kind (enum-to-enum) move with changed values still reports
MOVED + CHANGED, proving the `kind` check refuses a mismatch and nothing else
(`tests/scripts/test_abi_snapshot.py:708` ("def test_diff_reports_moved_and_changed_for_same_kind_enum_across_headers(tmp_path):")).

`docs/abi/removed-symbols.json` is untouched here — #2129 owns its `evk_sdio_select_t`
entry and drops it once this merges.

### Fixed — TAS2563 TDM clock fault is now armed, and a live TDM-detect readback is now available (#2140)

`TAS2563_FAULT_TDM_CLOCK` reads `INT_LTCH0[2]`
(`include/alp/chips/tas2563.h:346` ("TAS2563_FAULT_TDM_CLOCK")), but
`INT_MASK0`'s reset value `FCh` leaves that bit masked, and `INT_MASK`
gates the IRQZ / `AMP_FAULT` pin only -- not the latched readback
(SLASET3D §7.4.x p.35: "the IRQZ pin will assert low if the clock error
interrupt mask register bit is set low ... The clock fault is also
available for readback in the live or latched fault status registers
(INT_LIVE[2] and INT_LTCH[2])"). So `tas2563_read_faults()` could already
see a masked TDM clock fault before this change; what it could not do was
raise the pin, so a caller wired to `AMP_FAULT` rather than polling the
register directly never saw one. That the mask gates only the pin is measured, not inferred (#2182, E1M-AEN803
serial 2026W36-0002): with `INT_MASK0` at its POR `FCh`, an amp switched
`ACTIVE` with no I2S clock latched `INT_LTCH0[2]` while `AMP_FAULT` stayed
high; with bit 2 cleared, the same stimulus pulled the pin low within
10 ms. An earlier version of this entry reported the flag reading
`0x00000000` while playing at `cfeafd148`; that reading is withdrawn -- it
conflicts with the `0x80510004` fault word (TDM clock bit set) recorded
during the same investigation, and no surviving log reconciles the two.

`tas2563_configure_fault_pin()` now clears `INT_MASK0` bit 2 as part of
binding the fault pin
(`chips/tas2563/tas2563.c:647` ("reg_update(ctx, TAS2563_REG_INT_MASK0")),
citing the register address already modelled by the fake at
`tests/zephyr/chips/src/fake_tas2563.c:97` ("INT_MASK0   §7.5.28 p.77") and the
bit position already recorded in the driver header
