(`include/alp/chips/tas2563.h:776` ("INT_MASK0[2]"), pre-fix). Unmasking
`INT_MASK0[2]` is what routes the TDM clock fault to the IRQZ /
`AMP_FAULT` pin -- `tas2563_read_faults()` already saw the latch either
way -- so a caller that binds a fault pin now gets an edge on TDM clock
loss too, rather than silence, without having to know to write
`INT_MASK0` directly. `tas2563_read_faults()`'s doc comment
(`include/alp/chips/tas2563.h:880` ("@note `INT_MASK` gates the IRQZ / fault pin"))
now states that the mask governs the pin only, not the
latch, with the per-register POR mask values kept for reference:
over-temperature/over-current unmasked to the pin at reset (`INT_MASK0`),
VBAT brown-out/speaker open-short (`INT_MASK1`) and VBAT POR
(`INT_MASK2`), TDM clock error unmasked to the pin only once a fault pin
has been configured (#2140), and `INT_MASK3` (`FFh`) masked wholesale
from the pin with nothing in this driver unmasking it -- those bits still
latch and `tas2563_read_faults()` still reports them.

A new public accessor, `tas2563_read_tdm_detect()`
(`include/alp/chips/tas2563.h:975` ("tas2563_read_tdm_detect(tas2563_t *ctx, tas2563_tdm_detect_t *detect_out)"), implemented at
`chips/tas2563/tas2563.c:761` ("tas2563_read_tdm_detect(tas2563_t *ctx, tas2563_tdm_detect_t *detect_out)")), decodes the LIVE auto-rate detector at `DSP
Mode & TDM_DET` (register `0x11`, read-only, SLASET3D §7.5.19 Table 7-119,
p.73) into a `tas2563_tdm_detect_t` (`include/alp/chips/tas2563.h:387`): a
detected SBCLK:FSYNC ratio, a detected sample-rate pair, and a `clock_valid`
flag. This answers a different question from `TAS2563_FAULT_TDM_CLOCK`
above: that bit is a latched history of clock faults, gated on a fault pin
having been bound; this readback is unlatched, needs no fault pin, and
reflects what the auto-rate detection engine sees on the wire right now.
Register `0x11` resets to `7Fh` (`FS_RATIO=Fh` "Invalid ratio", `FS_RATE=7h`
"Error condition"), which the function decodes as `clock_valid == false`
with no special-casing needed. Table 7-119 -- the register's own field
description -- disagrees with §7.4.2 Table 7-23 "PCM Audio Sample Rates"
(p.40) and Table 7-24 "PCM SBCLK to FSYNC Ratio" (pp.40-41) at the edges of
both fields (Table 7-23 marks `FS_RATE` `000b`/`010b` Reserved where Table
7-119 gives them real rates; Table 7-24 marks `FS_RATIO` `0h`-`3h` Reserved
and `Fh` "Error Condition" where Table 7-119 decodes `00h`-`03h` as real
ratios and `0Fh` specifically as "Invalid ratio"); the decode follows Table
7-119 -- what the silicon reports back on this exact read -- and the field
macros' comment in `chips/tas2563/tas2563.c:89` names both tables rather
than picking one silently, the same discipline `samp_rate_code()` already
applies on the write side.

`examples/aen/aen-evk-demo`'s TAS2563 phase ("Phase 11", `src/main.c`) now
prints `tas2563_read_tdm_detect()` alongside `tas2563_read_faults()` at both
the fault baseline (`examples/aen/aen-evk-demo/src/main.c:4490` ("tas2563_read_tdm_detect(0x%02x) baseline")) and the post-teardown re-read
(`examples/aen/aen-evk-demo/src/main.c:4756` ("tas2563_read_tdm_detect(0x%02x) after")), rather than swapping the latch for the live read: the
latch answers "did a clock fault ever happen", the live read answers "what
is the clock doing right now", and the phase now reports both. The existing
`TAS2563_FAULT_SHUTDOWN_CAUSES` exclusion of `TAS2563_FAULT_TDM_CLOCK`
(`examples/aen/aen-evk-demo/src/main.c:4737` ("const uint32_t shutdown_fault_mask ="), #2146) is unchanged by this -- the live reading is
additional diagnostic output, not a new pass/fail gate.

### Documentation — refresh remaining stale CC3501E bridge firmware claims (#2141)

`docs/cc3501e-bridge.md`'s Versioning section still named SemVer 0.4.0 / wire
protocol 5 / stamp `0.4.0.0` as the current release, and only distinguished
two firmware states (merged vs. shipped). There are three: nine fixes merged
to `cc3501e-bridge-firmware:main`; **v0.9.0** (firmware PR #151), cut
carrying all nine but not yet bench-verified or published; and **v0.8.0**
(wire protocol 4.0, GPE `0.254.5.0`, `prebuilt/cc3501e-v0.8.0.bin`), what
`prebuilt/` actually publishes today and what every bench unit still runs,
carrying none of them. The doc now says so plainly.

`include/alp/chips/cc3501e/sockets.h`'s `cc3501e_sock_recv()` doc described a
zero-length result as always ambiguous ("no data, or the peer closed —
poll again"). That is only true against v0.8.0;
`cc3501e-bridge-firmware#140` (merged to `main`, cut into the unreleased
v0.9.0) makes EOF sticky on the worker path, so a zero-length result against
a `#140` bridge is unambiguous. The doc now covers both. `aen-cc3501e-
socket-throughput`'s `SOCKTP_ZERO_STREAK_DONE` host-side workaround for the
ambiguity stays in the code — v0.8.0 still needs it — with its comment
updated to say so and to note it is bench-validated 5 of 5 against a `#140`
build too, so it is correct against both firmware generations.

Most of the audit's other stale-claim candidates (the connect-budget/DHCP
family across the console and every `aen-cc3501e-*` example, the
"not-yet-merged" framing in `chips/cc3501e/cc3501e_sockets.c`) turned out to
already be correct on `dev`, fixed by #2111/#2113/#2115 — left untouched.

### Fixed — `alif_pdm.c`'s per-channel gain (`0x0D`) made E1M-EVK mic captures 31.9 dB quieter than the corrected default; no calibrated default exists yet (#2143)

A mid-capture register readback during a silicon session on E1M-AEN803 serial 2026W36-0002 found `CH0 GAIN=0x0000000D`. On `dev`, `examples/aen/aen-pdm-mic-alif` hardcoded `CH_GAIN 0x0000000D` and called `pdm_set_ch_gain()` directly from app code; this issue moves gain-setting into the driver itself, applied from a new DT `channel-gain` property by `pdm_apply_channel_defaults()` (`zephyr/drivers/audio/alif_pdm.c:608` ("pdm_set_ch_gain(dev, hw_ch, cfg->channel_gain);")). `PDM_CH_GAIN`'s `GAIN` field is bits `[11:0]`, unsigned 8.4 fixed-point, reset `0x10` = 1.0x (Alif SVD `AE822FA0E5597BS0_CM55_HP_View.svd`, `PDM_CH_GAIN` register, `GAIN` field: "Gain in unsigned 8.4 format"; matches the Alif DFP's `PDM_MAX_GAIN_CTRL 0xFFFU`, alif-dfp-ref drivers/include/pdm.h:99, not vendored in this tree) -- so `0x0D` = 0.8125x (-1.8 dB vs unity). That value is Alif's own register-level driver test value (`sdk-alif tests/drivers/pdm/src/alif_test_pdm.h:93` ("CH1_GAIN 0x0000000D"), and `sdk-alif samples/drivers/audio/dmic_alif/src/main.c:22`), never an audio-tuned one, and 31.9 dB below the corrected provisional default (`0x200`) below.

As evidence, a `0x800` (128x) gain run on E1M-AEN803 serial 2026W36-0002 (quiet room, no controlled stimulus) found `GAIN` read back `0x800` on every enabled channel as expected, every unclipped sample a multiple of `0x80` (the gain is a saturating multiply applied AFTER the datapath quantizes, so a coarser gain step moves only the clip point, never resolution), and the start-of-capture block plus the first window after every restart pinned at `+/-32767` (decimator settling reading as clipped, not a calibrated full-scale figure). Fixed with a **provisional default of `0x200`** (32x, +30.1 dB), added as a new DT-configurable `channel-gain` property on the `alif,alif-pdm` binding, default `0x200`, bounds documented and cross-referenced against the register's own hardware range. Full-scale headroom at `0x200` is UNMEASURED, and `0x200` does not bracket a documented "voice-tuned" BLE Audio range either: `ALIF_BLE_AUDIO_PDM_MICROPHONE_GAIN`'s Kconfig (`range 1 256`, left-shifted by 4 before writing this register) carries three DIFFERENT values in the same codebase, none described as tuned for anything -- `0x140` is its Kconfig DEFAULT (20), `0x320` is a DIFFERENT `#ifndef` fallback (50, `sdk-alif subsys/bluetooth/le_audio/audio_source_pdm.c`), and `sdk-alif samples/bluetooth/le_audio/unicast_initiator`'s `prj.conf` ships a THIRD value, 100 (`0x640`).

**`PDM_INIT`'s `BUILD_ASSERT` bounds `channel-gain` to `0x001..PDM_CH_GAIN_MAX`** -- the register's own 12-bit hardware range, not an arbitrary Kconfig-style range (`zephyr/drivers/audio/alif_pdm.c:1760` ("BUILD_ASSERT(DT_INST_PROP_OR(n, channel_gain, 0x200) >= 0x001 && \")): `PDM_CH_GAIN_MAX` (`0xFFF`, 4095) is the largest value the 12-bit `GAIN` field can hold -- a value above it truncates to bits `[11:0]` (`0x1000` exactly truncates to 0, muting the channel); the lower bound is `0x001`, since `0x000` is 0.0x, silently indistinguishable from a dead channel. A runtime write above the bound (from a caller-supplied value, not just DT) is independently clamped through `pdm_ch_gain_clamp()` rather than written unclamped -- see issue #2133's fragment for that fix and its host test. Phase (`0x1F`) and FIR (`pdm_default_fir_voice512`) are unchanged and match Alif's own audio-capture examples; the IIR coefficient (`0x4`) does too, but whether it filters at all depends on the board's `bypass_iir_filter` DT property -- every current overlay bypasses it. No example overlay sets a non-default `channel-gain`.

New host-testable coverage: none added specifically for the gain VALUE change itself -- the DT-to-`BUILD_ASSERT` wiring has no pure-function surface to extract (compile-time devicetree validation); a temporary `channel-gain = <0x0>;` and, separately, `<0x1000>;` on `examples/aen/aen-pdm-mic-alif`'s board overlay both failed the build with the expected `_Static_assert` message, and `<0xFFF>;` built clean -- all three overlay edits were then discarded. `pdm_apply_channel_defaults()`'s `cfg->channel_gain` read is a one-line change to an existing, already-covered call site. The clamp itself (`pdm_ch_gain_clamp()`) IS host-tested -- see issue #2133's fragment.

**Silicon evidence, E1M-AEN803 serial 2026W36-0002.** Mic liveness was NOT established by the `0x0D`/`0x800` data above -- both runs were register-level/quiet-room observations, neither a controlled acoustic test. What the `0x800` run DID establish: the datapath quantizes before the gain multiply, and the start/restart transient reads full-scale (decimator settling, not calibrated headroom evidence). A speaker-to-mic loopback -- the `PROBE_LOOPBACK` mode of `examples/aen/aen-i2s-tas2563-probe` on branch `test/u46-i2s-tas2563-on-reworked-mux` (commit `56631094d`), 2026-09-15 14:49Z -- separately confirms real, frequency-correct audio reaches mic ch0/ch1 (PDM controller 0) at 48 kHz with gain `0x200` (readback-confirmed): the 1 kHz Goertzel bin went from 9.3/0.1 dB in silence to 43.4/48.8 dB at volume 16 and 57.8/57.6 dB at volume 48; peak-to-peak (per channel, 960 ms window, after `zephyr_drv.c`'s `dc_block_s16()` high-pass, hence not a multiple of 32) went from 128/128 in silence to 266/292 at 1 kHz/volume 16 and 651/652 at 1 kHz/volume 48. The D2 pair (HW 4/5) is register-level verified only, never acoustically tested. **What is STILL unmeasured: full-scale headroom at `0x200`** -- the loopback used a fixed speaker level, not a calibration sweep; see issue #2133's fragment for the full loopback account.

### Fixed — CC3501E GPIO proxy: per-pin, fail-closed revision guard (#2144)

`src/backends/gpio/cc3501e_proxy.c:305` ("static bool is_rev_dependent")
replaces the old all-or-nothing `g_hw_rev_mismatch` guard (#1859) with a
PER-PIN check at `src/backends/gpio/cc3501e_proxy.c:357` ("is_rev_dependent(pin_id) && !g_hw_rev_confirmed_match"), refusing only the E1M pins that `metadata/e1m_modules/aen/hw-revisions.yaml:44-46` ("E1M_GPIO_IO") move between the Alif SoC and the CC3501E across AEN hw_revs -- IO8 (:44), IO10 (:45) and IO21 (:46) -- instead of dropping every proxied pin, including revision-independent ones like IO20 (the SD mux enable), on any hw_rev disagreement.

It also fails CLOSED: `src/backends/gpio/cc3501e_proxy.c:129` ("static bool g_hw_rev_confirmed_match") defaults false, and `src/backends/gpio/cc3501e_proxy.c:146` ("cc3501e_proxy_hw_rev_confirmed_match") only reports a match past a CRC-valid `alp_hw_info_read()` AND a `CONFIG_ALP_SDK_SOM_HW_REV` compare -- a missing, unprovisioned or corrupt identity-EEPROM manifest now refuses a revision-dependent pin instead of the old guard's fail-open default. `alp_gpio_cc3501e_attach()` logs a one-shot `LOG_WRN_ONCE` naming the read status, the live manifest `som_hw_rev` (when read), and the build's `CONFIG_ALP_SDK_SOM_HW_REV` when it cannot confirm a match; `px_open()` separately logs a one-shot-per-pin `LOG_WRN` naming the #2144 guard specifically, since it returns the SAME `ALP_ERR_NOSUPPORT` as the unrelated #1854 unrouted-pad guard.

The revision-dependent pin set is derived from metadata, not hand-typed: `scripts/gen_cc3501e_gpio_routes.py:126` ("def _revision_dependent_e1m_pads") reads `metadata/e1m_modules/aen/hw-revisions.yaml`'s `pad_route_overrides:` and, unlike an earlier draft of this change, writes it ONCE into an SDK-owned generated file, `src/backends/gpio/cc3501e_rev_dependent_pins.c`, compiled whenever `src/backends/gpio/cc3501e_proxy.c` itself is (`zephyr/CMakeLists.txt`) -- not duplicated into every AEN example's `cc3501e_gpio_routes.c` the way `cc3501e_gpio_routes[]`/`cc3501e_gpio_unrouted[]` correctly are (this list is identical on every AEN board regardless of hw_rev or carrier, so a per-app copy was the exact triplication issue #1859 already removed once for `cc3501e_gpio_routes[]` itself). `tests/scripts/test_gen_cc3501e_gpio_routes.py` imports `scripts/gen_cc3501e_gpio_routes.py:148` ("REVISION_DEPENDENT_E1M_PADS") rather than recomputing it, so generator and test can never disagree.

`examples/aen/aen-evk-demo/prj.conf:81` ("CONFIG_ALP_SDK_HW_INFO_EEPROM_I2C_BUS_ID=0") and `examples/aen/aen-evk-demo/prj.conf:93` ("CONFIG_ALP_SDK_HW_INFO_EEPROM_I2C_BITRATE_HZ=100000") now configure that standalone app (previously built with the EEPROM bus disabled and no recorded hw_rev, per the issue) to read the identity manifest over the same bus phase 5 already reads it from, at the same 100 kHz phase 8's `ctx.carrier_bus` open already uses -- the Kconfig's 400 kHz default would otherwise leave that shared controller reconfigured to 400 kHz for the rest of the app's lifetime (`.close = NULL`; nothing restores it), which is not bench-validated on this bus. This lets phase 11's `alp_gpio_open(ALP_E1M_GPIO_IO8)` be confirmed instead of refused -- provided the running module carries a CRC-valid manifest reporting `hw_rev` `"2626-r2"`. Phase 11 itself stays compiled OUT by default (`AEN_EVKDEMO_SOUND_PLAYBACK 0`, `examples/aen/aen-evk-demo/src/main.c:3813` ("#define AEN_EVKDEMO_SOUND_PLAYBACK 0")), and this change has NOT been run on the bench -- the manifest-confirms-IO8 path is a design claim, not a silicon-verified one. A factory-fresh or unprovisioned module still fails closed.

`examples/aen/aen-evk-demo/src/main.c:4241` ("mux_en_open_err") captures `alp_last_error()` immediately after IO8's `alp_gpio_open()`, before any later call can overwrite it; the phase 11 failure message at `examples/aen/aen-evk-demo/src/main.c:4265` ("mux not drivable -- IO8's #2144 revision") now names the #2144 revision guard specifically when `mux_en_open_err == ALP_ERR_NOSUPPORT`, instead of blaming phase 8's bridge attach or the build for every mux-not-drivable case.

New host coverage: `tests/unit/gpio_cc3501e_rev_guard` (native_sim ztest) proves `cc3501e_proxy_hw_rev_confirmed_match()` against a matching, mismatched, corrupt (`ALP_ERR_IO`) and missing (`ALP_ERR_NOT_PROVISIONED`/`ALP_ERR_NOSUPPORT`) manifest, both with hand-set inputs and -- `tests/unit/gpio_cc3501e_rev_guard/src/test_gpio_cc3501e_rev_guard.c:191` ("test_classify_bad_crc_does_not_confirm") and `:206` ("test_classify_blank_eeprom_does_not_confirm") -- with CRC-valid/CRC-corrupt/blank `alp_hw_info_eeprom_t` buffers routed through the real `alp_hw_info_classify_manifest()`. It proves `px_open()`'s gate itself is wired in: a revision-dependent pin (`:234`, "test_rev_dependent_pin_refused_when_not_confirmed") refuses with `ALP_ERR_NOSUPPORT` unless confirmed, while a revision-independent pin (`:257`, "test_revision_independent_pin_opens_regardless") always opens. `:277` ("test_attach_resets_stale_forced_true_on_read_failure") closes the gap a dev-review mutation found: forcing the cached decision `true` via the test hook, then calling the REAL `alp_gpio_cc3501e_attach()` (not the hook), proves attach() re-derives the decision from a real (and, on native_sim, failing) `alp_hw_info_read()` rather than leaving a stale forced value standing -- the earlier test suite never called `attach()` itself, so a mutation hardcoding `g_hw_rev_confirmed_match = true;` inside it passed all 8 prior tests unnoticed.

A second review round found the mirror gap: no test observed attach() PRODUCE a confirmed match, so a mutant hardcoding `g_hw_rev_confirmed_match = false;` in `alp_gpio_cc3501e_attach()` (`src/backends/gpio/cc3501e_proxy.c:216`) passed all 13 tests unnoticed. `tests/unit/gpio_cc3501e_rev_guard/src/test_gpio_cc3501e_rev_guard.c:320` ("test_attach_confirms_match_from_injected_manifest") closes it with a new `CONFIG_ZTEST`-only seam, `cc3501e_proxy_test_inject_hw_info_read()` (`src/backends/gpio/cc3501e_proxy_internal.h`, `src/backends/gpio/cc3501e_proxy.c:175`): it arms a one-shot canned `alp_hw_info_read()` result for the next `attach()` call, so attach()'s real body -- not the pre-existing force hook -- derives and assigns the cached decision, and a confirmed IO8 opens. Chosen over an I2C EEPROM emulator (native_sim has no devicetree I2C0 node backing `CONFIG_ALP_SDK_HW_INFO_EEPROM_I2C_BUS_ID` in this test build, and wiring a real 24C128-protocol emulator is a materially larger diff) and hand-verified red against the exact mutant above before being restored. A third hook, `cc3501e_proxy_test_reset_bridge_ctx()`, resets the cached bridge-context pointer to NULL after each test that stands up the never-dereferenced sentinel `(cc3501e_t *)(uintptr_t)1`, so it cannot outlive its test and be dereferenced by a later one.

### Fixed — TAS2563 amps stayed silent after an I2S restart following clock loss (#2146)

The TAS2563 amps (`0x4d`/`0x4e`) put themselves into software shutdown on
their own -- bench-measured within roughly 100 ms of their TDM/I2S bit clock
stopping, not the ~1 s an earlier pass of this note claimed (see the
register-level bench evidence below) -- and nothing in the audio stack
re-armed them afterwards
(`TAS2563_FAULT_SHUTDOWN_CAUSES`, `include/alp/chips/tas2563.h:376`
("#define TAS2563_FAULT_SHUTDOWN_CAUSES"), citing SLASET3D §7.3.12). The
clock stops on every I2S stop path and on an underrun
(`zephyr/drivers/i2s/i2s_dw.c`'s `tx_stream_disable()`
calls `i2s_clock_disable()`; keeping the clock running across an underrun
instead is tracked separately in #2149), and every in-tree caller set the
amps ACTIVE right after `alp_audio_out_start()` -- since #2132, a
`z_start()` with nothing queued only arms a pending start, so the real
START (and the bit clock with it) does not fire until the first write,
which also explains why
`INT_LTCH0` bit 2 (TDM clock error) was observed latched at the *start* of
playback, not only after a stop/restart.

Added `tas2563_resume()` (`chips/tas2563/tas2563.c`,
`include/alp/chips/tas2563.h:1060` ("alp_status_t tas2563_resume")): clears
the latched faults via the existing self-clearing `CLR_INTP_LTCH` bit
(`INT & CLK CFG`, 0x30 bit 2 -- the same mechanism `tas2563_clear_faults()`
already used), then switches `PWR_CTL.MODE` to ACTIVE, in that order --
clearing after ACTIVE would leave a shutdown-causing latch standing.
Precondition: the caller must not call it until after the first successful
`alp_audio_out_write()` following a start or restart, since that write is
what confirms the bit clock is actually running again.

`examples/aen/aen-evk-demo/src/main.c`'s sound phase now checks that
priming write's own return before doing anything else
(`examples/aen/aen-evk-demo/src/main.c:4633` ("silence_rc = alp_audio_out_write")):
on failure it prints the rc, skips `tas2563_resume()` entirely -- leaving
the amps in the shutdown `tas2563_init()` already left them in, rather than
forcing `MODE = ACTIVE` with no confirmed clock, which would reproduce the
exact defect this fix removes -- and fails the phase through its existing
playback-on verdict check
(`examples/aen/aen-evk-demo/src/main.c:4840` ("if (silence_rc != ALP_OK)")).
On success it calls `tas2563_resume()` instead of the old
`tas2563_set_mode(ACTIVE)`; the stale "a quiet stream is already running"
comment, false since #2132, is corrected. The phase's playback-on verdict
also now fails when `resumed_amps != ok_amps`
(`examples/aen/aen-evk-demo/src/main.c:4845` ("if (resumed_amps != ok_amps)")),
so one amp's failed resume no longer PASSes on the strength of the other
amp's PDM-correlated signal. The post-playback fault re-read no longer fails on
`TAS2563_FAULT_TDM_CLOCK`
(`examples/aen/aen-evk-demo/src/main.c:4737-4738` ("shutdown_fault_mask")),
since the bit alone cannot tell a real shutdown apart from a latch that left
`PWR_CTL` at MODE ACTIVE. `include/alp/audio.h`'s
`alp_audio_out_stop()` doc gained an `@note` ordering contract: mute any
external amplifier before calling `alp_audio_out_stop()`, since what
happens to an amp still ACTIVE when the I2S clock stops is chip-specific --
re-arming it afterward is likewise chip-specific (e.g. `tas2563_resume()`),
and that mechanism and the audible thump it produced stay documented on
`tas2563_resume()` (`include/alp/chips/tas2563.h`) rather than duplicated in
`audio.h`. The note's underrun clause -- the clock also stops on an
underrun, not only a deliberate stop -- is scoped to the Zephyr DesignWare
I2S backend (`zephyr/drivers/i2s/i2s_dw.c`); #2149 tracks keeping the clock
running across an underrun instead.

**Dependency: this evk-demo change does not run yet on `dev`.**
`alp_audio_out_start()` on current `dev` fails `-ENOMEM` on an empty TX ring
(`i2s_dw.c`'s `tx_stream_start()` -> `queue_get()`) -- #2132's deferred-start
change, which is what makes "write, then resume" possible at all, has not
landed there yet. Until #2132 merges, `phase_sound()`'s entire
`if (spk != NULL && spk_rc == ALP_OK)` block, including the priming write
and `tas2563_resume()` call above, never executes on a `dev`-only checkout.

**Verification: register-level and audible PASS on E1M-AEN803 serial 2026W36-0002.**
Bench run 2026-09-15 14:58Z, PROBE_RESUME image built from this branch at
`e3fde8705`, both amps, `PWR_CTL`/`INT_LTCH0` read back over I2C:

- Write one block, then `tas2563_resume()`: `PWR_CTL` `0x0c/0x0c`
  (MODE ACTIVE on both amps), `INT_LTCH0` `0x00` immediately after resume.
- After `alp_audio_out_stop()`: `0x0c` at +0 ms, already `0x0e/0x0e` (MODE
  SHUTDOWN on both amps) by the +100 ms poll, and still `0x0e` at +3000 ms --
  the amps shut down within roughly 100 ms of the clock stopping, not the
  ~1 s an earlier pass of this note and of `tas2563_resume()`'s own doc
  claimed (both corrected alongside this fragment).
- Restart WITHOUT calling `tas2563_resume()`: stays `0x0e/0x0e` -- the bug
  this issue reports is reproduced at the register level.
- `tas2563_resume()` called after restart: `0x0c/0x0c` at every checkpoint
  taken -- the fix is confirmed at the register level.
- Gaps of 200 / 500 / 1500 ms between stop and restart, with no
  `tas2563_resume()` call, all ended at `0x0e` -- **no self-heal was observed
  at any tested gap**, so a caller cannot rely on waiting the shutdown out.
- Zero I2C write failures and no faults reported during the run.
- **Open, not diagnosed:** `INT_LTCH0` bit 2 (TDM clock error), `INT_LTCH3`
  bit 6 (boost clock error) and `INT_LTCH4` bit 7 (device power-down event)
  were observed re-latching *during* playback while `PWR_CTL` stayed `0x0c`
  (MODE ACTIVE, not shut down) -- cause not yet diagnosed.

**Audible confirmation.** Attended bench run 2026-09-15 15:20Z on
E1M-AEN803 serial 2026W36-0002, test branch `test/u46-i2s-tas2563-on-reworked-mux` at
`094570cc4` carrying this branch at `bf77cb961` and #2132/#2137 at
`36bc7f03a` (PROBE_RESUME2, RAM load, no MRAM write):

- Tones 1 and 3 each followed `tas2563_resume()` after a successful write,
  with `PWR_CTL` reading `0x0c/0x0c` beforehand: the on-board PDM mics
  measured 1000 Hz at 63.9 dB and 63.4 dB above the in-band median, and
  the maintainer heard both as beeps.
- Tone 2 (restart, no resume) and tones 4-6 (stop, then a 200/500/1500 ms
  gap, then start, no resume) read `0x0e/0x0e`: the mics saw only noise
  and the maintainer heard silence -- exactly the 2 beeps out of 6 tones
  the register readings predict.
- **Thump.** In three trials where the probe called `tas2563_resume()`
  and then stopped the stream within milliseconds, with no further
  writes, the maintainer heard three "kicks". This evidence
  does not separate a power-up pop from a shutdown-on-clock-loss
  transient, so it does not say which one caused it -- see the ordering
  contract on `tas2563_resume()`
  (`include/alp/chips/tas2563.h:1026-1034` ("@par Ordering contract"))
  and on `alp_audio_out_stop()`
  (`include/alp/audio.h:268-278` ("@note Ordering contract")).

**Known gap this fix does not close.** `tas2563_resume()` only helps a
caller that actually calls it after a restart. A caller who never learns
that an underrun happened -- once #2137 lands, the playback stack will
recover I2S from an underrun transparently; #2137 is still open and
unmerged -- has no trigger to call it at all, and the "no self-heal
observed" result above means the amp will not recover on its own either.
The TAS2563's own clock-error auto-recovery behaviour, if the part offers
one (see this issue's original "Expected" section), remains untested.

### Fixed — mid-playback I2S underrun stopped the TAS2563 bit clock and left the amps in SHUTDOWN while `alp_audio_out_write()` kept returning `ALP_OK` (#2149)

**Measured** on E1M-AEN803 serial 2026W36-0002 (`alif:ensemble:e8` M55-HE, bench
test branch `test/u46-i2s-tas2563-on-reworked-mux` @ `094570cc4`, dev plus the
unmerged #2132/#2137 @ `36bc7f03a`, #2146 @ `bf77cb961`, and #2133): a
`aen-i2s-tas2563-probe` run wrote a continuous 1 kHz tone (16 kHz, S16
stereo, 256 frames/block, volume 128) on I2S3, then stopped calling
`alp_audio_out_write()` for a gap the log timestamps at ~4.6 s (`TONE 1/6 ON`
`15:20:23.769199Z` to `TONE 1 mic peak` `15:20:29.164074Z` = 5.395 s, minus
the ~800 ms 50-block tone-plus-mic-measure window itself = ~4.6 s) without
ever calling `alp_audio_out_stop()`. Across that gap both TAS2563 amps
(`0x4d`, `0x4e`) went `PWR_CTL` (`0x02`) `0x0c` → `0x0e` (MODE `00b` ACTIVE →
MODE `10b` SHUTDOWN) with `INT_LTCH0=0x04` (TDM_CLOCK) latched; `INT_LTCH4`
(power-down) is corroborated from run D of the same bench session:
`INT_LTCH4` `0x00` at `15:20:57.539884Z` → `0x80` at `15:21:03.146125Z`,
alongside `INT_LTCH3` `0x11` → `0x51` — bit 3 (`DC_DETECT`, `0x08`) is clear
in both reads, the bench baseline for the SDO-idle precondition noted below
(run A's own `INT_LTCH4=0x80/0x80` read at "after resume",
`15:20:23.766088Z`, was already latched on both sides and is not cited
here), while every subsequent `alp_audio_out_write()` kept
returning `ALP_OK` (0 write failures the whole run) and the PDM mics went
from measuring the tone at 1000 Hz, 63.9 dB above the in-band median, to
noise-floor at that frequency after the gap, with no self-heal observed
within ~1.2 s of continuous post-gap writes.

**Inferred mechanism**, confirmed by code reading at that base: when the TX
queue empties mid-playback, `i2s_tx_irq_handler()` moves the stream to
`I2S_STATE_ERROR`
(`zephyr/drivers/i2s/i2s_dw.c:651` ("stream->state = I2S_STATE_ERROR;")) and
fell into `tx_stream_disable()`, which ended in `i2s_clock_disable()` —
clearing `CER.CLKEN` and stopping the master SCLK/WS generator entirely.
TAS2563 reads that bit-clock loss as its own cue to latch software SHUTDOWN
(`TDM_CLOCK`/`INT_LTCH0` bit 2). Issue #2137's transparent ERROR recovery —
a retried `i2s_write()` after its own `I2S_TRIGGER_PREPARE`
(`src/backends/i2s/zephyr_drv.c:707` ("err == -EIO && h->cfg.direction == ALP_I2S_DIR_TX")), then a deferred `_start_trigger()` once a block is
genuinely queued
(`src/backends/i2s/zephyr_drv.c:798` ("alp_status_t start_rc = _start_trigger(dev, h->cfg.direction);")) — re-enables the clock and
resumes the I2S stream, but nothing in that path re-arms the amp, so
playback resumes silently muted.

**Fixed** at the ISR underrun exit only, the narrow form: the queue-empty
branch that sets `I2S_STATE_ERROR`
(`zephyr/drivers/i2s/i2s_dw.c:767` ("tx_stream_park_keep_clock(stream, dev);")) now calls
`tx_stream_disable_ex(stream, dev, /*keep_clock=*/true)` instead of the
plain `tx_stream_disable()`
(`zephyr/drivers/i2s/i2s_dw.c:653` ("tx_stream_disable_ex(stream, dev, true);")), which still disables the TX channel/block/interrupt and
still sets `I2S_STATE_ERROR` exactly as before — it only skips the final
`i2s_clock_disable()`
(`zephyr/drivers/i2s/i2s_dw.c:1514-1525` ("if (!keep_clock) {")). Every other
teardown path keeps gating the clock unconditionally: STOP/DRAIN/DROP
(`i2s_dw_trigger()`) all route through the `stream->stream_disable` function
pointer, wired to the `tx_stream_disable()` wrapper
(`zephyr/drivers/i2s/i2s_dw.c:1533-1536` ("static void tx_stream_disable(struct stream *stream, const struct device *dev)")),
itself wired as `.stream_disable = tx_stream_disable` in the
`i2s_dw_data_##index` initializer
(`zephyr/drivers/i2s/i2s_dw.c:1716-1718` ("static struct i2s_dw_data i2s_dw_data_##index")),
which always calls `tx_stream_disable_ex()` with `keep_clock=false` — and
the ISR's own already-`I2S_STATE_ERROR` and `last_block` exits call the
same shared body directly with `keep_clock=false` too, so PM suspend's
`i2s_disable_controller()` remains the only other TX-side path (unchanged)
that clears `CER.CLKEN` directly — `rx_stream_disable()` also clears it, on
the RX side. `I2S_TRIGGER_PREPARE` is the only trigger valid
from `I2S_STATE_ERROR`
(`zephyr/drivers/i2s/i2s_dw.c:545-552` ("PREPARE trigger: invalid state"))
and moves straight to `I2S_STATE_READY` without touching the clock at all —
so a recovering stream keeps the clock alive exactly through the #2137
recovery window, unchanged in shape. `I2S_TRIGGER_DROP` is the other
trigger `i2s_dw_trigger()` accepts from `I2S_STATE_ERROR` (`STOP`/`DRAIN`
both require `I2S_STATE_RUNNING` and refuse `ERROR`, so those two are not
reachable from it at all) and calls the SAME `tx_stream_disable()` wrapper
with `keep_clock=false` via the `stream->stream_disable` function pointer,
so an abandoned errored stream still has its clock gated, not left running
forever.

**Clock state after every `I2S_STATE_ERROR` exit:**
- `I2S_TRIGGER_PREPARE` (ERROR → READY): clock **stays on** (unchanged by
  this fix; `tx_stream_disable()`/`_ex()` is never called on this path).
- `I2S_TRIGGER_DROP` (ERROR → READY, abandon): clock **gated off**, same
  as before this fix.
- `I2S_TRIGGER_STOP` / `I2S_TRIGGER_DRAIN` from ERROR: not reachable — both
  require `I2S_STATE_RUNNING` and refuse otherwise; no change.
- A second ISR entry while already `I2S_STATE_ERROR`
  (`zephyr/drivers/i2s/i2s_dw.c:670-674` ("Stop transmission if there was an error")),
  or the `last_block` exit
  (`zephyr/drivers/i2s/i2s_dw.c:676-680` ("Stop transmission if we were requested")):
  both still call the shared body with `keep_clock=false` — clock gated
  off, same as before this fix.

**Restart-glitch guard.** `tx_stream_start()` re-runs
`clock_control_set_rate()` and writes `CCR` (`i2s_configure_clock()`, whose
own doc comment says it "Should be called with Clock disabled" —
`zephyr/drivers/i2s/i2s_dw.h:441-446` ("Should be called with Clock disabled.")).
Note that `CER.CLKEN` has been `1` from `i2s_dw_initialize()` onward (it
calls `i2s_enable_controller()`, which calls `i2s_clock_enable()`), so in
practice CCR has always been written with the clock already live, on every
first start since boot — not only on a restart following the keep-clock
underrun path. What actually changes here is narrower: **skip**
`clock_control_set_rate()`/`i2s_configure_clock()` specifically to avoid
RE-touching the divider during underrun recovery, since re-deriving the
same divider gains nothing and a live CCR rewrite is not something to do
without silicon proof it's glitch-free.

Round 1 of this fix tracked that via a remembered sample rate
(`clk_frame_freq_configured`) compared against the stream's current
`cfg.frame_clk_freq`. **Round-2 review finding 1:** that cache was never
invalidated on `rx_stream_start()` (which reprograms the SAME shared
divider unconditionally), `rx_stream_disable()`, `i2s_suspend()`,
`i2s_resume()`, or a `tx_stream_disable_ex()` teardown that actually gates
the clock — so a TX restart could find `CER.CLKEN` set by an unrelated
RX/PM transition and wrongly skip reprogramming onto a divider that was
never actually programmed for its own rate. Fixed by replacing the cache
with a one-shot flag, `clk_restart_skip_ok`
(`zephyr/drivers/i2s/i2s_dw.c:238-252` ("bool      clk_restart_skip_ok;")):
set ONLY by the ISR's keep-clock underrun exit
(`zephyr/drivers/i2s/i2s_dw.c:652` ("stream->clk_restart_skip_ok = true;")),
consulted and unconditionally cleared by `tx_stream_start()`
(`zephyr/drivers/i2s/i2s_dw.c:1387-1391` ("clk_needs_reprogram = !stream->clk_restart_skip_ok")),
and also cleared by every other path that can invalidate it before that
restart happens: `rx_stream_start()`, `rx_stream_disable()`,
`tx_stream_disable_ex()` when `!keep_clock`, `i2s_suspend()`, `i2s_resume()`,
and `i2s_dw_configure()` when the TX rate actually changes. Paired with the
existing `i2s_clock_is_enabled()` helper
(`zephyr/drivers/i2s/i2s_dw.h:436-439` ("__STATIC_INLINE bool i2s_clock_is_enabled")).
`i2s->cfg.wss_len`/`sclkg` (CCR's other inputs) are fixed device-config
constants no `i2s_dw_configure()` call ever changes, so the flag being set
already implies `frame_clk_freq` is unchanged; a rate change between
PREPARE and this START (not exercised by the #2137 recovery flow) clears
the flag and reprograms normally.
**BENCH-VERIFY:** confirm no BCLK/WS glitch on the restart path that DOES
still reprogram.

**Known remaining gap, NOT fixed here:** `rx_stream_start()` reprograms
`clock_control_set_rate()`/CCR unconditionally on every RX start, including
while the shared clock may already be running (e.g. a TX stream left it on
via this fix's own keep-clock underrun exit), and `rx_stream_disable()`
still unconditionally clears `CER.CLKEN` on every RX overrun
(`zephyr/drivers/i2s/i2s_dw.c:1475` ("i2s_clock_disable(i2s);")) —
either one on a controller sharing this clock with an active TX stream
would reprogram or kill the TX bit clock out from under it. This driver is
half-duplex in practice (`dev_data->dir` is a single field, not
per-direction state), which narrows but does not eliminate the exposure,
since the two directions can still be reconfigured back to back on the same
physical clock. Refs #2150 (tracking issue already filed); out of scope for
this fix.

**Not yet verified on silicon** that this restores audio. `i2s_dw.c` is not
compiled by either default example build (`aen-evk-demo`, `aen-i2s-amp-alif`
build with I2S3 disabled by default) — the actual compile evidence is the
`-DEXTRA_DTC_OVERLAY_FILE=i2s3-enable-post-u46-rework.overlay` builds of
`examples/aen/aen-evk-demo` and `examples/aen/aen-i2s-amp-alif`, which do
enable I2S3 and were confirmed to build `i2s_dw.c.obj` with no warnings on
the AEN801 `rtss_he` target. That, plus the native_sim regression suites
below, is all that has re-run since this fix landed — nothing has been
re-run on an AEN EVK bench unit yet.

**Bench precondition, check before any long stall:** this fix intentionally
leaves `CER.CLKEN` set with `TER.TXCHEN=0` during the underrun window.
What the DesignWare I2S core drives on SDO while `TXCHEN=0` and the clock
keeps toggling is **not established from the TRM/source excerpts read for
this fix** — if it holds the last transmitted (non-zero) sample rather than
forcing 0, that is DC into the amp for the whole gap, which is a distinct
failure mode from the SHUTDOWN latch this fix targets and needs checking
before a long stall is left running unattended. Verify with SHORT stalls
first (seconds, not the ~4.6 s repro's actual duration) and watch
`INT_LTCH3` bit 3 (`DC_DETECT`, `0x08`) — clear in both bench reads cited
above, but that predates this fix and does not by itself prove SDO's idle
level under it. Also check:
- No `TDM_CLOCK` (`INT_LTCH0` bit 2) latch across a gap-then-resume cycle.
- A tone is audible after a stall WITHOUT calling `tas2563_resume()`
  (distinguishing this fix from #2146's explicit-restart case, which still
  needs it).

**Also updated:** the recovery-path comment in
`src/backends/i2s/zephyr_drv.c` that used to say an underrun's clock loss
leaves the amp un-re-armed by this layer now reflects that the clock
itself no longer drops on the TX underrun path
(`src/backends/i2s/zephyr_drv.c:153` ("As of issue #2149, i2s_dw.c's underrun ISR path keeps")), while still calling out the two paths that ARE
unaffected by this fix: an explicit stop()/start() cycle
(`I2S_TRIGGER_STOP`/`DROP` still gate the clock, same as issue #2146
documents) and the RX-overrun gap noted above.

**Prose left describing pre-fix behaviour, owned by the #2146 rebase.**
Three sites go stale for a plain TX underrun once this fix lands but are
NOT edited here, because editing them now would conflict with the unmerged
`#2146` branch, which touches the same paragraphs for its own (explicit
restart) case:
- `include/alp/audio.h:243-245` ("that shut itself down when the bit clock stopped is not re-armed by") —
  still true for an explicit stop()/start() cycle and for the RX-overrun gap
  (Refs #2150), but no longer true for a plain TX underrun gap.
- `#2146`'s additions to the same paragraph, in both `include/alp/audio.h`
  and `include/alp/chips/tas2563.h` — neither exists on this branch yet
  (this branch stacks on `#2132`, not `#2146`), so their exact wording is
  not re-verified here.

The merge order is `#2132` → `#2146` → `#2149`: this branch (`fix/2149-...`)
rebases onto `#2146` once that lands, and THAT rebase — not a follow-up
issue with no owner — is where all three sites get corrected together,
since by then both the explicit-restart and TX-underrun re-arm stories are
final. Whoever performs that rebase owns fixing these three sites as part
of it.

**Regression harness built (round-2 review finding 4).** Round 1 of this
fix argued a native_sim unit compiling `zephyr/drivers/i2s/i2s_dw.c` itself
against a RAM-backed register block was infeasible — that turned out to be
wrong on both cited blockers. `tests/unit/i2s_dw_underrun/` now does
exactly that: `src/test_i2s_dw_underrun.c` `#include`s `i2s_dw.c` directly,
with NO `snps,designware-i2s` DT node anywhere in the test, so
`DT_INST_FOREACH_STATUS_OKAY(I2S_DW_INIT)`
(`zephyr/drivers/i2s/i2s_dw.c:1743` ("DT_INST_FOREACH_STATUS_OKAY(I2S_DW_INIT)"))
expands to nothing — neither `i2s_dw_initialize()` nor a
`DEVICE_DT_INST_DEFINE()` instance is ever wired up, side-stepping round 1's
first cited blocker (`device_is_ready(i2s->clk_dev)`) entirely, since that
call site is simply never reached. The second blocker (`DT_INST_REG_ADDR()`
needing a DTS-compile-time literal address backed by real memory) does not
apply either, for the same reason: with zero DT instances, that macro is
never expanded. What actually makes every other static function
(`tx_stream_start()`, `i2s_tx_irq_handler()`, `i2s_suspend()`/`i2s_resume()`,
...) directly callable is that `#include`-ing the `.c` file puts them in the
SAME translation unit as the test — no linkage, no fake device driver
needed. The test manually builds an `i2s_dw_cfg` whose `paddr` points at a
plain `static struct I2S_Type` in test BSS (the `__IOM` register accessors
just read/write it like any other struct) and whose `clk_dev` points at a
fake `clock_control` device with a counting `.set_rate`/`.on`/`.off`/
`.configure` — the ONLY genuinely hardware-specific pieces the driver
touches; everything else (`k_mem_slab`, `k_sem`, `irq_lock()`, the ring
buffer) is real Zephyr kernel code, unchanged, running normally on
native_sim. The CMSIS macros (`__IOM`/`__OM`/`__IM`/`__STATIC_INLINE`/
`_VAL2FLD`/`_FLD2VAL`) and `CONFIG_I2S_DW_{RX,TX}_BLOCK_COUNT` (gated by
`CONFIG_I2S_DW`, which itself depends on
`DT_HAS_SNPS_DESIGNWARE_I2S_ENABLED` — deliberately absent here) are
predefined by the test ahead of the `#include` for the same reason.

Eight tests drive `i2s_dw_configure()`/`i2s_dw_write()`/`i2s_dw_trigger()`
and `i2s_tx_irq_handler()` directly, matching finding 4's list: (a) a
queue-empty underrun leaves `state == I2S_STATE_ERROR`, `CER` bit 0 `== 1`,
`TER` bit 0 `== 0`, and the TX interrupt masked; (b) `PREPARE` then a
same-rate restart does not call `set_rate`; (c) `DROP` clears `CER` bit 0;
(d) `STOP`/`DRAIN` (two tests) gate the clock; (e) the finding-1
stale-divider sequence (TX underrun arms the skip flag → `PREPARE` → RX
starts on the SAME shared clock at a DIFFERENT rate → TX restarts at the
ORIGINAL rate) DOES call `set_rate`, proving `rx_stream_start()`'s flag
invalidation; (f) suspend then resume then start reprograms; (g) the
finding-1 invalidation site in `i2s_dw_configure()` itself — TX underrun
arms the skip flag → `PREPARE` → `i2s_dw_configure()` at a DIFFERENT rate →
TX restarts — also reprograms, proving the rate-change clear at
`zephyr/drivers/i2s/i2s_dw.c:406` ("stream->clk_restart_skip_ok = false;").

**Mutation-proven**, all runs restored afterward: (a) fails on base
`36bc7f03a` — reverting the `i2s_tx_irq_handler()` underrun exit back to

`dev_data->tx.clk_restart_skip_ok = false;` with `(void)dev_data;` (a plain delete fails the build under `-Werror`) leaves the one-shot flag
armed across the RX start, so the TX restart wrongly skips `set_rate` and

**Existing regressions re-run, unaffected:** `tests/unit/i2s_start_defer`
and `tests/unit/audio_out_start_defer` both stay green (`twister -p

### Fixed — an RX-only path could still stop or reprogram the shared I2S bit clock out from under a live TX stream (#2150 phase 1)

**Not full duplex.** #2150 itself is filed as a full-duplex feature request.
This is phase 1 only: the shared bit-clock ownership gap the driver's own
file header already named as a known remaining hazard after #2149. Refs
#2150; `i2s_dw_configure()` still maps `I2S_DIR_BOTH` to `-ENOSYS` and
`dev_data->dir` is still a single field
(`zephyr/drivers/i2s/i2s_dw.c:248` ("struct i2s_dw_data {")), both
deliberately unchanged.

**Why now.** #2149 made the TX underrun ISR exit deliberately leave
`CER.CLKEN` set so a TAS2563 on the same bus does not read bit-clock loss as
its own cue to latch SHUTDOWN. `rx_stream_disable()` and `rx_stream_start()`
were the two remaining places that could still pull that clock out from
under a transmitting stream, reopening the exact bug #2149 just closed —
this driver has one CGU-derived bit clock shared by both directions, not one
per direction.

**Fixed.** A new helper, `tx_clock_is_live()`
(`zephyr/drivers/i2s/i2s_dw.c:1176-1180` ("static bool tx_clock_is_live(const struct i2s_dw_cfg *i2s, const struct i2s_dw_data *dev_data)")),
decides whether TX is depending on the shared clock right now:
`I2S_STATE_RUNNING` qualifies, and so does `tx.clk_restart_skip_ok` **on its
own, regardless of state** — ANDed with the hardware `CER.CLKEN` bit itself
(`i2s_clock_is_enabled()`) so software state alone can never claim TX is
live.

**Round-3 review finding: the first version of this fix shipped with a
reachable silent-amp hole.** It qualified the flag only when
`tx.state == I2S_STATE_ERROR`, narrower than the flag's own documented
contract. `I2S_TRIGGER_PREPARE` moves TX `ERROR`→`READY` without clearing
the flag, and `z_start()`'s own PREPARE-retry
(`src/backends/i2s/zephyr_drv.c`) commonly leaves TX parked there for as
long as its producer stays stalled — not a narrow window, as an earlier
draft of this note claimed, but the exact gap the field exists to close, for
however long recovery takes. With `state == READY && flag == true &&
CER.CLKEN == 1` reachable, the old ERROR-only check answered "TX not live"
and let an RX stop/overrun gate the clock the flag was protecting. Dropping
the state qualifier — the flag's own comment already documents it as
state-independent — closes that hole; the `i2s_clock_is_enabled()` AND
covers the case a hardware-only check would get wrong the other way
(`CER.CLKEN` reads 1 from `i2s_dw_initialize()` onward, so hardware alone
would gate an RX-only stream that never had a live TX at all), and for free
closes PM suspend's own gap too: `i2s_suspend()` gates `CER.CLKEN`
unconditionally without touching `tx.state`, so a suspend mid-stream can
leave `tx.state == RUNNING` with the clock actually off — the hardware read
correctly answers "not live" for that case without any separate fix.

- `rx_stream_disable()` — the single shared body reached from
  `STOP`/`DRAIN`/`DROP` (via `stream->stream_disable`) and all four of
  `i2s_rx_irq_handler()`'s `goto rx_disable` routes (the `ERROR` exit, the
  `STOPPING` exit, and the failed-alloc / failed-`queue_put()` exits) — now
  skips `i2s_clock_disable()` when TX is live
  (`zephyr/drivers/i2s/i2s_dw.c:1473` ("if (!tx_live) {")), and deliberately
  leaves `tx.clk_restart_skip_ok` untouched in that case, since the clock
  never actually stopped. When TX is not live, behaviour is unchanged from
  before this fix.
- `rx_stream_start()` now skips reprogramming
  `clock_control_set_rate()`/CCR when TX is live at the SAME
  `frame_clk_freq`
  (`zephyr/drivers/i2s/i2s_dw.c:1269` ("clk_needs_reprogram = !tx_live;")),
  mirroring the `clk_needs_reprogram` shape #2149 already established in
  `tx_stream_start()`. If TX is live at a DIFFERENT rate, RX cannot silently
  retune the one shared divider without also retuning TX's stream out from
  under it, so it now returns `-EBUSY`
  (`zephyr/drivers/i2s/i2s_dw.c:1197-1208` ("return -EBUSY;")) before touching
  any hardware state or allocating a block, instead of pretending to
  succeed. `-EBUSY` was chosen over `-ENOTSUP` (this is not a permanent
  incapability) or `-EINVAL` (the RX config is fine on its own; the conflict
  is with the CURRENT shared clock state) — retrying once TX stops, or
  reconfigures to the same rate, succeeds. When TX is not live, behaviour is
  unchanged from before this fix.

**Documentation gap, also from round-3 review: the driver's own header
under-counted its known remaining gaps.** It named one; there are two.
Alongside the pre-existing channel-enable gap (`rx_stream_start()` and
`tx_stream_start()` each still unconditionally disable the OTHER
direction's channel-enable bit on every start), `i2s_dw_configure()` writes
`dev_data->dir`
(`zephyr/drivers/i2s/i2s_dw.c:397` ("dev_data->dir = dir;")) on every call,
and that single field is the ONLY thing `i2s_dw_isr()` consults to decide
whether to run `i2s_tx_irq_handler()` at all. Every RX-owning path this fix
protects requires RX to have been configured, which overwrites `dir` to
`I2S_DIR_RX` and permanently stops TX's IRQ from firing — so a "live" TX can
no longer refill its FIFO once RX is configured, and `tx.state ==
I2S_STATE_RUNNING` becomes stale software state from that point on. This fix
still delivers real value in that case (the amps key on BCLK presence, and
`tx_clock_is_live()` correctly keeps `CER.CLKEN` set for a TX the driver
itself can no longer service), but `tx.state == RUNNING` must not be read as
"TX is actually streaming" once RX has been configured. Both gaps are
full-duplex territory and stay with #2150's later phase(s).

**Public API surface.** `alp_i2s_start()`'s `@return` now documents the new
`ALP_ERR_BUSY` outcome
(`include/alp/i2s.h:144-149` ("ALP_ERR_BUSY (issue #2150 phase 1")) —
`-EBUSY` reaches callers as `ALP_ERR_BUSY`
(`src/common/alp_errno.h:70-72` ("case EBUSY:")), passed through untouched
by `z_start()` and `src/i2s_dispatch.c`. No ABI snapshot change: this is a
new value already reachable through the existing `alp_status_t` mapping, not
a new symbol — `python3 scripts/abi_snapshot.py --diff
docs/abi/v0.16-snapshot.json` reports "ABI unchanged".

**Known remaining gap, out of scope for phase 1:** `rx_stream_start()` and
`tx_stream_start()` each still unconditionally disable the OTHER
direction's channel-enable bit (`i2s_tx_channel_disable()` /
`i2s_rx_channel_disable()`) on every start — a genuinely concurrent RX+TX
session would still have one direction's channel silenced by the other's
(re)start, clock ownership aside. `dev_data->dir` being a single field (see
above) is the same territory from the ISR-dispatch side. Both are
full-duplex territory and stay with #2150's later phase(s), and are now
explicitly bounded — not the underrun-recovery `PREPARE` window, which this
fix's `tx_clock_is_live()` now covers correctly.

**Not verified on silicon.** No hardware access for this change. The bench
check still owed: on an AEN EVK bench unit, an RX overrun during active TX must
leave `CER=0x00000001` and both TAS2563 amps at `PWR_CTL=0x0c`.

**Tests.** `tests/unit/i2s_dw_underrun` — the suite that compiles
`zephyr/drivers/i2s/i2s_dw.c` directly against a RAM-backed register block —
gains four cases: RX `STOP` with TX `RUNNING` leaves `CER.CLKEN` set
(mutation-proven: reverting `rx_stream_disable()`'s `if (!tx_live)` guard to
unconditional gating turns it RED); RX `STOP` with no TX stream configured
still gates the clock, unchanged; RX `START` with TX `RUNNING` at the same
rate does not call `set_rate` AND leaves `CCR` itself untouched
(mutation-proven: deleting `rx_stream_start()`'s second
`if (clk_needs_reprogram)` guard around `i2s_configure_clock()` left all 12
cases green before this addition; the `CCR` sentinel assertion now catches
it); RX `START` with TX `RUNNING` at a different rate returns `-EBUSY`,
never touches `set_rate`, and never allocates (and leaks) an RX slab block
before refusing (mutation-proven: moving the `-EBUSY` return below
`k_mem_slab_alloc()` now goes RED on the slab's
`k_mem_slab_num_free_get()` count)
(`tests/unit/i2s_dw_underrun/src/test_i2s_dw_underrun.c` new
`test_rx_stop_with_tx_running_keeps_clock`,
`test_rx_stop_with_tx_idle_gates_clock`,
`test_rx_start_with_tx_running_same_rate_skips_reprogram`,
`test_rx_start_with_tx_running_different_rate_fails`). The pre-existing
`test_rx_start_invalidates_tx_restart_skip` case, which asserted the
ERROR-only qualifier's hole as correct behaviour, is renamed
`test_rx_start_rejected_preserves_tx_restart_skip` and now asserts the RX
start is refused with `-EBUSY` and `clk_restart_skip_ok` survives the
rejection (mutation-proven: re-adding the ERROR-only qualifier turns it
RED). `twister -p native_sim/native/64 -T tests/unit/i2s_dw_underrun`:
12/12 test cases pass.

### Added — EEPROM Secure Data Page mirror + write/lock API (#2151)

A new 64-byte `alp_secure_page_mirror_t` (`<alp/hw_info.h>`) and two new
driver calls, `eeprom_24c128_secure_page_write()` /
`eeprom_24c128_secure_page_lock()` (`<alp/chips/eeprom_24c128.h>`), give
alp-sdk a write + permanent-lock path for the onsemi N24S128's Secure Data
Page (`0x58`, selector `0x00`, 64 bytes) — a recovery copy of the array
manifest's immutable core (`sku`, `hw_rev`, `serial`, mfg date, CRC), since
the array manifest at `0x50` offset `0x0000` has no write protection at all
and one stray `eeprom_24c128_write(ctx, 0, ...)` from customer code can wipe
it. `_Static_assert`-pinned at exactly 64 bytes, magic `0x414C5350` ("ALSP"),
`schema_version` independent of the array manifest's. Full byte table + the
width reasoning: `EEPROM-MANIFEST-SPEC.md`'s Secure Data Page section
(alp-sdk-internal).

Deliberately NOT a straight truncation of the 128-byte manifest's field
widths — those sum to exactly 64 with no room left for a magic or a schema
version, which would make a blank (unprovisioned, all-`0xFF`) page
indistinguishable from a provisioned one whose serial happens to start with
`0xFF`, and would freeze every locked unit at whatever version shipped
first. The new struct's field widths (`sku[16]`, `hw_rev[12]`, `serial[23]`)
are sized from what the data needs today (10/7/12 chars respectively) plus
headroom sized to how likely each field is to outgrow it, not copied from
the manifest's and not split evenly: `sku` gets the most headroom (1.6x)
because it is both the field the array itself budgets the most headroom for
(24 bytes against the same 10-char pattern) and the one this mirror exists
to recover — a future SKU the array could still hold but this locked mirror
could not represent would defeat the mirror's purpose. `hw_rev` gets the
least (1.7x, but off a smaller base) because it tracks a physical Altium
board revision, the field least likely to ever need more room. A reader
that encounters a `schema_version` it has no code for — lower or higher —
must refuse to parse the struct rather than guess, the same rule the array
manifest's reader already applies, stated explicitly in the spec because a
locked page's reader bugs are permanent in a way the rewritable array's
are not.

Two separate functions, not one write-and-lock call, so the lock is
gateable on a caller-verified read-back — the lock is one-shot and
permanent (`docs/som-batch-provisioning-procedure.md` §7,
alp-sdk-internal): after it, "Any write instructions to the Secure Data
Page will return No ACK from the device." `eeprom_24c128_secure_page_write()`
takes no offset/selector parameter — it always writes the full page from a
compile-time-fixed selector — so it is structurally impossible for it to
ever construct a write to selector `0x06` (the Device Configuration
Register), where a stray byte would land on the `SWP` bit and permanently
write-protect the array, this page, and the register together.
`eeprom_24c128_secure_page_lock()` re-reads Secure Page Lock Status after
issuing the lock, rather than trusting the write's own ACK, and neither
function implements the datasheet's other lock-check method (attempt a
page write and see whether it ACKs) since that method is itself a write.
Both functions are [UNTESTED] / [PAPER-ONLY] against silicon — their exact
wire bytes are transcribed from the provisioning procedure doc, the only
source available, and need a real bench run before the first production
lock.

`examples/aen/aen-eeprom-provision` gains two new build-time modes
alongside its existing array-write default: `-DALP_SECURE_PAGE_BIN=<path>`
writes the mirror and verifies the read-back in the same run (never
locks); `-DALP_LOCK_SECURE_PAGE=1` (which requires
`-DALP_SECURE_PAGE_BIN` too) permanently locks it, refusing unless the
page currently on the device — read fresh, since a RAM-run cannot survive
a power cycle — is byte-exact against the same blob the write mode used.
The lock is never a side effect of writing; it needs its own explicit
opt-in flag, the same shape as `-DALP_PROVISION_FORCE=1`. A new sibling
script, `scripts/program_eeprom_secure_page.py`, builds the 64-byte blob
from the same `board.yaml` + `--serial` + `--mfg-date` inputs
`program_eeprom.py` takes for the 128-byte manifest — a separate script
rather than a mode of that one, since `check_board_id_doc_parity.py`
resolves `program_eeprom.py`'s five length constants by exact name and a
second, differently-sized set risks colliding with that gate's parser.

Graceful degradation is unchanged from `eeprom_24c128_read_identity()`'s
existing contract: on the approved footprint-compatible alternate part
(STMicro `M24128-BFMH6TG`, no second device-select header at all), both new
example modes fail cleanly with a "no second device-select header" message;
the array manifest, and everything that reads it, is unaffected either way.

Also adds `alp_secure_page_mirror_classify()` (`<alp/hw_info.h>`, header-only
`static inline`, following the existing `<alp/protocol/crc16.h>` pattern):
the mirror equivalent of `alp_hw_info_classify_manifest()`, refusing to
parse a page whose `magic`/`schema_version` don't match exactly what this
build understands, in either direction — the same forward-compatibility
rule the spec states. It copies through `memcpy` rather than casting the
raw device buffer, because `eeprom_24c128_identity_t::secure_page` sits at
a 1-byte-aligned offset with no stronger guarantee, and this struct's own
`uint16_t`/`uint32_t` fields need 2/4-byte alignment — a straight cast is a
real misaligned-access bug, not just a style nit. Both provisioning-example
modes route every raw device-page read through it.

`eeprom_24c128_secure_page_lock()`'s post-lock wait (replacing the removed
ACK poll, since a correct lock NAKs any further write to the page) uses
`alp_delay_ms()`, not `alp_delay_us()` — the ~20 ms wait belongs on the
yielding primitive; `alp_delay_us()` is a non-yielding busy-wait documented
for sub-millisecond sequences only, and 20 ms of that stalls every
equal-or-lower-priority thread on the core (issue #1621's defect class).
The wait budget is now its own named `EEPROM_LOCK_WAIT_MS` constant rather
than a runtime `(EEPROM_WRITE_POLL_STEP_US / 1000u) * EEPROM_WRITE_POLL_MAX`
product — that expression is integer division of two independently-tunable
constants, and any `EEPROM_WRITE_POLL_STEP_US` below 1000 rounded the whole
term to 0, silently deleting the wait.

Review before the first production lock (this code permanently locks a
64-byte identity page on customer modules, run without a rehearsal on a
sacrificial part) found and closed three more gaps in
`examples/aen/aen-eeprom-provision` mode 3 (the permanent-lock mode):

- The mirror about to be sealed was never checked against the module's own
  128-byte array manifest at `0x50` — the two are written by separate tool
  runs, in different production steps, from separate `.bin` files, so a
  self-consistent, CRC-valid mirror belonging to another module, or one
  carrying a typo'd `--serial` or the wrong `--mfg-date`, would lock forever
  undetected. Note the limit: `scripts/program_eeprom_secure_page.py`
  imports `scripts/program_eeprom.py` and reuses its `board.yaml` loader, so
  `sku` and `hw_rev` resolve through the same code from the same field —
  generate both blobs from one `board.yaml` and those two fields carry no
  independent signal, and a `board.yaml` that is wrong for the module agrees
  with itself here. `serial` and the mfg date are independent either way.
  Mode 3 now reads the array manifest fresh, integrity-checks
  it (magic + schema_version + CRC — a missing or corrupt manifest refuses
  exactly like a real disagreement, not as "nothing to disagree with"), and
  refuses to lock unless it agrees with the mirror on `sku`, `hw_rev`,
  `serial`, and the mfg date, comparing each as a NUL-terminated string
  (the two objects use different field widths: manifest 24/8/24 bytes,
  mirror 16/12/23) rather than a raw byte range.
- Mode 3's own comment claimed a fresh `read_identity()` call inside a
  single RAM-run "IS the cold-cycle read-back the provisioning doc
  requires" — false: a Flow C RAM-run is a J-Link/OpenOCD halt-load-go over
  SWD that never interrupts the power rail, so an operator could chain
  mode 2 then mode 3 with power continuous the whole time. Mode 3 now
  refuses to lock without a second, separately-named build flag,
  `-DALP_SECURE_PAGE_COLD_CYCLED=1` (distinct from `-DALP_LOCK_SECURE_PAGE`,
  wired the same way in `CMakeLists.txt`) — an operator attestation that a
  real cold cycle (rail confirmed at 0.0 V, not a warm reset) happened
  between the mode 2 write and this run; the actual evidence belongs in the
  bench log's power telemetry, not in this flag.
- `eeprom_24c128_secure_page_lock()` confirms only the Lock Status bit,
  never the payload, so mode 3 now re-reads the page and byte-compares it
  against the intended blob after a successful lock, before ever printing
  `RESULT PASS` — the same check the "already locked" branch already
  performed for a page found pre-locked, now mirrored for the branch that
  just performed the lock itself. A lock-frame bug that also writes INTO
  the page (two such bugs were found and fixed on this driver during
  review) would otherwise set the lock bit, corrupt the payload, and still
  print PASS.

`alp_secure_page_mirror_t` and `alp_secure_page_mirror_classify()` now
carry an explicit `@par ABI status: [ABI-EXPERIMENTAL]` tag (previously
inheriting `hw_info.h`'s file-level `[ABI-STABLE]` by omission) — the
format cannot be frozen while the driver functions that write and lock it
are still `[UNTESTED]` / `[PAPER-ONLY]` against silicon. `docs/abi-markers.md`
updated to match.

Also fixes four pre-existing misaligned-cast reads of `alp_hw_info_eeprom_t`
(the same bug class `099923591` fixed for the Secure Data Page blob, left
unswept on the 128-byte array-manifest path): the array-write mode of
`aen-eeprom-provision`, the two `*-eeprom-manifest*` read/dump examples,
`aen-evk-demo`'s EEPROM-identity phase, and the `eeprom_manifest_fuzz.c`
libFuzzer harness (where the cast additionally defeated the harness's own
purpose — an x86 host tolerates the unaligned read silently, so the bug it
exists to catch on the real ARM target could never trip). All now `memcpy`
into an aligned local instead of casting a `uint8_t[]`/`uint8_t*` buffer.

`eeprom_24c128_identity_t` also gains `lock_status`, the Lock Status Read
byte verbatim, alongside the `secure_page_locked` bool it already carried.
The bool is that byte's bit 1, and that polarity is transcribed from the
provisioning procedure rather than confirmed against a part that has
actually been locked — so on a first production lock the bool alone cannot
distinguish "the lock did not take" from "the lock took and the indication
is not bit 1", on an operation that cannot be repeated. Mode 3 now logs the
raw byte before and after the lock and includes it in the UNCONFIRMED
failure message, and `aen-eeprom-manifest` prints it beside the decode.
`device_config` was already surfaced raw; this gives Lock Status the same
treatment.

The Secure Data Page write and lock are no longer `[PAPER-ONLY]`. Both ran
against real silicon on 2026-09-16, on three E1M-AEN modules — `2026W36-0005`
(E4, `AE402FA0E5597LE0`) and `2026W36-0006` / `2026W36-0007` (E8,
`AE822FA0E5597LS0`). On each the 64-byte page read back byte-identical to the
staged blob after a cold power cycle, the lock frame `{0x04, 0x00, 0xFF}` took,
and Lock Status moved `0xFD` → `0xFF`, setting exactly bit 1 and holding it
through a further cold cycle; Device Config stayed `0x1D` and was never
written. That is the first evidence for the `(byte & 0x02) != 0` polarity the
driver has always assumed. `include/alp/chips/eeprom_24c128.h`,
`docs/verification-status.md` and `docs/test-plan.md` say so; the operation is
still one-shot and irreversible, and no automated HIL job covers it.

### Added — the 15 copies of `cc3501e_bridge.{c,h}` under `examples/` are now gated against drift (#2163)

`cc3501e_bridge.c` / `.h` is copied per example -- 16 identical pairs when this
gate landed, plus one deliberately different -- and nothing asserted the copies
stayed in sync. It is not boilerplate: it writes the LP-GPIO pad control
registers for `WIFI_EN` / nRESET, runs the reset pulse, and pokes the
silicon-tuned DW SSI `RX_SAMPLE_DLY` register that makes the 25 MHz link sample
MISO correctly (`examples/aen/aen-cc3501e-bringup/src/cc3501e_bridge.c:86`
("the DW SSI RX_SAMPLE_DLY register (0xf0) delays")). A silicon fix applied to
one copy and missed in the other fifteen compiles clean, passes CI, and shows
up only on hardware. #1859 is the same failure already realised once: the
hand-copied `cc3501e_gpio_routes.c` drifted to a wrong `hw_rev` pad map, and
the fix there was to generate it from one source
(`scripts/gen_cc3501e_gpio_routes.py`).

The duplication itself stays, because two documented properties depend on it:
the header presents the pair as a customer-facing template
(`examples/aen/aen-cc3501e-bringup/src/cc3501e_bridge.h:15`
("copy this pair")), and `tan init --from-example <dir>` copies
exactly one directory, so an example that reached into a shared
`examples/aen/common/` would no longer scaffold. So the new gate detects drift
rather than removing it: `scripts/check_cc3501e_bridge_copies.py` compares
every copy byte for byte against
`examples/aen/aen-cc3501e-bringup/src`
(`scripts/check_cc3501e_bridge_copies.py:55` ("CANONICAL_DIR =")), the
bring-up example the AEN `board.yaml` files already name as the shape to match.
A failure prints the first differing lines and the `cp` command that re-syncs
that copy; `--fix` re-syncs every graded copy at once.

A copy that differs on purpose is declared by name with its reason
(`scripts/check_cc3501e_bridge_copies.py:63` ("DIVERGENT_COPIES = {")), and
today there is exactly one: `examples/peripheral-io/alp-console/src`, whose
bring-up retries `cc3501e_hard_reset()` in a cold-boot soak instead of
returning the first `cc3501e_reset()` status, and carries no `RX_SAMPLE_DLY`
poke. That list is graded in both directions -- an entry naming a directory
with no copy fails, and so does one whose copy has come back into line
(`scripts/check_cc3501e_bridge_copies.py:150` ("declared divergent in")) --
because an exemption nobody removes is where the next drift hides. A directory
carrying one half of the pair without the other fails too.

Registered as a hard gate in the quick / pr / full / release profiles
(`metadata/quality-tasks-v1.json:165` ("cc3501e-bridge-copies")) and wired into
CI (`.github/workflows/pr-metadata-validate.yml:775`
("cc3501e_bridge copies are in sync")). The tree passes today: 15 copies byte-identical to the
canonical pair, one declared divergent. Note that the 18-copy survey in #2163
counted a copy under `examples/aen/aen-sdcard-readout`, which no longer carries
one -- that example ships only a `boards/` directory on `dev`.

### Fixed — `aen-evk-demo` no longer leaves both TAS2563 amps in hardware shutdown (#2164)

Phase 11's idle restore drove `AMP_ENABLE` / `SD_N` (`P5_2`, `gpio5`) LOW on the
way out. A pin driven low keeps `SD_N` asserted after the app exits, so both
TAS2563s stayed in **hardware** shutdown — and a part in hardware shutdown does
not ACK on I2C. Every later image that scanned the carrier bus therefore
reported the two amps as missing hardware, with no indication why.

Measured on E1M-AEN803 serial 2026W36-0002, same resident diagnostics image both times, the
only variable being the state of `P5_2`: `alp i2c scan 0` returned 12
responders after a run of this phase (`0x40 0x41 0x42 0x47 0x49 0x4a 0x4b 0x50
0x58 0x68 0x69 0x73`, with `E: NACK on i2c@49012000` / `E: IO Fail on
i2c@49012000`), and 15 after a reset released the pin — `0x48`, `0x4d` and
`0x4e` all returning together and the NACK lines gone. The parts were never
faulty: a run that pulses `SD_N` low-then-high reported
`tas2563_init(0x4d) -> 0`, `tas2563_init(0x4e) -> 0`, fault words
`0x00000000` on both, and `2/2 amp(s) up, no fault`.

`0x48` is the TAS2563 *broadcast* address, not a third device — all three
addresses belong to the same two chips, which is what distinguished this from
a bus-wide fault.

The idle restore now RELEASES the pin instead
(`examples/aen/aen-evk-demo/src/main.c:4778`
("RELEASE AMP_ENABLE; do not drive it low")): configuring it as an input stops
driving it, so `R138`'s 10 kOhm pull-up to `+VIO` defines the resting level
exactly as it does at power-on. An actively driven low overrides that pull-up,
which is why "the pull-up will release them" did not hold before. The amps are
deinitialised just above, and nothing this phase leaves behind needs them held
in hardware shutdown.

The `ok_amps == 0` failure path did the same thing and is fixed the same way
(`examples/aen/aen-evk-demo/src/main.c:4346`
("gpio_pin_configure(gpio5, AMP_ENABLE_PIN, GPIO_INPUT)")) — leaving `SD_N`
asserted on the way out of a failure would make the next run's scan see absent
hardware and mask whatever actually went wrong.

Phase 11's step-13 header, which promised "AMP_ENABLE driven LOW", is corrected
to say what the pin is actually left as and why.

**Cost of the old behaviour, for the record:** a bench verification session
aborted reporting a suspected hardware failure on E1M-AEN803 serial 2026W36-0002, and a
second bench session was needed to establish the board was fine.

### Fixed — Alif PDM refused the first START with `-EIO` after a warm boot (#2167)

`alif_pdm` inherited the previous image's `PDM_INTERRUPT` enables (`0x303`) and
sticky `PDM_ERROR_IRQ`/`PDM_WARN_IRQ` status across a Flow C or warm boot, and
`irq_config()` armed the NVIC lines on top of them, so `pdm_error_handler()` set
`overrun` and `DMIC_TRIGGER_START` failed. Cold init now masks `PDM_INTERRUPT`,
read-clears both status registers, pulses `FIFO_CLR` and clears `overrun`
before `irq_config()`. The DesignWare I2S driver already quiesces IER/IMR
before arming its NVIC line (#2179, #2205), so the I2S storm path is already
masked and needed no change.

Not fixed: the intermittent all-zero PDM capture stays open under #2167; this
change only removes the inherited-state `-EIO` on START. The warm
(`PM_DEVICE_ACTION_RESUME`) path is unchanged.

### Fixed — references to `aen-i2s-tas2563-probe` say it lives on a bench branch, not in the tree (#2170)

`examples/aen/aen-i2s-tas2563-probe` exists only on the unmerged bench branch
`test/2149-underrun-bench`. `changelog.d/2132.md` listed it among "in-tree
callers", and the `audio_out_start_defer` unit test called it the silicon
repro without saying where it lives. Both now name the branch, and the test
points at `examples/aen/aen-evk-demo` as the maintained in-tree caller.
Mentions that already named the branch (`aen-pdm-mic-alif`, `alif_pdm.c`,
the `alif,alif-pdm` binding, `changelog.d/2149.md`, `2205.md`) are unchanged.

### Fixed — the connectivity examples build for AEN again: mbedTLS' PSA core is now on wherever mbedTLS is (#2173)

`mqtt-telemetry`, `iot-fleet-ota` and `production-deployment` did not compile
for an AEN target at all, and the same break is why each carried a
`CONFIG_MBEDTLS=n` workaround on `native_sim`. Root cause, now established: the
`mbedtls` library manifest emits `CONFIG_MBEDTLS=y` +
`CONFIG_MBEDTLS_BUILTIN=y` and nothing else, which builds the library's SSL
sources with PSA crypto off. The pinned mbedTLS does not survive that — its own
internal `library/ssl_misc.h` declares `extern const mbedtls_error_pair_t
psa_to_ssl_errors[7]` unconditionally, while `mbedtls_error_pair_t` itself is
inside `#if defined(MBEDTLS_PSA_CRYPTO_CLIENT)` in tf-psa-crypto's
`psa_util_internal.h`, so every translation unit that pulls in `ssl_misc.h`
fails with `unknown type name 'mbedtls_error_pair_t'`. It is an alp-sdk
integration gap, not an upstream bug and not a Zephyr one: upstream has no
non-PSA TLS path left to fall back to.

The fix is one Kconfig rule rather than a per-example knob
(`zephyr/Kconfig.alp-libraries:364` ("config ALP_SDK_MBEDTLS_PSA_CRYPTO")):
whenever `MBEDTLS` is on and TF-M is not building the crypto partition, the SDK
selects `MBEDTLS_PSA_CRYPTO_C`. `MBEDTLS_PSA_CRYPTO_CLIENT` — the symbol the
header actually tests — is not directly assignable; it is a non-prompt bool
defaulting y on `BUILD_WITH_TFM || MBEDTLS_PSA_CRYPTO_C`, and
`MBEDTLS_PSA_CRYPTO_C` itself `depends on !BUILD_WITH_TFM`, hence the condition
on the default (`zephyr/Kconfig.alp-libraries:367`
("default y if !BUILD_WITH_TFM")) rather than an unconditional select.

Verified by building each app end to end on this change (arm-none-eabi 13.2 +
picolibc, Zephyr v4.4.1): `mqtt-telemetry` and `iot-fleet-ota` link for
`alp_e1m_aen801_m55_hp/ae822fa0e5597ls0/rtss_hp`, and `mqtt-telemetry`,
`iot-fleet-ota`, `iot-dashboard` and `production-deployment` all build for
`native_sim/native/64` with mbedTLS ON. `mqtt-telemetry` still reaches its
`[mqtt] done` marker when run on `native_sim` with TLS enabled.

Because the workaround is no longer needed, the two `native_sim.conf` files
that existed only to carry it are deleted, `production-deployment`'s keeps just
its littlefs block, `iot-dashboard`'s keeps just its panel wiring, and
`iot-dashboard` now builds MQTT over TLS rather than forcing `MQTT_LIB_TLS=n`.
The `EXTRA_CONF_FILE=native_sim.conf` arguments those two deleted files needed
are gone with them, so the `native_sim` scenarios now build the same
TLS-enabled configuration the SoM does — that is the point of the change, not a
side effect: these apps' whole subject is a TLS transport.

The reason a break this total went unnoticed is that nothing built these apps
for AEN. `iot-fleet-ota`'s AEN scenario named `ensemble_e8_dk/...` — Alif's own
DevKit board, which no `-p` flag in this repo selects — and `mqtt-telemetry`
had no AEN scenario at all. Both now name the target their own `board.yaml`
describes (`examples/connectivity/mqtt-telemetry/testcase.yaml:53`
("alp_e1m_aen801_m55_hp")), and both are added as bounded testsuite roots of
the AEN twister job (`.github/workflows/pr-twister-aen.yml:602`
("alp-sdk/examples/connectivity/mqtt-telemetry")), build_only, so the next regression
in this path fails a PR instead of a bench session.

**Not fixed, and not silently left implicit.** Two things this does not do:

- `iot-dashboard` still does not build for AEN, for an unrelated reason: LVGL
  requires a `zephyr,display` chosen node and no panel is wired for this app on
  the E1M EVK. The EVK solders no panel at all; its documented default is an
  SSD1306 over the I²C/Qwiic header, the app declares an ST7789, and per the
  2626-R2 netlist SPI1 terminates on the on-module CC3501E while every SPI0 pad
  is repurposed (IO-expander reset, amplifier fault/enable, Arduino DIO3/DIO4).
  The one real AEN display path in the tree is the MIPI-DSI chain
  `examples/aen/aen-dsi-display` drives on the M55-HE core. Which panel this
  demo targets is a hardware decision, so it is left open rather than guessed
  at; the app's AEN scenario still names `ensemble_e8_dk/...` and still runs
  nowhere.
- `iot-dashboard`'s AEN scenario is unchanged and still runs nowhere, now said
  so in its own `testcase.yaml` rather than looking like coverage.

### Added — a build that would ship TLS on a predictable RNG is now refused (#2192)

Turning the PSA core on selects `CSPRNG_NEEDED`, and Zephyr satisfies that with
a generator it documents as not random whenever no true entropy driver is
bound. There is no Alif Ensemble entropy driver in this tree or upstream, so
every AEN target was in exactly that state: TLS linked, ran, negotiated, and
derived key material from a predictable source, with a boot-log `WARNING:
Using a test - not safe - entropy source` as the only thing between that and a
shipped product.

A warning does not stop that shipping, so the build refuses it. A new
non-prompt result symbol is y when the PSA core is compiled against
randomness that is not cryptographically secure
(`zephyr/Kconfig.alp-libraries:390` ("config ALP_SDK_MBEDTLS_WEAK_RNG")), and
CMake turns that into a hard failure naming the board and the fix
(`zephyr/CMakeLists.txt:1875` ("CONFIG_ALP_SDK_MBEDTLS_WEAK_RNG AND NOT")).
Kconfig cannot refuse a configuration, hence the CMake half.

The check is `CSPRNG_ENABLED` — Zephyr's own "a true entropy driver is in this
build" signal — plus two terms for the drivers that set `ENTROPY_HAS_DRIVER`
while stating they are not real entropy sources, so `native_sim`'s
`FAKE_ENTROPY_NATIVE_SIM` does not read as a pass.

Acknowledging it is one visible line,
`CONFIG_ALP_SDK_ALLOW_TEST_ENTROPY=y`, and it is legal only where the build
never ships: a twister scenario's `extra_configs`, a `native_sim.conf`, or
`tests/`. It is deliberately **not** in any example's `prj.conf`, because
`tan init --from-example` copies `prj.conf` into a customer's tree and
`testcase.yaml` stays behind — so a scaffolded product built for a real SoM
gets the refusal rather than the acknowledgement. A test enforces that
containment (`tests/scripts/test_weak_rng_optin_is_not_shippable.py:69`
("test_optin_is_only_enabled_where_the_build_never_ships")).

The policy reaches further than TLS, because it asks whether the PSA core is
compiled at all rather than whether a handshake happens. That blast radius was
measured rather than assumed: a configure-only twister sweep of every `tests/`
and `examples/` scenario on `native_sim` (257 configurations) and on the four
AEN targets (167) finds exactly three other builds in the tree that compile the
PSA core with no cryptographically secure random source. Each now says so, in
the place that cannot travel to a customer.

Two are `native_sim`-only ztest suites, where the acknowledgement goes in
`prj.conf` because `tan init --from-example` does not copy anything under
`tests/`: `tests/zephyr/ble_gatt_server/prj.conf:26`
("CONFIG_ALP_SDK_ALLOW_TEST_ENTROPY=y"), where `CONFIG_BT` brings in Zephyr's
own PSA provider (`PSA_CRYPTO_PROVIDER_MBEDTLS` selects
`MBEDTLS_PSA_CRYPTO_C`), and `tests/zephyr/security_mbedtls/prj.conf:34`
("CONFIG_ALP_SDK_ALLOW_TEST_ENTROPY=y"), which exists to exercise the real PSA
AEAD path.

The third is the interesting one. `examples/aen/aen-se-crypto` runs its own
TRNG demo through the Secure Enclave, but that source is not bound as a Zephyr
entropy driver, so the MbedTLS-PSA fall-through the same image builds — for the
algorithms the SE declines — would draw from Zephyr's non-cryptographic
generator. Its `build_only` bench scenario acknowledged that by carrying the
`CONFIG_ALP_SDK_ALLOW_TEST_ENTROPY=y` opt-in while the app's `prj.conf` did
not, so someone scaffolding this example for a shipping product still met the
refusal. It was also the clearest evidence that #2192 had a hardware answer
waiting, and #2192 took it: the SE TRNG is now each AEN board's default
`zephyr,entropy`, and that scenario no longer carries the opt-in.

Verified four ways by hand on this change (arm-none-eabi 13.2 + picolibc,
Zephyr v4.4.1), since twister cannot assert a build failure: `mqtt-telemetry`
for `alp_e1m_aen801_m55_hp` is refused without the opt-in and links with it,
and the same app on `native_sim` is refused without it and builds with it.
The AEN and `native_sim` scenarios therefore carry the opt-in; the apps do
not.

Both halves of the decision are also locked down in CI, evaluated over the
real Kconfig and CMake text rather than restated: a truth table covers the
refuse path (AEN with no entropy driver, `native_sim` behind its fake one)
and the allow path (the same two with the acknowledgement, a target that
binds a real driver, and a TF-M build where the secure partition owns
crypto) — `tests/scripts/test_weak_rng_policy_paths.py:167`
("test_refuse_and_allow_paths_both_decide_correctly").

The real fix stays open silicon work: an entropy driver over the Secure
Enclave TRNG, filed as #2192.

- `ALP_SDK_MBEDTLS_PSA_CRYPTO` is also now scoped to `MBEDTLS_BUILTIN`. The
  break is a property of the mbedtls sources Zephyr vendors; a build selecting
  a custom implementation supplies its own headers and must not inherit
  Zephyr's PSA policy from this SDK.

### Fixed — `iot-dashboard` builds for AEN now, with a real panel (#2173)

Item (3) of #2173. `iot-dashboard`'s AEN scenario named `ensemble_e8_dk/...`
— Alif's own DevKit board, which no `-p` flag in this repo selects — so it
built nowhere, and #2173's mbedTLS fix (already on `dev` via #2193) could not
retarget it the way it retargeted `mqtt-telemetry` and `iot-fleet-ota`: LVGL
needs a `zephyr,display` chosen node, and this app's declared ST7789 has no
working SPI route on the E1M EVK (its SPI0 pads are all repurposed on the
2626-R2 netlist). The maintainer's call: give the demo the RK055HDMIPI4MA0
