unlike SDO/SCLK/WS, which are wired backwards against the SoC's own I2S3 TX
and are the reason this node ships `status = "disabled"` by default. The
omission was a deliberate TX-only scope decision at the time, not a hazard;
that scope has since widened.

`<PIN_P9_2__I2S3_SDI_A>` is now declared in its own `pinctrl_i2s3` group with
`input-enable` set, in all four in-tree `i2s3` board overlays -- the
E1M-AEN801 pair,
`examples/aen/aen-i2s-amp-alif/boards/alp_e1m_aen801_m55_he_ae822fa0e5597ls0_rtss_he.overlay:70`
(`pinmux = <PIN_P9_2__I2S3_SDI_A>;`) and
`examples/aen/aen-evk-demo/boards/alp_e1m_aen801_m55_he_ae822fa0e5597ls0_rtss_he.overlay:794`
(`pinmux = <PIN_P9_2__I2S3_SDI_A>;`), and the E1M-AEN803 pair, which carries
the identical U46 wiring and the identical stale TX-only comment,
`examples/aen/aen-i2s-amp-alif/boards/alp_e1m_aen803_m55_he_ae822fa0e5597ls0_rtss_he.overlay:70`
(`pinmux = <PIN_P9_2__I2S3_SDI_A>;`) and
`examples/aen/aen-evk-demo/boards/alp_e1m_aen803_m55_he_ae822fa0e5597ls0_rtss_he.overlay:794`
(`pinmux = <PIN_P9_2__I2S3_SDI_A>;`). `input-enable` is load-bearing, not
decoration: on this SoC a pad's input buffer is gated by a separate REN bit
that Zephyr's upstream `alif,pinctrl` binding's `input-enable` property
programs (`soc/alif/ensemble/pinctrl_soc.h` in the pinned Zephyr v4.4.1
module, outside this repo) — muxing the pin alone is necessary but not
sufficient to receive, since REN defaults off. An
earlier commit's claim that read-enable is "not in the upstream
`alif,pinctrl` binding" was true of the fork's own `read-enable = <0x1>`
property name, but the mainline binding's equivalent `input-enable` boolean
is already the established idiom elsewhere in this same repo (e.g. the PDM
data pin a few groups below in the `aen-evk-demo` overlay) and programs the
identical REN bit, so it is used here too rather than inventing anything new.

Both groups stay inert on their own: `i2s3` ships `status = "disabled"` by
default on EVK rev 2626-R2, so `pinctrl-0` is not applied until
`i2s3-enable-post-u46-rework.overlay` flips it `"okay"` — that switch-overlay
only sets `status`, and inherits `pinctrl_i2s3` from the board overlay
unchanged, so no separate edit was needed there. Neither example's app code
calls `i2s_configure()`/`i2s_read()` in the RX direction, so this change is
pinctrl-only groundwork; actually reading over I2S3 SDI still needs that
app-level RX wiring, which is out of scope here.

Bench caveat, not a reason to hold this change: U46 is a 3257-type switch
with `VCC` on `+3V3`, while `+VIO` measured 1.8 V on E1M-AEN803 serial 2026W36-0002, and a
3257 passes the amp's SDOUT level through rather than re-driving it, so the
logic level that actually lands on `P9_2` depends on the amp's IO rail and
has not been established — enabling REN here adds no contention regardless
(the SoC never drives `P9_2`, an input-only function, and U46's `4Y` drives
that net either way), but someone must check the level on hardware before
trusting a long RX run.

### Fixed — `check_cross_platform.py`'s `IMPLICIT-ENCODING` rule no longer demands a fix that cannot be applied, and no longer skips `**kw` subprocess helpers (#2197)

Before the #2197 drain starts, the rule itself gets fixed, so that no
baselined site is one the drain cannot clear.

**Some `.open()` calls were flagged even though the suggested fix cannot be
applied.** `tokenize.open()` has no `encoding=` parameter, so following the
advice raises `TypeError`. `tarfile.open(..., mode="w")` is also not a
text-mode open: its `"w"` is a tar mode. Four baselined sites had these shapes,
and one of them used a function-scope `import tarfile as _tf`. The check now
resolves the call's owner through `import m` / `import m as a` at any scope,
and through a module-level `from m import open`. It skips modules whose `open`
takes no `encoding=`: `scripts/check_cross_platform.py:513`
("_OPEN_WITHOUT_ENCODING_MODULES: frozenset"). The list also includes `os`,
because `os.open(path, flags=...)` would otherwise be read as a text open.
`from m import open` inside a function is not honoured, because treating it
file-wide would exempt every builtin `open()` in the file. `.open()` on an
owner the check cannot resolve, such as `widget.open()`, is still flagged.

**`Path.open()`'s mode was read from the wrong argument.** The mode was always
taken from the second positional argument. That is correct for
`open(file, mode)`, but `Path.open(mode)` takes the mode first. As a result,
`path.open("rb")` in `scripts/provision_som.py` was flagged while
`open(p, "rb")` was not. The slot now depends on the call shape:
`scripts/check_cross_platform.py:667`
("_open_mode_is_binary(node, 1 if builtin_shape else 0)"). The builtin, every
module-level `m.open(file, mode)` (so `gzip.open(p, "rb")` stays unflagged and
`gzip.open(p, "rt")` stays flagged) and any call with two or more positionals
read the second slot. Only a one-argument method call such as
`Path.open("rb")` reads the first.

**`os.fdopen()` was never checked.** Its call name is `fdopen`, so the check
never matched it, although it opens text mode by default just like `open()`.
It is now matched when its owner resolves to `os`, with the builtin
`(fd, mode)` shape: `scripts/check_cross_platform.py:516`
("_OPEN_CALL_NAMES: frozenset[str]"). This adds one finding,
`scripts/flash_backends/swd_probe.py`'s `os.fdopen(fd, "w")`, under that
file's existing baseline entry.

**`subprocess` helpers that forward `**kw` were never checked.** A blanket
`**kwargs` skip hid 13 `_run(*args, **kw)` helpers that call
`subprocess.run([sys.executable, ...], text=True, **kw)`. Their `**kw` passes
through `cwd`/`env`/`check`, not an encoding. A subprocess call whose explicit
`text=True` proves text mode is now flagged even when `**kw` is also passed:
`scripts/check_cross_platform.py:630`
("if name not in _SUBPROCESS_TEXT_CALLS and any("). `read_text`, `write_text`
and `open` calls with `**kw` are still skipped: nothing in the call proves the
mode or rules out an encoding, so the check does not guess. Three of the 13
helpers were in files outside the baseline, so they are fixed here. Each one
now passes `encoding="utf-8"` and makes the Python child write UTF-8, merged
over any `env` the caller passes (an explicit `env=None` falls back to
`os.environ`): `tests/scripts/test_check_doc_drift.py:16`
("env={**(kw.pop("), and the same line in
`test_check_i2c_bus_doc_consistency.py` and `test_check_version_doc_sync.py`.
The other ten are in files that are already baselined and will be drained
there.

**The baseline advice described an escape hatch that does not exist.** The
baseline comment and the size-pin failure message both pointed to "an inline
exemption at the call site". The module docstring said there was none, and the
scanner had none. This change made both say the same thing
(`scripts/check_cross_platform.py`, "there is no inline exemption (see the" —
that comment was removed with the rest of the baseline machinery when #2197
finished the drain; the surviving docstring paragraph makes the same point at
`scripts/check_cross_platform.py:103` ("There's no legitimate reason for a call under scripts/, tests/, or")).

**The baseline shrank from 139 to 137 files.**
`scripts/check_write_text_newline.py` and
`tests/scripts/test_alp_model_adapters.py` no longer produced any finding,
because their only findings were the false positives above. The shrink-only
size pin moved with them (`tests/scripts/test_check_cross_platform.py`,
"len(linter.IMPLICIT_ENCODING_BASELINE) <=" — the pin was removed when #2197
finished the drain; the test itself survives as a plain zero-findings check).
The total number of baselined
findings went from 478 to 484. Five false positives were gone, and eleven real
sites were then counted: ten that the `**kw` skip used to hide and the
`os.fdopen()` above.

### Fixed — 52 files leave the `IMPLICIT-ENCODING` baseline: 168 file-IO and non-Python subprocess calls now pass `encoding="utf-8"` (#2197)

This is the second #2197 drain batch. It covers every baselined file whose
remaining findings are all file IO or subprocess calls with a non-Python child:

- 123 `read_text()`/`write_text()` calls;
- 45 subprocess calls whose child is `git`, `nm`, `cmake`, `cc`, `gh`, `awk` or
  plain `bash`.

Each call now passes `encoding="utf-8"`. Before this change, all 168 calls used
the platform locale: cp1252 on `windows-latest`, ASCII under `LC_ALL=C`. With
`LC_ALL=C` and `PYTHONUTF8=0`, the drained test files had 17 failures and 7
errors, all `UnicodeDecodeError: 'ascii' codec`. They read non-ASCII metadata
and `scripts/test-all.sh`, for example
`tests/scripts/test_topology_unresolved_core_type.py:90` ("E1M-AEN301.yaml").
All 564 tests now pass. `IMPLICIT_ENCODING_BASELINE` shrank from 137 to 85
files, and the size pin moved with it
(`tests/scripts/test_check_cross_platform.py`, "IMPLICIT_ENCODING_BASELINE) <="
— the pin was removed when #2197 finished the drain; the test itself survives
as a plain zero-findings check). The
baselined finding count dropped from
484 to 316.

**A file joins this batch only if none of its calls starts a Python child** -- with one exception handled in place: `baremetal_cmake_flash.py`'s `cmake --build --target flash` runs a project-supplied target that is often a Python flasher, so that call also sets `PYTHONIOENCODING=utf-8` in the child's environment.
Python children include `sys.executable`, `python3`, `west`, `twister`, `pyocd`,
`vela`, `dxcom`, and any bash script that runs `python3` while its output is
captured. For those calls, `encoding=` is only half the fix. The child also
needs `PYTHONIOENCODING=utf-8` (see #2201), so those files wait for the next
batch.

Two bash-driven test files stay in this batch after tracing:

- `tests/scripts/test_bench_jlink_run.py` and
  `tests/scripts/test_bench_ram_run_two_session.py` both source
  `scripts/bench/aen/bench-env.sh`. That script's only `python3` call runs when
  `LG_PLACE` is set, and both tests unset it.
- The fake J-Link wrapper in the ram-run test also calls `python3`, but it
  writes a timestamp to a file, not to the captured pipe.

**`errors="replace"` goes only where output is shown to a person or searched
for an ASCII marker.** Seven calls get it:

- the `cmake` configure, build and flash steps;
- the `cc` compile diagnostics in `scripts/check_stub_symbol_matrix.py`;
- the conflicting `git merge` in the conflict-resolver test.

For example, `scripts/flash_backends/baremetal_cmake_flash.py:87` ("errors=").
Calls whose output is parsed as data stay strict: git paths, `nm` symbols and
`gh` JSON.

**Four `read_text()` calls inside double-quoted f-strings use
`encoding='utf-8'`.** `requires-python` is `>=3.10`, and reusing an f-string's
own quote inside `{}` needs Python 3.12:
`scripts/gen_soc_caps.py:632` ("read_text(encoding='utf-8')").

**The edit was mechanical and checked file by file.** The keyword was inserted
at each linter-reported (line, column) position, guided by the AST. Two checks
passed for every edited file:

- the file re-parses, and its `ast.dump` matches the original once the added
  keywords are stripped;
- the added keywords are on exactly the flagged `read_text`, `write_text`,
  `run` and `Popen` calls.

### Fixed — 83 files leave the `IMPLICIT-ENCODING` baseline, and their Python children now write the UTF-8 their parents decode (#2197)

This is the third #2197 drain batch. It covers every remaining baselined file
except `scripts/alp_quality.py` and
`tests/scripts/test_check_example_board_overlay_parity.py`, which are kept for
the last batch. These are the files that start a Python child process. They
also hold 164 plain file-IO calls, which are fixed here too.

The batch changes 307 calls:

- 163 `read_text()`/`write_text()` calls and one `os.fdopen()`;
- 109 subprocess calls whose child is Python itself: `sys.executable`,
  `python3`, `west`, `twister`, `pyocd`, `bmaptool`, `vela` or `dxcom`;
- 17 subprocess calls that reach Python through bash: `scripts/test-all.sh`
  stages, the `release.yml` and `pr-generated-files.yml` `run:` steps, and
  `scripts/bootstrap.sh`;
- 17 subprocess calls whose child is not Python: eight `git` calls, `hostname`, `whoami`,
  `JLinkExe`, `dd`, `pwsh`, a `bash -c printf` probe, and three bash runs
  that never reach their `python3` line.

**A Python child needs two changes, not one.** Today both ends of the pipe use
the locale, cp1252 on `windows-latest`, and they agree by accident. Setting only
the parent's `encoding="utf-8"` breaks that agreement; #2201 did exactly this
and #2202 fixed it. So each of the 126 Python-child calls gets
`encoding="utf-8"` and also a child environment with `PYTHONIOENCODING=utf-8`.
Four shapes cover them all:

- With no `env=`, the call passes `env={**os.environ, "PYTHONIOENCODING": "utf-8"}`.
  64 files needed a new `import os` for this.
- An `env` built from `os.environ` gets the key added to its dict. For example
  `scripts/alp_model/adapters/drpai.py:213` ("PYTHONIOENCODING").
- A minimal environment built from scratch gets the key inside that dict, and
  `os.environ` is not merged in, so the test still controls exactly what the
  child sees: `tests/scripts/test_check_bootstrap_manifest.py:596`
  ("str(shim_dir)") and `tests/scripts/test_release_tag_verify.py:73`
  ("PYTHONIOENCODING").
- A helper that receives `env` from its caller merges the key over that `env`,
  or over `os.environ` when there is none:
  `scripts/alp_mcp/server.py:477` ("env={**(env or os.environ)"),
  `tests/scripts/test_provision_som.py:70` ("env={**(env or os.environ)"), and
  the ten `**kw` helpers that the linter fix above exposed, for example
  `tests/scripts/test_check_test_coverage.py:16` ("env={**(kw.pop(").

The two shared helpers are fixed once for every caller: the MCP server's
`_run` above, and `_run_loader`, which every `test_project_*.py` file uses:
`tests/scripts/_project_support.py:46` ("env={**os.environ,").

**The `release.yml` changelog step's output file is UTF-8 too.** That step
redirects the child's stdout into `release_notes.md`, so `PYTHONIOENCODING`
sets the encoding of the file itself:
`tests/scripts/test_release_changelog_slice.py:95` ("PYTHONIOENCODING").

**`errors="replace"` goes only where tool output passes straight through.**
Nine calls get it: `west build` in `scripts/alp_orchestrate/kconfig_symbols.py`,
`west flash` in `scripts/flash_backends/zephyr_west_flash.py:137`
("errors="), the J-Link, pyOCD/OpenOCD, `dd` and `bmaptool` flash calls, the
build/flash/capture runner in `tests/hil/run_smoke.py`, and `pwsh`. Compiler,
flasher and UART bytes reach these pipes without going through Python, and
`pwsh` writes the console codepage, so `PYTHONIOENCODING` cannot make that
output UTF-8.

**The J-Link command script is written in the locale encoding, on purpose.**
J-Link Commander reads its command file in the platform ANSI codepage on
Windows, so a UTF-8 file would garble a non-ASCII path (`C:\Users\<name>\` with an `é`).
The `os.fdopen()` call therefore names the locale encoding explicitly. It uses
`locale.getencoding()`, because in UTF-8 Mode `locale.getpreferredencoding()`
returns `utf-8`. On Python 3.10, which has no `locale.getencoding()`, it falls
back to `locale.getpreferredencoding(False)`:
`scripts/flash_backends/swd_probe.py:279` ("enc = (locale.getencoding()").

**The adapter tests now check the child encoding.** Their fake
`subprocess.run` functions accept the new keywords. The Vela, DRP-AI and DEEPX
tests assert that each call both decodes UTF-8 and asks the child for it:
`tests/scripts/test_alp_model_adapters.py:163` ("assert seen["). The DEEPX test
checks both `dxcom` calls, the `-v` probe and the compile:
`tests/scripts/test_alp_model_adapters.py:593` ("probe_io").

**`check_tan_docs_surface.py` asks `tan` for UTF-8 too.** That gate was not on
the baseline, because it already decoded `tan`'s output with
`encoding="utf-8"`. But `tan` is a Python program, so it still wrote its
locale. It now gets `PYTHONIOENCODING=utf-8` as well:
`scripts/check_tan_docs_surface.py:511` ("PYTHONIOENCODING"). A new test runs
a `tan` stub that prints the Rich table through its default stdout while the
gate inherits `PYTHONIOENCODING=cp1252`. Without the override the stub crashes:
`tests/scripts/test_check_tan_docs_surface.py:364`
("def test_tan_child_is_told_to_write_utf8").

`IMPLICIT_ENCODING_BASELINE` shrank from 85 to 2 files
(`scripts/check_cross_platform.py`, "IMPLICIT_ENCODING_BASELINE: frozenset" —
removed when #2197 finished the drain). The size pin moved with it
(`tests/scripts/test_check_cross_platform.py`, "IMPLICIT_ENCODING_BASELINE) <= 2"
— the pin was removed too when #2197 finished the drain; the test itself
survives as a plain zero-findings check). The baselined finding count dropped
from 316 to 9 -- the last 2 files are drained, and the baseline machinery
itself retired, in `changelog.d/2197-retire-encoding-baseline.md`.

**Measured: the child's encoding now wins over the caller's locale.** The 113
test files that are touched here, or that run a changed script, were run with
`PYTHONIOENCODING=cp1252` and then with `PYTHONIOENCODING=ascii` set in the
pytest environment. Before this change, every child inherited that setting:

- under `cp1252`, 64 tests failed (68 counting subtests) with
  `UnicodeDecodeError: 'utf-8' codec can't decode byte 0xb7` (or `0xa7`),
  because the child wrote `·` or `§` as cp1252;
- under `ascii`, 28 tests failed (43 counting subtests) with
  `UnicodeEncodeError: 'ascii' codec can't encode character '\xa7'` inside the
  child.

Both runs now pass all 2105 tests. The largest group is
`tests/scripts/test_check_template_catalog.py:27` ("PYTHONIOENCODING"), with 17
failures under `cp1252`.

Six calls whose child is not Python today also set `PYTHONIOENCODING`, because
the command they run belongs to the project or the bench and may call Python
later. These are the J-Link command in `swd_probe.py` (the `JLINK_EXE`
override can be a wrapper script), `pwsh bootstrap.ps1`, `test-all.sh --help`,
two `bench-env.sh` runs through the shared `_sanitized_env()` helper, and
`git worktree add` on the real checkout, which runs the local `post-checkout`
hook. The variable has no effect on a child that is not Python.
