### Fixed — AEN803 example overlays had drifted from their AEN801 siblings, re-enabling SD against the 2626-R2 mux; content-parity and stranded-overlay gates now catch it (#2198)

`df628b6ab` (#2176) backfilled every AEN801 example overlay to AEN803 by
copy. Three AEN801 fixes merged after it and never reached the copies, so
four AEN803 overlays now take the AEN801 content, SKU name aside:

- **`aen-evk-demo` — `sdhc0` disabled, the hazard half.** The AEN803 file
  still declared its own `sdhc0: sdhc@48102000` with `status = "okay"` and
  `pinctrl-0 = <&pinctrl_sdmmc>`. The 74LVC157 SDIO mux (U38/U39) has no
  Hi-Z state and holds `E1M_CLK`, `E1M_CMD`, `E1M_D3..D0` and
  `E1M_SDIO_RST` low whenever powered, so `sdhc_dwc_init()` starting the
  400 kHz ID clock at `POST_KERNEL` would fight it before `main()` runs —
  the contention #2051 removed from the AEN801 file. No AEN803 module has
  run that overlay in a 2626-R2 carrier, so the fight is inferred from
  #2051, not measured. Now
  `examples/aen/aen-evk-demo/boards/alp_e1m_aen803_m55_he_ae822fa0e5597ls0_rtss_he.overlay:485` ("&sdhc0 {")
  keeps it disabled with #2051's rationale, and the `pinctrl_sdmmc` state is
  gone because nothing applies it any more.
- **`aen-evk-demo` + `aen-pdm-mic-alif` — MP34DT05TR-A PDM clock bounds
  (#2133).** `clk-frequency-min = <1200000>` / `clk-frequency-max =
  <3250000>` at
  `examples/aen/aen-evk-demo/boards/alp_e1m_aen803_m55_he_ae822fa0e5597ls0_rtss_he.overlay:838` ("clk-frequency-min = <1200000>;")
  and
  `examples/aen/aen-pdm-mic-alif/boards/alp_e1m_aen803_m55_he_ae822fa0e5597ls0_rtss_he.overlay:68` ("clk-frequency-min = <1200000>;"),
  so an out-of-spec mic clock fails `alp_audio_in_open()` with `-EINVAL`
  on AEN803 instead of silently under-clocking the mic.
- **`aen-qenc-readout` — the AEN803 target did not compile (#2104).** Its
  overlay lacked the `gpio-qdec` node now at
  `examples/aen/aen-qenc-readout/boards/alp_e1m_aen803_m55_he_ae822fa0e5597ls0_rtss_he.overlay:170` ("qdec_sw: qdec-sw {"),
  the `&gpio3` enable and two binding includes, while
  `examples/aen/aen-qenc-readout/src/main.c:211` ("INPUT_CALLBACK_DEFINE(DEVICE_DT_GET(DT_NODELABEL(qdec_sw))")
  references that node unconditionally. Building `dc12826a1` (the `dev`
  this branch is cut from) for `alp_e1m_aen803_m55_he/ae822fa0e5597ls0/rtss_he`
  fails with `'__device_dts_ord_DT_N_NODELABEL_qdec_sw_ORD' undeclared`.
- **`aen-sdhc-probe` — stranded overlay moved.** #2051 renamed
  `aen-sdcard-readout` to `aen-sdhc-probe` while #2176 was adding
  `examples/aen/aen-sdcard-readout/boards/alp_e1m_aen803_m55_he_ae822fa0e5597ls0_rtss_he.overlay`;
  both merged, leaving that file alone in a directory with no app, still
  enabling `sdhc0`. It is deleted, and `aen-sdhc-probe` gets the AEN803
  copy of its own overlay, `sdhc0` disabled at
  `examples/aen/aen-sdhc-probe/boards/alp_e1m_aen803_m55_he_ae822fa0e5597ls0_rtss_he.overlay:56` ("&sdhc0 {").

**`aen-ospi-regcheck` now covers E1M-AEN803 too.** #2176 left it out,
because its pass/fail might have assumed a floating OSPI0 bus that stops
floating on AEN803, where the HyperRAM (SS0) and NOR (SS1) are fitted. The
app does no device I/O at all. It binds the node, checks the rc of
`alif_hal_ospi_initialize()` and reads `CTRLR0` back against its reset
value, `examples/aen/aen-ospi-regcheck/src/main.c:165` ("#define OSPI_CTRLR0_RESET_VALUE 0x00C00407U").
It sends no transfer, pulses no reset on `P15_6`/`P15_7`, enables no XIP and
writes nothing. It has also already run on AEN803 silicon:
`docs/verification-status.md:479` ("Bench-verified 2026-09-13 on two E1M-AEN803 modules")
records serial `2026W36-0001` and serial `2026W36-0002` giving
`alif_hal_ospi_initialize() rc=0`, `CTRLR0=0x00c00407` and
`RESULT PASS: OSPI/HexSPI node BINDS` through the AEN801 board target. The
AEN803 overlay is the AEN801 one with the SKU changed, and
`alp_e1m_aen803_m55_he/ae822fa0e5597ls0/rtss_he` is in `platform_allow`.
The app's `CMakeLists.txt` no longer pins the AEN801 overlay with
`DTC_OVERLAY_FILE`. That pin would have handed the AEN801 file to the
AEN803 build; Zephyr now picks each target's own overlay.

**Six more AEN examples no longer pin the AEN801 overlay.** `aen-aipm-read`,
`aen-isp-regcheck`, `aen-power-iwic`, `aen-se-crypto`, `aen-se-service-info`
and `aen-se-service-query` each set `DTC_OVERLAY_FILE` to the AEN801 overlay
unconditionally, so every build for the AEN803 target applied the AEN801
file and never read its own. The pins date from 2026-06-18, when these
overlays were named `alp_e1m_aen801_m55_he.overlay` and Zephyr's
board-qualified lookup could not find them. #834 renamed the files to the
fully-qualified stem Zephyr does find, but re-pointed the pins instead of
removing them. No app declared an HP target that could have been borrowing
the HE overlay (each declared only
`alp_e1m_aen801_m55_he/ae822fa0e5597ls0/rtss_he`), and each ships an overlay
for both SKUs, so the pins are gone, as at
`examples/aen/aen-aipm-read/CMakeLists.txt:24` ("No DTC_OVERLAY_FILE: Zephyr applies").
`aen-jpeg-regcheck` guarded its pin on `BOARD MATCHES "^alp_e1m_aen801_m55_he"`,
so it was SKU-correct, but its comment pointed at the `aen-isp-regcheck` note
removed here and restated the same stale premise; its pin is removed too.

Every touched AEN803 target builds against this tree: `aen-evk-demo`,
`aen-qenc-readout`, `aen-pdm-mic-alif`, `aen-sdhc-probe`, `aen-ospi-regcheck`
and the seven un-pinned apps. So does every target those apps declare: the
AEN801 HE target of all eight CMake-touched apps, and `native_sim/native/64`
for `aen-jpeg-regcheck`, which reads no board overlay. Each generated
`zephyr.dts` names exactly one overlay as its source, the one for its own
SKU. Nothing here has run on hardware.

**CI now builds twelve of these apps for AEN803.** Every bench EVK carries an
E1M-AEN803 by the maintainer's account, recorded at
`metadata/e1m_modules/E1M-AEN803.yaml:203` ("so it rests on the maintainer's word").
The SKU cannot be read from silicon, because both SKUs use the same part.
Until now the AEN803 bench runs on record were built for the AEN801 target
anyway. `aen-ospi-regcheck`, the seven un-pinned apps and the four whose
AEN803 overlays this change repairs (`aen-evk-demo`, `aen-pdm-mic-alif`,
`aen-qenc-readout`, and the `aen-sdhc-probe` base scenario) now declare
`alp_e1m_aen803_m55_he/ae822fa0e5597ls0/rtss_he` next to their AEN801 target,
as at `examples/aen/aen-aipm-read/testcase.yaml:23` ("alp_e1m_aen803_m55_he/ae822fa0e5597ls0/rtss_he").
`pr-twister-aen.yml` already hands that platform to twister at
`scripts/select_aen_twister.py:65` ("-p alp_{prefix}{cpu}/ae822fa0e5597ls0/{soc}"),
but twister builds a scenario there only if its `platform_allow` names it, so
until now CI never compiled these AEN803 overlays. A twister `--dry-run` over
`examples/aen` now selects 14 AEN803 scenarios: these twelve on the HE target
plus `aen-adc-regcheck`'s existing HE and HP ones. All are
`build_only: true`. The AEN803 board has no simulator and no workflow runs
device tests, so CI compiles them and runs nothing. The workflow's own
comments now say so. Each app's `sample.description` now names both SKUs.

The other 50 AEN scenarios that ship an AEN803 overlay but declare only the
AEN801 target are not extended here, because the job's time budget cannot
absorb them. The twister step took 697–1220 s across the last eight runs, at
about 80 builds, against its then 30-minute cap (raised to 36 minutes by
#2541) at `.github/workflows/pr-twister-aen.yml:579` ("70s under the old 30min cap").
This change takes it to 92 builds. Adding the other 50 takes it to about 140
and, scaled linearly, a worst case near 2,100 s, past the cap. #2209 splits
the job per SKU first. Two more scenarios, `aen-sdhc-probe`'s
`.sdhc_build_coverage` and `aen-ethernet-link`'s `.mdio_managed`, list the
AEN801 overlay in `extra_dtc_overlay_files`, so an AEN803 entry there would
build the AEN801 file for AEN803. Each needs its own AEN803 twin instead.

**New gate — `scripts/check_example_board_overlay_content_parity.py`.**
`check_example_board_overlay_parity.py` checks that an overlay exists for
each target, not what it says, so it passed throughout. The new gate diffs
every pair of `examples/**/boards/alp_e1m_<sku>_*` files that differ only by
SKU, where both SoM presets declare the same `family` and `silicon_variant`:
today that means E1M-AEN801/803, E1M-V2N101/102 and E1M-V2M101/102, and 82
pairs. Comments are stripped first, because a bench result measured on one
SKU is not a claim about the other. Kconfig's `# CONFIG_FOO is not set` is
kept, because it is an assignment. Each file's own SKU name is normalised,
and only its own, so an AEN803 overlay still naming `aen801` in real content
fails:
`scripts/check_example_board_overlay_content_parity.py:155` ("re.sub(re.escape(sku)").
A SKU with no preset is an error rather than a skip, so a moved preset cannot
leave the gate passing on zero pairs. Any remaining line fails unless it is
listed in
`scripts/check_example_board_overlay_content_parity.py:103` ("ALLOWED_DELTAS: dict[tuple[str, str], str] = {}"),
which is empty: those SKUs differ only by BOM population (E1M-AEN803's
OSPI0 HyperRAM + NOR), and the one paired overlay that touches OSPI0 is
controller-only. Run on `origin/dev`, it flags exactly the `aen-evk-demo`,
`aen-pdm-mic-alif` and `aen-qenc-readout` pairs.

The same gate also fails an app `CMakeLists.txt` that names one SKU's paired
file outside an `if()` whose condition names that SKU, at
`scripts/check_example_board_overlay_content_parity.py:208` ("def _pin_problems(root: Path"),
because the sibling SKU's build would read that file instead of its own. Run
on the tree before the six pins were removed, it flags exactly those six. Only
a positive `BOARD MATCHES` or `STREQUAL` on one literal naming the SKU counts
as a guard. `NOT`, `AND`/`OR`, a `|` alternation, `else()`, or an `elseif()`
on anything else fails closed. The same check covers twister: a scenario whose
`extra_dtc_overlay_files`, `extra_conf_files`, `extra_overlay_confs` or
`extra_args` names one SKU's file while its `platform_allow` reaches the
sibling SKU fails, at
`scripts/check_example_board_overlay_content_parity.py:256` ("def _testcase_pin_problems(root: Path").
Adding the AEN803 target to `aen-sdhc-probe`'s `.sdhc_build_coverage` now
fails it. The check does not see a pin reached through an `include()`d
`.cmake` file, a filename built from variables, or `file(GLOB)`.

Twenty-two AEN app `CMakeLists.txt` headers told users to build with
`-DEXTRA_DTC_OVERLAY_FILE=<this-dir>/boards/alp_e1m_aen801_…overlay`. On an
AEN803 build that layers the AEN801 file over the AEN803 one. The instruction
is replaced with a note that Zephyr applies
`boards/<fully-qualified-board>.overlay` by itself.

**Stranded `boards/` directories now fail CI.** Closes #2207.
`check_example_board_overlay_parity.py` also fails any `examples/**/boards/`
directory whose parent holds no `CMakeLists.txt`, at
`scripts/check_example_board_overlay_parity.py:543` ("def _stranded_boards_dir_problems(root: Path)").
That is the class the `aen-sdcard-readout` file above belonged to. Neither gate
could see that file: it had no build target and no SKU sibling. Only
git-tracked files count, so a local `west build` inside an example is not
reported. `<app>/sysbuild/<image>/boards/`, sysbuild's per-image
configuration directory, is accepted when `<app>/CMakeLists.txt` exists.

### Changed — the CDC200 framebuffer comes from a devicetree `memory-region`, not a fork linker section or a fixed address (#2199)

`display_cdc200.c` placed its layer framebuffers in the Alif fork's
`__alif_sram0_section` / `__alif_ns_section` linker sections, which upstream
Zephyr's link script does not have, or, under `-DNO_RELOCATE_SRAM0`, at the
hardcoded `0x02000000` / `0x02177000`. `aen-dsi-display` had to build with
`-DNO_RELOCATE_SRAM0`.

The `tes,cdc-2.1` binding now has a `memory-region` phandle. Layer 1's
framebuffer is that node's reg base; layer 2's, when `enable-l2` is set, follows
it, rounded up to 64 bytes. The driver `BUILD_ASSERT`s that the property exists
and that the region covers every enabled layer. It is a plain pointer, not a
linker section, so the 1.8 MB framebuffer is not loaded into an ITCM RAM-run
`.bin`. The data-cache flush after each framebuffer write is unchanged.
`CONFIG_FB_USES_DTCM_REGION` now only means the region is a CPU-local DTCM
address that needs `local_to_global()`. The property is not `required:` in the
binding so a bind-only node stays valid; the driver enforces it.

### Added — any app on an E1M-AEN SoM can drive the E1M-EVK's RK055HDMIPI4MA0 panel with one shield (#2199)

The Alif E8 display chain (CDC200 -> DesignWare MIPI-DSI host -> D-PHY -> the
upstream `himax,hx8394` driver) used to exist only inside
`examples/aen/aen-dsi-display`: its overlay defined the SoC nodes, and its
`src/main.c` did the SoC clock/power setup. It is now split so an app gets the
whole chain by adding a shield; the shield defaults `CONFIG_ALP_SDK=y` itself
(#2204's follow-up), because the Alif display-driver symbols live under
`if ALP_SDK` and are unreachable without it:

- **SoC nodes.** `zephyr/dts/alif/ensemble_e8_peripherals.dtsi` declares
  `cdc200: cdc200@49031000` (`tes,cdc-2.1`) and `mipi_dsi: mipi-dsi@49032000`
  (`snps,designware-dsi`), `status = "disabled"`, with SoC facts only: reg, the
  ten CDC IRQs 333..342 and DSI IRQ 343 with their names, the re-authored
  `ALIF_DPI_CLK` / `ALIF_DSI_CLK` / `ALIF_CDC200_PIX_SYST_ACLK` clocks,
  `cdc-if = <&cdc200>`, `phy-if = <&dphy 1>`, `dpi-shutdn-active`,
  `dpi-colorm-active`, `ecc-recv-en` and `crc-recv-en`. No `frame-ack-en` and no
  panel timings, layers or framebuffer. The `tes,cdc-2.1` timing properties stay
  `required:`; edtlib enforces that only on `okay` nodes.
- **D-PHY clocks.** The shared `&dphy` node's `pllref-clk` / `pllbypass-clk` /
  `tx-dphy-clk` are now the real `ALIF_MIPI_PLLREF_CLK` / `ALIF_MIPI_BYPASS_CLK` /
  `ALIF_MIPI_TXDPHY_CLK` (`MIPI_CKEN` bits 8 / 12 / 0) instead of the
  `ALIF_CSI_DPHY_CLK` placeholder, which made `dphy_dw_master_setup()` stall the
  AXI on unclocked config registers. `rx-dphy-clk` (camera RX) stays on the
  placeholder. This applies to every build with `dphy` okay, not only the
  display: `dphy_dw_init()` now turns on the real PLL-reference gate
  (`MIPI_CKEN` bit 8) at boot, and `dphy_dw_slave_setup()` the real bypass gate
  (bit 12) for a D-PHY id other than 0 -- including `aen-camera-regcheck` and
  `aen-dsi-regcheck`.
- **SoC glue.** `zephyr/soc-bridge/alif/mipi_display_e8.c`
  (ADR-0017-ADJACENT: a register sequence from the Alif DFP / DevKit, not a HAL
  consumer), built on E8 with `CONFIG_MIPI_DPHY_DW`, `CONFIG_MIPI_DSI_DW` or
  `CONFIG_DISPLAY_CDC200`, does what no driver does, each hook gated on its DT
  node:
  - at `PRE_KERNEL_1`, when `dphy` is okay, it enables the D-PHY clock sources
    (CGU `CLK_ENA` +0x14 bits 21 and 23: HFOSC 38.4 MHz and the 100 MHz CFG
    clock) and D-PHY analog power (VBAT `PWR_CTRL` +0x08: clears bits
    0/1/4/5/8/9/12). A CSI-camera build gets this too;
  - at `POST_KERNEL` `CONFIG_KERNEL_INIT_PRIORITY_DEFAULT`, BUILD_ASSERTed below
    both `CONFIG_DISPLAY_INIT_PRIORITY` and `CONFIG_MIPI_DSI_INIT_PRIORITY`, it
    sets `CDC200_PIXCLK_CTRL` (`CLKCTL_PER_MST` +0x04) bits [24:16] to
    `SYST_ACLK / cdc200 clock-frequency`, keeping the other bits. A
    `clock-frequency` that is not SYST_ACLK over an integer divider in 2..511 is
    a build error, since the DSI host times its lanes from the same property;
  - at `PRE_KERNEL_1`, with the DSI host driver built, it muxes the pad of each
    DSI panel's `bl-gpios` to GPIO with the input receiver on, when that GPIO is
    on a main-domain `snps,designware-gpio` port (gpio0..gpio14); other
    controllers are skipped.

  The CGU, VBAT and `CLKCTL_PER_MST` bases come from the clock controller's
  `reg-names`, the 400 MHz from the `syst_aclk` fixed clock. The pad mux lives
  here because `display_cdc200.c` does not apply its `pinctrl-0` in a MIPI-DSI
  build. The Secure Enclave's aiPM run profile (`run_profile_t.phy_pwr_gating` /
  `ip_clock_gating` in hal_alif `aipm.h`) also manages the D-PHY power and the
  CDC200 / DSI clocks; the glue bypasses it, so a `se_service_set_run_cfg()`
  whose profile lacks those bits may power them down under a running display.
  In-tree only `alp_power_profile_set(RUN)` calls it; not observed.
- **Shield.** `e1m_evk_rk055hdmipi4ma0` (`zephyr/boards/shields/`, found through
  the module's `board_root`) sets `zephyr,display` and `alp-display0` to
  `&cdc200`; adds the panel-enable `regulator-fixed` on expander P0, the
  `nxp,pca9538` expander at `0x73` on `&i2c2`, a 2 MiB `mmio-sram` framebuffer
  region (`lcd_fb`) at `0x02200000` (a 720x1280 RGB565 layer is 1,843,200 B),
  and the `himax,hx8394`
  panel (reset on expander P1, `bl-gpios` on `&gpio5 5`, 2 lanes, RGB888 DSI
  link with an RGB565 framebuffer layer); and
  turns on `&dphy`, `&cdc200` (timings, `clock-frequency = <40000000>`,
  `memory-region`, layer 1), `&mipi_dsi` (`vid-pkt-size = <720>`) and `&gpio5`.
  It shrinks the SoC `sram0` (also the "SRAM0" linker region) to the bottom
  2 MiB, `reg = <0x02000000 DT_SIZE_M(2)>`, so SRAM0 data reaching the
  framebuffer is a link error rather than a silent overwrite. Its
  `Kconfig.defconfig` defaults on `DISPLAY`, `MIPI_DSI`, `HX8394`, `I2C`, `GPIO`,
  `GPIO_PCA_SERIES`, `REGULATOR`, `REGULATOR_FIXED`, and under `ALP_SDK`
  `MIPI_DPHY`, `MIPI_DPHY_DW`, `MIPI_DSI_DW` and `DISPLAY_CDC200`. No system
  heap is added: none of the chain's drivers allocates from it. The I2C2 pins,
  clock and `alp-i2c0` alias stay with the board devicetree.

`aen-dsi-display` now just appends the shield in `CMakeLists.txt`. Its overlays
shrink to the ITCM RAM-run retarget, `src/main.c` loses
`dphy_clock_power_enable()`, `cdc_pixclk_div_fixup()` and `backlight_on_early()`,
and `prj.conf` drops what the shield provides, including
`CONFIG_GPIO_PCA_SERIES_INIT_PRIORITY=60` and `CONFIG_HEAP_MEM_POOL_SIZE=4096`:
the defaults already order I2C (50), the expander (50, after its bus by
devicetree dependency), the regulator (75), the CDC and DSI host (85) and the
panel (90). Its
`testcase.yaml` now builds both the AEN801 and AEN803 HE targets.
`aen-dsi-regcheck` now enables the SoC nodes instead of declaring its own
copies. `aen-evk-demo` builds with or without the shield: with it, the TCAL9538
at `0x73` belongs to the GPIO driver, so its phase 4 checks for the shield's
`lcd_exp` node and skips its raw register writes (`SKIPPED`), and its phase 12
reports the display it can now open.

Build-verified on E1M-AEN801 and E1M-AEN803. On the bench (E1M-AEN803 2026W36-0009,
2026-09-18) the RAM-run read back the expected registers -- `0x4903F004 =
0x00070001`, CDC L1 framebuffer `0x49031134 = 0x02200000`, backlight level 1,
DSI `INT_ST1 = 0x00000000` over 100 ms of scanout; pixels on glass were not yet
observed.

On 2026-09-21, on the same module (carrier 2626-R2), pixels appeared on glass
for the first time. The root cause was hardware, not software: a jumper was
missing on the RK055HDMIPI4MA0's own daughter board, so that board's DC/DC
never started. The HX8394's logic domain runs off the ungated `+L_VIO`, so it
answered DCS perfectly the whole time while nothing could reach the pixels.
Fitting the jumper produced pixels on the first cold run, and the GT911 touch
controller -- silent for the entire campaign -- answered immediately: `touch :
RESPONDING at 0x14 (alternate) product-id[0x8140] rc=0 data=39 31 31 00`.

### Fixed — the DesignWare D-PHY driver no longer breaks every `CONFIG_LOG=y` build that enables it (#2199)

`zephyr/drivers/mipi_dphy/dphy_dw.c` registers its log module with
`CONFIG_MIPI_DPHY_LOG_LEVEL`, but nothing defined that symbol: upstream Zephyr
has no `mipi_dphy` class to supply it. Any build with the D-PHY enabled and
`CONFIG_LOG=y` stopped with `'CONFIG_MIPI_DPHY_LOG_LEVEL' undeclared`; the
existing D-PHY users (`aen-dsi-display`, the camera and DSI regchecks) all run
with logging off, which hid it. The `aen-evk-demo` + `e1m_evk_rk055hdmipi4ma0`
shield build found it. `zephyr/kconfigs/vendor-alif-peripherals.kconfig` now
defines the log level for `MIPI_DPHY_DW` from Zephyr's standard log-config
template.

### Fixed — `aen-dsi-display` never drove the SoM backlight controller (#2199)

Nothing in `aen-dsi-display` drove the panel backlight, so the glass could not
light whatever state the DSI chain was in. The backlight driver sits on the SoM,
and its enable input is Alif `P5_5`, a SoM-internal signal rather than an E1M
pad. E1M pads A31/B31 `BL_LED_A`/`BL_LED_K` are the driver's LED output, not a
GPIO.

The `himax,hx8394` panel node now carries `bl-gpios = <&gpio5 5 GPIO_ACTIVE_HIGH>`
and `&gpio5` is enabled; both now live in the `e1m_evk_rk055hdmipi4ma0` shield.
`gpio_dw` applies no pad mux, so the Alif E8 display SoC glue
(`zephyr/soc-bridge/alif/mipi_display_e8.c`) muxes the panel's `bl-gpios` pad to
GPIO at `PRE_KERNEL_1`, with the input receiver on so the level reads back. The
upstream panel driver drives `bl-gpios` only at the END of a successful init, so
a dark backlight means the panel init failed; `aen-dsi-display` prints the pin
level after its panel check.

The backlight is on/off at full brightness, not PWM-dimmed: the driver gives
full LED current with its enable held constant high. The enable is driven
straight to a static high and never pulsed, because short low pulses are the
driver IC's serial dimming protocol. Dimming would need an Alif UTIMER `pwm`
driver, which Zephyr does not have.

### Fixed — `aen-dsi-display` drove the LCD control expander at the wrong address and part (#2199)

Both `aen-dsi-display` overlays defined `lcd_exp` as `gpio@20` / `nxp,pca6408`,
which targets `EVK_I2C_ADDR_TCA6408A_MAIN` in `metadata/boards/e1m-evk.yaml` -- a
part the metadata marks `assembled: false` on this EVK revision. The example never
picked up the U35 address correction from alp-sdk#1974.

`lcd_exp` is now `gpio@73`, `reg = <0x73>` (in the `e1m_evk_rk055hdmipi4ma0`
shield, which replaces the example's own overlay wiring): the assembled U35,
`EVK_I2C_ADDR_TCAL9538_MAIN`. The compatible is `nxp,pca9538`, not `nxp,pcal9538`.
Both bind `gpio_pca_series.c` under `CONFIG_GPIO_PCA_SERIES=y`, but
`pcal9538` is the TYPE_2 variant whose init also writes the Agile-IO block at
`0x40`..`0x45`, which is untested on this part. `nxp,pca9538` stays on the TYPE_0
base registers that #1974 read back at POR. The P0/P1 assignments (panel power
enable / HX8394 reset) are unchanged.

The example also stops pulsing Alif `P10_2` as an "expander reset". That pin came
from a naming mix-up: the EVK's `IO_EXP_RST` is E1M pad N1 =
Alif `P3_6` (`metadata/pinmux/aen.yaml`), and pulsing even that line changed
nothing on 2 of 2 boards. U35 answers at POR without any reset action, so the hook
and its `&gpio10` enable are removed.

### Fixed — the CDC200 -> MIPI-DSI display chain never started its scanout (#2199)

On the Alif E8 display chain, `display_blanking_off()` on the `tes,cdc-2.1`
display now starts the pixel stream. Before this fix, every stage of
`aen-dsi-display` reported READY and `display_write()` returned 0, but the pixels
never left the SRAM0 framebuffer. Three things kept the scanout off:

- `dsi_dw_set_mode()` had no callers, so the DSI host stayed in the command mode
  that `dsi_dw_attach()` leaves it in;
- `cdc200_set_enable()` had no callers, so `CDC_EN` was never set;
- `cdc200_blanking_off()` / `cdc200_blanking_on()` returned `-ENOTSUP`.

`cdc200_blanking_off()` now switches the DesignWare DSI host whose `cdc-if` names
this CDC to video mode, then sets `CDC_EN`. `cdc200_blanking_on()` does the
reverse, in reverse order, so the DSI host is reset only after the CDC has been
told to stop feeding it. Whether `CDC_EN=0` stops at the end of the frame is not
verified, so the last frame may still be cut. The panel's init sequence still runs in command mode first:
in DW video mode, commands only leave during DPI blanking, and there is none
before `CDC_EN`. With no DSI host, blanking is just `CDC_EN`, for a parallel-RGB
panel.

Two `dsi_dw.c` defects that only video mode exposes are fixed too.
`dsi_dw_set_mode()` now records `curr_mode` when switching back to command mode;
without that, a blanking on/off cycle never re-entered video. `dsi_dw_msg_config()`
no longer clears `PHY_TXREQUESTCLKHS` for an LP command while in video mode,
which would have stopped the HS clock under the running scanout.

`dsi_dw_attach()` also stops trusting `mdev->timings`. It used the `cdc-if`
controller's timings only when the panel driver passed `hactive == 0`, but the
upstream `himax,hx8394` driver leaves `mdev->timings` uninitialized on its stack.
So the D-PHY lane rate, the DPI line/frame registers and the LP-command windows
were computed from stack contents: the same code gave different
`DSI_DPI_LP_CMD_TIM` / `DSI_PHY_TMR_RD_CFG` values on two builds. The host packs
exactly the DPI stream the CDC generates, so it now always programs the `cdc-if`
timings.

The DSI host now takes the DPI pixel clock from the `cdc-if` controller's
`clock-frequency` instead of assuming 60 Hz. The example ran its CDC at 400/6 =
66.67 MHz into a host timed for 59.98 MHz, so the DPI payload FIFO overflowed on
every line (`INT_ST1` `DPI_PLD_WR_ERR`). The `cdc200` node now declares the rate
the CDC really runs, 400/10 = 40 MHz (`clock-frequency = <40000000>`, in the
`e1m_evk_rk055hdmipi4ma0` shield; `90d450387` moved it here from 400/7 =
57.142857 MHz), and the SoC glue derives the CDC divider from that same
property, so the two can no longer disagree. 66.67 MHz would need about
539 Mbps per lane, above the host's default 500 Mbps `panel-max-lane-bandwidth`.

`dw_setup_timeout()` no longer truncates the non-burst HS-TX timeout. A 720x1280
frame (about 1.1M lane-byte clocks) does not fit the 16-bit `HSTX_TO_CNT` at the
fixed timeout-clock divider of 10, and the truncated count was about 8 ms, so
`TO_HS_TX` fired inside every ~17 ms frame. The divider now widens until the
count fits.

The host's DSI mode now starts as command mode, which is where it comes out of
reset, and returning to command mode drops the HS clock request that video mode
set.

`dsi_dw_set_mode()` now returns `-ENODEV` until `dsi_dw_attach()` has succeeded,
so `display_blanking_off()` can no longer report success on a host that was
never configured. `cdc200_set_enable()` is removed: it toggled `CDC_EN` without
the DSI mode and had no callers.

The display chain no longer requests a peripheral ACK at the end of every frame
(`frame-ack-en`; neither the SoC `mipi_dsi` node nor the shield sets it). The upstream RK055 setup does not use it, and a frame whose ACK
never comes stalls the host in LP receive long enough to overflow the DPI
payload FIFO.

### Fixed — the DesignWare DSI host serialises attach, transfer and mode switches, and exposes its mode API in a public header (#2199)

`dsi_dw_attach()`, `dsi_dw_transfer()` and `dsi_dw_set_mode()` touched the same
host registers with no lock, so a panel driver's DCS traffic could interleave
with a display blanking mode switch. `struct dsi_dw_data` now carries a
`k_mutex`, initialised in `dsi_dw_init()`, that all three take.

`enum dsi_dw_mode` and `dsi_dw_set_mode()` move to the devicetree-independent
public header `<zephyr/drivers/mipi_dsi/dsi_dw.h>` (`zephyr/include/`, the path
the Alif fork included but never shipped). `display_cdc200.c` includes it
instead of the driver's private `../mipi_dsi/dsi_dw.h`, whose
`struct dsi_dw_config` layout depends on the including driver's `DT_DRV_COMPAT`.

### Known behaviour — the RK055HDMIPI4MA0 panel's first init stalls on a variable fraction of boots; the shipped retry recovers it (#2199)

On a variable fraction of boots of the `e1m_evk_rk055hdmipi4ma0` shield at the shipped 40 MHz / RGB888-link setting, the first `hx8394_init()` returns `-EIO` because one DCS write stalls in the DSI host's command FIFO. The SDK retries the init before `main()` (`src/zephyr/panel_init_retry.c`, up to five retries, recorded in `2199-panel-init-retry.md`), so an app gets a working panel with no code of its own; `examples/aen/aen-dsi-display` prints a one-line pointer to this issue if all attempts fail.

The signature, in the diagnostic's shipped form (`zephyr/drivers/mipi_dsi/dsi_dw.c`, `dsi_dw_log_fifo_stall()`) -- grep a build for `Failed to write command FIFO`:

```
E: Failed to write command FIFO (header=0x%08x CMD_PKT_STATUS=0x%08x PHY_STATUS=0x%08x).
E: PWR_UP=0x%08x CLKMGR_CFG=0x%08x MODE_CFG=0x%08x CMD_MODE_CFG=0x%08x LPCLK_CTRL=0x%08x
```

Measured on `E1M-AEN803 2026W36-0009`, with the earlier one-line message that had no `header=`, `CLKMGR_CFG=` or `LPCLK_CTRL=`: `CMD_PKT_STATUS=0x00040015`, `PHY_STATUS=0x000015bd`, `PWR_UP=0x00000001`, `MODE_CFG=0x00000001`, `CMD_MODE_CFG=0x010f7f00`, all lanes in Stop and no interrupt latched (`GEN_BUFF_CMD_EMPTY`, bit 16, parked at 0 while bits 0, 2 and 18 are set): the payload path drained and only the command buffer did not. A rarer stall also hits the first DCS read after `display_write`.

Rates without the retry, same module; the rate is not stable (it varies between sessions and drifts within one), so each figure is a sample: 6 of 15 cold boots reached READY, then 9 of 16 in a later session (RGB565 framebuffer 6/8, RGB888 3/8, failures clustered late in the session and hitting both builds). A 16-bit-link 57.142857 MHz config tried for 60 Hz is worse, 5/10 init stalls against 1/10 at 40 MHz in the same session, and adds read stalls; it is not shipped (the shield overlay's header comment has the reason).

With the retry, on `2026W36-0002`: `RESULT PASS` 5 of 5 RAM-runs over a resident app that had already initialised the panel, the worst needing attempt 4 (attempts 1-3 returned `-5`). That is the residual: no failure in 5 runs; the rate is not characterised beyond that.

### Fixed — the RK055HDMIPI4MA0 panel was powered with its reset line floating (#2199)

On the `e1m_evk_rk055hdmipi4ma0` shield, nothing defined the HX8394 `RESX` level
between the panel-control expander coming up and the panel driver's reset pulse.
The TCAL9538 at `0x73` leaves its own reset with every pin an input, and
`gpio_pca_series_init()` only restores that POR state (`OUTPUT=0xff`,
`CONFIG=0xff`), so expander `P1` stayed high-impedance from
`CONFIG_GPIO_PCA_SERIES_INIT_PRIORITY` (50) until the `hx8394` driver configured
it at `CONFIG_APPLICATION_INIT_PRIORITY` (90) — while
`CONFIG_REGULATOR_FIXED_INIT_PRIORITY` (75) turned the panel supply on in
between. The panel therefore saw its supply ramp against an undefined reset
level. That was the leading suspect for the intermittent whole-panel DCS
silence per cold cycle on `E1M-AEN803 2026W36-0009` (two cold cycles of the
same ELF gave all 11 DCS reads `rc=-5` in one and eight of 11 answering in the
other), but a marginal FFC contact found later on the same board produced the
same all-`rc=-5` signature. The hog is a reset-ordering fix in its own right;
it is not shown to explain that silence.

The shield now hogs that pin low as soon as the expander exists:
`zephyr/boards/shields/e1m_evk_rk055hdmipi4ma0/e1m_evk_rk055hdmipi4ma0.overlay:214`
("lcd_reset_hog: lcd-reset-hog {") with `output-low` and `GPIO_ACTIVE_HIGH`, so
`gpio_hogs_init()` drives the expander pin physically low — `RESX` asserted —
before the regulator runs. Upstream's hog priority default of 41 is below the
expander, where `gpio_hogs_init()` would find the port not ready and configure
nothing, so
`zephyr/boards/shields/e1m_evk_rk055hdmipi4ma0/Kconfig.defconfig:53`
("config GPIO_HOGS_INIT_PRIORITY") pins it to 60, strictly inside the 50..75
window. Zephyr hogs only call `gpio_pin_configure()` and claim nothing, so the
`hx8394` driver re-configuring and pulsing the same pin at 90 is unchanged, and
the driver itself is untouched.

No `startup-delay-us` was added to the `lcd_pwr_en` regulator: Zephyr 4.4.1
applies that property only on the `regulator_enable()` path inside
`regulator_common_init()`, and a `regulator-fixed` with
`regulator-boot-on`/`regulator-always-on` passes `is_enabled=true` and takes the
refcount-only arm instead, so the property would never be read. The settle before
`RESX` is released stays the `hx8394` driver's own 1 ms VCC-to-RESX-valid wait
plus its 1 ms reset-low hold.

`dsi_dw_send_max_return_packet_size()` built the maximum-return-packet-size
header's high byte as `(uint8_t) value >> 8`, where the cast binds first and the
result is therefore always 0 — any size above 255 was silently truncated. It is
now `zephyr/drivers/mipi_dsi/dsi_dw.c:1415` ("(value >> 8) & 0xff);"). No in-tree caller
asks for 256 bytes or more, so this changes no current behaviour.

### Fixed — DCS reads of more than one byte timed out, and the video pattern generator was never armed (#2199)

Fixes to the DesignWare MIPI-DSI host, found bringing the RK055HDMIPI4MA0
panel up on the E1M-EVK, plus a command-FIFO stall diagnostic.

**`MAX_RD_TIME` was sized from the video LP-command window, so the DCS read
timeout moved with the pixel clock.** The driver computed it only from the
DesignWare constraint `[MAX_RD_TIME] * LANEBYTECLK_period < [OUTVACT_LPCMD_TIME]
* 16 * TXCLKESC_period`, which is an *upper* bound and only applies to reads
issued during active video. `MAX_RD_TIME` also has a *lower* bound that formula
ignores — how long the peripheral actually takes to answer — so the timeout was
effectively derived from the line time, not the read. On the same panel and
driver, differing only in pixel clock, the computed register value moves with
it: RGB888/40 MHz gives a 60.0 MHz lane byte clock and `rdtime` = 949 (a
15.8 µs budget); RGB565/57.142857 MHz gives a 57.1 MHz lane byte clock and
`rdtime` = 591 (a 10.3 µs budget). The value is now floored at what a
read needs — a long response (4-byte header + payload + 2-byte CRC) plus BTA
turnaround and LPDT entry/exit, with margin — and clamped to the register width
`zephyr/drivers/mipi_dsi/dsi_dw.c:444` ("if (outvact > 0) {"). Reads are issued
in command mode, where there is no video LP window to fit inside, so raising it
past the video-derived value costs nothing there.

This is a correctness fix on its own terms, and it is not what closed the
"reads of more than one byte never answer" behaviour seen on
`E1M-AEN803 2026W36-0009` — that symptom was never a MAX_RD_TIME problem.
With the floor in place, `rdtime` went from `0x24f` (591) to `0x00000a00`
(2560) as intended, but `RDDID` (3 bytes), `RDDST` (4) and `RDDDB` (5) still
returned `rc=-5` (`INT_ST1` bit 1, `TO_LP_RX`) while 1- and 2-byte reads kept
working — across four bench runs, 100% correlated with the pixel clock
(failing at RGB565/57.142857 MHz, answering at RGB888/40 MHz). That
correlation was confounded: a marginal FFC contact on the panel flex was
corrupting the DCS read path for the whole campaign, and every one of those
runs was measured through it. Before a connector reseat, every DCS read
returned `rc=-5` with `int1=0x00000002` (`TO_LP_RX`) and `SETEXTC` did not
land at all. After the reseat, on the same build, `SETEXTC` gates as expected,
and `RDDID` returns `rc=3 data=83 94 0f`, `RDDPM=1c`, `RDDST=80 73 04 00` —
3-, 4- and 5-byte reads now answer correctly at BOTH pixel clocks. The
short-versus-long-read-response boundary the failures had fallen on was a
property of what a bad LP-RX turnaround corrupts, not a MIPI protocol limit or
this timeout.

What actually distinguishes the two pixel clocks now is not reads at all. A
controlled A/B on the same board and the same (good) contact state, 100 ms of
scanout each: RGB888/40 MHz gives `int0=0x00000000 int1=0x00000000
dpi-wr-err=0 dpi-under=0 pixclk-ctrl=0x000a0001`, with pixels on glass;
RGB565/57.142857 MHz gives `int0=0x00000000 int1=0x00000080 dpi-wr-err=1
dpi-under=0 pixclk-ctrl=0x00070001`, still set after 5 s of video, with glass
dark. `INT_ST1` bit 7 is `DSI_INT_1_DPI_PLD_WR_ERR`
`zephyr/drivers/mipi_dsi/dsi_dw.h:379` ("#define  DSI_INT_1_DPI_PLD_WR_ERR		BIT(7)"):
the DPI payload FIFO overflows continuously at the higher pixel clock. That
overflow, not a DCS read timeout, is why the shield stays at 40 MHz. It is a
link-bandwidth limit, not a host defect: the A/B changed only the CDC layer to
RGB565, and the layer format never reaches the link, which runs at the panel's
`pixel-format` (RGB888). 57.142857 MHz at 24 bpp needs about 690 Mbps per
lane, the host clamps to the 500 Mbps `panel-max-lane-bandwidth`, and the line
then comes out at 762 * 62.5 / 57.142857 = 833 lane-byte clocks -- the
`hline` the host programmed -- against about 1086 of payload. A 16-bit link
(panel `pixel-format = <MIPI_DSI_PIXFMT_RGB565>`) would need about 462 Mbps
per lane; it has not been tried on a powered panel.

The same clamp fixes an underflow: `outvact` is signed and has had the
LPDT-entry delay subtracted, so on a short line it can go negative, and the old
expression assigned that straight into a `uint32_t` — producing a *huge*
`MAX_RD_TIME` rather than a small one.

**`VPG_EN` was set at the end of attach, which cannot work.** `dsi_dw_attach()`
deliberately ends in command mode, and the later switch to video in
`dsi_dw_set_mode()` power-cycles the host, clearing the bit. The pattern
generator is now armed in `dsi_dw_video_mode_config()`
`zephyr/drivers/mipi_dsi/dsi_dw.c:969` ("switch (config->dpi.vpg_pattern) {"),
where it survives. Any VPG result taken before this change is void.

**A board can now declare the video mode and EoTp its panel needs.** A panel
driver is supposed to do this, but upstream ones frequently do not: Zephyr's
`himax,hx8394` sets `mdev.mode_flags = MIPI_DSI_MODE_VIDEO` and nothing else, so
burst and EoTp could never reach this host whatever the panel wanted. The new
`dpi-video-mode` and `autoinsert-eotp` properties
`zephyr/dts/bindings/mipi-dsi/snps,designware-dsi.yaml:74` ("dpi-video-mode:")
are ORed into the flags the panel driver supplies, because the board is what
knows which panel is fitted. CRC and ECC reception are now driven by their
devicetree properties instead of being forced on; `BTA_EN` stays forced, since
it gates bus turnaround for DCS reads and is unrelated to `frame-ack-en`.

`MAX_ESC_CLK` drops from the 20 MHz D-PHY ceiling to 15 MHz. The divider is
integer, so a lane byte clock just above a multiple lands the escape clock
within a few percent of the spec maximum, leaving a peripheral's LP receiver no
margin; Linux's `dw-mipi-dsi` sizes the same divider against 15 MHz, and
matching it costs only LP command time.

The CDC200 also reloads its shadow registers once the controller is running
`zephyr/drivers/display/display_cdc200.c:507`
("cdc200_shadow_reload_control(DEVICE_MMIO_GET(dev));"). This is belt and
braces, not a fix for a known defect: it was added on the theory that a reload
requested on a stopped CDC does not transfer, and the bench refuted that — the
layer's active registers read back exactly as configured either way.

**Both `Failed to write command FIFO` sites now log `DSI_CMD_PKT_STATUS`,
`DSI_PHY_STATUS`, the parked `DSI_GEN_HDR` value, and five more registers
(`DSI_PWR_UP`, `DSI_CLKMGR_CFG`, `DSI_MODE_CFG`, `DSI_CMD_MODE_CFG`,
`DSI_LPCLK_CTRL`) at the moment of the stall**, since a FIFO that never
drains latches no interrupt and the bare message said nothing about why
`zephyr/drivers/mipi_dsi/dsi_dw.c:1363`
("static void dsi_dw_log_fifo_stall(uintptr_t regs, uint32_t pkt_status, uint32_t header)").
`PHY_LOCK`, `PHY_DIRECTION`, and the clock/lane-0/lane-1 stop-state bits each
narrow the stall to a different signature — a lost PLL, a stuck bus
turnaround, or a lane that never returned to LP-11.  The five extra
registers are a hypothesis aid, not proof: the DW config registers accept
writes with `PWR_UP[SHUTDOWNZ]=0`, so a readback that disagrees with what
the driver programmed only suggests a dropped config write while the host
was still in reset. The parked header is the more direct clue: it is the
exact `DSI_GEN_HDR` value the call site just wrote, so it names which packet
is stuck — hx8394's first command is a generic long write (`B9 FF 83 94`,
WC=4), whose payload goes to `DSI_GEN_PLD_DATA` before the header does, so a
parked long-write header with `GEN_BUFF_PLD_EMPTY=1` would point at a
payload-starved handler rather than the header itself. A third command-FIFO
wait, `dsi_dw_transfer_locked()`'s own poll for FIFO space,
`zephyr/drivers/mipi_dsi/dsi_dw.c:1469` ("Timed-out waiting get available Command-FIFO."),
still logs bare — no header write has happened yet at that point in the
call, so there is nothing to report.

Found while chasing an intermittent first-command stall on
`E1M-AEN803 2026W36-0009` (#2199); the extended log narrows a stall to a
signature, it does not say which one is the root cause on this board. A
power-up reorder and a stop-state settle poll were also tried against that
same stall and bench-verified NOT to fix it (20 cold boots); see
`changelog.d/2199-aen-panel-init-intermittent.md` for the numbers and what
else was ruled out.

### Fixed — the E1M EVK HX8394 panel is brought up with retries before `main()` (#2199)

`hx8394_init()` returns `-EIO` when one DCS write stalls in the DSI host's
command FIFO (`Failed to write command FIFO`), on some cold boots and on
every warm re-init of a panel another image already drove. Zephyr never
retries a failed boot-time init, so the panel stayed dead with the backlight
off. The `e1m_evk_rk055hdmipi4ma0` shield now marks `lcd_panel`
`zephyr,deferred-init`, and `src/zephyr/panel_init_retry.c` initialises it
at `APPLICATION` level, before any app's first `display_blanking_off()`:
`device_init()`, then up to five retries that hold RESX low and re-run the
driver's own init (its normal reset pulse and DCS sequence, nothing else --
no OTP writes), then a static-high backlight enable. Every app using the
shield gets it with no code change.

Bench, E1M-AEN803 serial 2026W36-0002, `examples/aen/aen-dsi-display`
M55-HE RAM-run over a resident app that had already initialised the panel:
without the retry, `RESULT FAIL` (`panel init failed`) 4 of 4; with it,
`RESULT PASS` 5 of 5, the worst run logging attempts 1-3 `-> -5` and
success on attempt 4.

### Fixed — `e1m_evk_rk055hdmipi4ma0` shield failed to link with no app Kconfig (#2199)

Zephyr's own `samples/subsys/display/lvgl` and `samples/drivers/display`, built
for `alp_e1m_aen803_m55_he/ae822fa0e5597ls0/rtss_he` with only
`-DSHIELD="e1m_evk_rk055hdmipi4ma0"` and no app-side Kconfig, failed to link:
`undefined reference to '__device_dts_ord_113'` (the `cdc200` node) and
`'__device_dts_ord_114'` (`mipi_dsi`). The Alif CDC200 / DesignWare DSI /
D-PHY driver Kconfig symbols (`DISPLAY_CDC200`, `MIPI_DSI_DW`, `MIPI_DPHY`,
`MIPI_DPHY_DW`) live under `if ALP_SDK` in `zephyr/Kconfig`, and the shield
did not default `ALP_SDK` on -- so without an app explicitly setting
`CONFIG_ALP_SDK=y`, those symbols did not exist at all and the DT nodes they
back never got a device driver, failing at *link* time rather than configure
time.

`zephyr/boards/shields/e1m_evk_rk055hdmipi4ma0/Kconfig.defconfig` now defaults
`CONFIG_ALP_SDK=y` itself (`default y`, not `select`, matching every other
symbol in this file). Setting `CONFIG_ALP_SDK=n` is not a supported way to run
this shield -- it reproduces the exact `__device_dts_ord_113`/`_114` link
failure this fragment describes, since the display-driver symbols live under
`if ALP_SDK` and nothing else provides them. `CONFIG_I2C`, `CONFIG_PINCTRL`
and the rest of the chain's Kconfig were already defaulted by the shield (or
transitively selected once `I2C` is on, in `PINCTRL`'s case) -- `ALP_SDK` was
the one gap. `examples/aen/aen-dsi-display/prj.conf` drops its own
`CONFIG_ALP_SDK=y`, now redundant with the shield's default.

### Fixed — AEN pad map wrongly claimed Alif ownership of the SoM backlight LED pins (#2203)

`metadata/e1m_modules/aen/from-alif.tsv` and the generated
`metadata/pinmux/aen.yaml` carried a row for E1M pad A31 (`BL_LED_A`)
claiming it was Alif-owned, driven by silicon pad `P5_5` / peripheral
`UT2_T1_B`. Per the authoritative SoM netlist, A31 and its partner B31
(`BL_LED_K`, not in the map at all) are the LED output/feedback pair of the
E1M-AEN family's on-module backlight driver — a boost-converter output far
above logic level, reaching the panel through the carrier's display
connector directly from the driver, never through the SoC. `P5_5` is that
driver's enable input, a SoM-internal signal with no route to any E1M edge
pad. Anything consuming the pad map — pin-conflict checking, the generated
pin tables, an app or carrier design following the docs — was told A31 was
a free Alif GPIO/PWM pad, which risked a carrier wiring a logic-level signal
onto the backlight supply.

The A31 row is dropped from `from-alif.tsv`; A31/B31 now claim no Alif (or
other SoC) ownership anywhere in the generated pad map (AEN's pinmux table
drops from 96 to 95 pads, honestly reflecting that neither backlight pin is
silicon-backed). The underlying facts — the backlight driver's enable input
at `P5_5`, and A31/B31 as its LED output/feedback pair — are now recorded in
`metadata/e1m_modules/aen/on-module-links.yaml`, the family's existing home
for on-module wiring facts that don't belong in the edge-pad TSVs, alongside
a note explaining why this entry (unlike its neighbours) documents pads that
DO reach the E1M edge connector.

Found during `aen-dsi-display` (#2199) bring-up, where the backlight is lit
by driving `P5_5` directly rather than through any E1M-pad-derived route.

### Fixed — `i2s_dw` on the Alif E8: a channel "disable" that stops nothing left TX RUNNING with no ISR to drain it, and init never masked `IMR` bit 6 (#2205)

**The silicon fact.** On the Alif E8's `i2s3` (`0x49017000`, a DesignWare I2S
built with TDM support), `TER` bit 0 (`TXCHENX`) and `RER` bit 0 (`RXCHENX`)
cannot be cleared. Measured on E1M-AEN803 serial 2026W36-0002 at a hardware breakpoint just
after the init-time clears, with the block idle (`IER 0x00000F00`,
`IRER`/`ITER`/`CER` `0`), `RER` and `TER` both read `0x00FFFF01`. The E8 SVD
(peripheral `LPI2S`) documents both bits read-only, "always enabled" in the TDM
configuration, with bits 8-23 as the per-slot enables; the E7 SVD has them
read-write and no slot fields. So `i2s_tx_channel_disable()` and
`i2s_rx_channel_disable()` have always been no-ops on the E8. The bench record
is the #2205 row of `docs/test-plan.md`.

**What that broke.** `rx_stream_start()` relied on `i2s_tx_channel_disable()`
to stop a running TX. On the E8 TX kept running in hardware while
`dev_data->dir`, the only field `i2s_dw_isr()` consults, had moved to
`I2S_DIR_RX`, so nothing drained TX's queue. `tx.state` still read
`I2S_STATE_RUNNING`, so the backend never took its ERROR recovery: every later
`write()` waited on the backend's 2-block slab
(`src/backends/i2s/zephyr_drv.c:412` ("k_mem_slab_init(&s->mem_slab, s->slab_buf, block_bytes, 2)"))
until its own timeout, and the stream never came back. The same `dir` field
also stayed on RX after an RX session, so a TX restarted without a fresh
`configure()` was never serviced.

**The fix, in `zephyr/drivers/i2s/i2s_dw.c` and `i2s_dw.h`.** The `&= ~1`
channel-disable calls stay: an ignored write on the E8, real on the E7.

- **A START pre-empts a RUNNING stream of the other direction.** An RX START
  parks a RUNNING TX in `I2S_STATE_ERROR` through `tx_stream_park_keep_clock()`
  (`zephyr/drivers/i2s/i2s_dw.c:649` ("static void tx_stream_park_keep_clock")),
  the exit #2149's queue-empty underrun already took and now shares:
  `ITER.TXEN` cleared, TX interrupts masked, `CER.CLKEN` kept,
  `clk_restart_skip_ok` armed. The next `write()` gets `-EIO`, and the
  backend's existing ERROR→PREPARE→START retry restarts TX on the kept clock
  without reprogramming it. The #2150 phase 1 / #2171 contract holds: the armed
  flag keeps `tx_clock_is_live()` true, so the RX teardown that follows leaves
  `CER.CLKEN` set (`zephyr/drivers/i2s/i2s_dw.c:1246` ("tx_stream_park_keep_clock(&dev_data->tx, dev);")).
  A TX START pre-empts a RUNNING RX the same way, into `I2S_STATE_ERROR`
  through `rx_stream_disable()`
  (`zephyr/drivers/i2s/i2s_dw.c:1374` ("rx_stream_disable(&dev_data->rx, dev);")),
  which keeps `CER.CLKEN` whenever TX's clock is live; a TX START that fails in
  `queue_get()` leaves RX alone. Both run under `irq_lock()` together with the
  `dir` switch, before the new direction's interrupts are unmasked, and the
  RX pre-emption runs before `tx_stream_start()` consumes
  `clk_restart_skip_ok`, so a TX retry that pre-empts RX never gates the clock
  even for an instant.
- **A reader or writer blocked on the pre-empted stream is released with
  `-EIO`.** The backend waits with `SYS_FOREVER_MS`
  (`src/backends/i2s/zephyr_drv.c:427` (".timeout        = SYS_FOREVER_MS,")), and once
  `dir` has moved nothing else would ever give the semaphore. A TX START
  pre-empting RX gives `rx.sem`
  (`zephyr/drivers/i2s/i2s_dw.c:1382` ("k_sem_give(&dev_data->rx.sem);")); the
  woken reader finds the queue empty and returns `-EIO`. Before this, the
  backend's own automatic TX retry after an RX START (write `-EIO` → PREPARE →
  write → START) left an RX reader blocked forever, and `alp_i2s_close()` on
  that RX handle then deadlocked in `alp_handle_begin_close_blocking()`
  (`src/i2s_dispatch.c:174` ("alp_handle_begin_close_blocking(&i2s->lifecycle, &i2s->active_ops)")),
  because the DROP that would reset the semaphore only runs after that wait.
  An RX START pre-empting TX gives `tx.sem` the same way
  (`zephyr/drivers/i2s/i2s_dw.c:1252` ("k_sem_give(&dev_data->tx.sem);")), and
  `i2s_dw_write()` now fails a writer that wakes to find its stream parked in
  ERROR instead of queueing into it and reporting success
  (`zephyr/drivers/i2s/i2s_dw.c:613` ("if (dev_data->tx.state == I2S_STATE_ERROR) {")).
- **`dev_data->dir` follows START.** `rx_stream_start()` and
  `tx_stream_start()` set it, as `configure()` still does
  (`zephyr/drivers/i2s/i2s_dw.c:1384` ("dev_data->dir = I2S_DIR_TX;")).
- **The #2179 ISR guard masks every unserviced source**, not only TXFE and
  RXDA, limited to the named `IMR` bits
  (`zephyr/drivers/i2s/i2s_dw.c:1004` ("unserviced &= I2S_IMR_ALL_Msk;")).
- **`i2s_dw_initialize()` writes the full named `IMR` mask in one store**
  (`zephyr/drivers/i2s/i2s_dw.c:1104` ("i2s_set_interrupt_mask(I2S_IMR_ALL_Msk, i2s);")).
  It used to read-modify-write only bits 0/1/4/5, so a previous image's
  unmask of bit 6 would have survived into every boot (the block is outside
  the SYSRESETREQ reset domain), and nothing in the driver services that
  source. Nothing in-tree unmasks bit 6 today, and no capture shows it
  unmasked: this closes a hole, it fixes no observed fault.
  From the E8 SVD: bit 6 is `TXFU`/`TXFUM`, the Tx FIFO underrun, now defined
  in `i2s_dw.h`; `IMR` resets to `0x00000073`; and bits 2-3 have no field in
  `ISR` or `IMR` in either the E7 or the E8 SVD. `I2S_IMR_ALL_Msk`
  (`zephyr/drivers/i2s/i2s_dw.h:139` ("#define I2S_IMR_ALL_Msk")) is therefore
  `0x73`, and no 1 is written to bits 2-3. The E7 SVD has no bit 6 either
  (`IMR` resets to `0x00000033`); no in-tree board binds this driver on an E7.
- **The channel-enable helpers read-modify-write**
  (`zephyr/drivers/i2s/i2s_dw.h:508` ("i2s->paddr->RER |= I2S_RER_RXCHEN_Msk;")).
  The plain write of `0x1` zeroed the E8's per-slot enables in bits 8-23:
  harmless in standard I2S mode, wrong under TDM.
- **Offset `0x44` is documented** as `TOR0` on the E7 and `I2S_TICR0` on the
  E8, where one read clears both `TXFO` and `TXFU`
  (`zephyr/drivers/i2s/i2s_dw.h:262` ("I2S_TICR0 (TXCHOU)")).
- **A DRAIN or STOP refused because the stream is in ERROR logs at debug
  level, not error level.** Both are still refused with `-EIO`, and the stream
  stays in ERROR for DROP or PREPARE. ERROR is now an expected state, reached
  from the underrun exit and from a pre-emption, and the backend's `stop()`
  tries DRAIN before falling back to DROP. Without this, every clean teardown
  after a pre-emption printed `E: DRAIN trigger: invalid state` (see the bench
  run below). A refusal from any other state, such as READY, is still a caller
  bug and still logs at error level
  (`zephyr/drivers/i2s/i2s_dw.c:522` ("DRAIN trigger: invalid state")).
- **Stale comments corrected.** The file header, `i2s_dw_isr()` and
  `i2s_dw_initialize()` used to say that no `ISR`/`IMR` capture exists. #2179
  has since closed on an A/B capture that proves the RX-start storm (TXFE
  unmasked while `dir` is `I2S_DIR_RX`), in which `rx_stream_start()`'s TX mask
  prevented it and the ISR guard never fired; the comments now say so. The
  all-zero `CER`/`TER` read after a RESETPIN reset is now described as an
  unclocked block rather than a reset value. `rx_stream_start()`'s "disabling
  the channel does not deassert TXFE" note described a disable that never
  happened on silicon, and is gone.

**Bench.** Bench-verified on E1M-AEN803 serial `2026W36-0002` at
`4efc10692`, with the `PROBE_RX_TEARDOWN` mode of
`examples/aen/aen-i2s-tas2563-probe` cherry-picked from `test/2179-isr-capture`:
4/4 PASS, with step 4 reading `PWR_CTL=0x0c/0x0c` and `CER=0x00000001`,
teardown `CER=0`, 0 write failures, and `IMR` at `0x00000073` after the run. In
that run the RX START pre-empts the RUNNING TX into ERROR while `CER.CLKEN` and
both TAS2563 amps stay up. The init mask was measured on the same board: with
`IMR` forced to `0x00000033` over SWD just before the init-time store, it read
`0x00000073` after it. Every run also printed `E: DRAIN trigger: invalid state`
at teardown, which the debug-level change above addresses; that change, a TX
restart after an RX session, the blocked-reader/writer release, the TDM slot
enables and the `TXFU` guard are host-tested only.

**Tests.** `tests/unit/i2s_dw_underrun` now models the E8: SVD reset values,
and `TER`/`RER` bit 0 reading 1 whatever the driver wrote
(`tests/unit/i2s_dw_underrun/src/test_i2s_dw_underrun.c:218` ("fake_ter(void)")).
It also counts every `CER.CLKEN` clear the driver makes, through a wrapper
around the driver's own `i2s_clock_disable()`, because a 1→0→1 glitch inside
one call is invisible in the final register value. The two assertions that
encoded a writable bit are gone: test (a) checks `ITER.TXEN` instead, and test
(r) no longer checks `RER`/`TER` bit 0. It counts the driver's `LOG_ERR()`
calls the same way, so a case can assert which level a refusal logged at.
Thirteen new cases, plus one extended case, each went RED with their own change
reverted and GREEN with it restored:

- (s) init masks an inherited TXFU unmask;
- (t) the guard masks an unserviced TXFU;
- (u) and (v) a TX or RX restart after the other direction's session is
  serviced;
- (w) a RUNNING TX pre-empted by an RX START is ERROR, keeps `CER.CLKEN`
  through that START and the RX teardown, gets `-EIO` on the next write, and
  restarts without reprogramming the clock: no `set_rate()`, and no live `CCR`
  rewrite;
- (x) a RUNNING RX pre-empted by a TX START is ERROR;
- (y) the enable helpers preserve bits 8-23;
- (z) and (aa) a reader or writer blocked with `SYS_FOREVER_MS` on the
  pre-empted stream is released with `-EIO`;
- (ab) a TX START that fails `-ENOMEM` leaves a RUNNING RX running;
- (ac) a TX retry pre-empting a RUNNING RX makes zero `CER.CLKEN` clears;
- (ad) DRAIN and STOP from ERROR return `-EIO` with no error log, and leave the
  stream in ERROR;
- (ae) DRAIN and STOP from READY still return `-EIO` with an error log each;
- (k), extended: an RX START refused with `-EBUSY` leaves TX RUNNING with
  `ITER.TXEN` set.

An after-hook now DROPs both streams, so one aborted case can no longer starve
the shared slabs for every later case. 32 of 32 pass on native_sim/native/64.

**Known and deferred.**

- `i2s_dw_configure()` still repoints `dev_data->dir`, so configuring one
  direction while the other is RUNNING stalls the running one until the new
  direction's START pre-empts it. That START now releases a reader or writer
  blocked on the stalled stream with `-EIO`, so the stall ends in an error and
  `alp_i2s_close()` no longer deadlocks on it. Removing the `configure()`
  assignment turns the #2179 tests (m) and (q) RED, so it needs its own change.
  It is the one full-duplex gap still listed in the file header.
- `i2s_global_enable()` still writes `IER` whole, which zeroes the E8's
  `TDM_SLOTS` field (reset `0xF00`). The same write leaves `INTF_TYPE` at 0,
  standard I2S, and `TDM_SLOTS` is the slot count of a TDM frame, so this only
  matters once TDM is used.

### Added — grade changelog citations on the merge queue's own base, in a small dedicated job (#2206)

`scripts/check_changelog_citations.py` already grades a PR's merge commit on
`pull_request` -- `pr-metadata-validate.yml`'s `validate` job checks out
`refs/pull/N/merge` with no `ref:` pinned, and #2186's new-citation rule keys
off `DIFF_BASE` there. That workflow carries no `merge_group:` trigger at all,
unlike `pr-twister.yml`, `pr-static-analysis.yml`, and
`cross-platform-zephyr.yml`. So a citation `dev` breaks by moving between a
PR's last push and the merge queue landing the entry is never graded before it
lands -- it only turns the gate red on the *next*, unrelated PR, the #2122
treadmill.

A new `merge-queue-changelog-citations.yml` closes that gap without putting
the whole ~18-minute `pr-metadata-validate.yml` job on every queue entry: its
only job runs `check_changelog_citations.py --verbose` and nothing else. Its
primary trigger is `merge_group:`, matching the three files above, each of
which already carries one:
`.github/workflows/pr-twister.yml:52` ("merge_group:"),
`.github/workflows/pr-static-analysis.yml:49` ("merge_group:"), and
`.github/workflows/cross-platform-zephyr.yml:205` ("merge_group:"). The
`${{ github.workflow }}-${{ github.ref }}` concurrency group is theirs too;
`cancel-in-progress: true` is inert on a merge_group run, where `github.ref`
is the unique `refs/heads/gh-readonly-queue/dev/pr-N-<sha>` and so never
collides across entries.

It also carries a `pull_request:` trigger **path-filtered to itself**, and a
`workflow_dispatch:` with an optional `diff_base` input. Neither is
decoration. Without the path-filtered `pull_request` leg the workflow would
get no validation at all before landing -- its first real execution would be
its own PR's queue entry, where, being deliberately not a required context, a
broken job would block nothing and notify nobody. And without `diff_base` a
manual dispatch could not exercise the rule this gate exists for: `DIFF_BASE`
would be empty, `_resolve_base()` treats empty exactly like unset and falls
back to `origin/dev`, and dispatched on `dev` that makes
`merge-base(origin/dev, HEAD)` equal to `HEAD` -- zero added lines, so the
new-citation rule passes vacuously.

`DIFF_BASE` is set from
`github.event.merge_group.base_sha || inputs.diff_base` -- the merge queue's
own base on the primary trigger, the operator's input on a manual dispatch --
not `HEAD^1` (this checkout's first parent can be a *previous* queue entry
stacked ahead of this one, not `dev` itself), and not the `origin/dev`
default. The reason for rejecting `origin/dev` is **not** that a merge-queue
checkout lacks that ref: under `fetch-depth: 0` `actions/checkout` uses its
all-history refspec (`+refs/heads/*:refs/remotes/origin/*`), so
`refs/remotes/origin/dev` does exist in this job. That "no such ref"
reasoning holds only for a *shallow* checkout. The real reason is
freshness -- `origin/dev` is fetched at job time, so if `dev` moved after the
entry was enqueued it is *ahead* of the base the entry is landing on, and the
gate would grade against a tree that is not the merge result. `base_sha`
cannot drift under the run.

The script resolves `DIFF_BASE` with `git rev-parse --verify
DIFF_BASE^{commit}` in `_resolve_base()` and diffs new lines with `git
merge-base DIFF_BASE HEAD` in `_added_lines()`; both accept a raw SHA exactly
as well as a symbolic ref, so `base_sha` resolves with no local branch
pointing at it. Those two are named by function rather than by `path:line` on
purpose: `check_changelog_citations.py` sits outside the set this gate
grades, so a line citation into it would drift silently -- the exact failure
class #2206 closes.

`fetch-depth: 0` is required rather than merely generous: `git merge-base`
over a grafted shallow history can miss or misresolve the common ancestor,
and `base_sha` -- `dev`'s own tip at enqueue time -- has to be a resolvable
ancestor of HEAD for the new-citation rule to run at all rather than warn
that it did not.

`tests/scripts/test_merge_group_changelog_citations_workflow.py` structurally
pins the workflow: the trigger set is exactly `merge_group` +
`pull_request` (path-filtered to the workflow's own file) +
`workflow_dispatch` (carrying `diff_base`); the single job stays named
`changelog citations · merge queue` with no `if:`; `fetch-depth: 0` and
`persist-credentials: false` stay set; `DIFF_BASE` stays
`github.event.merge_group.base_sha || inputs.diff_base`; and
`pr-metadata-validate.yml` keeps carrying no `merge_group:` trigger of its
own.

`docs/ci/README.md`'s workflow table gains a row for
`merge-queue-changelog-citations.yml`, keeping its workflow count (25) and
its table in sync.

Not a required context, and it cannot become one without a shape change
first. #2206 asks whether it should be required; the answer is not yet. A
required context whose workflow is skipped by a `paths:` filter never reports
a check run at all, and GitHub holds it at `Expected -- Waiting for status to
be reported`, so every ordinary PR would be unable to enter the merge queue.
The `merge_group:` leg does not rescue that, because required contexts gate a
PR *before* it is enqueued. Both of `dev`'s required-context workflows carry
an unfiltered `pull_request:` for exactly this reason --
`.github/workflows/pr-twister.yml` and
`.github/workflows/pr-static-analysis.yml`, each citing #1415
(`AWAITING_CHECKS`). Promoting `changelog citations · merge queue` therefore
means FIRST either dropping the `paths:` filter (accepting a second, PR-side
citation verdict on every PR) or adding an always-run job that reports the
context unconditionally.

Until then it carries the same weakness that let #2201 merge with a red,
non-required `python-smoke` leg: the queue does not wait for it.

### Fixed — M33 library routing no longer claims a nonexistent DRP-AI TFLM backend (#2208)

The `tflite-micro` Zephyr hardware-backend profile used the SoM-wide
`drp_ai` capability to emit `CONFIG_ALP_TFLM_DRP_AI=y` for V2N101 and V2M101
M33 slices.  No Zephyr/M-class DRP-AI backend exists, so the symbol was an
inert but false build claim.  The DRP-AI entry and its Zephyr-only Kconfig
symbol are removed, the affected emit fixtures now pin their absence, and
the M33 examples describe the backend set actually available to their slice.

The independent A55/Yocto backend remains unchanged: `PACKAGECONFIG[drpai]`
still enables `ALP_SDK_USE_DRPAI_V2N` and compiles the real Linux userspace
backend in `src/yocto/inference_drpai.cpp`.

### Fixed — `pr-twister-aen.yml` split per SKU, and the AEN803 target declared for the ~50 scenarios #2198 held back (#2209)

**Every bench EVK carries an E1M-AEN803 module, but CI never compiled most
of its board overlays.** #2198 declared the AEN803 target for 12
scenarios and held back ~50 more because the single combined `twister-aen`
job had no time budget left: the last run before it took 24m21s against
the twister step's 30-minute cap. Declaring the rest would have pushed
that past the cap.

**`twister-aen` is now a 2-way SKU matrix.** Each leg selects only its own
SKU's two platforms via `matrix.platform_flags`, at
`scripts/select_aen_twister.py:71` ("platform_flags"), and the
two legs run in parallel. Neither is a required branch-protection context on
`dev` (the required contexts are `twister-shard 1/4`..`4/4`, `clang-format
· diff-only` and `distro install · all`, verified against the branch's
own protection rules), so the split blocks nothing, at
`.github/workflows/pr-twister-aen.yml:88` ("instead of one job building all four board targets, so the two").
The `--testsuite-root` list stays a single
block shared by both matrix legs rather than duplicated per SKU, at
`.github/workflows/pr-twister-aen.yml:455` ("here. The --testsuite-root list below is scoped to examples/aen --").
The per-SKU report artefact is renamed to avoid an upload collision between
the two legs now running in the same workflow run, at
`.github/workflows/pr-twister-aen.yml:632` ("name: twister-out-${{ matrix.sku }}").

A local `--dry-run` against this tree (examples/aen + firmware-update-log +
drone-autopilot) counts 153 configurations total: 78 AEN801, 75 AEN803 (up
from the pre-split 92). Scaling the 1461s/92-build #2198 measurement
linearly, AEN801 projects to about 1240s/20.7min and AEN803 to about
1195s/19.9min -- both comfortably under the unchanged 30-minute
twister-step cap and 41-minute job ceiling, so neither is tightened per
leg. `examples/connectivity/firmware-update-log` and
`examples/peripheral-io/drone-autopilot`, the two non-examples/aen roots
this job also builds, are unchanged: neither ships an AEN803 overlay at
all under `boards/`, so declaring AEN803 for either would be the exact
silent-overlay-drop hazard this issue exists to close, not a safe
addition.

**The AEN803 target is now declared across 53 scenario files.** 45 files
(50 `platform_allow` additions -- five dual-core files declare both HE and
HP) only where the example's `boards/` already ships the matching AEN803
overlay for that core, re-derived from the tree rather than trusted from
#2198's own held-back list (#2214 may have already covered some), for
example at
`examples/aen/aen-wdt-feed/testcase.yaml:23` ("alp_e1m_aen803_m55_he/ae822fa0e5597ls0/rtss_he")
and, for a dual-core scenario declaring both cores, at
`examples/aen/aen-dualcore-doorbell/testcase.yaml:29` ("alp_e1m_aen803_m55_hp/ae822fa0e5597ls0/rtss_hp").
A further 8 files (9 scenarios -- `aen-dualcore-probe` builds both cores)
ship no `boards/` directory at all (an `app.overlay`-only or overlay-free
shape), so `check_example_board_overlay_parity.py`'s guards have nothing
to compare against them; declaring AEN803 there is still safe because
`app.overlay` content is SoC/pin-routing fact (same PCB, same pinout), not
SKU-specific, at
`examples/aen/aen-can-regcheck/testcase.yaml:23` ("alp_e1m_aen803_m55_he/ae822fa0e5597ls0/rtss_he").
Every stale "platform_allow = the AEN801 ... board only" testcase.yaml
comment these declarations made false is reworded -- examples are
documentation, and a reader trusting the comment over the YAML below it
would get the wrong picture of what CI actually builds.

**Two scenarios get an AEN803 twin scenario instead of a `platform_allow`
line.** `aen-sdhc-probe`'s `.sdhc_build_coverage` and `aen-ethernet-link`'s
`.mdio_managed` both name the AEN801 board overlay explicitly in
`extra_dtc_overlay_files`, which REPLACES rather than supplements Zephyr's
own board-default-overlay auto-discovery -- adding AEN803 to their
`platform_allow` alone would have built the AEN801 overlay for an AEN803
target, the exact #2198 hazard. Each gets its own scenario naming its own
SKU's file instead, at
`examples/aen/aen-sdhc-probe/testcase.yaml:85` ("alp_sdk.examples.aen.sdhc_probe.aen803.sdhc_build_coverage:")
and
`examples/aen/aen-ethernet-link/testcase.yaml:88` ("alp_sdk.examples.aen.ethernet_link.aen803.mdio_managed:").
A grep across `examples/aen/*/testcase.yaml` for `extra_dtc_overlay_files`
naming an AEN801 file found no other scenario shaped this way.

**New guard -- `check_example_board_overlay_parity.py` extended, not a new
script.** A narrower, declaration-triggered relative of the "broader,
deferred alternative" that file's own docstring filed as a follow-up when
#2101 landed (that fuller alternative -- keying off `boards/` content with
NO platform_allow declaration required at all -- is still not
implemented; see the docstring for why it would still be red today). This
one requires a real `platform_allow` declaration to trigger: a scenario
declares SKU A's core target while `boards/` ships the same-PCB SKU B's
file for that same core (same `family` + `silicon_variant`, the pairing
`check_example_board_overlay_content_parity.py`'s `_pcb_key` already
uses), undeclared anywhere that scenario's own build reaches, at
`scripts/check_example_board_overlay_parity.py:647` ("def _same_pcb_sibling_undeclared_problems(root: Path) -> list[str]:").
Unlike the plain #2101 check, this one DOES catch the ~50 scenarios #2209
declared the AEN803 target for.

A scenario is "pinned" -- cannot declare its own sibling target this way
by design -- only when it sets `extra_dtc_overlay_files`, or an
`extra_args` entry starting `DTC_OVERLAY_FILE=`/`CONF_FILE=`: those are
the only twister keys that actually REPLACE (not supplement) Zephyr's
board-default-overlay auto-discovery (verified against
`zephyr/cmake/modules/configuration_files.cmake`'s `if(NOT DEFINED
DTC_OVERLAY_FILE)` guard); `extra_conf_files` and `extra_overlay_confs`
only ADD files and must not be treated as pinned. A pinned scenario is
satisfied only by another PINNED scenario in the same testcase.yaml
declaring the sibling SKU's own target for the same core -- its twin --
not by a coincidental declaration in an unrelated non-pinned scenario
elsewhere in the file. `platform_allow` is read as Twister actually
resolves it: a scenario's own value MERGES with the file's `common:`
default (a `set`-type field) rather than replacing it.

That second guard the issue asked for -- a scenario's extra board files
naming SKU A's paired file while its `platform_allow` reaches SKU B --
already existed from #2214
(`scripts/check_example_board_overlay_content_parity.py:256` ("def _testcase_pin_problems(root: Path")),
so no second gate was added for it. Both guards are green on this tree
with no allowlist, and both are wired into `pr-metadata-validate.yml`
already, no CI/registry changes needed (neither is a new `check_*.py`
script).

Mutation-proof: removing the AEN803 `platform_allow` line from
`aen-brd-i2c-scan/testcase.yaml` reproduces the exact #2101/#2209 class and
fails `check_example_board_overlay_parity.py`; restoring it passes again.
Deleting the AEN803 twin scenario from the real `aen-sdhc-probe/
testcase.yaml`, with nothing else in the file pinning AEN803's own
overlay, now fails the same gate (its base scenario declaring both SKUs
does NOT save it, since only another PINNED scenario counts) -- restoring
it passes again. Adding an AEN803 `platform_allow` entry to
`aen-ethernet-link`'s `.mdio_managed` scenario without changing its
`extra_dtc_overlay_files` reproduces the #2198 class and fails
`check_example_board_overlay_content_parity.py`'s `_testcase_pin_problems`;
restoring it passes again. Both scripts gained regression tests for their
respective mutations, including the reverse-direction pin case
`_testcase_pin_problems` itself already checked but nothing previously
exercised.

**One real, previously-unbuilt compile break found and fixed, and 29 SKU
board-macro sites corrected.** `aen-dualcore-he-master`'s HP-peer role
select hardcoded the AEN801 board symbol, so an AEN803 HP build silently
took the HE-master branch instead, reaching `#include <alp/mproc.h>` in a
role that never enables `CONFIG_ALP_SDK` (by this example's own asymmetric
design) -- `error: alp/mproc.h: No such file or directory`. The exact
#2198 class, only reachable once this issue's twister invocation actually
compiled the target. On review, the same class turned out to be
widespread: 29 sites across `examples/` gated on the AEN801-specific
`CONFIG_BOARD_ALP_E1M_AEN801_M55_H[EP]` when what they actually depend on
is the SoC core (both SKUs select the identical
`CONFIG_SOC_AE822FA0E5597LS0_RTSS_H[EP]` symbols) -- most seriously the 17
`examples/**/cc3501e_bridge.c` copies, where the WIFI_EN/nRESET LP-pad mux
compiled OUT entirely on AEN803, so the CC3501E companion would never
power. All 29 now gate on the SoC-core symbol instead, at
`examples/aen/aen-dualcore-he-master/src/main.c:108` ("#if defined(CONFIG_SOC_AE822FA0E5597LS0_RTSS_HP)")
and
`examples/aen/aen-cc3501e-bringup/src/cc3501e_bridge.c:10` ("#if defined(CONFIG_SOC_AE822FA0E5597LS0_RTSS_HE)").
clang-format-22 diff-only: clean.

Proof for the cc3501e fix: a direct `west build` of `aen-cc3501e-bringup`
for `alp_e1m_aen803_m55_he/ae822fa0e5597ls0/rtss_he` now disassembles to
the two `sys_write32` stores at `0x42007014` (P15_5 WIFI_EN) and
`0x42007004` (P15_1 nRESET) that were previously compiled out. Proof for
the HP-role fix: `aen-dualcore-doorbell`'s `hp_master_receiver` scenario,
built for both AEN801 and AEN803 HP, links the HP-specific
`SELF_MAGIC=0xB1B10090` literal on both, confirming both take the HP
branch. Proof for `aen-power-iwic`: built for AEN803 HE, `.config` shows
`CONFIG_HAS_PM=y` / `CONFIG_PM=y`.

Every newly-declared AEN803 scenario, plus the two twins and the 9
no-`boards/`-dir scenarios, was built locally with the same twister
invocation the workflow step uses (a local Zephyr v4.4.1 checkout,

`aen-dualcore-he-master`'s `hp_peer`, above; after the fix: 66 built, 0

### Added — OV5647 Zephyr sensor driver for a Raspberry-Pi-style CSI-2 camera shield (#2213)

A board-agnostic Zephyr shield lands under `zephyr/boards/shields/`:
`raspberry_pi_camera_module_1` (OmniVision OV5647, 5 Mpx raw Bayer, 25 MHz
oscillator, CCI 0x36, 2 MIPI data lanes). It carries no Alif/EVK specifics —
it just wires the sensor's `fixed-clock` and endpoint onto the upstream RPi
camera shield label contract (`chosen zephyr,camera`, `&csi_interface`,
`&csi_ep_in`, `&csi_i2c`); build with
`SHIELD="<carrier-connector-shield> raspberry_pi_camera_module_1"`.

`zephyr/drivers/video/ov5647.c` is a byte-for-byte, ADR 0017 Tier-1
upstream-PENDING backport (INTERIM) of the still-open upstream PR
zephyrproject-rtos/zephyr#119301 @ `d81b1f630ee0f5078de6e3a47e7bc1b3613424c2`
— not yet in the pinned Zephyr v4.4.1 base. Its own binding treats
`pwdn-gpios` as optional, and the `raspberry_pi_camera_module_1` shield
omits it: the E1M-EVK's 15-pin RPi camera connector carries no PWDN GPIO
line to wire it to. Delete the driver, its Kconfig, and its binding — see
the file header and the ADR 0017 amendment — the moment the Zephyr pin
advances past a revision containing that PR.

`tests/zephyr/video_sensors` stays compile-coverage for OV5647 (no
emulator) in the same runtime suite that ztests OV9281. See
`docs/camera-shields.md` for the full driver/shield/control reference.

### Documented — J5 pin 11 has no pull-up on the E1M-EVK, and the OV5647 bring-up is blocked at D-PHY Stop-state, not working (#2213)

Bench-proven 2026-09-22 on an E1M-AEN803 (serial 2026W36-0001) on an
E1M-EVK (hw_rev 2626-r2). `docs/boards/e1m-evk.md`'s `CAM_EN` row and RPi
camera connector (J5) section previously said only "keep `CAM_EN = 0` so
the module self-enables" — true for a module with its own pull-up, silent
about one that has none. The `CAM_EN_#` net has exactly three nodes: J5
pin 11, `Q1` (`BSS138PW,115` N-channel MOSFET, gate on `CAM_EN`, source on
`0V`) pin 3, and `D45` (`D5V0L1B2S9-7`, a bidirectional 5V TVS — an ESD
clamp, not a pull-up) pin 2; `R2` is a 10k gate pull-down. Nothing on the
EVK can source current into pin 11, so firmware can only leave it floating
or pull it to ground — never drive it high. A new "J5 pin 11 pull-up
rework" section documents the fix for a module without its own pull-up
(the InnoMaker CAM-OV5647): a resistor from J5 pin 11 to J5 pin 15
(`+3V3`), sized to roughly a quarter of the module's own measured
pull-down (a 10k-vs-10k pair divides to 1.65 V, below VIH), and a
resistor, never a bare wire — with pin 11 hard-tied, any firmware that
asserts `CAM_EN` turns `Q1` on and shorts `+3V3` to ground through it.
Measured effect: before the rework a full `0x08`..`0x77` I2C sweep found
zero devices and `alp_camera_open` returned `ALP_ERR_IO`; after, the
sensor answers at `0x36` with chip ID `0x5647` and board draw rises from
0.065-0.067 A to 0.074-0.080 A at 16.0 V. `CAM_EN` must stay `0` after the
rework too — asserting it still powers the module down.

`docs/camera-shields.md` previously listed the OV5647 module as
"Build-only / not run on hardware", which is now stale: with the pull-up
fitted the sensor answers on I2C, and camera bring-up was bench-attempted
and found BLOCKED, not working. `alp_camera_open` fails at
`ALP_ERR_TIMEOUT` with `E: D-PHY not locked to Stop-state. PHY status -
0x00010000 DPHY ID: 0`. That `PHY status` field is `CSI_PHY_RX`
(`0x49033048`), the register the driver's log line prints, and it reads
`0x00010000` — `RXULPSCLKNOT` set, `RXCLKACTIVEHS` (bit17) clear.
`CSI_PHY_STOPSTATE` (`0x4903304c`) is a separate register and reaches
only `0x00000001` (bit0 `STOPSTATEDATA_0`); bit1 (`DATA_1`) and bit16
(`CLK`) never assert, unlike the OV9281 path on the same receiver, which
reaches `CSI_PHY_STOPSTATE` = `0x00010003` (`CLK|DATA_1|DATA_0`). Ruled out by
control-validated bench runs: module power, the sensor's own MIPI PHY
being disabled (register `0x3018` = `0x44`), the mainline "coax lanes
into LP-11" park sequence, sensor-before-receiver ordering, and the
receiver's D-PHY frequency bin (identical at `hsfreqrange 0x16` and
`0x09`, the OV9281's own bin). Open candidates: the physical clock/data-1
pairs through the P/N-crossing adapter, a module-level fault, and `0x4837
PCLK_PERIOD`, which the driver never programs and sits at its reset value
`0x15`. The OV9281 rows and their bench-verified claims are unchanged.
