### Fixed — Flow D MRAM writes sector-pad neighbours and prove themselves with a fresh-session read-back, not `verifybin` (#2233)

Two defects measured on real hardware during the #2067 persistence proof made
every Flow D MRAM writer unsafe as written. SEGGER's built-in
`AE822FA0E5597LS0_M55_HE` loader always erases and reprograms WHOLE 16 KiB
sectors and never reads a sector's prior contents first, so a `loadbin` that
does not start and end on a sector boundary silently turned every other byte
in its first/last sector to `0xFF`. Separately, `verifybin` was comparing
against J-Link's own in-process flash cache, never a fresh chip read — a
`Verify successful.` proved nothing about what MRAM actually held.

`scripts/bench/aen/flowd_sector_pad.py:65` (`class FlowdSectorPadError(Exception):`)
is a new, pure host-side helper: given the blob(s) a write touches, it merges
their sector-aligned ranges, overlays the blob bytes on a pre-read sector
image, and refuses on a blob outside the MRAM window, a non-power-of-two
sector size, or two blobs overlapping with different bytes. It also pre-reads
and proves a GUARD sector immediately before/after each padded range, so
collateral damage just outside the intended write is visible, not just damage
inside it. `scripts/bench/aen/bench-env.sh:2176` (`bench_flowd_proof() {`) is
the shared bash orchestration — plan, read the touched sectors, build the
padded images, and a FRESH read-only J-Link session that `savebin`s each
range (and its guards) back and `cmp`s it against the padded image, which
proves both that the blob landed and that its immediate neighbours survived
THIS write.

Every affected writer — flash-jlink.sh, flash-jlink-hp.sh,
flash-jlink-mramxip.sh, flash-update-log-dual.sh,
flash-update-log-firewall-probe.sh, and the #1430 provisioning
erase-storage.sh — now gates on `bench_flowd_proof()` instead of `verifybin`,
and each write session also `savebin`s its own touched sectors immediately
before the load line(s) so a host-side compare against the original pre-read
can catch (not prevent — the pre-read is not halted) a write racing this
one between the read and the load. `FLOWD_DRY_RUN=1` is a THREE-layer
guarantee, not a flag with one effect: every writer exits right after
printing its would-be write CommandFile, `bench_jlink_run()` independently
refuses any `loadbin`/`erase` CommandFile while it is set, and
`bench_flowd_proof()` itself never reports success in this mode — an earlier
version of this fix only did the first of the three, so the write session
still ran for real underneath a "dry run" label.

`erase-storage.sh` additionally now resolves where the RESIDENT ATOC package
actually starts before erasing (`scripts/bench/aen/atoc_trailer.py`,
bench-measured on one real E1M-AEN803 board, serial 2026W36-0001,
2026-09-19) and refuses outright if the erase window would overlap it — on
that board the live package started well inside the nominal customer storage
window this script erases, which a metadata-window-only erase would have
zeroed part of. `--sku`/`ALP_AEN_SKU` picks which module preset a run
targets (previously hard-coded to E1M-AEN801), and every pre-write sector
read is copied to `$BENCH_ROOT/flowd-backup/<timestamp>-erase-storage/`
before any write, printed at run time — the only restore source on a board
with no SE-UART.

None of this is a persistence proof across a power cycle: the fresh-session
read-back proves the write landed and its neighbours survived within the
SAME power cycle, not that it survives one. flash-jlink-mramxip.sh's own
"ACCEPTANCE ON THIS PATH IS A COLD-CYCLE READBACK" requirement is unchanged
and still stands on top of this proof, not replaced by it.

A third adversarial review round found the proof itself failing OPEN:
`scripts/bench/aen/bench-env.sh:2247` (`rc=$?`) used to sit after a separate
`if cmd; then break; fi`, whose OWN exit status is 0 when the `if` takes no
branch — exhausting all 3 connect retries returned success. `rc=$?` now sits
on the same line as the command it reads. Every writer's write-session
invocation now captures `bench_jlink_run()`'s own exit status (a bare
`|| true` used to swallow a FLOWD_DRY_RUN backstop refusal, rc 13) and exits
13 before any race check, proof, or boot; the race check and the read-back
proof now both always run and both print, with a detected race winning the
exit code (11) even when the proof passed, instead of the race check
exiting first and hiding the proof's verdict. `erase-storage.sh` treats
FLOWD_DRY_RUN exactly like `--dry-run` (it used to back up SYNTHETIC
all-zero sectors as if real), reads the WHOLE `atoc` region rather than only
the trailer's own sector so a blank trailer next to a live signature is
refused (`scripts/bench/aen/atoc_trailer.py`'s own blank-trailer search),
rejects an unrecognised argument or a value-less `--sku`
(`scripts/bench/aen/erase-storage.sh:336` ("ATOC_REGION_SIZE=$((ATOC_KIB * 1024))")),
and no longer hard-codes `/tmp/aen-erase-storage.jlink`/`/tmp/aen-erase-storage.out`/
`/tmp/aen-storage-erased.bin` (every writer now uses `${TMPDIR:-/tmp}`, so
concurrent test runs no longer collide on the same host `/tmp`).
`scripts/bench/aen/atoc_trailer.py` also now refuses a header outside its
own package or a zero-size package, not just a bad checksum or signature.

A fourth round added `erase-storage.sh --check-only`: a READ-ONLY mode that
runs the DPIDR preflight and the whole-atoc-region trailer read/overlap
decision exactly like a real run — so the overlap GUARD ITSELF is exercised
on real silicon, not just its arithmetic — then exits
(`scripts/bench/aen/erase-storage.sh:395` (`if [ "$CHECK_ONLY" = 1 ]; then`))
before the pre-write backup, `bench_flowd_prepare_write`, or any
write-session CommandFile is ever built. Exit 0 means the erase would
proceed (the resolved package start, or "blank trailer", is printed); exit 7
means it would be refused for an overlap; exit 6 means the trailer was
undeterminable — the SAME exit codes and the SAME trailer-check code the
real path uses, not a parallel simulation. `--check-only` is mutually
exclusive with `--dry-run`/`FLOWD_DRY_RUN` (exit 1), which is the opposite
promise (no probe opened at all); `bench_jlink_run()`'s `FLOWD_DRY_RUN`
backstop is also set internally as defense in depth, exported only AFTER
the existing `--dry-run`-aliasing check so it does not also skip the real
reads this mode exists to run.

A fifth round found the trailer layout itself wrong by one word, on real
E1M-AEN803 silicon (serial 2026W36-0001, 2026-09-19): `mem32` twice plus a
`savebin` tail agreed on `0x8057FFF0` = `4966A80E 8057FF90 8056A3C0
00015C40`, but `header_address`/`package_start`/`package_size` were being
unpacked from trailer offsets `+0x0/+0x4/+0x8` instead of the REAL
`+0x4/+0x8/+0xC` — `+0x0` holds an opaque word (`word0`, bench-measured
`0x4966A80E`, unknown meaning, possibly a checksum, never validated).
`scripts/bench/aen/atoc_trailer.py:101` (`word0, header_addr, pkg_start, pkg_size = struct.unpack("<IIII", data)`) now reads all four words at the
right offsets; the old offsets misparsed `word0` as `header_address` and
refused every real trailer, so `erase-storage.sh --check-only --sku
E1M-AEN803` exited 6 ("undeterminable") on real hardware instead of the
expected 7 (overlap) — the guard failed CLOSED, but the overlap decision
was never reached. Every fixture that built a trailer (`test_atoc_trailer.py`,
`test_bench_flowd_write.py`, `test_flowd_review_round3.py`) reproduced the
same wrong layout, which is why the tests passed anyway; new tests build a
trailer from the EXACT measured 16 bytes and confirm the OLD (wrong)
three-word layout is now refused, not misparsed into a false proceed.

The same round bench-measured the `savebin` SUCCESS line (J-Link V9.50,
`savebin <file> 0x80578000 0x8000`): `Reading 32768 bytes from addr
0x80578000 into file...O.K.` `scripts/bench/aen/bench-env.sh:1915`
(`if grep -qiE 'Could not read memory|Cannot read memory|\*\*\*\* ?Error' "$out"; then`)
and its `bench_flowd_proof()`/`erase-storage.sh` trailer-read counterparts
now require ONE such line per planned `savebin`, on top of (not instead
of) the failure-string refusal an earlier version of this file's own
comment said had no positive counterpart to cite — this is that string.

Checked (read-only): `bench_jlink_run()` already injects `exec
DisableAutoUpdateFW` as the first line of every CommandFile before any
probe open, independent of which installed J-Link build `bench_jlink_exe()`
resolves — so the auto-firmware-update brick hazard is covered regardless
of the DLL/firmware-version mismatch board-farm's `jlink-run.sh` (commit
`29d6bb8`) found on this probe. That commit's bundle-match DLL selection
(107 changed lines, plus a dependency on reading the probe's OWN running
firmware before choosing which JLinkExe to launch at all) was NOT ported
here — it is not small and self-contained; left as a follow-up.

### Fixed — AEN flash paths refuse an ATOC package that overlaps customer `storage` (#2234)

The E1M-AEN presets reserve a 32 KiB `atoc` band at `0x80578000`, with the
customer `storage` region directly below it. SETOOLS grows the signed ATOC
package down from the top of App MRAM, and it stores an ITCM load image
(`loadAddress`) inside the package. A plain Flow A package therefore measured
89152 B and started at `0x8056A3C0`, 56384 B inside `storage`. A runtime that
writes `storage` (NVS, littlefs, settings) or `erase-storage.sh` would then
overwrite the boot image.

`scripts/aen_atoc.py` gains `validate_package_extent()` and a
`--package-map <app-package-map.txt>` mode, which read the package start and
refuse anything below the band. Every bench script that runs `app-gen-toc`
now calls it through `bench_atoc_extent_guard` in `scripts/bench/aen/bench-env.sh`:
`flash-run.sh`, `flash-run-dualcore.sh`, `flash-jlink.sh`, `flash-jlink-hp.sh`,
`flash-jlink-mramxip.sh`, `flash-update-log-dual.sh` and
`flash-update-log-firewall-probe.sh`. The `alif_flash` west runner calls it
too. For an image that never writes `storage`, set
`ALP_ATOC_ALLOW_OVER_STORAGE=1` to accept the overlap. The memory map itself
is unchanged.

### Fixed — the board-qualified preflight now catches near-miss names, stem conflicts and .conf mismatches too, and AEN803 gets its own twin for alp-console (M55-HE), blink (M55-HP), pwm-led-fade (M55-HP) and drone-autopilot (M55-HP) (#2235)

The unlanded remainder of closed PR #2232, itself the follow-up to #2094's
board-qualified overlay preflight in `scripts/bench/aen/build.sh`.

**The guard now checks `.conf` exactly like `.overlay`, and accepts
Zephyr's own SHORT stem, not only the FULL one.** Zephyr computes two
candidate filenames for both extensions -- the FULL stem (board + every
qualifier segment, `/` -> `_`) and a SHORT stem dropping the FIRST
qualifier segment (the SoC id), legal only for a single-SoC board -- both
AEN803 HE and HP declare exactly one SoC, so both stems are live targets
here, at
`scripts/bench/aen/build.sh:67` ("single-SoC board").
One shared function,
`scripts/bench/aen/build.sh:203` ("bench_build_require_board_qualified() {"),
is now called once per extension rather than duplicating the overlay-only
check #2094 shipped.

**User-visible effect of the rescoping to `alp_e1m_*_rtss_h[ep]`.** On
`origin/dev`, `build.sh`'s unscoped overlay loop refused (exit 2) on
every AEN target any app whose `boards/` ships overlays but none
`alp_e1m_*_rtss_h[ep]`-qualified -- 35 examples on this tree are in that
shape: 34 with no `alp_e1m_*` overlay at all (e.g.
`examples/peripheral-io/gpio-button-led`, `i2c-master`, `uart-echo`, each
shipping only `boards/native_sim_native_64.overlay`), plus the V2N-only
`examples/connectivity/iot-connected-camera`. The preflight no longer
refuses them, matching `check_example_board_overlay_parity.py`'s own
policy that an example whose `boards/` ships zero `alp_e1m_*`-qualified
overlays "IS legitimately board-agnostic" for that SoM family. (This
change does not claim they build for AEN -- only the four examples
below were built.)

**Three more refusal shapes, matched against Zephyr v4.4.1
(`cmake/modules/extensions.cmake`, `cmake/modules/boards.cmake`):**

- A file misnamed for THIS board specifically -- the bare board name, or
  board+SoC with the trailing RTSS qualifier dropped -- is invisible to
  the guard's `alp_e1m_*_rtss_h[ep]` scoping glob, itself new in this
  change: that glob only proves an app ships SOME real board-qualified
  file, not one shaped for this board. Zephyr auto-applies neither name
  (both accepted stems require the RTSS qualifier).
  `origin/dev`'s own unscoped `boards/*.overlay` loop already refused a
  bare-name overlay -- any `.overlay` present but not the exact
  `${BOARD//\//_}.overlay` match tripped it -- so the new `_rtss_h[ep]`
  scoping keeps refusing this board's own bare and board+SoC names too,
  for both kinds now: `.overlay` (matching what `origin/dev` already
  caught) and, newly, `.conf` (never checked there at all).
  `BOARD_BARE`/`BOARD_BOARD_SOC` name both, at
  `scripts/bench/aen/build.sh:185` ("BOARD_BARE="), and are folded into
  the same "have a file of this kind" check the generic glob already fed,
  at
  `scripts/bench/aen/build.sh:265` ("near_bare").
  They cannot collide with the `_firewall_probe`/`_firewall_proven`
  `EXTRA_CONF_FILE` fragments `examples/connectivity/firmware-update-log`
  ships: those always carry that suffix past the full stem, never a bare
  board or board+SoC filename.
- Both accepted stems present for the same extension passed the guard
  silently, and Zephyr's own `zephyr_file(CONF_FILES ...)` then
  FATAL_ERRORs ("Conflicting file names discovered. Cannot use both
  ${filename_0} and ${filename_1}...", `cmake/modules/extensions.cmake`
  line 2950 for `.overlay` / line 2997 for `.conf`) with a message
  `build.sh`'s own grep-based output filter drops. The guard now refuses
  this pair itself, naming both files and
  recommending the full stem -- the same one Zephyr's own error
  recommends -- at
  `scripts/bench/aen/build.sh:224` ("ships BOTH the full and short board-qualified").
- A malformed `$AEN_BOARD` -- a leading `/`, a trailing `/` (which
  `IFS='/' read -a` silently drops, so the stems would look well-formed
  and the bad target would reach `west build -b`), or an empty qualifier
  segment -- is now refused early (exit 2).
  `$AEN_BOARD` with an empty qualifier segment (`board//rtss_he`) is legal
  Zephyr shorthand for a single-SoC board -- upstream `boards.cmake` lines
  271-272 (not vendored in this tree) resolve the omitted SoC during
  Zephyr's OWN board lookup -- but that
  resolution never runs in this preflight, so a bare `/` -> `_`
  substitution on it produced a double-underscore stem no real file
  matches, and a false refusal. The guard now refuses early instead of
  guessing, asking for the board fully qualified, at
  `scripts/bench/aen/build.sh:152` ("empty qualifier segment ('//').").

`scripts/bench/aen/bench-env.sh`'s own `AEN_BOARD` note is reworded to
match -- each kind is checked SEPARATELY, and the scope is AEN
board-qualified `alp_e1m_*_rtss_h[ep]` names plus same-board near-misses,
not every board-qualified file -- at

**Known limitation, found on bench review, not fixed here: a twin-built
example's SoM-derived banner/Kconfig facts do not vary per SKU.**
alpCaner's 2026-09-30 silicon check of `alp-console` on an E1M-AEN803 slot
found `examples/peripheral-io/alp-console/board.yaml` still declares
`som.sku: E1M-AEN801`, so the AEN803 build's generated
`CONFIG_ALP_SDK_SOM_DRAM_MBIT`/`_FLASH_MBIT` read 0 and the boot banner
drops its `EXT:` line, although E1M-AEN803 populates 512 Mbit of each
(`metadata/e1m_modules/E1M-AEN803.yaml`). Root cause traced to
`scripts/alp_orchestrate/kconfig.py`'s `_emit_soc_summary()`: these Kconfig
lines are transcribed from `project.som_preset["memory"]`, which
`load_board_yaml()` resolves once, statically, from `board.yaml`'s single
`som.sku` string (`scripts/alp_orchestrate/loader.py:775`
("sku = project")) -- there is no BOARD-qualified
override anywhere in the loader or `alp_orchestrate`'s build-plan/
topology/partition/storage resolvers, all of which key off that same
single `sku`. The Zephyr BOARD string itself already disambiguates the
SKU (`alp_e1m_aen801_m55_he/...` vs `alp_e1m_aen803_m55_he/...`), but
nothing threads that back into the SDK-side Kconfig emission, which
(`scripts/gen_example_alp_conf.py`) writes one static
`generated/alp.conf` per (app, core) with no BOARD input at all. This is
not new: `examples/connectivity/camera-mjpeg-stream/board.yaml` already
declares `som.sku: E1M-AEN803` while its own `.aen` scenario builds both
AEN801 and AEN803 targets from that one static file, so its AEN801 build
has carried the mirror-image defect (AEN803's memory facts on an AEN801
build) since #2265, predating this PR. `blink`, `pwm-led-fade` and
`drone-autopilot` (all `som.sku: E1M-AEN801`) have the same gap on their
AEN803 twin. A correct fix needs a multi-SKU mechanism in the `board.yaml`
schema plus a BOARD-qualified emission path threaded through
`alp_project.py`/`alp_orchestrate` and every consumer keyed off the
single `project.sku` today (build-plan, system-manifest, partition,
storage) -- a design change larger than this PR, left as a follow-up
rather than built here.

**Merge fallout from dev's #866 (retiring the CMakeLists `--emit
zephyr-conf` bridge): the three new `.aen` scenarios were missing their
`EXTRA_CONF_FILE`.** `alp_console.aen`, `blink.aen` and `pwm_led_fade.aen`
were written before #866 landed on `dev`, when each example's
`CMakeLists.txt` ran `alp_project.py --emit zephyr-conf` itself at
configure time and applied the result implicitly -- no `extra_args` needed
in `testcase.yaml`. #866 retired that bridge in favour of
`scripts/gen_example_alp_conf.py` pre-generating `generated/alp.conf`
ahead of the build, which only takes effect when the scenario passes
`extra_args: EXTRA_CONF_FILE=generated/alp.conf` itself -- the pattern
every sibling `native_sim` scenario in these same files already uses. The
new tree-wide gate that ships with #866,
`tests/scripts/test_gen_example_alp_conf.py::test_every_test_loads_generated_alp_conf_first`,
caught the gap post-merge (`len(vals) == 1` fails with `[]` for all
three). Fixed by adding the missing `extra_args` line to each scenario, at
`examples/peripheral-io/alp-console/testcase.yaml:28`
("extra_args: EXTRA_CONF_FILE=generated/alp.conf"),
`examples/peripheral-io/blink/testcase.yaml:32`
("extra_args: EXTRA_CONF_FILE=generated/alp.conf"), and
`examples/peripheral-io/pwm-led-fade/testcase.yaml:33`
("extra_args: EXTRA_CONF_FILE=generated/alp.conf") -- matching
`drone-autopilot`'s own `.aen` scenario, which already carried it.
`pytest tests/scripts/` on the macOS dev host then shows only the two
pre-existing macOS base-reds, both unrelated to this diff:
`test_alp_template.py::test_validate_minimal_passes_via_twister` and
`test_emit_kconfig_workspace.py::test_emit_kconfig_happy_path_on_bootstrapped_workspace`.

Refs #2094, #2232.

### Fixed — bench J-Link runs use the install whose bundled firmware matches the probe (#2237)

`bench_jlink_run` used to launch the newest installed J-Link build. A
probe running older firmware was then protected from a bricking update
(the bench probes are OEM clones) only by the injected
`exec DisableAutoUpdateFW`. It now first reads the probe's running
firmware string over OpenOCD, by the labgrid-resolved USB path. OpenOCD
never offers an update. `bench_jlink_exe` then picks the newest install
whose bundled `Firmwares/JLink_V*.bin` carries exactly that string. That
is the same selection as the board-farm `jlink-run.sh`.

- It searches `ALP_JLINK_SEARCH_ROOT` (`JLink_Linux_V*_x86_64`) and
  SEGGER's default `/opt/SEGGER` (`JLink_V*`, overridable with
  `ALP_JLINK_OPT_ROOT`).
- It prints which install it chose and why.
- It falls back to the newest install when nothing matches or the
  firmware can't be read.
- `JLINK_EXE` still wins, and `DisableAutoUpdateFW` stays unconditional.

Bench: on E1M-AEN803 2026W36-0009 the probe reported
`J-Link V13 compiled Aug 26 2026 13:07:02`, and the V9.74 install was
chosen as the bundle match.

### Fixed — the `iot` scaffold now carries `src/cc3501e_bridge.{c,h}`, and the template gate rejects any app-dir file the catalog forgets (#2241)

`--emit scaffold` copies exactly a template's `files.user_owned` list, and the
`iot` entry listed only `board.yaml`, `prj.conf`, `CMakeLists.txt`,
`src/main.c` and `README.md`. Its canonical example, `mqtt-telemetry`, compiles
a second source since #2112 / #2172
(`examples/connectivity/mqtt-telemetry/CMakeLists.txt:14`
("target_sources(app PRIVATE src/cc3501e_bridge.c)")), so every emitted `iot`
project referenced a `src/cc3501e_bridge.c` it did not contain and could not
link. The two bridge files are now in the list
(`metadata/templates/catalog-v1.json:546` ("src/cc3501e_bridge.c")), and
the scaffold carries them byte for byte.

`scripts/check_template_catalog.py` gains the check that would have caught
this (`scripts/check_template_catalog.py:242`
("def _check_core_files_declared(rec: dict) -> list[str]:")). Every file git
tracks in a record's `cores[].dir` app dirs must appear in
`files.user_owned`. The one exemption is a path that `test.testcase_yaml`
lists: that is SDK CI wiring, which the scaffold drops on purpose (the
`multicore-*` records' `m55_hp/testcase.yaml` and `peer/testcase.yaml`). The
check reads `git ls-files`, not the directory, so a stray untracked file such
as `.DS_Store` cannot trip it. A core whose `dir` is the example root is
skipped, because the root also holds CI-only files by design. Across the nine
current templates, `iot` was the only violation.

For tan-cli: tan's in-process `--emit scaffold` mirrors this envelope byte for
byte, and its planner re-sync (alplabai/tan-cli#1275) worked around the gap by
vendoring the two files as `NON_ENVELOPE_EXTRAS`. That workaround can be
dropped on the first re-sync that picks this up.

### Fixed — whole-repo doc audit: wrong and misleading claims corrected (#2243)

A whole-repo documentation audit (every md surface cross-checked against the
current code, metadata, schemas, and workflows) found a set of claims that
were factually wrong. Corrections, each verified before editing:

`docs/v0.6-tbd-and-assumptions.md` no longer claims an in-tree
`cc3501e-v0.4.0.bin` (+ `.sha256`/`.sig`): per ADR 0031 the CC3501E firmware
lives in the `cc3501e-bridge-firmware` repository, and AEN modules ship from
production factory-flashed with the latest firmware (v0.9.0 as of this
change); OTP updates stay recovery-only. The never-shipped
`cc3501e_usb_bootloader` flash-backend row is marked historical, and §6.5's
`src/yocto/rpc_yocto.c` pointer is re-aimed at the real
`src/backends/rpc/yocto_drv.c`/`yocto_uio_drv.c`.

`docs/threat-model.md` now states honestly that the SDK registers no BLE
pairing/bonding callbacks — pairing policy is application-owned (Zephyr host
stack or CC3501E firmware), not an SDK-enforced mitigation — and records that
`keys/` tracks the release-signing PUBLIC key. `docs/bring-up-v2n.md`
reverses the stale "OTA host helpers not yet shipped" paragraph (the full
`gd32g553_ota_*` set is on `include/alp/chips/gd32g553.h` and
silicon-validated) and expects the current 0.9.x wire protocol from
`GET_VERSION` instead of 0.1.0. `docs/bring-up-v2n-m1.md` and
`docs/firmware-quickstart.md` stop instructing a 0x48 probe for the DEEPX
LPDDR buck (that address is the on-module TMP112; the buck's address is TBD).
`docs/bring-up-aen.md` replaces the "host-side helper TBD" paragraph with the
shipped `cc3501e_init()`, the `examples/aen/aen-cc3501e-bringup/` helper, and
the `alp companion` console verbs. `docs/tutorials/11-mqtt-tls-publish.md`
now compiles: `broker_uri`/`ca_file`/`keepalive_s` replace the three
invented field names, and `docs/tutorials/04-cross-family-portability.md`
drops the nonexistent `include/alp/log.h`. `README.md` names `ssd1306`
instead of the nonexistent `ssd13xx`. `AGENTS.md` matches ADR 0026 (tan owns
the planner; `alp_orchestrate` output is provisional and needs
`PYTHONPATH=scripts`). `docs/zephyr-version-policy.md` records that
`hal_alif` is our own top-level west pin (v2.3.0), `docs/e1m-pinout.md` fixes
the E1M-X pad range (A1..AR64) and the e1m-spec v1.0 lock, and
`docs/board-config-hardware.md`, `docs/ci/README.md`,
`docs/branching-and-merge-policy.md`, `docs/cc3501e-companion-commands.md`,
`docs/_aen-runbook-section.md`, `CONTRIBUTING.md`, and
`docs/contribution.md` get their respective dead pointers, conventions,
required-check, console-surface, and matrix corrections.
