hardware" or "BENCH-UNVERIFIED": `docs/test-plan.md` (and its generated
projection `docs/verification-status.md`), `docs/architecture.md`,
`docs/aen-bench-bringup.md`, `examples/aen/README.md`,
`examples/aen/aen-camera-firstlight/README.md`, and
`examples/aen/aen-camera-firstlight/src/main.c`. All now read
bench-attempted, BLOCKED — not working, not verified — and cite issue #2248.
The IMX219 row is untouched: no module is seated, so it remains genuinely
unbenched. IMX296 was in the same state at the time of this change; issue
#2287 (a later PR in this same unreleased history) seats a module and
bench-verifies it — see `changelog.d/2287.md`. The OV9281 rows are
untouched: it is bench-verified. No `metadata/chips/ov5647.yaml` exists — the RPi-style camera
shields are board-agnostic Zephyr shields, not SoM-resident chips in
`metadata/chips/`, so there is no metadata status field to update.

### Fixed — OV5647: 640x480 is now the full-array subsampled+binned mode, with register values taken from the RPi/OmniVision reference driver (#2248)

`zephyr/drivers/video/ov5647.c`'s 640x480 was a 648x488 1:1 centre crop -- a heavy telephoto
crop over roughly 25% of the array width -- not the full-array subsampled+binned 640x480 mode.
The register VALUES this fix programs are taken as hardware facts from the RPi/OmniVision
reference driver: raspberrypi/linux branch rpi-6.6.y, `drivers/media/i2c/ov5647.c`,
`ov5647_common_regs[]` and `ov5647_640x480_10bpp[]` (GPL-2.0 -- this file copies no source text
from that driver, only numeric register addresses/values, which are hardware facts about the
silicon, not expression). The tables are not applied byte-identically: `0x0100`/`0x0103` are
owned by this driver's own reset/park sequence; `0x3017` stays at this driver's `0xf0` (the
re-park step, AUTHORIZED LOCAL DIVERGENCE #1, writes it before streaming); `0x3503` is left to the
app's own exposure control; and `0x4800` uses this driver's park/stream-on value (`0x04`).

**Bench evidence** (E1M-AEN803 serial 2026W36-0001 / E1M-EVK hw_rev 2626-r2, DesignWare CSI-2 RX,
RAW10). Run 61 streamed clean: "[stg] 75 regs 0 failed", MFR start `ALP_OK`, zero `E:` lines / CSI
fatals, frame CRC-matched against a real scene. Run 62 verified the committed driver itself, not a
modified bench app: it wrote no mode registers and read back 77 registers against the reference,
0 mismatches; column fixed-pattern noise was 1.65 / 1.19 / 1.18 / 0.97 LSB per Bayer plane (~1.1%
of signal, plane mean ~107, 0.51 s x15.5 gain exposure), down from 6-8 LSB (3.7-5.9%) with an
earlier register mix sourced from Alif's own OV5647 table (Alif Ensemble CMSIS-DFP
`components/Source/OV5647_camera_sensor.c`), which is a variant of the reference rather than an
independent source. Which single register of that earlier mix caused the stripes is not
established. The maintainer confirmed a host-demosaiced colour render of the run-62 frame is the
correct image: orientation `0x3821 = 0x01` / `0x3820 = 0x41` is unmirrored, Bayer order BGGR, green
channels diagonal and equal (107.2 / 106.8). Run 63 re-verified the committed driver (VTS `0x0833`,
`fps_x100=1501`, 77/0 register mismatches, column FPN unchanged). The CSI-2 receiver's
hsfrequency bin 20 (`{300, 0x14}`) is configuration computed from the declared
`VIDEO_CID_PIXEL_RATE` via `video_get_csi_link_freq()`, not evidence; the evidence is that runs
61/62/63 streamed with zero CSI fatals (a PLL/bin mismatch shows up as `ERRSOTSYNCHS` or
`PHY_FATAL`).

**PLL**: `OV5647_PLL_MULT` is 70 (`0x46`, matching the reference's 640x480 10bpp table): VCO
25 MHz / 3 * 70 = 583.33 MHz, lane bit rate 291.67 Mbps/lane, `OV5647_PIXEL_RATE` 58333333. The
reference declares `.pixel_rate = 55000000` for this mode; `OV5647_PIXEL_RATE` is instead derived
from this driver's PLL constants and bench-matched: run 63 measured `fps_x100=1501` at VTS
`0x0833`/HTS 1852, which the driver's VTS formula gives from 58333333, not 55000000. It is one
global PLL for both the 640x480 binned mode and the crop path, so the crop path also runs at
291.67 Mbps/lane -- safe (a lower bit rate cannot exceed the receiver's timing budget) but
unverified against mainline's crop-mode PLL constants; only 640x480 has bench evidence.

**HTS is per mode**: the 640x480 binned mode writes the reference's `0x380c`/`0x380d` = `0x073c`
(1852); the crop path keeps the driver's bench-proven `2700`. `ov5647_frmrate_to_vts()`,
`ov5647_enum_frmival()` and `ov5647_set_frmival()` derive HTS from the active mode via
`ov5647_hts_for()`.

**Default format and frame rate.** The default format before any `set_format()` call is 640x480
SBGGR10P (`ov5647_init()`'s boot format), where 15 fps is reachable (VTS 2099/`0x0833` >=
`480 + 24`); the non-negotiated camera backend path allocates buffers from this default. A full
resolution crop gets a valid, lower rate -- HTS 2700 cannot sustain 15 fps at 1944 lines, a real
line-time limit -- and `video_closest_frmival()` falls back to the next reachable entry.

**Sticky frame interval.** `ov5647_set_frmival()` stores the caller's whole request in
`data->requested_frmival` (a `struct video_frmival`, so a numerator != 1 such as `{2, 60}`, the
shape Zephyr's `video frmival` shell command sends, is preserved) only after
`video_closest_frmival()` and the VTS write both succeed; `ov5647_set_fmt()` re-requests it on every
format change, so a clamped 10 fps at 2592x1944 does not stick after a later `set_format(640x480)`.
`set_frmival()` reports `{1, ov5647_framerates[fie.index]}` -- what `ov5647_enum_frmival()`
produces for that index -- so it never echoes a request that `video_closest_frmival()` did not
match and that was not applied.

**Flip controls survive a format change.** `ov5647_set_mode_regs()` writes `0x3820`/`0x3821` as
whole bytes, so `ov5647_set_fmt()` re-applies both ctrls (`ov5647_set_ctrl_hflip()` /
`ov5647_set_ctrl_vflip()`, also used by `ov5647_set_ctrl()`) right after it. At the defaults the
mode bytes are unaffected: `TC_REG20_BINNED`/`TC_REG21_BINNED` (`0x41`/`0x01`) already equal the
maintainer-confirmed orientation with bits[2:1] clear.

**Bayer order follows the flip ctrls.** Flipping the sensor flips the Bayer colour order. In terms
of this driver's ctrl values (its `HFLIP` bit is the `0x3821` mirror bit directly, the logical
inverse of the reference's `V4L2_CID_HFLIP`), `(hflip, vflip)` maps `(0,0)` to SBGGR (the
maintainer-confirmed default), `(1,0)` to SGBRG, `(0,1)` to SGRBG and `(1,1)` to SRGGB.
`get_format()` reports the flip-adjusted fourcc and `set_format()` accepts it back (mapping it to
its base fourcc when it equals what the current flip ctrls derive), so a `get_format()` ->
`set_format()` round trip works, as does submitting a base fourcc while flipped. Every failure path
of `set_fmt()` restores `fmt->pixelformat` through a single `err:` label. `get_caps()` is
unchanged: callers request the base SBGGR8/SBGGR10P size/depth. Only the default order is
bench/maintainer-verified; the three flipped orders derive from the reference mapping.

**Orientation (maintainer-confirmed, run 62)**: `0x3821` bits[2:1] are this driver's
`OV5647_TC_REG21_MIRROR` mask. `0x01` (bits clear) is correct and unmirrored; Alif's `0x07` produced
a left-right-mirrored scene. The reference's own `hflip` ctrl sense is inverted relative to this:
it reports `hflip=1` for the register state that is the correct unmirrored orientation on this
silicon. `0x3821 = 0x01` pairs with `MEDIA_BUS_FMT_SBGGR10_1X10`, matching the advertised
SBGGR10P/SBGGR8 formats.

`ov5647_set_mode_regs()` picks the full-FOV binned register set for exactly 640x480 (window, output
size, subsample `0x3814`/`0x3815` = `0x35`, binning `0x3820`/`0x3821` = `0x41`/`0x01`, binned-mode
analog `0x3612`/`0x3618`/`0x3708`/`0x3709` = `0x59`/`0x00`/`0x64`/`0x52`, HTS `0x073c`, and the
50/60 Hz AEC band step `0x3a08`/`0x3a09`/`0x3a0a`/`0x3a0b`/`0x3a0d`/`0x3a0e` and `0x4004`). The band
step is in LINES, so it depends on line time/HTS and lives in the per-mode set, not the common
init. Every other size keeps the centred crop and explicitly re-asserts the 1:1 values
(`0x3814`/`0x3815` = `0x11`, `0x3820`/`0x3821` = `0x40`/`0x00`, HTS `2700`, mainline's
full-resolution analog values `0x3612`/`0x3618`/`0x3708`/`0x3709` = `0x5b`/`0x04`/`0x64`/`0x12`,
cited from mainline and bench-unverified on this module) and the crop path's own AEC band step.
Mainline's band step assumes its 32.51 us line time (HTS 2844 / pixel_rate 87500000) while the crop
path runs a 46.29 us line (`OV5647_HTS_CROP` 2700 / `OV5647_PIXEL_RATE` 58333333), so it is scaled by
the line-time ratio: `0x3a08`/`0x3a09` = `0x00`/`0xd0` (208 lines), `0x3a0a`/`0x3a0b` =
`0x00`/`0xad` (173 lines). The max-bands-per-frame registers `0x3a0d`/`0x3a0e` are computed per crop
size from that height's own minimum-blanking VTS (`floor(VTS/band)`, floored at 1 band); at 2592x1944
(VTS 1968) that is `0x0b`/`0x09`. `0x4004` = `0x04`. All crop-path values are bench-unverified.
Writing the binning registers and then letting `ov5647_set_window()` rewrite the window to a crop
made the sensor emit short lines against a 640-pixel frame declaration and the CSI host raised
"Fatal Interrupt due to mismatch of Frame Start and Frame End" on VC0 44 times in 2 s (bench run
54), so the window, output size, subsample, binning, HTS and AEC-band-step registers are always
written as one coherent set per mode.

**Common init** is sourced from the reference's `ov5647_common_regs[]`, minus `0x0100`/`0x0103`
(park/reset), minus `0x3017` (kept at this driver's `0xf0`, AUTHORIZED LOCAL DIVERGENCE #1/#2),
minus `0x3503` (left to this driver's exposure-control logic), and minus the mode-specific AEC band
step registers (including `0x3a08`). It includes the reference's ISP block enables `0x5000 = 0x06`,
`0x5003 = 0x08`, `0x5a00 = 0x08`, which run 61 streamed clean with. Alif's different ISP set
additionally writes `0x5001`/`0x5002` and `0x4050`/`0x4051` (CSI "incorrect frame sequence" fatals
were seen with that set); none of those four are in the reference table and none are written here.
`0x3000`/`0x3001`/`0x3002` = `0x00` and `0x3018` (MIPI PHY/route control) = `0x44` are literal
reference bytes, superseding the targeted `PHY_PD_MIPI`/`PHY_PD_LPRX`/`MIPI_EN` bitfield modify.

`OV5647_EXPOSURE_DEFAULT` moves from `0x20` (2 lines -- effectively a closed shutter for a
manual-exposure user) to `0x0FFF` (~256 lines), matching the order of magnitude of Alif's shipped
default; the AEC gain/limit registers are unchanged. The `VIDEO_CID_ANALOGUE_GAIN` default stays
`0`: auto-gain (`VIDEO_CID_AUTOGAIN`) defaults on, so the manual gain only applies once auto-gain is
disabled, the same gating `VIDEO_CID_EXPOSURE_AUTO` applies to `OV5647_EXPOSURE_DEFAULT`.

**Low light**: at the default 15 fps VTS in a dark lab the AEC railed at both limits (502 lines = 2x
the `0x3a0b` band step; gain at the `0x3a19` ceiling) and a real image needed ~16000 lines (0.49 s)
-- a scene limitation, not a driver bug. The OV5647 is a colour Bayer sensor; the driver delivers
RAW10 BGGR and demosaic is a downstream ISP job, so raw frames viewed as grey show the Bayer mosaic
as fine stripes, which is not the column fixed-pattern noise above.

The vendored driver's RETIREMENT note in `zephyr/drivers/video/ov5647.c` requires all three fixes -- lane park, PLL + MIPI-TX
pad-drive init, and this full-FOV/per-mode-HTS/AEC-band-step/common-init/exposure-default/
frame-rate/flip-ctrl change -- to be confirmed present upstream before the vendored copy can be
deleted.

`tests/zephyr/video_sensors/src/ov5647_test.c` covers: the full 640x480 binned register block
landing after the `0x3034` bit-mode write and before the lane park; the 640x480 default VTS being
the 15 fps value; `ov5647_enum_frmival()` accepting 60 fps and rejecting 90 fps at 640x480; the
run-54 ordering trap (640x480 -> another size -> back never leaves binning, its HTS or its AEC band
step armed on a crop window, checked via the write log on the crop side too); the frame rate not
sticking at a prior mode's clamped value, and preserving a numerator != 1 request across a format
change; `VIDEO_CID_HFLIP`/`VIDEO_CID_VFLIP` surviving a format change (and producing exactly
`0x41`/`0x01` at their defaults); `get_format()` reporting each of the four Bayer orders, RAW8 and
RAW10 `get_format()` -> `set_format()` round trips, and `fmt->pixelformat` restoration on
unsupported fourcc/size requests (including a flip-shifted request); an exhaustive table-driven
check of every `ov5647_init_regs[]` common-init entry (including `0x303c`/`0x3106`/`0x301c`,
`0x3016`/`0x301d`/`0x3017` and `0x3503`/`0x350c`/`0x350d`); and a guard that `0x5001`, `0x5002`,
`0x4050` and `0x4051` are never written. A `ZTEST_SUITE` before-hook resets both flip ctrls, the
frame interval and the format ahead of every test; the emulator's write-log capacity
(`OV5647_EMUL_LOG_CAPACITY`) is 1024. `docs/camera-shields.md`'s OV5647 row and driver section, and
`docs/adr/0017-alp-sdk-over-the-vendor-sdk.md`, are updated to match.

### Fixed — OV5647: park the CSI-2 lanes at LP-11; pixel-rate fix reverted pending further investigation (#2248)

`2248-ov5647-root-cause.md` found two claimed defects in the vendored,
upstream-pending `zephyr/drivers/video/ov5647.c` (backport of
zephyrproject-rtos/zephyr#119301) but left both unpatched, because the file's
header forbids divergent local patches on a verbatim backport. The maintainer
has now explicitly overruled that for the one real fix — an authorized,
recorded divergence, not an oversight — and the header is updated to say so
and to gate the file's eventual retirement on the fix being re-applied or
confirmed present upstream first.

**Fixed — no LP-11 presented, so a Stop-state-gated CSI-2 receiver could
never open the link.** The driver left the sensor in bare software standby
(`0x0100` = `0x00`) after init, in which `CSI_PHY_STOPSTATE` reads
`0x00000000` — no lane at LP-11 — bench-measured on an E1M-AEN803 (serial
2026W36-0001) / E1M-EVK (hw_rev 2626-r2) with a DesignWare CSI-2 receiver.
Writing `0x0100` = `0x01` (sensor running) and then `0x4800` = `0x25`
(`CLOCK_LANE_GATE|BUS_IDLE|CLOCK_LANE_DISABLE`), `0x4202` = `0x0f`, `0x300d` =
`0x01` — in that order, matching mainline Linux's `ov5647_power_on()` calling
`ov5647_stream_stop()` under the comment "Stream off to coax lanes into LP-11
state" — makes the same register read back `0x00000001` steadily (50/50
samples at 20 ms). **CORRECTION (see `2248-ov5647-root-cause.md`)**: this was
originally attributed to "a hardware fault on the module under test, limiting
it to bit0". That is retracted — the module is healthy. The gap to
`0x00010003` (all three lanes) was the vendored driver's power-on `0x3017`
(LP TX pad drive) left too low, fixed separately by bench run 52's
PLL/MIPI-TX pad-drive divergence. A new `ov5647_lane_park()` helper applies
this sequence,
called at the end of `ov5647_init()` so the sensor is left parked rather than
in bare standby, and again from `ov5647_set_stream(dev, false, ...)` so a
stopped stream still presents LP-11 for the next open.
`ov5647_set_stream(dev, true, ...)` unparks first: `0x4800` = `0x04`
(`BUS_IDLE`), `0x4202` = `0x00`, `0x300d` = `0x00`, then the existing
`0x0100` = `0x01`. `ov5647_set_fmt()` now also drops to standby before its
register writes and re-parks afterwards (it previously ran against a running,
parked sensor), and `ov5647_lane_park()`'s error paths make a best-effort
drop back to standby rather than leaving the sensor streaming mid-sequence.

**Investigated, then reverted — the claimed pixel-rate defect.** The
root-cause note claimed `OV5647_PIXEL_RATE(clk)` = `(clk) * 10 / 3`
(83333333 at 25 MHz XVCLK, a datasheet fps figure) was 2.1x too low against
the sensor's power-on PLL registers, and steered the CSI-2 receiver's D-PHY
frequency-bin lookup to the wrong bin. A follow-up commit changed it to a
PLL-derived 175000000; that change was reverted at the time because nothing
had yet programmed the PLL to match it, and both 83333333- and
175000000-implied lane rates landed in the SAME `{450, 0x16}` D-PHY
frequency bin either way, so the revert did not regress bring-up.
`OV5647_PIXEL_RATE` in `zephyr/drivers/video/ov5647.c` was left
byte-identical to its pre-#2248 form at that point.

**CORRECTION (see `2248-ov5647-root-cause.md`)**: this file previously
concluded from that revert that the pixel-rate claim was "disproven" and
83333333 "approximately correct". That conclusion is retracted. 175000000
was actually right about the sensor's *power-on* link rate, and "it doubled
the programmed VTS" was the correct consequence of a doubled pixel clock,
not evidence the number was wrong. The real defect was that the PLL was
never *written* to match either number — bench run 52 fixes that
separately, and `OV5647_PIXEL_RATE` is corrected there to 87500000 (derived
from the same PLL constants the fix now programs), not the 175000000 this
entry describes as reverted. **AT THE TIME (run 52's PLL multiplier 105);
SUPERSEDED by a later #2248 fix-up (run 61), which retargets the
multiplier to 70 to match mainline's 640x480 10bpp table instead of its
full-resolution one — the CURRENT `OV5647_PIXEL_RATE` is 58333333, not
87500000.** See `docs/camera-shields.md` for the full, corrected writeup.

### Added — runtime regression test locking in the OV5647 lane-park fix (#2248)

`zephyr/drivers/video/ov5647.c`'s header requires the vendored, upstream-
pending driver to be deleted the moment the alp-sdk Zephyr pin advances past
a revision containing upstream PR zephyrproject-rtos/zephyr#119301 -- but not
before the lane-park fix from #2248 is confirmed re-applied or already
present. `tests/zephyr/video_sensors` previously covered OV5647 as
compile-only (no emulator); it now also gets a real runtime ztest against a
new I2C emulator, `ov5647_emul.c`, mirroring the OV9281 pair
(`ov9281_emul.c` / `ov9281_test.c`) already in that suite. Both now sit on
native_sim's real `zephyr,i2c-emul-controller` (`&i2c0`), at their existing
addresses (OV5647 `0x36`, OV9281 `0x60`); OV5647 keeps its 2-lane endpoint.

The suite covers only the lane park -- not `OV5647_PIXEL_RATE` /
`VIDEO_CID_PIXEL_RATE`, a previous "fix" to which was investigated,
disproven and reverted, so pinning that value here would cement a number
nobody has validated. Coverage: the chip-ID probe; the parked quartet
(`0x0100`/`0x4800`/`0x4202`/`0x300d` = `0x01`/`0x25`/`0x0f`/`0x01`) after
`ov5647_init()`; that `0x0100` is written running BEFORE the three park
registers, not just that the four end up at the right values -- parking
while still in software standby writes the identical final register content
but never reaches LP-11 (Stop state), a bug a values-only check cannot see;
unpark on `video_stream_start()`; re-park on `video_stream_stop()`; a
stop-then-start cycle leaving the sensor unparked and streaming; and that
`video_set_format()` leaves the sensor parked again afterward, not stuck in
the software standby `ov5647_set_fmt()` drops into before reprogramming the
PLL bit-mode field.

The ordering assertion is the point of the new emulator: past the register
map it already shares with `ov9281_emul.c`'s I2C-transaction model, it also
records every register WRITE in issue order at
`tests/zephyr/video_sensors/src/ov5647_emul.c:116`
("static void ov5647_emul_log_write(struct ov5647_emul_data *data, uint16_t reg, uint8_t value)"),
and `ov5647_test.c` walks the tail of that log against an expected
register/value sequence at
`tests/zephyr/video_sensors/src/ov5647_test.c:326`
("assert_write_sequence_tail(const struct ov5647_emul_write *expect, size_t n, const char *why)")
rather than only reading back final register contents.

Verified both ways: `west twister -T tests/zephyr/video_sensors -p
native_sim -p native_sim/native/64` passes 15/15 test cases on each platform
(8 OV9281 + 7 new OV5647), and reordering the writes inside
`ov5647_lane_park()` (temporarily, reverted before commit) fails the new
ordering test while leaving the final-register-value test green -- proving
the log-based check catches what a values-only one would miss.

### Fixed — OV5647 bring-up: the driver programmed no PLL and no MIPI-TX pad-drive registers; the module was never at fault (#2248)

**CORRECTION to the earlier "root-caused to a module fault" entry in this
file**: that conclusion is retracted. The InnoMaker CAM-OV5647 module is
healthy; the earlier bench finding (`CSI_PHY_STOPSTATE` reading `DATA_0`
50/50 and `DATA_1`/`CLK` 0/50, with an OV9281 on the same cable and
connector reaching `0x00010003`) measured the vendored driver's power-on
LP-TX drive strength, not a silicon defect. With the driver programming no
PLL either, the sensor free-ran at 875 Mbps/lane and a 175 MHz pixel clock
against a receiver binned for 416.67 Mbps — a 2.1x mismatch giving
`ERRSOTSYNCHS` on both data lanes on every burst, with the clock lane
still locking (a clock lane locks far outside the range a data lane can
sync SoT in).

Fixed on an E1M-AEN803 serial 2026W36-0001 / E1M-EVK hw_rev 2626-r2, RAW10
640x480 (bench run 52): `PHY_FATAL` 7712 -> 0, `capture ALP_OK`, 60 frames
at 15.96 fps, frame buffer md5 `61cdf7a021584f4bfaa2ae282c7b2256` with
`a5=0/614400` (every pre-fill byte overwritten), `CAM_FRAME_ADDR`
advancing `0x02000080` -> `0x020960c0`. `zephyr/drivers/video/ov5647.c`
now writes eight registers (`0x3017 0x3035 0x3036 0x3037 0x303c 0x301c
0x301d 0x3106`) in software standby, before the existing lane-park fix
runs — the PLL dividers latch at the `0x0103` software reset, not on
standby exit, so the same writes issued after the park update the
register file without moving the running PLL (a bench run 51 ordering
mistake). PLL values are matched to mainline Linux's own declared
constants (prediv 3, multiplier 105, sysdiv 2 -> 437.5 Mbps/lane, matching
mainline's `link_freq` 218750000) — **AT THE TIME, for mainline's
FULL-RESOLUTION mode; SUPERSEDED by a later #2248 fix-up (run 61), which
retargets the multiplier to 70 (291.67 Mbps/lane, `OV5647_PIXEL_RATE`
58333333) to match mainline's 640x480 10bpp table instead, since 640x480
is the mode this driver actually ships. Do not read 105 / 437.5 Mbps as
current.** `0x3017` (LP TX pad drive) is
bench-bisected: reset `0x10` -> no lane reaches Stop state; `pgm_lptx =
01` -> `DATA_0` only; `10` -> `+DATA_1`; `11` -> `+CLK`, reaching
`CSI_PHY_STOPSTATE` = `0x00010003` with `0x3017` = `0xf0` — one step
higher drive than mainline's `0xe0`, which never brings the clock lane to
Stop state; mainline's own receiver does not gate on that lane but ours
does. This is a second AUTHORIZED divergence on top of the existing
lane-park fix, recorded the same way in the file header.

`OV5647_PIXEL_RATE` is also corrected, not "disproven" as this file
previously said: a prior attempt to fix it in isolation to a PLL-derived
175000000 was reverted, and a follow-up investigation concluded that
attempt was wrong and the unmodified upstream value was "approximately
correct". Both conclusions are now retracted: 175000000 was actually
right about the *power-on* link rate, and "it doubled the programmed VTS"
was the correct consequence of a doubled pixel clock, not evidence against
it. The defect was that the PLL was never *written* at all. The macro now
derives from the same PLL constants the register table programs
(`OV5647_PLL_PREDIV`/`MULT`/`SYS_DIV`), giving 87500000 at 25 MHz XVCLK —
matching mainline's own declared `pixel_rate` for this PLL **AT THE TIME
(run 52's multiplier 105); SUPERSEDED by run 61's multiplier 70, which
gives the CURRENT value 58333333 — see the later #2248 fix-up fragment.
Do not read 87500000 as the driver's current `OV5647_PIXEL_RATE`.**

**Honest limits, not established by this fix**: which of the eight
run-52 registers are individually load-bearing — only `0x3017` is
independently bisected; the rest are shipped together because, matched to
mainline's values, that is what bench-proved. `0x4837` (PCLK period)
stays at its power-on `0x15` (mainline writes `0x19`); safe at 437.5 Mbps
at the time, and safer still after run 61 lowers the bit rate further to
291.67 Mbps — not changed in either working run. `0x3017` = `0xf0` has no
characterised drive-strength margin. `OV5647_PIXEL_RATE`'s correction is
fixed at 10bpp (RAW10, the only bench-proven format); the 8-bit (SBGGR8)
path would need a different pixel rate that this change does not derive
or verify — flagged in the driver, not fixed. AT THE TIME (run 52's PLL)
that value would have been 109375000; with the driver's CURRENT PLL (run
61, multiplier 70) the equivalent 8-bit value is 72916666 — still neither
derived nor verified, the gap simply moved with the PLL correction.
`CSI_PHY_RX`/`CSI_PHY_STOPSTATE` read byte-identically in the failing and
working runs at every capture point and should not be used alone as a
bring-up gate.

A new runtime regression test asserts the eight registers are written
*while the sensor is in software standby and before the park sets*
`0x0100` = `0x01`, not just that the values are eventually present — a
values-only check would pass the exact reordered variant that cost bench
run 51.

`docs/camera-shields.md` records the corrected root cause, the run-52
evidence, and all of the above limits. The OV5647 shield is now
bench-verified for RAW10; RAW8 is unverified.

### Fixed — absent OV9281 sensor reported `ALP_ERR_IO`, indistinguishable from a genuine I2C bus fault (#2249)

`alp_camera_open()` on the E1M-EVK's J5 CSI-2 pipeline (InnoMaker
CAM-OV9281) returned `ALP_ERR_IO` when no sensor was connected -- the same
code a real bus fault produces -- instead of `ALP_ERR_NOT_READY`. Confirmed
on an E1M-AEN803 (2026W36-0009) with nothing on J5: `RESULT FAIL: camera
did not open -- ALP_ERR_IO` on 3 of 3 cold cycles.

`ov9281.c`'s `ov9281_init()` already reads and validates the sensor's
chip-ID registers (`0x300A`/`0x300B`, a fixed `0x9281`) and correctly fails
its own init -- and therefore its own `device_is_ready()` -- when the
sensor never answers. That not-ready state just never reached
`alp_camera_open()`: `alp-camera0` resolves to the CPI capture controller
(`&cam`, `video_alif.c`'s `alif_video_cam_init()`), which only checked that
its upstream device pointer was non-NULL, and the DesignWare CSI-2 host in
between (`&csi`, `video_csi_dw.c`'s `csi2_dw_init()`) only checked that a
sensor pointer/D-PHY mapping existed in devicetree -- neither called
`device_is_ready()` on the device downstream of it. So an absent sensor
sailed through `alp_camera_open()`'s readiness gate at the CPI and only
surfaced later, as an I2C NACK (`-EIO`) on the first `video_set_format()`
forwarded all the way down to the sensor, which `_errno_to_alp()` maps to
`ALP_ERR_IO`.

The first attempt at this fix added a `device_is_ready()` check to each
driver's own `_init()` and was wrong: dev-review caught, from a built
image's `.z_init_POST_KERNEL_P_*` link order (`aen-camera-firstlight`,
`alp_e1m_aen803_m55_he`, `SHIELD="e1m_evk_rpi_csi innomaker_cam_ov9281"` --
`csi@49033000` at priority 41, `cam@49030000` at priority 59, `ov9281` at
priority 60), that `csi2_dw_init()` (`CONFIG_VIDEO_MIPI_CSI2_DW_INIT_PRIORITY`,
default 41) and `alif_video_cam_init()` (`CONFIG_VIDEO_ALIF_CAM_INIT_PRIORITY`,
default 59) both run strictly *before* a sensor's own
`CONFIG_VIDEO_INIT_PRIORITY` (default 60, e.g. `ov9281.c`/`arx3a0.c`) --
`CONFIG_CHECK_INIT_PRIORITIES` cannot catch this because the dependency is a
DT `remote-endpoint-label` string, not a `zephyr,init-dep` edge. A
readiness check at init time therefore always saw the sensor as
not-yet-initialized and rejected a genuinely *present* one too, breaking
every Alif CPI camera path.

Both intermediate drivers now check readiness at first USE instead --
`csi2_dw_sensor_ready()` (called from `csi2_dw_get_caps()`/
`csi2_dw_set_format()`/`csi2_dw_get_format()`) and
`alif_cam_endpoint_ready()` (called from `alif_cam_get_caps()`/
`alif_cam_set_fmt()`/`alif_cam_get_fmt()`), both returning `-ENODEV`. By the
time an application calls `alp_camera_open()`, every driver's own
`POST_KERNEL` init -- including the sensor's chip-ID check -- has already
run regardless of priority ordering, so checking there is correct without
requiring any priority reshuffle across drivers (ISP-Pico, ARX3A0, or any
`prj.conf` override). `alp_camera_open()`'s existing `!device_is_ready(dev)`
check at `src/backends/camera/zephyr_video.c` -- unchanged -- still gates
the CPI device itself (a real hardware-init failure inside
`alif_video_cam_init()`, e.g. clocks/pinctrl, as opposed to sensor
absence); `alif_video_cam_init()` only ever checked `config->endpoint_dev
!= NULL`, never the CSI-2 host's own readiness, so a CSI-2 host init
failure is now caught by the new `alif_cam_endpoint_ready()` at first use,
not by that unchanged check. `_errno_to_alp()`'s existing `-ENODEV` mapping
is what turns the new checks into `ALP_ERR_NOT_READY`. No new error code.

Bench-verified on E1M-AEN803 2026W36-0009 (Flow C
RAM-run on the M55-HE, `aen-camera-firstlight`), absent-sensor path: with
the `raspberry_pi_camera_module_1` (OV5647 @`0x36`) shield and no OV5647
fitted, the unfixed build reports `alp_camera_open FAILED: ALP_ERR_IO` and
the fixed build `ALP_ERR_NOT_READY`. The same held for the
`innomaker_cam_ov9281` shield (unfixed `ALP_ERR_IO`, fixed
`ALP_ERR_NOT_READY`), because that board had no camera fitted: a direct
probe of I2C1 (`0x49011000`) got an ACK from the GT911 at `0x14` and a
7-bit address NACK (`IC_TX_ABRT_SOURCE = 0x00000001`) at `0x60`.
**The present-sensor path is therefore not
bench-verified** -- that a fitted, answering sensor still opens rests on
the init-order measurement above, not on a run.

### Fixed — an absent CSI-2 camera sensor now opens as `ALP_ERR_NOT_READY` (#2249)

`alp_camera_open()` on the AEN CSI-2 pipeline returned `ALP_ERR_IO` when no
sensor was fitted, the same code as a genuine I2C fault. The sensor driver
already failed its own chip-ID init, but the CPI (`video_alif.c`) and the
CSI-2 host (`video_csi_dw.c`) init before the sensor, so neither could check
it at init time, and the sensor's `get_caps` returns a static table without
touching I2C. The absence only surfaced as an I2C NACK on the first
`set_format`.

Both drivers' `get_caps` forwarders now check `device_is_ready()` on the
device below them and return `-ENODEV`, which the portable camera backend
maps to `ALP_ERR_NOT_READY`.

Verified on E1M-AEN803 2026W36-0009 with nothing on the EVK's J5 connector:
`aen-camera-firstlight` with the `innomaker_cam_ov9281` shield now prints
`alp_camera_open FAILED: ALP_ERR_NOT_READY`.

### Added — Alif Ensemble E8 ISP-Pico: real AE/AWB through the standard Zephyr video ctrl path (#2252)

`zephyr/drivers/video/isp_pico.c` (the VeriSilicon ISP Nano driver,
`vsi,isp-pico`) now drives auto white balance and auto exposure/gain through
the same portable Zephyr video ctrl registry any other video device uses --
`VIDEO_CID_AUTO_WHITE_BALANCE` and `VIDEO_CID_EXPOSURE_AUTO` on the ISP
device -- instead of the driver having no `.set_ctrl` at all (the v4.4
video-API port had dropped the fork driver's old value-pointer ctrl
callbacks along with their only callers of the hal_alif libisp wrapper's
`isp_vsi_set_param()`/`isp_vsi_get_param()`).

3A (AWB + AE) runs from the calibration by default (hal_alif patch 0009,
below) -- a generic ISP driver has no business embedding its own calibration
table, so `isp_apply_wb()` round-trips `isp_vsi_get_param()`/
`isp_vsi_set_param()` to flip only `.enable`/`.op_mode` on whatever
calibration the integrator's build already compiled in (`isp_param_conf.h`,
selected by which `CONFIG_ISP_LIB_*_MODULE` Kconfigs are on) -- no sensor
calibration table lives in this driver. AE's own limits (exposure-time
ceiling, gain ceiling) have no calibration-table equivalent for this sensor,
so they are pushed once, at the first stream start: the exposure-time
ceiling from the sensor's own reported frame interval (`video_get_frmival()`,
now forwarded down the isp -> cam -> csi -> sensor chain by new
`.get_frmival` implementations in `video_alif.c`/`video_csi_dw.c`) and the
gain ceiling from the sensor's own registered `VIDEO_CID_ANALOGUE_GAIN` range
(`video_query_ctrl()`) -- both sensor-agnostic; the one remaining
sensor-specific constant is the register-value-to-library-fixed-point gain
conversion factor, which a future sensor with a different "1x" register value
would need to update. Whenever `CONFIG_ISP_LIB_AE_MODULE` is built, the
driver also forces the sensor's own `EXPOSURE_AUTO`/`AUTOGAIN` to
manual/off at every stream start (`isp_apply_ae_sensor_gate()`), in both
library AE modes, so the ISP's own exposure/gain write-back
(`VIDEO_CID_EXPOSURE`/`VIDEO_CID_ANALOGUE_GAIN`) never fights the sensor's
own AEC. A `k_mutex` now serializes the hal_alif library calls
between the app thread (`isp_set_ctrl()`) and the ISP's own frame-end
workqueue (`isp_bottom_half()`); a ctrl change made mid-stream is recorded
but only takes effect at the next stream start (the ISP must be stopped for
an apply to stick), not live. The `<alp/camera.h>` viewfinder path now also
recycles stale buffers instead of leaking them across a restart.

`isp_flush()`'s stop path (`cancel=true`) now cancel-syncs the frame-end
bottom half before draining buffers back to the caller, closing a window
where an already-queued (or mid-run) bottom half could still hand hardware a
buffer after the caller believed it owned every buffer back. The other path
(`cancel=false`, a plain flush while streaming) waits for the fifo to drain
the normal way, one frame-end at a time, but that wait is bounded: if it
times out with the MI still DMA-ing into the current buffer, it now returns
`-ETIMEDOUT` and leaves every queue and the streaming state untouched,
instead of draining a fifo the hardware is still writing into and reporting
a stop that never happened. A caller that hits the timeout can retry with
`cancel=true`, which does stop the ISP before it drains.

`zephyr/drivers/video/video_alif.c` (the Alif CPI capture controller): the
packed/unpacked Bayer-fourcc translation table (`cpi_unpacked_fmts[]`) now
`break`s on both the forward and reverse lookups. Each `.mem`/`.link` value
is already unique in the table, so neither lookup was actually ambiguous;
the `break`s are defensive/symmetry only, guarding against a future
duplicate row rather than fixing an observed collision.

`zephyr/drivers/video/video_csi_dw.c` (the DesignWare CSI-2 host bridge):
`csi2_dw_init()` now masks every `CSI_INT_MSK_*` interrupt source before
arming the NVIC line, and `csi2_dw_irq_on()` reads (clears) every
read-to-clear `CSI_INT_ST_*` status register before unmasking the real
sources -- closing a window where the CSI-2 host's own interrupt could fire
from a stale/reset register state while a sensor on the same bus was still
completing its own power-up lane park.

hal_alif v2.3.0 carry patches (`zephyr/patches/hal_alif/`): 0003 adds a
packed-BGGR10 Bayer-fourcc-to-pixel-format mapping the wrapper was missing;
0004 fixes a `CONFIG_` prefix typo that silently disabled an AWB-measurement
Kconfig; 0005 ports the AE module's sensor write-back
(`isp_vsi_bottom_half()`) from the pre-v4.4 3-argument `video_set_ctrl()`
form to the pinned Zephyr v4.4.1 `struct video_control` API (dead code until
now -- no example previously enabled `CONFIG_ISP_LIB_AE_MODULE`), and
latches its own write-back failures to log once rather than once per frame;
0006 replaces a generic placeholder sensor-timing table with values derived
from a real sensor's own register facts; 0007 guards `VSI_MPI_ISP_SetCalib()`
in `isp_vsi_update_cfg()` with a once-flag, so the calibration blob loads
once instead of being reloaded (and stomping the driver's own runtime AE/WB
state) on every restart; 0008 carries an OV5647-derived AWB/CCM calibration
(centre line, white-point range, illuminant gains, CCM matrices), selected
by `CONFIG_VIDEO_ISP_VSI_CALIB_OV5647`, in place of the compiled-in ARX3A0
one -- RPi-derived (Raspberry Pi libcamera's `ov5647.json`, BSD-2-Clause),
then scaled onto the INNO-MAKER module on the bench (kR 0.770, kB 0.778;
runs 159/162) against the untouched ARX3A0 table's own internal gain
relation; one scene, provisional, flagged for a further bench-driven
retune. CCM amplifies an existing low-saturation cast on this module's
room scenes (runs 163/164) rather than causing it: runs 171/172
(colour-bar test pattern, all 8 bars at the correct hue and full
saturation, CCM on -- run 172 through `<alp/camera.h>`) and run 178 (the
pattern's faded and dark bars land exactly where expected, e.g. pure red
at raw 110 gives V +50 = BT.601) show the ISP pipeline is colour-correct,
and run 176 (a same-frame CPI raw-vs-ISP comparison) shows the ISP
matches the raw scene to 1.5% while the raw scene itself varies only ~4%
(white ceiling raw R/G 0.98, B/G 0.97). So the muted colour and cast come
from the sensor/lens (likely an IR leak) plus the provisional AWB/CCM
calibration, not from the ISP; CCM ships enabled
(`CONFIG_ISP_LIB_CCM_MODULE=y`) in both ov5647 examples' `prj.conf` --
`aen-isp-capture` and `aen-isp-ov5647-viewfinder`, same as
`aen-isp-regcheck` -- and a grey-card/chart calibration will retune that
provisional calibration; the sensor/lens sets the room-colour ceiling.
0009 moves
`VSI_MPI_ISP_SetCalib()` to before the AWB/AE algorithm callbacks are
registered in `isp_vsi_init()`, matching upstream's own order -- without it
neither algorithm ever converges (both callbacks register against a library
that hasn't loaded a calibration yet), so this is the fix that actually gets
AWB/AE running at all.

The AWB/CCM calibration is provisional (one scene, RPi-derived); room-scene
colour stays muted (saturation 0.16 with CCM on vs 0.08 off) because the
sensor/lens delivers a nearly neutral raw scene (±4%, likely IR leak; run
176, ISP matches raw to 1.5%), not because the ISP loses colour.

`examples/aen/aen-isp-capture`: a real OV5647 sensor frame through
the full camera -> csi -> cpi -> isp -> memory graph. AE + AWB run by
driver default now (no ctrl calls needed to turn them on), mirroring Alif's
own sdk-alif `samples/drivers/viewfinder` recipe.

User-visible backend changes: `src/backends/camera/alif_isp_pico.c` (the
`<alp/camera.h>` `alif_isp_pico` backend) never gets RGB565 straight from
the ISP -- its MI output is YUV/mono/Bayer only -- so a caller requesting
`ALP_PIXFMT_RGB565` now has that negotiated as a YUV format instead (YUV420
planar tried first, YUYV as the fallback) and converted to RGB565 on the
CPU, via the new table-driven fast path in `src/backends/camera/
yuv_to_rgb565.h` (`tests/unit/camera_yuv_to_rgb565` covers it) rather than
the naive per-pixel reference converter. The backend also recycles stale
buffers instead of leaking them across a restart. New example:
`examples/aen/aen-isp-ov5647-viewfinder`, the portable-header counterpart to
`aen-isp-capture` -- same OV5647 pipeline, driven entirely through
`<alp/camera.h>` instead of the raw Zephyr video API. `examples/aen/
aen-isp-regcheck` is updated to match the ISP init-order fix below.

`zephyr/drivers/video/isp_pico.c`: `video_isp_init()` previously enabled the
ISP's IRQs before `fifo_in`/`fifo_out`/`data->dev`/`lib_lock` existed. A core
reset does not reset the ISP, so an MI frame-end already latched by a
previous image could fire the instant the IRQs came on, and the frame-end
bottom half would then lock an uninitialised mutex and HardFault during
boot. IRQs are now enabled last, after that state exists, and the bottom
half ignores frame-ends while no stream is running so a stale latched
frame-end never reaches the VSI lib before `isp_configure()` runs
(bench runs 165/166).

### Fixed — E8 ISP-Pico: 4:2:0 output chroma was vertically wrapped, corrupting real-scene colour (#2255)

Bench-proven on E1M-AEN803 + OV5647 (runs 186/187): the ISP core always
produces 4:2:2 chroma internally, and neither `VSI_MPI_ISP_SetScaleAttr()`
(closed VSI lib) nor `zephyr/drivers/video/isp_pico.c` ever programmed the
main resizer's (MRSZ) vertical chroma downscaler — `MRSZ_CTRL`, `SCALE_VC`,
and `FORMAT_CONV_CTRL` all read back 0 at stream start. For a 4:2:0 MI
output (`VIDEO_PIX_FMT_YUV420`/`NV12`/`NV21`) this meant the MI wrote a
full-height chroma plane (e.g. 480 lines) into a half-height buffer sized
for the format's own subsampling, wrapping the Cb/Cr write address ("Main
picture Cb/Cr address wrap" in the MI ISR) and leaving the bottom half of
each frame's chroma corrupted. Luma was unaffected and vertical colour bars
looked correct, which is why this was not caught by the bar-pattern
regression; a real scene lost or misplaced colour.

`isp_stream_start()` now programs MRSZ directly right after `isp_vsi_start()`
succeeds: for a 4:2:0 output it computes `SCALE_VC` from the actual output
height (`((height/2 - 1) * 65536) / (height - 1)`), zeroes `PHASE_VC`, sets
`FORMAT_CONV_CTRL` to 4:2:0, and enables the scaler with `CFG_UPD`/
`AUTO_UPD`; any other output format bypasses MRSZ, zeroing
`FORMAT_CONV_CTRL`/`SCALE_VC`/`PHASE_VC` before `CTRL=CFG_UPD` so a previous
4:2:0 stream's config cannot persist into a 4:2:2/raw one — `FORMAT_CONV_CTRL`
is not `CFG_UPD`-shadowed and takes effect immediately, so it must be cleared
explicitly rather than left at a stale 4:2:0 setting. `isp_set_fmt()` also
now rejects a 4:2:0 output height that is odd or below 4 (`-EINVAL`), and
`isp_apply_mrsz()` bypasses defensively below that height, closing a
reachable divide-by-zero (`DIV_0_TRP`) in the `SCALE_VC` computation.

### Fixed — E8 ISP-Pico's TPG branch refuses a 0x0 port rect instead of leaving `VSI_MPI_ISP_SetChnAttr` to fail with `-EINVAL` (#2256)

`isp_configure()`'s test-pattern-generator branch (`zephyr/drivers/video/isp_pico.c`)
set the TPG pixel format but never `port_fmt.width`/`height`, so
`VSI_MPI_ISP_SetChnAttr` got a 0x0 port rect and failed with `-EINVAL`
("Setting the Channel config failed!", bench-confirmed on E1M-AEN803
2026W36-0009 -- runs 179-181 confirmed 1280x720 and 1920x1080 both make
`SetChnAttr` succeed). The binding
(`zephyr/dts/bindings/video/vsi,isp-pico.yaml`) now carries
`tpg-width`/`tpg-height` (default 0, fail closed); `examples/aen/aen-isp-regcheck`'s
two overlays now set 1920x1080, the TPG's real size (below). `isp_set_fmt(INPUT)` also no longer calls
`video_set_format()` on a NULL `config->controller` (TPG-only builds have no
camera pipeline to forward to), per the issue's "Next step". Adds a
`native_sim` unit test for the new `isp_tpg_geometry_is_valid()` guard
(`tests/unit/isp_pico_tpg_geometry`).

Finding 2 narrowed on silicon (E1M-AEN803 serial 2026W36-0001). The TPG's
frame size is not hidden: disassembling `VSI_ISP_CoreSetTpg` in `libisp_gcc.a`
shows it writes fixed timing whatever size is requested -- only the CTRL
resolution bits change -- and a read-back after configure gives
`TPG_ACT_IN` = 1920 x 1080 active (total 2844 x 1968), with the acquisition
window (`ACQ_H_SIZE`/`ACQ_V_SIZE`) also at 1920 x 1080. With the geometry
matched end to end, every TPG frame still raises `INTR_SIZE_ERR`
(`int_st 0x00000008`, 143 frames), so the violation comes from another
window in the closed pipeline, not the TPG/acquisition size. That, and
finding 3 (YUYV MI output never completing), stay open. Refs #2256, does
not close it.

### Fixed — `isp_pico.c`: dequeued YUV420/NV12 buffers reported `bytesused` 0 (pitch tracked luma only) (#2259)

Silicon-proven on E1M-AEN803 (bench run 200). `zephyr/drivers/video/isp_pico.c`'s
`isp_dequeue()` sized every dequeued buffer as `channel->output_fmt.pitch *
channel->output_fmt.height`, and `src/backends/camera/alif_isp_pico.c`
negotiates the output format with `pitch = 0`. For a pass-through YUV
request (`ALP_PIXFMT_YUV420_PLANAR` / `ALP_PIXFMT_NV12` through
`<alp/camera.h>`), every dequeued buffer therefore reported `bytesused = 0`,
so the backend returned `out->size = 0` and callers copied nothing and saw
stale memory. The RGB565 path hid this because the backend converts using
`width*height`, not `bytesused`; the post-dequeue cache invalidate (guarded
by `CONFIG_DCACHE=y`) also keyed off `bytesused`, so it invalidated 0 bytes
too.

Both `isp_set_fmt()`'s pitch fill-in and `isp_dequeue()`'s `bytesused` now
route through a new shared header,
`zephyr/include/zephyr/drivers/video/isp_frame_size.h` -- the same header
`alif_isp_pico.c`'s buffer-pool sizing includes, so all three call sites
share one implementation instead of three independently-driftable copies:

- `alp_isp_default_pitch()` fills an unset (`pitch == 0`) output pitch: for
  planar/semi-planar YUV (`YUV420`/`YVU420`/`NV12`/`NV21`/`NV16`/`NV61`/
  `NV24`/`NV42`) that's the luma-only line stride (one byte per pixel),
  never `video_bits_per_pixel()`'s chroma-subsampled average (12 bpp for
  4:2:0, i.e. `width*1.5`, not a whole number of bytes/pixel); every other
  fourcc uses `bpp * width / 8`. `isp_set_fmt()` now returns `-EINVAL` if
  this comes back 0 (an output fourcc neither this function nor
  `video_bits_per_pixel()` can size) instead of silently latching a
  zero pitch. The driver's own RGB888-planar-private default-output-format
  path (`isp_get_fmt()`, hit when no output format has been negotiated yet)
  had the same zero-pitch bug and now goes through the same helper.
- `alp_isp_frame_size()` sizes `bytesused` (and `alif_isp_pico.c`'s
  buffer-pool allocation) off the format's true average bits/pixel,
  chroma included -- `width*height*bpp/8` -- never `pitch * height`, which
  after the pitch fix would size a planar buffer for the luma plane alone.
  `isp_dequeue()`'s `bytesused` is additionally capped at the buffer's own
  `size`, so a mis-sized buffer can't make the following
  `sys_cache_data_invd_range()` invalidate past its end.
- `alp_isp_pixel_bpp()` extends `video_bits_per_pixel()`, which returns 0
  for the two Alp Lab-private fourccs `VIDEO_PIX_FMT_YUV422P` and
  `VIDEO_PIX_FMT_RGB888_PLANAR_PRIVATE` (`isp_pico.c`'s own default output
  format) -- sized the way `fourcc_to_plane_size()`
  (`zephyr/drivers/video/video_alif.c`) splits their planes: `YUV422P` at
  16 bpp (1/2 + 1/4 + 1/4), `RGB888_PLANAR_PRIVATE` at 24 bpp (three equal
  1/3 planes). Both were 0-pitch/0-`bytesused` before this fix too.

Unit-tested under `tests/unit/isp_frame_size/` on `native_sim` -- the test
includes the exact header the driver and backend call, not a stand-in copy,
covering all three helpers (`alp_isp_default_pitch()`,
`alp_isp_frame_size()`, the `YUV420`/`NV12`/`RGB565`/`YUV422P`/
`RGB888_PLANAR_PRIVATE` cases).

Also fixed in passing: `supported_output_fmts[]`'s `YUV422P` entry advertised
a `width_max` of `19200` (a typo -- every other entry in that table is
`1920`), and `examples/aen/aen-isp-capture/src/main.c` set
`.pitch = FRAME_WIDTH*3/2` for its `YUV420` output format, which was never
the luma stride this driver now expects -- both corrected to `1920` /
`FRAME_WIDTH`.

### Fixed — AEN Ethernet: pin GMAC descriptor rings + net_buf pools to SRAM0 without moving all of main RAM (#2260)

On Alif E8 (E1M-AEN801/803), the GMAC DMA cannot reach the M55 DTCM: the descriptor
rings and the net_buf packet pool must live in the global on-chip SRAM0
(`0x02000000`). The fix so far was `chosen { zephyr,sram = &sram0; }` in
`examples/aen/aen-ethernet-link`'s board overlays, which moves **all** of main
RAM off DTCM to SRAM0 — slower than DTCM for everything that is not Ethernet-DMA
traffic, and it intermittently broke the ISP.

**Silicon-verified on E1M-AEN803 (bench run 202):** pin only the Ethernet-owned
buffers to SRAM0 and leave main RAM on DTCM. `aen-ethernet-link` built from this
mechanism (`b240f01cb`) on E1M-AEN803 pulled DHCP lease `192.168.10.123`,
reported `PHY link UP after 2000 ms`, was confirmed server-side (dnsmasq
DHCPACK), passed host ping 5/5 (avg 0.271 ms) with the neighbour `REACHABLE`,
and the live descriptor rings at `0x02001740`/`0x02001840` resolved into
`net_buf_data_rx/tx_bufs` (`0x0200xxxx`), while `_kernel` and main RAM stayed on
DTCM. E1M-AEN801 is build-verified only (same E8 memory map, not itself
benched). `examples/aen/aen-evk-demo`'s use of the same mechanism — sharing its
64 KiB SRAM0 window between the relocated buffers and separate JPEG buffers —
is build-verified only, not benched. An earlier, different prototype of the
same placement idea ran on silicon in scratch bench run 200, but that scratch
used a different app-level relocation of net_pkt.c and the glue file,
`CONFIG_NOCACHE_MEMORY=y`, and different ring addresses than this mechanism.

`zephyr/dts/bindings/ethernet/alif,ethernet.yaml` gains an optional
`memory-region` phandle property (precedent:
`zephyr/dts/bindings/display/tes,cdc-2.1.yaml:98`, "memory-region:").
`zephyr/dts/alif/ensemble_e8_peripherals.dtsi`'s
`ethernet` node sets `memory-region = <&sram0>;`. `zephyr/drivers/ethernet/eth_dwmac_alif_ensemble.c`
places `dwmac_tx_descs`/`dwmac_rx_descs` in that DT region via
`Z_GENERIC_SECTION(LINKER_DT_NODE_REGION_NAME(DT_INST_PHANDLE(0, memory_region)))`
when the node carries `memory-region`, falling back to the previous
(`zephyr,sram`-inherited) placement when it does not; the `BUILD_ASSERT` that
`CONFIG_DCACHE` stays off is unconditional now (the E8 D-cache maintenance loop
hangs on this silicon, see `scripts/bench/aen/aen-bench-shared.conf`) — there is
no more `__nocache` arm, since with `memory-region` set that would conflict with
the section the DT region already gives the rings and fail to build when
`CONFIG_NOCACHE_MEMORY=y`. The rings are uncached solely because `CONFIG_DCACHE`
is required off, not because their section is itself tagged nocache.

`zephyr/kconfigs/vendor-alif-peripherals.kconfig` drops `ETH_DWMAC_ALIF`'s
`select NOCACHE_MEMORY if ARCH_HAS_NOCACHE_MEMORY_SUPPORT` (its nocache section
lands in DTCM, which the DMA cannot see) and adds
`ETH_DWMAC_ALIF_NET_BUF_IN_DMA_REGION` (default y, depends on `ETH_DWMAC_ALIF` +
`NETWORKING`), selecting `CODE_DATA_RELOCATION`. `zephyr/CMakeLists.txt` resolves
the region the same way the driver resolves the node — `dt_comp_path(...
COMPATIBLE "alif,ethernet" INDEX 0)`, then the `memory-region` phandle, then
that node's `zephyr,memory-region` string (single phandle properties export as
node paths) — and calls `zephyr_code_relocate(FILES ${ZEPHYR_BASE}/subsys/net/ip/net_pkt.c
LOCATION <REGION>_DATA / _BSS / _NOINIT)`; `net_pkt.c`'s net_buf pools are
`__noinit`. Both the Kconfig help and the CMake comment say this prints a
CMake `WARNING` (not a silent no-op) when the Kconfig is on but no usable region
resolves. LIMIT, called out in the binding, the Kconfig help and the README:
only `net_pkt.c`'s own pools are relocated — an application's own net_buf pool
(e.g. `NET_PKT_DATA_POOL_DEFINE` via `net_context_setup_pools`) still lands on
DTCM and the DMA would silently fail against it.

**HAZARD GUARD.** Because the SoC dtsi now sets `memory-region = <&sram0>;`
unconditionally, a board/app overlay that ALSO points `chosen { zephyr,sram =
...; }` at that same node (e.g. the old whole-RAM-move `&sram0`) would make the
linker allocate BOTH the whole system-RAM region and the memory-region's linker
region into the identical address window, independently, with no link-time
warning — main RAM silently aliasing on top of the relocated buffers, the exact
class of corruption `examples/aen/aen-evk-demo`'s overlay already documents and
avoids with a disjoint-window layout. `zephyr/CMakeLists.txt` now resolves
`chosen zephyr,sram` via `dt_chosen(... PROPERTY "zephyr,sram")` and
`FATAL_ERROR`s at configure time when it resolves to the same node as the
ethernet node's `memory-region` while `CONFIG_ETH_DWMAC_ALIF_NET_BUF_IN_DMA_REGION=y`,
naming the two fixes (drop the `chosen` override, or `/delete-property/
memory-region;` + `CONFIG_ETH_DWMAC_ALIF_NET_BUF_IN_DMA_REGION=n`). Proven: a
build of `aen-ethernet-link` with an extra overlay re-adding
`chosen { zephyr,sram = &sram0; }` now fails configure with that message; the
normal build (no such overlay) still passes.

`examples/aen/aen-ethernet-link`'s board overlays (both AEN801 and AEN803, kept
content-identical) drop `zephyr,sram = &sram0` — main RAM now stays on DTCM.
`docs/aen-bench-bringup.md`, the example README, `src/main.c`'s file header and
`testcase.yaml` are updated to describe the new placement and its bench-run-202
evidence, without pairing the 2026-06-17 DHCP-lease bench evidence (which used
the whole-RAM-move mechanism) with the new narrower one.

Because the ethernet node's `memory-region` is now set at the SoC-dtsi level,
it also applies to `examples/aen/aen-evk-demo`, which shrinks `&sram0`'s linker
region to a 64 KiB window shared with phase 13's JPEG buffers: the GMAC
descriptor rings and the relocated net_buf pools now land in that same window
too, and `jpeg_out` no longer starts at `0x02000000`. Several of that
example's comments described a stale state and are corrected: the two
overlays' "no narrower fix available to an application ... so system RAM
moves" claim and address-map table; `prj.conf`'s comment about
`eth_dwmac_alif`'s BUILD_ASSERT being an OR that `select NOCACHE_MEMORY`
satisfied unconditionally (now unconditional, so `CONFIG_DCACHE=y` fails the
build — proven by building with it set); `testcase.yaml`'s description of the
same removed OR-assert; and the README's "Memory map" section, which now
mirrors the overlay's corrected address-map table. `sram0_sys` (the separate
512 KiB system-RAM window) is left in place; whether it could now be dropped
in favour of the generated `zephyr,sram = &dtcm` default is an open question
this change does not answer.

**Silicon finding, bench runs 203/204 (E1M-AEN803, ETH_DWMAC_ALIF):** with
Zephyr's default `CONFIG_NET_BUF_DATA_SIZE=128`, every Ethernet frame above
896 B (more than 7 fixed 128-byte fragments) was silently dropped — ICMP
payloads of 56 and 868 B passed, 869/1000/1400/1472 B lost 100%, and any TCP
body segment was lost too (HTTP headers arrived over a 13737-byte JPEG body
that never did). Changing only `CONFIG_NET_BUF_DATA_SIZE` to 1536 made every
one of those ping sizes pass at 0% loss, and a TCP MJPEG stream then ran at
17 fps, ~12.8 KB/frame; `DWMAC_NB_TX_DESCS`/`DWMAC_NB_RX_DESCS` were 16 in
both builds. `zephyr/kconfigs/vendor-alif-peripherals.kconfig` now redefines
`config NET_BUF_DATA_SIZE` with `default 1536 if ETH_DWMAC_ALIF`, the standard
Zephyr module-Kconfig-overrides-a-subsys-default pattern: Kconfig picks the
first matching `default` in file-parse order, and `zephyr/Kconfig` `rsource`s
this file, which `Kconfig.zephyr` sources via `source "modules/Kconfig"`
before `source "subsys/Kconfig"` (the path that eventually defines
`NET_BUF_DATA_SIZE`'s `default 128`) — confirmed in a built
`aen-ethernet-link` `.config`: `CONFIG_NET_BUF_DATA_SIZE=1536`. The help text
records what the upstream driver code shows without over-claiming: RX
allocates one `CONFIG_NET_BUF_DATA_SIZE`-sized fragment per descriptor on
refill and chains fragments via the first/last-descriptor bits; TX consumes
one descriptor per net_buf fragment and aborts the whole packet if it runs
out mid-frame — neither of which, read alone, explains a failure specifically
above 7 fragments rather than above the 16-descriptor ring capacity. The
exact root cause, in the upstream dwmac chaining versus the descriptor count,
is **not bisected**.

Because the relocated net_buf pools now grow (2 × 16 × 1536 ≈ 48 KiB in
SRAM0), `aen-evk-demo`'s 64 KiB SRAM0 window — previously 20800 B used
(31.7%) — overflowed by 320 B at its original
`CONFIG_NET_BUF_RX/TX_COUNT=16` (`region 'SRAM0' overflowed by 320 bytes`, a
link error, not a silent one). `examples/aen/aen-evk-demo/prj.conf` trims
`CONFIG_NET_BUF_RX_COUNT`/`CONFIG_NET_BUF_TX_COUNT` to 6 (phase 10's proof is
a DHCP lease, not sustained payload throughput), bringing usage to 34576 B
(52.8%); the overlay and README's address-map tables and `jpeg_out`'s address
are updated to match (measured `0x02004f10`).

Verified: `aen-ethernet-link` builds clean for both
`alp_e1m_aen801_m55_he/ae822fa0e5597ls0/rtss_he` and
`alp_e1m_aen803_m55_he/ae822fa0e5597ls0/rtss_he`, 0 new warnings, both with
`CONFIG_NET_BUF_DATA_SIZE=1536` confirmed in `.config`. `nm` confirms
`net_buf_data_rx_bufs`, `net_buf_data_tx_bufs`, `dwmac_rx_descs` and
`dwmac_tx_descs` land at `0x02xxxxxx` (SRAM0) while `_kernel`/`z_main_stack`
land at `0x20xxxxxx` (DTCM), identically on both boards. `aen-evk-demo` builds
clean on both AEN801 and AEN803 (identical overlays), 0 new warnings, fits its 64 KiB SRAM0 window at 52.8%.
`aen-isp-ov5647-viewfinder` (non-network, `alif,ethernet` disabled) builds
unaffected. The hazard-guard negative test (extra overlay re-adding the
whole-RAM `chosen`) fails configure with the intended `FATAL_ERROR`; the
positive case (no such overlay) still configures and builds clean.

### Added — `E1M-V2N103` / `E1M-V2M103`: the 4 GB RAM / 16 GB eMMC memory tier of the V2N-family PCB (#2261)

Two new SoM presets join `metadata/e1m_modules/`, filling out the Alp Lab
SKU catalogue's third E1M-X V2N memory tier:

- `E1M-V2N103` — "E1M-X Renesas RZ/V2N - 4 GB RAM / 16 GB ROM", a clone of
  `E1M-V2N101` (same 32 Gbit LPDDR4X, larger 128 Gbit eMMC).
- `E1M-V2M103` — "E1M-X Renesas RZ/V2N + DEEPX DX-M1 - 4 GB RAM / 16 GB ROM",
  the DEEPX-populated sibling, a clone of `E1M-V2M101` on the same terms.

Both SKUs share the V2N-family PCB and silicon with their siblings — chips,
I2C addresses, pad routes, and `TBD` markers are unchanged from the clone
source; only the SKU identity, display name, `memory.flash_mbit`, and the
per-SKU Yocto MACHINE / Zephyr board-target identifiers differ. Neither
SKU has a generated Zephyr board tree yet (same state as `E1M-V2N102` /
`E1M-V2M102`), so `topology.m33_sm.board` is the bare, unqualified target
and both are declared in `check_board_target_tree_parity.py`'s
`_NOT_YET_SUPPORTED` allowlist pending their own board bring-up.

**`E1M-V2N102` / `E1M-V2M102` eMMC size corrected.** Both presets declared
`memory.flash_mbit: 65536` (8 GB) — one tier short of the catalogue's "8 GB
RAM / 16 GB ROM" naming for these two SKUs. `flash_mbit` now reads `131072`
(16 GB); `memory.dram_mbit` (64 Gbit / 8 GB) was already correct and is
unchanged.

Propagated to the generated portability/peripheral-support matrices, the
Yocto `meta-alp-sdk` machine confs (new `e1m-v2n103-a55.conf` /
`e1m-v2m103-a55.conf`, mirroring the `E1M-V2N101` / `E1M-V2M101` confs —
their per-SKU BL2 DDR param + 4 GB U-Boot SDRAM size entry is a separate
follow-up, #2261-firmware-pack), a pre-staged
`zephyr/boards/alp_e1m_{v2n103,v2m103}_m33_sm.overlay` pair (same
IPC/mailbox wiring as every V2N/V2M sibling, mirroring
`E1M-V2N102` / `E1M-V2M102`'s existing overlays; like those, nothing in
the tree consumes them yet), the `tests/hil/` bench
directories (new `v2n103-x-evk/` / `v2m103-x-evk/`) and
`tests/scripts/test_hil_run_smoke.py`'s shipped-board list, the SoC-JSON
`alp_module_skus` reverse-lookup lists, and every doc/tutorial/comment
that named the prior "four E1M-X SKUs" / "V2N101, V2N102, V2M101,
V2M102" roster (`README.md`, `docs/soms/v2n.md`, `docs/soms/v2n-m1.md`,
`docs/board-config.md`, `docs/portability.md`,
`docs/portability-matrix.md`, `docs/tutorials/04-cross-family-portability.md`,
`docs/tutorials/09-board-yaml-deep-dive.md`,
`docs/tutorials/16-inference-mobilenet.md`,
`docs/adr/0011-intra-family-portability.md`'s current-state "Today:"
line, `docs/bring-up-drpai-v2n.md`, `docs/gd32-bridge.md`,

### Added — `E1M-V2N103` / `E1M-V2M103` firmware pack: BL2 DDR param + 4 GB U-Boot config (#2261)

Closes the `TODO(firmware-pack)` the two x103 machine confs carried since
they were added: `bitbake trusted-firmware-a u-boot` (+ `firmware-pack`)
now produces the correct 4 GB boot firmware for `e1m-v2n103-a55` /
`e1m-v2m103-a55`.

- `trusted-firmware-a_%.bbappend`: the BL2 DDR param file is now selected
  per MACHINE via `ALP_TFA_DDR_SRC` — the rzv2n-family default
  (`ddr_param_def_lpddr4-alp.c`, config `L4X.R2W32X16D16S32.ADEE`) for
  every existing MACHINE, and a new 4 GB sibling
  (`ddr_param_def_lpddr4-alp-d8s32.c`, config `L4X.R2W32X16D8S32.ADEE`,
  bench-proven 2026-09-24 on an E1M-V2M103: 30/30 cold boots, memtester
  16/16) for `e1m-v2n103-a55`/`e1m-v2m103-a55` only. Both files stay
  private (`alp-sdk-internal` overlay), same split as the existing
  default.
- `u-boot_%.bbappend`: a new `0003-rzv2n-dev-ALP-E1M-4gb-memory-tier.patch`
  (applies after 0001/0002) sets `CONFIG_SYS_SDRAM_SIZE` and the control
  DT's `memory@48000000` node to 4 GB, gated to the two x103 MACHINEs only.

**Also fixed in the same slice — the DDR-param install was a silent
no-op through bitbake, for every rzv2n-family MACHINE, until now.**
`do_configure[noexec] = "1"` in meta-arm's `trusted-firmware-a.inc` means
bitbake never executes a noexec task's function body; the DDR-param
install lived in `do_configure:append:rzv2n-family()`, so it silently
never ran, for `e1m-v2n101-a55`/`e1m-v2n102-a55`/`e1m-v2m101-a55`/
`e1m-v2m102-a55` too, not just the new x103 MACHINEs. Every bitbake-built
BL2 to date compiled the **stock Renesas DDR param** (`ddr_version_str`
`"03.01"`), plus meta-rz-drpai's `0000-ddr_param_def_lpddr4-rzv2n_1.patch`
MC-arbitration tweaks where that layer was present — **not** the intended
ALP gen_tool file. Moved the install to `do_compile:prepend:rzv2n-family()`
(not noexec) and added a build-time assertion that the two x103 MACHINEs
actually resolve to the D8S32 file. Confirmed on alplab-gw (2026-09-24):
`e1m-v2n103-a55`/`e1m-v2m103-a55` compile the correct D8S32 file into BL2,
byte-identical to the intended source; `e1m-v2m101-a55` compiles its
D16S32 file the same way.

**Also confirmed the same day (2026-09-24):**
- **V2x101 production DRAM part/tier: still undecided, a production
  blocker.** `E1M-V2N101`/`E1M-V2M101`'s own catalogue entry
  (`metadata/e1m_modules/E1M-V2N101.yaml`, `E1M-V2M101.yaml`:
  `dram_mbit: 32768` = 4 GB) states the same 4 GB size this x103
  firmware targets, yet those MACHINEs continue to ship the
  family-default D16S32 (8 GB) config. Decided: firmware **stays**
  D16S32 for V2N101/V2M101; which of the two facts is actually right
  remains open — see the `# OPEN` note added to both machine confs and
  `docs/build-yocto-v2n.md`.
- **Fold meta-rz-drpai's DDR MC-arbitration register values in: YES,
  applied.** `param_setup_mc` `0x0134`/`0x0135`/`0x0178`/`0x017f`/`0x0181`/
  `0x02cd`/`0x02cf`/`0x02d0` — which the ALP gen_tool files didn't carry,
  and which `do_compile:prepend`'s whole-file replacement was discarding
  on any DRP-AI-enabled build — are now folded into both
  `ddr_param_def_lpddr4-alp.c` and `-alp-d8s32.c`
  (`alp-sdk-internal@9f88a4d`, 16 lines, CRLF preserved). Density-independent
  (identical baseline in both files) and non-colliding with the D8 range
  regs/tRFC rows; `param_phyinit_2d_dat1[15]` stays at the ALP value (the
  drpai patch doesn't touch it). Rebuilt from the committed SHA on
  alplab-gw (`e1m-v2m103-a55` BL2, `e1m-v2n101-a55` TF-A) and confirmed
  via the built `bl2.bin` that all 8 entries carry the folded-in values
  and the prior values are gone, for both D8S32 and D16S32. **Not yet
  silicon-verified** — needs a cold-boot DDR training pass, memtester,
  and a DRP-AI inference run on the bench.

See `alp-sdk-internal docs/bootloader-equivalence-verdict.md` (corrected the
same day) for the discovery trail and exact target values.

### Fixed — the `alif_flash` west runner burned a fresh ATOC without reading the resident one first, silently delisting every other app entry (#2262)

`scripts/west_commands/runners/alif_flash.py`'s `do_run` (the `west flash`
runner wired into all six `zephyr/boards/alp/e1m_aen*` boards) staged a
signed ATOC config holding only `DEVICE` + this build's own `ALP-HE`/`ALP-HP`
entry, then burned it with `app-write-mram -c <SE_UART> -p` — a write that
REPLACES the whole resident ATOC, not merges it. Every other resident app
entry (the other M55 core's own entry, an A32 Linux boot chain
`BOOTLOAD`/`A32_APP`, ...) was silently delisted the instant the write
landed, with no error and no SES warning (`[SES] ATOC ok` prints either
way). #2025 closed this exact hazard (an AEN EVK bench unit's A32 Linux boot
chain, 2026-09-07) for the bench shell helpers alone (`bench_atoc_replace_guard`
in `scripts/bench/aen/bench-env.sh`); it never reached this `west flash`
door.

`do_run` now reads the resident ATOC back over the SE-UART before burning,
with the same two documented, non-destructive SETOOLS queries the bench
guard uses (`maintenance -opt getbanner` then `-opt gettoc`), and refuses the
burn — before anything is written — when a resident entry outside this
run's own `ALP-HE`/`ALP-HP` section would be delisted, or when the read
could not be verified (a missing `maintenance` binary, a malformed/absent
SES banner, or a non-zero query exit). The new `--replace-atoc` runner
option is the explicit override, spelled identically to
`flash-run.sh`'s own Flow A flag — distinct from, and never merged or
aliased with, Flow D's `--atoc-unqueryable` (#2027). A new `--se-uart-baud`
option (default `$SE_UART_BAUD`, else `57600`) matches the bench guard's own
baud fallback.

The parse/decision logic (`compute_query_status`, `foreign_resident_entries`,
`decide_atoc_guard`) is a single shared, pure-Python port of
`bench_atoc_replace_guard`'s semantics, added to `scripts/aen_atoc.py` next
to the existing ATOC-assembly guard (#1069). A parity test
(`tests/scripts/test_atoc_guard_parity.py`) feeds fixture transcripts
through both implementations and asserts identical verdicts (bash's exit
0/5 vs. Python's richer status, and — parsing bash's own `This board also
carries: ...` line — the identical foreign-entry NAME SET, not a substring
check). Some of those fixtures are the real, bench-verified 2026-09-07 AEN
EVK captures (the 9-row A32-Linux-boot-chain table, the clean two-row
table, the leading-space SES banner); others (an ANSI-coloured 2-row table,
a CRLF-only table, a truncated/NBSP-only-name row, a non-zero `gettoc` exit
after partial rows, `No ATOC found on target device.` on its own) are
hand-written to exercise one specific parser rule and were never captured
off real hardware — this changelog and the fixtures' own comments say
which is which; **do not read every fixture here as bench-proof.**

The guard also covers these edge cases:
- **Short and NBSP-only rows** (a row with fewer than 3 `|`-delimited fields,
  or a Name cell of pure NBSP) are read as real — if oddly-shaped —
  resident entries with `awk`'s own field/trim semantics, with unit +
  parity coverage for both).
- **Pre-provisioned module's factory ATOC.** Alp
  Lab's factory-provisioned MCUboot bootloader shows up as a resident
  `MCUBOOT-` entry (`zephyr/sysbuild/aen/README.md`); this guard correctly
  refuses to burn over it, but `--replace-atoc` deletes it and leaves the
  module unable to boot — the refusal message for that specific entry name
  says so and points at the already-documented Option B (plain
  J-Link, no ATOC) path instead of inviting `--replace-atoc`.
  `docs/aen-provisioning.md`, `docs/_aen-runbook-section.md`,
  `docs/aen-bench-bringup.md`, and `zephyr/sysbuild/aen/README.md` are
  say plain `west flash` does not work day-1 on such a module.
- **No stale verdict file.** A run that fails BEFORE reaching the guard
  (no SETOOLS, no `zephyr.bin`, a rejected ATOC window, ...) now removes
  any `atoc-guard.json` a PREVIOUS run left behind, so its mere absence —
  not a stale `status` field — is what tells a caller "the guard did not
  reach a verdict this attempt".
- **Wedged SE-UART query.** `maintenance -opt getbanner`/`gettoc` now time out (120s) and
  report `unverified`, the same fail-closed shape as any other query
  failure, so `west flash` cannot hang on it.

Every run leaves `<build_dir>/alif_flash/atoc-before.txt` (the raw
transcript) and `<build_dir>/alif_flash/atoc-guard.json` (a
machine-readable verdict — see "The verdict contract is frozen as v1"
below for the exact field set), written before any refusal is raised so
a caller such as tan-cli's `zephyr_west_flash` backend (tan-cli#1267) can
tell this refusal apart from any other `west flash` failure without
parsing stderr.

### The verdict contract is frozen as v1

`atoc-guard.json`'s `schema` field is the literal string
`alp-sdk.alif-flash-atoc-guard.v1`. The exact field set the code writes
(`schema`, `status`, `foreign`, `transcript`, `allowed`, `query_status` —
their types, allowed values, and what "absent file" / `query_status`
mean for telling the two `replaced` shapes apart) is documented once, in
`docs/aen-provisioning.md`'s "The ATOC-replace guard verdict contract"
section, rather than duplicated here. (`docs/_aen-runbook-section.md`, an unpublished draft fragment,
carries only a pointer to it.) Any future change to that field set must bump the schema
string (`...v1` -> `...v2`), the same convention
`metadata/schemas/*-v1.schema.json` already uses elsewhere in this repo.

### Sysbuild multi-domain `west flash` was NOT supported through `alif_flash` — refused by `alif_flash` since alp-sdk#2274 (see `changelog.d/2274.md`)

Zephyr's own multi-domain flash plumbing (in its `scripts/west_commands/`:
`flash.py` passes `build/domains.yaml` to `do_run_common`; `run_common.py`
resolves every domain in flash order and its own per-domain loop
instantiates and calls the board's flash runner ONCE PER DOMAIN, not once
per `west flash` invocation -- upstream Zephyr, not something alp-sdk
ships or can cite a stable line number in) means a sysbuild AEN build
(MCUboot domain + app domain) runs `alif_flash`'s `do_run` -- and
therefore this guard -- TWICE, once per domain's own build directory.

The guard identifies a resident entry by NAME ONLY. MCUboot (ITCM
`0x58000000`) and the HE app (HE slot0) both map to the identical ATOC
section name `ALP-HE` via `_atoc_section_name`, so on the SECOND
invocation the resident `ALP-HE` entry (written by the FIRST invocation)
is already in that run's own `allowed` set — not foreign — and the guard
reports `clear`. It still burns a fresh single-entry ATOC, silently
replacing whatever the first invocation wrote: the guard only ever
detects a FOREIGN name, never a same-name overwrite by a different
domain's build. **This is not a regression** — the pre-`#2262` runner did
exactly the same thing with no check of any kind — but it is a real,
unclosed gap in what this guard can catch, tracked as alp-sdk#2274
(closing it needs either a per-domain-aware `allowed` contract or a
binary-identity check this PR does not attempt). Do not read the
`clear`/`replaced` distinction above as covering this case: a same-name
overwrite between two sysbuild domains is exactly the kind of collision
neither status can currently name. (An untested hypothesis about whether
the app-domain invocation might fail earlier, at `_reset_vector`, on a
signed image's `imgtool` header, belongs to alp-sdk#2274's own
investigation, not this changelog — it is not claimed here.)

**Refused by `alif_flash` since alp-sdk#2274** (`changelog.d/2274.md`): rather than attempt a
per-domain-aware `allowed` contract or a binary-identity check, `alif_flash`
now REFUSES outright, before any side effect, whenever the build being
flashed is a multi-domain sysbuild — so this same-name-overwrite gap is
never reached at all. This section is left as the historical record of
when and how the gap was found.

### Guard behaviour (#2262)

- **Structural completeness is required.** `compute_query_status` (and its bash mirror,
  `bench_atoc_replace_guard`) reads a `gettoc` result as `ok` only when it exited `rc=0`, carried a
  valid SES banner, parsed >=1 resident row, AND the boxed table carries BOTH the `| Name |` header
  row and a closing `+---+` separator strictly after its last data row; otherwise it reads
  `unverified`. A real 9-row capture cut short after four rows (a serial timeout mid-download can
  still exit `rc=0`) would otherwise silently delist the cut-off tail (`BOOTLOAD`/`A32_APP`/
  `HP_APP`/`HE_APP`), the 2026-09-07 hardware loss this guard exists to close. There is no
  exemption for a transcript with neither marker: noise can swallow the top separator and header
  while a timeout cuts the tail, a different SETOOLS build could use unseen box-drawing glyphs, and
  SES boot-banner rows interleaved by a mid-query reset carry no markers either, so a transcript
  with no recognised table structure is `unverified` on both legs. The refusal message for that
  shape says the table format was not recognised and asks for the transcript, rather than steering
  at `--replace-atoc`. Fixtures cover a truncated-after-baseline-rows table, a table cut mid-row, a
  table missing only its closing separator, and (as a negative control, in each suite) a boxless
  table without markers.
- **The abort decision is boolean.** The runner branches on `decide_atoc_guard`'s `refused`
  directly, with a fail-closed catch-all raise for any refused status it has no dedicated message
  for.
- **The generic foreign-entry refusal does not steer toward `--replace-atoc`.** Both legs lead with
  "capture/restore first" and present `--replace-atoc` only as the last resort ("...only once you
  know it is safe to lose"), naming the pre-provisioned-module factory-bootloader risk. This is the
  branch a module falls into if its factory bootloader's real ATOC name differs from `MCUBOOT-`.
- **`_FACTORY_MCUBOOT_ATOC_NAME = 'MCUBOOT-'` is unsourced.** It traces to one sentence in
  `zephyr/sysbuild/aen/README.md`, documenting a SETOOLS-shipped config alp-sdk does not ship; no
  capture of a real pre-provisioned module's `gettoc` output exists in this repo to confirm it.
  Marked **TBD (unverified, no gettoc capture of a pre-provisioned module)** in the code comment
  and in every doc that names it (`docs/aen-provisioning.md`, `docs/_aen-runbook-section.md`,
  `zephyr/sysbuild/aen/README.md`). A wrong literal does not make the guard unsafe: an unrecognised
  factory name still refuses, it only loses its dedicated message.
- **Availability check.** The maintenance binary is checked with `os.access(path, os.X_OK)`,
  matching the bash guard's `[ -x ... ]`, with a test that isolates the availability check itself.
- **Unwritable build_dir.** The transcript/verdict `write_text` calls re-raise a `RuntimeError`
  naming the path; the burn is never reached either way. This is the one case where the "a refused
  run always leaves a verdict" contract cannot hold, since there is nowhere to put it.
- **`transcript` is always absolute** (`.resolve()`d), tested through a relative `build_dir`.
- **`_run_maintenance`** catches `TimeoutExpired`, `OSError` and `ValueError` (e.g. a NUL byte in a
  garbled `se_uart` string), all becoming the same rc=1 failed-read.
- **Padded `" No ATOC found on target device."`** (leading/trailing whitespace, the way SETOOLS pads
  the SES banner) reads as `empty` on both legs (`is_no_atoc_found` and the bash `grep`), with a
  parity test.
- **Post-burn log line.** It states only that the write completed; `do_run`'s only write is
  `app-write-mram -p` (never an erase), and the AEN bench notes document the SE preferring a STALE
  resident slot0 image over a freshly written ITCM-load ATOC, so boot is not verified by this
  command. `docs/aen-bench-bringup.md`'s guard section states that `west flash` is a Flow-A-class
  destructive MRAM/ATOC write (not a safe incremental update), and that the canonical
  `person_detect` slot0 restore's own `ALP-HE` entry sits *inside* this guard's allowed set, so a
  subsequent `west flash` overwrites it silently, by design, not as a bypass.
- **Test provenance.** `_REAL_MULTI_ENTRY_ATOC` is not a `gettoc` capture: it is "trimmed from the
  alp-sdk#2025 incident report" (PR #2026), hand-assembled from prose with no header row, no
  `+---+` separators and no SERAM `Time (ms)` column. It is kept in its boxless shape as each
  suite's negative control; a `_boxed()`/`_REAL_MULTI_ENTRY_ATOC_BOXED` variant covers the
  foreign-entry-detection tests. Every synthetic "ok"/"foreign" fixture across the four test files
  carries the header+separator bookends a real capture has, via a shared `_boxed()`/
  `_boxed_bytes()` helper.

### Not yet verified (bench-owed before this is safe to rely on in the field, same "Bench before merge" caveat the issue itself named)

The Python port + this runner's wiring have not been run on a real AEN
EVK slot at all — the parser semantics are bench-proven only in bash.

Three specific gaps remain, all needing the bench, not a doc guess, to
close:

- **Truncation reachability (measured, #2538).** On an E1M-AEN803 (serial
  2026W36-0009, `SES A1 v1.110.0`) a stalled SE-UART read right after a
  complete entry makes `maintenance -opt gettoc` exit 0 with 4, 7 or 8 rows
  and no closing `+---+` line (3/3 at byte 548); a reply later than 0.5 s
  gives a header-only table, also exit 0. The closing line is printed only
  when the 0xa8 end packet arrives, so the structural-completeness rule is
  the primary defence, not defence in depth. A closed port exits 1, and a
  complete table followed by `[ERROR] ... readSerial reporting
  disconnected` is caught only by the exit code, so a non-zero exit stays
  refused.
- **The factory `MCUBOOT-` name.** Still TBD — see above. Capturing a
  real pre-provisioned module's `gettoc` output is a Stage 2 bench task;
  until then this is a plausible, not confirmed, literal.
- **Mid-table row loss or a merged line is undetectable by structure
  alone (residual gap).** The
  structural-completeness check proves the transcript's HEADER and
  CLOSING SEPARATOR both arrived; it says nothing about whether every row
  BETWEEN them arrived intact. A serial glitch that drops exactly one
  `\n` mid-table merges two rows into one (the dropped row's own name
  ends up concatenated into field >=4 of the surviving row -- an address
  or flags column, never re-parsed as a second Name), or a glitch that
  silently drops one whole row without disturbing the header/separator
  count at all, both leave a structurally "complete" table that is
  missing a resident entry the guard can no longer see to protect. This
  is not a hypothetical unique to this guard -- it is the same class of
  gap a fixed-width/line-oriented parser always has against a corrupted
  byte stream — but it is real, unclosed, and not something either
  `_is_table_structurally_complete` or its bash mirror can detect from the
  transcript text alone. No fix is proposed here; recorded as an open,
  understood limitation.

### Fixed — the u-boot 0002 patch was malformed (corrupt hunks) and GigaDevice xSPI NOR support was missing (#2264)

- **`0002-rzv2n-dev-ALP-E1M-production-boot.patch` had two hunks with wrong `@@` line counts** — `git apply` rejected the file outright and GNU `patch` dropped the `CONFIG_ALP_E1M_FDTFILE` Kconfig block instead of erroring, so `do_compile` failed with `error: expected '}' before 'CONFIG_ALP_E1M_FDTFILE'`. Regenerated from a clean `renesas-u-boot-cip` checkout at the pinned SRCREV (`bcf29d98547d448776573abe643ecbdcbaa44b7d`) with the patch's content unchanged.
- **`CONFIG_SPI_FLASH_GIGADEVICE` is now enabled** via a new `gigadevice-xspi.cfg` fragment, so U-Boot's `sf probe` detects the GigaDevice LX-family xSPI NOR some production E1M V2N-family modules carry (`docs/soms/v2n.md`).
- **Known limit:** reads crossing the 16 MiB boundary fail in this U-Boot's Renesas xSPI driver (bench-observed `Read: ERROR 1` at `0xFFFF00+0x200`); writes above 16 MiB are untested.

### Added — `examples/connectivity/camera-mjpeg-stream`: camera → JPEG → MJPEG HTTP stream (#2265)

New connectivity example: capture a frame with `<alp/camera.h>`, JPEG-encode it
