with `<alp/jpeg.h>`, and serve it over a plain Zephyr BSD TCP socket on port
8080 — `GET /stream` (multipart/x-mixed-replace, one boundary per frame) and
`GET /snapshot.jpg` (a single JPEG with `Content-Length`). No host tool ships;
point a browser, VLC (`vlc http://<ip>:8080/stream`), or ffmpeg at the printed
URL. See `examples/connectivity/camera-mjpeg-stream/README.md`.

The encoder is opened first and its `alp_jpeg_caps_t::pixfmt_mask` decides the
source layout everything downstream builds against — `ALP_PIXFMT_NV12` when
the won backend advertises it (the Hantro VC9000E hardware encoder on the
E1M-AEN family), `ALP_PIXFMT_YUV420_PLANAR` otherwise (the portable software
encoder, everywhere else including native_sim). The camera path is gated on
`alp_has(ALP_CAP_ID_HW_MIPI_CSI)`, not on SoC identity, and falls back to a
synthetic test-pattern frame when there is no camera capability or no camera
actually attached — no `#ifdef` on which SoC this is. Requested at 640×480.
The camera-capture/JPEG-encode loop (the app's main thread) never touches a
socket: it encodes directly into one of two SRAM0 ping-pong buffers
`src/mjpeg_http.c` owns (`mjpeg_http_claim_write_buffer()` /
`mjpeg_http_publish_frame()` — zero-copy, no `memcpy` on either side), which
swap under a mutex on publish unless a client is mid-send of the current
`front` buffer, in which case the new frame is dropped rather than tearing
the one in flight. `zsock_recv`/`zsock_send` on every accepted socket carry
`SO_RCVTIMEO`/`SO_SNDTIMEO` (`CONFIG_NET_CONTEXT_RCVTIMEO`/`_SNDTIMEO`), so an
idle or stalled client can't wedge the single server thread. A failed capture
is logged (rate-limited), backs off with `k_msleep`, and falls back to the
synthetic frame after 10 consecutive failures — an unbacked-off error loop at
the capture thread's priority would otherwise starve the (lower-priority)
HTTP thread outright. DHCP is fired once at boot and negotiates concurrently
in Zephyr's own net-stack thread; a `net_mgmt` event callback prints the
lease IP plus the stream/snapshot URLs once bound, off the capture loop's own
critical path.

`src/mjpeg_http.c` and the native_sim-only `src/selftest.c` call the
`zsock_*`-prefixed socket API (`CONFIG_NET_SOCKETS`) rather than the plain
POSIX names: on native_sim the example links as an ordinary host executable
against the host's own libc, and depending on archive link order the plain
POSIX socket names can silently resolve to the HOST's `socket()` instead of
Zephyr's — every call then fails immediately with `EPROTONOSUPPORT` because
the host interprets Zephyr's `AF_INET` (1) as its own `AF_UNIX`. `zsock_*` has
no libc counterpart, so there is nothing to collide with.

On the E1M-AEN family the JPEG source/output buffers are placed in the global
on-chip SRAM0 bank (`section("SRAM0")`, gated on
`CONFIG_ALP_SDK_JPEG_ALIF_HANTRO`) — the Hantro VC9000E is an external AXI
bus master and cannot reach the M55's local TCM, the same constraint
`examples/aen/aen-jpeg-regcheck` and `examples/aen/aen-evk-demo` document. The
AEN board overlays carry two pieces of DT graph wiring, each mirroring the
example it's drawn from: the ISP capture path from
`examples/aen/aen-isp-ov5647-viewfinder` (routes the camera shield's sensor
port through the ISP-Pico), and an INTERIM Ethernet bring-up from
`examples/aen/aen-ethernet-link` (RMII pin group + PHY power/reset GPIOs;
board generation doesn't grow real Ethernet routing yet). The PHY MDIO/refclk/
power sequence lives in the AEN-only `src/aen_eth_phy.c`, compiled in only for
`alp_e1m_aen*` targets and never referenced by the portable `main.c`.

native_sim streams the synthetic frame through the portable software JPEG
encoder (`CONFIG_NET_LOOPBACK`, no camera, no Ethernet) and proves the server
end to end with an in-app loopback selftest: `GET /snapshot.jpg`'s JPEG
SOI/EOI markers, and `GET /stream`'s multipart framing (boundary line,
`Content-Type`/`Content-Length` header pair, blank line, trailing CRLF), over
127.0.0.1 (`\[camera-mjpeg-stream\] selftest ok`). Two board-conf files
(`native_sim.conf` and `native_sim_native_64.conf`) are needed, not one --
Zephyr's board-conf auto-apply resolves a different filename per qualifier
string, and there is no single name that matches both `native_sim` (32-bit)
and `native_sim/native/64`. The E1M-AEN801/AEN803 scenario now also runs in
`pr-twister-aen.yml` (build-only — no camera/Ethernet hardware in the
runner); it did not before. Bench run 204 (E1M-AEN803 + OV5647, 320×240,
before this example's resolution was raised to its intended 640×480): a
valid 15571 B `/snapshot.jpg`, `/stream` at 17 fps / ~12.8 KB/frame over
255 parts in 15 s, with a 1536 B Ethernet net_buf data size (at the 128 B
default, run 203, frames over 896 B were dropped and no JPEG body arrived
at all — `CONFIG_ETH_DWMAC_ALIF` now defaults `CONFIG_NET_BUF_DATA_SIZE`
to 1536 itself, #2260). Run 205 (640×480, dark scene, taken before the
driver fixes below landed): 10 fps, ~37 KB/frame. The captured frame
content was dark (AWB, still under separate investigation, not an issue
in this example's own code) and its bottom two rows rendered solid green
— an ISP main-resizer chroma-row rounding bug, fixed at the driver level
by #2267/#2269; see the README's Limits section. Repeat-encode stability
is bench-proven, not unverified: runs 204/205 encoded 255+/300+ frames
back-to-back with no encoder error.

Second pass, addressing review + bench findings on the first: raised
`MJPEG_HTTP_MAX_JPEG` to 128 KiB (bench run 205 measured ~37 KB/frame at
640×480 on a dark scene; a lit scene compresses worse). `wait_and_claim()`
(the `/stream` frame wait) now
times out after `IDLE_TIMEOUT_S` instead of blocking `K_FOREVER` — a
stalled capture loop can no longer wedge the server thread through a
`/stream` client that never sees a send failure. `GET /stream`/
`GET /snapshot.jpg` on an idle-timeout `zsock_recv()` (no request line
ever arrives) now close quietly instead of replying 404. The AEN video
buffer pool math was corrected: only 3 ISP buffers actually exist (2
queued to the ISP MI, 1 converting) — a previous pass over-counted this as
5 and sized the heap accordingly; `CONFIG_VIDEO_BUFFER_POOL_HEAP_SIZE` is
now sized for the real 3×460,800 bytes (`NUM_MAX` keeps one spare
descriptor slot above that, which costs no heap bytes). `src/aen_eth_phy.c`'s
MDIO read now returns the "nothing here" sentinel when the post-transaction
wait times out too (not just the pre-transaction one), and `phy_find()`
aborts its whole scan on the first MDIO timeout rather than retrying all
32 addresses against a bus that is not coming back. `src/selftest.c` now
also verifies `Content-Length` against the real body length (both
endpoints) and guards a `size_t` underflow in the `/stream` body-length
computation that a malformed response could have driven far out of
bounds; its response-buffer caps are derived from `MJPEG_HTTP_MAX_JPEG`
instead of separately hand-picked numbers that could fall out of sync
with it.

Third pass, restacked onto dev after the Hantro driver fix (#2268) and
the ISP `bytesused` (#2263) and MRSZ chroma-row (#2267/#2269) fixes
landed there: dropped the app-side margin this example used to reserve
against the Hantro output-buffer overrun — the driver now derives its own
HW output-size-limit register from the buffer capacity it is handed, so
`main.c` passes `alp_jpeg_encode()` the full `MJPEG_HTTP_MAX_JPEG`
capacity directly. The two AEN board confs drop their explicit
`CONFIG_NET_BUF_DATA_SIZE=1536` — redundant now that
`CONFIG_ETH_DWMAC_ALIF` defaults it itself (#2260). The README's green-
bottom-rows and Ethernet-net_buf caveats are now stated as fixed rather
than open; the dark/AWB image-quality caveat remains open and unrelated,
and run 205's bench numbers are now labeled as taken before these fixes.

### Fixed — ISP MRSZ SCALE_VC truncation dropped the last 4:2:0 chroma row (E1M-AEN803) (#2267)

`zephyr/drivers/video/isp_pico.c`'s `isp_apply_mrsz()` (added by #2258)
programmed `ISP_MRSZ_SCALE_VC` for the main resizer's 2:1 vertical-chroma
downscale (4:2:2 internal -> 4:2:0 output) as a plain
`((out_h - 1) * 65536) / (in_h - 1)`. For 480 -> 240 that truncates to
`0x7FBB` (32699), which the resizer computes back to
`floor((479 * 0x7FBB) / 65536) + 1 == 239` output lines -- one short of the
240 the 4:2:0 output needs. The last chroma row was never written.

**Silicon-confirmed, E1M-AEN803:** bench run 205 (`camera-mjpeg-stream`,
640x480 NV12 -> Hantro JPEG) showed image rows 478-479 (the last chroma
row, line 239) solid green in every frame -- the look of a never-written
chroma row; bench run 201 (`aen-isp-capture`, I420) showed the last
U row (239) holding stale garbage.

`ISP_MRSZ_SCALE_VC` (HWRM §17.3.4.3.169) documents only the register's
meaning, no formula, and neither the Alif DFP nor `hal_alif` programs this
register anywhere. The ISP main resizer is rkisp1-lineage silicon
(VSI/rkisp1 IP); its downscale ratio formula takes a `+1` a naive
`floor(((out-1)<<16)/(in-1))` misses:
`((len_out - 1) * RKISP1_CIF_RSZ_SCALER_FACTOR) / (len_in - 1) + 1`.

`isp_apply_mrsz()` now calls a new shared `alp_isp_mrsz_scale_vc()` helper
(`zephyr/include/zephyr/drivers/video/isp_frame_size.h`, the same header
`isp_pico.c`'s pitch/frame-size math already shares with
`tests/unit/isp_frame_size`) that applies the `+1` rounding, so the
resizer's output line count and the register formula can only drift once,
not into two independently-wrong copies. 480 -> 240 now programs `0x7FBC`.
New unit tests pin the corrected 480x240 value and the general
"produces exactly `out_lines`" property at two more sizes (360x180,
1080x540).

### Fixed — Hantro JPEG driver: output-buffer overrun, a leaked import slot, and a stale-completion race (#2268)

**Fixed an output-buffer overrun (SWREG9 was programmed from the raw buffer
capacity instead of relative to the SWREG8 base it actually bounds,
letting the encoder write past the caller's buffer), a permanently-leaked
video-buffer-pool slot on every encode timeout, and a stale-completion race
that could attribute one job's result to another.** A timeout now polls the
hardware's own `SW_ENC_E` bit before stopping the encoder and always
releases its pool slot instead of parking it; the completion semaphore and
latched status are cleared before every new encode and on stream stop --
closed for completions latched before re-arm, but a job the hardware never
finishes remains a known limit. `alp_jpeg_encode()`'s Doxygen now documents
`out_buf` as undefined after `ALP_ERR_TIMEOUT`. Full ownership map, SVD
citations, and bench evidence are in the PR description.

### Fixed — ISP AE writeback clamps to the sensor's registered control range, and the OV5647 AE calibration envelope brought in line with the sensor (#2271)

**Defensive clamp.** hal_alif's per-frame AE writeback called `video_set_ctrl()` for `VIDEO_CID_ANALOGUE_GAIN`/`VIDEO_CID_EXPOSURE` with no bound check, so on E1M-AEN803 + OV5647 an out-of-range EXPOSURE writeback (`intLine` 94470, `ctrl.val` = `intLine * 16` = `1511520`, against OV5647's registered range `[0, 0xFFFFF]`) was rejected with `-EINVAL` every frame forever; new patch `zephyr/patches/hal_alif/0010-isp-clamp-ae-writeback-to-ctrl-range.patch` saturates into the sensor's `video_query_ctrl()`-reported range before each write and logs (latched, once per episode) whenever a clamp actually changes the value.

**Fallback ceiling fix.** `zephyr/drivers/video/isp_pico.c`'s `isp_apply_ae()` fallback `again_max` constant, only reachable when the live `video_query_ctrl()` range lookup fails, was corrected `16368` -> `65472`.

**Calibration envelope.** `isp_param_conf.h`'s compiled-in OV5647 AE calibration block was never updated off Alif's stock ARX3A0 envelope (`expTimeRange.max` 3000000 us, decoding to the same out-of-range 94470-line writeback above); new patch `zephyr/patches/hal_alif/0011-isp-ov5647-ae-calib-envelope.patch` sets it from the same `OV5647_AE_*` facts `sensor_attributes.h` already used, and changes the OV5647 calibration's `aeTarget` from `255` to `CONFIG_VIDEO_ISP_VSI_AE_TARGET` (90). Bench run 213 (0010+0011 applied) held within the sensor's real envelope with 0 rejected writes; the exact mechanism by which the calibration block wins over `isp_apply_ae()`'s own push is not established.

### Fixed — the `alif_flash` runner now refuses a multi-domain sysbuild flash instead of silently overwriting the resident ATOC entry (#2274)

Zephyr's own sysbuild flash plumbing runs `scripts/west_commands/runners/
alif_flash.py`'s `do_run` ONCE PER DOMAIN, not once per `west flash`
invocation. Confirmed against Zephyr v4.4.1 (this repo's pinned revision,
`west.yml`'s `zephyr:` entry): its `scripts/west_commands/flash.py` hands
`do_run_common` the sysbuild's top-level `domains.yaml`, and its
`run_common.py`'s `get_domains_to_process`/`do_run_common` loop
instantiates and calls the board's runner once per resolved domain, each
time with that domain's own per-domain `build_dir` (upstream Zephyr's
`run_common.py`, `for d in domains: ... do_run_common_image(..., d.
build_dir, ...)`). On an
AEN MCUboot sysbuild both the `mcuboot` domain (ITCM `0x58000000`) and the
app domain (HE slot0) map to the SAME ATOC section name `ALP-HE` via
`_atoc_section_name`. The #2262 ATOC-replace guard identifies a resident
entry by NAME ONLY, so on a SECOND invocation any `ALP-HE` entry a
previous `alif_flash` run of the OTHER domain wrote is already this run's
own `allowed` set — the guard reports `clear`, but burning a fresh
single-entry ATOC over it silently replaces whatever the earlier run
wrote. This is not a regression (the pre-`#2262` runner did the same with
no check at all); it is a real, unclosed gap the guard's name-only
matching can never catch on its own, tracked as this issue since the
`#2262` changelog fragment first documented it. (On a factory-provisioned
module the resident MCUboot entry is instead named `MCUBOOT-` (entry name
TBD/unverified, see `zephyr/sysbuild/aen/README.md`'s provisioning
section), which the #2262 guard already refuses as foreign; this gap is
specifically about two
`alif_flash` runs of the same repo's own sysbuild both writing `ALP-HE`,
e.g. a from-scratch bring-up or a re-keyed module.)

`do_run` now refuses, before ANY staging/gettoc/J-Link/burn side effect,
whenever the build being flashed is itself a multi-domain sysbuild — keyed
on the build's OWN `domains.yaml` declaring more than one FLASHABLE
domain, not on how many domains THIS `west flash` invocation happens to
process. A single `--domain <x>` invocation of a 2-domain sysbuild refuses
too: flashing only one domain would still replace any `ALP-HE` entry a
previous run of the other domain wrote, the same way. A plain
(non-sysbuild) build with no `domains.yaml`, and a sysbuild with exactly
one flashable domain, are unaffected and behave exactly as before.

The new pure helper `_parse_sysbuild_domains_yaml` (in `alif_flash.py`)
reads `domains.yaml` from the sysbuild's top build dir — one level ABOVE
the per-domain `build_dir` `west flash` hands this runner as `self.cfg.
build_dir`. Confirmed against Zephyr v4.4.1: `share/sysbuild/cmake/
domains.cmake` generates the file at `${CMAKE_BINARY_DIR}/domains.yaml`
(the top build dir), and `share/sysbuild/cmake/modules/
sysbuild_extensions.cmake` sets each domain's own binary dir to
`${CMAKE_BINARY_DIR}/${ZBUILD_APPLICATION}`, one path component below. It
prefers `flash_order:` over the full `domains:` list when computing which
domains are "flashable" — `domains.cmake` builds `flash_order:` already
filtered to exclude each image's `BUILD_ONLY` property, the same list
Zephyr's own `run_common.py` reads for a plain multi-domain `west flash` —
so a build-only image (never a candidate for `west flash` to process at
all) does not trip the refusal. It is deliberately independent of
Zephyr's own `Domains` class (`scripts/pylib/build_helpers/domains.py`),
which is only importable from an active west workspace — this runner
already avoids that dependency for the same reason its module docstring
gives for importing only `runners.core` + the stdlib.

Four cases are handled explicitly: no `domains.yaml` (not a sysbuild —
proceed as today); exactly one flashable domain (proceed as today); this
build's own `build_dir` not listed among ANY of its domains.yaml's domains
at all (a relocated/stale build tree — refuse with a distinct "does not
list this build dir" message, fail-closed, since a same-name overwrite
against an unknown build is unverifiable rather than safe); more than one
flashable domain (refuse, naming the domains found and pointing at the
supported J-Link path, `docs/aen-provisioning.md` §0.5 Option B). Every
refusal message includes the `domains.yaml` path it read. A `domains.yaml`
that exists but cannot be read, does not parse as the documented shape
(`default`/`build_dir`/`domains: [{name, build_dir}]`/`flash_order`),
declares an empty `domains:` list, has a non-string `name`/`build_dir`, or
declares two `domains:` entries with the same `name`, also refuses —
fail-closed, never silently treated as "not a sysbuild" or "single
domain, proceed". `_sysbuild_domains_path` locates `domains.yaml` with
`.absolute()`, not `.resolve()` — a symlinked per-domain `build_dir` must
resolve `domains.yaml` relative to the symlink's own location (where
Zephyr's `flash.py` actually navigated), not its resolved target;
`.resolve()` is used only for the listed-build-dir equality comparison,
where both sides must be resolved the same way for the check to be
meaningful.

The refusal message additionally states that the Option B J-Link path it
points at writes the **app only** — it requires MCUboot already resident,
and names the SETOOLS provisioning steps (`zephyr/sysbuild/aen/README.md`)
needed first on a bare, wiped, or re-keyed module, since a missing
MCUboot otherwise leaves the module unable to boot (recoverable via
SETOOLS re-provisioning).

Documentation, file by file (a short pointer note at the existing
sysbuild-build-then-`west-flash` spot in each, not a rewritten
procedure or identical boilerplate — wording differs per file to stay
accurate to its own context):

- `zephyr/sysbuild/aen/README.md` — its Usage section's `west flash`
  commands are replaced by the Option B `JLinkExe` block (copied
  verbatim from `docs/aen-provisioning.md` §0.5) plus a rewritten
  provisioning paragraph explaining the #2274 refusal and the app-only
  caveat.
- `docs/_aen-runbook-section.md` — Flow A's "via west" section and the
  ATOC-verdict-contract callout each get the pointer note; also fixed
  a dangling "the SETOOLS MCUboot provisioning above" reference (that
  section is an app-only ATOC write, not MCUboot provisioning) to point
  at `zephyr/sysbuild/aen/README.md`'s actual provisioning section.
- `docs/aen-provisioning.md` — §0.5's Option A is relabeled as REFUSED
  on every module (bare or pre-provisioned) under #2274, not just "not
  the day-1 path" for a pre-provisioned one; its build-command comment
  no longer promises a write; a bullet notes a plain non-sysbuild
  `west flash` also refuses on a pre-provisioned module via #2262
  (independent of #2274); the original `--replace-atoc`-deletes-the-
  factory-entry wording is restored. §0.6's verdict-contract note is
  broadened to cover every #2274 refusal reason (not just multi-domain),
  and states `atoc-before.txt` is not touched on such a refusal either.
- `docs/secure-boot.md` — its signed-image output path is fixed to
  `build/<app>/zephyr/...` (was the single-domain `build/zephyr/...`),
  plus the pointer note after its "flash both" step.
- `docs/bring-up-aen.md` — two pointer notes (§4 step 4, §7 step 3);
  §4 is further rewritten so it no longer tells a reader with a
  pre-provisioned module to build sysbuild and `west flash` as their
  actual path — the build+flash commands are kept only as the context
  that produces the artefact Option B flashes.
- `docs/tutorials/10-secure-boot-signing.md` — NOT touched: it builds
  `alif_e7_dk_rtss_he`, a board that does not default to the
  `alif_flash` runner, so this fix does not apply there.
- `changelog.d/2262.md` — its own note on this gap is reworded from
  "closed by alp-sdk#2274" to "refused by `alif_flash` since
  alp-sdk#2274" (a refusal, not full multi-domain support).
- `docs/superpowers/specs/2026-07-29-tan-python-port-master-plan.md` —
  a short correction note next to its historical `west build
  --sysbuild ... && west flash` example; otherwise left unchanged.

`tan flash` does **not** hit this refusal on AEN: tan-cli's
`select_flash_method` dispatches any `zephyr_west_flash` entry carrying
`jlink_flash_device` (every published Ensemble SoC variant does) to Flow
D (`alif_mram_jlink`, a direct J-Link/SWD burn) instead of `west flash`,
so `alif_flash`'s `do_run` is never reached.

The MEDIUM-3 (#2262) stale-verdict `atoc-guard.json` unlink now runs
BEFORE the #2274 check, not after: clearing this runner's own prior
output is not an MRAM/ATOC side effect, so a #2274 refusal must still
clear it the same as every other early-abort path — otherwise a refused
run would leave a PREVIOUS run's `clear`/`replaced` verdict looking like
its own. `docs/aen-provisioning.md` §0.6 (the verdict contract) now notes
this as a second honest exception to "a refused run always leaves a
verdict": a #2274 refusal leaves none at all, clearing any stale one.

This fix makes moot, but does not itself resolve, the separate open
question of whether `zephyr.signed.bin` might already be rejected
earlier by `_reset_vector`/`_select_app_shape` on a signed image's
header — that remains unclaimed either way.

### Fixed — AEN ISP-Pico camera backend ignored the caller's requested fps, always streaming at 10 fps (#2276)

`src/backends/camera/alif_isp_pico.c`'s `open()` hard-coded
`video_set_frmival(sensor_dev, {1, 10})` on the OV5647 shield path,
ignoring `alp_camera_config_t::fps` entirely — every `<alp/camera.h>`
stream through this backend ran at 10 fps no matter what an app asked
for. `examples/connectivity/camera-mjpeg-stream` set `ccfg.fps = 15` and
still measured 10 fps end to end (its own README's bench run 205).

Now requests `cfg->fps` (falling back to 10 fps, the same choice as
before, when `cfg->fps == 0` — this backend's own default, per
`<alp/camera.h>`'s `alp_camera_config_t::fps` doc, not the "must choose
or `alp_camera_open()` rejects" sentinel `width`/`height` use), reads the
effective rate back with `video_get_frmival()` (the OV5647 driver settles
on the closest of `ov5647_framerates[]` — 10/15/30/45/60/90/120 — it can
actually reach at the requested mode, VTS-clamped), and logs the
requested-vs-settled rate (`LOG_INF` when they differ, `LOG_DBG` when
they match), plus a `LOG_WRN` if `video_set_frmival()` itself fails or
the OV5647 device isn't ready.

`isp_pico.c`'s `isp_apply_ae()` derives its `int_time_max` ceiling from a
live `video_get_frmival()` read on every apply — confirmed on silicon
(bench run 220, E1M-AEN803 + OV5647, module 2026W36-0001, bright daylight, 30 fps
request): boot readback `AE readback: int_time_max=32667 ...`, matching a
30 fps frame period, AE settling around intLine ~331-351, no `E:`/`W:`
log lines. But the OV5647 calibration AE block (`hal_alif` patches
`0006-isp-ov5647-ae-sensor-defaults.patch` /
`0011-isp-ov5647-ae-calib-envelope.patch`) still pins the exposure
ceiling to 3145 lines — the VTS for the sensor's 10 fps mode — and that
calibration block wins over `isp_apply_ae()`'s own push. In a dim scene
at 30 fps, AE may legitimately want to command an exposure longer than
one 30 fps frame period (VTS ~1049 lines), which the pinned 3145-line
ceiling doesn't reflect and which can lower the effective frame rate or
truncate the exposure AE wanted — unverified on silicon (run 220 was
bright daylight, so it never exercised this path); tracked in #2277, not
fixed here (fixing it means touching the `hal_alif` patches, out of this
PR's scope).

`examples/connectivity/camera-mjpeg-stream` now requests 30 fps
(`FRAME_FPS`, was a bare `ccfg.fps = 15` literal), confirmed end to end
at 30.03 fps by bench run 220 above; its README and file-header comment
are updated with that measurement.
`examples/aen/aen-isp-ov5647-viewfinder` pins `cfg.fps = 10` explicitly
instead of taking the new 30 fps default — its CPU YUV->RGB565
conversion headroom and dim-scene AE headroom are only bench-proven at
10 fps (runs 147/154), and it has not been re-benched at 30.

Also opened: #2278 (the `zephyr_video` and `v2n_n44_isp` camera backends
ignore `alp_camera_config_t::fps` entirely) and #2279 (`<alp/camera.h>`
has no way to report back the frame rate a backend actually settled on).
Refs #2277. Refs #2278. Refs #2279.

File-header comments in `alif_isp_pico.c` that called the hard-coded
10 fps a "floor" are corrected: 10 fps genuinely is the lowest entry in
`ov5647_framerates[]`, but calling it a floor implied the backend
couldn't run any other rate — it could always have requested a higher
one and simply never did. The comments now describe it as this
backend's own default choice (AE exposure headroom in a dim scene),
used only when the caller hasn't stated a preference.

### Fixed — OV5647 auto-exposure never held: the manual AEC/AGC bits (`0x3503`) cleared between the ISP's gate and streaming, letting the sensor's own on-chip AEC/AGC run active and override every exposure write (#2277)

The ISP's manual-mode gate set `0x3503`'s AEC/AGC-manual bits at stream
start, but something cleared them between that gate and
`MODE_SELECT_STREAMING` — leaving the sensor's own on-chip AEC/AGC
active for the whole session and silently overriding every exposure
write the ISP made.

**Fixed by re-asserting manual AEC/AGC as the last write before
streaming, and clamping exposure to the active mode:**
`ov5647_set_stream(true)` (`ov5647.c`) now re-asserts both AEC/AGC-manual
bits (`0x3503`) immediately before `MODE_SELECT_STREAMING`, and
`ov5647_set_ctrl_exposure()` clamps every `VIDEO_CID_EXPOSURE` write to
the active mode's VTS - 4 lines. The ISP AE library's own compiled-in
exposure ceiling (3145 lines, pinned to the sensor's 10 fps VTS
regardless of requested rate) is unchanged by this fix — the sensor-side
clamp is tighter and masks it.

Bench run 251 (E1M-AEN803 2026W36-0001, OV5647, 640x480 requesting
30 fps): `0x3503` reads `0x07` (AEC/AGC/VTS manual) held at stream start
and on every ~1 s poll during streaming; sensor exposure holds at 1045
lines (VTS 1049 - 4), ISP frame rate 30.00 fps.

### Fixed — the Zephyr video and V2N N44 ISP camera backends now apply `alp_camera_config_t::fps` (#2278)

`zephyr_video.c` (the portable Zephyr video-class backend) and `v2n_n44_isp.c`
never read `cfg->fps`, so a caller's requested frame rate had no effect and
no diagnostic. Both now call `video_set_frmival()` with the request after
format negotiation, through a shared `camera_frmival.h` helper. `fps == 0`
keeps the driver's default. A driver with no settable rate, or one that
rejects the request, logs a warning and keeps streaming at its own rate, as
the AEN ISP-Pico backend already did.

### Added — `alp_camera_get_fps()` reports the frame rate the camera actually settled on (#2279)

`alp_camera_config_t::fps` is a request: the sensor or mode picks the nearest rate it supports, and until now the caller could not find out which one. `alp_camera_get_fps(camera, &fps_x1000)` returns the rate the backend read back at open, in thousandths of a frame per second, so fractional rates such as 29.97 fps (29970) survive.

The three Zephyr video-class backends (`zephyr_video`, `v2n_n44_isp`, `alif_isp_pico`) record it from `video_get_frmival()` right after applying the request. A driver that cannot report its frame interval, the stub backend and the NULL-driver path all answer `ALP_ERR_NOSUPPORT`. A NULL output pointer returns `ALP_ERR_INVAL`, and a NULL or closed handle returns `ALP_ERR_NOT_READY`.

### Added

- `provision_som.py run` gains two V2N/V2M steps: `clkgen_verify` reads the
  on-SoM 5L35023B clock generator's OTP image one byte at a time and checks
  it (with U-Boot's per-boot register fixup accounted for) against the
  bench-proven factory image, and records `clkgen_otp_raw` and
  `clkgen_i2c_addr`. `dxm1_npu_flash` programs the V2M DX-M1 NPU's SPI-NAND
  over its UART recovery path and verifies a PCIe link after a cold boot; it
  is **bench-pending** (it has never run on silicon) and skipped unless
  `--enable-dxm1-flash` is passed. See `docs/provisioning-v2n.md`.

### Fixed — carrier microSD (SDHI1) now works on the E1M-X EVK (#2282)

`e1m-x-evk.dtsi` left `sdhi1_pins` empty, so `pinctrl-rzg2l` logged
`no mapping found in node /soc/pinctrl@10410000/sd1` and SDHI1
(`mmc@15c10000`) never probed. The SD1 node is now complete:

- `sdhi1_pins` carries the dedicated `SD1CLK`, `SD1CMD` and `SD1DAT0-3` pads.
- Card detect is a real `cd-gpios` on `PA1` (`SD1_SD1CD`), active-low.
- `vqmmc_sdhi1` (now in `e1m-v2n-som.dtsi`, where the selector lives) switches
  the SD1 IO rail on `PA2` (`µSD1_V_SEL`): low = 3.3 V, high = 1.8 V.
- UHS is enabled up to SDR104 (200 MHz). The SD1 pads use output-impedance
  2, one step weaker than the eMMC: at 3 (strongest) SDR104 through the carrier
  SDIO mux fails the data phase with CRC errors (`-84`).
- Card power (`PA3`, `SD1_SD1PWEN`) stays an always-on hog: the card-detect
  pull-up is on the switched card rail, so cutting power would make an empty
  slot read as occupied. `SDCARD_RST` (`PA4`) is the M.2 Wi-Fi SDIO reset and
  stays undriven.

Bench (E1M-V2M103 on the E1M-X EVK, blank GD32, 32 GB SDHC card): `mmc1: new
ultra high speed SDR104 SDHC card`, 512 MiB read in 6.5 s (~78 MB/s), two
1.5 GiB reads with identical md5, 10/10 unbind/bind re-enumerations at SDR104,
no errors.

U-Boot still numbers `mmc 1` as SDHI2 (`mmc@15c20000`, the Wi-Fi SDIO
controller); its device tree needs the same SD1 node before `mmc` there
reaches this slot.

### Added — U-Boot can boot from the E1M-X EVK microSD: SDHI1 is now `mmc1` (#2282)

U-Boot's boot-medium test is `mmc dev 1`, used by the vendor `bootcmd_check`
and by the ALP `CONFIG_BOOTCOMMAND` from patch 0002. On the E1M-X EVK the
microSD slot is on SDHI1 (`mmc@15c10000`). `rzv2n-dev.dts` pointed `mmc1` at
SDHI2 (`mmc@15c20000`) and left SDHI1 disabled, so U-Boot never looked at the
SD card and always booted from the eMMC. The V2N provisioning flow needs the
SD path: the unit boots the release image from microSD, and Linux then does
every production write.

The new
`meta-alp-sdk/recipes-bsp/u-boot/u-boot/0008-rzv2n-dev-ALP-E1M-sdhi1-microsd.patch`
has five parts:

- **Device numbering.** SDHI1 becomes `mmc1` and SDHI2 moves to `mmc2`. The
  SDHI0 eMMC stays `mmc0`, so the environment device does not change.
- **Card power and IO voltage.** Under `CONFIG_ALP_E1M_SD1_MICROSD` (off by
  default; `sd1-microsd.cfg` enables it for the E1M-V2N/V2M MACHINEs only,
  where PA2/PA3 are the SoM's own `uSD1_V_SEL`/`SD1_SD1PWEN` nets), `board_init()` drives PA2
  (`uSD1_V_SEL`) low for 3.3 V. It turns PA3 (`SD1_SD1PWEN`) off for 20 ms and
  then on, so a card that Linux left in 1.8 V UHS signalling starts again at
  3.3 V after a warm reboot.
- **Pad setup.** The SD1CLK, SD1CMD and SD1DAT0-3 pads get drive strength 2
  and slew rate 0, with input enabled on CMD and DAT. This matches the Linux
  `sdhi1_pins` group.
- **Limits.** The slot runs at 3.3 V only, because this U-Boot has no UHS
  support. There is no card detect: an empty slot fails `mmc dev 1` by timeout,
  and the boot falls back to the eMMC as before.
- **Data cards still boot the eMMC.** Once `mmc1` is the microSD, any inserted
  card passes `mmc dev 1`. The ALP boot command now takes the SD branch only
  when `ext4size mmc 1:2 boot/Image` also succeeds, so a card without a boot
  image falls back to the eMMC instead of stopping at the U-Boot prompt.

The patch applies with and without the x103-only patch 0003. It has not been
tested on hardware yet. If the GD32 controls the carrier SDIO mux, a blank
GD32 may leave the mux off the microSD socket (see #2282).

### Added — `provision_som.py plan | run | status`: a step machine that provisions a V2N / V2N-M1 SoM from blank silicon

The flat `provision_som.py --bundle` flow could only plan the V2N writes. The
new subcommands drive a blank module end to end: SCIF download and the Flash
Writer put a transient eMMC-boot BL2 and the FIP into eMMC boot partition 1, U-Boot
boots the release image from the microSD, and Linux then writes xSPI, eMMC
boot partition 1, the eMMC rootfs, the identity EEPROM, the GD32 and the Secure Data
Page. The flow and its hazards are in `docs/provisioning-v2n.md`.

- **Dry run by default.** `plan` and `run` without `--execute` run the
  read-only probes and print every command a step would issue. Every step has
  a read-only probe and counts as done only when the probe passes again after
  the step runs, so a rerun skips finished work.
- **Gates before any write.** The bundle must match its hashes and carry
  `bl2`, `bl2_mmc`, `fip` and `system_image`. The SKU and the DDR tier must
  agree across the CLI, bundle, preset, BL2 images and U-Boot banner. A
  `v2n-m1` FIP must carry the DEEPX rail line, and the dtb U-Boot loads must
  be in the image. The FIP write can never reach the CM33 image region.
- **Identity EEPROM safety.** Only the five known N24S128 `0x58` frames can
  be built, and none of them writes selector `0x06`. The manifest is written
  only to a blank, unlocked array. The Secure Data Page is written and
  verified; locking it is a separate `run --lock` that needs a shippable
  ledger record, a fresh re-read of the page and the serial typed again.
- **Ledger.** Facts go to the private per-unit ledger even when a step fails.
  A unit with the known power-chip register defect, a gate override, or an
  unsigned `--build-dir` image is recorded as not shippable.
- **Bundle schema.** New component role `bl2_mmc` (`emmc:boot1`) and an
  optional `memory_tier` (`dram_mbit`, `label`).
- **Backend rename.** The `xspi_flashwriter` flash backend is now
  `renesas_flashwriter_scif`. It plans xSPI and eMMC boot partition 1 writes and refuses a
  confirmed write. The flat flow reports a `bl2_mmc` component as skipped.

First bench run (E1M-V2M103 2026W38-0001, 2026-09-28) found the target's
busybox has no `head -c`, no `dd conv=`/`status=`/`iflag=` and no
`blockdev`. The md5 probes had hashed an empty stream, so every step looked
unfinished. Reads and writes now use plain `dd` (whole blocks plus a `bs=1`
tail, then `sync`), an empty read of a non-empty span is an error, the
partition re-read falls back to the `BLKRRPART` ioctl, `mmc-utils` ships in
every Alp image, and `detect` runs `sync` on a live Linux before it
power-cycles the unit.

Review follow-ups: `boot_sd_linux` checks the live SoM (every
non-optional on-module I2C device the preset declares must ACK) before the
first xSPI write, and a resume refuses a Linux booted from the eMMC;
`--pmic-expect` is checked in preflight under `--execute`; the boot partition 1 write is
bounded by the partition size; `status` flags a state `run` would supersede
and returns 1 only with `--require-shippable`; the FIP's dtb is read from its
`bootcmd`; a `.py` bench probe wrapper runs under the current interpreter;
and `ScpiPower.is_on()` reads the Siglent SPD3303X `SYST:STAT?` bits.

### Added — word-copy `memcpy()` override + Ethernet buffer sizing for AEN camera streaming throughput (#2285)

`examples/connectivity/camera-mjpeg-stream` on E1M-AEN803 topped out well
short of its OV5647 sensor's frame rate: bench run 223 showed the
camera-capture loop keeping up with 60 fps while the HTTP `/stream` send
took 24-30 ms per 32-41 KB frame, dropping 45-51% of frames.

Two changes landed together; only the Ethernet buffer sizing is
bench-proven on its own to fix run 223's drops (runs 224-228, module
2026W36-0001) -- see the word-copy `memcpy()` entry below for its own,
separately measured A/B:

- **`CONFIG_ALP_SDK_FAST_MEMCPY`** (new Kconfig,
  `zephyr/kconfigs/core.kconfig`, default `n`, enabled explicitly on
  `examples/connectivity/camera-mjpeg-stream`'s AEN801/AEN803 board
  confs; requires Alif Ensemble + GCC + `CONFIG_SIZE_OPTIMIZATIONS` +
  picolibc-from-toolchain): on a
  -Os AEN image, `CONFIG_SIZE_OPTIMIZATIONS` links picolibc's "space"
  multilib, whose `memcpy()` copies one byte at a time. The full
  `CONFIG_SPEED_OPTIMIZATIONS` build copies faster but overflowed this
  app's ITCM budget by about 41 KB running from ITCM RAM, so it isn't
  an option here. The new `src/common/alp_fast_memcpy_core.c` walks a
  word (and, where aligned, four words) at a time instead — falling
  back to the byte loop whenever source/destination don't share the
  same 4-byte alignment phase — compiled at the TU's own -Os (no local
  optimize("O2") — an earlier version paired one with the loop and
  that, not -Os itself, let GCC auto-vectorize the loop to Arm MVE
  Cortex-M55 Q-register instructions, putting `memcpy()` on FPU/MVE
  state everywhere it runs; dropped). It carries
  `__attribute__((optimize("no-tree-loop-distribute-patterns")))` as
  insurance: without it, GCC's loop-idiom pass could rewrite the
  byte-copy loop shape back into a call to `memcpy()` — which, since
  this function *is* `memcpy()`, would recurse forever and hang the
  board. Confirmed against GCC 14.3, that pass does not rewrite this
  exact loop shape at plain -Os; the guard is insurance against a
  future -O2 build of this TU and a future loop edit — this file
  originally paired the guard with a local optimize("O2"), and it was
  under that O2 pairing that the recursion hung the board for real
  (bench run 227, before the network came up). GCC-only: Clang's own
  loop-idiom pass would still do the same rewrite regardless of that
  attribute, so the
  Kconfig depends on the GCC toolchain variant and the core `.c` also
  `#error`s under Clang as a second check. `src/zephyr/fast_memcpy.c`
  aliases `memcpy`/`__aeabi_memcpy`/`__aeabi_memcpy4`/`__aeabi_memcpy8`
  onto the core; Zephyr's link step wraps the `alp_sdk` Zephyr library
  in `-Wl,--whole-archive`, so this object is always pulled in and
  already resolves `memcpy` before the linker reaches picolibc's own
  (non-whole-archive) archive, so there is no multiple-definition
  error. New host unit test `tests/unit/fast_memcpy` (native_sim)
  exhaustively checks every source/destination alignment pair (0-3 byte
  offset each) crossed with every length 0-70 against a byte-at-a-time
  reference copy, calling the core function directly so the test binary
  never defines its own `memcpy()`; that target also compiles in a
  test-only assert that the word loop only ever runs against
  word-aligned pointers, so a mutated alignment check that still
  happens to copy the right bytes on this host still fails the test.

  Buffer sizing (below) is bench-proven on its own to take run 223's
  frame drops to 0%. A same-scene A/B against that buffer-sizing-only
  baseline (E1M-AEN803, module 2026W36-0001, 640x480 @ 30 fps,
  camera-bound) found no measurable gain from this word-copy override:
  A1 (memcpy ON) 30.03 fps / 1,089,750 B/s, B1 (memcpy OFF) 30.03 fps /
  1,092,219 B/s, A2 (memcpy ON) 30.03 fps / 1,088,302 B/s, 0 drops
  throughout. The send-bound case run 223 actually hit is still
  unmeasured — see this example's README.

- **Ethernet TX/RX buffer sizing**, added to both
  `examples/connectivity/camera-mjpeg-stream/boards/alp_e1m_aen801_m55_he_ae822fa0e5597ls0_rtss_he.conf`
  and the AEN803 sibling conf (content-identical, per this example's
  README convention): `CONFIG_NET_BUF_TX_COUNT=64`,
  `CONFIG_NET_PKT_TX_COUNT=32`, `CONFIG_NET_BUF_RX_COUNT=32`,
  `CONFIG_NET_PKT_RX_COUNT=16`, `CONFIG_NET_TCP_MAX_SEND_WINDOW_SIZE=65535`,
  `CONFIG_NET_TX_STACK_SIZE=2048` — overriding the smaller portable
  `prj.conf` defaults for these two hardware targets only (native_sim
  keeps the portable defaults; it has no Ethernet). Bench-proven to
  take frame drops to 0% on its own.

Combined, runs 224-228 reached **60.1 fps** end to end — the OV5647
sensor's own rate — 1803 frames in 30 s, interval stdev 0.1 ms. Two
caveats on that number, both called out in the example's README: it
used a simpler scene with a smaller mean frame (14.7 KB) than the
runs it's compared against, so it is not a clean same-scene A/B; and
the PHY was confirmed at 100 Mbit full duplex with TCP congestion
avoidance making no measurable difference.

### Added — 1280x960 camera streaming (15 fps capture/encode, ~7.5 fps delivered, send-bound) on E1M-AEN801/AEN803 + OV5647, Stage A (#2286)

`examples/connectivity/camera-mjpeg-stream` gains a `CONFIG_CAMERA_MJPEG_STREAM_1280X960`
build variant (`Kconfig`, this directory) that streams the OV5647's existing 1280x960
centre-crop mode at 15 fps through `<alp/camera.h>` — no sensor register-table change; a
full-FOV 2x2-binned 1280x960 mode is Stage B, tracked separately. 1920x1080 and 2592x1944
stay out of scope: the ISP caps table stops at 1920x1080, and two NV12 frames at either size
do not fit the AEN's 4 MiB SRAM0 bank.

Three sizing changes make the larger frame fit SRAM0 alongside the JPEG output buffers:
`src/backends/camera/alif_isp_pico.c`'s raw ISP buffer count is now the
`ALP_SDK_CAMERA_ALIF_ISP_VBUF_COUNT` Kconfig (`zephyr/kconfigs/power-camera-display.kconfig`,
default 3, was a fixed `#define`) so the new
`boards/overlay-1280x960.conf` can drop it to 2 — safe here because this app
requests NV12 (no CPU-side RGB565 conversion holds a buffer); the video buffer pool is
resized to 2 x 1,843,200 B plus slack (`CONFIG_VIDEO_BUFFER_POOL_HEAP_SIZE=3751936`); and
`mjpeg_http.h`'s `MJPEG_HTTP_MAX_JPEG` rises to 160 KiB per buffer under the new Kconfig.
`src/main.c`'s synthetic-frame fallback (used when there's no real camera, e.g. native_sim,
or when the camera stalls) is compiled out entirely at this resolution — a second SRAM0
buffer at 1,843,200 B has no budget left once the ISP and JPEG buffers are paid for; a
stalled/absent camera at 1280x960 just stops publishing instead.

A `camera_mjpeg_stream.aen_1280x960` build-only twister scenario (`testcase.yaml`,
AEN801 and AEN803) keeps this variant compiling in CI. Build result (linker map, not a
bench run): SRAM0 usage 4,131,200 B / 4 MiB (98.50%), ending at 0x023f0980 — inside the
4 MiB bank (0x02000000-0x023FFFF0) and nowhere near the unpowered SRAM1 (0x02400000+); 0
compiler warnings with `-DCONFIG_COMPILER_WARNINGS_AS_ERRORS=y`. Bench run 243
(E1M-AEN803 2026W36-0001, see README.md's Stage A section) since measured 0 CSI/IPI
fatals, 0 JPEG buffer-full, 15 fps capture/encode (encode ~2 ms), JPEG 131-135 KB at
quality 60 against the 163,840 B cap, and ~7.5 fps / 997,544 B/s delivered to the host
(the HTTP send path, not capture/encode, is the bottleneck); the AE envelope for this
resolution is left to #2277.

### Fixed — 1280x960 camera stream: JPEG encoder buffer-full once AE converged, `/stream` dropping clients during the retry burst (#2286)

Bench run 242 (E1M-AEN803 + OV5647, 1280x960 @ 15 fps): capture stayed clean (0 CSI/IPI
fatals) and frames 0-11 encoded fine (~130 KB, dark scene while AE converged), then EVERY
later encode failed with `ALP_ERR_NOMEM` (`alp_jpeg_encode failed (rc=-7 ...)`) as the
scene brightened — quality 80 (the 640x480 default) routinely exceeded
`MJPEG_HTTP_MAX_JPEG` (160 KiB) at this pixel count, and 160 KiB has no SRAM0 headroom
left to grow (98.5% bank usage). Downstream, every `/stream` client got re-served one
stale frame and disconnected after ~2.1 s: `mjpeg_http.c`'s `wait_and_claim()` gave up
and dropped the client the moment its single `IDLE_TIMEOUT_S` (2 s) wait for a new frame
came up empty, even though the capture pipeline was still alive and about to recover.

`src/main.c` now starts 1280x960 encodes at quality 60 (comfortably under the cap for a
typical frame) and, on `ALP_ERR_NOMEM`, retries the same frame once at a lower quality
via the new `jpeg_quality_step_down()` (`src/jpeg_quality_ladder.h`, floor 40,
native_sim-tested in `tests/unit/mjpeg_quality_ladder`) instead of dropping it outright.
`src/mjpeg_http.c`'s `wait_and_claim()` now gives a `/stream` client up to
`STREAM_STALL_TIMEOUT_S` (30 s) total for the next frame, spent across multiple shorter
condvar waits instead of one — `IDLE_TIMEOUT_S` still bounds socket I/O, but no longer
also doubles as the patience for an encode-retry burst. `src/main.c` also gained a
once-a-second stats line (fps, cumulative encoded/failed/retried counts, this-window
JPEG size min/avg/max, encode ms, and `mjpeg_http.c`'s last send ms) so the next bench
run's numbers are readable straight off the console.

Both 640x480 and 1280x960 variants still build with 0 warnings under
`-DCONFIG_COMPILER_WARNINGS_AS_ERRORS=y`. Bench run 243 (E1M-AEN803 2026W36-0001)
re-ran against these fixes: 0 JPEG buffer-full, 0 dropped `/stream` clients, and the
encode-retry ladder never triggered (0 retries — every frame encoded under cap at
quality 60 on the first attempt); see the README's Stage A section.

### Added — full-FOV 2x2-binned 1280x960 mode in the OV5647 driver, Stage B (#2286)

Stage B of #2286: 1280x960 on E1M-AEN801/AEN803 + OV5647 now reads out the sensor's WHOLE
pixel array and bins it 2x2, instead of Stage A's ~49%-width centre crop at the same
output size. `ov5647_set_mode_regs()`'s new branch at `zephyr/drivers/video/ov5647.c:1002`
("if (width == OV5647_MODE_1280X960_WIDTH && height == OV5647_MODE_1280X960_HEIGHT) {")
writes the new mode's window, output size, subsample/binning, analog, HTS and AEC
band-step registers as one coherent block, the same discipline AUTHORIZED LOCAL DIVERGENCE
#3 established for the 640x480 mode — binning must never be left armed against a different
window. Register values are re-derived from the RPi/OmniVision reference driver's OWN
2x2-binned mode (raspberrypi/linux rpi-6.12.y `drivers/media/i2c/ov5647.c`, the `reg_list`
its `ov5647_modes[]` names for a 1296x972 output) — cited by register meaning, no source
text copied (GPL) — then cropped further, to the delivered 1280x960, via the ISP offset
registers 0x3811/0x3813, `OV5647_BINNED1280_X_OFFSET` at `zephyr/drivers/video/ov5647.c:513`
("#define OV5647_BINNED1280_X_OFFSET 16"), the first mode in this driver to need a
non-default value for them — every OTHER mode (640x480 and the generic crop path) now
re-asserts their datasheet power-on default explicitly instead of leaving them unwritten,
so a prior 1280x960 selection can never leave this mode's crop armed on a different window
(fix-first review finding, issue #2286).

**PLL stays global**, per the issue: this driver keeps one `ov5647_init_regs[]` PLL write
(58,333,333, run 61's bench-proven value) for every mode. The reference's own HTS for this
mode, `OV5647_HTS_1280X960_BINNED` at `zephyr/drivers/video/ov5647.c:549`
("#define OV5647_HTS_1280X960_BINNED 1896 /* 0x0768 */"), is used unscaled despite the PLL
difference, which makes this mode's real line time 1896 / 58,333,333 = 32.503 us — 1.5x
the reference's OWN binned-mode line time (1896 / 87,500,000 = 21.669 us), not a match to
it (the arithmetic does not "cancel" against the reference's own line time; 32.503 us instead coincides,
by an unrelated numeric coincidence, with the reference's full-resolution line time, HTS
2844 / pixel_rate 87,500,000 = 32.497 us, since 2844 = 1896 × 1.5 exactly). Because the real
line time here is 32.503 us, the AEC 50/60 Hz band-step line counts are NOT the reference's
own 296/246 lines (those are its binned-mode line counts, the wrong real-time period at
this line time) — they are recomputed the same way the crop path's own band step already
is, to 308/256 (`OV5647_AEC_BAND_50HZ_1280X960BIN`/`OV5647_AEC_BAND_60HZ_1280X960BIN`).
`ov5647_hts_for()` at `zephyr/drivers/video/ov5647.c:902`
("static uint32_t ov5647_hts_for(uint32_t width, uint32_t height)") now returns this HTS
for 1280x960, which the frame-rate math below and any future VTS-derived exposure-limit
logic both depend on.

**Mode selection**: 1280x960 becomes the binned mode outright, not an opt-in alongside the
old crop — the crop delivered identical output pixels from a narrower FOV and a slower
line time (HTS 2700 vs 1896), so the binned mode strictly dominates it at this exact size.
The generic crop path stays available, unchanged, at every other size.

The mode also reaches 30 fps (VTS 1025 at HTS 1896, vs 15 fps's VTS 2051) — 45 fps is
rejected (VTS 683 < the 984-line minimum blanking). The driver's exposure clamp (#2277)
follows this mode's VTS, so exposure is capped at 2047 lines at 15 fps and 1021 at 30 fps.
`examples/connectivity/camera-mjpeg-stream`
still requests 15 fps by default; raising it needs its own bench pass. `SENSOR_CTRL09` for
this mode (0x3709, undocumented) is not in the reference's own reg_list at all; it reuses
the 1:1 value by register grouping (0x52 only ever pairs with 640x480's heavier subsample)
and is flagged BENCH-UNVERIFIED, same honesty convention as the crop path's own analog
values.

First bench result: E1M-AEN803 2026W36-0001 + OV5647, 1280x960 requested at 15 fps,
full-FOV binned mode — 0 CSI/IPI fatals, 0 picture-size violations, 0 encode failures; the
board encodes 15-16 fps (~109 KB JPEG frames, dark scene); the host receives 7.50 fps
(send-bound, ~0.82 MB/s); frames show a real scene with no banding (even/odd row and column
means equal within 0.02). This run predates the fix-first review's two register fixes
above (the power-on ISP-offset writeback and the 296/246 → 308/256 AEC band-step
correction) — it measured the mode BEFORE those two fixes.

Bench with the corrected registers (same unit, daylight scene): 1280x960 at 15 fps delivers
15.00 fps to the host over 60 s (900 frames, ~35 KB JPEG, max gap 68 ms) with 0 CSI/IPI
fatals, 0 picture-size violations, 0 encode failures and no row/column banding, and AE/AWB
settle on the scene; the 640x480 mode on the same branch still delivers 30.03 fps with no
errors. 30 fps at 1280x960 is not benched yet.

**The 1280x960 stream variant resets the TCP send window to auto.** After #2285 the
AEN board confs set `CONFIG_NET_TCP_MAX_SEND_WINDOW_SIZE=65535` for the larger 640x480
buffer pools, and the 1280x960 overlay inherited it while keeping 16/8 TX buffers; the
stream then sent only its multipart headers and every JPEG send stalled to the 2 s socket
timeout. `boards/overlay-1280x960.conf` now sets the window to 0, and the merged tree
streams 1280x960 again on E1M-AEN803 2026W36-0001 (13.80 fps over 60 s at ~39 KB JPEG,
at ~0.54 MB/s; 0 errors; frames distinct).

`tests/zephyr/video_sensors/src/ov5647_test.c` gains `test_set_format_1280x960_binned_
fullfov_before_park` (the coherent register block, ordered before the lane park, mirroring
the existing 640x480 test), `test_set_format_1280x960_binned_30fps_vts` and
`test_enum_frmival_1280x960_accepts_30_rejects_45` (the 15/30 fps VTS math and the 30/45
fps reachability boundary); `test_set_format_switch_never_leaves_binning_on_crop_window`
and `test_crop_aec_max_bands_computed_per_mode`, which previously exercised the generic
crop path at 1280x960, now use 1920x1080 instead, since 1280x960 no longer takes that path.
All three new tests fail against the pre-Stage-B driver (native_sim twister,
`alp_sdk.video.rpi_csi2_sensors`: 39/42 passed, 3 failed with the driver reverted).

`examples/connectivity/camera-mjpeg-stream`'s `Kconfig`, `README.md`,
`boards/overlay-1280x960.conf` and `src/main.c` are updated to describe the new full-FOV
binned mode in place of Stage A's centre-crop description — output size and the 15 fps
default request are unchanged; only the field of view and the per-mode register table
changed. Existing bench runs 242/243 in the README were measured under Stage A's crop mode
and are labelled as such; the bench runs of this driver-mode change are the two paragraphs above.

Builds 0 warnings under `-DCONFIG_COMPILER_WARNINGS_AS_ERRORS=y` for
`camera-mjpeg-stream` (640x480 and the 1280x960 overlay), `aen-isp-ov5647-viewfinder` and
`aen-camera-firstlight` on `alp_e1m_aen803_m55_he/ae822fa0e5597ls0/rtss_he`.

### Added — Sony IMX296 Zephyr sensor driver + Raspberry Pi Global Shutter Camera shield; Stage A raw capture bench-verified (#2287)

`zephyr/drivers/video/imx296.c` adds a Sony IMX296 driver for the
INNO-MAKER CAM-IMX296RAW-TRIGGER-compatible module (IMX296LQR-C colour
part), authored from the Sony IMX296 datasheet — no permissive-licence
IMX296 driver exists anywhere to consume (not in upstream Zephyr v4.4.1,
hal_alif, or Espressif esp_cam_sensor; Linux's and libcamera's are
GPL/LGPL, not consumable under this project's licence). Linux's imx296.c
was used strictly as a REGISTER-NAME reference for a handful of names this
datasheet leaves unnamed (e.g. SENSOR_INFO, `0x3148`) — no code, text or
table from it was copied into this driver. ADR-0017-ADJACENT. All-pixel
scan mode only: 1456x1088 `SRGGB10P` RAW10 (the sensor's whole transmitted
frame — 1440x1080 is the datasheet's "recording pixels" crop inside it),
**1 MIPI CSI-2 data lane** (unlike the sibling OV5647/OV9281 shields, both
2-lane), 60.3 frame/s (datasheet mode rate; not measured), 37.125/54/74.25 MHz INCK (any other frequency
rejected at runtime with `-ENOTSUP`). Controls: exposure (lines of
integration via `SHS`), analogue+digital gain (0.1 dB step via `GAIN`), H/V
flip, pixel rate (118.8 Mpix/s), link frequency (594 MHz).

The `raspberry_pi_global_shutter_camera` shield wires the sensor's 54 MHz
`fixed-clock`, CCI address 0x1A, and single-lane endpoint onto the same
board-agnostic `raspberry_pi_camera_module_2`-style label contract as its
siblings (`chosen zephyr,camera`, `&csi_interface`, `&csi_ep_in`,
`&csi_i2c`); build with
`SHIELD="<carrier-connector-shield> raspberry_pi_global_shutter_camera"`.
`examples/aen/aen-camera-firstlight` gets a matching IMX296 `#elif` +
`testcase.yaml` scenario — see `docs/camera-shields.md` for the full
driver/shield/control reference and bench-status split.

**Stage A scope, bench-verified on E1M-AEN803 2026W36-0001 (E1M-EVK,
`csi_i2c` = I2C1 @ `0x49011000`)**: I2C identity (bench run 229 — CCI
`0x1A`; `STANDBY`/`XMSTA` match datasheet POR defaults; SENSOR_INFO
register `0x3148`/`0x3149` reads `0x4A00` — **undocumented in the public
preliminary datasheet**, so treated as an opaque bench-confirmed signature
for the colour LQR variant, not a documented chip-ID register, and gates
`imx296_init()`), CSI-2 streaming, and a full 1456x1088 RAW10 frame
captured through `<alp/camera.h>` and verified against a real scene: bench
run 292 (single capture, no discard, evening light, gain 0) reads mean
pixel value 61.19, max 108, a clean close-out (no crash, no error return)
and no mod-4-column RAW10 byte-phase-slip pattern in the captured image;
its 8x8-block correlation against diag control run 293 (`SHS`=14 written
directly, same light) is 0.98. Both runs are still dim — about 1 code
above black (60) under this bench's evening light — so this confirms the
register writes and capture pipeline now agree and produce a real (if
faint) image, not yet a well-exposed one; better lighting or exposure
tuning is a follow-up. **Run 292's build had `CONFIG_LOG` unset (no log
output at all)**, so nothing about its console — clean or otherwise — says
anything about `INT_IPI_PIXEL_IF_HLINE_ERR` or
`INT_IPI_PIXEL_IF_FIFO_OVERFLOW`: their status on the product build is
UNKNOWN, not "not seen". The `37-80` per-capture and `~10.8k` HLINE_ERR
counts elsewhere in this changelog were measured in EARLIER diag runs (the
269-276-era diag-instrumented builds, and run 285's 16-frame continuous
diag run, which DID have logging), all predating the init-period-wait,
SHS, and CPI-only-pause fixes below. Continuous streaming has not been
benched on the product (non-diag, logging-enabled) build at all, so
whether HLINE_ERR/FIFO_OVERFLOW occur there, post-fix, remains open.

**NOT yet bench-verified at Stage A**: the ISP-Pico colour path,
auto-exposure, and `camera-mjpeg-stream`-style continuous streaming
beyond the single-capture/starvation-paced loop `aen-camera-firstlight`
exercises. Stage B (below) since benched ROI mode, the ISP-Pico data
path, AE, and continuous MJPEG streaming — see that section's own "Not
verified" list for what remains open (colour/AWB/CCM, fast-trigger mode,
and the rest). Whether a paused 2-lane sensor (OV5647, OV9281 — this
CPI's other sensors) can back-pressure the IPI into overflow during a
longer starvation pause is also still untested.

`tests/zephyr/video_sensors` adds a real runtime ztest suite
(`imx296_test.c`) against its own I2C emulator (`imx296_emul.c`), cloning
the OV5647/OV9281 emulator+ztest shape: the SENSOR_INFO identity probe
(accept and `-ENODEV` reject paths), the STANDBY/XMSTA/init register-write
ORDER (not just final values), the exact init register values (`VMAX`
1118, `HMAX` 1100, `INCKSEL0..3`, `0x418C`, `BLKLEVEL`, ROI-disable,
`0x3005`, `SHS`/`GAIN`/`REVERSE` defaults), the one fixed format, and the
exposure/gain/flip control paths.

#### Fast-trigger exposure mode (external trigger) — added, UNVERIFIED

`imx296.c` also adds a driver-private control, `IMX296_CID_TRIGGER_MODE`
(`VIDEO_CID_PRIVATE_BASE + 0x01`, default free-run — unchanged behaviour),
switching the sensor into the datasheet's Global Shutter **Fast Trigger
Mode** (`TRIGEN` at `0x300B`, `LOWLAGTRG` at `0x30AE`, `SYNCSEL` at
`0x3036` — "Global Shutter (Fast Trigger Mode) Operation", page 64). This
is the only one of the datasheet's two trigger sub-modes this hardware can
reach: Sequential Trigger Mode is "slave mode only" (page 62) and, like
every sensor on the RPi-style 15-pin CSI connector, this module has no
XVS/XHS lines wired, so slave mode is never reachable. Trigger mode is
still MASTER mode, started by the same `XMSTA` write as free-run; only
frame output and exposure timing become XTRIG-driven afterward. The mode
switch is applied in `imx296_set_stream()`, before `STANDBY` is cancelled,
since "Mode Transitions of Global Shutter Operation" (page 66) requires
it. Setting the control while already streaming is rejected `-EBUSY`.

`examples/aen/aen-camera-firstlight` gets an opt-in `-DAEN_CAMERA_TRIGGER=ON`
CMake option (`CMakeLists.txt`, `trigger_gpio.overlay`): arms the
control and pulses a GPIO on Alif P5_1 (Arduino D4 / `EVK_PIN_CK_DIO4`,
E1M pad M2) to capture and timestamp a few frames, for the sensor module's
own opto-isolated J3 Trig+ header (on the INNO-MAKER module, not the
E1M-EVK carrier). **Trigger electrical polarity is UNVERIFIED** — the
INNO-MAKER module's J3 input circuit has not been checked against that
module's own documentation, so the DT `GPIO_ACTIVE_HIGH`/`GPIO_ACTIVE_LOW`
flag on `imx296-trigger-gpios` is a guess — **do not wire J3 until that
circuit is confirmed**. **UNTESTED ON SILICON**: both the driver's trigger
mode and this example's build mode compile clean (0 warnings) but have not
run with a trigger pulse, and the 150 ms sensor init-period wait added
below (`IMX296_INIT_PERIOD_MS`) covers free-run timing only — trigger-mode
init timing is unhandled and unbenched.

### Fixed — bring-up bugs found and fixed before Stage A shipped (#2287)

- **LP-11 clock-lane park.** `imx296_init()` leaves the sensor in STANDBY,
  and this datasheet documents no register that forces the CSI-2 CLOCK
  lane to Stop-state (LP-11) short of exiting STANDBY into full
  master-mode streaming — the same shape OV5647 hit (#2248), fixed there
  with an explicit lane-park sequence this datasheet gives no equivalent
  registers for. An earlier version of this fix made the D-PHY's
  Stop-state wait (`dphy_dw_slave_setup()`) warn-and-continue on ANY
  timeout, for every sensor; that was wrong (it would have silently
  re-opened the exact class of bug that same wait caught for OV5647,
  #2248) and is reverted. Fixed narrowly instead: `struct
  dphy_csi2_settings` gains a `skip_clk_lane_stopstate` field, set only
  from `raspberry_pi_global_shutter_camera.overlay`'s
  `no-lp11-clock-lane-park` DT property, skipping ONLY the clock-lane
  Stop-state bit for this one sensor; every data-lane bit and the wait's
  timeout stay fatal for this sensor and every other.

- **CSI-2 data lane stuck in LP-11 without a bench-derived register
  write.** Without writing register `0x3005 = 0xF0` (undocumented in the
  datasheet; bench runs #263/#264 found it by sweep, not from the
  register map) the data lane never left LP-11 at all — no HS output.
  `imx296_init()` now writes it unconditionally, documented in-code as
  bench-derived. Also added, datasheet-cited this time (pages 49, 51-52):
  `BLKLEVEL` (`0x3254`, the datasheet's recommended `0x03C`) and the
  `FID0_ROIH1ON`/`FID0_ROIV1ON` pair (`0x3300`, disabled) — the latter is
  this datasheet's actual all-pixel-vs-ROI-mode switch, written explicitly
  so a prior ROI-mode session's crop window can't leak across a warm SoC
  reset (the module stays powered across one).

- **IPI-fatal log/reset flood capped.** `video_csi_dw.c`'s `csi2_dw_irq()`
  used to `LOG_ERR` and IPI-soft-reset on every single
  `CSI_INT_ST_MAIN_IPI_FATAL` event, uncapped — with bad IPI framing this
  could fire once per line, flooding the log and storming the IPI reset
  line. It now logs only the first 16 occurrences per unmask window
  (`CSI2_DW_IPI_FATAL_LOG_LIMIT`), then masks `CSI_INT_MSK_IPI_FATAL` and
  logs one "masked after 16" line; the window resets via
  `csi2_dw_irq_on()`, which now also runs from `csi2_dw_stream_start()` on
  every user stream (re)start, not just from `csi2_dw_configure()` — so a
  mask a previous stream left set no longer hides every fatal on the next
  one. A separate, never-reset `ipi_fatal_total` field keeps the lifetime
  count for diagnostics.

- **Runtime `CSI_IPI_SOFTRSTN` toggle removed from the IPI-fatal ISR.**
  Bench run 271 (product image), WITH the runtime toggle present, panicked
  at buffer close: the CPI's DMA wrote ~2744 bytes past a 3,168,256-byte
  frame buffer's end, corrupting the next heap chunk header
  (`sys_heap_free()`'s hardening check caught it). Bench runs 272-276,
  WITHOUT the toggle, all completed capture+close with no panic — 1
  overrun in 1 run with the toggle vs. 0 in 5 without it: a correlation,
  not a confirmed mechanism (run 271's own logging was disabled, so which
  IPI-fatal event fired that run is unknown). `csi2_dw_irq()` no longer
  soft-resets `CSI_IPI_SOFTRSTN` on any fatal event, matching the vendored
  Alif DFP reference's own IPI-fatal handler, which never resets IPI at
  runtime either. This hazard is not IMX296-specific in principle —
  OV5647/OV9281 use the same zero-slack frame buffers and are **likely
  exposed** but this has **not been bench-reproduced** on either.

- **DW CSI-2 IPI switched to Controller timing mode.** The host's default
  "Camera" IPI mode derives its line timing from the D-PHY clock and
  emitted **no** IPI lines at all for this 1-lane sensor on silicon.
  `raspberry_pi_global_shutter_camera.overlay` now switches the `&csi`
  controller to IPI **Controller** timing mode with fixed
  `csi-hsa`/`csi-hbp`/`csi-hsd`/`csi-vsa`/`csi-vbp`/`csi-vfp` timings
  derived from this sensor's own `HMAX`/`VMAX` (HSD bench sweep: 503 gives
  zero IPI-FIFO overflow; 520 and 531 both overflowed and banded the
  frame). These `ipi-mode`/timing properties live on the `&csi` controller
  node itself, not a per-sensor endpoint, so they apply to whatever sensor
  is stacked on this controller, not IMX296 specifically -- today only one
  sensor is ever wired to a given `&csi` controller, so this is a
  scope note, not a live conflict. `csi2_dw_validate_data()` also drops
  its usual 20% bandwidth margin on the CSI IPI pixel-clock request in
  Controller mode: that margin exists to keep the IPI ahead of the sensor
  in Camera mode, where HSD is *derived from* the resulting clock; in
  Controller mode the DT timings *set* the drain rate instead, and the
  margined request picked a different, starving clock divisor (bare
  request → divisor 3, 133.33 MHz, matching the overlay's derivation;
  margined request → divisor 2, 200 MHz -- **calculated from the
  clock-control divisor rule, not independently bench-measured with a
  scope/analyzer; the margined request was never actually made on the
  bench** (the fix removes it before any hardware run). This is what took
  the capture path from "emits no IPI line at all" to full 1456x1088
  frames. `csi2_dw_validate_data()` also gained a `LOG_INF` (on every
  `set_format`, Controller mode only) reporting the pixel clock actually
  programmed, the DT-fixed `HLINE`, and the line time they work out to --
  so a future clock-control divisor change that silently invalidates this
  overlay's HSD derivation shows up in the log instead of only as a
  re-appeared FIFO overflow.

- **Buffer-starvation pause STANDBY-cycled the sensor on every frame.**
  The starvation pause (`alif_cam_work_helper()`) and its resume
  (`alif_cam_enqueue()`) used to call `video_stream_stop()`/`_start()` on
  the CSI-2 endpoint, driving the sensor into STANDBY on every pause and
  back to RUN on every resume — a full standby-to-run cycle per frame with
  a one-buffer capture/release loop. The datasheet's 8-frame
  initialization period after STANDBY cancel (below) made this worse: the
  kept frame was always still ramping up. Diag run 285 (predating the
  init-period-wait fix below) also showed a RAW10 4-column byte-phase-slip
  pattern with the old endpoint-cycling behaviour, SUSPECTED (not
  confirmed) to be the CPI's frame-boundary tracking desyncing from the
  CSI-2 IPI stream on each endpoint restart. Fixed: the pause now stops
  only the CPI capture engine (`hw_cam_cpi_only_stop()` — `CAM_CTRL` stop,
  `BUSY` poll, soft reset, clear latched interrupts, the same steps
  `alif_cam_stream_stop()` applies to the CPI side of its own teardown)
  and leaves the CSI-2 endpoint and sensor streaming across the stall; the
  resume path restarts only the CPI. A user `stop()`/`close()` is
  unaffected — `alif_cam_stream_stop()` still calls `video_stream_stop()`
  on the endpoint unconditionally, the only stop that ever reaches it
  while a starvation pause is in effect. While paused, the sensor, D-PHY
  and CSI-2 host keep running (and drawing power); frames the sensor sends
  during the pause are simply dropped at the stopped CPI. `hw_cam_cpi_only_stop()`
  lives in the shared CPI driver (`video_alif.c`), so this behaviour change
  applies to OV5647 and OV9281 too, not just IMX296 -- but it is
  bench-verified on IMX296 only; whether a paused 2-lane sensor can
  back-pressure the IPI into overflow during a longer pause is untested,
  and re-bench on OV5647/OV9281 is pending.

- **First frame after every stream start was inside the 8-frame init
  period.** "Standby mode" (datasheet p54): a normal image is output only
  from the 9th frame after STANDBY cancel. `imx296_set_stream(dev, true,
  ...)` used to return as soon as the `XMSTA` write started master-mode
  free-run, so the CPI's own capture-snapshot arm
  (`alif_cam_stream_start()` → `hw_cam_start_video_capture()`, called
  immediately once the sensor's `set_stream` returns all the way back up
  through `csi2_dw_stream_start()`) could land inside that init period.
  Fixed in the sensor driver, not the apps that tripped over it:
  `imx296_set_stream()` now blocks for `IMX296_INIT_PERIOD_MS` (150 ms, 9
  frames of margin over the 132 ms the 8-frame period works out to at
  `IMX296_VMAX` x 1H = 1118 x 14.81us, p44/p53) after the `XMSTA` write,
  before returning — free-run mode only (see the trigger-mode caveat
  above).

- **SHS init-write bug: an accidental 14-line exposure.**
  `imx296_init()`'s hardware-defaults write wrote `IMX296_REG_SHS =
  IMX296_VMAX - IMX296_SHS_DEFAULT` (1104), wrongly applying the
  exposure-lines-to-SHS conversion `imx296_set_ctrl()` uses for control
  values. SHS is the shutter START line, not exposure lines
  ("Calculation Formula of Exposure Time", page 60): the register value
  should be `IMX296_SHS_DEFAULT` (14) itself, giving the intended
  1104-line exposure — not `IMX296_VMAX` minus it. The wrong write put
  SHS=1104 in hardware, a 14-line (~0.2 ms) exposure instead of 1104
  lines — this, not "no light reaching the array", is why every product
  capture before this fix read flat black (mean pixel value 60.15,
  bench runs 288/291): `imx296_set_ctrl()`'s own conversion was already
  correct and is unchanged. Fixed to write `IMX296_SHS_DEFAULT` directly.
  `test_shs_gain_reverse_defaults_written_at_init` asserted the old,
  wrong register value; it now asserts the correct one. Confirmed fixed
  together with the init-period-wait fix above by bench run 292 (see the
  Stage A summary above).

`tests/zephyr/video_sensors` only emulates the IMX296 sensor over I2C/CCI
and never instantiates `video_csi_dw.c` or a clock-control device, so
there is no native_sim harness the DW CSI-2 IPI-timing-mode change above
can be asserted against; no test was added for it.

### Added — IMX296 Stage B: ROI mode, ISP-Pico data path, AE, continuous MJPEG streaming (#2287)

- **ROI mode (1280x960)** — `imx296.c` gains a second `video_format_cap`,
  a centred 1280x960 `SRGGB10P` crop inside the fixed 1456x1088
  full-frame mode (datasheet pp.51-53); `VMAX` stays 1118 for both.
  Bench-verified, runs 294/295: clean captures at both resolutions, the
  ROI frame correlates 0.91 against an (88,64)-offset crop of the
  full-frame capture.
- **CSI controller timing follows the format** — `video_csi_dw.c` derives
  `hsd`/`vfp` from new optional `csi-hline`/`csi-vtotal` DT properties and
  the active format's `hact`/`vact`, instead of one fixed `csi-hsd`/
  `csi-vfp` pair that was only ever correct for one resolution. The
  derived full-frame values reproduce the existing bench-swept numbers
  exactly (console: `"CSI IPI Controller-mode: pixclk 133333333 Hz,
  HLINE 1972 px -> line time 14790 ns"`, runs 294/295).
- **SRGGB10P through ISP-Pico** — new hal_alif patch 0012 +
  `isp_pico.c`'s input-format-cap entry give the ISP driver IMX296's
  fourcc. Data path bench-verified end to end (run 297: SRGGB10P ->
  ISP-Pico -> YUV420, 0.83 correlation against the pre-ISP raw ROI
  frame); image quality (AWB/CCM/AE) is not — see "Not verified" below.
- `examples/aen/aen-isp-ov5647-capture` renamed to `aen-isp-capture`
  (`git mv` + every reference across the tree) and gains an opt-in
  `-DAEN_ISP_IMX296=ON` variant; OV5647 stays the default.
- **IMX296 AE envelope** — new hal_alif patch 0013 (`imx296_ae_envelope.h`)
  + `isp_sns_gain_conv.h` give IMX296 its own AE calibration and
  gain/exposure unit conversion (0.1 dB/count logarithmic register <->
  library units, exposure lines -> `VIDEO_CID_EXPOSURE`); native_sim
  `tests/zephyr/isp_ae_conv` covers the conversion math (481-entry
  monotonic + round-trip sweep). AWB/CCM still fall through to the stock
  ARX3A0 defaults — no IMX296 colour calibration exists yet.
- `aen-isp-capture` gains an AE-on scenario, a raw `SHS`/`GAIN`
  register-dump diagnostic, and `AEN_ISP_N_FRAMES`/
  `AEN_ISP_IMX296_EXPOSURE_LINES`/`AEN_ISP_IMX296_GAIN` CMake options for
  manual-control bench captures. See its own README.md.
- **camera-mjpeg-stream IMX296 scenario** — reuses the existing 1280x960
  overlay unchanged (IMX296's ROI crop is the same NV12 frame size
  OV5647's binned mode already accounts for); AE on, AWB at the ISP's
  stock default (no IMX296 calibration). Bench-verified end to end, runs
  312-314: DHCP + MJPEG stream serving valid JPEGs, 61 fps encode, up to
  28.3 fps / 885 KB/s delivered to one client (run 314).

### Fixed — Stage B bring-up bugs (#2287)

- **ISP-driven CPI snapshot re-arm** — the CPI (SNAPSHOT capture mode)
  was being re-armed by `video_alif.c`'s own STOP-interrupt handler
  before the ISP decided whether a destination buffer existed for the
  next frame; the old "pause" mechanism then aborted an in-flight
  capture mid-frame, corrupting captured frames (visible as horizontal
  banding, runs 304-306). Re-arm responsibility moved entirely into
  `isp_pico.c`'s own bottom half, only after it has attached the next
  buffer to its MI (`isp_attach_buffer_to_hw()`); a new error callback
  (`alif_cam_register_error_cb()`) lets a CPI/CSI-level stall that never
  reaches the ISP's own frame-end interrupt still trigger re-arm.
  Bench-confirmed fixed, runs 309/310: `frame_end_count` advances exactly
  +1 per app frame, a whole-frame scene (vs. the earlier streaked
  bands), AE converging upward to its exposure/gain ceilings in the dim
  scene. Caller-visible: `video_set_format()` on the ISP returns `-EBUSY`
  while it is starvation-paused (stop it first), and an AWB/AE control
  change made during a pause forces a full restart on the next start.
- **GAINDLY (0x3212)** now written at init (`0x09`, "gain reflect at the
  next frame") — was left at its datasheet-prohibited POR default of
  `0x00`.
- **IMX296 AE exposure ceiling clamped to 1104 lines** (`SHS`=14, the
  sensor's own POR default) instead of the datasheet's `SHS`=4 floor —
  `SHS`=4 produced a flat black frame in this driver's ROI configuration,
  which the datasheet's own frame-rate table never itself tabulates
  against `VMAX`=1118 (run 304 vs. 306).
- **IMX296 AE gain ceiling capped at 24.0 dB** (the GAIN register's
  analog-only side of its gain-vs-code bend, datasheet p.56) instead of
  the full 48.0 dB — consistent with a dim scene's noise at full gain
  overflowing
  camera-mjpeg-stream's JPEG output buffer (run 312); a separate push
  that overwrote this calibration ceiling with the sensor's wider manual
  control range (spurious "AE attr mismatch" log) was also found and
  fixed (run 313), and `VIDEO_ISP_VSI_AE_AGAIN_MAX_DB_TENTHS` now clamps
  it. `again` bench-confirmed converging to exactly the new ceiling
  (`0x3f65` = 16229), never higher.
- **camera-mjpeg-stream's JPEG quality ladder** now actually engages on a
  buffer-full encode (its retry gate previously keyed off a value the
  failing backend path never set, so it never triggered) and only
  persists a lowered quality when a lower-quality retry actually
  succeeded (a pool-exhaustion failure no longer permanently lowers
  quality for later frames). `CONFIG_VIDEO_LOG_LEVEL_WRN=y` added to stop
  the VSI AE/AWB library's own continuous diagnostic chatter (~13 KB/s)
  from wrapping the 16 KiB RAM console buffer, which was also silently
  evicting this app's own DHCP lease/URL boot lines (runs 312-314).

### Fixed — the Linux `gpio-gd32-bridge` driver now replays requested GPIO output state after the GD32 comes up late or resets (#2297)

Bug observed and fix bench-verified on E1M-V2M103 (GD32 fw 0.2.13), 2026-09-26.
Two cases were checked. At cold boot, probe finds the bridge down and the
panel-reset write fails. The replay then logs `bridge reachable, 1 line(s)
in the replay mask` at ~5 s, with no driver rebind. With GD32_NRST held for
2 s mid-run, the log shows `output state replay failed (-6)` and then the
same "in the replay mask" line, and `GPIO_READ` confirms the pad level. Two
related bugs in
`meta-alp-sdk/recipes-kernel/linux/linux-renesas/0005-gpio-add-gd32-bridge-expander-driver.patch`
(`drivers/gpio/gpio-gd32-bridge.c`): (1) `gd32_bridge_gpio_set()` only
latched `output_mask`/`output_vals` **after** a successful I2C
`GPIO_WRITE`, so a write attempted while the bridge was not yet
answering was silently forgotten forever — seen at probe as `GPIO write
line 5 failed` against the Display-1 panel `reset-gpios` consumer,
since the gpiochip registers unconditionally even while the bridge is
still down; (2) nothing re-applied host-requested state after the GD32
came up late or after any GD32 reset (WDT, an OTA A/B swap), both of
which reset every pad to its boot default — including the Wi-Fi/BT
REG_ON lines 18/19, which this issue originally tracked.

Fixed by (1) latching `output_mask`/`output_vals` under a new
`state_lock` and holding that lock across the *entire* transfer (not
just the latch) in both the write path and the replay path, so a
concurrent replay can never read a stale snapshot and land its write
after a newer one — driving a line back down (e.g. `wl-reg-on` low
again mid `mmc-pwrseq`, or the panel reset line) — and (2) a
`delayed_work` that re-issues one idempotent `CMD_GPIO_WRITE(output_mask,
output_vals)` roughly once a second whenever `output_mask != 0`, queued
on `system_freezable_power_efficient_wq` (not the plain system
workqueue, which would keep running — and touching I2C — across
suspend). Re-asserting an already-correct level is glitch-free, so the
replay needs no reset detection — it just needs to run often enough
that a freshly-up bridge is re-promoted within about one period.
Deliberately does **not** use `CMD_RESET_REASON`: that opcode is
clear-on-read on the firmware side, so polling it would itself destroy
the very signal a second reader needs. The replay masks lines 18/19
back out unless `.request()`'s existing protocol-version gate
(`gd32_bridge_resolve_wifi_bt()`) has already confirmed the bridge
understands them. Costs one small I2C frame/s on BRD_I2C (`i2c8`) while
any line is held as output.

As a consequence, `direction_output()` always reports success instead
of propagating the transfer error. This chip's consumers (the Display-1
panel `reset-gpios`, `mmc-pwrseq-simple`, a Bluetooth `shutdown-gpios`)
are ordinary `gpiod_direction_output()` callers, **not** OF `gpio-hog`
lines, and have no `-EPROBE_DEFER` equivalent once past `.request()`:
a nonzero return here would fail the *consumer's* own probe permanently
over what is usually only a transient bridge-down window. Swallowing it
instead lets the consumer's probe proceed; the requested state is
latched regardless and the replay applies it once the bridge answers,
so the consumer just cannot tell the line is actually driven until the
next successful replay (now logged with a `dev_warn_ratelimited()` at
the call site too).

Stated plainly: this means a one-shot sequencer that acts the instant
`.request()`/`.direction_output()` return — `mmc-pwrseq-simple` (SDHI2
WLAN power-up) and a panel's `reset-gpios` (Display-1) — can silently
mis-drive its line for as long as the bridge stays unreachable, since it
never sees the failed transfer. The replay re-applies the latched level
within ~1 s (`GD32_REPLAY_PERIOD_MS`) of the bridge next answering, so
the window is bounded rather than unbounded.

Only the Linux side re-asserts. **#2297 stays open** for the CM33/Zephyr
side of the bridge, which does not yet re-apply anything after a reset,
and re-asserting REG_ON only restores the pin level — it does not
re-initialise the Linux Wi-Fi/BT drivers if the reset also disturbed the
Murata module itself.

See also: `docs/gd32-bridge-protocol.md` §3.1 (host-behaviour note,
including the BRD_I2C shared-bus/arbitration caveat, updated in the same
change).

**Follow-up (same branch; bug bench-observed 2026-09-26, E1M-V2M103,
this fix bench-verified 2026-09-26 on E1M-V2M103 with GD32_NRST held ~40 s
past probe: the resolve poller's fixed 1 Hz ticks (1..30 s, then 31, 33,
37, 45, 61 s ...) mean the bridge was first observed by the 45 s poll —
SDIO card enumerated 48.4 s, brcmfmac firmware 49.7 s, hci0 UP+RUNNING
54.8 s, devices_deferred empty, no rebind; a normal boot is unchanged):**
lines 18/19's `.request()` gate
(`gd32_bridge_resolve_wifi_bt()`) used to return `-EPROBE_DEFER` itself
when the bridge was still silent, which permanently deferred the
*consumer* -- `mmc-pwrseq-simple`'s `wlan-pwrseq` `reset-gpios` and
`hci_bcm`'s `shutdown-gpios` -- with nothing to ever retry it, since a
bare `-EPROBE_DEFER` only gets retried when some other driver's
