(un)registration happens to walk the deferred-probe list. Observed on
the bench: NRST release failed, and
`/sys/kernel/debug/devices_deferred` listed `15c20000.mmc`,
`wlan-pwrseq` and `serial0-0` for the whole boot, even though the
bridge came up seconds later. `.request()` must still return
`-EPROBE_DEFER` rather than grant the request while unresolved,
though: `mmc-pwrseq-simple` and `hci_bcm` each run a one-shot power-up
sequence (`mmc_rescan()` / loading the `.hcd` patch) immediately once
`.request()` succeeds, and SDHI2 being non-removable means that
sequence never reruns on its own if it runs before REG_ON can actually
move.

What resolves the deferral instead: a new, independent `delayed_work`
(`gd32_bridge_resolve_work()`) that polls `GET_VERSION` regardless of
whether any consumer has requested the lines yet (flat at ~1 Hz for
the first ~30 s, then backing off exponentially to a 30 s cap). This
poller is terminal, not perpetual: it stops rescheduling itself the
moment it gets a definitive answer (confirmed supported, or confirmed
unsupported) and kicks deferred probing once. It does not keep running
afterwards to notice a later bridge reset or OTA A/B swap — nothing
re-resolves the lines-18/19 *capability* answer once this poller has
settled it; only the separate output-state replay above keeps
re-applying pad *levels* after a reset. On its first definitive answer
it briefly registers a throwaway `platform_device`
(`gd32_bridge_kick_deferred_probe()`) purely so that device's bind runs
`driver_bound()` -> the kernel's own `driver_deferred_probe_trigger()`
(`drivers/base/dd.c`, confirmed present at that call site in this
kernel tree) -- a convenient in-tree hook module code can use to queue
a deferred-probe retry (asynchronous, on `system_unbound_wq`) on
demand, not the only such mechanism (`device_reprobe()` /
`bus_rescan_devices()` / `wait_for_device_probe()` also exist). That
gets `mmc-pwrseq-simple` / `hci_bcm` to retry `.request()` with the
real answer -- granted, or failing outright with `-ENODEV` -- instead
of lingering deferred indefinitely. `.request()` itself now makes only
a single non-blocking `GET_VERSION` attempt instead of a bounded
blocking wait, since the independent poller above is what actually
catches a slow bridge.

### Fixed — `gpio-gd32-bridge` probe retries `GET_VERSION` and no longer races its own workqueue cancellation on unbind/rebind (#2297)

Bench-observed on E1M-V2M103, 2026-09-29, in
`meta-alp-sdk/recipes-kernel/linux/linux-renesas/0005-gpio-add-gd32-bridge-expander-driver.patch`
(`drivers/gpio/gpio-gd32-bridge.c`). Two issues, both in
`gd32_bridge_gpio_probe()`.

(1) The probe-time `GET_VERSION` handshake made exactly one attempt: at a
cold boot the GD32 is still coming up at ~1.95 s in, so this consistently
missed — observed as `-EBADMSG` (-74, a torn reply) and `-EBUSY` (-16,
arbitration lost on a bus the GD32 hasn't released yet) — while a
`GET_VERSION` issued a few seconds later on the same bridge succeeded
cleanly (reply `00 00 0e 00 cf a7`). The "registering gpiochip anyway"
best-effort design (Refs #2297) is correct — a `-EPROBE_DEFER` here would
hold the whole DSI/DU pipeline hostage to the bridge's liveness via the
Display-1 panel reset line — but paying for only one attempt when the
bridge is this close to answering just pushed the wait onto
`gd32_bridge_resolve_work()`'s 1 Hz poller instead. Fixed with a bounded
retry: up to 3 attempts, 10-20 ms apart, before falling back to the
existing "bridge not answering" path unchanged.

(2) `echo 8-0070 > /sys/bus/i2c/drivers/gpio-gd32-bridge/unbind` then bind
printed a WARN stack trace at `gd32_bridge_gpio_probe+0x2cc` on the
re-probe. Root cause: `devm_gpiochip_add_data()` was registered *last* in
probe, after the two `devm_add_action_or_reset()` calls that cancel
`replay_work`/`resolve_work`. `devm` teardown runs LIFO, so on unbind the
gpiochip was removed *first*, while the driver's own delayed work could
still be queued or actively running an I2C transfer against the chip/state
being torn down under it — a race against this driver's own workqueue, not
against the other consumers (`wlan-pwrseq`, `hci_bcm`) of these lines.
Fixed by registering `devm_gpiochip_add_data()` before the two cancel
actions, so LIFO teardown now cancels and confirms both delayed_work items
finished (`cancel_delayed_work_sync()`) *before* the gpiochip they touch is
removed.

Compile-checked out-of-tree against the real E1M-V2M103 kernel source and
a configured `kernel-build-artifacts` tree with the SDK cross-toolchain;
bench-pending (no bench access from this change).

On a reply CRC mismatch the driver now logs the raw reply bytes (`cmd 0x01: reply CRC mismatch: ...`, rate-limited), so the next cold-boot `-EBADMSG` shows which bytes were torn instead of only the errno (alplabai/gd32-bridge-firmware#295).

### Changed — V2N-family boards take their hostname from the fitted SoM, not the image (#2298)

The hostname came from the image build: current images all report
`alp-e1m` (`alp.conf`'s `hostname ?= "alp-e1m"`), and an older image built
for `e1m-v2n101-a55` running on an E1M-V2M103 reported `e1m-v2n101-a55`.
U-Boot patch `0009-rzv2n-dev-ALP-E1M-publish-sku-to-chosen.patch` now
publishes the SKU from the validated identity-EEPROM manifest to the
kernel as `/chosen/alp,sku`, and the new `alp-hostname` recipe (in every
ALP image) sets the hostname from it at boot, e.g. `e1m-v2m103`. The
change needs the updated U-Boot (FIP) flashed; with an older bootloader,
or without a validated manifest, nothing is published and `alp-e1m` stays.

### Fixed

- V2N-family images no longer show two failed units on every boot (#2301):
  - `rng-tools` / `rng-tools-service` are dropped on `rzv2n-family`. On RZ/V2N, rngd 6.16 finds no usable source (hwrng, rndr and jitter all fail initialisation), so it failed after ~16 s of CPU without crediting anything. The kernel CRNG initialises on its own at ~6.9 s.
  - meta-rz-distro's `v4l2-init` (the Renesas EVK OV5645 CRU setup script) stays installed but no longer starts automatically. It exits 1 when that camera is absent, which is every E1M-X EVK today (#1149). New dynamic-layer bbappend under `meta-alp-sdk/dynamic-layers/meta-rz-distro/`.

### Fixed — the ACT88760 GPIO4 OTP default is a known workaround, not a shipping defect (#2301)

An ACT88760 register `0x10` OTP default of `0x88` on some early units (e.g. E1M-V2M103 2026W38-0001) held GD32_NRST in reset until `provision_som.py` released it with a volatile write; the tool then recorded that as `act88760_gpio4_defect: yes`, defaulted `disposition` to `bench-only`, and the ship check permanently refused the unit. Per maintainer decision (2026-09-29), that OTP value is expected on those units and U-Boot's `board_late_init` now releases GD32_NRST every boot (a no-op on the many units whose OTP is already `0x08`) — a separate U-Boot patch, not part of this change.

- **Renamed the concept from defect to workaround.** `linux_target.py`: `ACT88760_GPIO4_DEFECT`/`ACT88760_GPIO4_RELEASE` → `ACT88760_GPIO4_OTP_DEFAULT`/`ACT88760_GPIO4_RELEASED`; `act88760_gpio4_defect()` → `act88760_gpio4_held()`. Register values (`0x10`, `0x88` held, `0x08` released, bit 7) are unchanged, and the tool still never writes EEPROM/OTP.
- **New ledger keys.** The tool no longer writes `act88760_gpio4_defect`. `census` and `gd32_flash` record `act88760_gpio4_otp` (the raw value observed before any release); `act88760_gpio4_workaround` is `none` (OTP already `0x08`), `u-boot` (an 0x88-OTP unit released by the image on its own by the last cold boot), or `provision (volatile 0x08)` (the tool had to release it). `cold_boot_test` now re-reads register `0x10` after every cold boot and records `act88760_gpio4_after_boot`; the GD32 bridge is exempted from the post-boot I2C scan only while that read is still `0x88`.
- **Ship check.** No longer blocks on `act88760_gpio4_defect`. Blocks only when `cold_boot_test` saw `act88760_gpio4_after_boot: 0x88` — i.e. the shipped image did not release the GD32 on its own.
- **Backward compatible.** An existing `unit.yaml` carrying the legacy `act88760_gpio4_defect: yes` key is left untouched (informational only) and no longer forces `bench-only` or blocks shipping by itself.

`py -3 -m pytest tests/scripts -q` green.

### Fixed

- `scripts/provision_som.py` (V2N family): `cold_boot_test` now records `dram_size_mib` and `uboot_dram_banner` from the U-Boot `DRAM:` banner it already parses. Before, only `boot_sd_linux` wrote them, so a unit provisioned in two phases (phase B on an eMMC boot) kept failing the ship check with `missing dram_size_mib` even after 3/3 clean cold boots. Found on E1M-V2M103 2026W38-0001 (#2301).

### Fixed

- V2N family U-Boot (`meta-alp-sdk`, patch 0011): `board_late_init()` now releases the GD32 supervisor from reset on every boot. On early units whose ACT88760 (BRD_I2C 0x25) OTP powers GPIO register 0x10 up as 0x88, it clears bit 7 (0x88 -> 0x08). Production units carry the fixed OTP (0x08 at power-on), so the step is a no-op there. Until now the release existed only as a hand-installed Linux service on one early bench unit, so the release image booted that unit with the GD32 held in reset: `gpio-gd32-bridge 8-0070: bridge not answering (-6)`, and every bridge GPIO write (Wi-Fi REG_ON included) failed. Found on E1M-V2M103 2026W38-0001 booting the eMMC release image (#2301).

### Fixed — GD32 bridge protocol doc no longer claims non-CRC fields are big-endian (#2307)

`docs/gd32-bridge-protocol.md` §4 said the CRC was the only little-endian
field and every other multi-byte field was big-endian, contradicting §2 and
the firmware. Every multi-byte field on the wire is little-endian. A host
that followed §4 and packed `OTA_BEGIN`'s `size`/`crc32` big-endian got
`STATUS_OUT_OF_RANGE` (`0x08`) back. §4 now matches §2 and names the
MSB-first hex text in `protocol_vectors.txt` as the actual trap.

### Fixed — Ethos-U op tables re-pinned to vela 5.2.0, real-vela CI coverage restored (#2310)

`metadata/npu_ops/ethos_u/{u85,u55-u65}@vela-5.1.0.json` and
`scripts/gen_npu_ops.py`'s `_EXPECTED_U85_ONLY_DELTA` (17 ops) were pinned to
`ethos-u-vela` 5.1.0, but `pyproject.toml`'s `model-compile` extra declared
only `ethos-u-vela>=3.9`, so CI installed whatever the latest release was --
5.2.0 at the time this landed. #1470 had made the real-vela smoke test in
`tests/scripts/test_gen_npu_ops.py` skip rather than fail when the installed
vela disagreed with the committed pin, which kept CI green but also meant the
one test that proves the tables are fresh against a real toolchain never ran
in CI at all.

Regenerated both tables against a real `ethos-u-vela` 5.2.0
(`u85@vela-5.2.0.json`, 74 ops; `u55-u65@vela-5.2.0.json`, 55 ops), replacing
the 5.1.0 files -- the tables are keyed one-per-(variant, toolchain,
toolchain_version) identity, not versioned side by side, and
`scripts/gen_npu_ops.py` already deletes a variant's superseded-version file
on regeneration. `_EXPECTED_U85_ONLY_DELTA` is updated deliberately to the
19-op set vela 5.2.0 reports: the 17 ops pinned at 5.1.0 plus
`ASSIGN_VARIABLE` and `READ_VARIABLE`.

`pyproject.toml`'s `model-compile` extra now pins `ethos-u-vela==5.2.0`
exactly (not `>=`), so the CI job that installs it
(`pr-metadata-validate.yml`'s `pip install -e ".[dev,model-compile]"` step,
the only site that installs `ethos-u-vela` in this repo) matches the
committed tables' pin and the real-vela smoke test now runs instead of
skipping. `uv.lock` is re-pinned to the same `ethos-u-vela` 5.2.0 (it had
resolved 5.1.0 from before the exact pin existed, and no CI step runs `uv
lock --check` to catch that on its own) -- a new hermetic test reads
`uv.lock`'s own resolved version and fails if it ever drifts from
`pyproject.toml`'s pin again.

### Fixed — the storage-partition planner offered `flash_device: ospi0`/`ospi1` on SKUs whose preset declares that part not fitted (#2311)

`_known_flash_devices()` (`scripts/alp_orchestrate/partition.py:132`
("def _known_flash_devices(")) still advertised an `on_module.ospi_memories:`
key as a legal `storage[].flash_device:` target even when the SoM preset
marks it `assembled: false`, and `_resolve_flash_device()`
(`scripts/alp_orchestrate/partition.py:480` ("def _resolve_flash_device"))
resolved it to a live descriptor from `capacity_mbit` alone — on `E1M-AEN801`, whose
preset declares `ospi0`/`ospi1` unfitted, a `storage:` entry naming `ospi0`
silently planned a 32 MiB partition on silicon that carries no such part.

Both are fixed: `_known_flash_devices()` excludes an `assembled: false` key
from the advertised set, and `_resolve_flash_device()` refuses it directly
(defense in depth for a hand-built project bypassing the loader's cross-check),
naming the SKU, the device, and the declaring preset file. `assembled:
optional` and an absent key (schema default: `true`) are unaffected.

The same bug class hit `security.psa.its_storage` / `ps_storage`: the
loader's cross-field check (`scripts/alp_orchestrate/loader.py`) accepted
any `on_module.ospi_memories:` key as a valid PSA backing-store reference
without checking `assembled`, so `its_storage: ospi0` was accepted on
`E1M-AEN801` and `secure.py` emitted
`CONFIG_PSA_CRYPTO_ITS_BACKING_STORE="ospi0"` for a part the SKU doesn't
carry. The loader now shares the same `assembled: false` predicate
(`_is_ospi_key_unassembled()`, `scripts/alp_orchestrate/partition.py`) and
raises the specific "not assembled" reason for `its_storage`/`ps_storage`
naming an unfitted OSPI part, instead of the generic "does not resolve"
message. `examples/connectivity/production-deployment/board.yaml` (which
named `ps_storage: ospi0` on E1M-AEN801) is updated to use `mram_main`,
the SKU's real backing store.

### Fixed — the ethos_u adapter shipped a zero-SRAM footprint whenever vela's NPU-placement line couldn't be read, instead of refusing it (#2312)

`compile()`'s zero-SRAM check read `if npu_ops:` on `_parse_vela_placement()`'s
result, and `None` (the line absent from vela's stdout) is just as falsy as
`0` — an unreadable placement line skipped the refusal and shipped
`req_sram_kib = 0` exactly as a genuine full CPU fallback would, and that zero
then passes the on-device fit gate at
`src/backends/inference/alp_model_select.c:135`
("return e->arena_sram_kib == 0u || t->req_sram_kib <= e->arena_sram_kib;")
against ANY arena. `_parse_vela_placement()`
(`scripts/alp_model/adapters/ethos_u.py:204-216` ("def _parse_vela_placement")) now REQUIRES BOTH the
`CPU` and `NPU` placement lines vela prints per run -- an `NPU` line with no
matching `CPU` line is treated as unreadable, same as no placement lines at
all -- and `compile()`'s check
(`scripts/alp_model/adapters/ethos_u.py:291`
("if npu_ops != 0:")) refuses unless the NPU count was read AND is exactly
`0` — a confirmed full CPU fallback. An unreadable line is fail-closed, not
silently zero.

### Fixed — every compile target shared one output directory, so a stale summary CSV from a different accel_config could be read as this run's footprint (#2312)

`build_model()` (`scripts/alp_model/build.py`) reuses one `out_dir` across
every target a SoM declares, and `_parse_vela_summary()` globbed
`out_dir.glob(f"{stem}_summary_*.csv")` and took `sorted(matches)[0]` — right
only by accident of sort order. A summary CSV left over from a different
accel_config's compile (or planted by another process) answered for this
one's `req_sram_kib`. `VelaAdapter.compile()` now compiles each accel_config
into its own subdirectory of `out_dir`
(`scripts/alp_model/adapters/ethos_u.py:106-115` ("def _run_dir"), `_run_dir`), so a sibling
target's output is never glob-visible to this run, and
`_parse_vela_summary()` (`scripts/alp_model/adapters/ethos_u.py:159-182`
("missing, unparseable, or AMBIGUOUS")) now
refuses (returns `(0, 0)`, composing with the placement-fail-closed fix above)
when more than one `*_summary_*.csv` matches inside a run's own directory,
rather than guessing which one is this run's.

Per-accel-config isolation alone does not stop a REBUILD from reading a
PRIOR run's leftovers: `_run_dir` is reused across builds of the same
accel_config, so a summary CSV or `_vela.tflite` left by an earlier
compile (including one where vela itself failed to write a fresh summary)
was still glob-visible to the next run into the same directory.
`VelaAdapter.compile()` now deletes any stale `<stem>_summary_*.csv` and
`<stem>_vela.tflite` from the run directory
(`_clear_stale_run_output`, `scripts/alp_model/adapters/ethos_u.py:118-135`
("def _clear_stale_run_output"))
before invoking vela, so a rebuild can never read a previous run's CSV and
never trips the ambiguity refusal above on its own leftovers.

### Fixed — the ethos_u adapter ran vela with no memory profile at all rather than refuse, silently compiling against vela's own DRAM-backed default (#2312)

`compile()` accepted a `target=None` or a `TargetSpec` with an empty
`vela_memory_mode` and simply omitted `--memory-mode`/`--system-config` —
vela then falls back to `Ethos_U85_SYS_DRAM_Mid` / `Dedicated_Sram_384KB` and
reports the working set in `dram_memory_used` on a part that may have no DRAM
at all. `compile()`
(`scripts/alp_model/adapters/ethos_u.py:264-272` ("no vela memory profile for")) now raises a `RuntimeError`
naming the missing `npu_toolchain.vela.memory_mode` up front instead.
`build_model()` always threads a real, resolved `TargetSpec` (`target=spec`,
`scripts/alp_model/build.py:100` ("opts=backend_opts, target=spec)")), so no production caller is affected; this
closes the gap for direct/test callers that built one by hand.

### Fixed — a named `system_config` waited for `ALP_VELA_CONFIG` even when the SoC spec said it needed no vendor file (#2312)

`TargetSpec.vela_system_config` carried a `system_config` name unconditionally
and `_profile_flags()` always withheld `--system-config` until a vendor `.ini`
was on hand via `ALP_VELA_CONFIG` — ignoring
`npu_toolchain.vela.system_config_requires_vendor_config`
(`metadata/schemas/soc-spec-v1.schema.json`). `TargetSpec` now splits the name
into two fields by that flag: `vela_system_config` (a built-in Arm
`System_Config`, safe to pass alone) and `vela_vendor_system_config`
(vendor-gated, passed only alongside `--config` when
`ALP_VELA_CONFIG` names a readable file) —
`scripts/alp_project_loader.py:740-769` (`_soc_targets`; the split itself is
at :751-768). `_profile_flags()`
(`scripts/alp_model/adapters/ethos_u.py:138-156` ("def _profile_flags")) passes the former
unconditionally and the latter only with its vendor file. No shipped SoC spec
names a `system_config` today (every Alif Ensemble part and the NXP i.MX 93
leave it unset), so this is latent, not a behaviour change for any part in
metadata/ yet.

### Fixed — the zero-SRAM refusal said "zero SRAM working set in any memory area" even though the measured DRAM figure was nonzero (#2312)

The refusal message (`_refuse_zero_sram_footprint`,
`scripts/alp_model/adapters/ethos_u.py:219-250` ("def _refuse_zero_sram_footprint")) claimed no memory area
reported a working set at all; measured, a defaulted profile reports
`dram_memory_used = 0.28125` for the exact model the refusal fires on — the
SRAM figure is the only one that came back zero. The message now says "zero
SRAM", not "zero SRAM working set in any memory area", and separately reads
"vela's own NPU-operator-placement line could not be read from its stdout, so
this zero cannot be confirmed as a full CPU fallback" for the unreadable-line
case above, rather than crediting an unread `npu_ops` with an operator count.

### Changed — `req_sram_kib` is arena-only by design; the const/weight region is never counted (#2312, tan-cli#1011)

Settles the open question from #2312 (follow-up to #1470): `perf.req_sram_kib`
/ the `.alpmodel` manifest's `Target.requires.sram_kib` count the compiled
tensor **arena** alone (vela's `sram_memory_used` column), never the
const/weight region (vela's `on_chip_flash_memory_used` column). The const
region is carried in the model blob itself and sized by the blob's own byte
length (`blob_len`), provisioned by the integrator per the target's
`vela_memory_mode` placement — it is never summed into `req_sram_kib`. No
schema field changed and no `.alpmodel` version bump; the on-device selector
at `src/backends/inference/alp_model_select.c:135`
("return e->arena_sram_kib == 0u || t->req_sram_kib <= e->arena_sram_kib;")
is unchanged, comparing the arena against the arena as it always has. This is
the same contract as tan-cli's `_footprint()` (tan-cli#1011), not a
line-for-line port -- tan-cli's version additionally reads every memory area
and a DRAM-declared-or-not caveat this adapter does not carry -- and the
SRAM-port pinning in `src/backends/inference/ethos_u_aen.cpp` is unchanged
too. Documented in `docs/bench/model-perf-capture.md` and
`metadata/schemas/model-perf-v1.schema.json`'s `perf.req_sram_kib`
description.

### Documented — `ALP_VELA_CONFIG` (the vendor vela profile env var) has a customer-facing home in the docs (#2312)

`docs/bench/model-perf-capture.md` and `vendors/nxp-imx93/README.md` now
name `ALP_VELA_CONFIG` alongside the `memory_mode`/`system_config` profile
fields it complements: it points at a customer's own vendor vela `.ini`
(e.g. Alif's `ensemble_vela.ini`), which alp-sdk does not redistribute.
Both docs now also say plainly that `ALP_VELA_CONFIG` is inert today: it
only takes effect once a SoC spec's `npu_toolchain.vela` names a
`system_config` with `system_config_requires_vendor_config: true`, and no
shipped `metadata/socs/**` spec does that yet -- on i.MX 93 in particular
it never applies, since `imx93.json` sets
`system_config_requires_vendor_config: false`. AEN example builds
configure the same vendor `.ini` a different way, via the CMake
`AEN_NPU_VELA_CONFIG` variable
(`examples/aen/aen-npu-inference/README.md`), not this env var.

### Documented — E1M-NX9101's DRAM capacity and vela system-config stay TBD, explicitly (#2312 item 2)

`vendors/nxp-imx93/README.md` now says outright that
`metadata/e1m_modules/E1M-NX9101.yaml`'s `memory.dram_mbit: TBD` is deliberate
pending the authoritative hardware config, and that until then the vela
invocation relies on vela's own default `--system-config` (`imx93.json`'s
`npu_toolchain.vela` sets no `system_config`). No values are set.

### Fixed — AEN bench scripts: chunk mem8 reads >0x10000 and clear NVIC in openocd-ram-run.sh's HE path (#2313)

Two AEN bench-script gaps surfaced while bench-verifying #2299 on an
E1M-AEN803 EVK (2026W36-0009):

- `scripts/bench/aen/ram-run.sh` and `reread.sh` read the RAM console with a
  single JLinkExe `mem8 <addr>,<size>`. JLinkExe caps `NumBytes` at
  `0x10000` (`NumBytes should be <= 0x10000`), so any read larger than that
  returned nothing at all — silently, which is why `aen-inference-energy`
  had shrunk its buffer to exactly `0x10000` to work around it instead of
  fixing the read. A shared `bench_mem8_chunks()` helper (`bench-env.sh`)
  now splits any read into `mem8` chunks of at most `0x10000` bytes each,
  and both scripts route their read session through it; the existing
  line-oriented decoders need no change, since the chunked dump lines still
  land in the transcript in strict address order.
- `scripts/bench/aen/openocd-ram-run.sh`'s HE (and shared HP) path zeroed
  MSPLIM/PSPLIM before resuming a freshly loaded image but left NVIC state
  untouched. A resident HE app that left an IRQ enabled or pending ran the
  new image straight into that app's ISR the moment IRQs unmasked — seen:
  IRQn 333 (`CDC_SCANLINE0`), core stuck at IPSR `0x15D`. The script now
  clears every NVIC ICER and ICPR register (n = 0..15, IRQ 0-511) before
  `resume`, in addition to the existing MSPLIM/PSPLIM clear.

Not changed: a pre-load core/AP-identity assertion for the J-Link path
(read `0x58000000` HE ITCM before loading) was scoped out — `ram-run.sh`'s
JLinkExe generic `Cortex-M55` attach has no per-core AP selector to check
against in the first place (unlike `openocd-ram-run.sh`'s AP-addressed
core selection), so there is no non-trivial place to hang the assertion at
this layer without restructuring how that script attaches.

### Fixed — `gd32g553_init()` gave up on the first STATUS_BUSY in the OTA post-COMMIT/ROLLBACK trial window (#2314)

After `OTA_COMMIT`/`OTA_ROLLBACK` commits a trial-capable image (firmware
release >= 0.2.14, wire protocol 0.12, gd32-bridge-firmware#246), a GD32
bridge reboots into an unconfirmed TRIAL image. That image answers
`STATUS_BUSY` to every opcode, `PING`/`GET_VERSION` included, until it decodes
its first CRC-valid frame. That frame confirms the trial and triggers one
more reset before the link settles (`docs/gd32-bridge-protocol.md` §10). If
no valid frame lands before the bootloader's watchdog (FWDGT) window expires
(~32.8 s nominal), the bootloader reverts to the previously-active slot.

`gd32g553_init()` used to return on the first `ALP_ERR_BUSY`. It now rides
out a bounded (~2 s, one shared `alp_uptime_ms()` deadline across both the
PING and GET_VERSION phases) retry ladder, gated on: `ALP_ERR_BUSY` is always
transient; `ALP_ERR_IO`/`ALP_ERR_TIMEOUT` are transient **only** once this
same `init()` call has already seen at least one `ALP_ERR_BUSY` -- proof a
trial is genuinely in progress and a confirm-triggered second reset is the
explanation. An absent or unflashed bridge never answers `BUSY` at all, so it
still fails fast on the very first `IO`/`TIMEOUT`, unchanged from before this
fix -- load-bearing for `src/zephyr/v2n_supervisor.c`, which re-runs this
init on every `acquire()` while the bridge stays absent and budgets that on a
~1 ms bridge op, not a 2 s retry ladder. Non-transient failures (NOSUPPORT,
INVAL, a genuine version mismatch) still return immediately.

An `OTA_BEGIN` sent in the legacy 8-byte form (no `fw_version` triple) is
treated as an unknown incoming version, which is itself sufficient reason to
boot the result into TRIAL -- but this is only the right call for an image
that is ITSELF trial-capable (>= 0.2.14): an older image committed this way
is reverted by the watchdog ~33 s later, having no confirm logic of its own
to run. To install an older image that must survive, pass its real, known
version instead; an explicitly known version below 0.2.14 is a deliberate
downgrade guard -- the bridge commits/rolls back to it WITHOUT the TRIAL
dance at all (no `STATUS_BUSY` window). The watchdog-revert protection is the
bootloader's doing, not the app's: an old bootloader paired with a new,
trial-capable app still runs the TRIAL/confirm dance but never reverts a hung
image, so bootloader and app must ship together for the protection to apply.

Bench status: both the app-side confirm path (BUSY -> first valid frame ->
second reset -> normal operation) and the bootloader's watchdog-driven revert
path are silicon-validated on E1M-V2M103, 2026-09-26 -- a deliberately hung
image (misconfigured HXTAL) committed via the legacy `OTA_BEGIN` form was
reverted to the previous slot after ~33 s, `RESET_REASON` read back `WDT`,
and the bridge's own health check cleared the reverted slot's `slot_valid`
flag.

On the CM33, the V2N supervisor now arms a hold-off after a
`gd32g553_init()` that ends `ALP_ERR_BUSY`
(`CONFIG_ALP_SDK_V2N_SUPERVISOR_BUSY_HOLDOFF_MS`, default 1000 ms). While it
runs, acquirers get `ALP_ERR_BUSY` at once instead of each re-running the
~2 s init under the supervisor mutex against a bridge that is still in its
OTA trial.

### Fixed — the loader refuses an OPTIGA attestation root on SKUs where the OPTIGA is not fitted (#2316)

`security.psa.attestation_root: optiga_trust_m` was accepted whenever the SoM
preset named the OPTIGA Trust M under `on_module:` or set
`capabilities.optiga_trust_m: true`, without checking population. E1M-AEN801
and E1M-AEN803 do both, but their `optiga_trust_m` i2c_devices entry is
`assembled: false`. The loader now refuses that combination with the same
message shape as the #2311 OSPI guard: SKU, part, and
`assembled: false in metadata/e1m_modules/<SKU>.yaml`.
`examples/connectivity/production-deployment`, which targets E1M-AEN801,
switches to `attestation_root: tfm_internal`, and its README says where
`optiga_trust_m` does apply (E1M-AEN501/601/701).

### Fixed — `scripts/bench/aen/reread.sh` no longer shares fixed `/tmp` transcript paths across runs (#2317)

`reread.sh` wrote its J-Link command files and transcripts to fixed paths
(`/tmp/rr.jlink`, `/tmp/rr.out`, `/tmp/reread-preflight.{jlink,out}`). A
concurrent run, including the `tests/scripts` suite's fake-JLinkExe runs,
could overwrite a real read's transcript. It now uses a per-run
`mktemp -d "${TMPDIR:-/tmp}/reread.XXXXXX"` work dir, like `ram-run.sh`. The
dir is removed on success and kept on failure for inspection.

`tests/scripts/test_bench_jlink_connect_guard.py`'s read-back regex also
recognises `"$WORKDIR/..."` capture files. Without that, the moved read-back
would have dropped out of the every-read-back-asserts-the-connection check.

### Fixed — aen-inference-energy no longer faults after printing its RESULT (#2318)

The example's TFLM interpreter was a local in `main()`, so every `return`
ran its destructor, which re-walks the model flatbuffer staged in SRAM0.
SRAM0 is shared by every core: run on the M55-HP with another image
resident on the M55-HE, the HE overwrote the staged model (a read-back of
`model_sram` at `0x02000000` after the run held a pixel pattern, not the
model), and the teardown faulted in
`flatbuffers::Table::GetOptionalFieldOffset` (PC `0x0001764a`). The
resolver and interpreter now live in never-destroyed static storage, so
no exit path walks the model again.

Bench-verified on E1M-AEN803 2026W36-0009 (Flow C
RAM-run landing on the M55-HP): unfixed 3 of 4 runs faulted after
`RESULT FAIL: no INA236 answered on EVK_I2C_BUS_SENSORS` (two USAGE
FAULTs, one BUS FAULT at BFAR `0xd795bcba`); fixed 0 of 6, each ending
idle with IPSR 0 and CFSR `0x00000000`.

### Added — fleet-unique Ethernet MAC derived from the SoM serial (#2325)

E1M-V2N / E1M-V2M SoMs have two RAVB Ethernet interfaces (Linux end0/end1)
and no per-unit MAC source: the RZ/V2N has no MAC OTP and the module has no
MAC EEPROM. Left alone, both interfaces booted with whatever compiled-in
default the enabled BSP feature layers happened to bake into U-Boot's
environment — identical on every unit, and not a purchased IEEE OUI either
way — and buying an OUI block is off the table.

U-Boot now derives `ethaddr`/`eth1addr` from the unit serial already in the
validated identity-EEPROM manifest — an injective encoding, not a hash, into
IEEE 802c SLAP locally-administered space — making both MACs fleet-unique by
construction (unique across every serial the allocator has issued), not
globally unique. The MAC carries no SKU field, so the serial's index is
allocated fleet-wide per ISO week, across every SKU, not per SKU — that is
what makes the encoding actually unique. The derivation runs twice: once in
`board_late_init()` (so U-Boot's own networking has a MAC before `bootcmd`),
and again from a new `alp_eth_mac` command `CONFIG_BOOTCOMMAND` invokes
immediately after `env default -a` — that second call is the one Linux
actually sees, since `image_setup_libfdt()` runs `fdt_fixup_ethernet()`
before `ft_system_setup()`.
`CONFIG_BOOTCOMMAND` opens with `env default -a` on every boot, so there is
no env override slot on this board: the derived MAC always applies whenever
the serial parses, on any unit whose autoboot runs this compiled-in
`CONFIG_BOOTCOMMAND` — a unit with a saved `bootcmd` from an older FIP (no
`alp_eth_mac` call) still gets the DRP-AI vendor default instead. A unit
whose EEPROM has no parseable serial yet falls back, with a console
WARNING, to a MAC derived from the on-module eMMC's CID (prefix nibble
`0xD`, disjoint from the serial-derived `0xC` range) rather than the vendor
default every such unit would share. See
`docs/soms/v2n.md#ethernet-mac-address-policy` for the full policy, and
`scripts/alp_eth_mac.py` for the host-side implementation the device side
stays bit-for-bit identical to.

U-Boot now also publishes the validated unit serial as `/chosen/alp,serial`,
and `alp-hostname` appends it to the SKU hostname, so units of one SKU on a
LAN get distinct names (`e1m-v2m103-2026w38-0001`). Without the property the
hostname stays the SKU name (#2298).

### Added — Sony IMX335 camera: raw capture bench-verified + INNO-MAKER CAM-IMX335-5MP shield (#2327)

Raw capture only, no ISP/AE/streaming. This sensor's driver is **not
vendored into alp-sdk** — it reuses upstream Zephyr v4.4.1's own
`drivers/video/imx335.c` (`CONFIG_VIDEO_IMX335`, `compatible =
"sony,imx335"`) directly (ADR 0017 Tier 1, upstream-native), carrying one
repo patch on top. Bench runs 316-331 on E1M-AEN803 2026W36-0001
root-caused three real upstream-driver bugs at this sensor's
2-lane/10-bit/1188 Mbps-per-lane configuration; all three are fixed by the
patch below and the fix is bench-verified end to end: **6/6 consecutive
clean 1296x972 RAW10 raw captures (run 330), 0 CSI CRC errors, 0 IPI-fatal
events, correct stride, no overrun.**

**`zephyr/patches/zephyr/0004-imx335-2lane-link-freq-and-binning.patch`**
(registered in `zephyr/patches.yml`, applied per-module by
`scripts/bootstrap.sh` via `west patch apply`, checked by
`scripts/verify_west_patches.py`):

1. **No `VIDEO_CID_LINK_FREQ`.** The driver registers `VIDEO_CID_PIXEL_RATE`
   only. `video_get_csi_link_freq()` (`video_common.c`) falls back to
   approximating the D-PHY link frequency from `PIXEL_RATE` whenever a
   sensor reports no `VIDEO_CID_LINK_FREQ` control; for this sensor's 396
   MHz `PIXEL_RATE` (a v4l2 pixel-array-clock convention value, unrelated to
   the per-lane D-PHY bit rate) that approximation lands the DW CSI-2 host
   on 990 MHz (1980 Mbps/lane) instead of the sensor's real 594 MHz link
   clock (24 MHz INCK, 2-lane 10-bit mode: 1188 Mbps/lane, link_freq =
   per-lane bit rate / 2) — the same `ERRSOTSYNCHS`/`PHY_FATAL` storm
   signature OV5647 hit before its own fix (#2248). The patch registers
   `VIDEO_CID_LINK_FREQ` directly as a READ_ONLY int-menu `{594000000}`, the
   same shape `imx296.c`'s own `link_freq` control already uses.
   `PIXEL_RATE` itself stays **untouched** — 396 MHz is the correct v4l2
   pixel-array-clock value per `<video-controls.h>`'s own convention, and
   `VIDEO_CID_LINK_FREQ` alone is what `video_get_csi_link_freq()` reads
   once registered.

2. **No SYSMODE / MIPI output-timing registers.** The driver never writes
   `SYSMODE` (`0x319e`) or the `0x3a18`-`0x3a28` MIPI output-timing block
   for ANY lane/rate combination — bench run 318 found this produces a
   payload-checksum/CRC error storm on the CSI-2 receiver at 1188
   Mbps/lane, even with LINK_FREQ fixed above. Writing the values the
   mainline Linux imx335 driver (`raspberrypi/linux`, branch `rpi-6.12.y`)
   programs for this exact lane count and bit rate (`SYSMODE=1` plus nine
   `REG16` values — register values carried as hardware facts, no GPL code
   copied) eliminated it — 0 CSI CRC errors (runs 319-330), including 6/6
   consecutive clean 1296x972 captures through the E1M SoM R2 pinout
   adapter (run 330): **this VERIFIES 2-lane CSI-2 D-PHY lock at 1188
   Mbps/lane on E1M-AEN803 2026W36-0001 + this E1M-EVK.** An 891 Mbps/lane
   alternative timing set also gave 0 CSI CRC errors on the link (run 320,
   a different `IMX335_INCKSEL`/INCK selection — that run still had bug 3's
   buffer overrun below, so no clean frame resulted at 891 Mbps, only a
   clean link) but is not carried in the product — this driver is
   hardcoded to its own 2-lane/10-bit mode, which this repo's shield feeds
   at 24 MHz INCK, i.e. the 1188 Mbps/lane path only.

3. **2x2-binned mode overruns its own buffer.** `imx335_bin_2x2` leaves
   `HNUM` at the full-resolution `0x0a20` (2592) and sets `Y_OUT_SIZE` to
   `0x03d8` (984) — the sensor then transmitted a 1308x984 frame into this
   driver's own 1296x972 buffer, a 12-pixel/12-line overrun corrupting
   memory past the buffer. Bench-derived model (run 322, `HNUM` swept until
   the transmitted width matched exactly): binned width = HNUM/2 + 12, so
   `HNUM` must be `0x0a08` (2568). `Y_OUT_SIZE` corrected to the exact 972
   lines (`0x03cc`, bench run 321); `OPB_SIZE_V` (`0x304c`) cleared to 0
   (the mainline Linux imx335 driver's own binned-mode value). `HNUM` is
   restored to `0x0a20` when switching back to full resolution
   (`imx335_bin_none`). **Not fixed**: `imx335_bin_none`'s own `Y_OUT_SIZE`
   (`0x07ac` = 1964) — both upstream Zephyr's own `imx335_init_params`
   (`Y_OUT_SIZE` `0x0798` = 1944) and the mainline Linux driver's
   full-resolution mode use 1944, so `0x07ac` is the same overrun class as
   bug 3 above for any full-resolution caller. Full-resolution mode is
   UNBENCHED (only the 2x2-binned mode is exercised) — tracked as issue
   #2334.

If bootstrapping against a Zephyr checkout that already has alp-sdk's
0001-0003 patches applied, re-running the whole patch list fails
re-applying 0001 (`west patch` is not idempotent against an already-patched
tree) — apply 0004 by hand (`git apply` from the Zephyr repo root) or start
from a clean checkout.

**`csi-pixclk-hz` extended to Camera mode** (`zephyr/dts/bindings/video/
snps,designware-csi.yaml`; `struct csi2_dw_config` / `csi2_dw_validate_data()`,
`zephyr/drivers/video/video_csi_dw.{c,h}`) — originally Controller-mode
only, now effective in EITHER `ipi-mode`. Bench measurement (runs 329/330)
found this sensor's ACTUAL binned-mode line period (29.63 us, ~4H at HMAX
550, 972 HSYNC/frame) could not be matched by a Controller-mode
`csi-hline`/`csi-vtotal` pair the way IMX296's could — this driver never
surfaces that measured line period as a register read or control, so a
Controller-mode DT constant can't be derived from it reliably. The shield
below uses Camera mode instead, and Camera mode's own margined request
(285.12 MHz) *and* bare request (237.6 MHz) both exceed
`alif_pixclk_set_rate()`'s ~200 MHz practical ceiling for this 2-lane
sensor — so `csi-pixclk-hz` needed the same integer-pass-through override
Controller mode already had. An explicit `csi-pixclk-hz` that the clock
controller cannot reach now fails loudly (`LOG_ERR`) in EITHER mode, no
silent fallback to the derived request. Camera mode with an explicit
`csi-pixclk-hz` also switches the driver's legacy HSD derivation
(`csi2_dw_validate_data()`'s CAM branch) to a lanes-aware formula (divides
by `(pll_fin<<1)*num_lanes` instead of the legacy `(pll_fin<<1)` alone,
which OV5647/OV9281 remain bench-proven against and is therefore
UNCHANGED when this property is absent). A separate same-day fix
(commit before this one) corrected `csi-pixclk-hz`'s Controller-mode
pass-through from `float` to a direct integer (a `float`'s 24 mantissa
bits rounded `133333333` up to `133333336`, landing the wrong clock
divisor) — carried forward unchanged here.

**`zephyr/boards/shields/innomaker_cam_imx335/`** (new shield, same file
set as `innomaker_cam_ov9281`: `shield.yml`, `Kconfig.shield`, the overlay,
`doc/index.rst`): 24 MHz `fixed-clock`, CCI address 0x1A, 2 MIPI CSI-2 data
lanes, **Camera mode** with `csi-pixclk-hz = <200000000>`. Bench
measurement (runs 329/330) established the sensor's real binned-mode line
period (~4H, 29.63 us) and found Controller mode (a fixed
`csi-hline`/`csi-vtotal` pair) could not be made to match it — see the
overlay's own comment for the full reasoning. Build with
`SHIELD="e1m_evk_rpi_csi innomaker_cam_imx335"`.

`examples/aen/aen-camera-firstlight` gets a matching IMX335 `#elif`
requesting the sensor's 2x2-binned 1296x972 mode *explicitly* (the driver
boots at its native 2592x1944) plus a `testcase.yaml` scenario
(AEN801+AEN803, build-only), a `Kconfig` buffer-sizing override
(`ALP_SDK_CAMERA_ZEPHYR_VIDEO_VBUF_COUNT`/`VIDEO_BUFFER_POOL_NUM_MAX` = 1,
`VIDEO_BUFFER_POOL_HEAP_SIZE` = 2.75 MiB for `VIDEO_IMX335` — the
2x2-binned frame, 2,519,424 bytes, does not fit the plain 2-buffer/2-MiB
defaults every other shield uses), and discards the first captured frame
after stream start for this sensor (bench runs 329-331: the first
post-start frame was bad in 3 of the 4 first frames checked — run 329 and
both run-331 loads; run 330's was clean — while the kept second frame was
clean every time). `metadata/chips/imx335.yaml` catalogues the
part (`driver_status: none`, same catalogue-only shape as `imx296.yaml`,
allowlisted in `scripts/check_chip_manifest_parity.py`'s
`KNOWN_MANIFEST_NO_DRIVER`). See `docs/camera-shields.md` for the full
driver/shield derivation and the decision NOT to add a
`tests/zephyr/video_sensors` emulator+ztest (this patch's fixes are already
bench-verified directly against real silicon, a stronger proof for this
specific hardware than an emulator ztest would add) or a `csi-pixclk-hz`/
Camera-mode-HSD unit test (`video_csi_dw.c` has zero existing test coverage
in this tree to extend, same reasoning as `csi-hline`/`csi-vtotal` before
it).

**Bench-verified on E1M-AEN803 2026W36-0001 (bench runs 316-331)**: 2x2-binned
1296x972 RAW10 raw capture through `<alp/camera.h>` — 6/6 consecutive clean
captures (run 330), 0 CSI CRC errors, 0 IPI-fatal events, correct stride,
no overrun. **This VERIFIES 2-lane CSI-2 D-PHY lock at 1188 Mbps/lane on
E1M-AEN803 2026W36-0001 + this E1M-EVK through the SoM R2 pinout adapter**
(runs 319-330). The module answered at CCI `0x1A` (the only device on the
E1M-EVK's J5 camera bus) with `CAM_EN` (J5 pin 11) untouched, and
`STANDBY`/`VMAX`/`HMAX`/`LANEMODE` all read back at their power-on-reset
defaults before the patch's config writes. D-PHY Stop-state check
(`STOPSTATE 0x00010003` before stream start) passed normally once the
patch's MIPI-timing registers were written — no
`no-lp11-clock-lane-park`-style skip property was needed. **That E1M-EVK
carries the J5 pin-11 pull-up rework** (`docs/boards/e1m-evk.md`,
originally fitted for OV5647) — `CAM_EN` being untouched proves nothing
about whether this module self-enables on a *stock* carrier; that remains
unestablished, and IMX335 is not added to that doc's self-enables list.

**Run 331 — PRODUCT-CODE confirmation**: the `fbf9c8de3` tree with ONLY
patch 0004 applied on a pristine Zephyr v4.4.1 checkout, no diag-only code.
Run 331 applied patch 0004 at sha256
`2459cd9511dac95fa682197302b1d33b201dbacd3d4df02c2097e53dbd5278c0` (the
`fbf9c8de3` file); the committed patch file was regenerated afterward
(sha256 `47d7d5ac6dd2293b3ffb46562f031a543867a618b0da7dbe596c83ca609a400d`)
and differs from what run 331 tested ONLY in comments — no register
writes, ordering, or logic changed. The kept (second)
frame was clean: 0 IPI/CRC error lines, only one `FRAME_SEQ` event at
start, correct stride, 0 near-black rows, nothing written past the buffer,
a clean close, and `CSI_PIXCLK_CTRL` read back `0x00020001` (divisor 2 =
200 MHz, matching this shield's `csi-pixclk-hz`). `csi-halt-en` was left at
its default — no IPI-halt/"nohalt" DT override was needed. The discarded
first frame was bad in both loads this run checked: near-black rows
466-583 in one, all-zero rows 759-778 in the other.

**NOT bench-verified — do not claim any of the following happened on
silicon**: frame rate/fps (not measured); the module self-enabling on a
stock, non-reworked carrier (the J5 pin-11 rework is a module-enable
concern, unrelated to D-PHY lock); D-PHY lock on any unit/carrier other
than E1M-AEN803 2026W36-0001 on this specific E1M-EVK; the 891 Mbps/lane
alternative timing set (bench-confirmed clean on the link but not carried
in the product); ISP/AE/colour (see the Stage B section below, added
later in this same issue — colour remains uncalibrated even there); and
the sensor's full-resolution (non-binned) mode.

### Added — IMX335 Stage B: ISP-Pico, AE, and MJPEG streaming (#2327) — bench-verified, runs 332-334

Follows IMX296's own Stage B (issue #2287, `hal_alif` patch 0013) as
closely as the two sensors' real differences allow.

- **hal_alif patch 0014** (`drivers/isp/isp_wrapper/inc/
  imx335_ae_envelope.h`, `CONFIG_VIDEO_ISP_VSI_CALIB_IMX335`) — IMX335's
  own AE envelope: `fullLines` 4500 (`IMX335_VMAX_DEFAULT`), `maxIntLine`
  4483 (`VMAX - IMX335_SHR0_MIN_BINNING`, upstream `imx335.c`'s own
  binned-mode control-range ceiling), analog gain capped at 30.0 dB (a
  public Sony IMX335 datasheet-flyer figure — above that this sensor's
  single GAIN register, `0x30e8`, is documented as digital), `fps` 30
  (upstream driver default). AWB/CCM stay on the stock ARX3A0 defaults —
  no IMX335 colour calibration exists.
- **Gain-unit conversion generalised** (`zephyr/drivers/video/
  isp_sns_gain_conv.h`): IMX296's `VIDEO_CID_ANALOGUE_GAIN` control IS its
  raw 0.1 dB/count GAIN register value directly; IMX335's upstream driver
  pre-scales its own 0.3 dB/count register to MILLI-dB instead (0..72000
  mdB). Rather than a second 481-entry table, new
  `isp_sns_gain_db_tenths_ctrl_to_lib()`/`isp_sns_gain_lib_to_db_tenths_ctrl()`
  divide/multiply by `VIDEO_ISP_VSI_SNS_GAIN_CTRL_PER_DB_TENTH` (1 for
  IMX296, the identity case — unchanged behaviour; 100 for IMX335), reusing
  the same table. That alone is insufficient — a
  unit-conversion scale is not the same fact as the sensor's own
  hardware-register WRITE granularity (300 mdB for IMX335, matching
  `IMX335_GAIN_UNIT_MDB`) — so a SEPARATE `VIDEO_ISP_VSI_SNS_GAIN_CTRL_STEP`
  (1 for IMX296, a no-op; 300 for IMX335) now rounds the pushed control
  value to the nearest EXACT multiple of that step: without it, a
  tenths-of-dB value not itself a multiple of 3 would reach
  `imx335_set_ctrl()`'s own truncating `ctrl.val / 300` divide and silently
  under-drive gain by up to just under one register count on every write.
  `tests/zephyr/isp_ae_conv` gained cases for the identity path, IMX335's
  30.0 dB cap, and an exhaustive
  per-table-entry check that the rounded value is always an exact multiple
  of 300 — all pass on `native_sim`.
- **ISP crop for `camera-mjpeg-stream`** — IMX335's native 2x2-binned
  output is a fixed 1296x972, with no in-sensor crop this driver uses
  (unlike IMX296's ROI, already 1280x960 at the sensor). The ISP's own
  crop (`crop-x0`/`crop-y0` on `&isp`) reduces it to 1280x960 instead:
  `crop-x0 = 8`, `crop-y0 = 6` (`isp_pico.c`'s `out_form_rect` crops
  symmetrically — 1296 - 16 = 1280, 972 - 12 = 960), landing on the SAME
  frame size `camera-mjpeg-stream`'s existing buffer pool already budgets
  for. The crop lives in the `innomaker_cam_imx335` **shield's own overlay** — the
  crop is a property of this sensor module, not of any one example, and a
  per-example overlay left it silently untied to the ISP backend's own
  size assumption. `src/backends/camera/alif_isp_pico.c` (the portable
  `<alp/camera.h>` ISP backend) pins its ISP INPUT request to this fixed
  1296x972 native size for an IMX335 board rather than the caller's
  requested OUTPUT size — every other sensor's INPUT==OUTPUT shape let it
  skip this until now — and now reads the shield's own `crop-x0`/`crop-y0`
  DT values back, `BUILD_ASSERT`ing they still produce 1280x960; a future
  shield edit that breaks that assumption now fails the BUILD.
  `isp_pico.c`'s `isp_stream_start()` also gained a matching runtime guard
  (`-EINVAL` if the computed crop doesn't match the requested OUTPUT
  format — inert for OV5647/OV9281/IMX296, whose crop is always 0), and
  `isp_open()` rejects (`ALP_ERR_OUT_OF_RANGE`) an IMX335 caller requesting
  any size other than the shield's own cropped 1280x960. A `#error` now
  also fires if a board somehow enables both `sony_imx296` and
  `sony_imx335` compats at once — a configuration this backend has never
  supported and previously would have silently picked one.
- **Frame rate**: no explicit fps request is added for IMX335 (imx335.c only
  supports {25, 30, 50, 60} fps): `src/backends/camera/
  alif_isp_pico.c`'s `cfg->fps` request only ever reaches the OV5647
  sensor node (`DEVICE_DT_GET(DT_NODELABEL(ov5647))`, hardcoded), so
  `camera-mjpeg-stream`'s fps request was never forwarded to IMX335 (or
  IMX296) at all — that sensor free-runs at its own driver default, 30 fps
  (upstream `imx335.c`'s `.frame_rate = 30`), which already matches
  hal_alif patch 0014's AE envelope with no request needed. This
  app-level backend gap (fps only reaching OV5647) is tracked as issue
  #2338. `isp_pico.c`'s `isp_apply_ae()` still gained
  `CONFIG_VIDEO_ISP_VSI_AE_EXP_TIME_MAX_US_CAP` (33207 for IMX335,
  matching `IMX335_AE_EXP_TIME_MAX_US`), clamping the pushed exposure-time
  ceiling to the envelope's own assumption, the same way the existing
  gain-ceiling clamp already does — this backstops a DIRECT video API
  caller that sets a different rate on the sensor itself, not anything
  this example's own build exercises.
- `examples/aen/aen-isp-capture` gains an `-DAEN_ISP_IMX335=ON` variant
  (`overlay-imx335.conf`), same AE-on/off shape as the IMX296 variant,
  reusing IMX296's buffer-pool sizing unchanged (identical 1280x960 YUV420
  ISP output either way).
- **camera-mjpeg-stream IMX335 scenario** — `innomaker_cam_imx335` shield
  + the existing `overlay-1280x960.conf` (no per-example crop overlay
  needed now that the crop lives in the shield). AE on, AWB at the ISP's
  stock default.
- **Bench run 332** (`aen-isp-capture`, AE-on scenario, E1M-AEN803
  2026W36-0001): 60 frames, AE converged (`ae_stable=1` at frame 50, Y
  mean 152), ISP output YUV420 1280x960 via the crop above, scene
  complete/straight/centred — the first silicon confirmation of
  `out_form_rect`'s `left`/`top` crop offsets. Green cast with AWB off
  (expected — no colour calibration exists).
- **Bench run 333** (`camera-mjpeg-stream`, `aen_imx335` scenario, same
  board): 1280x960, app stats `fps=30 fail=0 retry=0`, one HTTP client
  29.99 fps / 772.7 KB/s over 30 s, ~26.3 KB JPEGs, mild lavender/cyan cast
  (stock AWB). Only error-class log line: one `FRAME_SEQ` event at stream
  start.
- **Bench run 334** (same scenario, after the crop-ownership/gain-rounding/
  exposure-cap changes above): crop 8/6 confirmed coming from the shield's
  own DT (no example overlay), driver `frame_rate` 30, `HMAX 0x0226`/
  `VMAX 0x001194` read back over I2C, `fps=30 fail=0 retry=0`, one client
  29.98 fps / 773.5 KB/s over 30 s, ~26.4 KB JPEGs, only error one
  `FRAME_SEQ` at start — ran without regression. The gain-rounding,
  exposure-time cap, `isp_open()` rejection, and `isp_stream_start()` crop
  guard were all present in that image; their specific effects are NOT
  separately bench-proven by this run (`tests/zephyr/isp_ae_conv` is the
  proof for the gain-rounding math).
- **AEN803 build verification** (`-Werror`, beyond the bench runs above):
  `aen-isp-capture`'s IMX335 AE-off variant (not itself bench-run) builds
  clean; `camera-mjpeg-stream`'s `aen_imx335` scenario rebuilds clean at
  SRAM0 98.50% usage. The existing IMX296 scenario rebuilds clean too,
  BEHAVIOURALLY UNCHANGED (the new `isp_stream_start()` crop guard IS
  compiled for it too, but is a no-op since its `crop-x0`/`crop-y0`
  default to 0; it never touches the `sony_imx335` DT compat, so every new
  `#if` branch compiles out, and its own gain-conversion Kconfig values
  stay at 1/1, both no-ops). It rebuilds clean; the unchanged behaviour
  follows from that reasoning, not from the rebuild or matching SRAM0
  numbers.

### Known limitations — IMX335 Stage B items not yet verified (#2327)

- Colour (AWB/CCM) — no calibration table exists yet, every IMX335 ISP
  build falls through to the stock ARX3A0 defaults.
- Frame rate AT THE SENSOR by an independent method — runs 333/334's
  `HMAX`/`VMAX` I2C readback confirms the DRIVER's own programmed state
  (30 fps), not an external timing measurement; Stage A's own raw-capture
  frame rate also remains unmeasured.
- AE behaviour in lighting other than runs 332-334's own scene.
- The `aen-isp-capture` AE-off scenario
  (`-DEXTRA_CONF_FILE=overlay-no-ae.conf`) — never bench-run.
- IMX335's full-resolution (non-binned) mode remains untouched by this
  ISP work, same as Stage A.

### Changed — `pytest tests/scripts/` no longer runs at its CI time cap: five slow test files stop repeating expensive work (#2328)

`pr-metadata-validate`'s `Pytest -- linter + schema regression + topology defaults`
step runs the whole `tests/scripts/` suite under `timeout-minutes: 20`, and on
`dev` it had reached 19 to 20 minutes, so unrelated PRs went red at random on a
timeout. Per-line CI timestamps showed that 51 of the 4,411 tests took 15.2 of
the 19.9 minutes. Five test files accounted for most of that. None of them was
slow for a good reason; each repeated the same expensive work or waited for
nothing.

- `test_alp_quality.py`: `test_run_profile_pr_matches_registry_selection`
  checks WHICH gate scripts the `pr` profile selects, but it executed every one
  of them. It now stubs the gate-execution subprocess call, while
  `run_profile`'s real selection and iteration still run. The assertion is
  unchanged, and dropping a task from the selection still fails it.
- `test_gen_catalog.py`: the full catalog was rebuilt in every test. It is now
  built once per module. `test_render_is_deterministic` still compares two
  independent builds (the cached one against a fresh one), never the cache
  against itself.
- `test_check_zephyr_conf_parity.py`: two tests ran the identical full-corpus
  gate separately. They now share one module-scoped run.
- `test_gen_portability_matrix_libraries.py`: five tests each regenerated the
  whole matrix. They now share one module-scoped generation, and the
  determinism test compares it against a fresh generation.
  `test_gen_portability_matrix.py` already worked this way and is unchanged.
- `test_apt_bounded_wrapper.py`: the tests waited out 12 s attempt slices
  against a fake `apt` that runs `sleep 9999`. They now pass smaller values
  through the wrapper's existing `APT_ATTEMPT_TIMEOUT` / `APT_STEP_BUDGET`
  overrides. The #1604 regression test still straddles the wrapper's fixed
  10 s give-up floor. `scripts/ci/apt-bounded.sh` itself is unchanged.

Locally the six files went from about 420 s to 104 s, and all 71 of their tests
pass. No production script changed, and no assertion was removed or loosened.

### Changed — `pytest tests/scripts/` runs in parallel with pytest-xdist in CI and in `test-all.sh` (#2328)

The `tests/scripts/` suite (about 4,400 tests) ran serially in three places.
`pr-metadata-validate`'s pytest step had reached 19 to 20 minutes of its
20-minute cap, and each `cross-platform-zephyr` `python-smoke` job took 9 to 15
minutes per OS. The suite is almost entirely independent tests plus
subprocess spawns, so it parallelises cleanly.

- `pytest-xdist>=3.5` joins the `[dev]` extra. `uv.lock` gains `pytest-xdist`
  and its dependency `execnet`, and nothing else.
- Both CI invocations now pass `-n auto`, one worker per runner core:
  `pr-metadata-validate.yml`'s `Pytest -- linter + schema regression +
  topology defaults` step and `cross-platform-zephyr.yml`'s
  `pytest tests/scripts/` step. The first step's comment claimed these tests
  "run in <2 s" and cited a stale 13.5-minute worst case; it now describes
  the whole suite. The step's `timeout-minutes: 20` cap is unchanged.
- **Tests that write into the real checkout now run on their own.** Nine
  modules temporarily write into the checkout and clean up afterwards: fake
  `docs/abi/v99.9x-snapshot.json` baselines, `.test-*` fixtures under
  `metadata/e1m_modules/` and `metadata/chips/`, and a `git worktree add`
  against the shared `.git`. Under xdist, another worker can glob one of
  those transient files mid-test. This was observed at 12 workers:
  `test_abi_snapshot`'s real-tree check took the freeze-gate test's fake
  `v99.99` snapshot as the last released baseline.
  `tests/scripts/conftest.py` now lists those modules in one place,
  `_REPO_WRITER_MODULES`, and gives their tests a `repo_writes` marker. Every
  runner runs `-n auto -m "not repo_writes"` first, then `-m repo_writes`
  serially (123 of 4,465 tests, about 4 s). In both workflows the two phases
  are separate steps. In `cross-platform-zephyr` that is required, because on
  Windows `run:` is pwsh, which only checks the last command's exit code.
  The serial step still runs when the parallel one fails
  (`if: ${{ !cancelled() }}`). Run under `-n` without the `-m` filter, the
  writer tests skip with a reason that names the serial command, so they
  never race.
- `scripts/test-all.sh`'s `pytest-scripts` stage runs the same two phases
  when `pytest-xdist` is importable, and otherwise still runs the suite
  serially, so a venv without the new extra keeps working.

Locally with 12 workers, the parallel phase took 3:00 in each of three
repeated runs, with the same result every time; the same suite serially takes
12:51. No test failed because of parallel execution, and none left a file
behind in the checkout.

### Changed — the hot metadata YAML readers parse with libyaml's C parser when PyYAML has it (#2328)

A per-call-site timing hook over the whole `tests/scripts/` suite found three
YAML readers responsible for about 78% of the time spent inside PyYAML:
`strict_yaml_load` (`scripts/strict_loaders.py`), the validator's
`_load_metadata_yaml` (`scripts/alp_cli/validator.py`), and
`load_family_table` (`scripts/alp_orchestrate/sdk_compat.py`). All three used
the pure-Python parser.

- `strict_loaders._StrictLoader` now subclasses
  `getattr(yaml, "CSafeLoader", yaml.SafeLoader)`. That is libyaml's C parser
  when PyYAML was built with it (PyYAML's wheels are), and the pure-Python
  parser otherwise. The constructor is the same Python `SafeConstructor`, so
  values, the `DuplicateKeyError` rejection, and its line/column marks are
  unchanged. Merge keys (`<<`) were checked too.
- New `strict_loaders.fast_safe_load(text)`: exactly `yaml.safe_load`
  semantics (a duplicate key keeps the last value) on the same loader. The
  validator and `load_family_table` call it instead of `yaml.safe_load`, so
  neither gains duplicate-key rejection it did not have before.
- Across all 701 git-tracked `*.yaml` / `*.yml` files, both loaders parse
  about 11.5x faster: 1.40 s down to 0.12 s. Locally, one serial run of
  `pytest tests/scripts/` took 16:26 on the base commit and 11:33 with this
  change. Run-to-run variance on that machine is large, though, so treat the
  suite-level figure as indicative.
- `tests/scripts/test_strict_loaders.py` pins the behaviour.
  - When libyaml is present, both loaders must use it.
  - The C and pure-Python loaders must return the same value, or raise the
    same exception class, on every tracked YAML file and on five malformed
    inputs: a duplicate key, a duplicate key after a merge, a tab indent, an
    unclosed flow sequence, and two documents. The malformed inputs are
    asserted to raise, so the error half of the comparison is actually
    exercised.

For tan-cli: `scripts/strict_loaders.py` is one of its hand-ported files,
guarded by the `STRICT_LOADERS_PINNED_SDK_COMMIT` fork-audit pin (ADR-0029).
tan's copy keeps the pure-Python parser until that pin is next re-audited;
the port is a two-line change.

### Added — E1M-X-EVK carrier audio: TAS2563 stereo ALSA card on V2N-family Linux (#2331)

`meta-alp-sdk/recipes-kernel/linux/linux-renesas/e1m-x-evk.dtsi` gains the
SoC audio side for the carrier's stereo TAS2563 smart-amp pair (U27 @0x4D
left, U28 @0x4E right, on I2C0 + I2S0 through the TMUX1574 path-mux): I2S0
pinctrl (SSIU1/SSI1 SCK/WS/SDATA at PFC function 7), `&audio_clkb {
clock-frequency = <24576000>; };` for the on-module 5L35023B SE3 24.576 MHz
feed, `&rcar_sound` enabled with an SSI1 playback endpoint, and both
`ti,tas2563` codecs on ONE audio-graph-card2 `multi` link (SSI1 fanned out
to both amps, so both follow the stream's hw_params and DAPM power
sequencing). Each codec endpoint declares 2 x 32-bit TDM slots to match
rsnd's fixed 32-bit SSI word. `tas2563-audio.cfg` enables
`CONFIG_SND_SOC_TAS2562=y` and pins `CONFIG_SND_AUDIO_GRAPH_CARD2=y` for
`e1m-v2n101`/`e1m-v2m101`. The same dtsi hogs Audio_CLKB_OE (P67) high so
the 5L35023B's 24.576 MHz output reaches the ADG, and drops the carrier
`&i2c6`/`&i2c7` nodes, which claimed the I2S0 pins (P44-P47) -- so
`/dev/i2c-6` and `/dev/i2c-7` no longer exist on these MACHINEs.

Kernel patch `0009-ASoC-tas2562-reset-the-amplifier-at-probe.patch`: the
6.1 driver's register cache assumes POR state (including page 0) but never
resets the part. SD_N is one shared net that does not toggle across a warm
reboot, so the amps kept the previous boot's page and settings -- gain
writes were dropped as cache no-ops and page-0 writes landed in page 2.
The driver now selects book 0 / page 0 and issues SW_RESET in its
component probe, at card bind, after every amp sharing SD_N has released
it.

A new `alsa-state` bbappend ships boot-time mixer defaults: each amp's
"ASI1 Sel" set to its own slot (Left/Right), and Amp Gain at its lowest
level (code 01h = 8.5 dBV) instead of the silicon default (10h =
16.0 dBV, ~10 W peak into 4 ohm). The 6.1 driver's dB scale for "Amp Gain
Volume" is one code off TI SLASET3D Table 7-105, so levels are given here
as raw codes.

Bench-verified on E1M-V2M103 (2026-09-27): card registers
(`rsnd-dai.0-tas2562-amplifier_multi`), both amps go software-shutdown ->
active with a 48 kHz stream and back, TDM detect reads 48 kHz / 64 bits per
frame on both, no live faults, and the mixer defaults are restored at boot.
Acoustic output is not yet confirmed by ear.

Still open on #2331: I2C-address ownership between this kernel codec
binding and the SDK's userspace `chips/tas2563` driver (no live conflict
today -- no `alp-chips` PACKAGECONFIG enables it on these MACHINEs).

### Fixed

- E1M-X EVK (V2N family): the TAS2563 ALSA card (`sound_card`) and `&rcar_sound` are now `disabled` (#2331). Playback on SSI1 drove the amps' SDOUT net (P46 -> `I2S0_SDI`), not their SDIN, so it produced no audio and could contend with the amps' IV-sense transmit. With both nodes off, `sound_pins` is never applied and P44/P45/P46 stay at reset. The TAS2563 codec nodes still probe over I2C0. Audio returns once playback moves to SSI2's data line (P47 -> `I2S0_SDO`).

### Fixed — V2N on-module CAN-FD rows carry a real E1M-X pad crosswalk (#2331)

`metadata/e1m_modules/v2n/renesas-peripheral-map.tsv`'s four `CANFD2_*`/
`CANFD3_*` rows (the on-module TCAN1044 CAN-FD transceivers, #2332) still
carried `e1m_pad`/`e1m_function: "TBD"` in `metadata/pinmux/v2n.yaml` after
#2405 filled the other 40 directly-routed V2N pads — the TSV's `pad_first`
shape supports the optional `e1m_pad`/`e1m_function` columns #2405 added,
but those four rows were left without them.

Filled from #2332's schematic-sourced transceiver-to-channel mapping
(CANFD3/U15 on P86/P87 is carrier CAN0, CANFD2/U16 on P84/P85 is carrier
CAN1) plus the public e1m-spec E1M-X pinout (`pinout/x-v1.json`, ball ids
`B21`/`B22`/`B24`/`B25`) — no private netlist data was needed or copied
into this repo. `metadata/pinmux/v2n.yaml` regenerated via
`gen_pinmux_capability.py`; route coverage (`check_e1m_route_capability.py`)
is unchanged at 33/48.

### Fixed

- **E1M-V2N/V2M SoM pad crosswalk filled from the SoM netlist (#2331).** `metadata/e1m_modules/v2n/renesas-peripheral-map.tsv` now carries the E1M edge ball and function for the 40 RZ/V2N pads the SoM routes straight to the connector (I2C0/1/2, SPI0/1/2, I3C, PDM, UART0, SD card detect/reset, AUDIO_CLK, I2S0, I2S1). `metadata/pinmux/v2n.yaml` shows them instead of `TBD`. `gen_pinmux_capability.py` reads the two optional columns.
- **I2S0/SPI direction corrections.** `check_e1m_route_capability.py` hand-mapped SSI1 SDATA to `I2S0_SDO`, SSI2 SDATA to `I2S0_SDI` and RSPI0 to `SPI1_*`. The netlist says the opposite for I2S (P46 -> AQ4 `I2S0_SDI`, P47 -> AR4 `I2S0_SDO`) and `SPI0_*` for RSPI0. Both tables are deleted; the rows now carry the netlist functions.
- **Audio DT flagged.** The E1M-X EVK card plays on SSI1, whose data pin reaches the TAS2563 SDOUT pins rather than SDIN. The `e1m-x-evk.dtsi` comment now says so and warns against playback until the SSI2 data-line fix lands.

### Fixed

- E1M-X EVK (V2N family): re-enable the TAS2563 ALSA card, now playing out of SSI2's data line (P47 -> `I2S0_SDO` -> amp SDIN) with SCK/WS from SSI1 (P44/P45) (#2331). RZ/V2N SSIU_SSI_MODE1.ssi2_pin = 110b (R01UH1072EJ0120, 8.5.2.3.16) makes this possible; new kernel patch 0014 teaches rsnd the SSI2-under-SSI1 parent case (`alp,shared-pin-ssi1` on `&ssi2`). P46 (the amps' SDOUT net) is never muxed. Bench listen still pending.
- E1M-X EVK (V2N family): drop `clk_a`/`clk_c` from the `&rcar_sound` clock list (#2331). Audio_CLKA (AUDIO_EXTAL oscillator) and Audio_CLKC are not fed on this SoM/carrier, so the CPG never raises their CLK_ON monitor and playback start failed with `Failed to enable CLK_ON` / `__pm_clk_enable ... error -110` (538 ms periods). The card now runs from Audio_CLKB only. Bench, E1M-V2M103: 2 s of 48 kHz stereo plays in 2.06 s wall time with no -110 (it was 538 ms per period before). Kernel patch renumbered 0013 -> 0014 because the CAN-FD bring-up (#2341) carries 0013.

### Fixed

- **TAS2563 kernel/userspace I2C-address ownership documented and closed out (#2331 item 1).** The E1M-X-EVK carrier's `ti,tas2563` ALSA codec nodes bind i2c0@0x4d/0x4e; the SDK's own userspace `chips/tas2563` driver (over `alp_i2c_*`) must not also be wired up against the same bus without racing the kernel driver's registers. Resolved without a PACKAGECONFIG lock-out: `tas2563_init()` already propagates its bus call's status verbatim (#2077), so when a kernel driver holds the address, `ioctl(I2C_SLAVE)` fails `EBUSY` on the Yocto backend and `tas2563_init()` returns `ALP_ERR_BUSY` -- a clear, distinct refusal rather than a register race or a misleading `ALP_ERR_NOT_READY`. Documented on `tas2563_init()`'s `@retval ALP_ERR_BUSY`, in `metadata/chips/tas2563.yaml`, and in `e1m-x-evk.dtsi`'s audio comment. Zephyr/CM33 behaviour is unchanged -- no kernel client exists on those targets.

### Fixed — E1M-X EVK TCAL9538 addresses (#2333)

The E1M-X EVK carries two TCAL9538 I/O expanders on its sensor bus (`XEVK_I2C_BUS_SENSORS` / E1M_X_I2C0), but `metadata/boards/e1m-x-evk.yaml` recorded a single one at `0x72`. The board strapping, confirmed against the E1M-X EVK V2 netlist and a live `i2c-0` sweep on an E1M-V2M103, is:

- U35 main expander at `0x73` (A0 and A1 high)
- U37 PCIe expander at `0x71` (A0 high, A1 low). It sits on `PCIE0_I2C`, which is joined to I2C0 through an LSF0102 level shifter.

The single `XEVK_I2C_ADDR_TCAL9538` macro is replaced by `XEVK_I2C_ADDR_TCAL9538_MAIN` (`0x73`) and `XEVK_I2C_ADDR_TCAL9538_PCIE` (`0x71`). `XEVK_I2C_ADDR_TCAL9538` stays as an alias for the main expander. `metadata/chips/tcal9538.yaml`'s address scopes and the v0.16 ABI snapshot are updated to match.

On Linux, the sensors on this bus are driven by the SDK's own `chips/` drivers over i2c-dev, the same drivers the AEN EVK uses, not by kernel drivers. Verified on the E1M-V2M103: `examples/v2n/v2n-power-monitor` (`chips/ina236`) reads 3V3 = 3.302 V and 1V8 = 1.792 V. Two carrier defects found while checking the netlist are tracked in #2343: U30 is an INA228 with SDA/SCL swapped, and the two IMUs are both strapped to `0x69`. The U32 VCAM2 monitor's `0x48` also collides with the TAS2563 broadcast address on this bus; U32 is removed on the current build batch and its metadata entry now says so.

### Fixed — IMX335 full-resolution mode's `Y_OUT_SIZE`/format-height mismatch, width bench-confirmed, line count not measured (#2334)

Upstream Zephyr's `drivers/video/imx335.c` all-pixel mode table
`imx335_bin_none` wrote `Y_OUT_SIZE` (`0x3056`) = `0x07ac` (1964 lines),
mismatched against the 2592x1944 format's advertised 1944-line height --
the same class of defect `zephyr/patches/zephyr/
0004-imx335-2lane-link-freq-and-binning.patch` already fixed for the
2x2-binned path (#2327). Both this driver's own `imx335_init_params`
(`Y_OUT_SIZE` `0x0798` = 1944) and the mainline Linux imx335 driver's
full-resolution mode table (`raspberrypi/linux`, branch `rpi-6.12.y` --
register value carried as a hardware fact, no GPL code copied) agree on
1944; `imx335_bin_none` is corrected to match. Patch 0004 extended (sha256
updated in `zephyr/patches.yml`), applies clean against a pristine Zephyr
v4.4.1 checkout.

No corresponding `HNUM`/`WINMODE` change was needed: unlike `imx335_bin_2x2`
(which set an explicit, bench-derived `HNUM` this driver had no formula
for), `imx335_bin_none`'s `HNUM` (restored to `0x0a20` = 2592 by #2327's own
fix) already matches both `imx335_init_params` and the Linux full-resolution
table, and its `AREA2_WIDTH_1`/`AREA3_WIDTH_1` pair (40 / 3928) already
matches the Linux table too.

**Bench runs 335-337 (E1M-AEN803 2026W36-0001), scratch-only diagnostics**:

- Run 335: the CPI's `CAM_INTR_VSYNC`/`CAM_INTR_HSYNC` interrupts do NOT
  fire while `CAM_CTRL_START` (the write-DMA arm bit) is left clear --
  counting HSYNC/VSYNC edges without engaging the write-DMA is not possible
  on this hardware. The same run read the sensor's registers back in
  all-pixel mode and confirmed the patch's writes: `WINMODE 0x00`,
  `HTRIMMING_START 0x003c`, `HNUM 0x0a20`, `Y_OUT_SIZE 0x0798`.
- Run 336 (2x2-binned): the CPI's `CAM_VIDEO_FCFG` register's `ROW` field
  bounds a capture to exactly `ROW + 1` lines in hardware -- the product
  driver itself writes `ROW = height - 1` when setting a format
  (`zephyr/drivers/video/video_alif.c`), and this run's 1296x972 control
  capture wrote `FCFG = 0x03cb0510` (`ROW` field `0x3cb` = 971, i.e. 972
  lines) and captured exactly 972 lines -- a real, safe, hardware-enforced
  bounding mechanism. Separately, a diagnostic build that arms
  `CAM_CTRL_START` and plans to cut the capture from an `INTR_HSYNC`
  handler via `hw_cam_cpi_only_stop()` (`CAM_CTRL = 0` plus a soft reset)
  found that software stop does NOT stop the DMA. Filed as issue #2342;
  `docs/camera-shields.md`'s recipe text no longer proposes it as a
  fallback.
- Run 337 (full-resolution 2592x1944): `CAM_VIDEO_FCFG`'s `ROW` field set
  to `2` (3 lines) and then `7` (8 lines) -- the same `ROW = lines - 1`
  encoding as run 336's control. Both captured exactly the requested line
  count (extent 15552 bytes = 3 x 5184 bytes; last non-zero byte at offset
  41471 for the 8-line request, i.e. 8 x 5184 = 41472 bytes with a zero
  final byte) at 2592 samples/line (5184 bytes/line -- 2 bytes/sample, this
  CPI's 16-bit-unpacked storage, not RAW10-packed), stride autocorrelation
  peak at exactly 5184 (= 2x2592, no row-to-row shear), canary intact both
  times, 4/4 identical. **Width is confirmed exactly 2592 at full
  resolution**, matching `HNUM`. Caveat: the DW CSI-2 host's Camera-mode
  `hact` was itself set to 2592 for this capture, so a sensor line longer
  than 2592 samples truncated to `hact` is not excluded by this
  measurement alone.
- **Lines/frame (1944 vs. 1964) was NOT measured** -- HSYNC/VSYNC counting
  needs the DMA armed (run 335), and a full 2592x1944x2 = 10,077,696-byte
  (~10.1 MB) frame can't be written to prove the line count directly. This
  fix is still justified without that direct measurement:
  `CAM_VIDEO_FCFG`'s `ROW` field bounds the CPI's write to a fixed row
  count in hardware regardless of the sensor's own `Y_OUT_SIZE` value (run
  336's finding), so upstream's buggy 1964 could never have overrun an
  `FCFG`-bounded capture buffer either way -- the memory-safety concern
  that motivated this diagnostic is independently covered by `FCFG`
  bounding. The `Y_OUT_SIZE` register fix itself remains justified by the
  driver's own init table (`imx335_init_params`) and the mainline Linux
  imx335 driver's full-resolution mode table, not by a bench measurement
  of the disputed line count.

See `docs/camera-shields.md`'s "Full-resolution mode: bench results (issue
#2334)" section for the full writeup. `metadata/chips/imx335.yaml` gains a
matching note.

### Fixed — ISP-Pico camera backend forwards the requested fps to every sensor, not just OV5647 (#2338)

`src/backends/camera/alif_isp_pico.c`'s `alp_camera_open()` forwarded the
caller's `alp_camera_config_t::fps` request to a hardcoded
`DEVICE_DT_GET(DT_NODELABEL(ov5647))` sensor device. For every other sensor
behind the ISP-Pico (IMX296, IMX335) the request was silently dropped and the
sensor free-ran at its driver's own default rate: bench run 333, IMX335 ran
at its upstream driver's default 30 fps regardless of the 15 fps
`examples/connectivity/camera-mjpeg-stream` requests on its shared 1280x960
path.

Fixed generically, with no per-sensor DT nodelabel list: `isp_pico.c` gains
`.get_frmival`/`.set_frmival` (forwarding to `config->controller`),
`video_alif.c`'s `alif_cam_set_frmival()` forwards to its endpoint (matching
its existing `alif_cam_get_frmival()`), and `video_csi_dw.c`'s
`csi2_dw_set_frmival()` forwards to the same
`config->sensor[data->current_sensor]` its own `.get_frmival` already reads
— so a 2-sensor CSI node's AE (which reads the rate back through
`.get_frmival`) sees the rate this sets. The backend now just calls
`video_set_frmival(dev, ...)` once on the ISP device itself, which walks the
whole isp -> cam -> csi -> sensor chain through those forwarders and lands on
whichever real sensor is wired. `cfg->fps == 0` still means "backend
default" (10 fps), unchanged. A sensor whose `set_frmival()` can't actually
change the rate (IMX296's all-pixel-scan mode has exactly one fixed 60.3
frame/s — `imx296_set_frmival()` always reports that fixed rate back rather
than erroring) or that returns `-ENOSYS`/`-ENOTSUP` outright (e.g. TPG mode,
no controller wired) now just keeps running at its existing rate, logged at
`INF`, not treated as a failure. The settled rate is still only logged, not
reported back to the caller — `<alp/camera.h>` has no settled-fps field yet
(#2279).

This surfaced a real consequence for IMX335: its `imx335_framerates[]`
(`{25, 30, 50, 60}`) has no 15 fps entry, so `examples/connectivity/
camera-mjpeg-stream`'s shared 1280x960 path would now round that request up
to 25 fps — a rate hal_alif patch 0014's AE envelope (calibrated at exactly
30 fps) was never derived against. Fixed by splitting the requested fps out
of that example's resolution-select Kconfig into its own
`CONFIG_CAMERA_MJPEG_STREAM_FPS` symbol, which the `aen_imx335` scenario in
`testcase.yaml` overrides to 30 via `extra_configs` — no sensor `#if` in the
portable example itself. OV5647 and IMX296 keep the unaffected 15 fps
default: OV5647 reaches it exactly (unchanged), IMX296 stays at its fixed
60.3 frame/s regardless of the request (also unchanged). `isp_pico.c`'s
`isp_apply_ae()`'s existing `CONFIG_VIDEO_ISP_VSI_AE_EXP_TIME_MAX_US_CAP`
backstop (33207 us for IMX335) now also covers this app-level path, not just
a direct `video_set_frmival()` caller bypassing the backend.

Also updated: `docs/camera-shields.md`'s Frame rate section,
`examples/connectivity/camera-mjpeg-stream/README.md`, and
`include/alp/camera.h`'s `fps` doc comment (generalized the OV5647-specific
example, since the behaviour is now sensor-generic).

**Bench run 338** (`camera-mjpeg-stream`, `aen_imx335` scenario, E1M-AEN803
2026W36-0001) proved the fix on real silicon. With
`CONFIG_CAMERA_MJPEG_STREAM_FPS=30` (this scenario's override): driver
`frame_rate` 30, IMX335 `HMAX 0x0226`/`VMAX 0x001194` read back over I2C,
`fps=30 fail=0 retry=0`, one HTTP client 29.98 fps / 779.4 KB/s delivered
over 30 s. With the symbol forced back to 15 (this fix's default, pre-fix
behaviour for comparison): the backend logged `camera0: requested 15 fps,
settled on 25/1`, driver `frame_rate` 25, `HMAX 0x0280` — proving the
request now actually reaches IMX335 and the sensor rounds it to its nearest
supported rate, exactly as designed. OV5647 was not bench-verified this run
(not fitted on this board); IMX296 was not bench-verified.

### Fixed — a mid-frame `video_flush(dev, true)` on the E8 CPI no longer overruns the frame buffer or hangs the SoC (#2342)

On the CPI AXI capture path, `alif_cam_flush(cancel)` in
`zephyr/drivers/video/video_alif.c` stopped a capture in progress with
`CAM_CTRL = 0`, then a `BUSY` poll (up to 1000 x `k_msleep(1)`), then the
soft reset. On E1M-AEN803 2026W36-0001 with an IMX335 (bench run 340), a
mid-frame cancel with the old driver kept the DMA writing past the buffer
through the rest of SRAM0 — 1,543,664 B past a 128 KiB guard — with no
fault raised. The register-level diagnostic (runs 336-339) showed why:
`CAM_CTRL = 0` does not stop the DMA (about 2x frame overrun), `BUSY` reads
0 while the DMA is still writing, and only the 3-step soft reset
(`CAM_CTRL` 0, then `SW_RESET`, then 0) stops a frame mid-capture.

A soft reset issued while a frame is still being written is not safe
either: the first revision of this fix, which reset the CPI immediately on
cancel, hung the SoC in 12 of 212 mid-frame cancels (run 341). The core
stalled, SRAM0 writes never completed, and only a power cycle recovered it.
Resets at a frame boundary (0/240) or after the pixel source was stopped
(0/50) never hung.

What changed:

- `alif_cam_flush(cancel)` masks the `STOP` interrupt, cancels the pending
  completion work item, then waits (1 ms steps, 500 ms cap) for the armed
  frame's hardware `STOP` before the soft reset, so the reset never lands
  on an active AXI write burst. If the source has stopped and no `STOP`
  arrives, it logs a warning and resets after the timeout.
- `hw_cam_cpi_only_stop()`, `alif_cam_stream_stop()` and
  `alif_cam_flush(cancel)` share one `hw_cam_quiesce()` helper: mask
  interrupts, soft reset, clear `CAM_INTR`, end at `CAM_CTRL = 0`. The
  useless `BUSY` polls are gone. The helper's doxygen states the rule:
  stop the source or wait for frame end first.
- Masking `STOP` before cancelling the work item (the `isp_flush()`
  ordering) closes a window where a late `STOP` resubmitted the work item
  into an empty IN-FIFO and stalled the stream. The work item returns
  quietly once a stop has run. A cancel while streaming sets `starved`, so
  the next `video_enqueue()` restarts capture.
- The ISR's post-`STOP` write keeps `FIFO_CLK_SEL` set instead of writing
  0, so a late ISR after a re-arm clears only `START`.
- `capture-mode = "continuous"` is rejected at devicetree build time
  (removed from the `alif,cam.yaml` enum). No overlay in this repo used
  it, and no stop path here has a safe abort for a mode without a
  hardware frame-end boundary.
- Never write `CAM_AXI_ERR_STAT` (CPI+0x18): it is not writable on this
  CPI, and a write bus-faults.

Bench, this revision (E1M-AEN803 2026W36-0001, IMX335, runs 342-343):

- Mid-frame `video_flush(dev, true)`: 0 hangs and 0 overruns in 520
  events, 200 of them on the stock devicetree. The aborted buffer was
  untouched after flush returned, restart worked every time, and flush
  latency was at most 29.7 ms (one frame).
- Mid-frame `video_stream_stop()`: 0 hangs and 0 overruns in 100 events.
- Forced timeout path (sensor put in standby mid-frame, then flush): the
  timeout fired 81 times out of 85, with 0 hangs and 0 overruns, and
  restart worked every time.
- `camera-mjpeg-stream`: 2471 frames at 26 fps, no errors.

Not fixed here: restart after a mid-frame `video_stream_stop()` on the CSI
endpoint fails the same way on the base driver (#2351).

Closes #2342.

### Fixed — E1M-X EVK metadata: U30 is an INA228 at 0x42, and the BMI323/ICM-42670 0x69 collision is documented (#2343)

The E1M-X EVK V2 netlist showed that the +5V input monitor U30 is an
INA228 (20-bit register map, A1 = GND, A0 = SDA → `0x42`), not an INA236
